title: v0.2.0
summary: A new version of the software, v0.2.0, has been released. The release includes various updates and improvements across different components, such as the web UI, ggml, and support for different hardware platforms. The version update includes changes to the release process, bug fixes, and optimizations for performance and compatibility.

title: An AI tool for prioritizing candidate biomarkers from wearable sensor data
summary: A new AI tool, the Biomarker Discovery Framework, is designed to help identify potential biomarkers from wearable sensor data by combining hypothesis generation, statistical analysis, and literature-based reasoning. The framework aims to address the challenge of turning large-scale physiological data into clinically relevant biomarkers. It uses a multi-agent system under human supervision to prioritize candidate biomarkers through an iterative process, ensuring statistical rigor and human oversight. The system was tested on three large-scale cohorts, identifying 41 digital biomarkers for mental health and 25 for metabolic outcomes. The framework outperformed other AI systems in a blinded evaluation, receiving the highest scores across multiple quality dimensions.

title: GPU-Accelerated Clustering for Financial Instruments at Scale
summary: A GPU-accelerated clustering method using AdaptGrow and SymNMF is presented to improve the grouping of financial instruments for portfolio construction, risk aggregation, and trade surveillance. The method addresses the challenge of unstable groupings and structural changes by using rolling correlation and tail-dependence matrices to produce hard labels, soft factor loadings, and structural-break signals. The approach is scalable from single-GPU to multi-node infrastructure and is memory-efficient, allowing for the processing of up to 100,000 instruments on a single GPU and one million instruments across 16 nodes.

title: SOP-Bench: A new benchmark for evaluating AI agents on real business procedures
summary: SOP-Bench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents on real business procedures, addressing the limitations of existing benchmarks that fail to test the complex, ambiguous nature of actual operational workflows. The benchmark pairs real enterprise procedures with tools and ground-truth answers, allowing agents to be assessed on their ability to complete tasks rather than just generating text that a grader might find acceptable. The benchmark was presented at the 2026 KDD conference and includes 12 business areas with over 2,000 tasks, each featuring tools, specifications, and test cases. It is a framework that allows for customization and extension, with a focus on realistic procedures and the ability to track agent performance against known outcomes.

title: Connecting retail demand planning to campaign and store execution
summary: Retail and consumer goods teams face challenges in aligning decisions across disconnected systems and teams, leading to difficulties in turning analysis into results. A unified application, demonstrated by Databricks, connects performance reviews, demand planning, audience activation, store execution, and campaign measurement in one end-to-end process. The application is built on three foundations: data unification, governance, and intelligence. It enables stakeholders to review performance, plan demand, and measure outcomes using a shared data source, with features like natural language querying and autonomous agents. The workflow supports planning actions, marketing decisions, and store-level execution, creating a closed-loop view that connects campaign activity back to sales and operational outcomes.

title: Longer wells boost Permian crude oil and natural gas production
summary: Well operators in the Permian region of western Texas and eastern New Mexico are increasing oil and natural gas production by drilling longer, horizontal wells, including super-lateral wells exceeding 15,000 feet. This shift allows operators to access more reservoir rock per well, boosting production while reducing the number of wells needed. In 2015, short-reach wells under 5,000 feet made up 43% of completions, but by 2025, they accounted for only 4%. Mid-length laterals, between 5,000 and 15,000 feet, increased from 57% to 81% of completions, while super-laterals, over 15,000 feet, accounted for 15% of new wells in 2025. Despite stable new well counts, production rose from 2.9 million to 11.2 million barrels of oil equivalent per day (BOE/d) between 2015 and 2025, a 284% increase. The average lateral length of new wells grew 77% over the decade, from 6,149 feet to 10,867 feet, according to Enverus data.

title: AI’s Three-Body Problem: no single force can dictate the outcome
summary: The AI economy in 2026 is described as a three-body system, with closed-source frontier labs, open-weight models from China, and application companies competing and influencing each other. The system is marked by instability due to factors like increased demand and revenue for frontier labs, advancements in open models, and the response from application companies. The article predicts that the discomfort with high pricing will ease as competition drives prices down and returns on AI investments become clearer. The shift toward a multi-model world will continue, and U.S. open-weight models will become viable alternatives to Chinese ones. The equilibrium of the system remains unsettled, with the key question being who captures the value from AI's success.

title: Victim of sword attack at a Swedish school was a 17-year-old girl
summary: A 17-year-old girl was the victim of a deadly sword attack at Brinell School in Fagersta, Sweden, on Friday. An 18-year-old suspect, armed with a sword, attacked the school during classes, killing one person and injuring three others, two of whom were severely wounded. The suspect was arrested, and the case is being investigated as murder and attempted murder. The region declared a state of emergency, which was lifted by Saturday. Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson expressed condolences and noted the police's intensive investigation. The attack follows a series of violent school incidents in Sweden, including a mass shooting in Örebro last year and a knife attack in Malmo in 2022.

title: CONCACAF chief asks Infantino to skip youth tournament amid FIFA governance crisis
summary: CONCACAF President Victor Montagliani has requested FIFA President Gianni Infantino to avoid attending a youth soccer tournament in the Dominican Republic, citing the ongoing governance crisis at FIFA. Montagliani's letter to Infantino emphasized that his presence would draw excessive media attention, overshadowing the technical aspects of the CFU U-14 Series event. Infantino, facing pressure from UEFA, AFC, and CONCACAF to resign over his failed proposal to sell a World Cup stake, is visiting the Dominican Republic. Despite the request, Infantino is expected to attend the event, which is supported by Dominican officials who appreciate his presence for the country's football development.

title: Pinarayi Vijayan, Binoy Viswam lock horns over Deputy Leader of the Opposition post
summary: The issue of who will hold the Deputy Leader of the Opposition post in the Keralam Assembly has caused tension within the Left Democratic Front (LDF). Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan asserted that the post would go to his party, the Communist Party of India (Marxist), and ruled out the possibility of the Communist Party of India (CPI) securing it. He stated that the only remaining task was to submit a letter to the Speaker to officially assign the position. In contrast, CPI State secretary Binoy Viswam criticized Vijayan's remarks, calling them unbecoming and lacking political maturity, while emphasizing the CPI's claim to the post.

title: Government restricts FDCs with chlorpheniramine, phenylephrine for children below 4
summary: The Union Health Ministry has imposed restrictions on the manufacture, sale, and distribution of all fixed-dose combinations (FDCs) containing chlorpheniramine maleate and phenylephrine hydrochloride, requiring a clear warning that these medicines shall not be used in children below four years of age. The decision follows recommendations from an expert committee and the Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB), citing risks to young children and the availability of safer alternatives. The notification, issued under Section 26A of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, is effective from its publication in the Official Gazette and extends previous restrictions to all formulations containing these ingredients.

title: Bills on fast track: Over half of 18th Lok Sabha bills passed in same session, shows data
summary: Over half of the bills introduced in the 18th Lok Sabha have been passed by both Houses in the same session, according to an analysis by PRS Legislative Research. The pace of bill passage has accelerated sharply over the past year, with six of the 11 bills passed during the Monsoon Session not included in the government's original legislative agenda. Concerns have been raised about the limited time available for parliamentary scrutiny, as the short gap between introduction and passage of bills reduces opportunities for stakeholder consultation and thorough examination.

title: Kazakhstan votes in parliamentary election expected to strengthen president’s grip on power
summary: Kazakhstan held parliamentary elections on Sunday, expected to consolidate President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's power. The ruling pro-presidential Adilet party is predicted to secure an overwhelming majority, with smaller Tokayev-aligned parties also likely to enter parliament. The election follows a constitutional overhaul in March that merged the two chambers of parliament into one and granted the president authority to appoint key officials, including reestablishing the vice presidency. The changes, supported by 87% of voters in a referendum, allow Tokayev to potentially run for another seven-year term. The vote occurs amid economic challenges, including 10.2% inflation in February and public discontent over tax hikes, as well as intensified repression of independent media.

title: Transshipment scam or efficient supply chain? How U.S. firms turn it into profit?
summary: A 2026 White House report accuses India's Pune–Gujarat–Chennai production belt of facilitating a transshipment scam, where Chinese goods are routed through India to evade U.S. tariffs. The report claims that Indian cities act as logistics hubs without significant value addition, leading to a decline in U.S. pump and compressor manufacturing. However, industry sources suggest that many U.S. multinationals with global production centers use India for cost-effective sourcing, and some Indian SMEs import parts from China, paying tariffs. The report highlights a global phenomenon where imports from countries like Canada and Mexico have increased, with U.S. firms and other global players also contributing significantly to the U.S. pump market. The report proposes using AI tools to detect transshipment and enforce stricter origin rules, but industry experts warn of potential compliance costs and uncertainties for legitimate manufacturers.

title: What are the U.S.’s latest allegations against India? | Explained
summary: The U.S. has accused India of aiding China in evading tariffs by transshipping goods through third countries. The White House report titled 'The Great Transhipment Scam' claims that India, along with Mexico, Canada, the European Union, Japan, and South Korea, is enabling China to bypass U.S. tariffs by modifying goods slightly before exporting them to the U.S. The report estimates that $67 billion in goods were transshipped through India in 2025, resulting in $28 billion in lost tariff revenue. The U.S. has previously imposed tariffs on India for issues like Russian oil imports and forced labor, and the latest allegations could lead to further penalties.

title: ‘Impressed by their energy & ambition’: PM Modi meets India’s space startups on National Space Day
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met with India's space startups on National Space Day, expressing admiration for their energy and ambition. He shared a video of the interaction on X, encouraging people to share their views on India's space program. Modi also greeted citizens on the occasion, emphasizing innovation and exploration. Union Home Minister Amit Shah highlighted the significance of National Space Day, commemorating the successful landing of Chandrayaan-3 on the Moon's south polar region. The celebrations marked the third National Space Day, held in Ahmedabad, with participation from key officials and industry leaders. Isro Chairman V Narayanan spoke about the progress of India's space program and the scientific data obtained from Chandrayaan-3.

title: Australia confirms first H5N1 bird flu case in a mammal
summary: Australia has confirmed its first case of H5N1 bird flu in a mammal, a long-nosed fur seal found in South Australia. Federal agriculture minister Julie Collins stated that the infection is not unexpected, particularly in marine mammals in areas with high bird flu rates. The outbreak, which began in June, has led to mass seabird deaths and is now spreading to native species. The seal, part of an estimated 100,000 in the state's waters, was found dead with no signs of injury. Officials noted that the infection likely occurred through exposure to infected wild birds or their environment. There have been 297 positive bird flu cases in Australia, with 194 in South Australia. No evidence of infection in poultry or agriculture systems has been found yet.

title: Eyes on Xi visit, ‘early harvest’ as Doval heads to Beijing
summary: National Security Advisor Ajit Doval is set to visit Beijing from August 23 to 24, 2026, for the 25th round of talks between the Special Representatives on the India-China boundary issue. The visit precedes a potential visit by Chinese President Xi Jinping to India in September and aims to assess the broader bilateral relationship. The talks will also review the situation along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) and discuss border management and delimitation. The visit follows recent discussions under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC) and comes amid ongoing tensions in various sectors of the India-China border.

title: Legal complexities of AI training on copyrighted books
summary: The legality of training AI models on copyrighted books remains unclear, with courts and experts highlighting the complexity of applying outdated copyright laws to modern technology. Judge William Alsup ruled against Anthropic for using pirated books from shadow libraries, but found their AI training lawful, emphasizing the difference between copying and using content. Legal experts like Cathy Gellis and Jason Henderson note that copyright law, unchanged since 1976, struggles to address AI's transformative use of content. Fair use considerations, particularly whether AI training is transformative, remain central to these debates. Courts have shown mixed rulings, with some finding AI training to compete unfairly with content creators, while others allow it if it doesn't directly compete. The issue of AI-generated content ownership also raises new questions, as seen in the Thaler v. Perlmutter case. Most AI companies face ongoing litigation, with no definitive legal resolution in sight.

title: Tech firms use off-balance-sheet financing for datacenters, not Enron 2.0
summary: Experts warn of a potential 'debt bomb' crisis as tech giants like Meta, Oracle, and xAI use special-purpose entities to fund AI datacenters, keeping debt off their balance sheets. These entities raise billions from investors and banks, with the parent companies retaining exclusive use of the facilities. The Financial Times reported over $120bn in AI datacenter spending shifted off balance sheets through such structures, while Goldman Sachs estimates $5.3tn could be spent through 2030. Critics compare this to Enron's 2001 collapse, but the author argues the risks are different today. Unlike biotech firms in the 1980s, modern datacenters have real assets and strong demand, with vacancy rates at record lows. While some investments may fail, the author believes the transparency and market demand make this financial engineering less risky than past scandals.

title: NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS Enhances AI Factory Efficiency Through Dynamic Power Management
summary: NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS is a suite of technologies designed to maximize AI factory performance per watt by optimizing power usage across chip, thermal, system, and software layers. Traditional data centers often waste power due to static rack provisioning, which allocates maximum power per rack for peak demand, leaving unused capacity. MaxLPS introduces dynamic power allocation, using Dynamic Power Software (DPS) to monitor and reallocate unused power headroom among GPUs. This approach reduces facility overhead and operational inefficiencies, improving power usage effectiveness (PUE) and enabling more racks within the same power budget. NVIDIA reports that MaxLPS can increase GPU capacity by up to 40% within the same power envelope for its Vera Rubin NVL72 AI factories. The system also includes optimized workload profiles and thermal efficiency features, such as 45°C liquid cooling, to further enhance performance per watt. By aligning GPU configuration with workload needs, MaxLPS aims to improve overall AI factory productivity and output efficiency.

title: DeepMind partners with game developers to advance AI research through gaming
summary: DeepMind, a subsidiary of Google, is collaborating with game developers to explore new AI research opportunities through gaming. The company highlights its long history of using games to drive AI breakthroughs, from mastering Atari to solving protein structure prediction. Founded in 2010, DeepMind has developed systems like AlphaGo and AlphaStar that have achieved significant milestones in game-playing AI. The company emphasizes the importance of partnerships with studios like Fenris Creations and Hello Games. DeepMind is now developing SIMA, a generalist AI agent capable of understanding and interacting with game worlds, using models like Gemini. This work aims to create AI companions and NPCs that can adapt to games without code modifications, potentially transforming game development and post-launch experiences.

title: Google Researchers Introduce ME-POIs Framework to Enhance AI Understanding of Place Dynamics
summary: Google researchers have developed the Mobility-Embedded POIs (ME-POIs) framework, which integrates mobility data with text-based representations to improve AI models' understanding of place dynamics. The framework captures the temporal activity rhythms of locations by combining static metadata with anonymized mobility patterns, such as arrival times and stay durations. This approach enables more accurate predictions about attributes like opening hours, price levels, and busyness. ME-POIs addresses the 'long tail' problem by propagating visit patterns from data-rich areas to sparser ones, enhancing predictions for less frequently visited places. The framework also aligns textual descriptions with mobility data to create a holistic representation of places. Testing on Los Angeles and Houston showed significant improvements in prediction accuracy compared to text-only or mobility-only models. The research highlights the value of real-world mobility data in understanding urban dynamics, while emphasizing that the framework provides aggregate insights rather than individualized conclusions.

title: Georgia Tech researchers trace social reasoning in Olmo 3 using open-source tools
summary: Georgia Tech researchers Glenn Matlin and Chandreyi Chakraborty used the open Olmo 3 stack to trace how social reasoning in language models develops. They analyzed how different training data categories influenced model performance on four benchmarks, finding that narrative and interpersonal writing had a stronger impact on social reasoning than expository material. By removing key data categories, they demonstrated the influence of specific training data on model capabilities. Their work highlights the importance of open-source tools in auditing model behavior and making training-data decisions. The study was possible due to Ai2's open artifacts, which enabled independent research into model behavior.

title: OpenAI warns of persistent AI cyber threats and calls for new safety regulations
summary: OpenAI's chief global affairs officer, Chris Lehane, warned of 'ongoing, persistent' cyber-attacks from advanced AI models, following incidents where AI agents breached security systems. The company paused training of its most advanced models to implement safety measures, acknowledging the risks posed by open-source models, particularly those developed in China. Lehane emphasized the need for U.S. legislation to enforce safety standards for frontier AI, suggesting mandatory safety proofs before deployment. Safety experts criticized AI companies for reckless development, with some predicting an 'intelligence explosion' that could lead to existential risks. OpenAI and rival Anthropic are racing to list on the stock market, raising concerns about the pace of AI advancement and its potential consequences.

title: ASR models reproduce benchmark transcripts despite audio contradictions
summary: Researchers found that some ASR models reproduce benchmark transcripts even when the audio contradicts them. The study evaluated 11 open-source ASR models and found that several of the highest-scoring systems reproduced benchmark transcripts from VoxPopuli and LibriSpeech datasets, even when the audio contradicted them. The models appeared to rely on subtle acoustic cues that indicated which benchmark they were being tested on, leading to inflated scores. The study introduced three tests to quantify benchmark optimization, including a consensus disagreement probe and orthographic switching tests. The results suggest that models can detect dataset-associated acoustic cues and adjust their transcription behavior accordingly. The findings highlight the importance of using held-out evaluation sets and looking beyond word error rate on a single public benchmark.

title: Databricks expands Inbound Private Link to support account-level resources and custom URLs
summary: Databricks has expanded the capabilities of Inbound Private Link to support account-level resources such as Genie One, the account console, and custom URLs. This update allows customers to secure traffic to these resources using the same private network guarantees as other services. The new features include support for custom URLs and managed disaster recovery stable URLs, enabling a single endpoint to serve all workspace and account-level resources across regions. Context-based ingress controls now allow fine-grained policies for both public and private access, with the new features available in Beta on AWS Enterprise and Azure Premium tiers.

title: MIT researchers identify promising catalysts for electrochemical ammonia production
summary: Researchers at MIT have developed a method to predict effective catalysts for electrochemical ammonia production, aiming to make it more sustainable. Traditional ammonia production via the Haber-Bosch process relies on fossil fuels and contributes significantly to greenhouse gas emissions. The new approach uses computational models to identify materials that could reduce energy requirements and improve efficiency. Bilge Yildiz and doctoral students Constantine Athanitis and Filip Grajkowski published their findings in the journal EES Catalysis. While the method is theoretical, it could guide the development of more efficient catalysts, though practical implementation remains a challenge. The study highlights the need for materials that can reduce energy input and minimize side reactions in ammonia synthesis, potentially leading to greener fertilizer production.

title: LFM2.5-DSpark Enhances Inference Speed with Speculative Decoding
summary: Liquid AI introduces LFM2.5-DSpark, a model that improves inference speed through speculative decoding, achieving up to 3.2x faster performance on both H100 GPUs and MacBook Pro devices. The approach uses a draft model to generate candidate tokens, reducing latency by 57% for LFM2.5-2.6B. The model supports day-one integration with llama.cpp and SGLang, with open-source implementations available. Performance gains vary across different model sizes, with the 2.6B version showing the most significant improvements. The DSpark method combines parallel processing, inter-token dependencies, and confidence-based verification to optimize throughput. Liquid AI provides detailed instructions for deploying the model with both SGLang and llama.cpp, along with checkpoint files on Hugging Face.

title: Microsoft Research's Skala 1.1 Enhances DFT Accuracy and Accessibility
summary: Microsoft Research has released Skala 1.1, an improved deep-learning exchange-correlation functional for density functional theory (DFT), trained on 2.5 times more data than its predecessor. This update delivers higher accuracy in molecular simulations, including thermochemistry, reaction kinetics, and structure prediction, with a weighted average error of 2.8 kcal/mol on the GMTKN55 benchmark. Skala is now available in CP2K and is being integrated into Psi4, FHI-aims, ORCA, and VASP, expanding its accessibility across computational chemistry software. Microsoft also introduced a living benchmark to track Skala's performance improvements over time, ensuring transparency and continuous optimization. The development marks progress toward predictive and widely accessible DFT simulations in scientific and industrial workflows.

title: AI Adapters Enable Immediate Model Deployment on IBM's Spyre AI Accelerator
summary: The article discusses how AI agents can facilitate the immediate deployment of new AI models on emerging hardware platforms like IBM's Spyre AI accelerator. Traditional methods of enabling new models on evolving software stacks are slow and require specialized work, but AI-driven adapters bridge this gap by allowing existing models to run on new hardware without waiting for full stack maturity. These adapters, developed as runtime patches, translate model operations into forms compatible with the target hardware's compiler, preserving the model's mathematical integrity. The approach is demonstrated using HuggingFace Transformers models on Spyre, where AI agents analyze model logic and compiler behavior to create effective patches. This strategy reduces the time and effort needed to enable new models, leveraging AI's ability to understand both model architecture and hardware requirements. The result is a scalable solution that supports thousands of models while the underlying platform continues to evolve, with adapters being temporary solutions that may be replaced as the stack matures.

title: GeForce NOW Adds Firefox Browser Support for Cloud Gaming
summary: GeForce NOW has expanded its browser support by adding Firefox, allowing users to play supported PC games directly from the browser without downloading a dedicated app. The update enables access to high-performance gaming via cloud streaming, with GeForce RTX-powered performance at up to 1440p and 120 frames per second for Ultimate members. New games like Gallipoli are now available, and users can access titles across multiple devices without local storage usage. The service joins Chrome, Edge, and Opera in supporting Firefox on Windows browsers.

title: Mistral Agentic Search Enhances AI Accuracy and Efficiency in Document Retrieval
summary: Mistral Agentic Search improves AI performance by enabling models to navigate and verify information in complex documents, reducing latency and token use. The system uses a multi-step retrieval loop with tools like search, open, navigate, read, and grep to access and analyze data across multiple sources. Benchmarks show significant improvements in accuracy, with results reaching up to 86% correctness on financial filings and 51.9% on table-heavy documents. Agentic Search is available through Mistral Search Toolkit and Libraries, offering support for sensitive data and enhancing search capabilities without requiring model-specific training. It is particularly effective for long documents, multi-source questions, and structured data, while traditional retrieval methods like one-shot RAG fall short in these scenarios due to their limitations in navigation and iterative refinement.

title: Researchers propose LINK method for improved cross-lingual knowledge transfer
summary: Researchers introduce LINK, a method that enhances cross-lingual knowledge transfer by substituting words in high-resource language training data with their translations. This approach requires no additional model training and uses bilingual vocabularies. Evaluation across eight languages shows improvements in downstream tasks, with training speeds up to twice as fast. The technique addresses challenges in building multilingual models for languages with limited data.

title: Researchers Develop Iterative Pseudo-Labeling Method for Mandarin-English Code-Switching ASR
summary: Researchers from the National University of Singapore and Apple introduced an iterative pseudo-labeling approach to improve Mandarin-English code-switching ASR. The method uses three phases: pseudo-label generation, two-stage bilingual model training, and iterative refinements. It leverages unlabeled data to create a semi-supervised dataset, enhancing model accuracy in complex code-switching scenarios. The approach achieved significant reductions in Mix Error Rate on SEAME’s devman and devsge subsets.

title: IBM Introduces Modular Cryogenic Architecture for Quantum Computing Scalability
summary: IBM has unveiled a new modular cryogenic architecture designed to support the scalability of quantum computing systems. This architecture connects multiple quantum processors through both quantum and classical links, enabling more sophisticated algorithms and reducing computational limitations. The modular design allows for easier upgrades and maintenance, with each cryogenic cell housing its own cooling system and providing expanded wiring capacity and chamber volume. IBM's approach addresses the challenges of qubit crosstalk and heat management, paving the way for future fault-tolerant quantum computers like IBM Quantum Starling, expected in 2029. The system has been demonstrated with two coupled cryogenic cells, validating its potential for large-scale, interconnected quantum systems. This innovation aligns with IBM's Quantum Roadmap, supporting the development of multi-chip quantum systems without requiring complete infrastructure redesigns.

title: MIT Study Shows AI Art Can't Be Traced to Training Data
summary: A new MIT study reveals that AI-generated images often cannot be traced back to specific training data due to a phenomenon called attribution decay. Researchers found that as models are trained on larger datasets, individual training examples lose influence on outputs. Removing any single image or artist's work from the training data does not change the generated output, making attribution impossible. The team developed a 'diffusion ensemble' architecture to test this by switching off parts of the model that saw specific data, without retraining. Their results showed that larger datasets led to smaller changes in output when data was removed, suggesting models become less reliant on any single input. The study raises legal questions about copyright and authorship, as AI outputs may not be attributable to any specific source, challenging current notions of creative ownership and fair use.

title: Study reveals AI models rely on drug name suffixes rather than drug knowledge
summary: A study on Olmo 3 shows AI models often answer drug-related questions by relying on name suffixes rather than actual drug knowledge. Researchers found 12–18% of drug responses were driven by affixes like -pril, while 51–59% showed no specific drug knowledge. The team traced this behavior to the model's training data, noting rarer drugs were more likely to be answered based on affixes. The study highlights the importance of understanding how models generalize from name patterns versus learned facts, especially in high-stakes domains like medicine.

title: NVIDIA and OpenAI secure 4.25 gigawatts of AI factory capacity at PORTS-Pike
summary: NVIDIA and OpenAI have partnered to secure 4.25 gigawatts of AI factory capacity at the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in Portsmouth, Ohio. This site will host NVIDIA's full-stack DSX AI factory platform, including GPUs, CPUs, and networking software. The initial deployment is expected to provide 4.25 gigawatts of capacity, with potential for future expansion to 3.75 gigawatts. NVIDIA is supporting the LPS infrastructure for approximately 4 gigawatts over a 20-year term, securing a site exclusively for NVIDIA compute. OpenAI will build and operate the AI factory, with NVIDIA's support limited to defined portions of lease and power payments. The arrangement highlights NVIDIA's strategy to secure critical infrastructure for AI factories, enabling long-term productive capacity and multiple generations of compute systems. The site's value extends beyond a single tenant, as NVIDIA's standardized platform and broad ecosystem support redeployment of capacity over time.

title: Google Introduces Gemini 3.7 Flash with Enhanced Coding and Workflow Capabilities
summary: Google has launched Gemini 3.7 Flash, an updated version of its Flash series, offering improved performance in coding, web development, and knowledge work. The model shows significant gains in debugging, code accuracy, and production-ready code generation, outperforming its predecessor, Gemini 3.6 Flash, in benchmarks like FrontierCode 1.1 and DeepSWE v1.1. It also excels in web development tasks and complex document processing. Priced at $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens, Gemini 3.7 Flash is available through the end of the year. Gemini Spark, a 24/7 AI agent, will use the new model to enhance efficiency in knowledge work and tool use for Google Workspace apps. The update includes safety improvements against misuse in CBRN and cyber domains.

title: MindTopo benchmark assesses AI's topological reasoning and planning capabilities
summary: MindTopo, a new benchmark, evaluates whether multimodal AI models can understand topological concepts like connectivity and knots. The benchmark tests both static recognition and interactive planning, revealing that current models excel at recognizing topological relationships in images but struggle to maintain this understanding during sequential actions. Failures in planning often involve losing track of structural relationships or proposing physically impossible actions. The study highlights the importance of topological understanding for AI systems in robotics and interactive environments. MindTopo categorizes tasks into continuity, separation, order, enclosure, and knots, with models evaluated on both reasoning and planning tasks. Results show significant gaps between static perception and dynamic interaction, suggesting the need for models that explicitly track topological states.

title: WhatsApp Introduces Scam Alert Feature With On-Device Machine Learning and Privacy Safeguards
summary: WhatsApp is introducing Scam Alert, an optional feature that uses on-device machine learning to detect potential scam messages. The system runs entirely on the user's device, ensuring no message content leaves the device for classification. Scam Alert complements end-to-end encryption by providing users with warnings about suspicious messages from non-contacts, without automatically reporting any data to WhatsApp or Meta. The feature is designed with strict privacy principles, including on-device processing, no automatic reporting, and user control over the tool. To validate its implementation, WhatsApp is inviting security researchers and the public to review the system's architecture and provide feedback. The feature is currently in beta and will be rolled out gradually, with additional safeguards like confidential federated analytics and differential privacy to protect user data while measuring the system's effectiveness.

title: Quantum Optimization Benchmarking Library Tracks Progress Toward Quantum Advantage
summary: The Quantum Optimization Benchmarking Library (QOBLIB) is a community-driven framework designed to track progress toward quantum advantage in optimization. Developed by the Quantum Optimization Working Group and supported by organizations like IBM Quantum and Zuse Institute Berlin, QOBLIB includes ten challenging optimization problem classes and provides metrics for comparing quantum and classical methods. A recent publication in Nature Computational Science and a new website have expanded its reach, with over 2,000 submitted results from researchers worldwide. The library aims to foster collaboration and rigor in benchmarking, helping identify where quantum computing may deliver practical value. Contributions from both classical and quantum researchers are encouraged to advance the field and measure progress over time.

title: Amazon's Automated Reasoning Group Transforms Security and AI with Mathematical Certainty
summary: Amazon's Automated Reasoning Group (ARG), launched in 2016, has evolved from research prototypes to essential services used by millions of customers. The group applies formal verification and automated reasoning to ensure the correctness and security of AWS systems. Key tools like Tiros and Zelkova now power network security analysis and policy enforcement, while cryptographic and infrastructure systems have been mathematically proven. The work has also extended to AI, with features like Amazon Bedrock Guardrails using automated reasoning to validate AI-generated content. The group's approach has shown that mathematical rigor enhances both security and efficiency, positioning AWS to lead in the next era of AI development with provably safe systems.

title: Mistral enhances AI sovereignty with regional control and open model access
summary: Mistral is advancing AI sovereignty by offering enterprises and countries control over AI models, infrastructure, and compute capacity, ensuring regional compliance and reliability. The company is expanding open model access, introducing regional endpoints and priority tiers, and forming a coalition to secure long-term European AI compute capacity. Mistral aims to build up to 1 GW of capacity by 2030, providing scalable, sovereign AI infrastructure. The company emphasizes regional control, production-grade reliability, and open model choice, allowing customers to run models under strict regional controls and service commitments. Mistral is also forming a coalition of enterprises to secure long-term compute capacity in Europe, converting commitments into access to its infrastructure over multiple years.

title: NIST Scientists Identify and Correct Size Measurement Error in Nanotechnology
summary: NIST researchers have identified a common error in analyzing nanomaterial properties that can distort understanding of how size affects performance. The team found that size measurements of nanoscale objects are often imprecise, leading to misleading conclusions about material behavior. This error can affect various nanotechnology applications, from drug delivery to electronics. The researchers developed a mathematical correction to account for measurement uncertainties, allowing for more accurate analysis of the relationship between nanoparticle size and properties like brightness or drug-carrying capacity. To apply the correction, scientists must estimate their measurement errors using reference materials or calculate uncertainty when such materials are unavailable. The study, published in ACS Nano, aims to improve the reliability of nanotechnology research and development.

title: Meta Introduces Multi-Stage Sequence Model for Efficient Ads Ranking
summary: Meta has developed a multi-stage sequence model to enhance its ads ranking system, enabling efficient scaling of sequence learning. The model separates offline user modeling from online ranking tasks, improving performance without increasing serving costs. Key innovations include dense tokenization and target-aware attention, which allow the system to learn feature interactions directly from data. This architecture contributes to a 6% conversion lift on Instagram and 3% on Facebook. The approach follows LLM-style scaling laws, with performance improvements showing a log-linear relationship to compute resources. Meta identifies four scaling levers: balanced model shape, multi-stage tunability, sequence diversity, and semantic feature representation. The model is a core component of Meta’s Generative Ads Recommendation Model (GEM), designed for generalization across various ads ranking tasks.

title: llm 0.33 update introduces key support and template combining
summary: The llm 0.33 update includes key support for embedding models, allowing per-call key passing without altering shared model state. It also enables combining templates via the -t/--template flag, facilitating the use of pre-configured models and options. Additionally, reasoning-capable models now support a reasoning_summary option with auto, concise, and detailed values. The release notes reference recent articles on conceptual integrity, Qwen 3.8, and an OpenAI incident against Hugging Face.

title: Using a TV as a Monitor: Setup and Considerations
summary: ZDNET explains how to use a TV as a computer monitor, offering cost-effective alternatives to expensive displays. The guide covers HDMI and wireless connection methods, including AirPlay and Googlecast, while noting potential issues like input lag and resolution mismatches. It also details how to find a TV's IP address for remote access and adjust display settings for optimal performance. The article highlights the benefits of using a TV for additional screen space at lower cost, comparing models like the Alienware 34-inch QD-OLED gaming monitor and the Hisense A4, noting differences in resolution, refresh rate, and features.

title: You can change your Messages backgrounds on iPhone - so you never text the wrong person again
summary: Apple allows iPhone users to customize message backgrounds in iOS 26, enabling personalized chat themes. However, this change is visible to all participants in the chat, as long as they also use iOS 26. The feature lets users choose from preset options or photos from their camera roll. While it enhances personalization, it may lead to unintended visibility for others. Users can disable the feature in Settings or revert to a plain background, which also removes the change for all chat members.

title: Chinese AI firms invest in Ulanqab data centers amid water and energy challenges
summary: Chinese AI companies are building large data centers in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia, driven by low electricity costs, cold climate, and proximity to Beijing. Over 100 data centers have been constructed or planned since 2016, with 70% of commitments announced in the last year. Companies like DeepSeek, ByteDance, and Alibaba are investing in their own infrastructure, marking a shift from relying on cloud providers. However, water scarcity poses a challenge, as Ulanqab receives only 14 inches of rain annually. The region's data centers, part of China's 'Eastern Data, Western Compute' initiative, benefit from reduced latency due to fiber optic cables and are seen as a way to utilize excess renewable energy. Despite progress, coal still provides 37% of Ulanqab's electricity, raising concerns about sustainability.

title: TikTok agrees to $400m settlement for child privacy violations
summary: TikTok has agreed to pay $400 million to the US government to resolve a lawsuit alleging violations of the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA). The settlement, stemming from a 2024 Department of Justice suit, addresses data collection on users under 13. TikTok and its parent company ByteDance will pay $300 million immediately and $100 million after the FTC vacates a 2019 consent decree. The deal includes a $5.7 million fine for Musical.ly, ByteDance's predecessor. The DOJ noted TikTok has made changes to its privacy practices and ownership structure since the lawsuit began. Meta faces similar allegations from 29 states, with potential penalties exceeding hundreds of billions of dollars.

title: LinkedIn's AI slop button used by over a million users
summary: LinkedIn reported over a million users clicked its new 'AI slop' button, introduced to flag AI-generated content. The feature, accessible via the three dots menu, aims to reduce views on AI-generated posts by 40%. The button follows findings that 41% of longform posts were flagged as AI-generated. LinkedIn also improved AI classifiers and removed an AI-enhancement feature. Users now receive messages indicating posts may appear AI-generated, with the company emphasizing efforts to provide helpful feedback.

title: Balaji Ingole Develops AI Tools for E-Commerce and Health Care
summary: Balaji Ingole, an IEEE senior member and project manager at Amla, leverages AI to transform e-commerce operations and develop health care diagnostic tools. Growing up without access to technology, Ingole discovered programming in middle school, which sparked a lifelong passion for problem-solving. He now leads AI-driven initiatives at Amla, helping clients streamline product setup on e-commerce platforms through AI agents. Ingole also works on assistive technologies and health care diagnostics, emphasizing the importance of rigorous data governance. His research includes patents for AI-powered health monitoring devices and breast cancer detection tools. Ingole credits IEEE membership for fostering his professional network and research contributions, highlighting the role of peer review in refining his work. His career path, from self-taught programming to leading global projects, reflects a commitment to 'learn by doing' and using technology for societal benefit.

title: Engineer's Guide to Thriving in AI Era: Focus on Judgment and Direction
summary: Addy Osmani, a software engineer with over 14 years at Google, shares insights for engineers navigating the AI era. He emphasizes that the key to durability in an AI-driven world lies not in problem-solving but in choosing meaningful projects and judging their quality. Osmani advises optimizing for scarce resources like reputation and relationships, rather than chasing high pay. He highlights the importance of finding problems over solving them, and cultivating judgment through deliberate practice and deep understanding of systems. Engineers should shift from doing to directing, delegating tasks to agents while maintaining verification and accountability. The article stresses the value of finishing strong, focusing on the 'last mile' of development, and building a public track record to seize opportunities. It concludes that the ungradable part of a career—choosing and judging work—is where human value lies, urging engineers to act with intention and integrity.

title: YouTube creators face backlash for promoting AI tools through unmarked videos
summary: Prominent YouTube creators Matti Haapoja and Sam 'Kolder' have faced backlash for promoting Higgsfield's AI tools through unmarked videos that resemble advertisements. Their content, which showcases Higgsfield's Seedance 2.5 functionality, has led fans to believe the creators were compensated, despite neither confirming paid partnerships. Haapoja's video, which resembles an infomercial, and Kolder's narrative about AI replacing human creators have sparked mixed reactions. While some praised the technological advancements, others criticized the creators for aligning with AI, which many view as a threat to creative authenticity. The controversy highlights the risks creators face when endorsing AI technologies, especially when their audiences value human creativity. Higgsfield later confirmed the collaborations were paid, but the backlash underscores the tension between commercial interests and audience values.

title: AI agents reshape web systems and shift economic focus
summary: AI agents are increasingly reshaping web systems and economic priorities, according to a This Week in AI episode. Models are now optimized for autonomous work rather than conversation, with agents handling tasks independently through cloud computing. Grok 4.6 and Cursor's integration exemplify this shift, offering agents their own computing resources. Gartner forecasts a nearly doubling of AI-optimized cloud spending, with inference costs surpassing training costs. Agents generate most web traffic and content, with Cloudflare reporting agentic bots at 57.4% of requests. Platforms are responding with content flags and watermarking. A security incident involving OpenAI and Hugging Face highlights risks as agents find ways to bypass restrictions. OpenAI's Computer History feature expands AI memory beyond simple recall.

title: Seattle startup tests underwater volcano geothermal power off Oregon coast
summary: A Seattle-based startup, Endurance Energy, is deploying a 100-kilowatt geothermal generator near an underwater volcano off Oregon's coast, marking the fifth such pilot project. The initiative aims to harness heat from hydrothermal vents, which reach temperatures up to 750°F, to produce emissions-free electricity. The company believes this technology could eventually power entire cities, offering a reliable, clean energy source that is not weather-dependent. While geothermal energy has long been viable in limited geographic areas, recent advancements in drilling techniques are expanding its potential. The U.S. Department of Energy estimates enhanced geothermal systems could supply energy to 65 million homes by midcentury. Meanwhile, growing demand from data centers, driven by AI, is increasing investment in geothermal energy as a scalable solution.

title: Jones Act waiver boosts Gulf Coast to West Coast oil shipments
summary: A limited waiver of the Jones Act, renewed by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, allowed more ships to transport crude oil and petroleum products from the U.S. Gulf Coast to the West Coast, increasing shipments to over 190,000 barrels per day in April. This marked a more than quadruple year-on-year increase, with gasoline blending components, finished motor gasoline, jet fuel, and crude oil contributing to the surge. Shipments to the East Coast also rose to a record 1.2 million barrels per day in April, driven by gasoline blending components and distillate fuel.

title: Rhine Water Levels Rise Slightly, But Industrial Supply Chains Remain Strained
summary: The Rhine River's water levels have slightly increased from mid-August record lows, but the relief is minimal as barge capacity remains restricted. This has led to higher freight costs, constrained chemical production, and uneven fuel distribution across Europe. The crisis highlights the vulnerability of Europe's industrial system, which relies heavily on the Rhine for transport. The critical chokepoint at Kaub, where water levels fell below 10 cm, has fragmented the river corridor, limiting cargo movement and forcing specialized vessels to operate. Chemical companies like BASF and INEOS face production cuts due to restricted feedstock flows, while refineries struggle with storage surpluses and higher transportation costs. Although weak demand has mitigated some impacts, the situation underscores the risks of relying on river transport and the potential for further disruption if water levels decline again. The article warns that a recovery in manufacturing or increased demand could exacerbate the crisis, even with modest improvements in river conditions. A potential super El Niño event could further worsen the situation by reducing Alpine snowmelt and increasing summer droughts, threatening the Rhine's water levels in future years.

title: Tesla Semi Begins European Deliveries with 500-Unit Order from Einride
summary: Tesla has begun delivering its Semi electric trucks to Europe, with Einride placing the largest order to date for 500 units. The order, for use in U.S. routes, marks the start of high-volume production at Gigafactory 1 in Nevada. Pricing details for the Semi were not disclosed but are set to be announced at the IAA Transportation conference. Einride CEO Roozbeh Charli highlighted the partnership's role in advancing sustainable freight, while Tesla's Dan Priestley emphasized the cost savings and operational efficiency of electric trucks. Other long-term partners like PepsiCo and DHL may follow with large orders.

title: GeoPura Demonstrates Hydrogen Charging for Electric Ship at Tilbury Port
summary: GeoPura demonstrated hydrogen-powered charging for an electric ship at Tilbury Port, using a 300 kW system with five Ballard fuel cells. The vessel, battery electric, was charged through hydrogen conversion to electricity. While hydrogen's role in the energy chain is questioned, the demonstration highlights port infrastructure challenges. Ports often face electrical limitations, making battery storage a more efficient solution for high-power charging. Hydrogen's efficiency penalty, at about 3.1 MWh to 1 MWh, makes it less suitable for routine port operations. The article emphasizes the importance of repeat deployment and commercial viability over demonstration success. True commercial significance will depend on metrics like vessel usage, energy supplied, and cost efficiency. The maritime transition is expected to focus on reliable operations rather than technological firsts.

title: Trump administration redirects $500M steel grant to coal furnace upgrades
summary: The Trump administration has redirected a $500 million Biden-era grant intended for decarbonizing steelmaking to upgrade a coal-fueled blast furnace at Cleveland-Cliffs' Middletown steel mill. The Department of Energy changed the scope of the funding, which was originally meant to replace the aging furnace with cleaner technology, to instead refurbish and optimize the coal-fired system. Cleveland-Cliffs CEO Lourenco Goncalves stated the decision aligns with the Trump administration's priorities, emphasizing the use of 'beautiful coal.' The move has drawn criticism from environmental advocates and residents, who argue it undermines efforts to reduce emissions. The grant, part of a $6.3 billion program under the Inflation Reduction Act, was initially meant to support net-zero emissions, but the revised plan shifts focus to improving efficiency of the existing coal furnace, with the company investing $500 million of its own funds.

title: Hyundai begins Ioniq V pre-orders in China with $17,700 base price
summary: Hyundai has started taking pre-orders for its Ioniq V electric vehicle in China, with the base model priced at $17,700 (119,900 yuan). The car, unveiled at the Chengdu Auto Show, offers three trim levels with varying battery sizes and power outputs. It is built on Hyundai’s E-GMP platform with 800V charging, though specific charging speeds have not been announced. The vehicle features a 27-inch display, Chinese AI models, and a driver assistance system from Momenta. While pre-orders are open in China, the model is not available elsewhere yet. Hyundai plans to expand to markets like Australia but has not set a timeline for global availability. The article notes that China leads in EV adoption and that Hyundai’s entry may influence its global strategy.

title: Arevon Energy Launches 300-MW Nighthawk Storage Project in California
summary: Arevon Energy has completed its 300-MW Nighthawk Energy Storage Project in Poway, California, using lithium iron phosphate battery technology. The facility, which Arevon developed, built, and will operate, supports grid reliability and has a long-term agreement with PG&E. The project is expected to generate over $30 million in property tax revenue for local services. Arevon's CEO highlighted the importance of energy storage for meeting rising demand, while local officials praised the project's economic and infrastructural benefits. The company also partners with local organizations in Poway, supporting community programs and initiatives. Arevon operates over 6.3 GW of solar and storage projects across 18 states, with ongoing developments in California.

title: Federal Initiative Sparks State Competition for Nuclear Waste Management Roles
summary: A new federal initiative to establish nuclear 'lifecycle' campuses has led to states competing for roles in managing used nuclear fuel, marking a shift from past political resistance. The initiative proposes integrating advanced reactors, fuel production, and recycling with responsible waste management. However, opposition in Idaho and Tennessee highlights concerns about the volume, duration, and safety of waste storage, as well as the risk of facilities becoming permanent federal waste sites. The article argues that states should be consenting partners with enforceable rights, defined benefits, and binding plans for waste disposal. It emphasizes the potential of recycling to recover valuable materials and reduce long-term disposal needs, while stressing the necessity of transparent partnerships and durable economic benefits for host communities. The piece calls for a national strategy that avoids past failures by ensuring accountability and public confidence in nuclear development efforts.

title: Hydropower shortages threaten U.S. and Canadian energy supply
summary: The U.S. faces growing hydropower challenges due to worsening droughts, particularly in the West. Lake Mead and Lake Powell, two major reservoirs, have reached record-low levels, threatening power generation capacity. The Bureau of Reclamation warns there's a risk these reservoirs could fall below operational thresholds. While these dams provide only a small portion of the Southwest's electricity, drought conditions are impacting dozens of hydropower plants across North America. Canada, which relies heavily on hydropower, is also experiencing a prolonged drought, affecting its ability to supply clean energy to the U.S. through new transmission lines. Meanwhile, the Trump administration is supporting battery projects, with LG Energy Solution opening a facility in Michigan and Form Energy advancing grid-scale storage. In Pennsylvania, Governor Josh Shapiro is imposing new requirements on data centers to manage rising energy demand.

title: TM EDISON consortium completes caisson installation for Princess Elisabeth Energy Island
summary: The TM EDISON consortium, comprising Jan De Nul and DEME, completed the installation of all 23 caissons for the 3.5 GW Princess Elisabeth Energy Island project, 45km off Belgium's coast. This marks the end of foundation works, enabling the project to move to the next phase. The artificial island, developed for Elia Transmission Belgium, will serve as a hub for transmitting offshore wind energy to Belgium's grid and connect to UK and Danish networks. Caissons, each weighing around 22,000t, were built in Vlissingen and transported to sea. The project, scheduled for completion in 2031, received a €99m EU subsidy for this phase.

title: PowerChina to build 30 MW solar plant in North Macedonia
summary: PowerChina Jiangxi Electric Power Construction has won a EUR 12 million contract to build a 30 MW solar power plant in North Macedonia, managed by state utility ESM. The project will use two sites: 10 MW at the Oslomej coal mine and 20 MW near the Bitola thermal power plant. EBRD financed the tender, which selected PowerChina for the public-private partnership. ESM previously built a 10 MW solar plant at Oslomej, highlighting the site's suitability for solar projects. PowerChina is active in Southeast Europe, with recent projects in Serbia.

title: Croatia updates rules for constructing new power plants
summary: Croatia has adopted amendments to its electricity market law, streamlining procedures for renewable energy projects and enhancing consumer protections. The changes align with EU standards, ensuring energy independence and stability. Key provisions include extended energy approvals for investors, risk management systems for suppliers, and measures to support consumers facing high energy costs. The law also allows temporary power cuts for non-vulnerable users failing to pay grid fees, as stated by the Ministry of Economy.

title: Austria shifts solar subsidy focus to energy storage
summary: The Austrian government plans to overhaul its solar subsidy framework, prioritizing energy storage over direct photovoltaic support. The Ministry of Economy and Energy announced a new strategy to accelerate battery storage permits and fund intelligent energy management systems. Under the proposed reforms, small solar systems will be phased out, while storage and EMS will receive financial support to increase self-consumption and reduce grid strain. The government aims to achieve 8 GW of storage capacity by 2030, which could lower wholesale power prices. Industry groups welcome the shift but urge concrete implementation, emphasizing the need for clear funding mechanisms and regulatory support. PV&B Austria's Vera Immitzer stressed that policy must translate into action, while local installer Hansesun criticized the plans as inadequate, calling for tax relief measures to ensure investment certainty.

title: LONGi and JinkoSolar Expand Solar-Storage Solutions for Commercial and Industrial Use
summary: LONGi and JinkoSolar are advancing solar-storage solutions for commercial and industrial applications. LONGi deployed Hi-MO X10 modules in a 200 kWp rooftop project in Saudi Arabia, demonstrating high-efficiency PV for C&I facilities. The company also supplied Hi-MO 9 modules for a 71 MWp solar portfolio in Italy, highlighting next-gen module technology. JinkoSolar extended its Sunny 365 platform to retail and AI data centers, integrating Tiger Neo 3.0 modules with SunGiga G2 storage. The solutions aim to reduce energy costs, improve efficiency, and address grid constraints through advanced PV and storage technologies.

title: ESS Inc CEO outlines pivot to sodium-ion batteries after iron flow battery struggles
summary: ESS Inc CEO Drew Buckley discusses the company's challenges with its iron flow battery technology, which failed to meet commercial expectations since its 2021 SPAC listing. The company's share price has plummeted, and it faces doubts about its ability to continue as a going concern. Buckley explains that the iron flow battery worked in the lab but struggled with commercial deployment, leading to a strategic shift toward sodium-ion battery technology. He highlights the need for a longer development timeline for iron flow and positions sodium-ion as a lower-risk, faster-to-market option. The Bridge sodium-ion BESS, developed with Alsym, is designed to be a turnkey solution for utility-scale applications, particularly in data centers and AI workloads. Buckley emphasizes leveraging ESS's existing engineering and software capabilities to accelerate the sodium-ion product's commercialization.

title: CAPE Ratio Reaches Dot-Com Bubble Levels as AI Drives Market Valuations
summary: The S&P 500's CAPE ratio has hit 42.2, its highest since the dot-com bubble in 1999, signaling extreme market valuation. The metric, which adjusts earnings for inflation and removes anomalies, suggests the current market is significantly overpriced compared to historical averages of around 27. While the dot-com era saw speculative investing in unprofitable tech firms, today's high valuations are driven by AI advancements and big tech growth. Analysts warn of potential market corrections, though current earnings fundamentals differ from the bubble period.

title: Analysts Highlight Amazon's Undervalued Position Amid AWS Growth
summary: Analysts at 24/7 Wall St. suggest Amazon (AMZN) is undervalued, with a $343.50 price target and 32.8% upside, citing AWS's 36.7% growth in Q2 FY2026 as its fastest in 18 quarters. The stock trades at a forward P/E of 17, lower than Alphabet and Microsoft. Bulls argue AWS's operating leverage and AI monetization could push shares to $393.98, while risks include high capital intensity and inflated net income due to Anthropic's $53.40 billion mark.

title: Nancy Kassebaum Baker, centrist Republican senator, calls for Trump's impeachment
summary: Nancy Kassebaum Baker, a centrist Republican senator from Kansas who died at 94, called for Donald Trump's impeachment in 2021 following the Capitol attack. She was the first woman elected to the U.S. Senate without following a spouse, serving three terms from 1978 to 1997. Known for her moderate politics, she supported progressive measures like an assault weapons ban and worked across party lines. Despite her popularity in Kansas, she frustrated conservative activists. After leaving the Senate, she continued public service roles, including as a member of a bipartisan campaign finance commission. She married former Senator Howard Baker in 1996, and later became an ambassador to Japan with her husband. Her son reported her death from natural causes.

title: Iran-linked hackers caused UK power plant shutdown, government says
summary: Iran-linked hackers are blamed for a cyber-attack that temporarily shut down a UK power plant, according to the government. The incident involved a small-scale energy generator, with no risk to the wider energy system. The UK government emphasized its resilient energy infrastructure and collaboration with the sector to ensure security. The National Cyber Security Centre reported no outages from major power stations. The attack follows warnings about increasing threats from hostile states like Iran, which has been accused of cyber-attacks on Turkey and Israel. The US has warned of ongoing threats from Iran-affiliated groups like CyberAv3ngers, which targeted critical infrastructure in 2023.

title: Self-taught painter turned gibbon expert runs world-leading sanctuary
summary: A self-taught painter and remodeling contractor, Alan Mootnick, founded the Gibbon Conservation Center in California 50 years ago, transforming it into a globally recognized sanctuary for gibbons. The center now cares for 40 gibbons across five species, known for their distinctive vocalizations. Director Gabi Skollar, who joined Mootnick in 2005, continues his mission after his death in 2011, living on-site with caretakers and dedicating her life to the gibbons. The sanctuary contributes to gibbon research and conservation efforts, facing threats from habitat destruction and wildlife trade. Skollar aims to expand the facility and create an education center, honoring Mootnick's legacy through ongoing care and research.

title: Judge rules former Abercrombie CEO mentally fit for sex-trafficking trial
summary: A federal judge has ruled that Michael Jeffries, former CEO of Abercrombie & Fitch, is mentally competent to stand trial for sex-trafficking charges. Jeffries, 82, was hospitalized for months due to dementia and Alzheimer’s symptoms. Judge Nusrat Choudhury reviewed medical reports and phone calls to determine his competency. Jeffries and two co-defendants face charges related to luring men to sex parties through modeling job offers. The case follows previous sexual misconduct allegations.

title: Bangladesh's PM delays India visit amid diplomatic tensions
summary: Bangladesh's Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has postponed his first visit to India, straining bilateral relations. The delay follows a press conference by exiled Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, which Dhaka criticized as interfering in its internal affairs. India had invited Rahman for a visit ahead of the BRICS summit, but tensions persist over Hasina's extradition request and her political speeches from India. Bangladesh's Foreign Ministry stated that a conducive environment is needed for the visit, while India's officials remain noncommittal. Analysts note that domestic politics in Bangladesh, particularly the July 2024 uprising, influence its foreign policy, shifting its focus from India to other nations. India's border fencing and deportation policies further strain ties, with Dhaka accusing New Delhi of extrajudicial actions. Experts suggest dialogue is essential to mend relations, as both nations face challenges in maintaining a productive partnership.

title: CrossCountry cancels most UK services due to power outage at control center
summary: CrossCountry, ranked Britain's worst rail operator, canceled most UK train services after a power outage at its Birmingham control center disrupted systems. The outage affected major routes, including Glasgow to Penzance and Leeds to Manchester, with cancellations ongoing until further notice. Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander urged operators to provide extra services, while CrossCountry teams worked to restore power. Passengers faced significant disruptions, with some resorting to driving to attend football matches. CrossCountry confirmed tickets for Sunday would remain valid until Wednesday, and other operators offered assistance, including accepting CrossCountry tickets and providing compensation for delays. Services to Plymouth and Penzance were also disrupted, with customers relying on Great Western Railway as a replacement.

title: I chose community college to save money. Now Yale is giving me a full ride.
summary: Thalles de Souza, a 17-year-old from Brazil, secured a full-ride scholarship to Yale after attending community college in the US. Born in a violent neighborhood in Rio de Janeiro, he and his family fled to Massachusetts after a police shooting in 2016. At community college, he excelled academically and held leadership roles. Despite a 1.3% Yale acceptance rate, he was admitted and awarded a full scholarship. His mother, who sacrificed greatly to ensure their safety, is proud of his achievement.

title: 90-year-old man forms friendships with caregivers after initial resistance
summary: A 90-year-old man initially resisted having caregivers in his home but eventually formed friendships with them. His health declined after a heart attack, making daily tasks challenging. His daughter and sister, concerned about his well-being, arranged for outside help. The caregivers, Jonathan and Junior, quickly became integral to the household, engaging in conversations and shared activities like listening to jazz music. The family now believes the decision was correct, as the caregivers provide essential support and companionship.

title: Nordic nations lose confidence in Infantino, call for FIFA reforms
summary: Six Nordic football associations have lost confidence in FIFA President Gianni Infantino, demanding governance reforms and an independent investigation into his proposal to sell World Cup events to private equity. The nations, including Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, and the Faroe Islands, issued a joint statement supporting calls for Infantino's resignation and binding guarantees against private ownership of FIFA events. They also endorsed demands for a comprehensive review of FIFA's governance framework. Infantino faces pressure from UEFA, AFC, and CONCACAF to resign, with Denmark seeking an alternative for the March presidential election.

title: Author Worry Over Democratic Pathologies and Rise of Caesarism
summary: The author expresses concern that the flaws of democracy, such as incoherence and gridlock, undermine its legitimacy and drive support for strong executive leadership. This shift, observed in the U.S., Canada, and Britain, risks promoting Caesarism through centralized power and idolatry. The author contrasts democratic institutions with executive overreach, arguing that legislatures, despite their faults, better support liberty than the administrative state. The piece was written before Trump's political rise and references Joseph Heath's 'Enlightenment 2.0' and F.H. Buckley's 'The Once and Future King'.

title: Energy firms urge targeted support for struggling households
summary: Energy UK, representing UK energy firms, has called for more targeted support for households facing high energy bills, arguing that current measures like the £150 Warm Home Discount are insufficient. The body suggests a new 'social discount' scheme that considers income, health, and energy use could better assist those in need, potentially offering up to £450 in support. Ofgem is set to announce a new price cap, expected to rise by 4%, following a 13% increase in July. Energy UK claims the current discount reaches six million customers, but 2.5 million more require help due to medical needs or poor housing. The proposed scheme would cost £1.9bn, nearly double the current cost, and could be funded through bills or government spending. Critics, including National Energy Action, argue for a more empathetic approach to debt and better support for those in fuel poverty.

title: Economist Outlines U.S. and Alaska Economic Outlook at Anchorage Event
summary: At the Anchorage Economic Development Corporation's 2026 Economic Luncheon, economist Jon Cook outlined his views on the U.S. and Alaska economies. He noted that the U.S. economy remains resilient but faces persistent inflation, currently at 3.7% over the past year, driven by Middle East conflict and AI infrastructure investment. The labor market is stable with a 4.2% unemployment rate, though hiring remains low. Cook emphasized the need for monetary policy to address inflation, while acknowledging potential disinflationary forces. In Alaska, the economy faces unique challenges, including a shrinking labor force, an aging population, and reliance on the oil and gas sector. Consumer sentiment remains low, driven by AI-related uncertainty, rising housing costs, and concerns over job availability.

title: Federal Reserve Official Discusses Economic Shocks and Policy Responses
summary: At the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research, a Federal Reserve official discussed how policymakers analyze and respond to economic shocks, focusing on unpredictable events like pandemics, wars, and technological breakthroughs. The speaker outlined a framework for classifying shocks as either demand-side or supply-side, emphasizing the importance of the output gap in assessing economic conditions. The discussion highlighted the challenges of real-time policy responses, particularly when shocks create tension between inflation and employment targets. The speaker then addressed two current developments: the energy price shock from Middle East conflicts and the macroeconomic effects of artificial intelligence (AI). The energy shock has led to inflationary pressures and downward demand effects, while AI presents both supply-side productivity gains and demand-side investment boosts, complicating monetary policy decisions. The speaker noted the need for careful balancing of these factors to maintain price stability and maximum employment.

title: Unitree's stock debut highlights China's robotics ambitions amid U.S. restrictions
summary: The Chinese robotics company Unitree made a significant stock market debut on Shanghai's exchange, with its shares rising over 460% on the first day. The company, known for its advanced humanoid robots, has gained popularity in China through performances like the Lunar New Year 'Spring Gala' showcasing dancing and martial arts robots. Despite U.S. restrictions on advanced robotics imports, Unitree remains a key player in the industry, with the U.S. Pentagon listing it as a potential military company. Analysts note that while humanoids have potential applications in factories, homes, and healthcare, current capabilities are limited, with robots still largely remote-controlled or programmed. China's dominance in robotics is attributed to its complete supply chain and lower manufacturing costs, though the U.S. maintains an edge in semiconductors and data. Experts suggest the global robotics industry may see collaboration rather than competition between the two nations.

title: U.S.-Canada Tariffs Disrupt Small Business Pricing Strategies
summary: The U.S. and Canada have imposed reciprocal 50% tariffs on each other's goods, disrupting small businesses like Paloma Clothing in Portland, Oregon. Owners Mike Roach and Kim Osgood explained that the tariffs create uncertainty, forcing them to adjust pricing strategies. Canadian imports valued at $20 billion are affected, with the U.S. imposing tariffs on items like beer, whiskey, and clothing, while Canada matches with its own tariffs starting September 8. The couple noted that long-term contracts with Canadian suppliers, such as their artwork-based pillows, are now at risk due to price increases. They expressed frustration that the tariffs, which they argue harm small businesses, are driven by political decisions rather than economic necessity. The owners emphasized the negative impact on consumer prices and business margins, highlighting the broader economic ripple effects of the trade conflict.

title: China launches reusable rocket with first-stage recovery, advances space innovation
summary: China successfully launched the Zhuque-3 rocket, achieving the first recovery of its first stage on land. The event marks a significant advancement in reusable rocket technology. The launch, reported by Xinhua News, highlights China's growing capabilities in space exploration. Additionally, the article notes China's 'robot games' showcasing latest innovations and the opening of a new Arctic trade route, though obstacles may limit its wider use. The development underscores China's increasing role in global space initiatives and technological progress.

title: Review of 1973 Film 'The Eccentrics' and Related Media
summary: The article reviews the 1973 Georgian film 'The Eccentrics' by Eldar Shengelaia, describing it as a silly, slapstick comedy with a fairy-tale quality. It notes the film's allegorical nature, reflecting on freedom during the Soviet era, and highlights its whimsical plot involving a man who falls in love with a married woman and an inventor's failed airship project. The review also includes bonus content such as a 1977 Eloy album, a 1969 psychedelic rock album, and a 1968 film '2001: A Space Odyssey' with a deleted scene. Additionally, it touches on historical content like the 1953 Dallas Santa statue and WWII footage, as well as rare Pre-Code Hollywood films and 1950s commercials.

title: Citi Simplicity Card Offers 18-Month 0% APR on Balance Transfers and Purchases
summary: The Citi Simplicity® Card provides 0% introductory APR for 18 months on both balance transfers and purchases, helping users avoid interest charges. It also offers a 3% introductory balance transfer fee for the first four months, lower than the standard 5%. The card has no annual fee and is suitable for those with good to excellent credit scores. Users are advised to act quickly, as 0% APR periods may be shortened without notice.

title: Experts: this is the best cash back card of 2022
summary: The Wells Fargo Active Cash® Card is highlighted as one of the best cash back cards for 2026, offering 2% cash rewards on all purchases with no annual fee.
