It provides a 0% introductory APR for 12 months on purchases and qualifying balance transfers, followed by variable APR rates of 18.49%, 24.49%, or 28.49%. New cardholders can earn a $200 cash rewards bonus after spending $500 within the first three months. The card also includes cell phone protection up to $600 with a $25 deductible. Approval is likely for those with a credit score of 670 or higher. The card is praised for its simplicity, no limits on rewards, and competitive features compared to other cards.

title: New Zealand names Richie Mo'unga at flyhalf for Lions clash ahead of Springboks test
summary: New Zealand has selected Richie Mo'unga at flyhalf and Beauden Barrett at fullback for their match against the Lions in Johannesburg. The All Blacks defeated South Africa 33-16 in the first test but will face the Lions before the second test against the Springboks. Mo'unga, returning from a club stint in Japan, replaces centre Billy Proctor. Coach Dave Rennie highlighted the squad's depth as all players have played on tour. The team includes Rieko Ioane at centre and Emoni Narawa and Fehi Fineanganofo in the back three, with several players from the previous test match on the bench.

title: Good Good Golf removes controversial ad depicting violence against women
summary: YouTube content creator Good Good Golf removed a promotional video for Callaway Golf that depicted a man pushing a woman, sparking backlash. The ad, which showed a man knocking a woman down and telling her not to touch his new driver, was taken down after criticism over its portrayal of violence against women. Both Good Good and Callaway deleted the content, though clips continued to circulate online. Good Good apologized, stating it stands for inclusivity in golf. Callaway expressed disappointment but appreciated Good Good's response. The PGA Tour, which has partnered with Good Good, condemned the video, emphasizing its commitment to inclusivity and respect.

title: Study reveals commercial spy device detectors may mislead domestic abuse victims
summary: A study by University College London found that commercial spy device detectors may give domestic abuse victims a false sense of security. Researchers analyzed 1,000 covert surveillance products and 500 detection tools sold in the UK, revealing many detectors fail to identify hidden devices effectively. In experiments, participants missed 67% of hidden devices without tools, compared to 59% with detectors. The study highlighted issues such as false positives, poor user guidance, and devices that could alert perpetrators. Researchers urged manufacturers to improve clarity and safety, while emphasizing that stopping the sale of spy devices is the only real solution. Domestic abuse charity Refuge noted a rise in reported hidden cameras and microphones, urging regulatory action. Platforms like eBay and Amazon have policies against covert surveillance, but enforcement remains a challenge.

title: Marine scientists urge expanded protections for Australia's coastal waters
summary: Over 270 marine scientists from 84 institutes have urged the Australian government to strengthen protections for coastal marine ecosystems during a review of marine parks. They argue that current highly protected zones, mostly in remote areas, leave mainland waters under-protected. Scientists call for at least 30% protection in every marine bioregion, banning industrial fishing and mining. They highlight the unique biodiversity of regions like the temperate east, facing climate change and human pressures. While the government claims progress toward its 2030 30% protection target, scientists warn that current protections are insufficient and biased toward less accessible areas.

title: 10,000 protest climate policies in Sweden ahead of election
summary: Around 10,000 people rallied in Stockholm, Sweden, to protest climate policies ahead of the general election. Climate activist Greta Thunberg joined the demonstration, criticizing the government for weakening emissions targets. Organizers accused the right-wing government of reducing petrol taxes and rejecting recommendations to phase out fossil fuels. The protest highlighted concerns over Sweden's climate goals, with 37% of voters prioritizing climate action according to a recent poll. Activists called for urgent measures to meet emissions reduction targets, citing recent extreme weather events.

title: Iranian Foreign Minister Claims US Sanctions Will Fail Amid Ongoing Conflict
summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed new US sanctions as a sign of desperation, asserting they will fail to defeat Tehran. The US Treasury Secretary, Scott Bessent, threatened 'the toughest sanctions in history' on Iran. Iran's economy faces severe pressure from existing sanctions, and its infrastructure has been damaged by airstrikes. Tehran has disrupted oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, causing global oil price increases. Araghchi emphasized that past US actions, including blockades and military moves, have failed, and this new measure will too. Meanwhile, Pakistan's army chief is set to visit Tehran to discuss regional peace efforts, and Iran's President Pezeshkian called for a diplomatic solution to end the war.

title: Zelensky warns of 300,000 Russian troop draft after September elections
summary: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that Russia plans to draft 300,000 new troops after September elections to capture Donetsk, according to the article. He argued that wartime elections would 'destroy' Ukraine by splitting citizens, responding to calls from former Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov. Meanwhile, Putin expelled Russia's ambassador to London, accusing Britain of confrontation. Norway announced $9.2 billion in 2027 aid for Ukraine, while Ukraine faces a shortage of Patriot interceptors. A drone attack hit a Russian online retailer's warehouse, and Ukrainian refugees opened America's first jellyfish museum in Florida.

title: Ukraine's attacks on Russian fuel infrastructure worsen crisis and threaten war end
summary: Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries have intensified a fuel crisis, affecting 30 regions and particularly impacting Moscow and surrounding areas. Gas stations like Gazprom Neft and Tatneft have restricted fuel sales, with locals reporting long queues and economic disruptions. Analysts like Nikolai Korzhenevsky warn of declining fuel quality and production, projecting potential economic collapse if trends continue. Russian authorities propose fuel imports, but critics argue this is unfeasible given geopolitical isolation. Economist Vyacheslav Shiryaev suggests Ukrainian attacks could cripple Russia's economy and hasten the end of the war, citing disruptions to transportation and industry. He warns that fuel shortages could destabilize Vladimir Putin's regime by crippling critical infrastructure and supply chains.

title: Ukrainian leaders meet in Kyiv as forces target Russian e-commerce sites
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met with Finnish President Alexander Stubb and US Senators Richard Blumenthal and James Lankford in Kyiv ahead of Independence Day celebrations. Zelenskyy rejected a call for a war-time election, warning it could harm Ukraine. Ukrainian forces struck Ozon logistics sites in Russia, marking a shift from targeting Wildberries. The attacks aim to disrupt Russia's economy and supply lines. Meanwhile, Russian forces attacked Ukraine's railway network, killing one and injuring four. Zelenskyy emphasized the need for more Patriot interceptors to counter ballistic missiles.

title: Carney's Test of Economic Resistance Against Trump's Tariffs
summary: Mark Carney, Canada's central bank governor, faces a critical test of his warnings about economic coercion as President Trump imposes steep tariffs on Canadian goods. The dispute began when Carney rejected U.S. demands during negotiations, leading to retaliatory measures. Canada announced dollar-for-dollar tariffs starting Sept. 8, signaling its resistance to economic pressure. Carney argues that middle powers must resist great power coercion, even at economic cost, as the trade conflict becomes a test of sovereignty. Trump has criticized Canada's independence, suggesting it should be treated as the 51st U.S. state. Analysts note Canada's vulnerability due to its heavy reliance on the U.S. market, with nearly three-quarters of its exports going there. The situation also raises questions about whether Carney's strategy could inspire other U.S. allies to resist economic pressure.

title: Iranian President defends U.S. memorandum as path to end stalled war
summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian defended a memorandum of understanding with the United States as the best way to end the stalled war, stating it does not amount to capitulation. The agreement, signed by former U.S. President Donald Trump, set a 60-day deadline for resolving the conflict and addressing Iran's nuclear program, but no progress has been made. Pezeshkian also linked the agreement to Iran's economic recovery, noting the country's struggles under sanctions and a naval blockade. Meanwhile, an Israeli airstrike in Gaza killed a 4-year-old child, and a Palestinian man was beaten by an Israeli settler. The judiciary executed a man arrested during January's protests, accused of collaborating with hostile states.

title: Trump claims Hormuz on Truth Social, Rezaei says 'shut until US changes'
summary: Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Mohsen Rezaei stated that the Strait of Hormuz remains closed and will not reopen until the United States changes its behavior. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump claimed the strait as 'new American territory' on Truth Social, a claim he has made before. The strait, a critical shipping lane, has been closed since the war began, with both sides disputing control. Rezaei also warned Gulf states against joining US sanctions and threatened retaliation against those that do. Talks between Iran and Oman on regulating Hormuz traffic have stalled.

title: 21 Former Cricket Captains Urge Pakistan to Honor Court-Ordered Medical Care for Imran Khan
summary: Twenty-one former international cricket captains, including Greg Chappell and Michael Atherton, have appealed to Pakistan's Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif to ensure the completion of a court-ordered medical assessment for Imran Khan. The letter follows reports that Khan was briefly hospitalized but not examined by the court-appointed medical board. The captains request that the board, including Khan's personal doctors, conduct a full assessment of his health, particularly his reported vision loss, and that weekly family visits be upheld. They emphasize the importance of respecting court orders and ensuring humane treatment for Khan, who has been in custody for over three years.

title: Lando Norris wins Dutch Grand Prix after slow pit stop costs Oscar Piastri
summary: Lando Norris secured victory at the Dutch Grand Prix after a dramatic race marked by Max Verstappen's crash and a slow pit stop that dropped Oscar Piastri from third to sixth. Norris, the reigning world champion, overcame early setbacks to claim his second win of the season, moving to fourth in the championship. Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli finished second, while teammate George Russell came third after obeying team orders. Piastri's struggles were compounded by a slow stop and a lack of pace in the second half. Norris highlighted his strategic management and crucial overtakes, particularly on Antonelli and Lewis Hamilton, to secure the win. The race featured a red flag after Verstappen's crash, and a virtual safety car period during which several drivers pitted.

title: Youth organize caravan to counter Ebola response violence in Beni
summary: Young people in Beni organized a caravan to raise awareness about Ebola and address violence against response teams. The event, supported by NGOs and the WHO, followed attacks on burial teams and treatment centers. Beni, previously an Ebola epicenter, now faces a rapidly spreading outbreak that has surpassed the 2018 epidemic in deaths. Organizers linked the violence to regional insecurity and called for government support. They emphasized the need for community engagement to combat misinformation and mistrust of health workers.

title: Zelenskyy rejects wartime elections amid calls from former defense minister
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy rejected calls for wartime elections, calling them a 'tsunami' that could split the country. Former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov had proposed the idea after being dismissed by Zelenskyy. Zelenskyy criticized Fedorov, suggesting he was being pushed toward 'wrong things'. The president also warned of Russia's potential mass mobilization and announced an agreement with Germany for missile interceptors, while Europe seeks to support Ukraine amid reduced US involvement.

title: Japan proposes 150 cybersecurity measures for critical infrastructure sectors
summary: Japan's government has proposed 150 cybersecurity measures to protect critical infrastructure sectors from cyberattacks. The draft guidelines, which include measures for both open and closed networks, emphasize the need for cybersecurity insurance and preparedness for ransomware attacks. The government will accept public feedback until Wednesday and plans to release the final version by September. The guidelines target 16 sectors, including finance, railways, and electricity, and warn against overconfidence in system security. The draft also recommends using advanced AI models and postquantum cryptography to counter emerging threats like AI-driven cyberattacks and quantum computing.

title: New Zealander Reflects on Tokyo's Changing Summer Climate and Adaptation Strategies
summary: A New Zealander returning to Tokyo after 25 years notes the city's increasingly intense summers, attributing the rise in temperatures to both climate change and the urban heat island effect. Climate experts explain that Tokyo's average temperature has risen by 3°C over the past century, with humidity exacerbating the discomfort. The article highlights how Japan has developed a culture of adaptation, including the use of portable fans, cooling products, and traditional methods like uchimizu. Experts emphasize the need for behavioral changes, such as adjusting activity times and acclimatizing gradually, to cope with extreme heat. The piece also warns of the health risks of prolonged heat exposure and the potential for future climate impacts, while concluding with a reflection on the beauty of Tokyo's summer festivals and the importance of adapting to a warming world.

title: Oceanographer Carl Wunsch discusses climate research, international cooperation, and the impact of political skepticism
summary: Oceanographer Carl Wunsch, a key figure in modern physical oceanography, reflects on his career and the evolution of ocean research. He emphasizes the importance of international cooperation in understanding the ocean's role in the climate system, noting that the ocean is a shared global resource. Wunsch highlights the transformative impact of new technologies like satellites and autonomous vehicles, which have allowed for more comprehensive ocean observation. He expresses concern over the political skepticism of climate science, particularly referencing the effects of Trump's denial of climate change, which has led to reduced funding for research. Wunsch stresses the need for scientists to communicate the risks of climate change clearly, even when precise timelines remain uncertain, using forest fires as an example of the gap between scientific warnings and societal action.

title: Mexican author explores Aztec empire in new novel
summary: Mexican author Enrique Serna, 67, has released his new historical novel 'El Dios Hambriento' (The Hungry God), set during the rise of the Aztec Empire. The book focuses on the rivalry between Nezahualcóyotl, ruler of Texcoco, and Tlacaélel, advisor to Aztec emperors. Serna, who has previously written about Mexican history, explains his fascination with the pre-Hispanic era, driven by childhood nightmares and a deep interest in Aztec culture. He emphasizes the importance of portraying complex characters and explores themes of power, religion, and the role of women in Mexica society. Serna notes that while the novel is fictional, it contributes to understanding the past by highlighting the intricacies of historical figures and events.

title: UK crash kills seven, Israel strikes Syria, Iran shifts military strategy
summary: A car traveling the wrong way collided with a police vehicle in northeast England, killing seven people, including two officers, according to Sky News. An Israeli drone strike injured one person in southwestern Syria, with Syrian media reporting the attack in the Damascus countryside. Iran announced a shift from a defensive to an offensive military posture, citing lessons from recent conflicts. Canada suspended trade talks with the US over insufficient progress, while Colombia reversed a coal export ban to Israel, calling past restrictions ideological and harmful to the economy.

title: Canada announces retaliatory tariffs as trade dispute escalates with U.S.
summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced retaliatory tariffs against U.S. imports starting Sept. 8, following the Trump administration's imposition of 50% tariffs on Canadian goods. Carney compared the situation to war, stating Canada would match the tariffs to protect its economy. Trade negotiations collapsed before a midnight deadline, with both sides blaming each other for the breakdown. The U.S. criticized Canada for rejecting a trade deal, while Canada accused the U.S. of unfair terms. President Trump also criticized Canada on social media, highlighting the ongoing tensions between the two nations.

title: Australia requires tech firms to pay for news content or face levy
summary: Australia has enacted laws requiring major tech platforms like Google and Meta to negotiate deals with Australian news publishers or pay a 2.5% levy on their digital advertising revenue. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described the measure as a model for democracies, aiming to fund journalism. The U.S. government and Meta have criticized the law, with concerns over trade relations. Experts suggest the move could lead to trade tensions, including potential tariffs from the Trump administration. The law also faces opposition from free TV groups, which argue it ensures fair contributions from global tech platforms to Australian journalism.

title: U.S. Warns China to Cut Ties with Iran Amid Sanctions
summary: U.S. officials, including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, have warned China to reduce business ties with Iran, citing its role in helping Tehran withstand sanctions. China, which purchased over 80% of Iran's oil in 2025, has not responded to the call, with a spokesperson stating sanctions do not resolve issues. Iranian leaders have vowed to retaliate against U.S. sanctions, which they describe as unjust. Meanwhile, the U.S. and South Korea ended joint military drills early, with experts suggesting Trump's actions may aim to ease tensions with North Korea. In other news, Zambian authorities faced criticism for the killing of a former cabinet member during post-election tensions, and Pakistan's Imran Khan was briefly taken to a hospital, sparking legal challenges over his treatment.

title: Anton Jager Explains 'Hyperpolitics' and Its Global Impact
summary: Political scientist Anton Jager defines 'hyperpolitics' as increased political activity without corresponding institutional growth, a phenomenon observed globally since the 2008 financial crisis. He contrasts this with the mass politics of the 20th century and the 'post-politics' of the 1990s. Jager notes that while voter turnout has risen, union and party memberships have declined, leading to a paradox where political engagement does not translate into systemic change. He cites examples like the Black Lives Matter movement and the 'yellow vest' protests in France, which lacked formal organization. Jager argues that right-wing movements have been more successful in hyperpolitics due to greater access to private funding and less entrenched power structures to challenge. He acknowledges that while the left has funding sources, they are less accessible and effective compared to those on the right.

title: Kinmen's Strategic Islands and Cold War Legacy
summary: Kinmen, an island administered by Taiwan but geographically part of China's Fujian province, remains a strategic location with historical ties to the Cold War. The island, along with Matsu, was held by the Kuomintang (KMT) after their retreat to Taiwan in 1949, as part of a plan to retake mainland China. Despite U.S. support waning, the KMT maintained control over Kinmen and Matsu, while Dachen was abandoned. Today, Kinmen lacks modern infrastructure and nightlife, reflecting its isolation and the legacy of martial law. The island's coastline is marked by remnants of wartime installations, including anti-tank spikes and abandoned turrets. Local residents, like fishermen, express a sense of peace and detachment from political tensions, though the island's proximity to China and ongoing military developments, such as a planned bridge to Xiamen, highlight its potential as a flashpoint in East Asia's geopolitical landscape.

title: Kathi Zellweger's Humanitarian Work in North Korea's Famine
summary: Kathi Zellweger, a Swiss aid worker, documented her efforts to provide relief during North Korea's severe famine in the 1990s. In Sinuiju, she visited families struggling with hunger, including Mrs. Kim and Mr. Lee, who relied on bartering for survival. The Public Distribution System had collapsed, leaving urban residents without food. Zellweger noted that markets emerged as a crucial survival mechanism, though they were tolerated only grudgingly by the government. These markets, often hidden, became a lifeline for many, despite rising prices and limited access. Zellweger's work highlighted the 'hidden famine' in North Korea, where suffering was less visible but no less real.

title: 22-Year-Old Woman Dies by Suicide After Alleged Harassment by Ex-Flame
summary: A 22-year-old woman, Vanishree, died by suicide at Agara Lake in Bengaluru, according to her sister's complaint. The police registered a case against Abhishek A.S., her former college friend, under Section 108 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for alleged harassment and blackmail. Vanishree had reportedly faced intensified harassment over the past year, leading her to leave a note before her death. The police are investigating and searching for Abhishek.

title: Ananta Maharaj's Netaji Remarks Spark Political Reckoning in Bengal
summary: Ananta Maharaj, a BJP MP, sparked controversy by questioning Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose's contributions to India's independence, calling him a 'war criminal' and suggesting the INA was composed of British-Indian soldiers 'handed over by Germany'. His remarks led to the withdrawal of the Banga Bibhushan award by the West Bengal government. Maharaj cited declassified National Archives material and Nehru's alleged 'war criminal' remark, though historical records show Nehru rejected such claims. The article explores the complex legacy of Netaji, his political rivalries, and the enduring nationalist icon status he holds in Bengal. It highlights the historical context of Bose's INA, his ideological clashes with Gandhi and Nehru, and the evolving political interpretations of his legacy. The piece also touches on the unresolved debates over Bose's alliances and the symbolic significance of his remains in Tokyo.

title: Two stock recommendations for Monday: Jayaswal Neco Industries and Alkyl Amines
summary: The article provides two stock recommendations for Monday. Jayaswal Neco Industries is suggested to be bought with a buying zone between Rs 100-101, a stop-loss at Rs 95, and a target of Rs 110. The stock is noted for a breakout above resistance at Rs 96 with increased volume, and technical indicators show bullish momentum. Alkyl Amines is also recommended to be bought with a buying zone between Rs 2,050-2,060, a stop-loss at Rs 1,975, and a target of Rs 2,250. Both recommendations are from Virat Jagad, a senior technical research analyst at Bonanza Portfolio.

title: India considers linking diesel supply to Bangladesh project progress
summary: India may tie its decision on additional diesel supplies to Bangladesh to progress on stalled infrastructure projects funded through Lines of Credit (LoCs), sources said. Bangladesh has requested more diesel to address an energy crisis, with the request under review by New Delhi. Implementation of three $7.3 billion LoCs has been slow, with 15 projects completed and 11 identified for cancellation. India seeks progress on projects amid concerns about China's growing influence in Bangladesh. The government is also examining the impact of India's sheltering of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on bilateral relations.

title: Karnataka CM meets Adani during airport visit; discusses Hebbal-Silk Board tunnel project
summary: Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar met Adani Group chairman Gautam Adani during his visit to Bengaluru, described as a courtesy meeting. The encounter occurred amid Adani Enterprises' bid for the Hebbal-Silk Board tunnel project, with Adani's offer reportedly ₹4,600 crore above the government's estimated cost of ₹17,698 crore. The project, aimed at decongesting a busy route, faces opposition from BJP and citizen groups. Shivakumar noted it was Adani's first visit since becoming CM, while opposition leader R Ashoka criticized Congress for inconsistent stance on Adani.

title: N Ram advocates for journalism fundamentals to restore public trust
summary: Eminent journalist N Ram urged adherence to core journalistic practices like ground reporting and investigative journalism to rebuild public trust. Speaking at a press conclave, he emphasized transparent codes of conduct, independent self-regulation, and statutory frameworks for media oversight. Ram called for self-regulatory bodies composed of journalists and media figures, not just editors. He also highlighted the need for legislative backing of ethical standards and the role of news ombudsmen. While acknowledging digital platforms, he stressed the importance of maintaining traditional journalistic principles. Ram cited reader-funded models and media literacy in education as potential solutions to address misinformation and media ownership issues.

title: Ohio company sues woman over one-star Google review alleging false claims
summary: Starr Manufacturing Inc., an Ohio-based family-owned manufacturer, filed a defamation lawsuit against Julie Watson over a one-star Google review, claiming she made false and malicious allegations about its quality and manufacturing practices. The company alleges Watson, who was not a customer, falsely accused it of issues and sought to damage its reputation. Starr is seeking over $25,000 in damages and court costs. The lawyer representing Starr stated the review stemmed from a personal dispute with an employee, not a business issue. Watson has posted several reviews on Google, with this one-star rating being her only negative review among them. The case highlights legal risks associated with online reviews.

title: India's National Security Advisor to Meet Chinese Foreign Minister Ahead of BRICS Summit
summary: India's National Security Advisor Ajit Doval will meet Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Beijing ahead of President Xi Jinping's visit for the BRICS Summit. The talks aim to address border issues and maintain peace along the Line of Actual Control. The meeting follows recent coordination efforts to resolve long-standing disputes. Meanwhile, Union Minister Pralhad Joshi cited El Nino and red rot disease as causes of reduced sugar production, leading to temporary raw sugar imports to meet festival demand.

title: Book explores food and personal lives of Indian prime ministers
summary: A new book titled 'The Prime Minister's Table' examines the personal lives and food culture of Indian prime ministers over seven decades. Authored by Purabi Shridhar and Sanghita Singh, it includes stories like Indira Gandhi playing antakshari with her doctor and Narendra Modi teaching a BJP worker's wife to make sabudana khichdi. The book draws from interviews with families, cooks, and associates, revealing the shift from royal kitchens to everyday meals in democratic India. The authors aimed to uncover the human side of leaders, sharing intimate family moments and personal relationships.

title: NSA Doval to meet Chinese officials ahead of Xi's India visit
summary: National Security Advisor Ajit Doval will visit Beijing for boundary discussions with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi ahead of President Xi Jinping's India visit. The talks aim to address border issues and maintain peace along the Line of Actual Control. Meanwhile, a Trinamool Congress leader was arrested on multiple charges including economic offences and arms procurement. Political tensions also flare within the Congress over remarks on ancient texts and women's rights, with Rahul Gandhi criticizing patriarchal views, prompting backlash from the BJP.

title: Isro chief announces India's plan to build space station by 2035
summary: Isro chairman Dr V Narayanan announced India's plan to establish its own space station, the Bharatiya Antariksha Station, by 2035. The first module has been approved, and the initiative reflects India's growing capabilities in space technology. Narayanan highlighted the country's use of space-based applications across over 50 areas, including Earth observation and disaster mitigation. He also mentioned upcoming projects like the Gaganyaan human spaceflight mission. The announcement occurred during the third National Space Day celebrations, which commemorated India's lunar achievements, including the Chandrayaan-3 mission. Union Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat noted the expansion of private participation in the space sector and the reduction in time for space-related activities.

title: Chennai police search Odisha for suspects in Tamil Nadu Express murder case
summary: Chennai police are searching Odisha for a couple suspected of murdering and dismembering Hayathun Nisha, a 38-year-old woman from Jagatsinghpur. The severed body parts were found in a suitcase on a train near Agra. Police believe the suspects may have fled to Odisha after the crime. Investigators traced the suspects to a rented residence in Chennai, where more body parts were recovered. The case began when railway staff discovered the remains in a trolley bag on August 5.

title: Alphabet out, Netflix in: Bill Ackman exits major stocks, reworks Pershing Square's portfolio — Here's what has changed
summary: Bill Ackman has significantly altered his investment fund Pershing Square's portfolio, exiting Alphabet, Universal Music Group, and Hertz while adding Netflix and other large-cap companies. The changes reflect a strategic shift toward firms with strong software and valuation fundamentals. Ackman's new fund, Pershing Square USA, has invested 95% of its capital, with a notable 5% allocated to Netflix. The fund also plans to launch a private equity arm focused on late-stage startups.

title: Canada's trade talks with US ended over tariff disputes, offering lessons for India
summary: Canada terminated trade negotiations with the US in August 2026 after the Trump administration offered limited tariff relief. The US had imposed 50% tariffs on Canadian goods, and Ottawa responded with retaliatory measures. The talks, which began in February 2025, aimed to address new US tariffs outside the USMCA framework, including Section 232, 301, and 338 tariffs. Canada sought exemptions and tariff cuts but found the US proposals too restrictive. Prime Minister Mark Carney called the terms 'uneconomic' and 'unfair,' emphasizing the need for balanced agreements. Ajay Srivastava of GTRI suggests India should prioritize clear, binding tariff concessions in its own negotiations with the US to avoid similar imbalances.

title: S&P 500 Shiller CAPE ratio hits 40, second time in 155 years
summary: The S&P 500 Shiller CAPE ratio reached 40 in June 2026, marking the second time in 155 years that the measure has hit this level. The CAPE ratio, developed by Yale professor Robert Shiller, uses a 10-year average of inflation-adjusted earnings to assess stock valuations. Historically, the ratio has averaged around 15.7 from 1871 to 2000, with levels above 40 occurring only during the dot-com bubble in 1999 and the 1929 market crash. While high valuations can signal market risks, the current situation differs from past episodes as earnings are growing faster than valuations. Investors are advised to remain cautious, focusing on high-quality companies and maintaining cash reserves in case of market corrections.

title: Bill Ackman shifts portfolio, sells AI stocks, buys financial and media firms
summary: Bill Ackman, managing Pershing Square, has significantly altered his investment portfolio in 2026 by selling major holdings in Alphabet, Universal Music Group, and Hertz, while acquiring six new stocks in financial services, entertainment, and healthcare. The shift reflects Ackman's strategy to move beyond the AI boom, focusing instead on undervalued sectors. Pershing Square USA, a new $5 billion fund, has invested 95% of its capital, leveraging market volatility to buy discounted assets. Ackman also expanded into private companies, planning a new venture fund to invest in late-stage private businesses. His new investments include Visa, Mastercard, Netflix, S&P Global, Intercontinental Exchange, and Alcon, which he believes offer long-term value outside the AI-focused market.

title: RMZ appoints Ankit Samdariya to lead $35 billion expansion and capital raise
summary: RMZ Corp has appointed Ankit Samdariya as managing director of equity capital markets to support its $35 billion expansion over five years. The real estate firm plans to fund developments through debt, equity, and an IPO. Samdariya, previously at LO-GOI Group, will focus on global partnerships with pension funds and asset managers. RMZ's expansion into commercial offices and data centres requires substantial institutional capital, with recent deals involving Blackstone, Mitsui Fudosan, and Brookfield. The company is also in talks to raise $400-500 million from global investors.

title: Jharkhand Protests: FIRs Filed Against Hundreds Over Police Clashes
summary: Hundreds of individuals, both named and unnamed, have been booked in Jharkhand following clashes between police and student protesters in Ranchi, Giridih, and Hazaribag. The protests, organized under the Jharkhand Public Service Commission-Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission Reforms Manch, were triggered by alleged irregularities in recruitment exams and subsequent legal actions. FIRs were filed against over 200 unidentified and 28 named individuals for obstructing government work and assaulting police. The state government canceled 44 exams conducted by a private firm, leading to legal challenges and a stay order from the High Court. Protests escalated when demonstrators attempted to burn effigies of Chief Minister Hemant Soren and Rahul Gandhi, resulting in confrontations with law enforcement and political workers.

title: Alibaba raises HK$80 billion for AI expansion, largest follow-on offering in Hong Kong
summary: Alibaba Group announced a HK$80 billion (₹95,000 crore) share sale in Hong Kong, the largest follow-on offering by a company on record, to fund its AI initiatives. The funds will support expanding AI infrastructure and enhancing full-stack AI capabilities. The offering, which includes 710 million shares at HK$112.70 each, marks Alibaba's first new share placement since its 2019 Hong Kong listing. The company's cloud and AI business saw a 45% revenue increase in the April-June quarter, with capital expenditure rising 75%. Alibaba's CEO, Eddie Wu Yongming, expects AI computing investments to break even within three years. The fundraising follows a 75% drop in quarterly net profit due to increased AI spending, while revenue rose 9% to ₹2.24 lakh crore. Alibaba's AI push includes expanding its Qwen language models and Zhenwu chips, which have served over 650 customers on Alibaba Cloud.

title: Madrassa Student Assaulted On Train After Refusing Alcohol Offer
summary: A madrasa student named Muntazir was assaulted on a train from Meerut to Deoband after refusing alcohol. A group of men, reportedly under the influence, offered him a drink, which he declined. He changed seats to avoid confrontation, but the men pursued him, verbally abused him, and physically attacked him, forcing him to disembark at Khatauli station. His phone and cash were allegedly stolen. Muntazir, who teaches at a madrasa, described the incident, noting that he was not a thief. The case is not isolated, as a cleric was killed in a similar incident in April. Officials have not yet released statements on the investigation, raising concerns about safety for religious minorities on public transport.

title: India's IT firms shift to outcome-based contracts amid AI-driven cost pressures
summary: India's IT services sector is transforming as companies adopt outcome-based contracts to meet client demands for cost reductions and increased productivity. Major firms like Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) and Cognizant are moving away from hourly billing, with TCS reporting 80% of its finance and HR contracts now tied to performance outcomes. This shift is driven by AI's ability to automate tasks, reducing reliance on large employee bases and leveling the playing field for smaller firms. Clients are pushing for more value for less, with some demanding 25-30% lower prices while expecting faster delivery. While mid-sized firms are gaining traction through agility and flexible pricing, larger companies face challenges as they adjust to a more competitive landscape. TCS, despite its size, has seen subdued growth and is implementing layoffs, signaling a shift away from traditional hiring practices.

title: Brazil's Heavy Rains Threaten Premium Arabica Coffee Quality
summary: Heavy downpours in Brazil have disrupted the production of premium arabica coffee, affecting quality and availability. The rains washed ripe coffee cherries from trees, leaving beans exposed to contamination and mold, which compromises the aromatic profile sought by premium roasters like Starbucks and Illycaffe. Simão de Lima of Expocacer cooperative estimates 20% of cherries were washed off, compared to 5-7% normally. A second wave of rain in July forced growers to restart drying, further damaging quality. Arabica coffee futures have risen 35% since June, with fine Brazilian coffees commanding premiums. ICE standards for quality may drop to 10-15% of output, down from 30-35%. While Brazil's overall production is expected to be a record, the quality issues may reduce the supply of premium arabica, impacting global markets.

title: Bangladesh's Commerce Minister highlights interest from Indian and U.S. businesses in investment opportunities
summary: Bangladesh's Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir noted growing interest from Indian and U.S. businesses in investing in the country. Indian businesspeople, who recently visited Bangladesh, have proposed improving land port operations and establishing task forces for infrastructure development. A U.S. trade delegation also expressed interest in creating a favorable investment climate. India remains Bangladesh's second-largest trading partner, with bilateral trade reaching $11.35 billion in the 2025-26 fiscal year. The minister emphasized the need to increase trade volume to match the country's economic size.

title: 20 IPOs on investors' radar next week with GMPs indicating up to 107% returns
summary: Twenty IPOs are set to open for subscription next week, with several mainboard and SME offerings drawing attention. The GMPs (Green Shoe Mechanism prices) suggest potential listing gains ranging from 4% to 107%. Tempsens Instruments leads with a 107% gain, while Kwick Forensic Solutions and Lumino Industries show gains of 56.7% and 63.4%, respectively. Other notable IPOs include Symbiotec Pharmalab (41.5%), Hy-Tech Engineers (50.9%), and Augmont Enterprises (50.1%). Some IPOs have already closed, such as Lalithaa Jewellery Mart (38.3%) and Horizon Industrial Parks (5%). The article also mentions several IPOs with GMPs indicating lower gains, including Annu Projects (4%) and Dhanwel Hybrid Seeds (1%). ETMarkets.com reports these figures, noting that some IPOs have not yet released GMP data.

title: Pride Hotels expands portfolio, plans Rs 1,000-cr IPO by December
summary: Pride Hotels, a Mumbai-based hospitality chain, is expanding its portfolio to 72 properties by 2027 through 32 new hotel contracts. The company's CEO, Satyen Jain, highlighted the focus on pilgrimage and leisure travel markets, noting rising holiday frequency and consumer preference for experiential travel. Pride Hotels plans to launch an IPO by December 2026, with a proposed issue size of Rs 1,000 crore, to fund renovations, debt repayment, and operational needs. The company is also exploring a new boutique brand, Pride Lux, while addressing rising operating costs through renewable energy investments and energy-efficient equipment. Chairman S P Jain identified licensing as a major challenge for the hospitality sector, calling for streamlined approval processes. The company remains focused on the domestic market for now, though it may explore international opportunities with significant Indian tourist traffic.

title: Satheesan's 100 Days of Policy Reversals and Controversies
summary: The first 100 days of V.D. Satheesan's government in Kerala have been marked by a series of controversial decisions and policy reversals, undermining public confidence. Despite initial optimism following a strong electoral victory, the UDF government has faced criticism for hasty decisions, including the implementation of the PM SHRI education scheme and the controversial sale of a port stake to Adani. These moves, which the UDF had previously opposed, have drawn backlash from both the public and opposition. The government's handling of internal party dynamics, including factional struggles within the Congress, has further complicated its governance. Meanwhile, the opposition, led by Pinarayi Vijayan, remains paralyzed, struggling to recover from its electoral defeat. The article highlights the challenges Satheesan faces as he navigates a politically turbulent landscape.

title: Mitra Phukan explores conflict and identity through her literary works
summary: Mitra Phukan, an Assamese writer and translator, explores themes of conflict, identity, and societal issues through her diverse body of work. With 18 published volumes, including novels, short stories, and biographies, she delves into topics such as insurgency, cultural tensions, and personal relationships. Her writing, influenced by her training in Shastriya Sangeet and her academic background in English Literature, blends realism with creative imagination. Phukan's novel 'The Collector’s Wife' and short story collection 'The Greatest Assamese Stories Ever Told' reflect her engagement with regional and global audiences. She emphasizes the importance of translating Assamese literature to a wider readership, highlighting the richness of the region's literary tradition. Phukan also discusses the impact of insurgency on her life and work, portraying multidimensional tragedies with a humanistic perspective.

title: India's Climate Readiness Assessment Stalled After Three Phases
summary: India initiated a climate readiness assessment for cities in 2019, using the Climate Smart Cities Assessment Framework (CSCAF) in three phases. The framework measured cities' readiness across five themes, including urban planning and waste management, with results showing national readiness at 30–34%. Despite progress, the assessment halted after Phase 3, leaving no current data on city climate readiness. The report highlights the importance of measurement in driving climate action, as it provides evidence for decision-making and accountability. However, without ongoing assessments, it is unclear if cities have improved their readiness or achieved climate outcomes. The lack of consolidated data on climate actions by Indian cities also remains a challenge, with calls for continued assessments and public disclosure of all climate initiatives.

title: Indigenous fruits face decline due to urbanization and commercial crops
summary: Indigenous fruits are disappearing from local diets and landscapes due to urbanization, land-use changes, and the dominance of commercial crops. These fruits offer nutritional, medicinal, and ecological benefits, yet their decline is driven by a lack of research, limited market demand, and the preference for exotic, high-yield crops. Experts emphasize that creating demand through value addition, documentation, and community support can help conserve these fruits, but commercialization must remain sustainable and community-centred. In regions like Assam and Meghalaya, local communities report a reduction in traditional fruits, with some species becoming rare or extinct. Researchers highlight the importance of indigenous crops for food security and genetic diversity, urging the need for better documentation, research, and support for farmers and home gardeners to preserve these vital resources.

title: University offers £2,000 esports scholarships to students
summary: The University of Roehampton is offering esports scholarships to undergraduate and postgraduate students, with over 100 awarded so far. Recipients must balance academic studies with competitive gaming, participating in weekly tournaments and representing the university. Scholarships initially at £1,500 were increased to £2,000 due to the team's performance and popularity. Students like Cameron Dray highlight the financial support as crucial for studying in expensive cities without part-time work. Experts note that many scholarships remain unclaimed due to lack of awareness, emphasizing the importance of utilizing available funding opportunities.

title: Anthropic's top AI model sees lower adoption compared to cheaper alternatives
summary: Anthropic's top AI model, Opus 5, saw limited adoption in July 2026, with Fable 5 and Sonnet 4.6 also underperforming compared to older models like Opus 4.8. The company reported $65bn in annualized revenue for July, up from $47bn in May, and expects Q3 to be profitable. OpenAI's revenue rose 35% to over $40bn, driven by the launch of GPT 5.6. The Ramp AI index, which tracks model adoption through credit card data, highlights the growing preference for more affordable tools over Anthropic's offerings.

title: Ox Alpha's Developer Remains Anonymous Amid Speculation
summary: A new AI model called Ox Alpha, released as a 'stealth model' on OpenRouter, has sparked speculation about its creator. The model is described as a reasoning tool for coding and production work. OpenRouter credits a third-party provider, who chose to remain anonymous. Speculation has focused on Chinese companies like Z.ai and Microsoft's MAI, with conflicting claims on forums like Reddit.

title: Drew Breunig reflects on Fable's impact and the shift in AI model development
summary: Drew Breunig discusses the transition in AI model development, noting that prior to Fable, improving coding tools felt unnecessary due to the rapid release of new models. He highlights Fable's exceptional performance, though its high cost made it less accessible compared to existing models like Opus, 5.6, K3, and GLM. Breunig emphasizes the growing consideration of where to allocate development efforts in light of Fable's emergence.

title: Linkdaze's smart calendar organizes households with AI meal planning and multi-calendar sync
summary: Linkdaze's smart calendar is designed to manage household schedules, integrating multiple calendar services and offering AI-driven meal planning. The device syncs Google, iCloud, Outlook, and Cozi calendars, using color coding to distinguish family members. It includes a 'Snap-to-Sync' feature that converts photos of recipes or lunch menus into digital meal plans. Linkdaze does not require a subscription for core features, unlike competitors like Skylight, and is priced lower than similar devices. It serves as a practical tool for families, college roommates, and busy professionals managing complex schedules.

title: NVIDIA's AVO Architecture Achieves 100% on ARC-AGI-3, Demonstrating General-Purpose Long-Horizon Agent Capabilities
summary: NVIDIA's AVO architecture, designed for long-horizon autonomous agents, achieved a 100.00 RHAE score on the ARC-AGI-3 benchmark, completing all 183 levels. The system, which uses persistent memory and supervision, was previously tested on GPU-kernel optimization tasks. AVO's success highlights the importance of the agent architecture over the model alone, showing that the same system can adapt to different environments. The benchmark evaluates agents' ability to infer environment dynamics, plan actions, and maintain progress over time. NVIDIA's results suggest that general-purpose agent systems can transfer across domains, emphasizing the role of sustained autonomous operation rather than domain-specific knowledge.

title: NVIDIA outlines security layers for AI agent stacks to prevent unauthorized actions
summary: NVIDIA's AI safety and security teams emphasize the importance of integrating security into AI agent stacks as agents become more capable. They highlight the role of each layer in the agent stack, including models, harnesses, and secure runtimes, and stress the need for clear boundaries and control mechanisms. Recent incidents involving frontier agents operating beyond their intended boundaries underscore the challenges of securing long-horizon agents. NVIDIA's research on Agentic Variation Operators (AVO) demonstrates how harnesses can guide agent behavior effectively. The article outlines five design rules for maintaining security, including authoritative policy location, just-in-time access, and isolation. It also discusses the importance of infrastructure enforcement and the need for consistent security practices across different agent profiles.

title: Cartoon depicts Ella Baron's views on AI and drought
summary: The article features a cartoon illustrating Ella Baron's perspectives on artificial intelligence and the ongoing drought. The visual commentary highlights the intersection of technological advancement and environmental challenges. The piece uses satire to explore the implications of AI in addressing resource scarcity. The cartoon's imagery conveys a critical stance on current drought management strategies. The artwork underscores the need for innovative solutions in times of crisis.

title: PyTorch Conference North America 2026 Announces Keynote Speakers and Sessions
summary: The PyTorch Conference North America 2026, scheduled for October 20–21 in San Jose, California, has announced its keynote lineup. The event will feature sessions on PyTorch updates, Trainium integration, agent workloads, and open science. Keynote speakers include Mark Collier from the PyTorch Foundation, Alban Desmaison and Edward Yang from Meta, and representatives from Amazon Web Services, Red Hat, NVIDIA, and Google Cloud. The program also includes sponsored talks from Qualcomm and Cohere, as well as a keynote from the Agentic AI Foundation.

title: NHS Trust Scrutiny and Healthwatch Cuts Raise Concerns
summary: A letter criticizes the proposed abolition of statutory governors in NHS trusts, arguing it removes local oversight by experienced professionals. The writer, a former health professional, questions the government's shift to 'dynamic stakeholders,' suggesting it favors industry shareholders. The letter also highlights the government's plan to eliminate Healthwatch, an independent body that allows public input on healthcare issues. Concerns are raised about reduced accountability and the impact on patient care, with the writer urging parliamentary intervention to preserve local voices in healthcare governance.

title: SQL Procedures Migrated to Lakehouse with Minimal Changes
summary: The article discusses the migration of legacy SQL stored procedures to a lakehouse environment with minimal code changes. It highlights a specific example of a procedure that processes daily orders, involving temporary tables, validation loops, and transaction handling. The migration was achieved by translating the SQL code rather than rewriting it, leveraging Databricks' support for procedural SQL features. Key points include the use of Unity Catalog for governance, the replacement of temporary tables with session-scoped CREATE TEMP TABLE, native cursor support in Databricks SQL, and the use of BEGIN ATOMIC for transaction semantics. The migration reduces effort by 50-75% and allows SQL teams to maintain their logic while integrating with modern data platforms.

title: Study finds optimal repetition of target data in mixture pretraining
summary: A study examines the trade-off between target data repetition and model performance in language model training. Researchers found that scarce target corpora can be reused 15–20 times, with optimal repetition depending on data size, compute budget, and model scale. They introduced a repetition-aware scaling law to determine effective mixture configurations for pretraining under data constraints. The work highlights the role of generic data in regularization and provides practical recommendations for data mixtures.

title: Genie Agents Enable Domain-Specific AI from Single Prompt
summary: Databricks Genie Agents allow users to create domain-specific AI assistants from a single prompt by leveraging trusted business context. The agents reason over structured data, documents, and files governed by Unity Catalog, addressing the issue of missing context that often leads to inaccurate responses. By focusing on a single use case, teams can test and trust agents more effectively, as the quality of the agent depends on the curated context provided. The process begins with a prompt that describes the desired outcome and points to relevant data sources, enabling the agent to draw from the right information. Genie Agents can handle both structured and unstructured data, ensuring answers are grounded in the correct sources. Testing with predefined benchmarks helps improve accuracy, and agents can be expanded over time as more data and knowledge are added. The success of these agents relies on the quality of the underlying data and systems, emphasizing the importance of governance and domain expertise.

title: Study explores human-like behaviors in LLMs across models and user factors
summary: A study examines the prevalence and control of human-like behaviors in large language models (LLMs), analyzing 21,000 conversations from four models. Researchers found these behaviors vary across models and user factors, with human evaluators perceiving self-referential and relationship-building behaviors as less appropriate from LLMs. System prompts can influence these behaviors, though careful evaluation is needed to avoid unintended effects. The study recommends responsible LLM design and evaluation practices.

title: Optimal Memory Dosing for AI Agents Varies by Model Capability
summary: A study evaluates how different AI models benefit from agentic memory, finding that the optimal amount of memory varies by model tier. Stronger models with headroom perform best with full guideline sets, while weaker models benefit from curated, task-specific retrieval. Saturated models show no measurable gain. The research, conducted on eight models ranging from 30B to 745B parameters, highlights that memory is distilled from an agent's past trajectories and injected at inference time without weight updates. The study uses AppWorld, a benchmark with 585 multi-step tasks, to measure performance improvements in task and scenario goal completion. Curated retrieval proved both accurate and cost-effective, with gpt-oss-120b achieving +16.1pp task completion at only +5% token cost. The findings suggest that memory should be calibrated to the model's capabilities, with prompt caching and efficient retrieval strategies helping to manage costs in production.

title: Multi-Vector Embedding Models Enable Enhanced Retrieval with Late Interaction
summary: Multi-vector embedding models, such as those from LightOn, use late interaction to improve retrieval by preserving token-level information. Unlike dense models that compress text into a single vector, these models retain one vector per token, allowing for more precise matching. This approach is particularly effective for visual document retrieval and complex queries with multiple requirements. The models can be loaded via the sentence-transformers library, with support for various checkpoint formats. Indexing and scoring use MaxSim to align query and document tokens, enhancing retrieval quality without sacrificing speed.

title: Eugene Fitzgerald discusses innovation's role in economic growth and research
summary: Eugene Fitzgerald, an MIT professor, explores the complexities of innovation in his book 'The Invisible Engine,' arguing that it is a multifaceted process involving science, economics, and implementation. He highlights that innovation is not just about ideas but a process of creating value through market applications, technology, and real-world implementation. Fitzgerald identifies three types of research investment: altruistic science, strategic research, and fundamental innovation, each with distinct goals and outcomes. He emphasizes the importance of understanding these distinctions for effective investment and policy-making, and encourages students and researchers to develop a T-shaped skill set that combines technical expertise with broad knowledge of business and economics.

title: NVIDIA and SB Energy Develop AI Campus in Ohio for OpenAI
summary: NVIDIA has partnered with SB Energy to develop the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in Ohio, which will exclusively host NVIDIA AI compute infrastructure. OpenAI will be the primary customer, utilizing NVIDIA's DSX AI factory platform. The project includes a $1.5 billion investment by NVIDIA in SB Energy, supporting the development of 8 IT-GW of AI capacity. SB Energy will build and operate the data center under a 20-year lease to OpenAI. The campus is expected to create tens of thousands of jobs and invest hundreds of millions in the local community. NVIDIA's investment aims to support SB Energy's growth and its commitments to Ohio, with the project planned to come online in phases starting in 2028.

title: Google Research Demonstrates Smartphone-Based Body Composition Estimation for Insulin Resistance Prediction
summary: Google Research scientists demonstrate PhotoScan, a deep learning framework that estimates body composition from smartphone photos, achieving accuracy comparable to DXA scans in predicting insulin resistance. The study highlights the limitations of BMI and traditional methods, showing that PhotoScan can measure body fat percentage, A/G ratio, and V/S ratio with high precision. Validated across clinical cohorts, PhotoScan outperforms smartwatch-based BIA sensors and offers a scalable, non-invasive alternative to DXA. The research shows that integrating body composition data from smartphone images improves insulin resistance prediction, with AUROC scores nearly matching clinical DXA data. The findings suggest a promising path for accessible, non-invasive screening of metabolic risk.

title: Indonesia Launches First University-Based AI Center to Develop Local Talent
summary: The UGM Indosat NVIDIA AI Technology Center, Indonesia's first university-based AI center, was launched to develop local AI talent and address national challenges. The initiative, supported by the government, Indosat, and NVIDIA, aims to foster AI innovation in healthcare, agriculture, and disaster response. The center provides access to advanced computing resources and global expertise, enabling researchers to tackle issues like tuberculosis detection, precision farming, and disaster preparedness. Officials emphasized the importance of AI sovereignty and economic growth through local talent development.

title: PyTorch Enhances FP8 Training on AMD GPUs with Optimizations and MoE Support
summary: PyTorch developers have integrated FP8 training optimizations for AMD Instinct GPUs into TorchAO and TorchTitan, improving performance on large models. These enhancements include native support for AMD's FP8 format, grouped GEMM for MoE architectures, and a Triton fusion pipeline to reduce quantization overhead. On Llama3-8B, FP8 training achieved a 13.4% throughput gain over BF16. For MoE models like DeepSeek-V3 671B, optimizations recovered 89% of the initial FP8 overhead through kernel fusion and memory-efficient techniques. The work, a collaboration between AMD and Meta, ensures FP8 training on AMD GPUs is now available out of the box for the PyTorch community.

title: NIST to Discuss Building Failures and Hurricane Impacts at Advisory Committee Meeting
summary: NIST will host a virtual meeting of the National Construction Safety Team Advisory Committee on Sept. 23 and 24, 2026, to update on building failure investigations. The meeting will focus on the impacts of Hurricane Maria on Puerto Rico and the collapse of Champlain Towers South in Surfside, Florida. NIST will also address its Disaster and Failure Studies Program and responses to 2025 advisory committee recommendations. Registration for the public meeting is open until Sept. 16, 2026, with a public comment period available for registered attendees. A video on the Champlain Towers South collapse was released in June 2026, and all related materials are available on dedicated websites.

title: Google collaborates with Deaf community to develop sign language AI
summary: Google has developed sign language AI technology, SL2T, in collaboration with the Deaf community. The project involved Deaf perspectives at every stage, from conceptualization to impact assessment. An AI Sign Language Advisory Committee (AISLAC) was formed to ensure community input. The technology is now available in Gboard and Live Transcribe on Pixel 11 devices. Google aims to expand the technology to additional sign languages and explore sign language generation. The development involved teams from Google DeepMind and Android, with contributions from numerous researchers and testers.

title: IBM Introduces DocLang to Improve AI Understanding of Documents
summary: IBM researchers have introduced DocLang, a markup language designed to enhance AI's ability to understand and process documents. DocLang, a constrained dialect of XML, aims to reduce latency and inference costs by providing a clear structure for AI models to interpret document content. It addresses the limitations of existing formats like PDF and DOCX, which were not designed for machine understanding. By encoding semantics, layout, and reading order, DocLang offers a standardized representation that improves accuracy and consistency. The language is open and governed by the Linux Foundation, with support from tools like Docling and ABBYY's FineReader Engine. While challenges remain in adoption and implementation, IBM argues that DocLang's benefits, including reduced hallucination and improved governance, make it a valuable addition to AI workflows.

title: LLMs Struggle with Recall, Not Missing Knowledge, Study Finds
summary: A study by Google Research scientists Nitay Calderon and Gal Yona reveals that large language models (LLMs) often fail to recall encoded facts rather than lacking them. The research introduces a framework called knowledge profiling, which distinguishes between encoding and recall failures. Using a benchmark called WikiProfile, the study evaluates 13 LLMs, finding that while most facts are encoded, recall remains a significant challenge. For models like Gemini-3-Pro and GPT-5, 26–34% of facts cannot be directly recalled, and even with thinking, 11–12% remain inaccessible. The study suggests that recall issues, not encoding gaps, are the primary cause of factual errors in frontier LLMs. It also highlights that rare facts are encoded but difficult to access, and thinking-optimized models show improved recall for these cases, indicating that better utilization of existing knowledge may be key to improving factuality.

title: CARE-X Model Combines Generative and Discriminative Capabilities for Enhanced Chest X-ray Interpretation
summary: CARE-X is a research model designed to address gaps in current radiology vision-language models by integrating generative and discriminative capabilities. It supports diverse clinical tasks through dual inference, providing both free-text generation and structured predictions with calibrated confidence scores. The model uses reinforcement learning with DAPO to optimize clinical fidelity and includes auxiliary heads for classification and visual grounding. Validation on Indian clinical data shows improved performance in detecting rare ICU conditions and measurement-dependent findings like cardiomegaly. A separate study using Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct with deterministic tools demonstrates that direct computation can enhance diagnostic accuracy for quantitative assessments. While CARE-X is not a medical device, its results highlight potential for future clinical applications in radiology workflows.

title: IBM and collaborators develop unified AI solver for grid analysis
summary: IBM Research and collaborators have developed GENCO, a unified AI solver for grid analysis, as part of the OpenGridFM project. The tool addresses the growing complexity of modern power grids by unifying three core tasks—power flow, optimal power flow, and state estimation—into a single model. GENCO significantly improves speed and accuracy compared to traditional methods, with performance gains up to 30 times faster for power flow and 85 times faster for optimal power flow. The project also includes the GridFM Development Framework, which enables reproducible and fair benchmarking of neural grid solvers. The model was validated on real-world data from Hydro-Québec's transmission network, demonstrating its practical applicability. The initiative emphasizes open collaboration among industry, academia, and government to advance AI-driven grid management.

title: AWS Trainium Frontier competition explores optimal AI model designs on purpose-built chips
summary: AWS launches the Trainium Frontier competition, inviting researchers to design and train language models on its purpose-built AI chips. The competition challenges participants to optimize model architectures, training loops, and custom kernels to achieve the best performance within a fixed time and compute budget. The goal is to explore how different hardware constraints influence the efficient frontier of model design. Participants start with a 50M parameter baseline and can modify all aspects of the model, including the optimizer and training process. The competition has two phases: an initial 30-minute training period and a four-hour phase with distributed parallelism. The final score combines training efficiency and inference performance. The competition aims to advance hardware-native model design and offers prizes, including recognition at a NeurIPS event and publication opportunities.

title: GeoPT enables faster, more accurate physics simulations for engineering applications
summary: Researchers at MIT's CSAIL and Tsinghua University have developed GeoPT, a new pre-training approach that allows AI models to simulate physical scenarios more efficiently. Unlike traditional methods that rely on numerical solvers, GeoPT uses synthetic dynamics to learn physics from 1.3 million particle interactions, enabling faster training and reduced data requirements. The system can predict how vehicles, robots, and everyday objects respond to forces like wind, water, and collisions, with results up to six times more accurate than existing models. GeoPT's ability to generalize across complex 3D shapes and physical phenomena could revolutionize engineering testing, reducing the need for physical experiments. The researchers believe their work represents a step toward creating physics foundation models, which could be used for tasks like simulating weather patterns or testing new materials.

title: TutorMoments evaluates AI tutors' ability to balance support and challenge in math sessions
summary: TutorMoments is a framework that assesses how well large language models (LLMs) can balance providing support and encouraging independent thinking during math tutoring. The system uses real tutoring transcripts from U.S. students in grades 2-7, annotated by experienced teachers, to identify key decision points where tutors must decide between scaffolding or pushing for rigor. LLMs are tested by taking over these sessions and simulating tutoring interactions. Results show models tend to over-help, giving too much support and rarely challenging students. While specifying the trade-off in prompts improves performance, LLMs still struggle to match human tutors' nuanced judgment. The project, developed by researchers, aims to help build AI tutors that adapt to individual student needs rather than doing the work for them. The dataset and code are released for open research.

title: WeatherNext model improves cyclone forecasting with AI
summary: WeatherNext's AI model, using Functional Generative Networks, now generates 15-day cyclone forecasts in under a minute on a TPU. The system, which scales to 1,000 ensemble members, captures rare events like rapid intensification. It achieves accuracy at a coarser 28x28km resolution than traditional models. The company is open-sourcing code and model weights to advance weather forecasting research. The model also provides global weather forecasts through Weather Lab, part of Google Earth AI.

title: Ai2 and Hugging Face expand partnership to enhance open AI infrastructure
summary: Ai2 and Hugging Face are expanding their collaboration to improve access and deployment of open AI resources. The partnership includes tripling storage capacity on the Hugging Face Hub to nearly two petabytes and removing rate limits for traffic. Since 2024, over 50 million models and datasets have been downloaded from the Hub. The collaboration supports the release of training data, intermediate checkpoints, and evaluation tools, enabling researchers to reproduce and build upon Ai2's work. Hugging Face's infrastructure will support future projects like multimodal models and scientific agents. The partnership also integrates Ai2's models into tools like LeRobot, allowing developers to use and fine-tune them. Hugging Face highlights the impact of Ai2's open research, including the olmOCR-Bench benchmark and climate-focused models like HiRO-ACE. The collaboration aims to create an ecosystem where anyone can access, inspect, and experiment with AI tools, driven by Hugging Face's infrastructure and Ai2's open, science-focused approach.

title: AWS Awards 34 Research Grants for AI Innovation Using Trainium Chips
summary: AWS has announced 34 research grants under the Build on Trainium program, offering $110 million in compute credits to support AI innovation. The grants focus on responsible AI, including topics like safety, sustainability, and synthetic data. Recipients gain access to AWS resources, datasets, and expert support. The initiative aims to democratize AI research through academic collaboration. The program emphasizes scalable access to Trainium chips for large-scale AI projects, with examples from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and the University of Washington.

title: NIST Researchers Successfully Transmit Entangled Photons Over Noisy Aerial Fiber
summary: NIST researchers and collaborators demonstrated the transmission of entangled photons over 62 kilometers of noisy aerial fiber, a critical step toward building practical quantum networks. The experiment, conducted using existing fiber-optic infrastructure, showed that entangled states could be preserved despite environmental disturbances like temperature changes and wind. By employing real-time polarization stabilization techniques developed by Qunnect, the team achieved a 92.8% success rate in maintaining entanglement over 24 hours. While not breaking distance records, the study highlights the feasibility of quantum networking in real-world conditions. The findings suggest that quantum networks could one day enable secure communications, advanced scientific research, and powerful quantum computing applications.

title: Shieldstral: Policy-Adaptive Multimodal Safety Classifier Outperforms Larger Models
summary: Shieldstral, a 3B open-weights multimodal safety classifier, outperforms models up to 7x its size by framing content moderation as a policy-adaptive question-answering task. Unlike traditional guardrail models, it accepts plain-language policies at inference time, unifying text and image safety evaluation without retraining. Released under Apache 2.0, it delivers calibrated safety scores across diverse benchmarks while running efficiently on a single 16GB NVIDIA GPU. The model processes requests by framing them as binary question-answering tasks, with three components: an instruction defining safety criteria, a yes/no question, and the content to evaluate. This approach allows policies to be adapted at deployment time without retraining, offering flexibility across text, image, and multimodal content. Shieldstral was trained on heterogeneous data sources, calibrated for strictness, and fine-tuned using LoRA and SLERP merging techniques. It is part of the Open Secure AI Alliance and is available for download under Apache 2.0.

title: Meta Enhances GEM Training Efficiency with Custom Kernels and Low-Precision Techniques
summary: Meta has significantly improved the efficiency of its Generative Ads Recommendation Model (GEM), doubling end-to-end training efficiency to 20–25% Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU) while scaling training FLOPs 4x in 12 months. The company achieved this through a combination of compute and scaling efficiency innovations. Customized attention mechanisms, such as Jagged Flash Attention (JFA) and Generalized Dot-Product Attention (GDPA), were developed to handle the unique challenges of recommendation workloads, including jagged sequences and asymmetric attention patterns. Additionally, mixed ultra-low precision training, including MXFP8, was optimized to maintain model quality while improving performance. The approach also involved advanced parallelism strategies and network topology mapping to reduce communication overhead across thousands of GPUs. These efforts enabled Meta to achieve better GPU utilization and efficient scaling for its large-scale recommendation model.

title: Orchard framework enables scalable agentic AI with open-source tools
summary: The Orchard framework introduces an open-source solution for scalable agentic AI, designed to overcome infrastructure bottlenecks in research. It features Orchard Env, a Kubernetes-based environment service that supports multiple agent types and tasks without modification. The framework includes three domain-specific training recipes—Orchard-SWE, Orchard-GUI, and Orchard-Claw—demonstrating that small open-weight models can achieve strong results on complex tasks. Orchard-SWE reaches 69.7% on SWE-bench Verified using about 3 billion parameters, while Orchard-GUI achieves 68.4% across web navigation benchmarks. The project also provides training data and evaluation methods to aid the research community. By enabling training directly within real deployment harnesses, Orchard reduces the gap between research and practical application, allowing agents to be trained and evaluated in the same environments they will operate in.

title: Meta Develops Hierarchical Interest Representation for Deep Funnel Ad Optimization
summary: Meta is exploring Hierarchical Interest Representation (HIR) as an upstream layer to enhance deep funnel ad optimization. This system learns unified embeddings connecting users' inferred interests with advertiser offerings through a transformer-based graph learning approach. HIR integrates real-world knowledge with engagement signals, using multimodal content processed by LLMs to enrich sparse interactions and enable generalization to unseen entities. The model is trained on billions of ad interactions and aims to improve personalization, retrieval, and ranking across Meta's ads stack, including systems like GEM and Andromeda. HIR addresses challenges like sparse engagement signals and long-range relationships in large graphs by using dimension reduction, knowledge enrichment, and multi-hierarchical granularities. The architecture combines world knowledge with user engagement data, employing efficient attention mechanisms and cross-view distillation for training. Meta's online graph infrastructure supports both training and real-time serving, ensuring consistent data distribution and performance.

title: Studio offers centralized system for managing AI prompts and skills
summary: Studio provides a centralized system of record for managing AI prompts and skills, addressing the challenges of unmanaged, scattered assets in enterprises. The platform enables versioning, ownership tracking, and traceability, ensuring consistent AI behavior and compliance. By treating prompts and skills as production assets, Studio allows for fast iteration and controlled deployment, with features like immutable versions, rollback, clear ownership, and audit logs. It connects prompts to actual AI behavior through observability and telemetry, offering governance and visibility for compliance purposes. Available to Mistral Studio customers, the system aims to transform unstructured AI assets into trusted, governed components.

title: Google lets users instantly customize Discover feed with specific topic requests
summary: Google is introducing a new feature that allows users to instantly customize their Discover feed by specifying exact topics or links they want to see or skip. The update, available via a three-dot menu in the Discover feed, lets users describe their preferences directly to the chat. For example, users can request long-form content on smart home tech while skipping product news. The feature adjusts the feed immediately and remembers user preferences. It is set to roll out in the coming days on the Google app.

title: AI coding tools lead to addiction and burnout among developers
summary: A survey of 305 developers reveals that 80% find AI coding tools more addictive than helpful, leading to workaholism and burnout. Developers report spending late nights watching AI refactor code, receiving dopamine hits when the AI succeeds and adrenaline rushes when it fails. AI tools create a continuous feedback loop, making it hard to stop coding, with 43% continuing after hours and 39% struggling to switch off. While AI improves productivity, 74% of developers report increased workload and 51% face burnout. Trust in AI accuracy has dropped from 40% to 29%, with 45% frustrated by near-miss answers.
