He explained how voice commands control browser and application tasks, including opening websites, navigating pages, and managing code repositories. Hewitt emphasized setting strict permissions to mitigate risks like unintended actions and prompt injection. The demo highlighted the implications of delegating tasks to AI agents, prompting consideration of what users are comfortable entrusting to automation.

title: SQLite database acts as executable via ELF format
summary: A Linux technique allows a SQLite database to function as an executable by setting its application ID to SELF and organizing ELF components into tables. The self-exec interpreter extracts and runs necessary parts, while binfmt_misc enables kernel execution of this format. Farid Zakaria demonstrated this on NixOS, with a registration command provided for non-NixOS systems.

title: AI Prototyping Tax Hinders Roadmaps, Solutions Found
summary: The article discusses the challenges of implementing AI agents in production environments, identifying a 'prototyping tax' that slows down development. This tax arises from the inefficiencies in traditional R&D processes, which are not well-suited for AI agents. The key issue is the gap between conceptualizing an AI project and delivering a working prototype, leading to lost momentum and failed initiatives. The article highlights that the problem is not with the AI agents themselves but with the organizational setup. Teams that succeed are those that provide agents with a strong foundation in business semantics, enabling faster development cycles. By integrating governance and context into the development process, these teams reduce the time-to-prototype and increase the rate of production-ready solutions. The article also presents case studies showing how platforms like Databricks' Genie Code improve efficiency by understanding data schemas and governance models. The conclusion emphasizes that addressing the prototyping tax is essential for successful AI implementation, with measurable benefits in productivity and compliance.

title: AI Functions Enhance Data Warehouse Integration for Structured and Unstructured Data
summary: Databricks introduces AI Functions to integrate AI capabilities directly into data warehouses, enabling seamless processing of both structured and unstructured data. These functions allow analysts to perform tasks like sentiment analysis, classification, and translation within SQL queries, eliminating the need to move data to external AI environments. By embedding AI within the data warehouse, organizations can maintain governance and security while scaling AI workloads efficiently. Key functions include ai_parse_document for converting binary files to text, ai_extract for extracting specific data, ai_classify for categorizing text, and ai_query for general-purpose AI tasks. The integration streamlines workflows, reduces complexity, and enables real-time insights without disrupting existing data pipelines.

title: Researchers Propose Efficient Unlearning Framework by Identifying Low Influence Data Points
summary: Researchers challenge traditional unlearning methods by identifying data points with negligible impact on model outputs. They propose an efficient framework that reduces dataset size before unlearning, achieving up to 50% computational savings in real-world examples. The study compares influence functions across language and vision tasks to determine which data can be safely removed. This approach addresses growing data privacy concerns in machine learning.

title: OlmoEarth Studio enables custom embedding exports for Earth observation analysis
summary: OlmoEarth Studio now allows users to generate and export custom embedding vectors from Earth observation data, supporting a range of downstream tasks. These embeddings, derived from open-source foundation models, are lightweight and shareable as Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs. Users can configure parameters like area of interest, time span, and encoder variant to tailor embeddings for specific applications. The embeddings capture surface characteristics, enabling similarity search, segmentation, and unsupervised exploration. A simple linear classifier trained on a few labeled pixels can produce detailed land-cover maps, demonstrating the embeddings' rich representation. The platform also supports supervised fine-tuning for higher performance. The embeddings are computed on demand, reflecting current conditions, and can be used for change detection across time periods. The article includes examples of using embeddings for land-cover classification and visualization through principal component analysis.

title: ALTK-Evolve and ACE Compare Agentic Memory Approaches Without Compression
summary: Two agentic memory systems, ACE and ALTK-Evolve, avoid compressing an agent's learned lessons into summaries. Both store lessons as individual guidelines, but differ in how they deliver them. ACE provides a comprehensive playbook on every step, while ALTK-Evolve delivers a curated subset based on the model's capacity. On the AppWorld benchmark, ALTK-Evolve achieves comparable or better accuracy at lower token costs, especially for weaker models. ACE excels on easier tasks with its full playbook, while ALTK-Evolve outperforms on harder tasks through selective retrieval. The difference lies in delivery calibration, with ALTK-Evolve optimizing for model efficiency. Both systems emphasize retaining detailed lessons rather than distilling them into generic rules.

title: NVIDIA and Open Source Community Advance Local AI with New Models and Tools
summary: NVIDIA and the open source community are driving progress in local AI by releasing new models and tools that enable developers to build and run advanced agents on personal and edge systems. The company highlights several recent developments, including the Qwen3.8-27B model optimized for NVIDIA RTX GPUs, which supports fast local inference for coding tasks. Other models like Cosmos 3 Edge, MiniMax-H3, and DeepSeek-V4-Flash are also being made available, with support for NVIDIA hardware. NVIDIA is also enhancing its DGX Spark systems with new features like the Sync Cluster Assistant, which allows developers to cluster multiple systems for running larger models. Additionally, the release of Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion-parameter model optimized for local agentic workflows, is enabling always-on AI assistants for coding and data processing. These advancements are part of NVIDIA's ongoing efforts to support the open source ecosystem and empower developers with high-performance, local AI solutions.

title: NVIDIA Releases Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and NeMo Switchyard for Enhanced Agentic AI Systems
summary: NVIDIA has introduced Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model designed for high-volume, specialized tasks in agentic AI systems. The model offers up to 4x faster output speed and 30% faster task completion compared to similar models. It is open and customizable, allowing organizations to post-train it with their domain-specific data. Additionally, NVIDIA released NeMo Switchyard, an open-source library for intelligent model routing, enabling developers to direct requests to the most suitable model for each task. This reduces costs and improves efficiency across various industries. Partners like Boomi, Cadence, and LangChain have tested NeMo Switchyard, reporting significant cost reductions and performance improvements. Both tools are available on multiple platforms, enhancing deployment flexibility for enterprises.

title: Researchers train 1.7B-parameter flow model for efficient text generation
summary: Researchers trained a 1.7B-parameter flow model on 2.1T tokens and self-distilled it into a Categorical Flow Map (CFM) capable of generating high-quality text in just 4 inference steps. The model maintains near-data-level token entropy and achieves results comparable to discrete diffusion methods on standard language benchmarks. The study also introduces a likelihood bound for CFMs in the semi-discrete setting and identifies challenges in scaling these models, offering insights on loss weighting and time scheduling.

title: MIT Researchers Advocate for Federal Science Funding During Congressional Visit
summary: MIT students and postdocs participated in Congressional Visit Days, meeting with 62 congressional offices to advocate for sustained federal investment in scientific research. The event, organized by the MIT Science Policy Initiative, aimed to connect researchers with policymakers and demonstrate how scientists can engage in policy advocacy. Participants discussed both general science funding and specific policies related to their research areas, including AI, environmental science, and energy. The experience highlighted the importance of bipartisanship in supporting science and emphasized the need for researchers to engage with policymakers to shape future decisions.

title: MIT's PhysioNet database transformed from local research tool to global health data standard
summary: In 1975, MIT researchers and Boston’s Beth Israel Hospital began creating a medical database to store and share electrocardiogram recordings, aiming to facilitate collaboration in arrhythmia research. The project, which took years to complete, eventually became the foundation for PhysioNet, a global platform for clinical data sharing. By 1999, PhysioNet had evolved into a comprehensive repository hosting hundreds of databases, with over 15,000 scientific publications citing it and users from 180 countries. The platform's open-access model and emphasis on data sharing have influenced the development of similar systems like MIMIC and Health Data Nexus. As artificial intelligence advances, PhysioNet has expanded to include electronic health records, imaging data, and AI models, becoming a cornerstone for health-care AI research. Researchers and platform stewards envision further growth, including new tools for user contributions and interdisciplinary collaboration.

title: PyTorch Foundation Launches 2026 Flare Pin Design Contest
summary: The PyTorch Foundation has announced a design contest for the 2026 PyTorch Conference North America flare pin. The winning design will be produced as a 1-inch die-cut soft enamel pin and the entrant will receive a complimentary conference ticket. Submissions must include the official PyTorch Foundation symbol, the year 2026, and be suitable for a professional event. Entries must be original, use official assets, and follow brand guidelines. The contest requires participants to submit designs via social media platforms with specific hashtags, and includes rules about AI use, copyright, and eligibility. The winning design will be selected by the PyTorch Foundation Marketing Committee based on originality, legibility, and brand compliance.

title: Helion enables efficient TPU kernel authoring with autotuned pipelining
summary: Helion, a PyTorch DSL for ML kernels, now supports TPU v7 with a backend that compiles kernels to Pallas. The system autotunes pipelining strategies to optimize performance across different input shapes. On flash attention workloads, Helion achieves 838 TFLOPs, utilizing TPU's VMEM and compute units effectively. The approach allows non-experts to write kernels with PyTorch-style code, while maintaining performance comparable to Pallas. Helion's autotuner selects between pipelining and unrolling strategies based on input size, balancing VMEM usage and compute efficiency.

title: IBM Acquires HRL Laboratories to Advance Quantum Computing
summary: IBM has signed a definitive agreement to acquire HRL Laboratories, a research institution with a 80-year history of scientific innovation. The acquisition aims to accelerate IBM's quantum computing goals by leveraging HRL's expertise in silicon-spin qubit engineering. HRL is renowned for pioneering the laser, advancing semiconductor technology, and contributing to fields like ion propulsion and artificial intelligence. The lab has also developed key technologies such as memristors and quantum dot systems. Today, HRL continues research in quantum computing, materials science, and sensing technology, complementing IBM's own 80-year legacy in computing innovation.

title: Gemini 3.6 Flash and 3.5 Flash-Lite models introduced for improved efficiency and performance
summary: Google has introduced three new Gemini models: 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, and 3.5 Flash Cyber. The 3.6 Flash model offers 17% better token efficiency and improved performance in coding, knowledge work, and multimodal tasks, with a lower cost per token. 3.5 Flash-Lite is the fastest in the 3.5 series, delivering 350 output tokens per second and a strong price-to-performance ratio for high-throughput workflows. The 3.5 Flash Cyber model is designed for cybersecurity applications, combining a specialized model with CodeMender to detect and fix vulnerabilities efficiently. These models are available now through various platforms, with Gemini 3.5 Pro in testing and Gemini 4 in development.

title: Google Launches Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber for Cybersecurity
summary: Google introduced Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber, a lightweight cybersecurity model designed to detect and fix software vulnerabilities more efficiently than previous models. Built on 3.5 Flash, it is optimized for speed and affordability, making it suitable for large-scale code analysis. The model will be available through CodeMender to governments and trusted partners in a limited-access pilot program. Google claims it can handle complex codebases by analyzing multiple code paths, and benchmark tests show it performs competitively against larger models on the CyberGym benchmark.

title: Diffusion Models' Creativity Arises from Score Smoothing in Neural Networks
summary: Researchers from Google Research explain that the creativity of diffusion models stems from the 'score smoothing' effect in neural networks, which allows them to interpolate between training data points rather than merely memorizing them. The study, presented at ICLR 2026, shows that diffusion models generate novel data by learning a smoothed version of the score function, which drives the denoising process to create new samples. This phenomenon occurs because neural networks, due to regularization effects like weight decay, naturally learn smoother approximations of the perfect score function. The research demonstrates that this score smoothing enables diffusion models to explore the data manifold, producing realistic yet novel outputs. The findings suggest that the 'creativity' of these models is a predictable mathematical outcome of their learning process, offering insights into how to design more effective generative models that balance quality and innovation.

title: Turnstile captures token IDs for accurate reinforcement learning in agent interactions
summary: Researchers introduce Turnstile, a proxy tool that records exact token-level histories during agent interactions to improve reinforcement learning. By capturing token IDs at the moment of generation, Turnstile ensures accurate training signals for models. The tool works with existing agent harnesses without requiring changes, providing a framework-neutral trajectory for RL training. It addresses issues like retokenization drift and context mismatches, enabling stable learning for both text-only and multimodal agents.

title: SensorFM: Towards a general intelligence and interface for wearable health data
summary: Google Research introduces SensorFM, a foundation model trained on over one trillion minutes of sensor data from five million people. The model learns a general-purpose representation of human physiology, enabling transfer to 35 health prediction tasks. SensorFM addresses challenges in wearable health data by using self-supervised learning to handle missing and fragmented data, improving performance on both classification and regression tasks. The model's ability to generalize across multiple health domains and support label-efficient adaptation is demonstrated through extensive experiments. Additionally, SensorFM is integrated into a Personal Health Agent, showing significant improvements in generating personalized health summaries compared to baseline methods.

title: Flint enables AI agents to generate polished charts from simple specifications
summary: Flint is a visualization language designed to let AI agents create expressive, visually polished charts from simple, human-editable specifications. It leverages semantic data types to guide design choices like scales, formatting, and color schemes, reducing the need for detailed, error-prone manual configurations. The system automatically adjusts layouts and adapts to data changes, ensuring readability without explicit user input. Flint specifications can compile to multiple backends, including Vega-Lite, Apache ECharts, and Chart.js, enabling flexibility across visualization tools. The project includes the flint-chart library and a flint-chart-mcp server, allowing agents to create, validate, and render charts in chat or coding environments. In testing, Flint outperformed direct Vega-Lite generation methods, achieving higher scores with various LLMs. It is now used in Microsoft Research's Data Formulator project for AI-assisted data analysis.

title: MolmoAct 2 enables general-purpose robotic tasks through open-source model
summary: Binh Pham, a robotics software engineer, demonstrated MolmoAct 2's capabilities at a hackathon, showcasing its ability to perform tasks without specific training. The model, available open-source, allows users to inspect, adapt, and customize it with provided artifacts. Pham noted its strong spatial awareness and generalization, comparing it to the GPT-2 moment for robotics. The release includes model weights, data, training code, and fine-tuning scripts, enhancing reproducibility and development in the field.

title: Arvind Raman Appointed as NIST Director
summary: Arvind Raman was confirmed as the 18th director of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) by U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick. Raman, previously the John A. Edwardson Dean of Engineering at Purdue University, will lead NIST's efforts to foster innovation through collaboration with industry and academia. His research spans nanotechnology, biomechanics, and electronics manufacturing. NIST, celebrating its 125th anniversary, supports U.S. innovation and industrial competitiveness through standards and technology development.

title: DFM uses FlexOlmo to enable modular, privacy-preserving language models for Danish
summary: The Danish Foundation Models (DFM) project leverages FlexOlmo to create modular language models for the Danish language, allowing institutions to train on their own data without sharing it. FlexOlmo's modular structure enables independent training of specialized experts, but its large size limited scalability. Researchers at the University of Southern Denmark and Ordbogen A/S developed FlexMoRE, a smaller version of FlexOlmo that uses low-rank adapters to reduce memory demands while maintaining performance. This allows broader access to modular models, especially for organizations with privacy and governance constraints. FlexMoRE outperforms a full-size baseline with less than one-third the parameters, supporting distributed training without data sharing. The project aligns with Ai2's vision of open, decentralized AI development, and extends modular approaches into other stages of model training through projects like EMO and BAR.

title: Amazon develops tailored carbon intensity metrics for decarbonization
summary: Amazon is refining its carbon measurement methods to better track decarbonization progress across its diverse operations. The company tracks emissions per unit shipped, reducing carbon intensity by 39% since 2019. It also updated its economic carbon intensity metric to align with industry standards, using revenue instead of gross merchandise sales. Amazon emphasizes the need for sector-specific metrics and collaborates with suppliers to drive industry-wide decarbonization efforts.

title: SkillOpt enables trainable agent skills without model weight updates
summary: SkillOpt introduces a method to train agent skills as external parameters, avoiding model weight changes. The approach treats skill files as trainable elements, using a forward-backward-update cycle to optimize performance. Across six benchmarks, seven models, and three execution modes, SkillOpt achieves the best or tied-best results in all 52 evaluation cells. It maintains compact, auditable skills through bounded edits, validation gates, and rejected-edit feedback. The optimized skills transfer across model scales and tasks, suggesting they capture reusable workflow knowledge. SkillOpt improves performance without requiring model retraining, offering a lightweight alternative for domain adaptation in agent systems.

title: NIST and SRI Establish Quantum Manufacturing Center to Boost U.S. Industry
summary: The U.S. Department of Commerce’s National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has partnered with SRI International to create the Quantum Manufacturing Engineering Center (QMEC). This initiative aims to advance quantum research, development, and manufacturing capabilities, with an initial $20 million investment. The center will focus on scalable, high-performance quantum components and systems, supporting growth in areas like sensing, communications, and biomedicine. The partnership builds on a previous collaboration through the Quantum Economic Development Consortium (QED-C), which includes major U.S. quantum technology developers and users. NIST seeks to address manufacturing gaps and accelerate the commercial readiness of quantum technologies.

title: Meta Develops Ultra-Narrow Steel-Can Batteries for AI Glasses
summary: Meta's engineers developed ultra-narrow steel-can batteries to power smart glasses like the Ray-Ban Meta and Oakley Meta Vanguards. Traditional pouch cells were unsuitable due to their difficulty in shrinking and shaping. Steel-can cells, used in power tools and watches, were modified to achieve widths as narrow as 7mm. The design uses stacked layers instead of wound electrodes, reducing impedance and improving power delivery during peak demands. The 10mm-wide cells maintain a shape tolerance of 100 microns, enhancing energy density. Battery capacity increased from 160 mAh to 248 mAh across generations through system-level efficiency improvements. The Oakley Meta Vanguards feature dual batteries in temple arms, introducing challenges in power distribution and synchronization. Meta aims to scale this technology across its hardware portfolio and ensure supply resilience for future wearables.

title: Mistral partners with Airbus, BMW, and ASML to advance industrial AI solutions
summary: Mistral has partnered with Airbus, BMW, and ASML to develop an AI stack for industrial engineering, aiming to optimize design, simulation, and production while ensuring data security. The collaboration includes implementing AI in Airbus' operations, supporting BMW's Large Industry Model initiative, and tackling complex engineering challenges with ASML. Mistral also announced the acquisition of Emmi to enhance its offerings. The company introduced Vibe, an agentic AI tool for long-horizon tasks, and plans to open a 10 MW data center in France by 2026 to improve compute control and security.

title: Mistral Launches Vibe: Unified AI Agent for Work and Coding
summary: Mistral has introduced Vibe, a unified AI agent designed to handle both work and coding tasks. Vibe offers Work Mode for managing complex, multi-step tasks across enterprise tools and Code Mode for remote coding sessions. It integrates with platforms like VS Code and CLI, enabling seamless collaboration. Vibe is available in free, Pro, Team, and Enterprise plans, with features such as visible reasoning, reusable skills, and secure deployments. The agent can assist with inbox management, research, document drafting, and coding workflows from feature development to pull requests. Mistral highlights Vibe's ability to streamline workflows and improve productivity for both individuals and organizations.

title: Thomas Ptacek urges developers to create native UIs despite low cost of GUIs
summary: Thomas Ptacek argues for building native user interfaces for personal tools, as coding agents have made GUI development nearly cost-free. He shares his ongoing use of vibe-coded macOS task bar apps for bandwidth and GPU monitoring. Ptacek encourages developers to transition from CLI tools to native apps, claiming it changes their approach to software design.

title: OpenAI researcher outlines steps for AI safety amid industry concerns
summary: Miles Brundage, an AI policy researcher, outlines four steps for companies to prepare for potential AI slowdowns, following concerns about uncontrolled AI development. He highlights the need for independent audits of safety practices, participation in industry coordination groups like the Frontier Model Forum, investment in verification technologies for global AI guardrails, and support for legislation promoting safety and oversight. Brundage notes that while companies like OpenAI and Anthropic have experienced AI models escaping test environments, the US government should act swiftly. He argues that companies must take responsibility for safety, not just call for regulatory brakes, as current federal AI legislation remains lacking.

title: Dangote refinery boosts Nigeria's petroleum exports and self-sufficiency
summary: The Dangote refinery in Nigeria, operational since January 2024, has significantly increased seaborne petroleum product exports, with average shipments reaching 561,000 barrels per day in 2Q26, up from 79,000 b/d in 2023. Vortexa data shows exports rose to 350,000 b/d in 2Q26, compared to 46,000 b/d in 2023. The refinery's expansion in February 2026, increasing distillation capacity to 700,000 b/d, coincided with supply disruptions at the Strait of Hormuz, further boosting shipments. Nigeria's reliance on imports decreased, with seaborne imports falling to less than 130,000 b/d in 2Q26 from 400,000 b/d in 2023. The Dangote Group plans to double its refinery capacity by 2028.

title: Ukraine seeks more air defense as European leaders meet in Kyiv
summary: European leaders, including France's Macron, Germany's Merz, and Britain's Burnham, meet in Kyiv to discuss continued military support for Ukraine, focusing on air defense and long-term security. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy urges the European Parliament to approve legislation for 30 billion euros in funding to counter Russia's ballistic missiles. Norway pledges $9 billion in aid for Ukraine next year, while Estonia emphasizes the need for more air defense and sanctions against Russia. Zelenskyy warns of Russia's expanding missile production and highlights recent drone strikes on Russian logistics hubs. The Coalition of the Willing, led by the UK and France, includes 34 countries supporting Ukraine, with no U.S. representative confirmed for the meeting.

title: Tesla FSD v14 Lite Overlooks Log, Raises Concerns Over Hardware Limitations
summary: A Tesla owner posted dashcam footage showing his car running over a log at 32 mph without braking or slowing down while using Full Self-Driving (FSD) v14.1 Lite on a Hardware 3 vehicle. The incident, shared by X user @donvarri, highlights ongoing issues with Tesla's Lite version of FSD, which is designed to run on older, less powerful hardware. The video has garnered over 800,000 views and adds to a pattern of reported problems, including overheating, system disengagements, and erratic braking. Tesla introduced v14.1 Lite to address these issues, yet the log incident occurred on this supposedly improved build. The event underscores the limitations of Hardware 3, which lacks the processing power of newer models, and raises questions about the feasibility of delivering full autonomy to vehicles sold as 'full self-driving capable.' The owner emphasized that while he should have been paying attention, the car should have stopped for the obstacle, highlighting the growing complacency issue with Level 2 systems. The incident also reflects a broader concern about the mismatch between software capabilities and hardware constraints, with Tesla having admitted it has no clear plan to resolve this for its older vehicles.

title: Kazatomprom Sees Shift in Uranium Market as Demand Grows
summary: Kazatomprom's CEO, Meirzhan Yussupov, highlighted the growing demand for nuclear energy, driven by a pledge from 38 countries representing 70% of global GDP to triple nuclear power by 2050. He noted that uranium prices have reached an 18-year high and are stable, creating a strong foundation for long-term contracts. The company reported a 9% year-on-year revenue increase to KZT718 billion, attributing it to financial discipline and favorable market conditions. Yussupov emphasized the end of the 'cheap uranium' era and the need for secure, emission-free power. Kazatomprom has signed agreements with SNURDC and Uranium One for uranium sales, with details kept confidential. The company also announced amendments to Kazakhstan's Subsoil Use Code, affecting uranium mining licenses and exploration frameworks. Meanwhile, the TQZ sulphuric acid plant faces delays due to paleontological findings, pushing its commissioning date to 2027-2028 and potentially impacting production plans.

title: Russia's refineries resume operations amid fuel shortages
summary: Russia's Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak reported that some oil refineries have resumed operations after repairs, which could increase domestic fuel supply. The resumption follows drone attacks by Ukraine on Russian refineries, causing shortages for over three months. Russia has been importing fuel from South Korea and India to compensate for the losses. Diesel exports have dropped to a multi-year low as Moscow restricts exports to manage domestic shortages.

title: Sunrun partners with Voltus to supply flexible power for hyperscalers
summary: Sunrun, a residential solar and energy storage provider, has partnered with Voltus to support its Bring Your Own Capacity (BYOC) programs for AI hyperscalers. Under the agreement, Sunrun will provide energy capacity from its solar-plus-storage systems to deliver reliable power to the PJM and MISO grid regions. Voltus' BYOC program allows hyperscalers to access flexible capacity, with a recent three-year deal with Google involving 100MW of distributed energy resources. Sunrun's involvement marks its continued expansion in virtual power plant initiatives, following a previous partnership with Renew Home and Tesla that delivered over 16GW of flexible capacity.

title: Japanese survey shows cost savings outweigh disaster prep for solar-storage
summary: A survey by iChoosr found 48% of Japanese respondents cited cost reduction as the main reason for solar panels or home batteries, compared to 19% for disaster resilience. The survey of 14,478 people showed financial considerations dominate over disaster preparedness. As Japan's FIT contracts expire, households find it more economical to store and use their own solar power. Other surveys also show cost savings outweigh resilience concerns. The findings come amid Japan's transition from FIT schemes and growing residential solar demand.

title: SWIF Rack and National Roofing Partners collaborate on commercial solar projects
summary: Solar mounting technology company SWIF Rack has partnered with National Roofing Partners to support commercial solar installations. The collaboration allows NRP roofing professionals to inspect solar projects and maintain roofing warranties. SWIF Rack's products are compatible with various commercial roof types, and the partnership aims to provide building owners with reliable solar solutions. Both companies emphasize combining solar technology with roofing expertise to ensure structural integrity and clean energy performance.

title: California Energy Storage Director Addresses Safety Concerns and Project Milestones
summary: Scott Murtishaw, executive director of the California Energy Storage Alliance (CESA), highlights the challenges of local opposition and safety misconceptions surrounding energy storage in California. He notes that while the state has successfully implemented policies to support energy storage, recent fires at large-scale facilities have fueled public fear. Murtishaw explains that containerised battery energy storage systems (BESS) are inherently safer, as they prevent fire spread between units. He emphasizes the importance of communicating safety data and technological advancements to counter misinformation. CESA is collaborating with partners to provide clear, accessible information to address public concerns. Murtishaw also discusses how energy storage has significantly reduced the 'duck curve' challenge by storing solar energy for evening use, demonstrating its reliability benefits.

title: Learnewable's AI tool helps solar developers assess local opposition risks
summary: Learnewable, a startup founded in 2023, offers an AI-based platform to help solar developers assess risks from local opposition. The tool, called Site Scout, uses data from public records, news, and social media to generate scores on a five-point scale for sentiment and permitting ease. Developers can analyze specific locations, identify key stakeholders, and monitor evolving narratives. The platform covers over 3,000 U.S. counties and aims to reduce the need for consultants by providing actionable insights. Jeremy Solomon, founder, emphasized the platform's unique stakeholder identification algorithm as its key advantage.

title: PX Group and SoHHytec test solar-to-hydrogen system for industrial use
summary: PX Group and SoHHytec are demonstrating direct solar-to-hydrogen technology through an industrial project. The system uses solar concentration and photoelectrochemistry to produce hydrogen from water, bypassing traditional electrolysers. The project aims to test the technology’s reliability and scalability for industrial applications. SoHHytec’s CEO highlighted the potential for green hydrogen production on-site using solar energy. PX Group sees the project as an opportunity to explore alternative renewable hydrogen methods while contributing industrial expertise.

title: Tesla's Senior Chip Engineer Joins Competitor DensityAI
summary: Tesla has lost a senior chip engineer, Shishuang Sun, to DensityAI, a startup founded by former Dojo team members. Sun, who held the role of Senior Director of AI Hardware Design at Tesla, brings expertise in AI chip packaging and system integration, critical areas for Tesla's in-house silicon ambitions. His departure highlights ongoing talent drain as Tesla shifts focus to Nvidia for training compute, while DensityAI aims to develop AI hardware for automotive and industrial markets. Sun's specialized skills in turning chip designs into functional systems are vital for Tesla's upcoming AI5 and AI6 chips, which face production delays and manufacturing challenges. The loss underscores the competitive landscape in AI chip development and the strategic importance of experienced engineers in the field.

title: U.S. Solar Industry Faces Challenges from Sec. 232 Tariffs on Components
summary: The U.S. solar industry is grappling with the impact of Sec. 232 tariffs on polysilicon and its derivatives, which have raised costs for manufacturers. Jim Wood of SEG Solar notes that panel prices are increasing, making domestic modules less competitive. The tariffs, effective Dec. 4, 2026, aim to boost domestic manufacturing but have created a no-win situation for U.S. module makers without domestic cells. ES Foundry's CEO, Alex Zhu, highlights that the tariffs push costs too high for small cell manufacturers, leaving little margin. He argues that integrated facilities are more profitable, but current policies make it difficult. While some companies plan to expand domestic production, uncertainty remains about government incentives. Project developers like Arevon are adjusting procurement strategies, prioritizing supply reliability over cost, as the full effects of the tariffs are expected to take months to materialize.

title: Ho Chi Minh City Evaluates 6 GW Offshore Wind Project Viability
summary: Ho Chi Minh City is reviewing a feasibility study for a 6 GW offshore wind development. The study assesses technical, economic, and environmental aspects of the project. Local authorities aim to determine if the project aligns with regional energy goals. The initiative could contribute to Vietnam's renewable energy targets. Further details are expected in upcoming reports.

title: Enviromena starts construction of Longpasture Solar Farm in UK, targeting 2027 energisation
summary: Enviromena has begun building the Longpasture Solar Farm in County Durham, UK, its second-largest project, with energisation planned for autumn 2027. The project, acquired from Bluefield Solar and Lightrock Power, is expected to generate enough renewable electricity for 14,000 homes. It also includes ecological enhancements and a £100,000 community benefit fund, managed by Point North. Lee Adams of Enviromena emphasized the importance of community investment, while Point North's CEO highlighted local involvement in fund allocation.

title: Green Energy Stocks in India Show Mixed Performance Amid Market Volatility
summary: Indian stock markets declined on August 24, 2026, with the S&P BSE SENSEX and NIFTY 50 falling by 0.22% and 0.14%, respectively. The green energy sector showed mixed results, with Kabra Extrusion and Praj Industries rising over 8% and 1.9%, while companies like Websol Energy and Borosil Renewables fell by 2.5% and 2.1%. Major firms such as Tata Power and Adani Green Energy also saw declines. The session reflected selective interest in clean energy stocks amid broader market weakness.

title: Reactors installed on nuclear-powered icebreaker Leningrad
summary: The nuclear-powered icebreaker Leningrad has installed reactors weighing over 147 tonnes each. These pressurised water reactors, designed by Afrikantov OKBM, are part of the RITM-200 series with a thermal capacity of 175 MW. They are engineered to withstand 45-degree rolls and have a 40-year service life. The Leningrad is one of several Project 22220 icebreakers being built at the Baltic Shipyard, contributing to Russia's strategy to develop the Northern Sea Route.

title: US renewables capacity to rise 33% and 50% in 2025 despite Trump administration's opposition
summary: S&P Global Energy forecasts a 33% increase in US solar and 50% rise in wind capacity in 2025, defying Trump's policies. The administration's attempts to block green projects have been challenged in court, leading to payments of $4 billion to developers to abandon leases, with $1.22 billion going to RWE for offshore zones. Rising electricity demand from AI, electric vehicles, and data centers is driving the expansion, with ICF projecting a 39% increase in consumption by 2035. The expiration of clean energy subsidies is expected to raise power prices by 40-120%, incentivizing further investment in renewables.

title: Norway extends deadline for first commercial offshore wind farm licence application
summary: Norway has extended the deadline for submitting licence applications for its first commercial offshore wind farm. The extension aims to provide more time for stakeholders to prepare. The original deadline was set for early 2024. The move reflects the government's commitment to renewable energy development. The wind farm is expected to contribute significantly to Norway's energy goals.

title: Middle East to lead global gas processing capacity growth by 2030
summary: The Middle East is expected to account for over 40% of global gas processing capacity additions by 2030, according to the article. This growth is driven by major projects in Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Iran. The region's strategic location and abundant natural gas reserves are key factors. The article highlights the shift in global energy infrastructure investment. Analysts note the Middle East's role in meeting rising energy demand in Asia and Europe.

title: U.S.-Canada Energy Trade Value Drops 11% in 2025 Due to Lower Crude Oil Prices
summary: The value of U.S.-Canada energy trade fell by 11% in 2025 to $137 billion, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. Crude oil, accounting for 69% of the trade, saw a 16% decline in value due to lower prices and trade volumes. U.S. crude oil imports from Canada totaled $111 billion, while exports to Canada amounted to $26 billion. Canada remains the primary source of U.S. crude oil imports, with average daily imports of 3.9 million barrels. U.S. petroleum product exports to Canada increased by 6% in volume but decreased in value by 12%.

title: Coalition of 95 Groups Calls for Rejection of Clean Air Regulation Rollbacks
summary: A coalition of 95 organizations has urged Congress to reject four Congressional Review Act resolutions aimed at overturning Clean Air Act preemption waivers. These waivers set standards for vehicles and off-road engines that manufacturers have already complied with for years. The letter argues that these standards reduce fuel costs and improve air quality, especially as communities face high pollution levels. The groups call on lawmakers to vote against the resolutions, which they claim would hinder states' ability to protect public health. The letter is signed by health, environmental, and business organizations.

title: Entrepreneurs Influence State Policies Through Legislative Roles
summary: A study by Aaron Chatterji, Jorge Guzman, Joyce Ma, and Ryan C. McDevitt examines how entrepreneurs shape public policy through their legislative roles. Using data linking financial disclosures to bill sponsorship, the researchers identify entrepreneurs as legislators who own and manage firms. They find that entrepreneurs, making up over 40% of state legislators, disproportionately sponsor pro-entry bills focused on deregulation and innovation rather than broader pro-business measures. The study highlights how entrepreneurs influence policy environments for entrepreneurship within political institutions.

title: Payment Convenience and Deposit Behavior: Evidence from Zelle Rollout
summary: A study by Xu Lu, Yang Song, and Yao Zeng examines how payment convenience affects deposit behavior. Using transaction data, they find shorter transfer delays correlate with more transfers and lower deposit balances. By analyzing Zelle's staggered rollout, they show faster payments reduce delays and deposit growth. The research suggests transfer delays influence deposit demand, with effects varying by interest rates and consumption volatility.

title: Graduate job vacancies drop by almost 50% in a year, survey suggests
summary: Graduate job vacancies in the UK dropped by nearly 50% in a year, according to Adzuna, which reported 8,383 vacancies in July 2026 compared to 15,397 in July 2025. The firm noted increased competition, with 2.14 job seekers per vacancy. Employers cited rising costs and AI adoption as reasons for reducing entry-level roles. Adzuna highlighted a record low for graduate vacancies since 2016. The UK's youth unemployment rate stood at 16.2%, with over a million young people classified as Neet. A government review is underway to address the crisis, while some sectors like travel and teaching saw increased vacancies.

title: Grant Thornton Australia joins global advisory platform to expand Asia-Pacific operations
summary: Grant Thornton Australia has completed a transaction to join the Grant Thornton Advisors multinational platform, enhancing its Asia-Pacific operations. The integration adds six offices and 1,500 staff to the region, expanding on an existing 300-person workforce in New Zealand. The agreement, signed in April, follows a July deal to acquire CBIZ, which is expected to bring the platform to over two dozen countries with more than 35,000 professionals. Grant Thornton Australia CEO Said Jahani will now lead the Asia-Pacific region, reporting directly to CEO Jim Peko. The move aims to improve cross-border services, operational quality, and client relations across the region.

title: MP Materials Reports Strong Revenue Growth and Pentagon Support
summary: MP Materials reported a 89% year-over-year revenue increase to $108 million in Q2, with adjusted EBITDA turning positive at $28.5 million. The company received $17.6 million from the Pentagon for price-protection on NdPr, as market prices fell below the $110 per kilogram floor. MP is now selling more refined NdPr products, increasing profitability. The company shifted from selling rare-earth concentrate to processing it in-house, enhancing value. Analysts suggest the stock's recent decline may reflect valuation adjustments rather than underlying performance.

title: Algeria shifts from French to English in primary education amid diplomatic tensions
summary: Algeria's education ministry announced that English will replace French as the primary foreign language taught in third-year primary schools starting in 2026-2027. This marks a significant shift in the country's linguistic policy, ending French's long-standing dominance in schools. The decision is part of President Abdelmadjid Tebboune's broader linguistic overhaul, which includes transitioning university subjects from French to English. The move comes amid heightened diplomatic tensions with France, following its support for Morocco's Western Sahara claims. Critics argue the reform lacks sufficient resources and planning, particularly in teacher training. Meanwhile, public interest in English-language books is growing, reflecting a broader cultural shift. Despite these changes, French remains widely spoken, with over 15 million Algerians fluent in the language. The reforms also highlight a regional trend of former French colonies reevaluating their linguistic ties to Paris, as seen in Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso's recent departures from the Francophone organization OIF.

title: Netflix, Disney+, and Amazon raise prices in Western Europe more than any other region
summary: Research by Ampere Analysis shows that Western European subscribers of Netflix, Disney+, and Amazon Prime Video have faced the highest average price increases globally over the past three years, rising by $1.86. This surpasses the US increase of $1.70. Price hikes, driven by content production costs, have led to basic packages costing £5.99 and premium tiers £12.99 in the UK. While revenue for Netflix rose to £2.06bn, price increases have decreased as consumers reach payment limits. Ampere's Jaanika Juntson noted that streamers are diversifying monetization strategies as competition intensifies.

title: Typhoon Narra causes heavy rain and flooding in China and Vietnam
summary: Typhoon Narra has caused heavy rain and flooding in northern Vietnam and parts of southern China. Thousands have been displaced, and at least one person has died in northern Vietnam.

title: Analysis reveals £464m moved through 3,000 UK shell companies
summary: A new analysis by SmartSearch reveals up to £464m has moved through over 3,000 UK shell companies disguised as beauty and convenience stores, used for money laundering and terrorist financing. These companies, with an average lifespan of six months, are heavily concentrated in specific areas. The research highlights patterns of repeated incorporation and dissolution, with 83% of hairdressing and 92% of convenience store companies formed in the first two quarters and dissolved in the fourth. SmartSearch warns that the volume of such activity outpaces regulatory responses, with conservative estimates suggesting £310m to £464m passed through these companies alone.

title: Treasury Secretary Bessent to announce new sanctions against Iran
summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is set to announce new economic sanctions against Iran, framing them as the 'single greatest financial offensive ever.' President Trump has called the measures an 'economic D-Day,' targeting countries that provide economic support to Tehran. The Iranian Rial has dropped to a record low in anticipation. The sanctions aim to cut off financial lifelines to Iran, with particular criticism directed at China, Iran's largest oil buyer. Analysts question the effectiveness of additional sanctions, noting the U.S. has already targeted many key entities. Iran's security chief warned of 'seismic' retaliation, including attacks on oil tankers in the Persian Gulf. The sanctions are expected to worsen Iran's already dire economic situation, with inflation reaching nearly 90 percent and daily life becoming increasingly difficult for ordinary citizens.

title: Federal Reserve approves FS Bancorp's merger with Pacific West Bancorp
summary: The Federal Reserve Board has approved FS Bancorp, Inc.'s application to merge with Pacific West Bancorp, which would allow it to indirectly acquire Pacific West Bank. The approval was announced on August 4, 2026. Both FS Bancorp and Pacific West Bancorp are based in Washington and Oregon, respectively.

title: Federal Reserve approves Coastal Bend Bancshares' acquisition of First National Bank
summary: The Federal Reserve Board has approved Coastal Bend Bancshares, Inc.'s application to acquire First National Bank in Port Lavaca, Texas. The approval was announced on Tuesday, August 4, 2026. The decision allows the Corpus Christi-based company to proceed with the acquisition of the Port Lavaca bank.

title: Waller Discusses Monetary Policy Transmission and Forward Guidance
summary: Christopher J. Waller, a Federal Reserve official, discusses two key aspects of monetary policy transmission at a conference in Rome. First, he emphasizes the importance of initial conditions in assessing policy effects, using the 2022 U.S. inflation experience as an example. He argues that past models, which rely on historical averages, fail to account for nonlinear behavioral changes during large shocks. Second, Waller addresses forward guidance, noting its potential to accelerate policy transmission but warning that overly rigid guidance can hinder effectiveness. He cites the 2020 FOMC guidance as an example of how inflexible signals can delay necessary rate increases. Waller concludes that forward guidance should be flexible and used judiciously, as it is more art than science.

title: Fed Official Highlights AI Adoption by Small Businesses in Speech
summary: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa D. Cook emphasized the growing adoption of artificial intelligence by small businesses during her speech at the State of Small Business Symposium. She noted that nearly half of small employer firms use AI, with 71 percent reporting increased productivity. This finding challenges the notion that large firms have an advantage in AI deployment. Cook highlighted the Federal Reserve's Small Business Credit Survey (SBCS) as a critical tool for understanding small business financial conditions, including credit access and operational challenges. She praised the survey's expansion over the past decade, now capturing real-time data on AI usage and other emerging issues. The speech underscored the importance of small businesses in driving economic growth and innovation, with Cook encouraging researchers and policymakers to explore the survey's data for insights into credit access and business strategies.

title: Intuit Anticipates Strong Q4 Earnings with $3.59 EPS Forecast
summary: Intuit is set to release its Q4 2026 earnings on August 25th. Wall Street expects the company to report an EPS of $3.59, representing a 30.5% year-over-year increase, alongside revenue of $4.27 billion, up 11.5% from the previous year.

title: Subway Commute Shaped Understanding of Shared Humanity
summary: A personal account describes how daily subway rides in the Bronx during the 1970s fostered a deeper understanding of social inequality and human connection. The author recounts the physical and emotional challenges of commuting through a segregated city, highlighting exposure to poverty and diverse cultures. The experience contrasted with modern car-centric life, which limits interaction with others. The author notes that shared spaces like subways can reveal the realities of different lives, while car travel creates distance and reduces empathy. The narrative underscores how transportation choices shape social awareness and the importance of direct human contact in fostering empathy.

title: Article: Spooks Influence Foreign Policy and Regional Conflicts
summary: The article argues that Western intelligence agencies increasingly shape foreign policy, often through covert operations and misinformation. It suggests that NATO-Zionist infighting is a deliberate strategy to delay actions against Russia, Iran, and China, and that spooks, or intelligence operatives, are central to this process. The text references historical examples, such as the Minsk Agreements and the JCPOA, which were later revealed to be part of larger geopolitical strategies. It critiques US policy toward Israel and Türkiye, suggesting that reports of conflict are often misleading. The article also highlights the role of intelligence cooperation between the CIA, Mossad, and Turkish intelligence, and questions the official narratives surrounding recent tensions between Israel and Türkiye. The author implies that the real goal of these actions is to maintain Western influence and control over regional dynamics.

title: Article Covers Ferguson Debate, Niederhoffer Obituary, and AI Safety Discussion
summary: The article features a discussion between Niall Ferguson and Iain Banks, alongside an obituary for Victor Niederhoffer. It also touches on the flypaper effect in AI safety work, noting potential secondary consequences. The piece includes various links and opinions from different sources.

title: U.S. national debt surpasses $40 trillion as Congress debates solutions
summary: The U.S. national debt has crossed the $40 trillion threshold, raising concerns about fiscal sustainability. The debt now exceeds the size of the U.S. economy, with economists noting that the debt is growing faster than the economy. The government is using debt to fund current spending rather than long-term investments, according to labor economist Kathryn Anne Edwards. The debt increase stems from automatic spending increases, wars, and stimulus packages, alongside tax cuts that failed to boost economic growth sufficiently. Proposed solutions include spending cuts and tax increases, with Republicans favoring spending reductions and Democrats advocating for investments in social programs. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent acknowledged the difficulty of addressing the $2 trillion annual budget gap, highlighting the complexity of finding solutions that balance fiscal responsibility with political realities.

title: Americans' Social Time with Friends Shifts Away from Weekend Nights
summary: A study using data from 2003 to 2024 shows a decline in Americans' time spent with friends, particularly on Friday nights. Previously, social interaction peaked on weekend evenings, but this pattern has weakened since the mid-2010s. Friday nights now resemble typical weeknights, while Saturday remains elevated but less so than before. The overall reduction in social time suggests a broader decline in social interaction, without a shift in activity types. The study highlights a temporal reorganization of social life, marked by the fading of the 'night out' tradition.

title: England drops Carse from Test squad amid club incident investigation
summary: England has removed fast bowler Brydon Carse from the squad for the second Test against Pakistan following an investigation into an incident at a Derby club, the ECB stated. The Cricket Regulator confirmed it would probe events from Saturday night, with Carse unavailable for selection until the investigation concludes. Carse, who missed the first Test, will be replaced by Sonny Baker. Social media videos showed Carse in handcuffs with police, though no charges were filed. This follows previous investigations into Stokes and Atkinson after a nightclub incident, which found insufficient evidence. The ECB's regulator has been active amid ongoing scrutiny of England's conduct and culture.

title: Former snooker champion Dott convicted of historical sexual abuse
summary: Former snooker world champion Graeme Dott was convicted of sexually abusing two children in a Scottish court. The 49-year-old was found guilty of lewd behavior toward a girl between 1993 and 1996, and making sexual remarks and touching a boy between 2006 and 2010. Dott denied the charges but was convicted after a trial in Glasgow. He will face sentencing next month. Police Scotland described him as a dangerous individual. Dott, who won the 2006 world championship, was suspended by the World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association following the charges.

title: Trump threatens 50% auto tariffs on Canada starting 2027
summary: US President Donald Trump announced plans to increase tariffs on Canadian vehicles and automotive parts to 50% starting January 1, 2027, following the collapse of trade negotiations with Canada. The move comes after the Trump administration imposed 50% tariffs on select Canadian goods, which took effect after talks failed. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney condemned the tariffs, calling them an 'attack' and announcing retaliatory measures. He criticized the US for using 'economic integration as a weapon' and accused Washington of making unacceptable demands. Trump's threat marks a significant shift from the traditionally cooperative US-Canada trade relationship, with both nations facing economic and political repercussions from the escalating trade dispute.

title: Ontario Premier Threatens to Cut Electricity and Critical Minerals to U.S. Over Trade Dispute
summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford warned that Canada should be prepared to cut off electricity and critical minerals to the United States if trade tensions escalate. Ford criticized President Donald Trump's trade policies, comparing them to Ronald Reagan's stance against protectionist tariffs. He emphasized Canada's willingness to endure economic pain rather than yield to U.S. pressure. Ford also highlighted the strategic importance of critical minerals to U.S. national security and suggested using oil and potash as leverage. The dispute intensified after the U.S. imposed 50% tariffs on Canadian goods, prompting Canada's retaliatory measures. Ford accused Trump of seeking to weaken Canadian industries, particularly in the auto sector, which is vital to Ontario's economy. He also revealed opposition to a preliminary trade deal and expressed skepticism about Trump's demands for U.S. approval in future negotiations.

title: Venice Film Festival includes Gaza documentary 'NAZA' in competition
summary: The Venice Film Festival has added the documentary 'NAZA' to its competition lineup, focusing on the civilian impact of the Israel-Hamas war. Directed by Israeli filmmakers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, the film was produced by The Guardian and others. 'NAZA' is the only documentary competing for the Golden Lion award. The film builds on reporting from 2023 to 2025 by various outlets. The festival, starting on Sept. 2, will announce winners on Sept. 12. Earlier this year, the Venice Biennale's Israeli pavilion remained closed due to Gaza-related protests.

title: Trump threatens 50% tariffs on Canadian vehicles and steel after trade talks collapse
summary: Donald Trump has threatened to impose 50% tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks, auto parts, and steel, effective 1 January 2027, following the collapse of trade negotiations with Ottawa. The president criticized Canada on Truth Social, claiming the country 'needs us' and accusing it of being 'among the worst Nations in the World to deal with.' Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney rejected the latest deal, calling Trump's demands 'too much and offered too little,' and vowed 'dollar for dollar' retaliation. The current tariff on Canadian automobiles and parts stands at 25%. The trade dispute comes amid other developments, including New Mexico's plans to continue funding gender-affirming care for minors and the U.S. Treasury's upcoming announcement of new Iran sanctions.

title: Trump Threatens 50% Tariff on Canadian Autos and Steel Starting January 1
summary: President Donald Trump threatened to impose a 50% tariff on Canadian automobiles, car parts, and steel starting January 1, 2027, as trade tensions with Canada escalated. The announcement followed the collapse of recent trade talks between the U.S. and Canada. Long-planned U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods had already taken effect after the talks ended, prompting Canada to vow retaliation. Trump criticized Canada's high tariffs on American farmers, calling them unsustainable and stating they would no longer be tolerated.

title: Tunisian protests follow migrant boat disaster near Ben Guerdane
summary: Protesters in Ben Guerdane, Tunisia, erupted after a boat carrying 15 migrants sank off the southeastern coast, killing 14 and leaving two missing. The incident sparked road blockades and tire burning, with search operations ongoing. Fourteen victims were from Ben Guerdane, a marginalized city near Libya. The area has seen similar tragedies, including a 2022 boat disappearance that led to weeks of protests. The central Mediterranean route remains the deadliest for migrants, with over 900 deaths or disappearances reported this year. Despite a 2023 EU-Tunisia agreement aimed at reducing irregular migration, dangerous crossings persist, particularly from southern coastal areas like Zarzis, where families continue to search for missing relatives.

title: Ontario Premier Threatens to Cut Electricity and Critical Minerals to U.S. Over Trade Dispute
summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford warned that Canada could cut off electricity and critical minerals to the United States if trade tensions escalate. Ford criticized President Trump's trade policies, comparing them to the economic warfare Reagan opposed. He emphasized Canada's willingness to endure economic pain rather than yield to U.S. pressure. Ford also mentioned using oil and potash as leverage, citing the strategic importance of critical minerals to U.S. national security. The auto industry, central to Ontario's economy, faces new tariffs from Trump, intensifying the dispute. Ford opposed a preliminary trade deal and expressed readiness to break with it, highlighting concerns over Canadian sovereignty. Despite the conflict, Ford urged continued negotiations.

title: Trump threatens 50% tariffs on Canadian auto imports
summary: President Trump announced plans to impose a 50% import tax on Canadian cars and auto parts starting in 2027, accusing Ottawa of unfair tariffs on U.S. farm products. The move comes as Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney criticized the shifting justifications for tariffs and warned of potential energy supply retaliation. Carney noted that U.S. energy imports from Canada are substantial, with 99% of natural gas and 85% of electricity coming from Canada. He stated that Trump's negotiators had pushed for terms that were 'uneconomic, unfair,' undermining potential trade benefits.

title: Ukraine's Zelenskyy vows defiance as UK pledges military support amid Russian threats
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy marked Independence Day with a defiant speech, vowing Ukraine would not surrender to Russian aggression despite ongoing war. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged continued support for Kyiv, including access to classified technology for producing long-range missiles. The UK announced it would allow Ukraine to use European SCALP cruise missiles, prompting Russian condemnation. Zelenskyy called for more air defense systems to counter Russian missile attacks, citing a $27 billion defense funding gap. He also warned of potential Russian troop mobilization later this year. Ukraine has made progress in halting Russian advances but faces shortages of anti-ballistic missiles, which Russia exploits to strike cities. The country has also launched attacks on Russian infrastructure, including drone strikes on Ozon logistics hubs. Zelenskyy honored fallen soldiers and announced the return of 10 missing servicemen through a prisoner exchange with Russia.

title: Europol reports rise in violent museum heists involving weapons and explosives
summary: Europol reports a growing trend of violent museum heists in Europe, with thieves using guns, axes, and explosives. The agency notes a shift from non-violent to forceful methods, suggesting new criminal networks targeting cultural artefacts. Precious metals and ancient Chinese porcelain are preferred due to their high value and ease of sale. Recent cases include a 2025 heist at the Louvre, where thieves smashed display cases and stole jewellery worth €88m. Europol warns of potential recruitment of low-level thieves for such crimes.

title: Trump administration proposes $103,265 fee for H-1B visas amid legal challenges
summary: The Trump administration has proposed a $103,265 fee for new H-1B visas, a significant increase from previous costs. The rule, which aims to make the visa program more expensive, was initially imposed in 2025 but blocked by courts. The proposed regulation, set to undergo a 30-day public comment period, could be finalized by year's end. Critics argue the fee violates existing law, while the administration claims it falls under presidential authority to restrict entry. Legal challenges from the U.S. Chamber of Commerce and Democratic-led states continue, questioning the legality of the fee and the Department of Homeland Security's authority to impose it.

title: Kenyan anime fans create elaborate costumes from recycled materials at Nairobi convention
summary: Thousands of Kenyan anime and manga fans gathered in Nairobi for the Otamatsuri convention, showcasing costumes made from recycled materials. Organizers reported over 4,000 attendees, highlighting the growing popularity of Japanese pop culture. Cosplayers like Julius Mokaya use cardboard and other affordable materials to create intricate outfits, emphasizing creativity and affordability. Yvonne Chockey won the costume competition by crafting detailed wings from PVC pipes. The event fosters a community for like-minded individuals, despite some cultural misunderstandings. Cosplay represents more than fashion for participants, embodying craftsmanship and cultural expression.

title: Canada and allies resume coordinated stance after trade discussions with Trump end
summary: Canada and its allies have re-established a unified position following the collapse of trade talks with Trump. The group had previously coordinated efforts to counter Trump's policies. The failed negotiations led to a shift in diplomatic strategy. Allies expressed concerns over trade practices during the discussions. The situation highlights ongoing tensions in international trade relations.

title: Israel Threatens Escalation Over Kite Incidents from Gaza
summary: Israel has warned Hamas of increased strikes on Gaza following the discovery of kites, drones, and balloons launched from the territory. These kites, not carrying explosives, were found in Israeli communities near the Gaza border, prompting Defence Minister Israel Katz to vow 'forceful actions' to stop the activity. Hamas denied responsibility, calling the kites 'children's toys' and accusing Israel of using the incidents as a pretext for continued attacks. The Israeli military believes Hamas may have tested its response to such threats, though no explosives were found. Meanwhile, Israeli strikes in Gaza resulted in casualties, with the military claiming to have targeted Hamas operatives. The conflict, which began after the October 7 attack, has caused significant civilian casualties in Gaza.

title: France seeks benefits from Saudi Vision 2030 investment plan during Paris talks
summary: French President Emmanuel Macron is meeting Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Paris. The discussions focus on the Middle East situation and France's potential to benefit from Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 investment program. The talks are described as rare, highlighting the strategic importance of the engagement.

title: Iranian Protester Describes Security Forces Shooting to Kill During 2026 Crackdown
summary: In January 2026, Iranian security forces used live ammunition and automatic weapons to suppress large-scale protests against the regime, according to a human rights physician. Massoud, a protester injured by pellets and gunfire, died months later due to untreated wounds, highlighting the lack of medical care for victims. Doctors report that many protesters suffered severe injuries to the head, chest, and limbs, with some cases indicating intentional killing. Security forces also used knives and machetes when ammunition ran out. Victims, fearing retaliation, avoided hospitals, leading to preventable deaths and long-term disabilities. A 32-year-old woman, Mahla, was shot while trying to get her son out of a protest, leaving her unable to work. Teenagers like Ashkan, who lost an eye and a leg, face lifelong disabilities and lost their professional futures. The regime continues to prosecute and execute those linked to the protests, with at least 56 executions since March 2026 on national security charges.

title: France's potato yield drops 23% to lowest in 30 years due to drought
summary: France's potato production is projected to decline by at least 23% from last year, marking the lowest yield in over three decades, due to heat waves and severe drought. The National Union of French Potato Producers reported a drop from 43.5 tonnes per hectare in 2025 to 34.5 tonnes this year. The decline follows a 10% reduction in potato-growing areas in France and 11% across northwestern Europe. The industry estimates nearly €400 million in economic losses, with concerns over rising consumer prices. The government is preparing a comprehensive plan to support farmers, including emergency cash flow assistance and regulatory exemptions, though aid amounts remain unspecified.

title: Washington Post ordered to reinstate columnist fired over comments on killing of conservative activist
summary: An arbitrator ruled the Washington Post wrongfully fired Karen Attiah, an opinion columnist, over her social media comments following the assassination of conservative activist Charlie Kirk. The decision stated the Post lacked 'good and sufficient cause' for the termination, violating its labor agreement. Attiah was dismissed in September 2025 for remarks defending her refusal to engage in performative mourning for Kirk. She argued her posts were part of her work as an opinion writer and challenged the dismissal under the newspaper’s labor agreement. The Post claimed her comments damaged its 'integrity' and breached social media civility standards.

title: Myanmar's Rohingya refugees face uncertain future amid ongoing conflict and camp crises
summary: Myanmar's military-backed government continues to discuss repatriating Rohingya refugees from Bangladesh, but analysts say safe return is unlikely due to ongoing civil war, lack of citizenship, and security risks. Over 820,000 Rohingya names were submitted for verification, but only 308,000 were confirmed as former residents. The UN and Gambia have accused Myanmar's military of genocide, while the Rohingya are denied citizenship and face violence from both the military and ethnic groups in Rakhine State. In Bangladesh, Rohingya refugees in camps face worsening conditions, including food shortages, overcrowding, and rising insecurity, leading to increased risky migration and social issues like child marriage. International aid remains insufficient, with only 60% of needed funds secured for 2026.

title: White police officer convicted of killing Sonya Massey dies in prison at 32
summary: Sean Grayson, a white police officer convicted of second-degree murder in the 2024 killing of Sonya Massey, died in prison at 32. Grayson shot Massey during an altercation at her home in Illinois after she reported a suspected intruder. He claimed he fired because he believed she was about to throw boiling water on him. Grayson, who was diagnosed with colon cancer, was sentenced to 20 years in prison. His death, confirmed by his lawyer, has drawn mixed reactions from Massey's family and legal representatives. The incident sparked protests and drew comments from former President Joe Biden.

title: Chess remains popular despite declining attention spans and digital distractions
summary: Chess continues to captivate millions globally despite growing concerns about declining attention spans and reliance on digital shortcuts. The game is increasingly used as an educational tool and mental exercise, supported by research showing its benefits for cognitive and emotional development. High-profile figures like Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and soccer players Erling Haaland and Unai Simón are among its devotees. The International Chess Federation (FIDE) has 203 member federations, while online platforms like Chess.com report over 250 million user accounts. The game's complexity, with more possible moves than atoms in the universe, and its historical and cultural significance across fields like AI and international politics, contribute to its enduring appeal. Despite challenges like the Spanish Inquisition's bans and gender imbalances, chess remains a vital part of global culture, with Spain leading efforts to integrate it into education and therapy programs.

title: Ukrainian Ex-Defense Minister's Election Call Faces Limited Support
summary: Ukrainian former defense minister Andriy Fedorov has called for early elections, but the proposal has received limited support. The article notes that the call for elections has not gained significant traction among political figures. Fedorov's initiative is seen as a potential move to address political instability. The article highlights the lack of widespread backing for his proposal. The situation reflects ongoing challenges in Ukraine's political landscape.

title: Essendon Appoints Mark McVeigh as New Coach
summary: Essendon has appointed Mark McVeigh as its new coach, effective immediately, following a unanimous board decision. Club president Andrew Welsh announced the move. The team concluded its worst season in history with a 10-point loss to Port Adelaide.

title: Chiikawa's Animated Film Surpasses ¥10 Billion at Japanese Box Office
summary: Chiikawa's animated film 'The Secret of Mermaid Island' has exceeded ¥10 billion in box office revenue in Japan, 30 days after its July 24 release. The movie, based on a web series by Nagano, attracted 7.66 million viewers and opened with ¥990 million, the seventh-largest debut in Japan's box-office history. The film's success has led to expanded theatrical experiences, including 4DX screenings, interactive singalongs, and glow-stick events starting in September.

title: Kim Jong-un leverages strategic alliances with Trump, Putin, and Xi
summary: Kim Jong-un has positioned North Korea as a strategic asset for the U.S., Russia, and China by offering each nation different benefits. Trump seeks renewed dialogue, Putin relies on North Korea's military support in Ukraine, and Xi Jinping has re-engaged with Pyongyang after years of isolation. Analysts note that Kim's influence stems from exploiting opportunities rather than a grand strategy. The U.S. recently reduced military exercises with South Korea, a move seen as a concession to North Korea. North Korea has supplied millions of artillery shells and thousands of troops to Russia, enhancing its role in the war. China, while still North Korea's main ally, has been pressured to adjust its policies due to the growing Russia-North Korea partnership. Kim's nuclear arsenal now serves as a tool for international influence, and Trump's approach may open new negotiation avenues. Analysts suggest Kim is willing to wait for favorable conditions before engaging with the U.S.

title: U.S. Announces Economic Measures Against Iran as Canada Imposes Tariffs
summary: The U.S. Treasury Secretary, Scott Bessent, is set to announce new economic pressures on Iran, aiming to push the country back into negotiations. President Trump described the measures as an 'economic D-Day,' while Iran's security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, warned of a 'seismic' retaliation. The sanctions are expected to worsen economic conditions in Iran, with reports of rising inflation and unaffordable medicines. Meanwhile, Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney announced retaliatory tariffs on U.S. imports starting September 8, following the Trump administration's 50% tariffs on Canadian goods. The trade dispute has led to the collapse of U.S.-Canada negotiations, with the new tariffs affecting only about 5% of bilateral trade.

title: France eyes ‘Dragon Ball’ theme park deal during Saudi crown prince visit
summary: French officials expressed hope that a Dragon Ball-themed amusement park, backed by a Saudi investment fund, will be signed during Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's visit. Valerie Pecresse, head of the Ile-de-France region, noted the project had been in development for 18 months. The agreement is expected to be finalized during a meeting at the Elysee Palace. A Saudi investment company is reportedly behind the project, which could be located in Courdimanche. Discussions on multiple economic agreements are ongoing ahead of the strategic partnership council meeting.

title: Farmers protest Kabini dam water release to Tamil Nadu
summary: Hundreds of farmers in Karnataka marched to the CADA office, demanding an immediate halt to water release from the Kabini dam to Tamil Nadu. Organized by the Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha, the protest highlighted concerns over water allocation for standing crops. Farmers accused the government of prioritizing Tamil Nadu and Bengaluru over local agriculture, citing the dam's construction as a sacrifice of over 20,000 acres of land and 33 tribal settlements. The leader, Badagalapura Nagendra, warned of intensified protests if water was not released for irrigation.

title: KNRUHS publishes provisional merit list for MBBS and BDS admissions under Competent Authority quota
summary: The Kaloji Narayana Rao University of Health Sciences (KNRUHS) in Telangana has released a provisional merit list for MBBS and BDS admissions under the Competent Authority quota for 2026-27. The university also listed ineligible candidates on its website. Candidates are urged to verify their details and check for discrepancies in the lists. Grievances must be submitted by August 26. After reviewing all complaints, KNRUHS will publish the final merit list, seat matrix, and counseling instructions.

title: TMC seeks Supreme Court intervention over delay in disqualification of 20 rebel MPs
summary: Trinamool Congress (TMC) general secretary Abhishek Banerjee has filed a petition with the Supreme Court, urging an expedited decision on disqualification pleas against 20 MPs accused of defecting to the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI). The case, scheduled for hearing on August 25, challenges the delay in resolving the petitions. The TMC argues that the MPs' alignment with NCPI constitutes a voluntary exit from the party, violating anti-defection laws. The rebel MPs claim their move represents a valid merger.
