The bank had initially activated a backup service, Monzo Stand-in, to allow transactions, but some users reported it was not functioning as expected. A spokesperson stated all services are now operational. The digital bank, founded in 2015, serves over 16 million customers globally. While the backup service works for some, others continue to experience problems with card functionality.

title: Mojo programming language transitions to open source
summary: The Mojo programming language, which initially aimed to be a superset of Python, has officially released its compiler and toolchain under an Apache 2 license. The open source release follows the 1.0 version launch and fulfills a promise made in May 2023. While Mojo may no longer aim to be a full Python superset, it remains optimized for GPU programming with Python-inspired syntax. The language's evolution reflects confidence in AI-assisted migration tools and future ecosystem development.

title: Three ex-SpaceX engineers launch AI-driven steel factory to automate infrastructure components
summary: Three former SpaceX engineers have founded 1872, a startup aiming to automate steel fabrication using AI and robotics. The company, based in Cincinnati, Ohio, plans to establish a prototype factory by 2027 focused on producing steel skids for modular buildings, AI data centers, and nuclear reactors. CEO Dan Summers emphasized a goal of achieving 80% autonomy, noting diminishing returns for full automation. The initiative addresses a growing shortage of skilled labor, with the American Welding Society projecting a need for 320,500 new welders by 2029. The Trump administration's immigration policies are also limiting workforce options for welding-intensive industries.

title: Amazon linked to rare book destruction for AI training via tracked Airtag
summary: A hidden Airtag in a rare book traced to Amazon's AI training facility in Las Vegas suggests the company is destroying books to scan their content for AI training. 404 Media reports that the tag was found in a book part of a bulk order and tracked to a warehouse with a T. rex logo symbolizing book destruction. Amazon declined to comment, stating it purchases books to improve customer products, though it is developing frontier AI models requiring unique training data.  Rivals like Anthropic and xAI do not use rare books for training.

title: Software Engineers Transition to Orchestrators as Systems Become Autonomous
summary: The article discusses the emergence of the role of 'orchestrator' in software engineering, replacing traditional developers. Orchestrators oversee systems that autonomously handle tasks previously done by teams, focusing on coordination rather than coding. They manage delegated intelligence systems, ensuring accountability and guiding autonomous agents. The role requires generalist expertise, with orchestrators acting as experts who understand end-to-end software development. The author shares personal experience with using AI tools to rapidly develop a DRM system, highlighting the shift from writing code to orchestrating systems. The article argues that while anyone can use AI tools, delivering scalable and secure systems requires human oversight, emphasizing the need for certified orchestrators in critical areas. It concludes that the role of orchestrator demands extensive training, akin to professions like medicine or law, to ensure reliability and accountability in autonomous systems.

title: AI-Generated Code Requires Dynamic Specifications to Stay Relevant
summary: The article discusses the challenges of maintaining documentation when AI rapidly generates code. As AI systems create code quickly, traditional specifications often become outdated, leading to a disconnect between the code and its documentation. The author argues that specifications should not be permanent natural-language descriptions but rather dynamic, change-focused documents that guide the next iteration of a feature. These 'change briefs' should capture the delta between current and desired states, including constraints, acceptance criteria, and risks. The author emphasizes that code itself is the ultimate specification, as it reflects actual behavior, while natural language specifications are prone to obsolescence. The piece also highlights the importance of durable artifacts like schemas, policies, and tests, which provide more reliable context than prose. The author advocates for lightweight, context-driven documentation that supports AI-assisted development without becoming a burden, and suggests that judgment and human oversight remain critical in defining the scope and direction of changes.

title: Lyten Acquires Morrow Batteries' Assets to Expand in Norway
summary: US-based lithium-sulphur battery company Lyten has acquired the assets of Norway's bankrupt Morrow Batteries, aiming to preserve jobs and continue battery production in Arendal. The deal, valued at NOK 8 million, involves the bankruptcy estates of Morrow's subsidiaries and state-owned Innovation Norway. Lyten, which previously acquired Northvolt's assets, plans to establish an industrial hub integrating battery manufacturing and other energy-related activities. The acquisition follows a competitive bidding process and aims to secure hundreds of jobs, with 70 already retained.

title: Gentari launches 243 MWp solar and 172 MW BESS project in NSW
summary: Gentari has started construction on the Maryvale Solar & Energy Storage project in New South Wales, combining 243 MWp solar with 172 MW/409 MWh battery storage. The project, expected to supply 82,000 homes and avoid 411,788 tonnes of annual emissions, is supported by a Long-Term Energy Service Agreement. It will create up to 360 jobs and use a DC-coupled design to enhance renewable energy utilization. The project is being developed by PCL Construction and uses Trinasolar modules and CATL Australia's BESS system.

title: CATL's Tener S BESS expands with 6.017 MWh capacity
summary: CATL has expanded its battery energy storage system (BESS) offerings with the Tener S, a 6.017 MWh liquid-cooled system. The product, also called EnerS, is designed for two-hour applications and operates at 1,500 V. It provides higher capacity than previous models like the EnerC and EnerC Plus. The Tener S fits in a 20-foot container and weighs 45 metric tons. Specifications show it can deliver up to 3.01 MW of power for two hours, with zero degradation and an IP55 rating.

title: Mozambique-Malawi Power Interconnector Approaches Commercial Use
summary: The high-voltage power transmission interconnector between Mozambique and Malawi is nearing commercial operations after completing initial testing. The 218-kilometer, 400-kilovolt line connects Matambo substation in Mozambique to Phombeya substation in Malawi, enabling electricity sharing. Malawi, which relies heavily on hydropower, will gain access to regional electricity trading through the Southern African Power Pool. The project, supported by the World Bank, aims to improve energy security and allow Malawi to import up to 200 MW of electricity from Mozambique, while also creating future export opportunities.

title: India's Crude Import Costs Rise Amid Hormuz Route Disruptions
summary: India's crude oil import costs have increased significantly due to rising shipping rates and war-risk insurance following the Iran war. Freight rates on the key route from Saudi Arabia to India surged over 400% since the war began, with VLCC rates reaching $4.34 per barrel. War-risk insurance for Hormuz voyages also rose to up to $10 million. Brent Crude prices increased by 25%, contributing to a 60% rise in India's import bill for the April-June quarter compared to the same period last year.

title: Ørsted Awards Baltica 2 Helicopter Medevac Contract
summary: Ørsted has awarded a helicopter medical evacuation contract to Baltica 2. The agreement covers emergency transport services for workers at the offshore wind farm. The contract includes provisions for rapid response and specialized medical support. The move aims to enhance safety and operational efficiency at the project site. The terms of the contract were not disclosed by the company.

title: Oman's PWP launches feasibility study tender for renewable energy in Musandam
summary: Oman's Nama Power and Water Procurement Company (PWP) has initiated a consultancy tender for a feasibility study on renewable energy in Musandam. The selected consultant will evaluate solar PV, wind, hybrid systems, and battery storage. Tender documents are available until September 3, with a fee waived for small and medium-sized enterprises. The deadline for applications is September 24. This follows PWP's recent tenders for solar projects and plans for a 6 GW solar cell and module facility.

title: Japan Maintains Oil Reserve Status Quo Amid Import Decline
summary: Japan's economy minister announced no new oil reserve releases despite a projected September import drop. Oil imports are expected to fall to 80% of the 2025 monthly average, down from August's 100%. The decision follows rerouting of tanker traffic to avoid Red Sea risks. Akazawa noted that some reserves remain unused due to alternative supply progress. Japan had previously released 80 million barrels in March to address supply issues, but now prioritizes diversification, increasing import costs to a July record of $89.46 billion.

title: UK government funds £28 million for ultra-long duration energy storage projects
summary: The UK government has launched a £28 million grant program to support energy storage technologies capable of storing and discharging energy for over 100 hours. The initiative, announced by the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade and others, aims to enhance energy security, create jobs, and lower energy bills. It follows the June selection of 16 projects totaling 7,645MW, which will provide storage for 8-22 hours. The new funding targets longer-duration solutions needed as solar and wind energy become more prevalent in the energy mix.

title: MacGregor Obtains DNV Certification for Floating-to-Floating Personnel Transfers
summary: MacGregor has secured DNV certification for its floating-to-floating personnel transfer system. The certification validates the system's safety and compliance with industry standards. The company stated the approval enables operational readiness for offshore operations. The system facilitates safe movement between offshore platforms. This development supports MacGregor's expansion in maritime solutions.

title: Ohio officials face challenge of fake comments in clean energy projects
summary: Public officials in Ohio are dealing with a growing issue of fabricated comments aimed at blocking renewable energy projects and promoting fossil fuels. Advocates argue that these fake comments undermine democratic processes by skewing public decision-making. The Crossroads Solar Grazing Center, a 94-megawatt solar project, faced rejection by the Ohio Power Siting Board, which cited substantial opposition, though the developer claims many comments were fabricated. Despite evidence of falsified submissions, the board has not referred any cases for prosecution. Legal experts and watchdog groups call for stronger enforcement against such practices, suggesting measures like verification systems and legal accountability. The issue has sparked concerns about public trust in government processes, with critics accusing officials of relying on unverified feedback to make decisions.

title: Europe's Solar Power Surpasses Other Sources Amid Heat and Drought
summary: Europe's solar power generation outperformed other energy sources during the summer's extreme heat and drought, according to Ember. As heat waves and droughts strained traditional power systems, solar panels produced 17% more energy than usual, helping meet cooling demand. Wind and thermal power plants faced reduced output due to cooling system limitations. France's nuclear plants lost 18% of capacity due to warm river water, while UK gas plants cut 2.5 gigawatts. Solar paired with batteries provided evening power when solar output declined. Experts highlight the need for storage solutions as cooling demand grows, with France planning $10 billion in upgrades. Solar and battery installations grew significantly in 2025, with experts calling for regulatory changes to enhance grid flexibility.

title: U.S. LNG exports surge to record 15.1 Bcf/d in 2025, driving global trade growth
summary: Global LNG trade volumes reached a record 56.3 billion cubic feet per day in 2025, up 5.4% from the previous year, according to the GIIGNL. U.S. exports rose 26% to 15.1 Bcf/d, the largest increase among all countries. The U.S. accounted for 26% of global exports, up from 21% in 2024. Qatar and Australia also saw growth, with Qatar's exports rising 3% to 10.6 Bcf/d. However, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz in 2026 disrupted 20% of global LNG supplies. European imports increased by 29% as pipeline gas supplies declined, while Asian imports fell 4% due to reduced Chinese demand.

title: U.S. crude oil production surpasses global rivals in 2025
summary: The United States produced 13.6 million barrels per day of crude oil in 2025, according to International Energy Statistics, setting a new record. This output, 40% higher than Russia and Saudi Arabia's combined average, was driven by improved shale basin productivity. The Permian Basin saw a 4% increase to 6.6 million b/d, contributing 48% of U.S. production. Despite lower WTI prices, output grew, with forecasts suggesting further increases to 14.2 million b/d by 2027. Russia and Saudi Arabia saw minimal growth, with Saudi production rising to 9.6 million b/d.

title: Hitachi Energy Launches SF6-Free Switchgear for Grid Modernization
summary: Hitachi Energy unveiled new SF6-free switchgear at CIGRE 2026, including EconiQ 300-kV GIS and 245-kV DTB circuit breakers. The company highlighted its commitment to reducing SF6 use, which has high global warming potential. Over 4,000 EconiQ units have been ordered by customers in 40 countries. Utilities in North America and Europe, including Hydro One and TenneT Germany, have placed orders for the equipment. The expanded portfolio supports grid modernization and accommodates increasing renewable energy integration.

title: U.S. Delegation to Explore Grid Modernization Partnerships in Southern Africa
summary: The U.S. Trade and Development Agency (USTDA) will host a delegation of power sector officials from Angola, Botswana, Mozambique, and Zambia in the U.S. to explore partnerships for modernizing Southern Africa's transmission and distribution systems. The group, comprising about 15 government and private-sector representatives, will visit Denver and Austin, meeting with U.S. companies and utilities to discuss grid security and AI-enabled control systems. USTDA highlighted the potential of advanced technologies to enhance grid stability and efficiency, driven by rising electricity demand from mining and urbanization. A public business briefing in Denver will connect U.S. firms with the delegation to showcase solutions.

title: Can-Am Pulse 2026 Review: Performance and Features Evaluated
summary: The Can-Am Pulse 2026 is a compact electric motorcycle designed for city commuting, offering agile handling and a comfortable ride. The reviewer tested it over 570 km of mixed city and highway riding, including in rain and heat, and found it to be confident in braking and with a well-tuned traction control system. The bike features a 6.6kW onboard charger and 50-minute Level 2 top-up time, which are competitive. However, it has some drawbacks, including a constantly running cooling fan in hot weather, Apple CarPlay restrictions, and no DC fast-charging option. The Pulse shares its battery pack with the Outlander Electric and Origin, using NMC cells, and has a 5-year/50,000km battery warranty. While it performs well for daily commuting, its range drops significantly on highways, and the reviewer suggests DC fast-charging would enhance its utility. The bike scores 51.5 out of 85 in overall performance, with strengths in electric performance and ergonomics, but weaknesses in engineering and value.

title: Fuyao Glass Introduces Solar Roof Glass for Vehicles, Limited Power Output
summary: Fuyao Glass, a major automotive glass supplier, has launched a semitransparent solar glass product that can generate electricity from a car's roof. While the glass produces around 150W per square meter, this is less efficient than standard solar panels, which generate about 200W per square meter. The technology is not intended to power entire vehicles but could offset the energy needs of car electronics, such as air conditioning and internet connectivity. Fuyao's product could be used in both electric and gas-powered vehicles, though its impact on vehicle range is limited. The company claims the glass could provide 720W at peak for BYD EVs, though this has not been confirmed. The article notes that solar-powered cars are unlikely to replace traditional vehicles due to physical limitations, suggesting that solar glass may offer more practical benefits for vehicle electronics rather than full propulsion.

title: Lynk & Co supports EuroVolley 2026 Women with mobility and brand activations in Gothenburg
summary: Lynk & Co, as official car partner in Sweden for the CEV Trendyol EuroVolley 2026 Women, provided mobility support during the tournament in Gothenburg. The company deployed a fleet of 08 vehicles with championship branding to transport teams and officials. At Scandinavium, Lynk & Co showcased its 08 plug-in hybrid and 02 all-electric models through on-site displays and activations. Patric Holm, VP Market Area Sweden, highlighted the partnership's role in enhancing the event experience and engaging fans. The 08 offers up to 200 km of electric range, while the 02 features updates like Onyx Black color and enhanced in-car technology for MY27.

title: Retired Engineer Shares Four-Year Experience with Genesis GV70 Electric Vehicle
summary: David Ball, a retired civil engineer, has owned his Genesis GV70 Electrified for four years and shares his experience with CleanTechnica readers. The car, built on a multi-fuel platform and a Hyundai sub-brand, appealed to him and his wife due to its conventional dashboard layout and long range. They opted for an electric vehicle over hybrids to avoid double maintenance costs. The Genesis offered sufficient range and space for their travel needs, though it cost AU$138,000, more than the Tesla Model Y and BMW i4. David appreciates the car's adaptive features, one-pedal driving, and safety innovations. He uses solar power to charge the vehicle and has spent around $1,500 on fast charging for trips to Melbourne. The Genesis also provides 5 years of free concierge service, which he finds exceptional. David, who is environmentally conscious, sees the car as a step toward reducing fossil fuel reliance.

title: RAICo1 facility enables remote nuclear decommissioning planning through immersive tech and robotics
summary: A new facility in Cumbria, UK, combines immersive technology and robotics to enhance nuclear decommissioning planning. Developed by AtkinsRéalis, Sellafield Ltd, and Igloo Vision Ltd, the RAICo1 facility allows engineers to visualize and test operational scenarios remotely, reducing time spent in hazardous environments by up to 40%. The 360-degree environment supports collaborative planning and decision-making, integrating digital twins, live data, and robotic systems. The project builds on previous immersive facilities and aims to improve safety and efficiency in decommissioning complex nuclear sites.

title: Zhangzhou 4 Reactor Gets Passive Safety Module
summary: A passive reactor cavity water injection tank, a key component of the reactor cavity cooling system, was installed at Zhangzhou 4. The tank, with a total height of 22 metres, was assembled from three modules weighing 132.8 tonnes each, lifted by a 2000-tonne crawler crane. Zhangzhou 4 is the fourth Hualong One unit at the site, following the commercial operation of units 1 and 2. The project, owned by CNNC-Guodian Zhangzhou Energy Company, plans to build two more Hualong One units, aiming for a six-unit plant that would generate over 60 billion kilowatt-hours of clean energy annually.

title: EVO Power and Ranial partner to offer nationwide energy management services
summary: Energy storage company EVO Power USA and Ranial Systems are forming a partnership to provide energy management services to commercial and industrial customers. The collaboration combines EVO’s battery systems with Ranial’s AI software to optimize energy use and reduce costs. A pilot project at Sunrise Toyota in New York, supported by Sprocket Power, demonstrated a 55% reduction in energy costs using the integrated system. EVO has completed over 125 global deployments, many operational for more than five years. EVO’s CEO emphasized the strategic value of Ranial’s technology in creating a smart energy platform.

title: Inox Clean Energy acquires Vena Energy India's renewable assets for $627m
summary: Inox Clean Energy, part of the INOXGFL Group, acquired Vena Energy India for $626.7m, expanding its renewable portfolio. The deal, finalized within two months, includes 1GW of operational assets and a 12GW development pipeline. Vena Energy India, owned by BlackRock’s GIP, manages 1.7GW of solar and wind capacity. Inox Clean Energy's combined operational portfolio is expected to reach 4GW, with BESS projects exceeding 2.5GWh. The acquisition also includes a 640MW wind-solar hybrid portfolio in Maharashtra.

title: LGES opens second Michigan battery manufacturing plant, now makes 80% of ESS in North America
summary: LG Energy Solution has begun operations at a new battery manufacturing plant in Lansing, Michigan, contributing to its goal of producing 80% of its energy storage systems (ESS) in North America by year-end. The facility will manufacture lithium-iron phosphate (LFP) cells for ESS and nickel-manganese-cobalt (NMC) cells for Toyota's electric vehicles. The Lansing plant, which received over $2 billion in investment since 2022, is expected to employ 1,700 workers at full capacity. LGES now operates two Michigan facilities and plans to achieve 50 GWh of LFP cell capacity in North America by 2026.

title: China's 15th Five-Year Coal Plan Outlines Peaking Goals and Green Transition
summary: China's National Development and Reform Commission and National Energy Administration released the 15th five-year plan for coal, covering 2026-2030, as the country approaches its carbon peak target by 2030. The plan emphasizes coal's role as a foundational energy source but also outlines a 'green and low-carbon transition' and aims to peak coal consumption during the period. It does not set a specific year for peaking, though state-affiliated organizations suggest 2027. Analysts note the plan reflects a broader trend of reinforcing coal's role due to Middle East conflicts, while also encouraging diversification into clean energy and chemicals. The plan includes targets for modernizing coal production, increasing the share of high-quality coal, and developing coalbed methane to reduce emissions. It also calls for centralized management of coal production and maintaining reserve capacity to ensure energy security.

title: Study examines deregulation's impact on cardiac care markets
summary: A study by Arnold, Richards, Singh, and Whaley explores how deregulation affects cardiac care markets. The research focuses on Medicare's expansion of non-hospital treatment options and its influence on market dynamics. It finds that market entry leads to business stealing among low-cost settings, increasing Medicare spending by about $2.5 million. The study highlights how federal policies interact with state regulations and market behaviors, creating externalities for other procedures and payers. Vertical integration by hospitals and physicians mitigates these effects.

title: Study Shows US Dollar Dominance Resists Shocks in Non-Linear Model
summary: A study by Bordo and Bastidon uses a non-linear dynamic model to analyze currency dominance. The model incorporates regime switches based on five shock categories, including democracy and conflicts. Calibration shows democracy's role in regime changes. Stress tests suggest the US dollar's dominance remains largely unaffected, with no other currency emerging as a major force.

title: Nintendo's Stock May Outperform AI Leaders as Switch 2 Sales Grow
summary: An article predicts Nintendo's stock could outperform the 'Magnificent Seven' in the second half of 2026. Despite concerns over memory chip shortages impacting its Switch 2 sales, Nintendo reported $900 million in operating income last quarter. The company raised Switch 2 prices by $50, and its current market cap of $64 billion suggests potential undervaluation if earnings growth continues. Analysts highlight Nintendo's conservative profit forecasts and its strong historical performance as factors supporting its stock's potential rebound.

title: Microsoft's AI Growth Drives Cloud Revenue Expansion
summary: Microsoft's AI initiatives are driving significant growth in its cloud services, with Azure and Copilot contributing to a 40% year-over-year revenue increase. The company reported a $37 billion annual AI revenue run rate, up 123% from the previous year, fueled by AI integration into Microsoft 365 and enterprise software. Microsoft plans $175 billion in capital expenditure for 2026, focusing on data centers and infrastructure, supported by strong revenue and backlog growth.

title: Life insurance market emerged from AIDS crisis and evolved into financial asset
summary: The life insurance market, now a multibillion-dollar industry, originated during the AIDS crisis in the 1980s. Frank Sierawski, diagnosed with cancer, discovered life settlements—a practice where individuals sell their life insurance policies to investors for a fraction of their value. This concept, initially a desperate solution for AIDS patients like Scott Page and his partner Greg, allowed families to access funds for medical expenses and end-of-life care. The Supreme Court's 1911 ruling enabled the sale of life insurance policies, creating a legal foundation for the market. As the AIDS crisis eased, the industry expanded to include elderly, wealthy individuals, evolving into a financial asset. Investors now buy policies expecting payouts, with companies ensuring long-term returns by managing large portfolios of policies.

title: Pakistani General Asim Munir Mediates Talks with Iranian Military Leaders Amid War Deadlock
summary: Pakistani Field Marshal Asim Munir met with Iranian officials in Tehran, including President Masoud Pezeshkian and Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei, amid stalled peace negotiations with the United States. Analysts suggest Munir's success hinges on persuading Iran's military leadership, which includes General Ali Abdollahi and IRGC commander Ahmad Vahidi, to return to talks. While Iranian officials expressed skepticism toward the U.S., they did not offer new concessions. The visit coincided with U.S. threats of economic sanctions and potential military action against Iran. Munir's role is seen as critical due to his direct access to Iran's top military decision-makers, a key advantage over other mediators like Oman. Analysts note the growing influence of Iran's security establishment in shaping war and peace decisions, with Rezaei and Vahidi seen as central to any political resolution.

title: Palestinian artist Sliman Mansour, giant of resistance art, dies aged 79
summary: Sliman Mansour, a leading Palestinian artist known for his resistance-themed works, has died at 79 after a long illness, his family announced. Born in 1947 in Birzeit, Mansour became a key figure in Palestinian art, using symbols of land and memory to depict the Palestinian narrative. His work blended ancient regional influences with Arab and Islamic art, while reflecting everyday life in Palestinian villages. During the first Intifada, he co-founded the New Vision group, using locally sourced materials after boycotting Israeli supplies. Mansour's art was seen as a visual archive of the Palestinian cause, capturing the homeland's essence through his brushwork.

title: OnlyFans owner received over $700m in dividends before death
summary: Leonid Radvinsky, the late owner of OnlyFans, received more than $700m in dividends before his death from cancer in March 2026. Fenix International Ltd, which owns OnlyFans, reported $714m in pre-tax profit for the year ending November 2025. The company paid $535m in dividends for that period and an additional $174m by March 2026. Radvinsky, who bought the platform in 2018, died at 43. OnlyFans, known for its adult content, has 132 million paying subscribers and 2.5 million active creators. The platform faces regulatory scrutiny over content and age verification issues, with a £1m fine from Ofcom. OnlyFans CEO Keily Blair stated the company has paid over $30bn to creators since its launch.

title: Sardine industry profits as demand rises amid stock collapse
summary: The Guardian investigates the sardine industry's profitability as demand surges due to viral trends, despite a collapse in Morocco's sardine stock. Influencers promoted sardines as a health trend, while sardinecore became a fashion trend. This has led to shortages in supermarkets. The article explores who benefits from the boom, its impact on local fishermen, and sustainability challenges amid global heating.

title: US Expands Gas-Fired Power for AI Datacenters, Outpacing China
summary: Global Energy Monitor reports the US is building twice as much gas-fired power capacity as China, driven by AI datacenter demand. This surge, with 76% more under-construction projects in the first half of the year, has increased US gas power capacity by 50% to 378GW. Around half of this new capacity is linked to datacenters requiring significant electricity for AI operations. The shift to gas, rather than renewables, could increase US power emissions by up to 20%. Analysts warn this locks in decades of pollution and volatile fuel costs. Meanwhile, the Trump administration has supported datacenter construction, reducing environmental reviews to expedite projects, despite growing local opposition and climate concerns.

title: U.S. Economic Sanctions on Iran Aim to Weaken Regime Amid Regional Tensions
summary: The U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has launched a new sanctions campaign against Iran, aiming to cut off all economic lifelines to the regime. This follows a protracted conflict with Iran that has damaged the global economy and weakened Trump's leverage. Analysts suggest that while sanctions may pressure Iran, the regime has historically bypassed them through smuggling. The Trump administration's strategy faces challenges, particularly with China, which remains a major buyer of Iranian oil. China's cooperation is critical, but it has resisted unilateral sanctions. Meanwhile, Iran's economy is suffering under the U.S. naval blockade, with citizens reporting severe shortages and financial strain. Iranian officials argue that the economic pressure is more damaging than the war itself, and they threaten retaliation against countries joining the U.S. sanctions.

title: Minimum Wages Linked to Lower Employment for Low-Income Workers
summary: A study by David Neumark and Emma Wohl finds minimum wages negatively affect employment, hours, and earnings of low-wage workers in poor and low-income families. Using data from the Survey of Income and Program Participation, the researchers report adverse effects rather than benefits. The findings suggest minimum wages do not reduce poverty, as they harm employment outcomes for these workers. The study does not show a stronger impact on the poorest workers, but the overall effects contribute to the lack of poverty reduction from minimum wage policies.

title: Gurkha families seek pension reform after decades of service
summary: Indumati Thapa, a 87-year-old widow, and other Gurkha families in Reading face financial hardship due to pensions based on Nepalese living costs, which are significantly lower than those in the UK. The government acknowledges their service but has not adjusted pensions to reflect British living standards. Labour MPs are pushing for reforms, while many elderly Gurkhas rely on family for support. Some, like Devisara Rana, wish to return to Nepal but fear they cannot afford the trip. The Ministry of Defence reaffirms its commitment to supporting Gurkha veterans and their families.

title: Federal Reserve Prohibits Former Bank Lending Officer Over Appraisal Misconduct
summary: The Federal Reserve Board has issued a prohibition order against James Burns, former chief lending officer of Heritage State Bank in Lawrenceville, Illinois, due to appraisal-related lending misconduct. The enforcement action was announced on July 16, 2026. The board did not provide further details on the specifics of the misconduct or the consequences of the prohibition order.

title: Federal Reserve Releases Discount Rate Meeting Minutes for June 2026
summary: The Federal Reserve Board released minutes from its discount rate meetings on June 8 and June 17, 2026. The documents detail the process used to determine discount rates for depository institutions through the discount window. The Board emphasized that this process differs from the Federal Open Market Committee's approach to setting the federal funds rate target range. The minutes were made public for release on July 14, 2026.

title: Citi Trends Raises 2026 Sales and EBITDA Forecasts, Reduces New Store Openings
summary: Citi Trends reported GAAP EPS of -$0.11, beating expectations by $0.21, and revenue of $211.63M, exceeding forecasts by $3.26M. The company raised its 2026 comparable store sales growth forecast to 9%-11% and total sales growth to 10%-12%. It also increased its gross margin expansion outlook to 50–70 basis points and adjusted EBITDA to $38M–$42M. Citi Trends reduced new store openings from 25 to 20 but increased remodels to 60–65 from 50.

title: Bolivian Lawyer's Attack Exposes US Influence in Latin America
summary: A failed assassination attempt on Bolivian lawyer Nadia Beller, orchestrated by her ex-boyfriend Fernando Cerimedo, has revealed the extent of US influence in Latin American politics. Cerimedo, a key advisor to Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz and linked to Trump-aligned leaders, was arrested after the attack. Beller accused him of domestic violence and corruption, claiming he was a CIA agent. Cerimedo faces charges of attempted femicide and money laundering. His role in political campaigns and disinformation operations, including bot farms, highlights the US's covert strategies in the region. The incident underscores the broader US strategy, dubbed the Donroe Doctrine, which seeks to reshape Latin American politics through influence and manipulation.

title: Haiti Gang Coalition Launches Violent Attack
summary: A gang coalition in Haiti carried out a violent attack overnight, resulting in at least 47 deaths and 22 injuries in a neighborhood near Port-au-Prince, according to the UN. The attack has sparked anger over the lack of protection from repeated deadly incidents.

title: Professor Discusses Thermal Safety and Its Implications for Public Health
summary: Professor Ronita Bardhan from the University of Cambridge emphasizes that thermal safety is a critical issue involving biology, physiology, and urban design. She highlights the importance of immediate cooling solutions during extreme heat events, stressing the need for both adaptation and mitigation strategies. Bardhan argues that protecting human life should be the priority, with access to shade, hydration, and cooling centers being essential. She also notes the interconnected nature of thermal safety with public health, energy security, and inequality.

title: French town shows solidarity one month after devastating megafire
summary: One month after a megafire destroyed much of a French town, residents have come together in unprecedented solidarity. Local authorities reported widespread community support, with neighbors helping each other rebuild. Volunteers organized efforts to clear debris and assist affected families. The town's mayor praised the collective spirit as a testament to resilience. Despite the destruction, the community remains focused on recovery and unity.

title: Australia bans AI-generated music from official charts
summary: Australia's music industry has banned AI-generated songs from its official charts, requiring tracks to be 'substantially human made'. The Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) argues this move protects the human nature of artistry as AI-generated music becomes more prevalent. The decision follows controversy over an AI-assisted cover of Madonna's 'Like A Prayer' that reached No. 1 on the ARIA dance chart. Under new rules, artists can use AI tools but must have written the song and performed the lead vocal. ARIA chief Annabelle Herd emphasized that unlicensed AI output would undermine the recorded music industry. Meanwhile, a study found 38.5% of global music released in July 2026 involved AI, with 23.2% fully AI-generated. Spotify plans to label AI-generated artists with an 'AI Persona' badge starting in September 2026. The Velvet Sundown, an AI-generated band, gained over a million monthly listeners on Spotify, highlighting the growing influence of AI in music.

title: UK government announces housing plan with 60% social renting, Burnham revises earlier pledge
summary: The UK government has announced a £10bn initial investment in a mix of subsidised housing in England, with 60% allocated to social renting. This aligns with the Starmer government's policy and marks a shift from Andy Burnham's earlier proposal to dedicate the entire £39bn Affordable Homes Programme to council housing. The plan includes building 70,000 homes outside London, with the remaining £6bn for London to be allocated later. The government aims to construct 300,000 affordable homes over the next decade through 33 strategic partners, including three local councils for the first time. Critics, including the Greens, accuse Burnham of backtracking on his commitment to council housing. Meanwhile, Burnham plans a trip to the US to lobby for Ukraine's access to Patriot missiles, and Reform UK has proposed evicting social housing tenants who fail to maintain their properties.

title: USS Abraham Lincoln docks in Thailand after 200-day Middle East deployment
summary: The USS Abraham Lincoln, a US Navy aircraft carrier, will dock in Thailand next week after a 200-day deployment in the Middle East during the Iran war, according to a Thai official. The ship, which has 5,000 sailors and marines, set a record for consecutive days at sea, with reports of deteriorating conditions, mental health concerns, and logistical issues aboard. A sailor's wife told the Guardian that her husband's messages showed less hope and exhaustion. Democratic lawmakers have criticized the Pentagon over these conditions. Meanwhile, Trump defended the ship's maintenance, dismissing reports of poor conditions as fake news. Canada announced it would retaliate against US tariffs, while political developments in South Carolina and Oklahoma unfolded.

title: Israeli defense minister labels Gaza kites as security threats akin to drones
summary: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz has declared that kites and balloons from Gaza will be treated as security threats, comparable to drones, despite no evidence of explosives. The move follows recent sightings of kites crossing into Israeli territory, raising concerns in communities affected by the October 7 attack. Netanyahu warned of targeted assassinations against those responsible, while Hamas accused Israel of using the issue to justify further aggression. Military inspections found no dangerous material on recovered kites, but Israeli officials continue to view them as potential threats. Gazans see kite flying as a rare form of recreation amid ongoing conflict and displacement.

title: Pediatricians advise adjusting children's sleep schedules for back-to-school transition
summary: Pediatricians recommend resetting children's sleep schedules before the school year begins to improve focus and learning. Dr. Gabrina Dixon emphasizes the importance of adequate sleep for cognitive function, noting varying sleep needs by age. Experts suggest gradually shifting bedtimes earlier, avoiding heavy meals and screens before bed, and incorporating relaxing activities. Parents are advised to adjust routines based on their child's needs, with examples of practical strategies. Sleep anxiety is addressed through open communication and gradual exposure to school-related activities. Experts stress the importance of starting the new routine with patience and reassurance.

title: Hungary investigates $965M ventilator deal for possible fraud
summary: Hungary's foreign ministry has filed a criminal complaint over a $965 million ventilator purchase during the pandemic, alleging possible fraud. The deal, made under the previous government, involved acquiring 17,000 ventilators from China at higher prices than other European nations. A ministry investigation found suspicions of breach of fiduciary duty and criminal offenses, with documents showing attempts to delete records. The procurement also involved intermediary companies with inflated revenues, defective units, and significant storage costs. Former foreign minister Péter Szijjártó, who oversaw the deal, recently resigned from Parliament to join a Chinese company, raising conflict-of-interest concerns.

title: Supreme Court's mail-voting order creates uncertainty for midterms
summary: The Supreme Court's decision to revive President Trump's mail-voting restrictions has introduced significant uncertainty into the voting process for nearly a third of American voters. While the ruling does not immediately alter procedures, it reopens legal challenges and forces states to adopt new mail ballot formatting and reporting systems by September 4. Critics argue the timeline is too tight for implementation, with election officials expressing concern over last-minute changes. The administration has submitted a motion to remove a court injunction on the Postal Service, but legal analysts believe enforcing the directive before November is highly improbable. Election officials warn of the strain on local operations, as they prepare for potential disruptions amid ongoing legal battles.

title: Malaysia reports 30 areas with unhealthy air quality due to transboundary haze
summary: Malaysia reported unhealthy air quality in 30 areas on Aug 25, with haze from fires in Indonesia affecting the west coast of Peninsular Malaysia and parts of Sarawak. The Department of Environment noted API readings up to 182, classifying the air as unhealthy. Haze movement from multiple directions, including hotspots in Kalimantan and Sumatra, contributed to the worsening conditions. Authorities activated national action plans to combat open burning and enforce stricter measures, including school closures and cloud seeding operations. Health officials reported increased asthma and respiratory infection cases linked to the haze.

title: NASA's Roman telescope to study dark energy, dark matter and exoplanets
summary: NASA is preparing to launch the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, a $4 billion observatory designed to investigate dark energy, dark matter, and exoplanets. Scheduled for launch in August 2023, the telescope will conduct wide-field surveys of over two billion galaxies to study cosmic structure and expansion. Scientists aim to unlock the nature of dark energy and dark matter, which make up 95% of the universe. The mission will also search for exoplanets, potentially discovering thousands and providing insights into planetary systems. The telescope will operate from Lagrange Point 2, similar to the James Webb Space Telescope, and may function for up to ten years. NASA officials noted that the telescope's capabilities will expand on the knowledge gained from the Hubble and James Webb telescopes.

title: Firefighters report Reno wildfire is about a quarter contained
summary: Firefighters in Nevada report that the Hawk Fire, which began near Reno on Saturday, is approximately 25% contained. The blaze, which has burned over 15,000 acres, remains a threat to 23,000 evacuated residents and has destroyed 32 homes. Officials warn that strong winds and dry conditions could drive the fire toward more homes, with no deaths reported but seven injuries. Firefighters from multiple states and countries are working to contain the fire, which is suspected to have human origins. Scientists link the extreme weather conditions to climate change, noting Reno's temperatures have risen by over 4°C since the 1970s. The University of Nevada in Reno continues operations but some staff have canceled classes due to the fire's proximity.

title: ACT Education Directorate revises school funding to prioritize student needs
summary: The ACT Education Directorate has revised public school budgets to prioritize funding based on student needs, following an independent review. Forty-three schools will receive similar funding as this year, 31 will see over 5% increases, and 18 will face over 5% cuts. The Australian Education Union warns these changes could lead to program cuts at colleges.

title: India and China hold 25th round of border talks in Beijing
summary: National Security Advisor Ajit Doval met with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Beijing for the 25th round of Special Representatives talks on the India-China border dispute. The discussions focused on maintaining peace in border areas and advancing bilateral relations. Doval emphasized the potential for cooperation between the world's two largest economies. The talks precede President Xi Jinping's planned visit to India for the BRICS Summit. Relations have improved since the 2024 meeting between Prime Minister Modi and Xi in Russia.

title: Video shows tornado in Aude destroying homes
summary: A video captured a tornado in Aude, France, which destroyed hundreds of homes. The incident highlights the destructive power of severe weather events. Local authorities are assessing the damage and providing emergency support. Residents reported strong winds and flying debris during the storm. The event underscores the need for improved disaster preparedness in the region.

title: Fukuoka Prefecture Marks 20 Years Since Tragic Drunken Driving Incident
summary: Fukuoka Prefecture held a conference to address drunken driving, 20 years after a 2006 incident where a drunk driver caused a fatal accident killing three children. The event followed the tragedy, which prompted stricter regulations on drunk driving. Kaori Onuma, mother of the victims, emphasized that adults should ensure the safety of children and prevent lives from being cut short due to impaired driving.

title: Japanese firms diversify imports to hedge against yen weakness
summary: Japanese firms, including supermarket operator Takara MC, are diversifying their imports from countries like the U.S., Spain, and Italy to hedge against the yen's prolonged weakness. Despite U.S.-Japan currency interventions in 2022, 2024, and 2026, the yen remains under pressure. Taku Ueno, CEO of Takara MC, and other business leaders are seeking ways to protect against further currency declines.

title: British man charged with theft in Singapore after two-year delay
summary: A British man has been charged with theft in Singapore more than two years after allegedly stealing a denim jacket from an airport store. Surveillance footage showed him removing the jacket worth S$350 from a mannequin and leaving without paying. Authorities identified him after he departed Singapore, leading to his arrest in transit at the airport. The Singapore Police Force emphasized that offenders cannot evade detection by leaving the country. A Polish woman was also charged with stealing perfume bottles from an airport store, arrested shortly before her departure.

title: AFL Awards: Nick Daicos wins multiple honors, Jagga Smith claims Rising Star
summary: The AFL Awards ceremony for 2026 highlighted several key recognitions. Nick Daicos of Collingwood won the Coaches Association Champion Player of the Year and the Leigh Matthews Trophy for Most Valuable Player, marking his first major awards. Jagga Smith from Carlton claimed the Rising Star award after a strong season following an ACL injury. Jordan Dawson of Adelaide received the AFLPA Best Captain and Robert Rose Most Courageous Player Award, acknowledging his resilience after personal tragedy. Harry Dean of Carlton was named AFLPA Best First Year Player, while Charlie Curnow won the Coleman Medal despite not attending the ceremony. The All Australian team was also announced, featuring notable players like Max Gawn and Marcus Bontempelli, with some players missing out due to eligibility issues or performance.

title: Trump urges durable peace in Ukraine on Independence Day
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported receiving a message from US President Donald Trump on Ukraine's 35th Independence Day. Trump called for 'a durable, lasting peace' in Ukraine, praising the nation's resilience and sacrifices. Zelenskyy said Trump's words 'lift our spirits' and offer hope for a dignified peace. Trump emphasized the importance of the 35-year diplomatic bond between the US and Ukraine. Zelenskyy compared Trump's message to the sound of a Patriot PAC-3 launch, symbolizing protection from Russian attacks.

title: Rwanda's Kagame Criticizes FDLR Disarmament Efforts as Superficial
summary: Rwandan President Paul Kagame has criticized recent efforts to disarm the FDLR as superficial, stating they fail to address the root causes of the threat. He emphasized that Rwanda will remain concerned as long as the armed group is active. Kagame and Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe criticized a recent disarmament protocol, calling it a political maneuver by the DRC. They argued that dismantling the FDLR is a commitment under the Washington peace agreement. Kagame also criticized international sanctions on Rwanda, claiming they hinder rather than help conflict resolution. His remarks highlight Rwanda's stance that any measures against the FDLR must address its security concerns.

title: Kremlin denies new mobilization claims, blames Ukraine
summary: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov denied reports of a new military mobilization in Russia, calling them 'information canards' planted by Ukrainian authorities. He accused Ukraine of attempting to 'ideologically destabilize' the situation in Russia. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy previously claimed Moscow planned to mobilize 300,000 to 500,000 additional troops after September elections. Russia had previously mobilized 300,000 reservists in 2022.

title: Guinea landfill collapse kills 30, rescue efforts ongoing
summary: A landfill collapse in Conakry, Guinea, caused by heavy rains has killed at least 30 people. Rescue operations are underway as authorities plan to evacuate families near the site. In the Democratic Republic of Congo, a peace roadmap was adopted between Kinshasa and the M23 following Swiss-mediated talks. Pope Leo XIV urged increased international support for Ebola victims in the DRC, which has claimed over 2,500 lives. Somalia faces worsening drought conditions, with six million people at risk of acute hunger. Tensions between Chad and Sudan escalated after alleged Sudanese air strikes on a Chadian convoy.

title: Trump administration proposes $103,265 fee for H-1B visas, impacting Indian workers
summary: The Trump administration has proposed a permanent $103,265 fee for new H-1B visas, significantly increasing costs for foreign workers in tech and research sectors. The fee, previously temporary, could be finalized by year-end. Indian workers, who make up 71% of H-1B beneficiaries, are expected to be most affected, as the surcharge may exceed their annual salaries. The policy faces legal challenges, with a federal judge previously ruling the fee unlawful. The move aims to protect American workers while allowing companies to hire highly skilled individuals.

title: American doctors document Gaza's healthcare crisis and its global implications
summary: The documentary 'American Doctor' follows three U.S. surgeons on medical missions to Gaza, revealing the devastated healthcare system under Israeli assault. The film highlights the challenges faced by Palestinian medical staff amid bombardments, displacement, and shortages of food and medicine. It also shows the doctors' efforts to share their experiences, despite Israeli restrictions on independent reporting. Director Poh Si Teng emphasizes the ethical balance in portraying the suffering, while surgeons describe the lack of medical supplies and the impact of Israeli policies on aid access. The film critiques U.S. military support to Israel and its potential role in prolonging the conflict.

title: National Guard Patrols in Washington One Year Later Spark Protests and Debate
summary: One year after President Trump deployed National Guard troops to Washington, D.C., protests continue to challenge the move, which he framed as a response to crime and homelessness. The deployment, announced following an attempted carjacking, has led to the presence of about 4,500 soldiers in the city, compared to 3,800 police officers. While crime rates have dropped, experts question whether the decline is due to the military presence. Critics argue the deployment is costly, politically motivated, and poorly suited for urban policing. Protests, led by groups like the Party for Socialism and Liberation, call for the troops' removal and statehood for Washington. The White House has extended the mission until 2029, with an estimated $3 billion cost. Legal and civil rights groups warn of the normalization of military presence in civilian life.

title: Egypt and Turkey compete to become Eastern Mediterranean energy hubs
summary: The competition in the Eastern Mediterranean for natural gas has shifted from ownership of reserves to control of infrastructure for energy trade. Egypt, with two LNG liquefaction plants, aims to become a major gas-trading hub, importing Israeli gas and re-exporting it to Cyprus, Lebanon, and Syria. However, disruptions in Israeli gas imports and declining domestic production challenge Egypt's ambitions. Turkey, by contrast, relies on a diversified strategy including pipeline flows, local production, and storage capacity, while signing LNG deals to reduce dependence on Russian and Iranian gas. Analyst Cyril Widdershoven notes that both countries face challenges: Egypt's infrastructure is constrained by domestic needs, while Turkey's success depends on market credibility and transparent rules.

title: U.S. sanctions four Indian companies for Iran petrochemical imports
summary: The U.S. has sanctioned four Indian companies for importing petroleum and petrochemical products from Iran, according to a State Department press release. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced 'Operation Economic Outcast,' aiming to block all revenue sources for Iran. The companies, including Portease Partners LLP and Sadashiva Overseas Limited, facilitated transactions totaling over $120 million. The sanctions broaden secondary sanctions risks for entities engaging with Tehran. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott cited Iran's destabilizing activities as justification for the action.

title: SEBI Introduces ITRI to Measure Financial Market Technology Resilience
summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has launched the IT Resilience Index (ITRI), a quantitative tool to assess the robustness of technology systems in market infrastructure institutions (MIIs). The index aims to evaluate the ability of MIIs, such as stock exchanges and clearing corporations, to handle operational shocks, cyber threats, and technical failures. SEBI's ITRI is based on nine weighted parameters, with availability and security given the highest priority. The initiative reflects a shift from compliance-based oversight to risk-monitoring frameworks, aligning with global trends in operational resilience. However, challenges remain, including the rapid pace of technological change and the need for substantial investments in automated monitoring systems. SEBI's ITRI could serve as a global model for future-ready financial architecture if implemented effectively.

title: Congress MP warns of Chinese robot army on LAC, BJP criticizes claims
summary: Congress MP Manish Tewari warned that India could face a robot-driven Chinese Army on the Line of Actual Control, citing China's lead in 67 of 75 critical technologies. BJP MP Sambit Patra accused Congress of spreading misinformation and undermining the Indian Army. The Times of India reported the exchange, highlighting the political tension over defense and technological advancements.

title: FSSAI orders food companies to remove misleading health and '100%' claims
summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has directed several major food companies to remove misleading health claims and '100%' labels from their products. Companies like Amway India Enterprises, Juza Foods, and Mondelez India Foods have taken corrective actions, including revising packaging and withdrawing advertisements. Amway removed 'Energy Drink' and '100%' claims from its products, with revised packaging set for release in 2026. Juza Foods agreed to remove claims such as '100% Ragi' and health benefits, while its website was shut down. FSSAI also noted that Vichi Agro Products delisted a product from Flipkart, and Mondelez India withdrew ads. The actions are part of a broader enforcement drive against misleading food labeling and advertising, with over 150 notices issued to major companies including Nestle and Coca-Cola.

title: Russia pledges uninterrupted fertilizer supply to India amid Middle East conflict
summary: Russia has assured India of uninterrupted fertilizer supply amid disruptions caused by the Middle East conflict, according to state-run TASS news agency. Fertilizer stocks in India rose sharply, with shares of Fertilizers and Chemicals Travancore (FACT) increasing by 13%. The External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar met President Vladimir Putin, who emphasized continued support for Indian farmers. The Indian government has spent 56% of its annual fertilizer subsidy in the first five months of the 2026-27 financial year, driven by elevated global prices of finished products and LNG. Production and imports of NP/NPK fertilizers fell significantly due to rising raw material costs.

title: Study from India’s first wolf sanctuary reveals when livestock are most at risk
summary: A study from India's first wolf sanctuary, Mahuadanr in Jharkhand, found that wolf attacks on livestock are most likely at night and early morning, during winter and early summer, and near forest edges. Over half of surveyed households reported livestock losses, with 415 goats killed and an estimated economic loss of ₹21 lakhs. Researchers identified ecological and socio-economic factors influencing attacks, noting that proximity to the sanctuary boundary increased losses. Despite significant livestock depredation, many tribal communities tolerate wolves, viewing them as part of the natural landscape. The study recommends targeted mitigation strategies, including predator-proof enclosures and improved livestock management, to reduce conflict while supporting conservation efforts.

title: L&T wins ₹10,000 crore BESS projects in West Asia
summary: Larsen & Toubro has secured three Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) projects in West Asia, valued at up to ₹10,000 crore, with a combined storage capacity of 6 gigawatt-hours. The projects will use liquid cooling technology to enhance safety and efficiency. The company’s renewable energy arm noted the order reflects client confidence in its engineering and project management capabilities. Separately, L&T’s EPC arm won a gas compression facilities project for new onshore installations. The stock rose 0.56% to ₹4,108.35 on August 25, 2026.

title: Augmont Enterprises IPO Subscribed 105x, Driven by Institutional Demand
summary: Augmont Enterprises' IPO saw a subscription of 105.23 times by 4.12 pm on the closing day, led by institutional investors. The NII portion was subscribed 121.28 times, while the retail and employee portions were subscribed 29.96 and 20.70 times, respectively. The ₹825-crore IPO, with a price band of ₹750-788 per share, includes a fresh issue of ₹620 crore and an offer-for-sale component of ₹205 crore. Promoters will offload shares through the OFS. At the upper price band, the company's post-issue market cap is expected to reach ₹7,200 crore. Proceeds will fund working capital, inventory expansion, and general corporate purposes.

title: Biker Killed in Bengaluru Car Collision, Driver Arrested
summary: A 33-year-old biker died after a speeding car collided with his motorcycle at a traffic signal in Bengaluru, throwing him 50 feet. The 63-year-old driver was arrested. Protests in Patna over exam allegations and political debates in Tamil Nadu over forest deaths were also reported. The Supreme Court ordered former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal to surrender within two weeks.

title: Engineer's family dies in Godavari; suspect arrested in UP
summary: A man accused of harassing and blackmailing a family whose three members died after jumping into the Godavari River in Andhra Pradesh has been arrested in Uttar Pradesh. Shaik Sadiq Khan, the accused, was arrested in Meerut on August 22 following a multi-state search. The family members, including an engineer and his wife, died near the Road-cum-Rail Bridge in Rajamahendravaram. Their 10-year-old grandson was rescued. Police allege Khan harassed the family, threatened them, and blackmailed them using private videos. A suicide note from the daughter accused Khan of poisoning her husband and making his death appear a suicide. Khan is also linked to a separate murder case. Authorities have formed six teams to investigate the case, which includes examining the suicide notes and the circumstances surrounding the family's deaths. A former MP has called for a CBI or NIA probe, alleging a wider conspiracy and international links.

title: Allahabad High Court Rules Headscarf Not Essential Religious Practice for Constitutional Claim
summary: The Allahabad High Court dismissed a petition from a student who sought to continue wearing a headscarf with her school uniform in Class 11. The student had worn the scarf since Class 6 without prior objection, but the school refused admission, citing its dress code. The court ruled that the claim of the headscarf being an essential religious practice was a 'bare assertion' lacking necessary factual and legal foundation. It emphasized that schools have the authority to enforce uniform policies as part of their disciplinary framework, provided they are applied without discrimination. The judgment drew criticism from Muslim clerics, who argued that hijab is an integral part of Islam and should be permitted within school dress codes. The court's decision highlights the distinction between institutional rules and constitutional claims, rejecting the petition on the grounds that it failed to meet the required legal standards.

title: Israeli strikes at Gaza hospital killed journalists; accountability remains elusive
summary: One year after Israeli strikes killed 22 people, including journalists, at Nasser Hospital in Gaza, no one has been held accountable. The attacks, which occurred on August 25, 2025, targeted a suspected Hamas camera on the hospital roof, but subsequent investigations have failed to confirm militant links among the victims. An anonymous Israeli soldier reported that the military found no evidence connecting the camera, belonging to Reuters cameraman Hussam al-Masri, to Hamas. The soldier also claimed none of the six individuals identified as Hamas-linked were the intended targets. The Israeli military has not provided details about its investigation or a timeline for completion, despite repeated requests from The Associated Press. Rights groups and journalists have criticized Israel’s lack of accountability, noting a pattern of retroactive incrimination of Palestinians. The strikes, which involved four tank shell attacks, resulted in the deaths of 33-year-old AP journalist Mariam Dagga and others, raising questions about the military’s rationale and potential war crimes. AP and Reuters have called for transparency and access to Gaza for journalists covering the conflict.

title: iranian security forces used mosques as bases during january crackdown: report
summary: iranian security forces used mosques across tehran as bases to monitor and confront protesters during a deadly crackdown in january, according to evidence obtained by iran international. intercepted communications, video footage, and eyewitness accounts show security personnel operating from several mosques, including imam hossein mosque, to deploy forces and equipment. witnesses described security activity around mosques after electricity was cut, with drones flying overhead. the report suggests some mosques functioned as operational bases rather than just places of worship. the crackdown occurred amid widespread protests in iran, which have since been overshadowed by the broader conflict involving iran, israel, and the united states. washington has shifted toward economic pressure, with new sanctions against iran-linked entities and warnings to countries doing business with tehran. iran's rial has fallen to a record low, adding to economic strain, while pakistan has sent a delegation to encourage negotiations between washington and tehran.

title: Delhi Health Minister Reports 2,308 H1N1 Cases Amid 3,000 Influenza Infections
summary: Delhi Health Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh reported 2,308 H1N1 cases among 3,000 influenza infections in 2026. The Chief Minister called an emergency meeting to review preparedness for H1N1 and vector-borne diseases. Singh assured that medical resources are sufficient and isolation wards are available in hospitals. He emphasized no panic is needed as patients are being treated and recovering.

title: US sanctions four Indian firms for Iran oil trade under Operation Economic Outcast
summary: The US has sanctioned four Indian firms for facilitating the import of Iranian petrochemical products, as part of 'Operation Economic Outcast' aimed at cutting Iran's financial lifelines. The companies, including Portease Partners LLP and Sadashiva Overseas Limited, were listed for knowingly engaging in transactions involving Iranian-origin petroleum products. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent emphasized the campaign's goal of broadening secondary sanctions risks for entities dealing with Iran. The move follows a broader US strategy to isolate Iran economically, with Iranian officials acknowledging the country's economic challenges. The US State Department stated the sanctions target entities enabling Iran's destabilizing activities, including military officials and procurement rings.

title: Supreme Court may form special bench on OBC quota rules for civil services exam
summary: The Supreme Court has agreed to form a special bench to examine whether its March 11 judgment on OBC creamy-layer criteria applies to the 2025 civil services exam. The Centre argues that applying the ruling to the completed selection process could lead to unequal treatment of candidates and delay training and cadre allocation. The Department of Personnel and Training seeks permission to allocate services to 958 candidates recommended under the previous creamy-layer rules. The government contends that candidates who applied under the old administrative interpretation may have acted on the legal position in force at the time, and a retrospective application of the judgment could create disparities. The court will consider setting up a special bench to address these concerns, with the government seeking clarity on the judgment's application to the completed process.

title: Anthropic's Hiring Process Explores Ethical Priorities Over Profit
summary: Anthropic, the developer of Claude AI, reportedly includes interviews assessing whether candidates prioritize mission over profit, according to Axios. These 'culture' interviews, which question applicants about hypothetical scenarios involving safety and financial impact, are not fully scripted and vary in phrasing. While some candidates describe being asked if they would accept a stock crash for safety, others dispute the inclusion of such questions. The company emphasizes mission-driven values on its careers page, aligning with past decisions to reject military contracts and limit model access for safety. Financial impacts of these ethical stances remain unclear as Anthropic is not yet public. Industry experts suggest the investment in interview preparation is justified by potential high salaries.

title: Colombian drug gangs use social media to recruit children for drone operations
summary: Human Rights Watch reports that Colombian drug gangs and rebel groups are recruiting children through social media to pilot explosive drones, marking a shift in their tactics. The report highlights that at least 1,500 children have been recruited since 2021, with 625 cases reported in 2024 alone. Armed groups are using platforms like Meta and TikTok to lure children, with algorithms potentially promoting content that encourages recruitment. HRW verified videos of children operating drones and noted that some commanders presented drone use as a game. The report also found that nearly half of the recruited children are Indigenous, and girls make up 40% of the cases. HRW urges the Colombian government to strengthen protections and hold recruiters accountable, while calling on social media companies to improve reporting tools.

title: Indian stock market ends higher amid mixed sectoral performance
summary: The Indian stock market closed higher on August 25, with the Nifty 50 and Sensex gaining 0.17% and 0.21%, respectively, driven by late-hour buying. The broader market showed mixed results, with the Nifty Midcap 100 rising and the Nifty Smallcap 100 falling. Pharma and consumer durables saw gains of nearly 1%, while private banks and metal stocks were top losers. Fertilizer stocks like FACT surged 11.4% following Russia's assurance of uninterrupted supply to India. Vodafone Idea and Cyient also rose sharply. Meanwhile, Hindustan Copper fell 7.2% after an OFS announcement, and other stocks like Balrampur Chini Mills and Redington declined. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and U.S. sanctions against Iran influenced market sentiment.

title: US sanctions four Indian firms for Iran petrochemical imports
summary: The US has sanctioned four Indian companies for importing petroleum and petrochemical products from Iran, according to the State Department. The firms include Portease Partners LLP and its partners, Sadashiva Overseas Limited, PP Softtech Private Limited, and Prakrutees Infra Impex Private Limited. The sanctions, part of Operation Economic Outcast, aim to cut off Iran's financial lifelines by targeting its oil revenue. The companies were listed for knowingly engaging in transactions involving Iranian petroleum products, with Sadashiva Overseas importing $69 million worth of goods. The Treasury Secretary described the campaign as unprecedented, seeking to pressure Iran into changing its policies through economic measures.

title: Say Again Press Launches Short Leadership Books to Counter AI's Impact
summary: Amrita Tripathi, founder of Say Again Press, introduces a new book series targeting modern leaders with short, accessible leadership guides. The books are designed for quick reading, featuring notes pages and QR codes linking to video content. The initiative aims to promote deep thinking and original thought in an age dominated by AI and short attention spans. The series is available through indie bookstores and online platforms, with a launch event planned in Mumbai.

title: India Considers Annual Random Drug Tests for All Airline Pilots
summary: India's Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) is considering expanding drug testing for commercial pilots from 10% to 100% annual random testing, potentially making it the first country with such a policy. Civil aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu stated that the proposal aims to enhance safety but acknowledges the operational challenges for airlines. The move follows an incident where an Air India pilot tested positive for narcotics, prompting one-time testing of all pilots. Airlines would need to manage increased testing volumes, infrastructure, and crew downtime. While some airlines already conduct higher testing rates, the DGCA is assessing the balance between safety improvements and operational feasibility. The Federation of Indian Pilots supports expanded testing but advocates for a gradual increase and the use of oral-fluid testing alongside urine-based methods.

title: Stock Market Rises on Oil Price Drop and Geopolitical Factors
summary: The Sensex and Nifty 50 rose on 25 August, driven by a 3% drop in Brent crude prices and eased U.S. sanctions on Iran. The 30-share index gained 0.37% to 77,656, while the Nifty 50 climbed 0.48% to 24,335. Analysts noted the relief in energy costs contributed to the positive close. Midcaps performed well, but smallcaps fell slightly. Key stocks like ICICI Bank and Infosys led the gains, while HDFC Bank and Eternal shares dragged down the benchmark. Analysts highlighted the importance of upcoming U.S. inflation data and Fed Chair Warsh's speech, with mixed views on potential market movements.

title: Fact-check reveals Lenin's letter on India division is AI-generated
summary: A social media image claiming to show a 1947 letter from Lenin to Mountbatten requesting India's division was debunked. The fact-checker found the image AI-generated through reverse image search and AI detection tools. Analysis showed Lenin died in 1924, making the letter impossible. The text also used modern slang, inconsistent with 1947 language. The image originated from a meme page, further indicating its falsity.

title: Government intervention lowers sugar ex-mill prices to ₹55/kg, curbing speculation and hoarding
summary: The ex-mill price of sugar dropped 18% to ₹55 per kg following government measures to allow imports and curb speculation and hoarding, according to Food Secretary Sanjeev Chopra. Prices had previously surged to ₹67/kg due to mills increasing rates, which Chopra attributed to non-fundamental factors. The government's actions, including importing 1 million tonnes of raw sugar and imposing stock limits, have helped stabilize prices. While ex-mill prices are expected to fall further, wholesale and retail prices remain higher at ₹58.29/kg and ₹63.05/kg respectively. The National Federation of Cooperative Sugar Factories noted a ₹2-3/kg gap between ex-mill and wholesale prices, and a ₹7-8/kg gap between ex-mill and retail prices.

title: Mumbai drivers challenge Marathi language rule in court, citing livelihood risks
summary: Four app-based cab drivers in Mumbai have filed a petition with the Bombay High Court challenging Maharashtra's new rule requiring Marathi language proficiency for auto-rickshaw, taxi, and app-based drivers. The petition argues the regulation exceeds the state's authority under the Motor Vehicles Act and violates constitutional rights. Petitioners claim nearly 9.65 lakh permits and badges have been issued, with many drivers unable to speak Marathi. They seek an immediate stay on the August 12 notification, warning of economic hardship for thousands of drivers. The case is scheduled for urgent consideration on August 26.

title: Karnataka MP urges CM to support Railway Ministry's decision to integrate Mangaluru under SWR
summary: Karnataka MP Captain Brijesh Chowta has urged Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar to support the Railway Ministry's decision to integrate Mangaluru Railway Region under South Western Railway (SWR). Chowta emphasized that the move aligns with Karnataka's developmental needs and allows for more integrated planning of rail networks. He highlighted the importance of the Mangaluru-Hassan-Mysuru axis as a key corridor for both passenger and freight movement. While Kerala's government opposes the decision, Chowta called on Karnataka to publicly endorse the August 21 notification, which he said reflects long-standing regional aspirations.

title: Government launches OFS for 6% stake in Hindustan Copper at ₹514/share
summary: The government initiated an Offer-for-Sale (OFS) for up to 6% in Hindustan Copper, selling 5.80 crore shares at a floor price of ₹514/share. The two-day auction, open to institutional bidders, aims to raise ₹3,000 crore. Retail investors can bid starting Wednesday. Hindustan Copper shares fell 6.37% to ₹537 on BSE on the first day of the sale.

title: Modi's Public Persona and Poetic Expression Compared to V.P. Singh
summary: The article explores the public persona of Narendra Modi through the lens of dramaturgical theory, comparing it to the more personal and introspective poetry of V.P. Singh. It argues that Modi's public image, or 'front stage' self, is carefully constructed and lacks the authenticity seen in Singh's work. The piece highlights how Modi's poetry, such as 'A Journey,' reflects a detached, idealized self, in contrast to Singh's candid and emotionally revealing verses. The author suggests that Modi's poetic expression, like his political persona, is more about projecting a polished image than revealing genuine emotion. The article concludes that Modi is not a 'dimagi poet'—a term implying a deep, introspective poet—because his work lacks the vulnerability and self-awareness found in Singh's poetry.

title: Cockroach Janta Party Reinstates Protest After Government Fails to Deliver Promises
summary: The Cockroach Janta Party in India has announced it will resume protests on Teachers' Day after the government failed to fulfill commitments made during a sit-in at Jantar Mantar. The party claims no delegation has been contacted about compensation, police cases have not been withdrawn, and formal talks on examination reform have not occurred. The group, which gained significant online support, warns against diluting or dishonoring the agreement. A 2015 Serbian activist's manual, which outlines a method for achieving political change, highlights the need for enforceable commitments, which the party has not received.

title: Netweb Technologies raises Rs 1,200 crore through QIP, shares fall 4%
summary: Netweb Technologies raised Rs 1,200 crore through a Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP), leading to a 4% drop in its shares. The company's Board of Directors approved the equity share allotment on August 20, 2026, marking its first capital raise since listing on NSE and BSE in July 2023. The QIP attracted participation from major investors like Goldman Sachs, Nomura, and Edelweiss Mutual Fund. The issue price was Rs 4,790 per share, with proceeds intended for working capital and growth initiatives.
