The method achieves up to 50% VRAM reduction and 30% latency improvement, though it lacks the full speed of the original Nunchaku engine due to the absence of architecture-specific fused kernels.

title: Grabette enables open-source robot manipulation data collection
summary: Pollen Robotics introduces Grabette, an open-source system for recording robot manipulation data using a handheld gripper. The device captures demonstrations with two cameras and magnetic encoders, producing a robot-ready dataset. Grabette is designed to be low-cost and accessible, allowing anyone to contribute to a collaborative dataset without requiring a robot or lab. It is inspired by the Stanford UMI and aims to lower the barrier to entry for robot learning by making data collection as simple as recording a video. The system integrates with the LeRobot framework and Hugging Face Hub for data sharing and processing. Users can build Grabette from standard components and contribute to a growing open dataset, which is essential for training robot policies. The release marks the beginning of a community-driven effort to address the data bottleneck in robot learning.

title: MIT Researchers Develop Self-Organizing Floating Robots for Dynamic Water Infrastructure
summary: MIT researchers have developed a system called FloatForm, which uses a swarm of small robotic boats to autonomously assemble and reconfigure floating structures on water. Each robot, about 21 centimeters square, operates with its own thrusters, sensors, and magnetic latches, enabling them to self-organize into bridges, platforms, or other structures with minimal human input. The system draws inspiration from ant rafts, where individual agents follow simple rules to create resilient formations. The robots communicate with their immediate neighbors to navigate, avoid collisions, and adapt to disturbances, allowing for parallel movement and scalability. The project, published in Nature Communications, aims to transform underutilized water surfaces into dynamic, programmable spaces for urban environments, emergency response, and temporary infrastructure. The team tested the system in controlled environments, achieving high success rates with minimal human intervention, and plans to scale it for real-world applications such as canals and harbors.

title: Air Force Cadet Uses AI to Develop Battlefield Software with Minimal Coding Experience
summary: U.S. Air Force cadet Joshua Lynch, with no coding experience, used AI chatbots to develop a battlefield application called ROMAD-AI. Working with mentor Laura Niss, Lynch employed 'vibe-coding' through prompts to guide AI models like Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini. The project aimed to create tools for reducing collateral damage and enhancing mission survivability. Lynch encountered challenges with AI limitations, leading to a re-scope of the project to focus on document processing instead of full battlefield capabilities. While the prototype showed AI's potential as a prototyping tool, it highlighted security risks and the need for code review. Niss noted AI's value in bridging non-technical and technical expertise, though collaboration remains essential for critical applications.

title: AI tool enhances student learning through guided interactions in Sierra Leone
summary: A pre-registered trial in Sierra Leone found that an AI-powered learning tool, Guided Learning, significantly improved math scores and student engagement. The tool, developed by Google and collaborators, uses a 'Socratic' approach to encourage conceptual understanding rather than direct answers. Students used the tool to build understanding in 91.4% of interactions, with AI posing scaffolding questions in 76% of cases. Teachers reported increased professional growth and shifted from lecturers to facilitators. Students using the tool saw a 0.258 standard deviation gain in math scores, with higher gains in classrooms where teachers integrated AI into lessons. Engagement was notably high, with 69% of students meeting usage targets. The study also noted a shift in student behavior toward skill-building queries. The findings highlight the potential of AI as a pedagogical partner, though the achievement gap suggests the need for targeted support. The results are part of a broader effort to build a global evidence base for AI's impact on education.

title: Google Research Introduces Smartphone-Based Heart Rate Monitoring System for Passive Health Tracking
summary: Google Research introduces PHRM, a system that passively measures heart rate and resting heart rate using smartphone cameras during everyday use. The system leverages deep learning and facial video captured after face unlock events to estimate heart rate with a mean absolute percentage error under 10%, meeting industry standards across skin tones. PHRM also estimates daily resting heart rate with an accuracy comparable to wearables, achieving a mean absolute error under 5 beats per minute. The study, published in Nature, includes the largest and most diverse dataset of smartphone videos for research and a pre-trained model for accessibility. The system addresses challenges in detecting photoplethysmography (PPG) signals in darker skin tones, improving inclusivity and accuracy. PHRM's performance was validated through both controlled laboratory settings and real-world 'free-living' studies, demonstrating its effectiveness across diverse populations. The research highlights the potential of smartphones to democratize heart health monitoring, offering wearable-like insights through ubiquitous devices.

title: Google opens-sources hydrology framework for flood forecasting
summary: Google Research has open-sourced its hydrology model to aid flood forecasting globally. The framework, available on GitHub, enables National Meteorological and Hydrological Services to integrate AI-based flood predictions into their workflows. The model uses Python and PyTorch, incorporating data on climate, topography, and weather to predict river flow rates. It includes LSTM-based architectures and training pipelines using the Caravan dataset, allowing users to refine models with local data. The release includes two versions: one from a 2024 study and an upgraded model powering real-time forecasts on Google’s Flood Hub. The initiative, supported by partners like the Czech Hydrometeorological Institute, aims to improve flood preparedness by enabling regional forecasters to customize models. Dr. Hwirin Kim of the WMO praised the open-source approach for its potential to enhance global disaster response.

title: Google DeepMind Launches Asia-Pacific Accelerator to Address Environmental Risks
summary: Google DeepMind is launching an accelerator program in the Asia-Pacific region to support innovators tackling environmental challenges. The initiative, focused on 'AI for the Planet,' aims to help startups, research teams, and nonprofits use advanced AI to address issues in climate, agriculture, and energy. Selected participants will receive mentorship and technical support from Google AI experts. The program begins with an in-person bootcamp in Singapore.

title: Amazon and vendors use mechanism design to improve supply chain coordination
summary: Amazon and its vendors face challenges in optimizing supply chain operations due to information asymmetry. The article explains how the Vickrey-Clarke-Groves (VCG) framework, combined with Amazon's consensus planning protocol (CPP), creates a system called Flo Pro that enables cost-effective collaboration. This system allows both parties to achieve socially efficient outcomes without fully revealing proprietary cost structures. The VCG mechanism ensures truthful reporting by calculating transfer payments that reflect each party's externality on the other. CPP provides the computational backbone, enabling iterative optimization without requiring full disclosure of cost data. The approach was tested successfully with a major manufacturer, demonstrating real-world cost savings. The system supports dynamic, rolling-horizon planning and offers an alternative 'menu-of-contracts' method for lower-dimensional decision spaces. The work highlights the potential of mechanism design in supply chain coordination and opens new questions for future research.

title: Amazon integrates responsible AI into all stages of model development
summary: Amazon has embedded responsible AI (RAI) into every phase of its AI model development, from pretraining to post-training and evaluation. The company's approach includes four key phases: pretraining, post-training, evaluation, and third-party monitoring. Senior scientist Chentao Ye explains that pretraining involves teaching models foundational RAI principles using diverse datasets, including internal and public guidance, to ensure adaptability across languages and cultures. Post-training uses reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) to align models with human expectations and policy guidelines. Evaluations focus on creating model-breaking datasets to test for unsafe responses, while third-party collaborations address systemic risks like AI-enabled CBRN research. Amazon has developed over 70 RAI tools, published 500+ research papers, and provided extensive training to employees, emphasizing a proactive, three-pronged strategy for responsible AI implementation.

title: Ai2's Interim CEO Discusses Long-Term AI Research and Open Science Commitment
summary: Interim CEO Peter Clark of Ai2 emphasizes the institute's commitment to long-term, high-impact AI research and open science. He highlights the importance of maintaining focus on foundational research despite the rapid pace of AI development. Clark notes that projects like ELMo, Olmo, and Molmo demonstrate the potential of open models to drive scientific progress. He also discusses initiatives such as AutoDiscovery and OlmoEarth, which apply AI to real-world challenges in oncology and environmental science. Ai2 is prioritizing areas like AI for scientific discovery, embodied AI, and AI for the planet. Clark stresses the value of open models in enabling broader scientific understanding and collaboration, as seen in the NSF OMAI project. The institute aims to build a future where AI is both transparent and impactful, inviting participation from those interested in advancing science through open innovation.

title: AstaBench benchmarks AI agents' scientific research capabilities with new results and industry adoption
summary: AstaBench, an open benchmark for evaluating AI agents' scientific research capabilities, has released updated results showing improved performance on coding, reasoning, and data analysis tasks. The benchmark tested models like GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.7, with the latter achieving the highest score at 58.0%. However, end-to-end discovery remains challenging, with GPT-5.5 scoring 52.9% and struggling with complex workflows. The benchmark also gained industry adoption, with organizations like the UK AI Security Institute and General Reasoning integrating AstaBench into their evaluation frameworks. The results highlight uneven progress across categories and rising costs, emphasizing the need for continued development in full scientific workflows.

title: NIST Releases Annotated Fingerprint Dataset and Open-Source Software for Forensic Use
summary: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has released a new annotated fingerprint dataset and open-source software to aid forensic scientists. The dataset, part of NIST Technical Note 2367, includes 10,000 fingerprints from 200 volunteers, with annotations detailing print quality. These annotations help train both human examiners and AI systems to evaluate fingerprint quality. NIST also released OpenLQM, a modified version of the LQMetric software, which assesses fingerprint quality and is now open-source. The tools aim to improve accuracy and efficiency in forensic analysis. NIST computer scientist Greg Fiumara noted that the resources will enhance education and algorithm training for fingerprint identification.

title: NIST Completes Major Technical Work on Champlain Towers South Collapse Investigation
summary: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has submitted its annual report to Congress detailing progress on the National Construction Safety Team (NCST) Act activities for fiscal year 2025. The report highlights the completion of most technical work on the Champlain Towers South collapse investigation, including material testing, full-scale replica tests, and data analysis. It also covers NIST's work on Hurricane Maria's impact on Puerto Rico and actions taken to implement recommendations from the Joplin tornado investigation. The NCST Advisory Committee noted the investigation's thoroughness and expects its methodologies to improve building safety practices. The team plans to present its next findings in June 2026.

title: Leanstral: Open-Source Code Agent for Formal Verification
summary: Leanstral, an open-source code agent for Lean 4, aims to enhance formal verification by generating code and proving its correctness. The project, developed by researchers, introduces a model with 6B active parameters, optimized for proof engineering tasks. It is released under an Apache 2.0 license, available through Mistral Vibe and a free API. Leanstral outperforms existing open-source models and competitors like the Claude suite in efficiency and performance, achieving higher scores with lower computational cost. The model was tested on real-world scenarios, including diagnosing issues in Lean 4 code and translating programs from Rocq to Lean. The team emphasizes its accessibility, offering zero-setup integration and the ability to run the model locally.

title: Autonomous agent improves Rails test coverage by generating and refining RSpec tests
summary: An autonomous agent was developed to address the issue of insufficient test coverage in large Rails monoliths. The agent reads source files, generates or improves RSpec tests, validates them against style rules and coverage targets, and runs within a CI/CD pipeline without human intervention. It operates in parallel across multiple files, handling different file types like models, controllers, and helpers with specialized instructions. The agent uses Vibe, a coding assistant, with custom tools like RuboCop and SimpleCov to ensure test quality and execution. By enforcing a strict self-review process and using LLM-as-a-judge metrics, the agent improved test quality scores from 0.68 to 0.74. The experiment showed that the agent successfully generated tests for uncovered files and improved existing ones, achieving 100% coverage. However, challenges like syntax errors and versioning issues highlight the need for ongoing refinement.

title: Amodei attributes public distrust in AI to broader trust crisis
summary: Dario Amodei argues that public skepticism toward AI stems from a broader crisis of trust in companies, governments, and the tech industry. He contends that ordinary people suspect these entities of exploiting them, a distrust rooted in decades of history. Amodei dismisses the idea of using positive marketing campaigns to rebuild trust, stating that such efforts risk appearing deceptive. Instead, he emphasizes that AI companies, including Anthropic, must deliver on their promises to benefit society, which he views as the core issue requiring attention.

title: Instagram updates logo with AI-driven design changes
summary: Instagram has refreshed its logo, with Adam Mosseri describing it as 'leaner and more modern' while referencing its original design. The update comes after 10 years without a change, a period the article notes as unusually long in the fast-paced tech industry. The author critiques the redesign, suggesting it reflects algorithmic data exploitation and influencer culture rather than simplicity. The article also humorously questions the new name 'Instagzam' as a possible typo.

title: Pakistan's Judges Report 6.3% Productivity Boost with JudgeGPT AI Tool
summary: A study in Pakistan found that judges using a custom AI tool called JudgeGPT, combined with training, resolved 6.3% more cases without a drop in judgment quality. The tool, developed by economist Sultan Mehmood and collaborators, integrates OpenAI's GPT-4 with a database of Pakistani legal texts. It was tested with 1,559 judges, with those receiving comprehensive training showing the most significant improvements. The tool helps with legal research and drafting, reducing time spent on case law searches and document summaries. However, the study acknowledges limitations, including the lack of direct human evaluation of judgment quality and the risk of over-reliance on AI. Researchers emphasize the importance of training to ensure proper use of the technology, while noting that efficiency gains may not fully address broader concerns about justice quality.

title: Interconnects Launches Artifacts Hub and Adoption Dashboard to Track Open Model Ecosystem
summary: Interconnects introduced the Artifacts Hub and Adoption Dashboard to enhance transparency in the open model ecosystem. The Artifacts Hub provides curated insights into 792 models from the past two years, including adoption metrics and intelligence analysis. The Adoption Dashboard tracks model downloads and usage by geography and organization, highlighting the US-China adoption gap. These tools aim to support the open ecosystem by offering data-driven insights and fostering growth through shared analysis.

title: AI Labs Seek Profitability Through Stack Migration Amid Concerns Over Lock-In
summary: Arvind Narayanan and Akash Kapur argue that AI companies are moving beyond model provision to higher stack layers to avoid the commodity trap. They highlight that current AI business models, reliant on inference charges, face challenges due to undifferentiated models, low switching costs, and price flexibility. The authors suggest that AI labs must adopt enterprise software strategies like vertical integration and switching cost creation to achieve durable profitability. They warn that this shift risks customer lock-in and reduced competition, raising broader concerns about market concentration and innovation. Drawing on historical examples, they note that infrastructure providers rarely capture value, but cloud computing and chip fabrication have escaped the commodity trap through software-like properties or market dominance. The authors caution that without regulatory intervention or structural changes, AI may follow a similar path to past infrastructure industries.

title: Software Engineering Jobs Remain Resilient Amid AI Adoption
summary: The article argues that AI has not replaced software engineers and is unlikely to do so, despite widespread fears of job displacement. It examines the 'decide-execute-deliver' model of software development, noting that AI primarily automates the 'execute' phase but leaves the decision-making and delivery layers resistant to automation. The piece challenges narratives of AI-driven mass layoffs, citing examples like Block, Snap, and Intuit, where layoffs were often attributed to financial pressures or restructuring rather than AI. Surveys indicate that executives frequently cite AI as a reason for layoffs without evidence of actual implementation. The article also highlights that AI's productivity benefits are more evident in slower hiring rather than increased layoffs. While AI may reduce demand for certain roles, it does not eliminate the need for software engineers due to the complexity of decision-making and accountability. The authors conclude with cautious optimism, suggesting that the software engineering profession will continue to grow, albeit at a slower pace, as AI adoption progresses.

title: Big Oil Companies Invest in Nuclear Fusion Development
summary: Major oil companies are increasing their investments in nuclear fusion, signaling a shift from traditional energy sources. Eni S.p.A. plans to deploy a commercial fusion power plant in Europe by the early 2040s, supported by its $1 billion agreement with Commonwealth Fusion Systems. The company is also developing fuel systems for fusion reactors, leveraging its experience in hydrocarbon processing. Commonwealth Fusion Systems raised $1 billion in July, bringing its total funding to $4 billion, with plans for a 400-MW plant in Virginia. Other oil giants like Equinor, Chevron, Shell, and Cenovus are also backing various fusion technologies, with some aiming to build commercial power plants by the mid-2030s. Eni is developing a tritium fuel-cycle facility to support future fusion reactors, as tritium is essential but difficult to obtain. The article notes that commercial reactors will need closed-loop systems to recycle tritium, a challenge that Eni is addressing through its joint venture with the UK Atomic Energy Authority.

title: BYD to Launch Larger Great Seagull Electric Hatch by End of 2026
summary: BYD is set to release a larger version of its Seagull electric hatchback, named the Great Seagull, by the end of 2026. The new model, which will be sold alongside the current Seagull, features a longer wheelbase and a more powerful 95 kW electric motor. It is expected to include BYD's new Blade Battery 2.0 and Flash Charging technology. The current Seagull offers two battery options with ranges up to 405 km. BYD has not yet disclosed pricing for the Great Seagull, but it is anticipated to be slightly higher than the current model's starting price of 69,900 yuan. The new variant was approved for sale by China's MIIT and will feature advanced safety features like a LiDAR sensor.

title: Maine selects wind farm and transmission plan for clean energy expansion
summary: Maine's utility regulators have selected an 800-megawatt wind farm and a 1.2-gigawatt transmission line proposal, marking a significant step toward clean energy development. The projects, proposed by Clearway Energy and Avangrid, aim to supply power to New England and reduce oil reliance. The wind farm could lower oil use by 10% in winter, with expected $400 million in net benefits for consumers and over 2,500 construction jobs. The transmission line, shared among six New England states, represents unprecedented regional cooperation. While the projects face challenges including financing and public opposition, advocates see them as a model for future clean energy efforts. The federal environment for wind development remains uncertain due to policy changes under former President Trump.

title: U.S. Expands Oil Influence in Iraq Amid Global Power Rivalry
summary: The U.S. is increasing its oil influence in Iraq, aiming to secure a strategic position as the country plans to boost production to 8-10 million barrels per day within six years. Iraq's vast oil reserves, geographic centrality, and role in the Shia Crescent make it a key asset for global powers. Russia and China previously held significant influence through infrastructure deals and control over key regions, but the U.S. has moved to counter this through sanctions and new oil field acquisitions. ConocoPhillips has acquired a 42% stake in BP's Kirkuk oil fields, targeting production of up to 450,000 barrels per day. Chevron is developing the West Qurna 2 field and the Nasiriyah oilfield, supported by projects like the Common Seawater Supply Project. These moves are part of a broader geopolitical strategy to challenge Russian and Chinese influence in the region.

title: Dreame Abandons Rocket-Powered Hypercar and Car Division
summary: Dreame, a Chinese company known for robot vacuums, has canceled its plans for a rocket-powered electric hypercar and all other car-related initiatives. The company, which announced its entry into the luxury electric vehicle market last year, unveiled a hypercar at CES and even planned an SUV to compete with the Rolls Royce Cullinan. However, its ambitions were deemed impractical, with the rocket boosters requiring recharging and the project appearing more as a marketing and fundraising effort than a serious manufacturing endeavor. CarNewsChina reports that Dreame is exiting the car business, having laid off nearly 1,000 employees in the department. The decision follows a trend of high-profile electric car project cancellations by companies not traditionally in the automotive industry, including Apple’s Project Titan and Sony/Honda’s joint venture. Analysts suggest Dreame’s project was overly ambitious and lacked sufficient detail, leading to its premature cancellation.

title: Hamburg's 100 MW hydrogen hub receives final electrolyser array
summary: The final electrolyser array for Hamburg's 100 MW Green Hydrogen Hub has arrived, advancing the project's construction phase. Developed by Luxcara and Hamburger Energiewerke, the facility repurposes the former Moorburg power plant site for hydrogen production. The electrolyser arrays will convert renewable electricity into hydrogen, supporting Hamburg's decarbonisation goals. The project aims to demonstrate how existing industrial sites can be transformed into energy hubs, reducing the need for new infrastructure. Commissioning and installation now follow, with the plant expected to supply renewable hydrogen to the region.

title: L&T wins 6 GWh battery storage projects in Middle East
summary: Larsen & Toubro has secured an order for three battery energy storage system projects in the Middle East, totaling 6 GWh of storage capacity. The projects, for an unnamed client, will use four-hour battery systems to shift electricity from surplus to peak-demand periods. L&T will also deliver grid infrastructure, including substations and underground cables. The contracts highlight the company's expanding role in energy storage, reflecting growing Middle Eastern investments in renewable generation and grid infrastructure. The company did not disclose the client, locations, contract value, or completion dates.

title: South Korean residential solar adoption may lead to energy rebound effects under tiered tariffs
summary: A study by researchers Jiyoung Eum and Gyeong-Seok Choi reveals that residential solar adoption in South Korea can trigger rebound effects under the country's tiered electricity tariffs. The research shows households that move to lower tariff tiers after installing solar panels offset 11-22% of expected energy savings. Net metering amplifies this rebound effect, with high-consumption households seeing their offset double. The findings suggest policymakers should account for tier transitions and net-metering in evaluating solar programs. The study highlights the need for adjusted policy frameworks to address these rebound effects in energy and emissions savings calculations.

title: Sweden's solar panel waste could reach 150,000 metric tons by 2060
summary: A new circular-economy roadmap by Axfoundation, KTH Royal Institute of Technology, and industry partners predicts Sweden's decommissioned solar panels could rise from 17 MT in 2021 to 150,000 MT by 2060. RISE Research Institutes of Sweden estimates this growth depends on solar deployment speed and repowering rates, with scenarios ranging from 40,000 MT to 150,000 MT by 2060. The roadmap highlights the need for circular solutions, including dedicated recycling infrastructure requiring 10,000 MT annual inflow. It warns that current panel waste is often mixed with general e-waste, limiting reuse opportunities. The report outlines five priority areas, including circular design, safer handling, and improved material recovery. It also notes that only six of 12 European countries met the 85% recovery target in 2021, under the EU's WEEE Directive.

title: Global Solar Energy Market to Grow to $974.7 Billion by 2031
summary: BCC Research predicts the global solar energy market will nearly double to $974.7 billion by 2031, growing at a 10.8% CAGR. Asia-Pacific leads with 57.8% market share, driven by manufacturing and policy support. Declining LCOE, government incentives, and integration with battery storage and EV infrastructure are key growth factors. Technological advances like N-type TOPCon and perovskite tandem cells are reshaping the market. However, challenges include overcapacity, margin pressure, and losses among major Chinese manufacturers. The report highlights opportunities in emerging markets and innovative technologies.

title: Xudabao plant unveils simulator for nuclear training
summary: China National Nuclear Corporation's subsidiary has commissioned a full-scope simulator for operator training at the Xudabao plant. The simulator, developed by CNNC Wuhan Nuclear Power Operation Technology Co, will support training for operators of units 1 and 2. The plant, owned by Liaoning Nuclear Power Company Ltd, is set to begin simulator training soon. Originally planned for six CAP1000 reactors, the project now includes two Russian VVER-1200 reactors for units 3 and 4, with commissioning scheduled for 2027 and 2028. Upon completion, the plant will generate 54 billion kilowatt-hours of clean electricity annually.

title: TCL Electronics Considers Spin-Off Of Solar Business For Separate Public Listing
summary: TCL Electronics Holdings is considering spinning off its solar business into a separate publicly listed company, according to a filing with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. The proposal would allow the solar division to access equity markets and dedicated capital for growth, while TCL Electronics could focus on consumer electronics. However, the plan remains in early stages, with details like valuation and ownership structure yet to be finalized. The move follows TCL's expansion in solar technology and recent acquisitions, though the company warned of potential delays or changes to the proposal.

title: Australia's battery storage market shifts toward commoditised contracts and diversified revenue streams
summary: Australia's grid-scale battery storage fleet has expanded fourfold in three years, reshaping financing, contracting, and operations. Industry experts at the Battery Asset Management Summit 2026 noted that spot prices and spreads are compressing, pushing operators to diversify revenue streams. Thomas Dargue of Eku Energy described a shift from physical tolls to commoditised products, with contracts becoming more interchangeable. Sally Torgoman of Ascera Energy highlighted a change in buyer profiles, with 70% of parties in her Riverina project not previously energy users. She emphasized the durability of system strength contracts over ancillary services. Investors now demand higher returns, with 13-14% expected instead of 8-10%. Jeremy Lloyd of Neoen noted declining ancillary services values as more capacity enters the market. Jake Dunstan of Aurora Energy Research pointed to delayed coal retirements as a disruptive factor. Household battery storage systems, while growing rapidly, pose operational visibility challenges for grid planning, though they are unlikely to replace utility-scale services directly. Torgoman cautioned against suppressing price signals, arguing that coal retirements will eventually drive market changes regardless of policy interventions.

title: Five U.S. States Lead in Energy Storage for Grid Reliability
summary: Energy storage is becoming critical for maintaining grid reliability as electricity demand rises. Five states—California, Nevada, Illinois, Virginia, and Massachusetts—are leading the way in adopting energy storage policies. California surpassed its 2024 target of 1,825 MW, now with over 21,000 MW of capacity. Nevada, with bipartisan support, reached 1,700 MW by 2023, exceeding its 2030 goal. Illinois aims for 3,000 MW by 2030, with projected savings of $13.4 billion. Virginia, driven by data center growth, targets 16,780 MW of short-duration storage by 2040. Massachusetts has surpassed its 2025 goal and is expanding long-duration storage. These states demonstrate how energy storage can enhance grid reliability, reduce costs, and meet growing demand.

title: NLR-NRRI Alliance Demonstrates Critical Minerals Processing at Scale
summary: The National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) and the University of Minnesota’s Natural Resources Research Institute (NRRI) have launched the Joint Research Alliance for Innovative Materials and Processing for Advanced Critical Technologies (IMPACT). This initiative aims to demonstrate industry-scale technologies for critical minerals and materials, supporting U.S. manufacturing and supply chain resilience. IMPACT bridges research and commercialization by advancing technology readiness levels through collaborative facilities and expertise. The partnership focuses on processes for metal recycling and recovery of critical minerals like lithium and copper, addressing challenges in scrap metal recycling and tramp element removal. NLR’s Jennifer King leads the effort, emphasizing the alliance’s potential to scale innovations from concept to commercial application.

title: Detect Offers Starlink Mini at T&D World Live 2026 for Remote Connectivity
summary: Detect is giving away a Starlink Mini at T&D World Live 2026, a compact satellite internet device designed for field teams working in remote locations. The device, which fits in a backpack and runs on a portable power bank, provides connectivity in areas with no cell coverage. It is particularly useful for drone pilots and field crews inspecting infrastructure in challenging environments. To enter a drawing for the device, attendees can visit Booth 512. CEO Matt Sattler will be present after his opening-day session with Xcel Energy and CenterPoint Energy.

title: DetectOS Evolves into Full Asset Management System for Utilities
summary: Detect has launched an enhanced version of its DetectOS platform at T&D World Live, transforming it from an AI defect-identification tool into a full asset management system. The update allows utility teams to manage the entire lifecycle of an issue, from defect detection to logging fixes and tracking structural health over time. The platform now includes a cleaner, faster interface customizable to workflows, supported by Detect's Data Quality Program to ensure consistent data capture. Justin Lee, Detect's chief technology officer, highlighted the platform's evolution as a major leap in utility infrastructure management. The new version will be demonstrated at Booth 512 during the event.

title: Windlab, Squadron Energy submit 500MW battery storage system for federal assessment in Queensland, Australia
summary: Windlab and Squadron Energy, a 50:50 joint venture, have submitted the Bungaban Solar Project for federal assessment under Australia’s EPBC Act. The 500MW solar PV facility, paired with a 500MW battery storage system, will be built on a 1,531.9-hectare site in Queensland’s Western Downs region. The project, which includes a transmission line to Powerlink’s Warranna substation, aims for construction to start in July 2028. The referral highlights the project’s alignment with Windlab’s broader renewable generation hub and its power purchase agreement with Rio Tinto. The ecological assessment suggests minimal impact on listed species and habitats, with 99.99% of ground disturbance occurring in already-cleared areas.

title: Ukraine's Chernobyl waste facility gets regulatory approval for new repository
summary: Ukraine's State Nuclear Regulatory Inspectorate of Ukraine (SNRIU) approved the construction of a new near-surface repository at the Buriakivka RAW Disposal Facility. The facility, operated by CERWM, has stored over 635,918 cubic metres of Chernobyl-related radioactive waste. SNRIU confirmed the safety of the design and CERWM's capability to manage construction activities. The new repository, No.11A, will allow continued disposal of low-level waste from Chernobyl decommissioning and other nuclear operations.

title: California Governor Candidate Proposes Free Electricity Hours to Reduce Costs
summary: California Democratic gubernatorial candidate Xavier Becerra proposes a 'Power Hour' plan to offer up to two free hours of electricity daily, starting with low-income families. The initiative aims to utilize excess solar energy during peak production times, potentially saving households about $1,000 annually. Becerra cites rising power prices in California, which have increased by 46% over the last decade, as a key motivator. The plan mirrors Australia's Solar Sharer program, where free power is available during specific hours, though it does not guarantee overall lower bills. Experts note the plan's effectiveness depends on broader market reforms and addressing fixed system costs. Becerra intends to collaborate with regulators and stakeholders to implement the policy within his first year in office.

title: China's 15th Five-Year Plan Outlines Climate Targets and Global Cooperation Strategies
summary: China has released its 15th five-year plan for climate change, covering the 2026-2030 period. The plan consolidates existing policies and includes new signals on non-CO2 greenhouse gases, carbon markets, and global climate governance. Officials describe it as the main policy instrument for advancing climate action during the period. The plan reaffirms China's commitment to peak emissions before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2060. It sets targets for reducing carbon intensity and expanding renewable energy use. The document also emphasizes China's role in global climate governance, aiming to increase its influence in international climate discussions. Experts note the plan's comprehensive target system supports China's Paris Agreement pledges and highlights the country's growing involvement in global carbon markets.

title: New York Imposes Data Center Moratorium Amid Grid Strain
summary: New York Governor Kathy Hochul has imposed a one-year moratorium on data centers consuming 50 megawatts or more, citing concerns over their impact on the state's power grid and water usage. The move comes as New York's electricity margins are thin, with only 417 MW of extra power available during peak demand. While data centers are not the primary cause of grid strain, the moratorium is seen as a preemptive measure. Experts note that the state's grid issues stem largely from the electrification of buildings and transportation, as well as aging infrastructure. NYISO, the state's grid operator, faces challenges from 14 GW of pending grid connections, including 12 GW from data centers. The moratorium aims to provide time for regulatory planning, but its long-term effectiveness remains uncertain. The state is also pursuing renewable energy and a nuclear reliability initiative to bolster the grid.

title: IEEE Course Teaches AI Integration for Grid Modernization
summary: The IEEE has launched an online course to train professionals in using artificial intelligence to modernize power grids. The course addresses the challenges of an aging grid strained by rising demand and renewable energy integration. It covers five modules, including AI fundamentals, grid control, forecasting, physics-informed AI, and generative AI applications. Experts emphasize that AI is essential for real-time data analysis, predictive maintenance, and grid resilience. The program aims to equip engineers and data scientists with the skills needed to implement AI solutions in power systems, ensuring safety and reliability in an increasingly complex energy landscape.

title: Heatwaves impact nuclear, gas, and wind power generation differently
summary: Heatwaves significantly affect various power generation sources, with nuclear, gas, and wind each facing distinct challenges. Nuclear plants, which rely on river water for cooling, often reduce output during extreme heat due to elevated water temperatures or low river levels, as seen in France, Romania, and Hungary. Gas power plants also experience efficiency losses and capacity reductions as temperatures rise, impacting their ability to meet demand. Wind generation is affected by reduced wind speeds during heatwaves, particularly in regions like Europe and Australia, though some areas may see increased wind. The article highlights that while heatwaves pose challenges, their overall annual impact on nuclear generation is minimal, and adaptation strategies are being developed to mitigate these effects. The piece also critiques the tendency to blame intermittent sources like wind and solar for energy shortages during heatwaves, while underplaying the role of nuclear and gas plants.

title: HYDAC's Square Wave Heat Exchanger Improves Wind Turbine Cooling Efficiency
summary: HYDAC's new Square Wave heat exchanger design addresses cooling inefficiencies in wind turbine gearboxes, reducing clogging and improving thermal management. Traditional panel cut designs are prone to debris accumulation, leading to increased maintenance and reduced reliability. Field trials on GE and Mitsubishi turbines showed the Square Wave exchanger maintains cooler operating temperatures, with some turbines running 20-25% cooler than conventional systems. This improvement supports better oil viscosity, reduced maintenance, and increased turbine availability. HYDAC's Erickson notes that effective cooling is critical for long-term gearbox health and operational efficiency. The technology offers a retrofit solution for aging wind fleets, enhancing reliability without major system overhauls.

title: Bulgarian government allows Russian imports for Kozloduy nuclear plant
summary: The Bulgarian government has granted a targeted sanctions exemption to the Kozloduy NPP, allowing imports of critical iron and steel products, original components, and technical assistance from Russian suppliers. This decision, under EU Council Regulation 833/2014, aims to ensure nuclear safety and operational reliability. The exemption is limited in duration and applies only to specific contracts listed in the decision’s annexes. The Kozloduy plant, which generates 30-40% of Bulgaria’s electricity, faced technical issues with non-Russian replacement parts, leading to shutdowns and economic losses. The plant’s Soviet-designed VVER-1000 reactors rely on Russian-origin systems, making alternative sourcing challenging.

title: EDF and Centrica seek 20-year extension for Sizewell B nuclear plant
summary: EDF and Centrica are nearing a £800m deal to extend Sizewell B's operating life to 2055, according to an EDF spokesperson. The agreement aims to address a projected nuclear generation gap as older reactors retire. Sizewell B, the UK's only pressurised-water reactor, provides 1.2 GWe, or about 3% of the country's electricity. The companies are negotiating a Contract for Difference framework with a proposed power price of £70 per MWh. EDF, owning 80% of the plant, and Centrica, with 20%, will split the costs, with Centrica contributing £160m. The extension supports power availability as new facilities like Hinkley Point C and Sizewell C face delays. Financial analysts at Citi view the £70/MWh strike price as attractive for returns. Centrica's interim results on 23 July will provide further clarity.

title: Interior Department halts offshore wind leases citing national security risks
summary: The U.S. Department of the Interior paused leases for five offshore wind projects under construction, citing national security risks identified in classified reports. Secretary Doug Burgum stated the action addresses vulnerabilities near East Coast population centers. The affected projects include Vineyard Wind 1, Revolution Wind, CVOW, Sunrise Wind, and Empire Wind 1. Dominion Energy criticized the pause, arguing the CVOW project supports national security, energy needs, and critical infrastructure. The company emphasized its security measures and bipartisan support for the project.

title: Israeli soldiers prevent Knesset member from accessing besieged Palestinian home
summary: Israeli soldiers prevented Knesset member Ofer Cassif from reaching a Palestinian family in Qusra, occupied West Bank, under a 17-day settler siege. Cassif later reached the family and offered support.

title: New York Mayor Opposes Hindu Nationalist Event at Madison Square Garden
summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani opposes a right-wing Hindu nationalist event at Madison Square Garden. The event is linked to India’s ruling BJP party. Mamdani criticizes the group for promoting an 'exclusionary vision'.

title: SpaceX to build $100bn Louisiana launch facility for Starship missions
summary: SpaceX plans to construct a $100bn launch site in Louisiana named Starbase, set to begin next year. The 125,000-acre facility will support thousands of Starship flights annually, targeting missions to Earth orbit, the Moon, and Mars. The project is expected to create over 8,100 indirect jobs and boost regional wages by 192%. SpaceX aims to launch its first Starship flight from the site in 2029. The company, which recently listed on Nasdaq, faces pressure to demonstrate profitability amid expansion plans.

title: Global Firms and Capital Markets Model Evaluates Reallocation and Welfare Effects of Globalization
summary: Economists Karabarbounis, Pellegrino, and Salomao developed a general-equilibrium model integrating global firms and capital markets. Using firm and country data, they analyzed how financial and trade liberalization concentrate activity among large firms, boosting welfare more in emerging and mid-sized open economies. They found product- and capital-market frictions amplify each other, reducing gains from liberalizing one market.

title: Study finds spending multipliers higher than tax multipliers in fiscal consolidations
summary: A new study by Roberto Perotti and Luca Sala examines marginal tax and spending multipliers during fiscal consolidations in 16 countries from 1978 to 2020. The research introduces a marginal cumulative multiplier to measure the effect of government spending or taxation on output while holding the other fiscal instrument constant. The authors estimate a marginal spending multiplier of 1.5 and a marginal tax multiplier close to 0 in their benchmark analysis. Using the policy counterfactual method, they find spending multipliers never below 1.3 and tax multipliers no higher than -1. The study suggests existing literature's higher tax multipliers may result from improper scaling of fiscal variables.

title: Bitcoin mining firms shift computing power to AI
summary: Bitcoin mining companies are redirecting their computational resources toward artificial intelligence, driven by declining cryptocurrency rewards and falling Bitcoin prices. Firms like Riot Platforms and TerraWulf have signed major deals with AI firms such as Anthropic, investing in high-performance computing infrastructure. Many companies are rebranding to reflect this shift, with some selling Bitcoin holdings to fund the transition. Analysts note the pivot is costly and irreversible, with some predicting that once infrastructure is adapted for AI, companies will not easily return to Bitcoin mining.

title: Meta's Adam Mosseri testifies about teen safety features and data transparency
summary: Adam Mosseri, head of Instagram, testified in a child safety trial against Meta, acknowledging that a 2021 feature to help teens manage screen time had low uptake. The feature, called Take a Break, was used by only 1.8% of teens, according to an internal document. Mosseri admitted Meta did not disclose this low usage rate to parents or users. The states suing Meta argue the company withheld information about the feature's ineffectiveness, violating consumer protection laws. Mosseri defended Meta's efforts to address teen overuse, noting multiple features were introduced. The trial is part of a broader legal challenge against tech companies over social media's impact on youth mental health. Potential penalties could reach $1.4 trillion, drawing comparisons to past tobacco litigation.

title: Trump's Economic Policies Test Global Dependence on US Financial Power
summary: The article discusses how Donald Trump's economic policies, including tariffs and sanctions, are testing the global reliance on US financial power. The Trump administration's sanctions against Iran and Canada, along with efforts to control bond yields, reveal the risks of repeatedly weaponizing economic leverage. The Guardian argues that while the US has leverage, its actions risk alienating trading partners and undermining the trust that sustains international economic relationships. The article highlights the potential for escalation, particularly with China, and questions the long-term viability of Trump's approach to economic coercion.

title: Canada imposes 50% tariffs on $20bn of US imports
summary: Canada announced 50% retaliatory tariffs on $20 billion worth of US imports, escalating the trade war. The move follows through on Mark Carney's vow to match US tariffs 'dollar for dollar'. The tariffs target hundreds of US goods. The decision comes as part of ongoing trade tensions between the two nations. The announcement was made in response to previous US tariffs on Canadian products.

title: Gold prices dip slightly after hitting 3-month high on Tuesday
summary: Gold prices opened at $4,710.10 per troy ounce on Tuesday, August 25, 2026, marking a 0.3% increase from Monday's close, before retreating slightly to $4,697.60. The price reached a 3-month high, driven by geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, the U.S. Treasury's bond buyback program, and global inflation concerns. Investors are monitoring the upcoming PCE report and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole speech. Analysts warn of price and speculation risks, emphasizing gold's role as a stabilizer in diversified portfolios rather than a high-return investment.

title: CD rates remain high at 4.30% APY as Fed policy influences market trends
summary: The article reports that as of Tuesday, August 25, 2026, the best CD rates are 4.30% APY, offered by Synchrony Bank and Marcus by Goldman Sachs. These rates are higher than traditional savings accounts and remain elevated compared to historical standards. The piece outlines the evolution of CD rates over the past two decades, noting that they fell to record lows during the 2000s and 2010s due to Fed policies and economic conditions. CD rates began rising in 2022 as the Fed raised interest rates to combat inflation, leading to higher APYs on savings products. However, the Fed has since cut rates, resulting in a gradual decline from their peak. The article also explains that longer-term CDs typically offer higher rates, but the current market shows a flattening yield curve, with the highest average rate for a 12-month term. It advises readers to consider factors like their financial goals, the type of institution, account terms, and inflation when choosing a CD.

title: US Sanctions on Iran Fail to Subdue Regime Amid Global Economic Concerns
summary: The article discusses the US Treasury's new sanctions against Iran, dubbed 'Operation Economic Outcast,' aimed at crippling the Iranian regime's economy. The strategy, however, faces skepticism due to its limited scope and the regime's continued economic growth. Critics argue that economic sanctions alone have historically failed to achieve regime change, citing examples from World War I and the Iraq War. The sanctions target key sectors like digital assets, technology, and shipping, but their effectiveness is questioned, particularly given Iran's trade relationships with countries like China. The article highlights the potential for global economic disruption and the risk of escalation, noting that China has rejected the sanctions and warned of retaliation. The US's approach is seen as a return to failed strategies, with experts suggesting that military pressure remains the only viable path to achieving strategic goals.

title: Calculated Risk Ends Daily Blog, Introduces Weekly Newsletter
summary: Calculated Risk, a financial blog, is ending its daily updates after 21 years. The author will transition to a weekly economic newsletter with three sections: a schedule of upcoming data, a review of previous data, and commentary on current topics. The Real Estate Newsletter will continue with 4 to 6 weekly updates. The author thanked readers for their support and expressed hope that the blog was useful and informative.

title: Hotel Occupancy Rate Rose 4.4% Year-over-year in Early 2026
summary: The U.S. hotel industry reported a 4.4% year-over-year increase in occupancy rate to 50.5%, according to CoStar’s data through January 3, 2026. Average daily rates rose 3.4% to $175.47, while revenue per available room (RevPAR) increased by 7.9% to $88.65. The data shows a seasonal pattern, with the red line representing 2026 performance, the blue line as the median, and the dashed light blue line for 2025. The report notes that early-year comparisons are challenging due to weak travel demand in January, and the 4-week average is expected to rise seasonally in the coming months.

title: Japan's Debt-Servicing Costs to Reach $230 Billion Record Next Year
summary: Japan's Finance Ministry plans to allocate a record $230 billion for debt-servicing in the next fiscal year, according to documents. This represents a 17% increase from the current year's allocation, driven by higher interest rates and bond yields. The ministry used a provisional rate of 3.8%, the highest in nearly three decades. Rising borrowing costs are linked to concerns over Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's fiscal policies, including a planned sales tax cut. The overall budget request is expected to exceed ¥130 trillion for the first time, with ministries aiming to include more spending in the initial package.

title: South Korea scrambles jets as Russian planes enter its air defense zone
summary: South Korea scrambled fighter jets after multiple Russian military aircraft entered its air defense identification zone over the East Sea, according to the country's defense ministry. The ministry stated the Russian planes did not violate South Korean airspace but failed to notify Seoul before entering the zone. This marks the second such incursion in weeks, following a similar event in late June involving Chinese and Russian aircraft. South Korea protested the incidents, demanding preventive measures, amid strained relations with Russia due to sanctions and military cooperation with North Korea.

title: Japanese Red Cross warns of evacuees' health risks in Kumamoto
summary: The Japanese Red Cross has raised concerns about the health of evacuees in Kumamoto Prefecture, nearly a month after a 7.0 magnitude earthquake. Officials noted potential health deterioration due to prolonged shelter life, including risks of aspiration pneumonia and heart failure. The organization highlighted improved relief efforts compared to past disasters, with faster delivery of supplies and quicker medical response. JRCS doctor Shinsaku Ueda emphasized the need for evacuees, especially the elderly, to maintain physical activity and proper nutrition to mitigate health risks.

title: Trump submits Saudi nuclear deal to Congress with Israel condition
summary: US President Donald Trump has submitted a civilian nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress for review, according to an administration official. The classified pact aims to bolster Saudi Arabia's nuclear program but is contingent on the kingdom normalizing relations with Israel. The agreement, signed last month, requires Saudi Arabia to join the Abraham Accords, raising concerns about its implementation. Congress has 90 days to review the deal, which could take effect without approval if not rejected. The deal, expected to last 30 years, involves US firms in developing the program.

title: Malaysian Commando Adrift in South China Sea After Parachute Drill
summary: Senior Seaman Michael Coccon Johen, a Malaysian navy special forces member, spent 15 hours adrift in the South China Sea after a parachute training exercise went wrong. The incident occurred during a free-fall drill when sudden weather changes disrupted visibility, causing the team to land in the sea instead of on an island. Johen, the last of six personnel to be rescued, remained calm and waited for naval assistance, though high waves prevented immediate recovery. The accident happened during the second jump at 4:30 pm, with the team 10 km from the island. The navy's safety vessels could not reach them due to dangerous sea conditions.

title: Longhaul Festival Cancellation Marks Another Blow to Australian Music Events
summary: The Longhaul Festival, launched by TEG Live in early 2027, has been cancelled just a month after its announcement. The festival, which featured Kacey Musgraves and Kane Brown, was set to take place in Melbourne, Sydney, and Brisbane. A TEG spokesperson expressed disappointment, stating the decision was made to provide certainty to fans and artists. The cancellation follows TEG's decision to cut its country music touring department, citing cost-cutting measures. Ticketek has confirmed all tickets will be refunded. The festival's cancellation joins a trend of declining music events in Australia, with several other festivals also facing cancellations or reduced operations.

title: Trump submits Saudi nuclear agreement to Congress for review
summary: US President Donald Trump has submitted a 30-year nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress for review, according to The Wall Street Journal. The agreement, announced last month, allows US companies to lead Saudi Arabia's nuclear infrastructure development while excluding foreign competitors. It has drawn controversy due to concerns that it could enable Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium domestically. The deal was formally transmitted to Congress on Monday, requiring a joint resolution and two-thirds majority in both chambers to block it.

title: Indigenous Voice to Parliament member's assault charges dismissed
summary: Danni Smith, an Indigenous Voice to Parliament member in South Australia, had assault charges dropped after pleading guilty to disturbing the peace. The magistrate ruled the incident was a one-off and not trifling, issuing a good behaviour bond instead of a conviction. Smith, who represents the South East and Riverland regions, faced domestic violence-related aggravated assault charges but maintained her innocence throughout the court process. The altercation occurred after she visited her parents' home following personal loss, with no physical contact made during the argument.

title: Ten Japanese players in Premier League set new record
summary: Ten Japanese players are registered with Premier League clubs, marking a record high. Clubs are drawn to their skill, cost-effectiveness, and low risk. Zion Suzuki's move to Aston Villa and Takehiro Tomiyasu's return to Crystal Palace highlight this trend. FIFA agent Joel Pannick notes increased confidence in Japanese players' adaptation and integration. Japanese players like Wataru Endo and Kaoru Mitoma are already established in the league. Pannick attributes the success to improved language skills and a more tactical Premier League style, which suits Japanese players' playing style. The league's shift toward coordinated play has made it easier for Japanese players to thrive.

title: Dolly Parton's Legacy Lives On Through Music and Philanthropy
summary: Dolly Parton, a legendary country music singer and songwriter, passed away at age 80 in Nashville, her family announced. Known for her heartfelt lyrics and business acumen, Parton sold over 100 million records and won 11 Grammy awards, including a Lifetime Achievement Award. Her music, including classics like 'Jolene' and 'I Will Always Love You,' resonated globally, and she became one of the best-selling female artists of all time. Parton was also a philanthropist, donating $1 million to vaccine research and launching literacy programs. Her ability to connect with people and her distinctive image, shaped by her signature look and vibrant personality, made her a cultural icon. Despite her fame, she remained grounded, emphasizing her work as a songwriter and her commitment to her roots.

title: Australia news live: Hundreds pay tribute to police killed by Dezi Freeman on one-year anniversary; value of Japan’s melon gifts to Albanese revealed
summary: Hundreds gathered at a police station in Porepunkah to honor two officers killed by Dezi Freeman one year ago, with a minute's silence and heartfelt tributes. The incident occurred on 26 August 2025 when officers attempted to serve a warrant at Freeman's remote property, resulting in two deaths and one serious injury. Family members of the slain officer, Neal Thompson, expressed their grief, highlighting his dedication to his job. Meanwhile, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's department confirmed that four Japanese melons gifted by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi were valued at $200 each, below the $750 threshold for declaration. The gifts sparked controversy after Albanese's comments on a podcast. Other news included a federal MP stepping aside from a special envoy role due to legal issues, inflation data showing a slight decrease, and reflections on Australia's immigration policies following the Tampa affair.

title: SpaceX to develop $100 billion launch site in Louisiana for Starship missions
summary: SpaceX announced plans to build a $100 billion rocket launch complex in southern Louisiana, named Starbase Louisiana, covering 125,000 acres on Pecan Island. The site, which will support Starship and AI satellite missions, is expected to handle thousands of launches annually once operational. Construction is set to begin next year, with the first Starship launch planned for 2029. The project includes methane production, power generation, and deep-water shipping capabilities. SpaceX emphasized environmental restoration efforts, including protecting migratory bird habitats. The site cleared legal hurdles after a settlement with ExxonMobil, allowing the project to proceed. The initiative is part of SpaceX's broader expansion in the southern U.S., including data centers and Starlink facilities.

title: Trump's Saudi nuclear deal faces congressional review amid Israel ties condition
summary: U.S. President Trump has submitted a classified civil nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress for review, as required by the Atomic Energy Act. The pact, signed by U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright and his Saudi counterpart, includes a condition that Saudi Arabia normalize relations with Israel through the Abraham Accords. The agreement's implementation hinges on this condition, raising concerns about its viability. Congress has 90 days to review the deal, which could take effect without approval. The deal, expected to last 30 years, involves U.S. firms in developing Saudi's civilian nuclear program. Critics warn it could enable Saudi uranium enrichment and nuclear proliferation. The Saudi Embassy did not comment, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu opposes Palestinian statehood, a prerequisite for Saudi normalization with Israel.

title: Golf Channel postpones ‘Big Break’ premiere after sponsor pulls out over Good Good Golf video
summary: Golf Channel postponed the premiere of 'Big Break x Good Good' by a week due to a sponsor's request to remove branding, following backlash against a video showing a man shoving a woman. The video, an ad for Callaway, was deleted after drawing criticism for depicting violence against women. Good Good apologized, and Callaway expressed disappointment, with its CEO acknowledging approval of the video. The PGA Tour also voiced concerns, while the sponsor's identity was reported as Golf Galaxy.

title: Vikings WR Jeshaun Jones Suspended for 3 Games Over Substance Abuse Violation
summary: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jeshaun Jones received a three-game suspension from the NFL for violating the league's substance abuse policy. The NFL did not specify the nature of the violation. Jones, who spent the past two years on the practice squad, was promoted to the active roster and played in the 2025 season's final game. He remains eligible for the remaining preseason games but will miss the first three regular-season games. His suspension begins on Sunday, with reinstatement possible on Sept. 28. Jones faces competition for roster spots with established players like Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison.

title: Tornado strikes Pomas, residents describe devastation
summary: A tornado devastated Pomas, with residents describing the destruction as 'like bombs were dropped on our heads'. The article notes technical issues preventing full loading, suggesting potential browser or network problems.

title: Suez Canal's colonial legacy and its decline
summary: The article examines the historical significance of the Suez Canal, tracing its origins as a colonial project and its eventual decline. It highlights how the canal, once a symbol of European imperial power, has faced challenges and transformations over time. The piece explores the political and economic factors that contributed to its rise and fall. The Suez Canal's role in global trade is discussed, alongside its impact on regional geopolitics. The article suggests that the canal's legacy is complex, reflecting both the ambitions and limitations of colonial rule.

title: Typhoon Narra causes record floods in Guangxi, China, prompting evacuations
summary: Typhoon Narra triggered record floodwaters in Guangxi, China, leading to the evacuation of over 54,000 people. In Chongzuo, water levels surpassed 2008 highs, submerging homes and reaching rooftops. Authorities ordered business closures and warned against returning to high-risk areas. Meanwhile, Typhoon Saudel approached Japan and Taiwan, causing separate flooding and casualties. In Taiwan, a tropical depression led to one death and four missing in Tainan and Kaohsiung, where rainfall exceeded that of Typhoon Morakot in 2009.

title: Darline Graham secures South Carolina GOP Senate nomination
summary: U.S. Sen. Darline Graham has won the Republican nomination in South Carolina's special Senate election, replacing her late brother Lindsey Graham. She defeated Rep. Ralph Norman in a runoff primary, gaining support from President Trump, who endorsed her campaign and campaigned with her. Graham, a political newcomer, emphasized her alignment with Trump's policies and her focus on domestic issues. Norman, a more experienced candidate, criticized Graham's lack of expertise in foreign policy during a debate. Graham will face Democratic nominee Annie Andrews in November. Trump's backing appears to be a strategic move to secure a Senate ally, as no Democrat has won a South Carolina Senate seat in decades.

title: San Diego Padres coach released after ICE detention
summary: Oswaldo Pirela, a San Diego Padres minor league catching coordinator, was released on bond after being detained by ICE at El Paso International Airport. His family disputes the government's claim that he overstayed his visa, stating he applied for asylum and obtained work permits. The Padres confirmed his release and will not comment further. Pirela's family emphasizes his lawful presence and contributions to the U.S., calling for due process. DHS has not responded to requests for comment.

title: Sufi Muslims in Cairo Celebrate Prophet's Birth with Procession and Chants
summary: Hundreds of Egyptian Sufi Muslims gathered in Cairo on Tuesday to celebrate the birth of Prophet Mohammed. Participants held banners and chanted religious hymns during a procession from the Sidi Saleh Al-Jaafari Mosque to the shrine of Al-Hussein. Saber Abd El Raouf, a Sufi shiekh, described the event as renewing faith within hearts. Hassan Abd El Nazeem, another Sufi member, explained the celebration involved chanting praises and reciting supplications for the Prophet's birthday.

title: US urges nations to sever economic ties with Iran amid sanctions campaign
summary: The United States has launched 'Operation Economic Outcast' to isolate Iran by urging countries to cut economic ties, warning of retaliation. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent emphasized that all entities must face sanctions, offering Iran two paths: global isolation or rejoining the global economy. The campaign follows US-Israeli strikes on Iran six months prior, with the regional conflict now at a stalemate.

title: Interpol arrests 58 in global operation targeting West African cybercrime networks
summary: Interpol coordinated Operation Jackal IV, arresting 58 individuals linked to West African cybercrime groups across 22 countries. The operation focused on romance and investment scams, identifying 263 suspects. It also examined trends like sextortion targeting minors and money laundering. Interpol emphasized international cooperation in disrupting financial flows. In South Africa, 39 arrests were made, with $2.67m seized. The operation is part of a series targeting networks like Black Axe, which engages in global criminal activities.

title: UN Condemns Israeli Raid on Qalandia Training Center
summary: The UN condemned the Israeli raid on the Qalandia Training Center, a UNRWA vocational school in occupied East Jerusalem. UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric called the entry unlawful and expressed concern over the disruption of education for Palestinian youth. The raid marked the fifth unauthorized entry since May, following other breaches of UN premises. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urged Israel to cease interference and restore the facility. The center, operational for over 70 years, provides vocational training to hundreds of students annually.

title: USS Abraham Lincoln ends 250-day deployment with Thailand stop
summary: The USS Abraham Lincoln, which spent over 250 days at sea without a port call, is set to make a brief stop in Thailand in early September. Thailand’s Navy described the visit as routine, providing rest and logistical support for the nearly 5,000 crew members. The ship left San Diego in November 2025 and had only one stop in Guam during its deployment. Concerns about living conditions, including cold showers and supply shortages, have been raised by family members and media outlets. Two Democratic senators requested an independent review of conditions aboard the ship and others involved in the Iran conflict. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth acknowledged the deployment’s difficulty but praised the crew’s performance. Meanwhile, a crew member’s father faces deportation after being detained by immigration agents in Key West.

title: Immigration raid in New Jersey separates 46 workers from families
summary: A large immigration raid at a bonded warehouse in New Jersey detained 46 workers, including María Eugenia García’s daughter Killy Tatiana, who was arrested during an immigration operation in October 2025. The raid, involving multiple federal agencies, disrupted the lives of over 50 people and their families, with many workers holding pending asylum applications or valid work permits. The Trump administration’s aggressive immigration policies, including daily arrest quotas and widespread raids, have intensified the crackdown on undocumented workers. Advocates argue these operations violate constitutional rights, as law enforcement lacked warrants for entry into the warehouse. Killy Tatiana was deported to Colombia, where she now lives under voluntary departure, while her mother struggles with the emotional toll of separation. The case highlights the broader impact of immigration enforcement on families and communities, with legal challenges ongoing as activists seek transparency and accountability.

title: Nigeria's president orders manhunt after kidnappers release victim video
summary: Nigeria's President Bola Tinubu has ordered a manhunt for kidnappers who attacked four villages in Niger state, killing over 40 people. The attackers, dressed in military-style clothing, abducted up to 500 people, though this has not been verified. A video released by the kidnappers showed some of the captives, identified by a local youth leader. Authorities suspect the attackers are bandits, not jihadists, and have not received ransom demands. The attack highlights growing insecurity in the region, with local officials warning of increasing jihadist activity.

title: Starlink's Vietnam Trial Faces Censorship and Cost Challenges
summary: Elon Musk's Starlink has begun offering satellite internet in Vietnam, a country with strict online controls. The service, operated through a local subsidiary, is available on a controlled trial basis with 600,000 subscribers allowed until 2030. Vietnam's government approved the trial in 2025 to avoid US trade penalties, but Starlink's high cost may limit its impact, especially in rural areas where average income is lower than its service price. Analysts suggest its primary benefit may be for institutions rather than individuals. Despite potential connectivity improvements, Starlink must comply with Vietnam's censorship laws, and experts believe it will not challenge the country's digital sovereignty. The service operates through licensed domestic infrastructure, ensuring it remains within the government's regulatory framework.

title: US sanctions target Iran's shadow economy networks
summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced new sanctions targeting Iran's shadow economy, focusing on digital assets, gold, and shipping networks. The measures aim to disrupt money laundering and pressurize foreign intermediaries. The US has sanctioned 60 entities and individuals but avoided major Chinese banks. Iran's economy faces severe inflation, with food prices rising 128% year-on-year, and many transactions now conducted in US dollars. Iranian businesses struggle with rising costs and disrupted supply chains, with over 70% of employees laid off at one company. Sanctions also affect Iranian entrepreneurs abroad, creating uncertainty for those operating in Dubai. Analysts suggest the measures may intensify inflationary expectations and deepen economic polarization without fundamentally altering Iran's behavior. The sanctions could strengthen informal economic networks, leading to a more uncontrolled underground economy.

title: IDF Orders Evacuation of Tehran Areas Before Strikes
summary: The Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) issued an evacuation order for certain Tehran neighborhoods ahead of planned strikes. The announcement was made by IDF Spokesperson Avichay Adraee in Arabic. The situation is described as a developing story with further updates expected.

title: Defense Ministry Conducts Exercise on Highway 35
summary: The Defense Ministry's Border Crossings Authority will conduct an exercise on Sunday between 11 a.m. and 1:30 p.m. at the Tarkumiya Crossing on Highway 35, according to a statement from the ministry. The exercise may involve gunshots and explosions, with high movement of emergency and rescue vehicles expected. The ministry warned that the activity could cause traffic disruptions.

title: Chennai's Evolution from Madras: A Century of Industrial and Technological Transformation
summary: Chennai, once known as Madras, has undergone significant transformation from a colonial trading hub to a diversified global business destination. The city's industrial development began in the late 19th century with initiatives like the Madras Chamber of Commerce and Industry, which aimed to stimulate technical education and industrial growth. Early industries such as cotton piece goods and indigo laid the foundation for later manufacturing, including the establishment of mills and factories like Binny’s Buckingham Mill and Simpson’s coach building. The automotive sector took root in the mid-20th century with companies like Ashok Leyland and TVS Motor Company. In recent decades, Chennai has embraced the IT revolution, becoming a hub for multinational corporations and startups, with over 5,134 startups and a growing focus on deep tech and innovation. The city is also expanding into new sectors like electric vehicles, animation, and space technology, with plans to create 200,000 jobs by 2030. Experts predict continued growth in GCCs, NBFCs, and new-age startups, positioning Chennai as a key player in India's evolving economic landscape.

title: Speeding bus collision with lorry kills six, injures twelve in Telangana
summary: A speeding bus collided with a stationary lorry near Suryapet in Telangana on August 26, 2026, killing six passengers and injuring twelve. The accident occurred at around 5 a.m. with the bus carrying 42 people traveling from Hyderabad to Eluru. Two injured are in critical condition. Chief Minister Revanth Reddy expressed shock and directed officials to provide medical care, while other ministers and local leaders also extended condolences and instructed emergency response measures. Further details remain pending.

title: Owaisi criticizes RSS and BJP over Manusmriti opposition to Ambedkar's Constitution
summary: Asaduddin Owaisi accused the RSS and BJP of opposing Dr. BR Ambedkar's Constitution and favoring the Manusmriti. During an Eid speech in Hyderabad, he highlighted historical tensions between Hindu nationalist groups and the Constitution, citing an RSS publication that criticized the 1949 Constitution. Owaisi also contrasted the stance of Hindutva ideologue VD Savarkar with Muslim freedom fighters like Allama Fazl-e-Haq Khairabadi. He emphasized the role of Muslim figures in India's independence struggle, noting Maulvi Alauddin as the first prisoner sent to the Andaman Islands. The debate over Manusmriti intensified amid political clashes between BJP and Congress, with Rahul Gandhi criticizing the text's patriarchal views.

title: Analysts caution retail investors on Hindustan Copper OFS due to limited upside
summary: Analysts warn that the Hindustan Copper OFS may not attract retail investors despite a 10% discount. The stock fell 7.04% to ₹533.20, with the OFS floor set at ₹514. Siddarth Bhamre notes the discount is not enough to justify investment, as valuations may not offer significant upside. Retail bids will open on Wednesday after the non-retail portion was oversubscribed. Gaikar highlights limited upside and risks of copper price declines, advising against chasing short-term gains.

title: Mid- and small-cap stocks outperform blue-chips as market breadth expands
summary: Mid- and small-cap stocks have outperformed blue-chip stocks, with the average advance-to-decline ratio reaching its highest level in four months. This indicates broader market participation, as retail investors favor these segments. In August, mid- and small-cap schemes received 56% of equity flows, compared to 40% in July, while large-cap funds saw outflows. The Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 have risen 22% and 31% since April, outperforming the Nifty 50's 15% gain. Analysts attribute this to strong earnings growth and value opportunities in smaller stocks.

title: New York Mayor Opposes RSS Leader's Event, Questions Legal Authority
summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani opposes a planned event featuring RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat at Madison Square Garden, stating the city may lack legal authority to cancel the private gathering. The event, part of the RSS's centenary outreach, is expected to draw 5,000 Indian diaspora members. Mamdani criticized the RSS's exclusionary vision, aligning with his family's values of pluralism and secularism. Protests against the event have been organized by interfaith groups. The AHEAD Forum promotes the event as a message of global unity.

title: Global brands face backlash over culturally insensitive campaigns
