NVIDIA reports the system delivers up to 9x higher throughput and 2.9x faster single-stream reasoning speed compared to alternatives. The architecture combines a hybrid Mamba-Transformer Mixture-of-Experts backbone with specialized encoders for vision and audio. NVIDIA details that the training process utilizes staged multimodal alignment and reinforcement learning on H100 clusters. The model handles 100+ page documents and processes audio inputs up to 1,200 seconds. NVIDIA notes the system achieves top accuracy on benchmarks like MMlongbench-Doc and VoiceBench. The company also highlights capabilities for agentic computer use, enabling the model to interpret screenshots and automate GUI tasks. NVIDIA makes BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 checkpoints available for download on HuggingFace.

title: Google introduces Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS with enhanced speech control
summary: Google announced the release of Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS, a new text-to-speech model offering improved quality and expressivity. The company reported an Elo score of 1,211 on the Artificial Analysis TTS leaderboard. Google introduced new audio tags allowing developers to control vocal style and pace through natural language commands. The model supports over 70 languages and includes SynthID watermarking to identify AI-generated audio.

title: Google introduces Groundsource to convert news reports into flood data
summary: Google Research engineers and scientists introduced Groundsource, a scalable methodology using Gemini to transform unstructured global news into historical disaster data. The team released an open-access dataset containing 2.6 million records of urban flash floods spanning over 150 countries since the year 2000. This approach addresses the lack of standardized observation infrastructure for hydro-meteorological hazards by extracting verified ground truth from news articles in 80 languages. Technical validation indicates that 82% of extracted events are accurate enough for practical real-world analysis. Google is now rolling out near-global urban flash flood forecasts up to 24 hours in advance through its Flood Hub. The authors note that this framework could eventually be applied to other hazards like droughts and landslides to improve global crisis resilience.

title: Mistral AI launches Mistral Compute to democratize frontier AI infrastructure
summary: Mistral AI announced Mistral Compute, a new infrastructure offering designed to provide private, integrated AI stacks globally. The company stated this initiative aims to prevent infrastructure concentration in a few powerful firms. Mistral Compute will offer GPUs, orchestration, and APIs from bare-metal servers to managed platforms. As a premier NVIDIA partner, the service provides tens of thousands of GPUs with rapid expansion plans. The launch partners include Black Forest Labs, BNP Paribas, and Thales among others.

title: Mistral launches Mistral Code for secure enterprise AI development
summary: Mistral introduces Mistral Code, an AI-powered coding assistant designed for secure enterprise deployment. The tool bundles models and in-IDE capabilities to address connectivity and customization limitations found in typical copilots. Private beta access is currently open for JetBrains IDEs and VSCode, with general availability planned soon. Early adopters include Abanca, SNCF, and Capgemini, who are utilizing the platform for hybrid and on-premises workflows.

title: Databricks presents Lakebase and LTAP innovations at VLDB 2026
summary: Databricks Co-founder Reynold Xin will deliver the opening keynote at VLDB 2026, discussing how AI agents are driving a new era of database engineering. The company has four accepted papers covering Lakebase, Spark Structured Streaming, and automatic Lakehouse optimizations. Stas Kelvich will present Lakebase, a serverless PostgreSQL architecture that decouples compute from open lake storage to support agentic workflows. Siying Dong will detail how Apache Spark Structured Streaming evolved to handle millions of weekly jobs through micro-batch pipelining. Yunjia Zhang will describe AutoLiquid, which automates table clustering and outperforms manual selection on over 95% of workloads. Eric Liang will present Ultron, a history-based optimizer that improved median join latency by 25%. Ippokratis Pandis will give a sponsor talk on LakehouseRT and the unified LTAP system.

title: Databricks improves agent chart retrieval with structured JSON extraction
summary: Databricks researchers report that structured chart extraction enhances agent retrieval and answer accuracy for enterprise documents. The team tested their approach using ai_parse_document to convert charts into structured JSON, which outperformed standard image inputs in answering questions about chart values. Evaluations on the ViDoRe V3 benchmark and a synthetic Chart-RAG dataset showed that this method achieves higher correctness rates than large multimodal embedding models. The study highlights that while captions often miss fine-grained data, structured extraction provides precise values for reasoning. Databricks plans to integrate this chart-JSON enrichment into ai_parse_document soon, automatically including chart values in parsed documents to improve Genie One's performance.

title: NVIDIA GeForce NOW Expands Cloud Gaming at Gamescom 2026
summary: NVIDIA GeForce NOW announced new features and games at Gamescom 2026, aiming to broaden access to cloud gaming. The service introduced DLSS 4.5 controls for Ultimate members and added support for Firefox, Steam Machines, and more Amazon Fire TV devices. A limited-time offer allows members to receive CONTROL Resonant with a 12-month Ultimate membership. Additionally, GeForce NOW is hosting a community giveaway with over 40 prizes, including hardware and memberships. Several major titles, including Gears of War: E-Day and STAR WARS Zero Company, are launching on the platform. The company encourages users to check back for weekly updates on new game additions.

title: Ai2 and Providence Swedish Cancer Institute partner to advance AI-assisted scientific discovery
summary: Ai2 and Providence Swedish Cancer Institute have partnered to advance AI-assisted scientific discovery within a secure local environment. The collaboration focuses on clinically meaningful research regarding lobular breast cancer using the AutoDiscovery platform. A joint research team led by Dr. Kelly Paulson, Dr. Sasha Stanton, and Bodhisattwa Majumder utilized the tool to analyze extensive breast cancer datasets. Their analysis uncovered a stronger immune signature in invasive lobular breast cancer than previously recognized, a finding subsequently validated through independent datasets and laboratory analysis. These results suggest that approximately 15% of breast cancer patients diagnosed annually in the US could benefit from immunotherapy. The partnership represents a significant milestone as it moves beyond public datasets into active oncology research programs. Ai2 emphasizes that AutoDiscovery is designed to amplify scientific expertise rather than replace it, allowing researchers to guide the AI in promising directions. The Providence Swedish Cancer Institute is now deploying the platform within its own cloud environment to maintain data security while accelerating discovery.

title: Tech firms urge global cyber defence upgrades before AI threats escalate
summary: One hundred technology companies, including Google and Microsoft, signed an open letter warning that current security measures cannot withstand AI-driven cyberattacks. The signatories, which include banks and utilities, call for governments to provide defensive AI tools and for tech firms to share models with under-resourced defenders. Recent breaches involving AI agents and attacks on US infrastructure highlight the urgency of the situation. Experts like Geoffrey Hinton warn that failing to manage AI risks could lead to a bleak future for society.

title: UN urges global social media reform following Meta settlement
summary: The UN human rights chief stated that all social media platforms must prioritize child safety. Meta agreed to a settlement involving up to $18bn in penalties to 48 US states and territories. The deal includes child safety features like time limits, contingent on TikTok and YouTube adopting similar measures. California Attorney General Rob Bonta expressed interest in coordinating with those platforms. The UN framework advocates for safer design but rejects outright bans on children's social media use.

title: Mathematician questions AI's role in future mathematical research
summary: Dr Henry Bradford argues that recent AI breakthroughs in mathematics rely on recombining existing ideas rather than creating novel theory. He notes that OpenAI's Astra model recently solved a group theory problem using a slight twist on previous theorems. Bradford cites mathematician Bill Thurston to suggest the true value of research lies in human understanding, not just proving theorems. He warns that if AI produces papers faster, universities might wrongly view human researchers as superfluous. Ultimately, the future of mathematics depends on society's collective decision about what human intellect values.

title: Nathan Lambert and Florian Brand discuss Kimi K3, Qwen 3.8, and open model progress
summary: Nathan Lambert and Florian Brand host a quarterly discussion on the accelerating landscape of open-source artificial intelligence models. The hosts analyze the recent release of Kimi K3, noting its strong performance in research tasks despite slower inference speeds due to server locations in China. They also examine the capabilities of GLM 5.2, which they describe as Sonnet-level and effective for grunt work when accessed via fast internal endpoints. The conversation highlights a significant shift in strategy, as Chinese leader Xi Jinping recently committed to openness and open source as a national strategy. Additionally, Qwen announced its next major model will be open-weight, marking a notable change in the sector. The hosts debate the validity of claims regarding how many months open models lag behind closed frontiers, arguing that benchmark selection often muddies the picture. They conclude by discussing the challenges of post-training large-scale models and the potential for fine-tuning to match frontier capabilities in niche domains.

title: Author argues AI is a creative medium like photography or painting
summary: The author contends that artificial intelligence functions as a creative medium rather than a replacement for human writers. While acknowledging that AI-generated content often lacks the concentrated intention found in high-quality work, the writer believes humans will eventually master the tool to produce exceptional results. The piece draws parallels between early photography and current AI writing, noting that both initially produced mediocre output before evolving into distinct art forms. The author references Ted Chiang's argument that art requires many choices, suggesting that skilled writers will learn to make significant decisions through their prompts. Comparing AI assistance to a pedal-assist bicycle, the writer argues that effort determines output quality, rejecting the notion that the process itself is the sole value of writing.

title: Toyota launches updated bZ5 electric SUV at half Tesla Model Y price
summary: FAW-Toyota launched the updated 2027 bZ5 electric SUV in China with prices starting at 109,800 yuan. The vehicle features advanced Chinese technology, including Momenta 6.0 software and a dual Driver Monitoring System. Although the model is roughly the size of a Tesla Model Y, it costs significantly less. Sales have recently declined as the company hopes these updates will attract new buyers in a competitive market.

title: Tesla FSD v14.3.7 nearly drove into a train at a railroad crossing
summary: A Tesla running Full Self-Driving version 14.3.7 failed to stop at an active railroad crossing and nearly collided with a passing train. Driver Lei Xing stated he had to brake manually to avoid being hit, noting that the crossing lights were flashing and the train horns were loud. This incident marks at least the third time Electrek has documented FSD attempting to drive a vehicle into a train this year. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has expanded an investigation into FSD to cover roughly 2.9 million vehicles following reports of crashes involving red lights and railroad crossings. Senators Ed Markey and Richard Blumenthal have urged the agency to specifically investigate these railroad crossing failures as a safety risk. Despite release notes claiming improved handling for unusual objects, the system continues to struggle with this common scenario.

title: California passes bill enabling remote solar inspections statewide
summary: The California Legislature unanimously passed AB 1738, a bill awaiting Governor Gavin Newsom's signature that would allow remote inspections for home energy projects. Assemblymember Juan Carrillo authored the measure, which permits homeowners and contractors to request virtual checks for solar, batteries, and other systems. SPUR analysis indicates contractors currently wait two to six hours for in-person inspections, increasing upgrade costs. Nineteen jurisdictions already offer remote options, with Los Angeles County conducting 20 to 40% of inspections remotely. The bill preserves inspector discretion to require in-person visits when necessary.

title: Trump Administration Discusses Direct Ownership of Venezuelan Oil Fields
summary: The Trump administration is reportedly in talks to acquire direct ownership stakes in Venezuelan oil fields containing 90 billion barrels of proven crude. Senior U.S. officials cited by Axios say the deal would shift Washington's energy policy toward direct resource control. While supermajors remain cautious, independent operators like SLB and Hunt Oil have already signed agreements with PDVSA. Analysts note that revitalizing these fields requires approximately $180 billion in investment over the next decade.

title: Trump Administration Halts Offshore Wind Projects, Leaving Thousands of U.S. Workers in Uncertainty
summary: President Trump has issued executive actions restricting offshore wind development, causing projects to be paused or cancelled. The New England industrial mechanics union, Millwrights Local 1121, reported that millions of dollars in training investments are now wasted as work dries up. By September 2025, nine permitted projects expected to create 9,000 jobs were paused or under investigation. Trump also barred new solar and wind projects from federal lands. While clean energy jobs grew under the previous administration, the current policies threaten the stability of the renewable energy sector. Workers who transferred skills from oil and gas face an insecure job market with few available roles.

title: Posiva begins drilling first deposition holes at Onkalo repository
summary: Posiva announced the start of drilling for the first deposition hole at the Onkalo repository on Wednesday. The operation utilizes a large Deposition Hole Boring Machine delivered from Germany in June 2022. Kimmo Lehtola, Posiva's Construction Manager for Operations, stated that the team has long anticipated this milestone. The initial hole will be drilled vertically into the Olkiluoto bedrock at a depth exceeding 400 metres. Posiva aims to produce approximately two finished deposition holes per working week once the process becomes routine. The company expects to achieve operational readiness for final disposal by the end of 2026. A positive opinion from the Radiation and Nuclear Safety Authority is required before the government can grant the operating licence.

title: Revolve Renewable Power Secures $24 Million Financing from Mexico Bank
summary: Revolve Renewable Power Corp. announced a $24 million project financing facility with Banco Multiva to support its distributed generation business in Mexico. The company expects to complete an initial drawdown of $7.7 million to refinance existing assets and recycle capital for future growth. CFO Tania Ontiveros described the deal as a significant milestone validating the firm's expansion strategy. Banco Multiva CEO Tamara Caballero noted the agreement reinforces the bank's ability to deliver long-term energy financing solutions. The 14-year facility is structured through Revolve's Mexican subsidiaries and aims to fund new solar projects while retaining ownership of underlying assets. Revolve reported that three projects have completed installation and seventeen are under construction, with an expected operational completion by the end of 2026.

title: EU approves Greece's 4.8 billion Social Climate Plan for clean transition
summary: The European Commission approved Greece's EUR 4.8 billion Social Climate Plan, the fifth largest under the Social Climate Fund. The scheme aims to support vulnerable households and micro-enterprises through energy efficiency upgrades, new social housing, and expanded mobility options. Funding will come from 75% EU contributions and 25% national funds. The plan targets greenhouse gas reductions between 2026 and 2032.

title: Brandon Oyer explains Amazon's strategy for sustainable data center energy and water
summary: Brandon Oyer, director of energy and water for Amazon Web Services, discusses the company's approach to sustainable data center operations. Oyer stated that Amazon aims to deliver power and water responsibly while ensuring local communities benefit from data center growth. He noted that the company is one of the world's largest purchasers of carbon-free energy, with over 700 projects representing 42 gigawatts of capacity. Oyer explained that Amazon pays the full cost of electricity and infrastructure without passing expenses to other ratepayers. He highlighted investments in small modular reactors and water efficiency projects, including a $235 million investment in Oregon to replace aging infrastructure. Oyer also mentioned that Amazon is 75% of the way toward its goal to be water positive by 2030.

title: Google signs deal to buy power from record-breaking Arkansas solar plant
summary: Google has agreed to purchase all electricity generated by the first two phases of the Steel River Energy Center in Mississippi County, Arkansas. The project, developed by Cypress Creek Energy, will feature 1.6 gigawatts of solar capacity and 1.9 gigawatt-hours of battery storage. Once operational in 2029, the power will feed into the Entergy Arkansas grid to supply Google's existing and future data centers. A spokesperson for the company stated that the facility helps address growing electricity demand with reliable, cost-effective power. Cypress Creek secured $3.5 billion in financing to build the initial phases, with lenders including Barclays and Wells Fargo. The project is expected to generate more instantaneous power than Arkansas's two nuclear reactors combined. Cypress Creek CEO Kevin Smith noted that solar is currently the most affordable electricity supply and fastest to market. The facility will utilize a significant amount of domestically sourced construction materials and panels.

title: US Army selects five microreactor vendors for Janus nuclear program
summary: The US Army has selected five vendors to develop and deploy microreactor technologies under the Janus Program. The selected companies are Antares Nuclear, BWXT Advanced Technologies, General Atomics Electromagnetic Systems, Radiant Industries, and Westinghouse Government Services. These contracts aim to provide resilient, secure energy for military installations by 2028. Funding is contingent on meeting technical goals, potentially reaching USD2.2 billion between 2027 and 2031. Army officials emphasized the need for reliable, long-duration power independent of external grids. Each vendor will operate at a specific military base, with technologies ranging from sodium heat-pipe cooled to high-temperature gas-cooled designs.

title: Five Companies Build 20 Microreactors for Army Under Janus Program
summary: Five advanced nuclear vendors will construct and operate more than 20 commercial microreactors at U.S. Army installations under the Janus Program. The Army selected BWXT Advanced Technologies, Radiant Industries, General Atomics Electromagnetic Systems, Antares Nuclear, and Westinghouse Government Services to deploy these units by 2028. The Department of War Innovation Unit negotiated fixed-price, milestone-based agreements totaling up to $2.2 billion through fiscal year 2031. These projects serve as anchor deployments intended to prove sustained operation and unlock broader commercial markets. Radiant Industries secured a binding agreement worth up to $750 million to deliver 15 Kaleidos units by 2030. BWXT will deploy a 20-MWe Advanced Nuclear Reactor at Fort Campbell, Kentucky, while other vendors target sites across Georgia, Texas, North Carolina, and New York. The Army declined to disclose an exact breakdown of the aggregate funding, noting that totals may change over time. Selected reactors range in output from 100 kWe to 20 MWe, utilizing various fuel strategies and targeting initial operations as early as 2028.

title: Trump declares national emergency to ban imported energy technologies
summary: President Donald Trump issued an executive order declaring a national emergency to prohibit the import and installation of specific bulk-power energy technologies. The order cites national security risks, claiming foreign equipment may contain digital backdoors. It affects components like transformers and inverters from countries under an arms embargo, including China and Russia. The Department of Energy is empowered to designate existing systems as security risks and require updates. This action classifies the technologies as defense materials under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.

title: SolarWindow launches 0.85 mm-thick, self-adhesive solar film
summary: SolarWindow Technologies announced the commercial launch of ElectroFlex, a self-adhesive solar film designed for flat and curved surfaces. The manufacturer states the product features a 0.85 mm thickness and 24.4% power conversion efficiency. SolarWindow reported the technology targets sectors including transportation, aerospace, and architecture. The company plans to expand sales to North America and Asia over the coming quarters.

title: Sungrow connects 200 MW battery to grid in 17 days
summary: Sungrow announced a 200 MW/400 MWh battery project reached commercial operation after a 17-day grid connection. The company stated it supplied the PowerTitan 3.0 system and used its digital platform to coordinate installation. Sungrow reported the rapid deployment highlights industry focus on reducing construction times. The firm noted its thermal management system reduced operating energy consumption by 10%. Sungrow also mentioned a separate agreement with Masdar for a UAE project.

title: Gabrovo builds solar-powered rainwater system for urban green spaces
summary: The Gabrovo Municipality announced plans to construct a solar-powered rainwater collection system for irrigating urban green spaces. Mayor Tanya Hristova stated the project supports the municipality's goal of achieving climate neutrality by 2030. Gabrovo previously established Bulgaria's first citizen-led energy community in 2024, which raised over BGN 160,000 to develop a shared photovoltaic installation. The new irrigation facility will draw water from the local theater roof and the Sinkevitsa River, powered by a photovoltaic plant to minimize its carbon footprint.

title: Federal Reserve Board issues enforcement action against former Banco Popular employee
summary: The Federal Reserve Board announced an enforcement action against Gadiel Rosario-Alvarado, a former employee of Banco Popular de Puerto Rico. The Board issued a consent prohibition order against the individual. This action stems from allegations of misappropriation of customer funds. The Federal Reserve Board released this information on Thursday.

title: Bank of America maintains Buy rating on Nvidia citing balance sheet scale
summary: Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya reiterated a Buy rating and $350 price target for Nvidia following the company's strong earnings report. The firm argues the market underestimated Nvidia's $300 billion in AI capital commitments, which include equity investments and guarantees for partners like OpenAI. Nvidia reported $96.2 billion in quarterly revenue, driven by a 117% increase in data center sales. The bank suggests these financial commitments to the AI ecosystem are more significant than standard earnings metrics.

title: Nvidia reports doubled quarterly revenue near $100bn as CEO declares golden age
summary: Nvidia announced quarterly revenue of $96.2bn, doubling from the prior year and beating Wall Street expectations. CEO Jensen Huang stated the AI industry has reached a golden age with productive tokens. Datacenter revenue rose 117% to $89bn, while earnings per share reached $2.22. The stock rose nearly 4% following the report. Analyst Jacob Bourne noted Nvidia strengthens its position across the AI stack. The company is addressing financing concerns with a $500bn capital pool and a new Ohio datacenter project.

title: OpenAI data center head Chris Malone leaves amid executive departures
summary: OpenAI head of data centers Chris Malone has exited the company, TechCrunch reports. OpenAI stated it recently reorganized its infrastructure organization and maintains a strong team. The departure adds to 13 senior executive exits in 2026, including COO Brad Lightcap and CRO Denise Dresser. OpenAI President Greg Brockman told CNBC the turnover is not atypical given the company's spotlight. The company prepares for a 2027 public market debut with an $852 billion valuation target.

title: Tesla recalls millions of cars in China over hidden door handle safety concerns
summary: China ordered a massive recall affecting over four million vehicles, primarily Teslas, due to safety risks associated with hidden door handles. The State Administration for Market Regulation stated these handles are difficult to identify and may hinder rescue efforts during electrical failures. New regulations requiring mechanical release mechanisms will take effect in 2027, prompting manufacturers like Xiaomi, XPeng, and Geely to join the recall. Experts argue current measures are insufficient as they do not guarantee a reliable mechanical way for rescuers to enter vehicles. While similar recalls are not yet planned in the US, regulators there are reviewing emergency exit requirements. Industry analysts note that safety standards from China may eventually influence global design practices.

title: Trump signs executive order banning some foreign grid equipment
summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order declaring a national emergency to restrict foreign-made equipment in the US bulk-power system. The Department of Energy has 120 days to publish formal rules implementing the policy. Experts warn that identifying existing foreign equipment is the most difficult part of compliance. The order does not ban all foreign equipment, but requires Energy Secretary Chris Wright to establish conditions for continued use. Michael Centrella of SecurityScorecard noted the next step is providing operators with visibility into risky assets without disrupting power reliability.

title: Zambia opposition leader questioned over alleged treason amid election dispute
summary: Zambia police questioned opposition leader Brian Mundubile and his running mate over alleged treason. Mundubile surrendered after seeking safety at a human rights organization following a raid. The Zambia Police Service recorded warn and caution statements without immediate details. President Hakainde Hichilema won 60 percent of the vote and is set for a second term. Courts closed before the opposition could file an election challenge, prompting criticism from rights groups.

title: Mike Ashley criticizes Burnham's retail policies in letter to PM
summary: Sports Direct founder Mike Ashley wrote to Prime Minister Andy Burnham criticizing recent retail policies as populist reactions. Ashley argued that rising business rates and employment costs are harming businesses, calling warehouse tax proposals delusional. A Downing Street spokesperson stated Burnham aims to build a new economy supporting British business. Ashley urged the government to lower employer costs in the upcoming October 27 Budget. The businessman also questioned plans to revive Harvey Nichols and opposed restrictions on recommended retail prices.

title: Questions for Yiyang Zhuge, translator and political theorist
summary: The text outlines a planned conversation with Yiyang Zhuge, a political theorist and translator. She is an instructor at Brandeis University and a PhD candidate at Boston College. Zhuge has translated major works by Hannah Arendt and published the first Greek-to-Chinese translation of Plutarch's Moralia. She runs Princeton University Press's Political Philosophy Book Club and hosts a popular Mandarin podcast with over one million subscribers. The article lists her various media appearances and publications as background for the interview.

title: Guardian editorial says vulnerable UK households need bill help amid soaring energy debt
summary: The Guardian editorial argues that vulnerable UK households require immediate financial assistance as energy debt reaches a record £6bn. Prime Minister Andy Burnham's VAT cut on electricity is largely negated by a rising price cap linked to geopolitical tensions. The publication calls for a new social discount scheme and boosted local council funds to protect low-income families. Additionally, the editorial suggests shifting environmental costs from household bills to general taxation to support the green transition.

title: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh prepares first major Jackson Hole speech amid inflation concerns
summary: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh is scheduled to deliver his first major speech at the Jackson Hole symposium on Friday. Investors seek clarity on his inflation strategy after he previously offered no specific details. Current inflation stands at 3.7%, remaining above the Fed's 2% target. While Warsh remains vague on immediate plans, he expressed optimism that artificial intelligence will eventually lower prices by boosting productivity.

title: Links cover space data centers, AI hacks, and New Zealand education
summary: This digest links to essays on space data centers, AI security, and New Zealand education. It also includes items on whale conservation, philanthropy, and political economy.

title: Anthropic launches Model Hardware Standard for AI physical device control
summary: Anthropic released a research preview of its Model Hardware Standard framework on Thursday. Anthropic stated the system allows AI agents to operate physical lab and manufacturing instruments simultaneously. The company aims to enable autonomous workflows with minimal human intervention for tasks like drug discovery. Anthropic noted the standard works on any device with a programmable interface. The firm is sharing an early version with partners to evaluate safety before open sourcing.

title: Opinion piece contrasts Dolly Parton's philanthropy with Elon Musk's politics
summary: An opinion article contrasts the late Dolly Parton's philanthropy with the political actions of Elon Musk and other billionaires. The author argues that Parton's selfless giving offers a better model than the techno-oligarchy's approach to global change. The text notes that Musk's 2025 decision to shut down USAID programs was linked to hundreds of thousands of deaths, according to studies. The author suggests that while difficult decisions drive progress, imposing sweeping solutions without considering consequences is dangerous. The piece advocates for incremental policy testing and serving others rather than relying on faith in a future society. Social media users shared the sentiment, praising Parton's generosity while criticizing Musk's influence.

title: Trump signs order renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America
summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America in the US geographic naming service. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney pushed back, citing the name's Indigenous origins. The move escalates tensions as the US imposes 50% tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian goods. Trump stated the change is effective immediately but the order allows 30 days for updates. He suggested future renaming of other bodies of water. Ontario Premier Doug Ford dismissed the prospect as rhetoric. The lake's name comes from the Huron Indigenous people's word for lake of shining waters.

title: Massachusetts jury deliberates on first-degree murder charges against mother Lindsay Clancy
summary: A Massachusetts jury is deliberating the first-degree murder charges against Lindsay Clancy, who is accused of killing her three children. Clancy's attorney argues she suffered from postpartum psychosis, while prosecutors claim she made a calculated decision to murder them. The jury must decide between a life sentence without parole, lesser murder charges, or a finding of not guilty by reason of insanity. Closing arguments highlighted conflicting views on Clancy's mental state and her suicide attempt.

title: Glacial collapse triggers deadly floods on Nepal-Tibet border
summary: Massive landslides and flash floods caused by a glacial collapse have killed hundreds and left many missing along the Nepal-Tibet border. The US Geological Survey clarified that a glacier disintegration, not an earthquake, generated a magnitude 5.2 impact that triggered catastrophic debris flows. Scientists warn that climate change is accelerating glacier melt and permafrost degradation, increasing the risk of future landslides. Authorities report at least 389 deaths and over 900 missing people, including numerous foreign tourists from India, China, and the UK. Governments from Nepal, China, India, and the UN are coordinating search efforts and offering humanitarian aid. There are fears of secondary flooding if debris blocks rivers, prompting ongoing assessments of river stability.

title: De Minaur faces qualifier in US Open first round as draw announced
summary: The US Open draw has been announced, placing world number six Alex de Minaur against a qualifier in the first round. Thirteen Australians are competing in singles, with three more seeking qualification. Novak Djokovic will face Mariano Navone, while Daria Kasatkina opens against Paula Badosa.

title: Family fears missing woman Stephanie Cordery will become another statistic
summary: Emergency services have found no trace of Stephanie Cordery, who disappeared in northern New South Wales three weeks ago. Joyce Cordery stated the family fears the search will end without answers, noting the region often lacks sufficient resources. NSW Police described the multi-agency operation as significant, utilizing drones, search dogs, and a geo-targeted text message sent to over 68,000 phones. Deputy Captain Charlie Cohen explained that steep terrain and dense canopy hindered aerial searches. A parliamentary inquiry highlighted hundreds of unsolved missing person cases in the area. Barry Cordery said his family refuses to give up hope despite the fading optimism. Police urged anyone with information to contact Crime Stoppers.

title: Trump staff reportedly want to leave amid White House tensions
summary: New York Times correspondent Maggie Haberman reports that most of President Trump's staff want to leave the White House following Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt's departure. The article notes reported tension involving aide Natalie Harp and a confrontation between Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth regarding munitions shortages. Additionally, the White House reportedly considered firing FBI Director Kash Patel after he socialized with Olympic athletes. Recent high-profile departures include Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem and Attorney General Pam Bondi.

title: Tunisia recovers all 14 victims from migrant boat sinking off Zarzis
summary: Tunisian authorities announced the recovery of all 14 victims from a migrant boat that sank off the southeastern coast. The National Guard stated the vessel carried 15 people, with one survivor and a final death toll of 14. Search teams, including naval units and helicopters, completed the operation by Wednesday. Human Rights Observatory head Mustapha Abdelkebir confirmed the boat capsized during an attempt to reach Italy.

title: Trump administration pays $900M to RWE for wind farm cancellation
summary: A report states that a settlement ending U.S. offshore wind projects will see $900 million of a $1.2 billion payment go to a firm led by Michael Dorrell. Dorrell, a neighbor of President Trump, runs Stonespeak, which is purchasing a Louisiana liquefied natural gas project. The Trump administration denies any conflict of interest, while some Democratic lawmakers call the deal corrupt. RWE confirmed it will invest the majority of the payout in conventional energy ventures.

title: Carney rejects Trump's Lake America renaming, says Canadians will keep Lake Ontario
summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney rejected US President Donald Trump's executive order renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America. Carney stated Canadians will continue using the historic name derived from the Wendat word Ontari'io. Trump signed the order amid trade tensions and tariff disputes between the two nations. Carney emphasized that naming reality means calling it Lake Ontario then, now and always.

title: Argentina keeps same starting line-up for test against Australia
summary: Argentina has selected the same starting XV for their upcoming test match against Australia, maintaining consistency after a narrow defeat to South Africa. Coach Felipe Contepomi made only two changes to the bench while retaining key players like captain Pablo Matera. The team will face the Wallabies without several overseas-based players who were absent during the previous fixture.

title: Trump signs order renaming Lake Ontario amid escalating trade war with Canada
summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order directing the Department of the Interior to rename Lake Ontario as "Lake America" following the collapse of trade talks with Canada. Trump stated that Canada treats the US very badly and is the worst trading partner to deal with. This announcement coincides with the implementation of a 50% tariff on several Canadian imports and Canada's retaliatory tariffs on hundreds of US goods. The renaming follows a similar order Trump issued earlier in his second term to rename the Gulf of Mexico. Democratic Congressman Tim Kennedy criticized the move, arguing it wastes time that should be spent making life more affordable for working families. While the trade war escalates, Canadian officials have opted to remove seafood from their list of counter-tariffs to protect against broader economic harms. Senator Susan Collins welcomed this gesture of good faith from Canada.

title: Deadly Nepal floods kill nearly 400 as rising lake threatens new danger
summary: Catastrophic flash floods in Nepal and Tibet have killed at least 359 people and left more than 1,300 missing, with the death toll approaching 400. A nurse in the UK described how relatives were swept away by the rapid waters, while officials warn that a newly formed lake at the disaster site is rising and risks bursting. Satellite imagery indicates a glacier collapse triggered the mud and water torrent that destroyed villages and infrastructure. Scientists attribute the event to climate change, noting that unusual heat weakened ice bonds and the monsoon saturated the soil. Rescue efforts are complicated by destroyed roads and bridges, though over 100 people were rescued by helicopter. International aid is being scrambled, with the UK offering £5m and the US confirming 90 citizens remain unaccounted for. The disaster highlights growing fears that global heating is destabilizing mountain geology worldwide.

title: Switzerland plans drone battalion by 2028 for reconnaissance and defence
summary: Switzerland's defence ministry announced plans to establish a military drone battalion by 2028. The unit will handle reconnaissance, operations, and defence while supported by a new civilian-military centre. Officials stated that drones, counter-drone systems, and robotics are now a strategic priority. The ministry noted an increase in drone flights over critical infrastructure. Switzerland maintains its long-standing policy of well-armed neutrality.

title: Scientists use satellite imagery to analyze Nepal floods
summary: Earth scientists reviewed satellite imagery to determine the cause of catastrophic flooding along the Nepal-China border that killed hundreds. Geomorphologists Kristen Cook and Dan Shugar identified that a massive chunk of bedrock collapsed from the Langtang Lirung peak, taking a glacier with it. The debris maintained momentum through steep valleys, burying villages and turning the Trishuli River brown with sediment. Alton Byers, a mountain geographer, stated the event is the largest glacier flood he has seen and linked it to climate change. While Cook and Shugar noted they cannot directly link the collapse to warming trends yet, they said such events are not unexpected as permafrost weakens.

title: ICE arrests rise in Connecticut despite local opposition and protests
summary: Federal immigration authorities detained dozens of people in Danbury, Connecticut, this week despite strong local opposition. ICE data shows nationwide arrests increased significantly in June and July, with nearly 50,000 people arrested in July alone. The Trump administration's campaign continues even in Democratic-led states with laws limiting ICE power. Local officials denounce the operation as traumatizing students, while the Justice Department challenges a Connecticut law restricting ICE actions. DHS stated agents addressed public safety threats, though many detainees had no criminal record.

title: Rescuers search for 1,400 missing after Nepal-Tibet glacial collapse floods kill nearly 400
summary: Rescue teams are searching for more than 1,400 people missing after flash floods and landslides struck the Nepal-Tibet border, raising the death toll to 392. The US Geological Survey stated the disaster was caused by a glacial collapse that triggered a vast flow of icy debris. Many of the missing are foreign tourists and Hindu pilgrims returning from Mount Kailash. Nepali police have recovered 389 bodies, while authorities warn of a potential second flood due to debris blocking the valley. Chinese Premier Li Qiang visited the area to oversee relief efforts, and international aid promises are beginning to arrive.

title: Thieves steal most of Villena Museum's Bronze Age gold collection in rapid raid
summary: Thieves raided the Villena Museum in Spain on Thursday morning, stealing nearly the entire Treasure of Villena collection. A town council spokesman stated the operation lasted only four minutes and was highly professional. Mayor Fulgencio Cerdan expressed devastation, noting the gold alone is worth approximately $2 million. The heist represents the latest in a series of high-profile museum thefts across Europe recently.

title: Ratko Mladic, former Bosnian Serb commander, dies at 84 in The Hague prison
summary: Ratko Mladic, the former commander-in-chief of the Bosnian Serb army, died at the age of 84 in a prison hospital in The Hague. The International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY) classified the 1995 Srebrenica massacre, in which more than 8,300 Muslim men and boys were killed, as genocide and held Mladic directly responsible. He was also found liable for the shelling of Sarajevo and other war crimes during the Bosnian War. Mladic evaded arrest for 16 years before being captured in 2011 and was sentenced to life in prison in 2017, a verdict upheld in 2021. Although he consistently denied responsibility and viewed himself as a defender of Serbian interests, international officials hailed the final verdict as a historic signal of accountability.

title: Seven French presidential candidates clash in first debate before 2027 election
summary: Seven French presidential candidates debated economic strategies at a forum organized by employer federation MEDEF. Marine Le Pen proposed a 125 billion euro cost-cutting plan, while Jean-Luc Mélenchon urged wage increases to prevent recession. Centrist Édouard Philippe accused Mélenchon of risking France's banking access. Polls suggest a potential runoff between Mélenchon and Le Pen, raising concerns about vote splitting among moderate candidates.

title: Trump signs order renaming Lake America in U.S.
summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America within the United States. The President stated the change is effective immediately and cannot force Canada to adopt the new name. This action occurred as the U.S. imposed 50% tariffs on $20 billion of Canadian goods. Trump suggested future renaming of the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans may follow. Canada responded with retaliatory tariffs on American goods.

title: Tunisia places most regions on high alert during second heatwave
summary: Tunisia faces a second intense heatwave with temperatures reaching 49.8C in Kairouan. The National Meteorological Institute placed most regions on high alert for two days. Officials urge citizens to stay hydrated while crowds seek relief at Mediterranean beaches. President Kais Saied blamed premeditated acts for recent power cuts and water scarcity. Recent demonstrations have called for Saied's ousting amid demands for improved basic services.

title: Video shows mudslide surging through Gyirong port in China
summary: Surveillance footage shows a mudslide hitting the Gyirong port in China, with CCTV reporting major casualties on the Nepalese side. AFP verified the video using satellite data after it was removed from Chinese platforms. Nepalese authorities reported at least 270 deaths and 823 missing, while Chinese state media cited three deaths and 558 missing. The US Geological Survey attributed the disaster to a glacial collapse rather than an earthquake. Nearly 800 Chinese emergency workers were deployed, with warnings of further flooding.

title: Documentary explores Barcelona woman who lied about surviving 9/11
summary: A new documentary titled La superviviente examines the case of Alicia Esteve Head, who fabricated a story about surviving the September 11 attacks. The film reveals that the woman known as Tania Head never entered the World Trade Center but instead constructed a compelling narrative of loss and resilience.
