title: Bharat Petroleum chief says no logistical issues with lower ethanol blend
summary: Bharat Petroleum Chairman Sanjay Khanna stated that the company faces no logistical challenges if a lower ethanol blend is introduced alongside E20 petrol. The firm clarified that reports suggesting a proposal to replace the 20% ethanol variant with a 10% blend are incorrect. Director Vetsa Ramkrishna Gupta reported that crude requirements for September are secured and October supplies are about 50-55% complete. Khanna also warned that a ban on Russian oil could create significant pressure given that Russian crude forms 35-40% of Indian OMCs' oil basket.

title: Kerala government sanctions first phase of KSRTC bus terminal at Karikkamury
summary: The Kerala government issued technical sanction for the first phase of the KSRTC bus terminal at Karikkamury. An official stated the Public Works Department will invite tenders in early September for the ₹13-crore project. The initial single-storey structure will be completed in approximately a year. Private buses will not be permitted in the new terminal. MP Hibi Eden emphasized preventing waterlogging and ensuring structural stability.

title: India and US officials discuss nuclear energy cooperation in Washington
summary: Atomic Energy Commission chairperson A K Mohanty and US Energy Secretary Chris Wright discussed strengthening Indo-US nuclear ties in Washington. Insiders noted the talks support India's goal of 100 GW capacity by 2047. The SHANTI Act passed in December 2025 allows private sector participation. American firms expressed interest in setting up plants in India. The meeting preceded the launch of the ATLAS initiative by the IAEA.

title: Congress rejects NC invitation to join Omar Abdullah government in J&K
summary: J&K Congress president Tariq Hamid Karra stated the party declined an invitation from the National Conference to join the Omar Abdullah government. Karra explained that Congress maintains a principled stand against joining the ministry until J&K's statehood is restored. The party affirmed it remains an ally of the NC government but will not compromise on constitutional rights. Congress leaders indicated continued support for the NC administration while reserving the right to raise issues like inflation and power tariffs.

title: Meta's $18 billion teen safety settlement requires TikTok and YouTube to follow suit
summary: Meta has agreed to an $18 billion settlement regarding teen safety on Facebook and Instagram, but the full amount depends on rival platforms adopting similar rules. The deal, announced Wednesday, imposes strict usage limits and safety measures on Meta's apps while requiring state funds for youth wellness programs. Approximately $5.3 billion of the settlement is contingent on TikTok and YouTube agreeing to comparable restrictions and paying their own settlements. Meta argues that without industry-wide standards, teenagers will simply migrate to less-regulated platforms. Currently, TikTok and YouTube have not publicly committed to the proposed framework, though both face separate legal challenges regarding children's privacy.

title: Police Apprehend Teen for Illegal Firearm in Instagram Video
summary: Police in northeast Delhi arrested a 17-year-old boy for displaying an illegal firearm in an Instagram video. Officers seized a countrymade pistol from the teenager's possession during a raid on Wednesday. Authorities registered a case under Section 25 of the Arms Act on August 26. Officials stated that further investigation is currently underway.

title: Nvidia reportedly plans $13 billion acquisition of open AI platform Hugging Face
summary: Nvidia is reportedly planning a $13 billion deal to acquire Hugging Face, a major platform for open-weight artificial intelligence models. The news emerged alongside Nvidia's report of doubled quarterly revenue and a 7% share price increase. Hugging Face previously rejected a $500 million Nvidia investment due to concerns over investor control. The proposed acquisition creates a contradiction as Nvidia would gain significant influence over the open AI ecosystem it aims to support. Nvidia seeks to maintain its dominance against competitors like OpenAI and Google by securing access to millions of developers. The deal represents a high multiple of Hugging Face's $150 million annual revenue, suggesting Nvidia values the company's developer network more than current earnings. Critics worry the move could undermine open-source AI principles and increase concentration of power in the industry.

title: TCS cuts variable pay for mid and senior staff while juniors get full bonus
summary: Moneycontrol reported that Tata Consultancy Services reduced variable pay for mid and senior employees to 60-70% in Q1, while junior staff received full payouts. The company faces margin pressure despite AI investments. TCS did not comment on the report. Meanwhile, TCS stock fell sharply as top Indian firms saw market value declines. CEO K Krithivasan plans to create 5,900-8,900 forward-deployed engineers representing 1-1.5% of the workforce.

title: NVIDIA reports record revenue but faces margin pressure from rising costs
summary: NVIDIA reported second-quarter revenue of $96.2 billion, more than doubling from the previous period, while adjusted profit reached $2.22 per share. The company expects revenue to grow by 70% in 2028, though investors are questioning the sustainability of this pace. CFO Colette Kress stated that demand acceleration continues even at the company's current scale, with customer forecasts indicating growth could double next year. However, experts warn that rising costs, particularly for memory chips, are squeezing profit margins. Viram Shah of Vested Finance predicts margins will fall from 75% to between 71% and 72% by January due to supply constraints. To protect profitability, NVIDIA may need to raise prices next year, a move that could face resistance from customers.

title: RBI reports manufacturing operating profit growth improved to 21.3% in Q1
summary: The Reserve Bank of India reports that manufacturing operating profit growth reached 21.3% in Q1 2026-27. Sales growth for listed private non-financial companies accelerated to 19.4% year-on-year. Raw material expenses for manufacturers rose 27.5% due to global supply chain disruptions. Staff costs increased across manufacturing, IT, and services sectors. Operating profit margins improved sequentially across all major sectors analyzed.

title: FISME warns RBI NBFC credit curbs could raise MSME borrowing costs
summary: The Federation of Indian MSMEs (FISME) cautions that the Reserve Bank of India's proposal to ban revolving credit from NBFCs may increase borrowing costs for micro, small and medium enterprises. FISME argues that a blanket ban on flexible credit products would create operational inefficiencies and push businesses toward less regulated lenders. The organization urges the regulator to adopt a targeted approach that preserves legitimate working capital tools while addressing risks like loan evergreening. Anil Bhardwaj, Secretary General of FISME, stated that business working capital differs fundamentally from consumer revolving credit and requires distinct regulation. FISME has submitted feedback proposing safeguards such as fixed limits and annual renewals to balance regulatory concerns with business needs.

title: Tata Motors rebrands passenger vehicles as Tata.Cars to align with Indian aspirations
summary: Tata Motors announced a rebranding strategy where Tata.Cars becomes the primary customer-facing identity while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles remains the legal entity. CEO Shailesh Chandra stated the move reflects growing Indian confidence and a unified expression of the portfolio. The automaker also unveiled Tata.ev for its electric vehicle range. In July 2026, the company reported total sales of 63,760 units, marking a 59% year-on-year increase.

title: US stocks rise as Nvidia leads gains while investors watch Fed signals
summary: US stocks opened higher on Thursday, driven by strong earnings from major technology companies. The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.8%, the S&P 500 gained 0.4%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average increased 35 points. Nvidia was the primary driver, with shares jumping 7% after the chipmaker beat expectations and provided a strong revenue outlook. UBS remains confident in the wider AI growth story, though it warns of potential volatility. Other semiconductor stocks like Broadcom and Marvell Technology also moved higher. Investors are closely watching the Federal Reserve's Jackson Hole symposium and recent jobless claims data. Additionally, reports suggest the Trump administration is considering new tariffs on semiconductors and related products.

title: Nvidia earnings boost Wall Street as Salesforce and CrowdStrike stocks surge
summary: Wall Street indices rose on Thursday, driven by a technology rally following Nvidia's strong earnings forecast. The S&P 500 gained 0.7%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 0.3%, and the Nasdaq Composite increased 1.4%. Nvidia shares jumped 7.3% after reporting quarterly revenue of $96.2 billion, more than double the previous year's level. Salesforce shares soared 20.7% after the company stated artificial intelligence contributed to a record quarter, while CrowdStrike stock jumped 14.5% following better-than-expected earnings. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh is scheduled to speak at the Jackson Hole gathering on Friday. Treasury yields remained steady at 4.66% for the 10-year benchmark. Other market movements included HP shares dropping 9% and Moderna stock declining 4.6% due to a bond sale announcement.

title: Grandma chats with ChatGPT believing it is a human
summary: Abhiruchi Bhatti shared a video of her grandmother, Nani, conversing with ChatGPT while believing the AI was a real person. Bhatti stated she lacked the heart to correct the misunderstanding. The clip sparked divided reactions online, with some praising the innocence while others criticized the video as a mockery of the elderly. Sounak Mukhopadhyay reported on the viral social media exchange.

title: RBI data shows India Inc sales growth rose to 19.4% in Q1 FY27
summary: The Reserve Bank of India reported that aggregate sales growth for listed non-government non-financial companies accelerated to 19.4% year-on-year in the first quarter of FY27. Manufacturing emerged as a primary driver, with private sector sales expanding 21.4%, led by the automobile, petroleum, and electrical machinery industries. Operating profit growth jumped to 21.3% for manufacturing firms, while debt-servicing capacity improved across sectors. The RBI noted that elevated input costs and global supply-chain disruptions remain key factors for companies to monitor as they seek to sustain margins.

title: Anthropic orders San Francisco staff to work from home amid potential security strike
summary: Anthropic instructed San Francisco employees to work remotely on Monday and Tuesday following a warning from security contractor Allied Universal about a possible guard strike. The Service Employees International Union stated no strike vote has been called or threatened. Anthropic is not part of ongoing wage negotiations between the union and Allied Universal but faces operational disruption if guards stop working. The company declined to comment on the instruction while Allied Universal emphasized a focus on safe operations. This precaution aligns with recent security threats against AI industry staff and Anthropic's upcoming initial public offering.

title: Mumbai Police Arrest Nine in Fake Delivery Franchise Scam
summary: Mumbai Crime Branch police arrested nine individuals from a Malad call centre for allegedly defrauding at least 20 people. The Mumbai Crime Branch police raided Insta Transfer Biz Pvt. Ltd. on August 24, 2026, after receiving confidential information about the operation. Police seized over 100 franchise agreements and electronic devices valued at approximately ₹25 lakh. A local court remanded the accused to police custody until August 28. The investigation remains ongoing as authorities identify additional victims.

title: Abhishek Banerjee alleges political vendetta after TMC office raid
summary: Trinamool Congress national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee alleged a political vendetta following police action at a party office in Kolkata. He claimed workers were manhandled and the signboard was removed without due process. Banerjee stated the party has moved the Calcutta High Court, with the hearing scheduled for Friday. He questioned the validity of the demolition order and accused BJP cadres of involvement. The party plans to present video evidence and seek legal action against officials.

title: NLSIU cancels 34th convocation citing unavoidable circumstances
summary: The National Law School of India University canceled its 34th annual convocation due to unavoidable circumstances and will confer degrees in absentia. The registrar stated students may receive certificates via courier or campus collection. This decision follows student and alumni objections to inviting the Chief Justice of India and Bar Council of India chairman, though the university did not attribute the cancellation to those protests. Alumna Mousami Das expressed disappointment over the missed milestone.

title: Bombay High Court questions Disha Salian probe procedure
summary: The Bombay High Court questioned the Maharashtra government over procedural lapses in the Disha Salian death investigation. Justices S.V. Kotwal and R.R. Bhonsale scrutinized the reopening of the Accidental Death Report and noted discrepancies in the post-mortem and witness statements. The bench emphasized the need for a lawful closure while rejecting political arguments. Arguments regarding the petition continue on Friday.

title: Trump says Putin will not attack NATO; Kremlin dismisses reports as false
summary: President Trump stated he does not believe Russia will attack NATO territory following his own assessment of talks with Vladimir Putin. He downplayed CIA Director John Ratcliffe's visit to Moscow, describing it as routine rather than a warning mission. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov dismissed reports of a potential Russian strike as scare stories with no connection to reality. Despite these assurances, intelligence agencies continue monitoring hybrid threats across Europe.

title: Indians lead UK immigration, citizenship, and voluntary return figures
summary: The Home Office released statistics showing Indians lead UK immigration across multiple categories. Indians received the most work visas, study visa applications, and visitor visas. They also topped the list for British citizenship grants and voluntary returns. Conversely, Indians ranked eighth for asylum claims with a low grant rate.

title: Police suspect suicide-murder after woman and two daughters found dead in Karnataka
summary: Police in Tumakuru, Karnataka, suspect a suicide-murder after finding Rabia and her two daughters dead at their residence. Authorities found froth in the victims' mouths but await postmortem results to confirm the cause of death. A case has been registered against Rabia's husband, Srikanth, who faces allegations of harassment and has a prior criminal record. Investigators are examining whether the mother poisoned her children before taking her own life.

title: Subhash Chandra clarifies he is only a personal guarantor with no borrowed funds
summary: Zee Group founder Subhash Chandra stated he has not borrowed money from any lender and serves only as a personal guarantor. He clarified that the total claim against him by objectors is ₹3,992 crore, not the full ₹22,000 crore. The statement noted that ₹620 crore of this claim has been settled and ₹1,063 crore is offered by borrower entities. Chandra added that the borrowing entities have repaid ₹43,000 crore and assured settlement of any remaining dues.

title: Aragen Life Sciences files DRHP for 800 crore fresh issue
summary: Aragen Life Sciences filed a Draft Red Herring Prospectus with SEBI for an IPO. The company plans a fresh issue of 800 crore rupees and an offer for sale of up to 27,329,192 equity shares. Proceeds will primarily repay borrowings and fund capital expenditure at Hyderabad and Bengaluru facilities. The firm, formerly GVK Biosciences, provides integrated solutions across the drug development lifecycle.

title: RBI special forex windows attract $40.8B, economists predict $70B-$100B total
summary: The Reserve Bank of India reported $40.81 billion in foreign exchange inflows under special programs by July 31, with FCNR(B) deposits reaching $36.72 billion. Economists from Karur Vysya Bank, IDFC First Bank, Emkay Global Financial Services, and Bank of Baroda estimate total mobilisation could reach $70 billion to over $100 billion. These revised forecasts suggest a potential balance of payments surplus of $35 billion to $40 billion in FY27.

title: Mohandas Pai urges Infosys to recall Nandan Nilekani amid leadership vacuum
summary: Former Infosys board member Mohandas Pai told ET Now that the company faces a leadership vacuum due to a poor CEO appointment three years ago. Pai noted that three extraordinary individuals appointed in June 2011 have all exited, including Ashok Vemuri, V Balakrishnan, and BG Srinivas. He argued that the entire layer of leaders below the executive board has departed, creating a need for a new succession plan. Pai suggested that Nandan Nilekani should return to mentor the next generation of managers and bridge the gap between the executive chairman and emerging leaders. He stated that a radical change is expected within the next two to three months as senior personnel step down. Pai emphasized that while an external team is difficult to find for a firm with 160,000 employees and $25 billion to $30 billion in market value, recalling Nilekani would be a great strategy.

title: Bihar students protest exam leaks amid job fears
summary: Student protests in Patna escalated to violence after allegations of Bihar Public Service Commission exam paper leaks. Aspirants demand exam cancellation and cite irregularities in recruitment processes. Economic expert Santosh Mehrotra attributes unrest to chronic unemployment and lack of government appointments. Rahul Gandhi and Tejashwi Yadav criticized police actions against demonstrators. Unemployment rates in Bihar exceed national averages, fueling desperation for government jobs. Political leaders call for transparency and dialogue with protesters.

title: NVIDIA announces upcoming financial conference presentation for investors
summary: NVIDIA announced it will present at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference on Thursday, Sept. 10. The company stated that interested parties can listen to the live audio webcast at investor.nvidia.com, with replays available for 90 days afterward.

title: Anthropic and OpenAI Lead AI Stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
summary: Anthropic and OpenAI are headlining the AI Stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 in San Francisco. The event, presented by Google for Startups, explores enterprise AI deployment, security, and new business models. Key sessions feature leaders from Anthropic, OpenAI, Databricks, Okta, and others discussing practical challenges in the industry. Attendees can learn about pricing strategies, agent security, and the emerging role of GTM engineers. Ticket sales are currently active with a limited-time discount available.

title: Anthropic faces new Claude Code Opus 5 auto mode vulnerability
summary: Anthropic recently set Claude Code Opus 5 auto mode as the default to protect against prompt injection attacks. Johann Rehberger discovered an attack that works 80% of the time by tricking the agent into executing local code. In some cases, auto mode blocked the agent from terminating malware processes. Rehberger recommends running agents in sandboxes with restricted network access.

title: Anthropic launches Model Hardware Standard for AI physical control
summary: Anthropic introduces the Model Hardware Standard to help AI agents control physical devices. The research preview aims to streamline experimental setups by providing a common interface for disparate components. Anthropic Technical Staffer Alek Kemeny notes the system could reduce setup time from weeks to minutes. Integrating the standard with AI models allows scientists to interact with devices using natural language commands.

title: Lawsuit claims xAI trained Grok on child abuse images
summary: A lawsuit alleges that xAI trained its Grok models on child sex abuse materials. Plaintiff Jane Doe states that the company identified AI-generated images depicting her. She claims xAI stored these outputs to further train the model. The complaint notes that regulators and courts are currently investigating the extent of this issue.

title: Google expands AI Mode to track flights and book hotels
summary: Google announced on Thursday that AI Mode can now track flight prices and assist with hotel bookings. The tool displays options from over 300 airlines and allows users to build itineraries or set price alerts. Hotel bookings will route through integrated partners like Booking.com and Hilton, with Google handling payment. Additionally, the feature now shows costs in points or miles globally.

title: PyTorch Conference North America 2026 Announces Core Sessions on Compiler and Runtime Work
summary: The PyTorch Conference North America 2026 will take place in San Jose, CA, on October 20–21, featuring a Core PyTorch program focused on the framework's internal machinery. Speakers from Meta, Red Hat, Huawei, and other organizations will present sessions covering compiler internals, distributed communication, and release engineering. The conference agenda includes talks on out-of-tree release readiness, AI agents for CI triage, and static tensor shape checking. Additional sessions address device-aware tensor layouts, nested graph breaks in torch.compile, and zero-GPU memory estimation for distributed training. Hardware integration topics include IBM Spyre accelerator support, AMD GPU symmetric memory via rocSHMEM, and Intel GPU scaling with XCCL. The event aims to discuss APIs, implementation work, and performance results shaping how PyTorch is built and extended.

title: ZDNET author tests old iPhone 4 and finds it mostly useless
summary: A ZDNET author tested an iPhone 4 from 2011 to determine if the device still holds value or should be recycled. The author reported that while the phone powered on and charged, its battery lasted only 15 minutes of use. Modern security protocols prevented the device from connecting to iCloud or Safari, rendering apps and web browsing unusable. Although the phone could connect to Wi-Fi and function as a media player via a Mac, its 3G network support is obsolete in the United States. The author concluded that the phone has no resale value and is best suited for recycling after a factory reset. ZDNET noted that older models like the iPhone 5s and iPhone 8 retain slightly more utility and value compared to the iPhone 4.

title: NVIDIA shares debugging lessons for closing AI infrastructure performance gaps
summary: NVIDIA reports that identical AI clusters can show 8% to 12% training throughput differences due to configuration choices in the kernel, hypervisor, and BIOS. The company details four case studies where specific tuning changes closed these gaps to meet Exemplar Cloud validation thresholds. Engineers can use these diagnostic patterns to identify issues like SMMU serialization, CPU power settings, and NCCL topology mismatches before formal validation. The article notes that gaps often compound from multiple layers, requiring checks on virtualization readiness, process placement, and fabric behavior. NVIDIA advises running diagnostics inside the actual workload container rather than on the host to catch silent configuration errors. These preflight steps help rule out common platform risks early, though they do not guarantee a pass if issues only appear under specific validation workloads.

title: Tutorial shows how to self-host a validated AI coding assistant using NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails
summary: The article explains how to self-host a validated AI coding assistant on NVIDIA infrastructure. It details deploying StarCoder2-7B with NeMo Guardrails policies, CI verification for hallucinated packages, and metrics loops to track defect rates.

title: OpenAI releases Privacy Filter for scalable web apps
summary: OpenAI released Privacy Filter, a 1.5B-parameter model for detecting private information. The authors report three scalable web applications built on gradio.Server to demonstrate its use. These tools include a document explorer, image anonymizer, and smart redaction paste.

title: DeepSeek launches V4 model with 1M-token context for agentic workloads
summary: DeepSeek introduces DeepSeek-V4, an open model designed to handle long-running agentic tasks without breaking. The architecture achieves efficiency by splitting attention into Compressed Sparse Attention and Heavily Compressed Attention mechanisms. DeepSeek-V4-Pro requires 27% of single-token inference FLOPs and 10% of KV cache memory compared to DeepSeek-V3.2. The model preserves reasoning content across user message boundaries when tool calls are involved. DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Max scores 67.9 on Terminal Bench 2.0 and 80.6 on SWE Verified. Four checkpoints are available on the Hub, supporting three reasoning modes including Think Max. The authors report that the model uses FP8 storage for most KV entries and BF16 only for RoPE dimensions.

title: Google introduces Gemini Robotics-ER 1.6 for enhanced embodied reasoning
summary: Google announced the release of Gemini Robotics-ER 1.6, a model designed to improve robot reasoning in physical environments. The company stated the update enhances spatial understanding and adds instrument reading capabilities developed with Boston Dynamics. Google reported significant improvements over previous versions in tasks like pointing and success detection. The model is now available to developers through the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.

title: Google launches Gemini 3.1 Flash Live for improved audio AI
summary: Google announced Gemini 3.1 Flash Live, its highest-quality audio and voice model designed for real-time dialogue. The company stated the model leads benchmarks in complex function calling and reasoning while offering improved tonal understanding. Google reported the model is available to developers, enterprises, and general users across various products. The firm noted that all generated audio includes an imperceptible watermark to detect synthetic content.

title: Google Research 2025: Bolder breakthroughs, bigger impact
summary: Google Research Vice President Yossi Matias announced that the team delivered pioneering breakthroughs in 2025, accelerating the translation of research into real-world solutions. The report highlights advancements in foundational AI, quantum computing, and scientific discovery tools. Key developments include the introduction of generative UI in Gemini 3 and the release of the LLM Re-Ranker to improve retrieval accuracy. Google also achieved a verifiable quantum advantage with its Willow chip, running the Quantum Echoes algorithm 13,000 times faster than classical methods. In scientific applications, the company released AI co-scientist to help generate hypotheses and DeepSomatic to identify genetic variants in cancer cells. Earth AI capabilities now cover over 2 billion people with flood forecasting, while the FireSat constellation aims to detect small wildfires globally. Additionally, Google expanded its multilingual models to over 140 languages and launched new tools for neuroscience and climate resilience. The team emphasized continued investment in efficiency and cultural intelligence to ensure responsible global impact.

title: Google tests Gemini AI tool for verifying theoretical computer science papers at STOC 2026
summary: Google Research scientists developed the Paper Assistant Tool to help theoretical computer scientists verify their conference submissions before peer review. The system, powered by Gemini 2.5 Deep Think, provided automated feedback on logic errors and typos within 24 hours of submission. Over 100 authors participated in the experiment at STOC 2026, reporting positive results regarding the tool's ability to identify critical bugs and its neutral tone. While the AI occasionally struggled with complex notation, experts successfully filtered the output to extract valuable insights. The project aims to augment rather than replace human peer review, with 88% of participants expressing strong interest in continuous access to such tools.

title: Mistral launches new Agents API for building autonomous AI systems
summary: Mistral AI announced a new Agents API designed to enable the creation of autonomous AI systems capable of performing complex tasks. The company stated that this framework combines powerful language models with built-in connectors for code execution, web search, and image generation. Mistral reported that agents utilizing web search capabilities achieved significantly higher accuracy scores on the SimpleQA benchmark compared to those without. The API supports persistent memory across conversations and allows developers to orchestrate multiple agents to handle specific parts of a workflow. Mistral described the system as a backbone for enterprise-grade agentic platforms that simplify implementing agentic use cases.

title: Mistral AI releases Mistral Small 3.1 with 128k context window
summary: Mistral AI announced the release of Mistral Small 3.1, an open-source model licensed under Apache 2.0. The company states the model features improved text performance, multimodal understanding, and a context window of up to 128k tokens. Mistral Small 3.1 reportedly outperforms comparable proprietary models like Gemma 3 and GPT-4o Mini while delivering inference speeds of 150 tokens per second. The model is designed for low-latency applications and can run on a single RTX 4090 or a Mac with 32GB RAM. Mistral AI made the base and instruct checkpoints available for download on Hugging Face and via API on its developer playground.

title: Lovelytics launches Databricks-based control tower to diagnose QSR performance issues
summary: Lovelytics has introduced a new QSR Executive Performance Control Tower built on Databricks to help leaders identify the root causes of performance changes. The tool connects signals across corporate performance, supply chains, and operations to explain why metrics shift rather than just reporting the numbers. By linking metric changes to likely drivers like guest demand or ingredient availability, the system provides a shared starting point for corporate and franchisees. This approach aims to protect restaurant-level margins before the next planning cycle closes. The solution adapts to different organizational priorities, translating complex data into actionable daily briefings for quick-service restaurant leaders.

title: Databricks partners launch vertical AI solutions on Lakebase
summary: Databricks partners have introduced a suite of industry-specific solutions built on the Lakebase platform to address unique operational challenges in sectors like finance, insurance, and retail. The authors report that Lakebase adoption has grown at more than twice the rate of the company's data warehousing product since its launch. These new tools combine deep vertical expertise with the platform's serverless Postgres capabilities to enable real-time decision-making and unified governance. Specific offerings include an AI-native claims operations platform for insurers, a regulation change agent for financial services, and a near real-time credit card fraud detection framework. Partners such as Capgemini, Impetus, and LTM are delivering production-ready accelerators that reduce manual effort and accelerate processes like claims adjudication from days to minutes. The solutions leverage Databricks Genie and Mosaic AI agents to provide conversational insights and automated risk scoring. By unifying transactional and analytical systems, these tools aim to eliminate data silos and improve compliance auditability across regulated industries.

title: ZDNET reviewer prefers base Pixel 11 over Pro models despite higher price
summary: A ZDNET reviewer states that the Google Pixel 11 base model remains their favorite phone among the four launched this summer. The article notes the device features a new Hibiscus color, a 6.3-inch AMOLED display, and a slimmed-down camera bar with a customizable LED indicator. Although the base model costs $899 for 256GB storage, the reviewer highlights that AI features like Rambler and Magic Capture perform exceptionally well on the minimal hardware. The reviewer points out limitations such as a 3,000-nit brightness cap and 30W wired charging compared to Pro models. Ultimately, ZDNET suggests the Pixel 11 is the safest purchase option if buyers find a trade-in offer or wait for holiday deals.

title: Researchers propose rubric-based alignment for grounded open-domain question answering
summary: Authors Aman Saini and colleagues introduce a rubric-based reward framework for open-domain question answering. The method generates query-specific rubrics grounded in retrieved evidence to improve answer quality. Averaged across three evaluation axes, the approach improves over instruction-tuned baselines by 6.5%. The authors report consistent gains across all evaluation datasets using this fine-grained supervision technique.

title: Failed Pizza Robots Prompt New Attempts at Automation
summary: Robotic pizza makers have struggled to succeed, with Seattle's Moto Pizza losing its equipment after supplier Picnic shut down. Analysts note that food preparation bots often lack the efficiency of humans, yet some entrepreneurs remain optimistic about future automation. While some chains prioritize consistent taste over artisanal experiences, others insist human interaction remains vital for customer satisfaction. Despite past failures, intellectual property from defunct companies continues to influence new food technology startups. Experts suggest the market was simply not ready for fully autonomous pizza production in the past.

title: AI Agents Hack Systems, Prompting US and China to Consider Cooperation
summary: WIRED senior writer Will Knight reports that researchers in the US and China are increasingly concerned about AI agents hacking systems. Knight observed that while the AI race is often viewed as a zero-sum game, shared fears over cybersecurity are driving interest in collaboration. During a visit to China, Knight found that local researchers prioritize reliability and guardrails for economically useful models rather than pursuing godlike intelligence. He noted that both nations worry about hackers misusing AI agents or systems running amok, creating a potential basis for joint safety rules. Knight also highlighted that a researcher he met could not collaborate with US counterparts due to export restrictions, despite wanting to share cybersecurity benchmarks. The article suggests that establishing communication lines and technical agreements could help prevent unpredictable systemic issues caused by rogue AI.

title: Georgia Cop Misused Flock Software to Track Ex and Another Officer
summary: WIRED obtained documents detailing how Alpharetta Police Department patrolman Dustin Bozzo allegedly misused Flock Safety software to track vehicles. Internal reports indicate Bozzo searched for his former romantic partner's license plate 56 times and another officer's plate 29 times between March and May. Lieutenant Jason Hiott stated Bozzo was placed on paid leave and resigned after an investigation. Police Chief Trent Lindgren confirmed the department took immediate action regarding the misuse. The internal report notes Bozzo admitted to a workplace romance that violated city policy, though he denied malicious intent. Investigators found his search categories were often selected as quick keystrokes rather than genuine traffic concerns. An ongoing criminal investigation is currently underway within the department's Criminal Investigations Division.

title: Readers question word choice and note Christmas catalogues
summary: David Jones writes to question the classification of a grocer as an old occupation. Other readers comment on The Terminator and the arrival of Christmas catalogues.

title: Israeli doctors use AI on mammograms to detect heart disease in women
summary: Israeli researchers analyzed over 97,000 mammograms to train an AI model that identifies cardiovascular conditions. The system reliably detected strokes, high blood pressure, and coronary heart disease within the scans. Experts presented these findings at a major European cardiology conference, suggesting routine breast screenings could become dual-purpose tools. Medical leaders welcome the potential for earlier detection but note that establishing clinical reliability remains the next challenge.

title: Meta settles with US states over child safety and data practices
summary: Meta agreed to an $18bn settlement with nearly every US state to implement new child safety measures on Facebook and Instagram. The deal includes time limits, screen time warnings, and enhanced parental controls, though Meta has not admitted wrongdoing. While these rules currently apply only to US children, experts suggest they could set a global precedent for other social media platforms. The UK government is monitoring the situation closely, noting its own stricter plans to ban social media for under-16s by 2027. Meta also urged competitors like TikTok and YouTube to adopt similar safety features to ensure a level playing field. Funds from the settlement will be distributed to states for mental health and education programs, excluding Florida and New Mexico. Privacy concerns remain as Meta must now use young users' data solely for age estimation.

title: MIT researchers use large language models to help robots follow vague instructions
summary: Researchers at MIT's Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory have developed a new method to teach robots using fewer demonstrations and clearer instructions. The team, led by Minyoung Hwang, created Masked Inverse Reinforcement Learning, which uses large language models to interpret ambiguous human commands and prioritize relevant environmental details. This system allows robots to safely navigate around obstacles like laptops without explicit warnings. According to the study, the approach correctly identified user preferences 15 percent more often than comparable baselines. The method requires nearly five times less demonstration data than previous techniques. The researchers plan to integrate cameras into the system to enable robots to visually identify and ignore irrelevant objects in their surroundings.

title: MIT faculty discuss curiosity-driven science and funding challenges
summary: Scientific American published a special section featuring MIT faculty commentary on the value of curiosity-driven research. President Sally Kornbluth emphasized that investing in American science is not a gamble but yields vast returns. The article highlights various initiatives, including Curiosity on a Mission and the Generative AI Impact Consortium, aimed at solving real-world problems. Faculty members like Robert Langer and Alan Guth expressed optimism about the resilience of the innovation ecosystem despite current uncertainties. However, concerns were raised regarding federal funding instability at the NIH and NSF, as well as immigration issues for international scientists. The piece also profiles students and alumni working on diverse projects, from Alzheimer's treatments to fusion power and earthquake safety, underscoring the importance of collaboration across disciplines.

title: NIST Physicists Achieve High-Fidelity Control of Unruly Molecules
summary: NIST physicists have demonstrated high-fidelity control over a calcium monohydride molecular ion, overcoming the difficulty of managing molecules' complex rotation and vibration. The team utilized quantum logic spectroscopy, employing a helper calcium ion to monitor the molecule's state via laser-induced flashes. This method allowed researchers to cool the molecule and maintain its quantum state for approximately 18 seconds in a cryogenic environment. The experiment achieved a 99.8% success rate in manipulating the molecule's rotation, providing thousands of measurement opportunities before thermal radiation disrupts the state. NIST physicist Dietrich Leibfried noted that this sensitivity could be a blessing for quantum technologies. The study, published in Physical Review Letters, suggests these tools can be adapted for various molecules, potentially enabling precise control over chemical reactions and new quantum sensors.

title: NIST releases new guidelines to secure smart speakers for home health care
summary: The National Institute of Standards and Technology released new guidelines to mitigate cybersecurity and privacy risks in telehealth smart home integration. Ron Pulivarti, a cybersecurity specialist at NIST's National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence, explained that smart speakers can expose confidential medical data to attackers. The publication outlines threat scenarios and recommends encryption and network segmentation to protect patients and providers. These guidelines build on prior NIST work and draw from the Cybersecurity Framework and IoT Core Baseline.

title: Waymo warns Tesla strategy is a false summit in autonomy
summary: Waymo published ten AI lessons derived from over 200 million fully autonomous miles, implicitly criticizing Tesla's self-driving approach. The company stated that upgrading driver-assist systems to full autonomy is a false summit requiring purpose-built systems instead. Waymo emphasized that cameras alone cannot ensure safety, advocating for sensor fusion including lidar and radar. The company also warned against relying on end-to-end neural networks, describing them as untrustworthy black boxes. Currently, Waymo serves over 500,000 paid rides weekly while Tesla operates a smaller unsupervised fleet. Waymo head of AI foundations Srikanth Thirumalai framed these lessons around safety and their operational record. The article notes Tesla has driven only 380,000 unsupervised miles compared to Waymo's daily output. Experts suggest Tesla's incremental upgrade path may not reach true autonomy levels.

title: Dolly Parton's Humanitarian Legacy Contrasts With Elon Musk's Philanthropy
summary: CleanTechnica contrasts the humanitarian efforts of Dolly Parton with the philanthropic record of Elon Musk. The authors report that Parton, who died in August 2026, used her wealth to fund education, disaster relief, and medical research, delivering over 332 million books globally. In contrast, a New York Times investigation suggests Musk's foundation has been haphazard and largely self-serving. The article notes the foundation failed to distribute required assets and that many donations benefited Musk's own businesses. Furthermore, the authors claim Musk criticized other philanthropists while his actions allegedly contributed to global deaths through policy changes. CleanTechnica concludes that Parton's purposeful giving stands in stark opposition to Musk's approach.

title: Tesla denies rumors it is abandoning Full Self-Driving push in China
summary: Tesla denied rumors that it has pulled its Full Self-Driving team out of China, stating its Shanghai data center is operating normally. The company told local outlets that recruitment for driver-assistance roles is accelerating and reported the claims to police. Despite the denial, China remains absent from Tesla's official list of markets where FSD subscriptions are available due to regulatory hurdles. While Tesla claims work is progressing steadily, local rivals like Xiaomi and Huawei continue expanding urban driver-assistance features. Analysts note that reporting rumors to police is a standard corporate move in China to counter misinformation. The core issue remains the lack of a clear rollout timeline for Chinese customers despite previous announcements.

title: East African nations pursue rival oil projects amid regional rivalry
summary: Kenya secured a $17 billion refinery on Lamu Island after billionaire Aliko Dangote selected the site, resolving earlier location disputes. Tanzania and Uganda countered by partnering with Vitol Bahrain to develop a $20 billion energy hub in Tanga. Uganda simultaneously supports both initiatives while advancing its own $4 billion refinery in Hoima. These parallel projects raise concerns about the viability of regional integration within the East African Community. Kenya and Tanzania are expanding infrastructure to compete for trade routes, with Uganda seeking alternatives to Kenya's Port of Mombasa. The situation mirrors the collapse of a 2014 pipeline deal between Uganda and Kenya.

title: Department of Energy tests fracking for geothermal energy in Utah
summary: The Department of Energy is testing hydraulic fracturing to create water reservoirs for geothermal power generation in Utah. Annick Adjei of Wood Mackenzie noted potential but highlighted repeatability risks as a key concern. Dr. Kristie McLin stated that recent FORGE project results are beneficial for industry growth. The current four-month test aims to generate reliable data on thermal decline and water loss. Experts emphasize that costs must decrease for the technology to become commercially viable.

title: Heat waves force European nuclear plants offline due to water shortages
summary: Extreme heat waves and droughts recently forced several European nuclear plants to shut down or reduce output due to water shortages. Plants in France, Switzerland, Romania, Hungary, and Bulgaria faced issues from high river temperatures and low water levels. Critics argue these events challenge nuclear reliability, while experts note the problems stem from older engineering designs. MIT's Jacopo Buongiorno stated that most plants operate fine during heatwaves and that capacity reductions are minimal annually. Solutions include installing cooling towers or using recycled water, though renovations are costly and time-consuming. The Hungarian government temporarily sank barges to raise water levels, but safety regulators deemed such measures unacceptable. Meanwhile, Arizona's Palo Verde plant demonstrates successful operation in arid conditions using recycled wastewater.

title: Archit Patnaik explains how BMS, PCS, and EMS control authority in battery systems
summary: Archit Patnaik explains that a battery energy storage system (BESS) often fails to deliver expected power because multiple control systems hold different authority. The battery management system (BMS) sets safety limits based on cell conditions, while the power conversion system (PCS) executes commands within those constraints. The energy management system (EMS) requests power but cannot override battery safety limits or grid export restrictions. Patnaik notes that troubleshooting requires identifying which of these three boundaries is the active constraint rather than assuming a single fault. He emphasizes verifying communication links and scaling factors, as errors there can cause strange system behavior without actual hardware failure. The author recommends a specific control boundary checkout process to ensure interfaces function as designed before project turnover.

title: Ember reports battery growth brings round-the-clock solar closer
summary: The British energy think tank Ember reports that solar photovoltaic generation nearly doubled globally between the first half of 2023 and 2026. However, the study notes that solar output remains heavily concentrated around midday in most markets. New battery storage installations in 2026 are projected to reach 459 GWh, a 50% increase from the previous year. Ember data suggests this capacity could theoretically shift 34% of new daily solar generation to non-solar hours. While global averages show progress, countries like Bulgaria and Chile have led the rollout with storage capable of shifting over 75% of new solar generation. Ember concludes that batteries do not eliminate the need for a diversified electricity mix including wind, nuclear, and long-duration storage.

title: Japan's 29th solar auction selects 38.2 MW of PV capacity
summary: The Green Investment Promotion Organization announced the results of Japan's 29th utility-scale solar auction. Twelve applications totaling 87.3 MW were submitted, but only eight projects were approved for a combined 38.2 MW. The winning bids averaged JPY 8.89/kWh, with the largest project reaching 29.9 MW. This event marks the second completed PV auction in Japan's 2026 financial year.

title: IAEA launches ATLAS initiative for maritime nuclear energy collaboration
summary: The IAEA launched the ATLAS initiative to coordinate global efforts for nuclear applications at sea. Twenty-four nations signed a joint statement supporting safe maritime nuclear deployment. The program aims to develop regulatory frameworks for small modular reactors and floating power plants. Six project groups will address safety, security, and regulatory challenges starting this year.

title: Over 10,800 US K-12 schools now use solar power
summary: A new report from Generation180 states that more than 10,800 K-12 schools across the United States now utilize solar energy. The authors report that total solar capacity on these schools has more than tripled since 2016, reaching over 2.4 GW. Districts are saving millions in avoided electricity costs to reinvest in classrooms and programs. The document also presents the first national census of battery storage at U.S. schools, identifying 155 installations since 2016.

title: Fortum's NuCore Energi applies for Swedish state support for new nuclear
summary: Fortum's subsidiary NuCore Energi has submitted an application to the Swedish government for state support to develop a new nuclear power project in Oskarshamn. The company, which owns reactors in Finland and Sweden, plans to explore options ranging from small modular reactors to large-scale units with capacities between 1,200 and 3,400 MW. Fortum emphasized that no investment decisions have been made yet, noting that the final scale depends on technology choices and electricity demand growth. The project requires commitments from industrial customers and long-term political support to proceed. NuCore Energi CEO Laurent Leveugle stated that new nuclear power would strengthen energy security and support industrial growth. Minister Niklas Wykman affirmed that the Swedish support model is well balanced. The Ministry of Finance indicated that work can now begin on deciding the terms of the support, including negotiations with the European Commission.

title: Rebecca Hendin creates cartoon about Mark Zuckerberg and Meta court settlement
summary: The provided text contains only a title for a cartoon by Rebecca Hendin regarding Mark Zuckerberg and a Meta court settlement. No article body or additional details were included in the source material.

title: Meta Stock Rises After $16.7 Billion Settlement With States
summary: Meta Platforms shares gained 4.1% after the company settled a lawsuit with 47 states and territories over allegations regarding children's mental health and data collection. The agreement requires payments of up to $16.7 billion over 10 years, alongside new safeguards for minors. Analysts note the settlement removes a significant overhang, though The Motley Fool Stock Advisor team did not include Meta in its current list of top ten stocks for investors.

title: Three AI ETFs Outperform Market While Diversifying Beyond NVIDIA
summary: The article suggests three exchange-traded funds offer diversified AI exposure beyond NVIDIA Corp. iShares Future AI & Tech ETF (ARTY) holds 66 global companies with NVIDIA representing less than 5% of assets. ARTY and CHPS significantly outperformed the broader market in 2026. PAVE provides indirect AI exposure through U.S. infrastructure companies with considerably less technology sector exposure. These funds allow investors to diversify while maintaining ties to the artificial intelligence industry.

title: Syria's President appoints former SDF commander as presidential advisor
summary: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa appointed Mazloum Abdi as a presidential advisor, according to the state news agency Sana. This decision follows the dissolution of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces and their integration into the Syrian military. The appointment marks a significant step in al-Sharaa's plan to reunify the country under central government control.

title: Selena Gomez denies fraud claims regarding Wondermind investment
summary: Selena Gomez is contesting allegations that she defrauded investors of nearly $1.2m by failing to support her mental health platform, Wondermind. Her lawyer argues the claims are threadbare and that Gomez never agreed to manage the company. While the dispute puts her mother in a difficult position, experts warn that family-run businesses often lack proper governance. Commentators suggest that celebrities should carefully consider how a business might impact their reputation before lending their name to it.

title: Haiti police face scrutiny after deadly gang attack kills 47
summary: Haiti's national police faced intense scrutiny following a deadly gang attack in Kenscoff that killed 47 people and kidnapped over 50. Police spokesperson Garry Desrosiers stated at a news conference that authorities could not discuss specific plans to respond to the incident. The attack underscores the continued influence of armed groups, with one leader threatening to execute hostages if any gang members are killed. While violence in the area had previously dropped by 66 percent, the UN warns that gang-related violence is spreading geographically. Currently, an estimated 70 percent of Port-au-Prince remains under gang control, displacing more than 1.5 million people. A UN-backed Gang Suppression Force has arrived to help dismantle organized violence, though critics question the success of such international efforts. Police head Vladimir Paraison indicated an investigation is underway to probe potential complicity or negligence within the force.

title: Andy Burnham announces crackdown on rogue bailiffs and cowboy builders
summary: Andy Burnham announced new measures to protect consumers from aggressive bailiffs and unscrupulous builders. The government will require private bailiffs in England and Wales to be accredited by the Enforcement Conduct Board. A government-backed scheme will help people identify trusted builders starting next month. Additionally, a new app service will allow consumers to release payment to builders in stages linked to project milestones.

title: US FTC investigates YouTube over consumer protection and account suspensions
summary: Bloomberg News reports that the US Federal Trade Commission is preparing a potential lawsuit against YouTube regarding consumer protection violations. The investigation, led by the Bureau of Consumer Protection, examines whether users were misled by content policies before having accounts suspended. While the probe is in its final stages, it remains unclear which specific accounts were covered. Some career staff within the agency have privately expressed disagreement with filing the case. YouTube declined to comment on the matter.

title: Nvidia pauses revenue-sharing deals with AI cloud companies
summary: The Wall Street Journal reports that Nvidia has paused revenue-sharing deals with AI cloud companies. The chip giant stepped back from the program last week, though it could revamp the initiative later. An Nvidia spokesperson stated the business model remains in place and continues to evolve. The move comes amid investor scrutiny over Nvidia's role in circular deals that could inflate demand. Some employees expressed concerns about potential antitrust scrutiny regarding the initiative's control over customer business practices.

title: ASX poised to rise after Nvidia drives Wall Street tech rally
summary: Australian shares are expected to edge higher following gains in the US market, where Nvidia helped fuel a technology sector rally. The ASX 200 futures are currently trading up 0.1% to 9,000 points. Nvidia shares surged 8.7% after the company exceeded analyst expectations and provided strong revenue guidance for fiscal 2028. Meanwhile, three major Australian banks have revised their forecasts, predicting the Reserve Bank of Australia will lift interest rates at least once more in 2026. CBA economist Belinda Allen stated that broad-based economic strength keeps a rate hike firmly on the table despite signs of a potential slowdown. Morningstar reported that the August corporate reporting season has improved modestly, with analysts raising fair value estimates for roughly one-third of companies. Additionally, Wesfarmers CEO Rob Scott highlighted how the Anko brand's design capabilities are expanding beyond Kmart into other group businesses like Officeworks and K Homes.

title: Nvidia launches employee-funded PAC to influence U.S. policy
summary: Nvidia is preparing to launch an employee-funded political action committee named NVPAC, according to a person familiar with the decision. The move follows similar initiatives by Meta and Google to direct donations toward candidates supporting business objectives. Nvidia executives previously contributed $443,000 to the Republican National Committee. CEO Jensen Huang has cultivated close ties with President Trump regarding AI regulation. Anthropic established a comparable group that raised over $350,000 from staff.

title: Man charged with alleged domestic violence murder of woman in Perth
summary: Police in Perth have charged a 38-year-old man with the murder of a 28-year-old woman found dead in St James. Authorities allege the victim suffered extensive injuries from an assault by the man in the days before her death. Homicide Squad detectives investigated the case and questioned the suspect in custody. The accused is scheduled to appear in Perth Magistrates Court today.

title: Stars and Stripes staff sue Pentagon over firings citing First Amendment
summary: Three Stars and Stripes staff members filed a lawsuit against the Pentagon alleging First Amendment violations following their terminations. Publisher Max Lederer, editor-in-chief Erik Slavin, and reporter Lara Korte claim the Trump administration breached their rights to oppose state interference in reporting. The suit argues the dismissals were retaliation for publishing a report on conditions aboard the U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln and opposing potential censorship. Lederer stated the Pentagon installed a new deputy publisher without his knowledge, signaling a shift toward greater editorial control. The plaintiffs are represented by multiple legal groups, with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth named as a defendant.

title: One Nation names Mike Newman as NSW leader ahead of 2027 election
summary: One Nation has appointed investment banker Mike Newman as its New South Wales leader and first lower-house candidate for the March 2027 state election. Newman, who previously worked as a trade bureaucrat in Asia, will contest the seat of Cessnock. During an interview, he outlined policy proposals including halving payroll tax, freezing public servant numbers, and implementing performance metrics in the public service. He also addressed concerns about the party's stance on migrants and social cohesion. Current polling data from the Sydney Morning Herald Resolve poll in July shows One Nation at 25% in NSW, ahead of the Coalition at 23% and Labor at 29%. Meanwhile, the Greens criticized the government's refugee intake adjustment as a lack of principle, while the Coalition expressed support for the government's humanitarian response to the Nepal floods. Additionally, NSW has launched a bird flu vaccination program for vulnerable native species.

title: Three journalists sue Pentagon over dismissals from Stars and Stripes
summary: Three journalists sued the Department of Defense on Thursday, claiming their firings from Stars and Stripes violated their First Amendment rights. The complaint alleges the dismissals were retaliation for reporting on deteriorating conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln and for public statements supporting press freedom. Former publisher Max Lederer refused to fire two colleagues, leading to his own dismissal and subsequent retirement. The lawsuit argues the Pentagon's actions undermined the news outlet's historical editorial independence.

title: TotalEnergies cuts Russian gas exposure but keeps some supply
summary: The article states that TotalEnergies is reducing its reliance on Russian gas while maintaining partial exposure. The text notes the company has not fully withdrawn from Russian energy sources. No specific figures or dates are provided in the source.

title: Trump signs order to rename Lake Ontario to Lake America
summary: US President Donald Trump signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America, effective immediately. The move follows collapsed trade talks and new tariffs between the US and Canada. Trump stated the change reflects American greatness, while Interior Secretary Doug Burgum pledged to implement it. Canadian officials, including Prime Minister Mark Carney and Premier Doug Ford, dismissed the proposal, noting the lake's 400-year history and international status. US lawmakers also criticized the order, with some proposing bills to nullify it. The White House claims the US Department of the Interior has 30 days to update the name with the Geographic Names Information Service. Canada is not required to recognize the change, as no international body governs such names for shared waters.

title: Hundreds gather in Oslo to support Norway's King Harald V
summary: Hundreds gathered in Oslo to support King Harald V, who is in an extremely serious condition at Oslo University Hospital. Queen Sonja and Crown Prince Haakon cancelled engagements to visit the King. Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and Parliament Speaker Masud Gharahkhani also returned to Norway from abroad. The King has ruled out abdication despite recent health issues.

title: Hundreds gather in Oslo to support Norway's King Harald V
summary: Hundreds gathered in Oslo to support King Harald V, who is in an extremely serious condition at Oslo University Hospital. Queen Sonja and Crown Prince Haakon cancelled engagements to visit the King. title: Kherson governor urges residents to flee as Russian strikes damage heating plant
summary: Regional governor Oleksandr Prokudin urged Kherson residents to leave after Russian attacks damaged a district heating plant. Prokudin warned of prolonged power and heating outages due to the severe infrastructure damage. He stated there is currently no way to destroy the glide bombs used in the strikes. The city, which had about 280,000 inhabitants before the 2022 invasion, faces an extremely difficult security situation.

title: Nepal floods and landslides in Nuwakot leave hundreds missing
summary: Catastrophic flash floods and landslides struck Nuwakot district in central Nepal on 26 August, following a glacial collapse near the Nepal-Tibet border. Communities along the Trishuli River basin suffered widespread destruction, with hundreds of residents, tourists, and security personnel still unaccounted for. The Nepal Army deployed MI-17 helicopters to evacuate injured survivors and support search-and-rescue teams. Authorities have placed communities along the Trishuli and Narayani rivers on high alert due to the risk of further flooding and landslides. Several bridges and key roads linking Nuwakot with neighbouring districts and Kathmandu have been swept away or severely damaged.

title: Catastrophic floods and landslides in Nepal's Nuwakot leave hundreds missing
summary: Catastrophic flash floods and landslides struck Nuwakot district in central Nepal on 26 August, following a glacial collapse near the Nepal-Tibet border. Communities along the Trishuli River basin suffered severe damage to infrastructure and buildings. Hundreds of residents, tourists, and security personnel remain unaccounted for as rescue operations continue. The Nepal Army deployed MI-17 helicopters to evacuate injured survivors and support search teams. Authorities have placed communities on high alert due to the risk of further flooding and landslides.

title: UK welcomes dissolution of SDF terror group in Syria
summary: Britain welcomed the dissolution of the Syrian Democratic Forces and their integration into state institutions. UK Deputy UN Representative Kate Foster stated that this move supports Syria's territorial integrity and sovereignty. The group's leader, Mazloum Abdi, announced the dissolution following a January agreement. Foster also praised recent Israel-Syria talks while warning against further strikes in Idlib.

title: Documentary traces final weeks of Saitama public pool closure
summary: Shingo Ota's documentary 'Numakage Public Pool' chronicles the last 49 days of a Saitama facility before its 2024 shutdown. The film uses grief stages to show lifeguards, elderly patrons, and staff resisting the 2022 government decision to build a school. The project captures the community's loss of a long-standing summer oasis.

title: Review: 'I Don't Know You' explores lonely protagonist in dark drama
summary: A review describes Ryota Nakano's film 'I Don't Know You' as a humanist drama featuring a lonely 28-year-old protagonist. The article notes the film centers on family and death while commenting on Japanese society. It contrasts this darker tone with Nakano's previous comedic work. The review highlights the protagonist's isolation and lack of meaningful connections.

title: US officials warn of critical Patriot missile shortage in Europe
summary: US and NATO officials report a 'beyond critical' shortage of Patriot missile interceptors in Europe, driven largely by the war with Iran. They warn that current stocks are insufficient to stop a sustained Russian ballistic missile attack, though no such assault is imminent. While US officials in Europe and a NATO spokesperson confirmed low inventories, US Army Col. Martin O'Donnell and Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell disputed the severity, calling claims of shortages false. Experts note that US stocks in the Middle East have been rapidly drained, with 65% of Patriots used in the Iran conflict. Production is expected to rebound by 2030, but some European nations currently lack ammunition for their systems. Ukraine continues to request more interceptors as Russian attacks intensify.

title: Connor Hellebuyck confirms he requested a trade from the Winnipeg Jets
summary: Connor Hellebuyck confirmed he asked the Winnipeg Jets to trade him, according to a statement from his agent. The goaltender, who won the Vezina Trophy three times, said he made the request months ago but felt it was necessary to go public as training camp approaches. General manager Kevin Cheveldayoff acknowledged the player's desire for a change but offered no update on the situation. Hellebuyck, who has played his entire career with Winnipeg, expressed gratitude for his time with the organization while hoping for a resolution soon.

title: Good Good Golf ends PGA Tour sponsorship and Callaway partnership after viral video controversy
summary: Good Good Golf lost its title sponsorship of a PGA Tour event and its partnership with Callaway following backlash over a video depicting domestic violence. The video, released on August 20, showed a man shoving a woman to the ground while she reached for a new golf driver. PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp described the sponsorship situation as fluid, and the tournament was renamed the Austin Championship. Callaway Golf CEO Chip Brewer admitted the company approved the video and announced it would investigate the incident. Additionally, Golf Channel postponed its "Big Break x Good Good" reality series. Good Good Golf stated it would step away to focus on organizational culture and learning from the situation.

title: Nepal pilot Andy Thapa rescues flood victims by helicopter
summary: Helicopter pilot Andy Thapa describes rescuing people stranded by catastrophic flooding in Nepal. He works for a Nepali helicopter company as a charter and rescue pilot. Thapa carries stranded individuals to safety during the disaster. NPR notes it does not accept money for coverage or interviews.

title: Turkish Ambassador commemorates Victory Day anniversary in Washington
summary: Turkish Ambassador Sedat Onal marked the 104th anniversary of Victory Day in Washington, highlighting the historical significance of the 1922 Battle of Dumlupinar. He stated that the victory remains an enduring source of inspiration for Türkiye as it enters its second century. Ambassador Onal also noted that bilateral ties between Ankara and Washington are in a positive trajectory. Defense attaché Brig. Gen. Alpaslan Guldal described the battle as a major turning point that demonstrated the Turkish nation's determination to protect its independence.

title: Former CIA officer Ric Prado says Cuba is next target after Iran
summary: Former CIA officer Ric Prado told EL PAÍS that the United States will likely turn its attention to Cuba once the war with Iran concludes. Prado, who retired in 2004 after 24 years of service, believes the current administration has accelerated plans that had stalled for decades. He stated that the agency has people inside Cuba and has presented the president with various covert options. Prado described his career, which included training Contras in Nicaragua and leading counterterrorism operations against Osama Bin Laden. He also discussed the human costs of those missions and the agency's use of black sites. Additionally, Prado addressed allegations linking him to organized crime in Miami, noting that a case was dropped when he joined the CIA. He expressed a desire to return to action but emphasized that his current focus is on his family.

title: Jury deliberates in trial of Lindsay Clancy accused of killing three children
summary: A jury is currently deliberating in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, a Massachusetts mother charged with murdering her three children in January 2023. While Clancy has admitted to the killings, her legal team argues she should not be held legally responsible due to severe mental illness. Prosecutors contend she made a calculated decision to kill her children and sent her husband away beforehand. The five-week trial featured testimony from Clancy's ex-husband and family members regarding her deteriorating mental health, alongside heated exchanges between lawyers and expert witnesses over the diagnosis of postpartum psychosis. Judge William Sullivan denied a request for a mistrial after prosecutors questioned witnesses about Clancy's Catholic faith, instructing jurors to disregard that testimony. If convicted, Clancy faces life in prison without parole.

title: State Department pauses immigrant visa interviews for public charge rule training
summary: The U.S. State Department has postponed immigrant visa interviews globally to train officials on a stricter public charge rule. This measure primarily impacts applicants seeking to reunite with family members or immigrate through sponsors. Officials must now assess factors like age, health, and finances to determine if an applicant might rely on government assistance after arriving. The pause began in early August and is expected to last until mid-September, though rescheduling details remain unclear. This delay follows recent court rulings that blocked previous attempts to halt visas for specific nationalities or visa categories. While the administration argues the rule prevents dependency on programs like Medicaid, many immigrants must wait five years before accessing major federal benefits. Employers sponsoring workers are not affected because applicants can demonstrate income. Applicants receive notification emails but await further communication regarding their rescheduled appointments.

title: Zambian opposition leader Brian Mundubile held in police custody for questioning
summary: State broadcaster ZNBC reported that opposition leader Brian Mundubile and his running mate are in police custody for interviews. A police spokesman stated the pair were questioned regarding potential threats to national security. Mundubile had been in hiding since election day, when police raided opposition sites and arrested several people. The opposition leader denies election irregularities and claims the government's accusations are fabricated. Zambia's judiciary was closed for security reasons while Mundubile sought to challenge results in court.

title: Deadly Nepal floods cut off villages as rescue efforts continue
summary: A massive flash flood in Nepal has killed hundreds and left many villages isolated from Kathmandu. Journalist Bidhya Rajput reported that her home in Sole village was swept away by the Trisuli River, while communication and electricity remain absent. Authorities declared Nuwakot, Rasuwa, and Dhading districts the most affected areas after destroying over 30 bridges and 12 hydropower dams. Minister Bikram Timilsina stated that more than 1,300 people remain missing, including foreign nationals, as rescue teams airlift survivors. Scientists debate the cause, with some suggesting an avalanche blocked a river before a landslide dam burst. Experts warn that further flooding could occur as upstream lakes in Tibet continue to overflow.

title: Ratko Mladic, ex-Bosnian Serb warlord, dies at 84 while serving life sentence
summary: Ratko Mladic, the former Bosnian Serb general convicted of war crimes, died Thursday at a hospital in The Hague at age 84. U.N. officials confirmed the death, noting he was serving a life sentence for atrocities committed during the 1990s conflicts in the former Yugoslavia. A relative confirmed the reports to The Associated Press, stating his son was traveling to The Hague. Mladic was sentenced to life in prison in 2017 after being in custody since 2011. He commanded forces that besieged Sarajevo and oversaw the Srebrenica massacre, where over 8,000 Muslim men and boys were killed. Munira Subasic of the Mothers of Srebrenica group expressed sorrow that Mladic died without facing further suffering. While some Bosnian Serbs mourned him as a patriot, victims' families continue to demand acknowledgment of his crimes.

title: Rahul Gandhi accuses Modi government of two systems after NCLT approves Subhash Chandra settlement
summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi criticized the Narendra Modi government for creating two systems in the country following the National Company Law Tribunal's approval of a resolution plan for businessman Subhash Chandra. The tribunal allowed Chandra to settle ₹22,006 crore dues for ₹6.5 crore, a move Gandhi described as 'Neta-Company Loot Tribunal.' Other Congress leaders, including Jairam Ramesh and Randeep Singh Surjewala, condemned the nearly 99.97% haircut on creditor claims as a mockery of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code. Surjewala alleged that such settlements amount to loan waivers for industrialists and demanded the Finance Minister disclose total bank losses over the past 12 years.

title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT advertising in India with over 50 brands
summary: OpenAI has begun displaying ads on ChatGPT in India for logged-in adult users on Free and Go plans, while Plus and Pro remain ad-free. More than 50 brands are expected to advertise on the platform this week, with WPP and Omnicom serving as initial agency partners. Starting Sept 4, businesses can access a self-serve ads manager with daily budgets beginning at Rs 725. An OpenAI spokesperson told TOI that the company anticipates early interest from sectors including travel, financial services, retail, and health and beauty. The company states that ads will appear below organic responses when user requests show commercial intent, without receiving conversation text or profile details. OpenAI argues this approach offers relevance through immediate conversational intent rather than traditional keyword bidding.

title: UP CM Adityanath calls state population a demographic dividend
summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath stated that the state's large population is a demographic dividend rather than a challenge. He told foreign delegations that the workforce is talented and energetic, requiring government support. Adityanath distributed over ₹3.42 crore in incentives to 107 startups and ₹1.79 crore to nine incubators. He highlighted the growth of the startup ecosystem from 120 to over 24,000 entities in the state.

title: Supreme Court orders faster dowry trials and periodic reviews
summary: The Supreme Court issued directions to expedite dowry trials due to concerns that offenders often escape punishment. A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Augustine George Masih directed high courts to periodically review pending criminal appeals. The apex court stated that the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, faces implementation difficulties and requires concentrated effort from various stakeholders. Trial courts must frame charges within 60 to 90 days after a chargesheet is filed. The bench also ordered periodic training for judicial officers and police officials to improve handling of such cases.

title: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles launches new TATA.CARS global brand identity
summary: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd. unveiled the TATA.CARS brand identity on August 27, 2026, nearly a year after the company demerged. Shailesh Chandra, MD & CEO, stated the move declares intent for a future where mobility empowers people. All showrooms will rebrand under the new identity, which spans hatchbacks, sedans, SUVs, and electric vehicles. The legal entity remains Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd., while the iconic vehicle ellipse and product brands stay unchanged. The company said the launch evolves its legacy for the next generation of customers.

title: Tata Motors launches tata.cars brand for passenger vehicles
summary: Tata Motors unveiled tata.cars as its new customer-facing identity for the passenger-vehicle business. The company retains tata.ev as a distinct electric-vehicle sub-brand. CEO Shailesh Chandra described the move as a springboard following the sale of seven million cars in India. The new brand will apply to retail, digital platforms, and after-sales services. Dealerships will adopt a redesigned visual identity over the coming months.

title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Ads in India with 50 brands
summary: OpenAI announced the launch of ChatGPT Ads in India, introducing paid distribution for logged-in adult users on Free and Go plans. More than 50 brands are set to go live this week with WPP and Omnicom as initial agency partners. Experts warn that maintaining user trust requires clearly marking sponsored placements separate from organic AI answers. The rollout aims to shift advertising from keyword-based searches to intent-driven conversational contexts.

title: Nvidia partnerships and US grid ban boost power equipment stocks
