Despite concerns, the event is set to proceed at Madison Square Garden.

title: Bitcoin drops below $78,000 as crypto market corrects after regulator comments
summary: Bitcoin fell below $78,000 while Ethereum declined to $2,430 over the past 24 hours. Delta Exchange analyst Riya Sehgal noted Bitcoin dropped from above $81,000 to around $77,700. WazirX founder Nischal Shetty stated total market capitalisation fell 1.27% to $2.65 trillion amid liquidations. Despite the correction, crypto ETFs recorded $482.13 million in inflows on August 25.

title: Anthropic launches Model Hardware Standard to unify AI control of physical devices
summary: Anthropic is developing the Model Hardware Standard (MHS), a unified interface allowing AI agents to read data from and control physical hardware like microscopes and robotic arms. The company states that standardized drivers reduce integration time for connecting multiple machines from weeks or months down to hours or minutes. Early tests with partners show AI can independently optimize workflows and generate scripts that run without a language model. However, Anthropic notes the system still struggles with understanding physical cause and effect, meaning human oversight remains necessary. The spec is currently available as a research preview for select labs and manufacturers.

title: Samsung launches new foldable form factor as Apple approaches
summary: Samsung is launching a new foldable phone called the Galaxy Z Fold8 to compete with existing models. The device features a wider outer display and a landscape 4:3 inner screen for better tablet use. Meanwhile, the Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra targets power users with a larger outer screen and advanced camera system. This release sets the stage for Apple's upcoming entry into the foldable market.

title: Article explains differences between proprietary, open weight, and open source AI models
summary: The article explains distinctions between three categories of large language models. Proprietary LLMs are owned by single entities like OpenAI and Google. These models remain closed and opaque regarding their code and training data. Frontier models offer high intelligence but require significant computational resources. Businesses can easily adopt proprietary models through available APIs.

title: Solar Plants Now Require Less Upfront Capital Than Fossil Plants
summary: An Ember analysis reports that solar plants now require less upfront investment than coal or gas plants to deliver the same electricity. This shift marks a critical economic tipping point where solar competes with fossil fuels before any fuel is purchased. IRENA data indicates solar PV total installed costs have fallen 87% since 2010 due to mass manufacturing. While batteries add costs, IRENA estimates firm solar-plus-battery electricity costs range from $54 to $82 per megawatt-hour in high-irradiance regions. The IEA notes commercial energy finance remains weaker in emerging economies, yet upfront-cost parity weakens the historical barrier preventing these nations from adopting solar. Leon Stille writes for Oilprice.com that fossil power has lost its primary economic defense of being cheaper to build initially.

title: Nvidia Rally Exposes JEPQ ETF Yield Tradeoffs
summary: The article explains that the JPMorgan Nasdaq Equity Premium Income ETF generates income by selling call options on the Nasdaq-100. Nvidia's recent 9% surge demonstrated how this strategy caps the fund's upside participation. Reuters reported Nvidia added roughly $442 billion in market value after guiding to about 70% revenue growth. The fund captured only 63% of the QQQ Trust's move during the rally. Distributions are taxed as ordinary income, making tax-advantaged accounts preferable for investors seeking the yield.

title: Sam Altman Says OpenAI Should Slow AI Development Amid Safety Concerns
summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told Time Magazine that it is a good time to slow down AI model development following recent safety failures. The article notes OpenAI filed an S-1 form for an expected 2027 IPO. Analysts suggest Altman may be seeking time to improve financial performance, as OpenAI reported $6.7 billion in Q2 revenue against a $12.3 billion operating loss, while rival Anthropic doubled sales to $11.6 billion and posted a profit.

title: Nepal survivors accuse government of delays in flood aid
summary: Al Jazeera's Barnaby Lo reports that anger is growing in Nepal's Nuwakot district. Survivors accuse the government of delays in delivering aid and locating missing people following a flash flood near the Nepal-Tibet border on Wednesday.

title: Iceland votes in tight race to resume EU accession talks
summary: Iceland held a referendum on Saturday to decide whether to resume talks on joining the European Union. Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir cast her vote as the country voted on the issue. The vote occurs 13 years after Iceland paused its previous EU accession talks.

title: Qantas plans to retire its A380 fleet by 2028 due to maintenance costs
summary: Qantas announced it will retire its A380 fleet in 2028, four years earlier than planned, citing high maintenance costs and new aircraft availability. The airline flew its first A380 in 2008, which was celebrated as a landmark moment for the carrier. While the aircraft offered spacious cabins and a unique travel experience, recent trips revealed ageing issues such as fraying seats and maintenance delays. Despite these problems, some flights on other airlines' A380s remain popular. Passengers have a few years left to experience the iconic double-decker jets before they are phased out.

title: LA Rapper ColdheartedAC Arrested in $8.1 Million Stolen Check Scheme
summary: The Department of Justice announced the federal indictment of rapper ColdheartedAC and two others for allegedly participating in an $8.1 million stolen-check scheme. Prosecutors allege the trio forged endorsements and used fake documents to cash over 50 stolen Treasury checks and hundreds of other fraudulent checks between April 2022 and December 2023. Investigators say the defendants targeted tax refunds, Social Security payments, and veterans' benefits across Los Angeles, Orange, and San Diego counties. Obayuwana remains in custody facing nine counts of bank fraud and other charges, while co-defendants Vu and Murrillo face similar accusations. If convicted, the defendants could face up to 30 years in federal prison for each bank fraud count.

title: UN and Nepal warn of climate threats after deadly Himalayan floods
summary: Nepal's foreign minister and UN climate chief warned of growing climate threats to the Himalayas following deadly floods. The US Geological Survey stated a glacial collapse caused the disaster, leaving nearly 3,000 people missing and 682 confirmed dead. Officials agreed to share hydrological data between Nepal and China. Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal emphasized Nepal's vulnerability despite contributing minimal greenhouse gases. UN climate chief Simon Stiell linked the tragedy to human-driven warming, noting increased risks for vulnerable communities.

title: Israeli army says it struck a Hamas commander in a Gaza hospital compound
summary: The Israeli army stated it struck a Hamas commander inside a Gaza hospital compound. The military provided this update regarding the specific location and target of the operation.

title: ABC launches quiz to rank Dolly Parton hits by chart peaks
summary: The ABC has released a new quiz challenging users to rank Dolly Parton's biggest hits. Participants must order the songs by their chart peaks on the US Hot 100, country charts, and in Australia. Sources for the data include Billboard and ARIA. The quiz allows three guesses per round and offers hints for stuck players.

title: Venezuela's PSUV backs oil deal with Washington as US Democrats criticize Trump
summary: Venezuela's ruling PSUV party expressed full support for a new oil agreement with the United States. Democratic lawmakers accused President Trump of prioritizing private profit over public interests and troop safety. The deal grants a private joint venture control over 65 billion barrels of reserves. Republicans defended the historic agreement as beneficial for both nations.

title: Older Australians face higher health insurance costs under proposed rebate changes
summary: The federal government proposed reducing private health insurance rebates for Australians over 65, aiming to save $3 billion over four years. Industry estimates suggest 62,000 older Australians may cancel their cover while 200,000 could downgrade policies. Health Minister Mark Butler stated government modelling predicts no material impact on public hospital capacity. Conversely, the Shadow Regional Health Minister Anne Webster warned regional hospitals would struggle with increased patient loads. Professor Yuting Zhang from the University of Melbourne estimated only 42,000 people would drop cover, arguing benefits outweigh costs. A Senate inquiry into the bill is scheduled for October 7.

title: IAEA reports Zaporizhzhia plant lost off-site power and relies on limited diesel
summary: The IAEA stated that Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant has lacked off-site power for over a week, forcing reliance on emergency diesel generators. Director General Rafael Grossi emphasized that fuel availability is critical for nuclear safety. The agency noted the plant has only a 10-day diesel supply and is negotiating a ceasefire to repair electrical lines damaged by military activity. Three recent drone incidents have also raised safety concerns at the Russian-occupied facility.

title: North Carolina defeats TCU 15-10 in Ireland to open Bill Belichick's second season
summary: North Carolina defeated TCU 15-10 in Dublin on Saturday to open coach Bill Belichick's second season at the school. The Tar Heels secured the victory with a 28-yard field goal by Aeron Burrell following a fumble recovery. Quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. completed 16 of 28 passes for 232 yards, while Jeremy Payne rushed for 142 yards for TCU. Coach Belichick credited his defensive front for stopping the Horned Frogs, noting they forced the quarterback to cut back inside. TCU coach Sonny Dykes stated that kicking field goals made sense when the team was not moving the football effectively. The game marked a positive start for Belichick, who finished 4-8 in his previous season with the Tar Heels.

title: Blocked roads and monsoon weather hinder aid delivery to Nepal flood survivors
summary: World Vision's Dhruba Gurmachhan explains that blocked roads and monsoon weather are complicating efforts to deliver food, shelter, and emergency hygiene to Nepal flood survivors.

title: Rescuers search for thousands missing after deadly Himalayan floods in Nepal and Tibet
summary: Rescue crews are struggling through blocked roads and dangerous terrain to find thousands of people missing after deadly floods in Nepal and Tibet. The article reports that search efforts are ongoing despite the challenging conditions. NPR notes that it does not accept money for coverage or interviews.

title: Netanyahu condemns settler attack in West Bank village
summary: The provided text contains a headline stating that Netanyahu condemned a settler attack. However, the body of the article failed to load due to technical issues.

title: NIL rules increase parity, making seven teams favorites for national title
summary: The Associated Press reports that Name, Image, and Likeness rules have increased parity in college football, resulting in seven teams having odds of 11-1 or better to win the national championship. Ohio State, Notre Dame, and Texas are each priced at +650 or better, while Indiana, Oregon, Georgia, and Miami also remain competitive contenders. Joey Feazel of Caesars Sportsbook noted that the landscape is more open than in previous years. Sportsbooks must also adjust for player movement through the transfer portal and eligibility court cases. Notre Dame faces a relatively easier schedule as an independent, though experts warn it is not without challenges. Additionally, Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr is currently favored over Texas QB Arch Manning for the Heisman Trophy.

title: Russian drone strike kills 37 at Kyiv weapons depot near homes
summary: A Russian drone strike on a Ukrainian weapons depot near Kyiv killed at least 37 people and injured dozens more. President Volodymyr Zelensky stated the storage site definitely should not have been located next to a residential area. The explosion damaged approximately 130 homes in the Myla village and triggered a secondary blast at a nearby care home. Ukrainian officials have launched criminal proceedings regarding official negligence in placing explosives so close to civilians. This incident marks the second munitions depot strike near Kyiv in recent months, prompting Prime Minister Sergiy Koretsky to express regret that lessons from previous failures were not learned. Meanwhile, fighting continues across the region with additional drone attacks reported in Odesa, Dnipropetrovsk, Sumy, and Zaporizhzhia.

title: Nepal and China floods leave nearly 3,000 missing as rescue efforts continue
summary: Rescuers in Nepal and China continue searching for nearly 3,000 people missing after devastating floods swept through the border region. At least 682 bodies have been recovered, with 675 in Nepal and seven in China. A breakthrough occurred when the Nepali army inserted a pipe into a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydroelectric site where over 100 workers are believed trapped. The US Geological Survey attributed the disaster to a glacial collapse, a phenomenon linked to climate change by UN climate chief Simon Steill. Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal stated reconstruction costs could reach billions of dollars while appealing for specialized rescue technology. Meanwhile, Chinese authorities paused operations in Gyirong due to flood risks from a newly formed lake before reporting it had drained. Families in Nepal face agonizing waits for news of missing relatives, including 933 hydropower workers and hundreds of foreigners.

title: New US-Canada Tariffs Will Raise Costs for Cars, Homes, and Households
summary: The article examines the economic impact of escalating tariffs between the United States and Canada. Bernard Yaros of Oxford Economics warns that higher duties on vehicles will eventually increase consumer prices. The Forest Products Association of Canada notes that metal and wood tariffs will raise construction costs. Bradley Saunders of Capital Economics suggests Canadians may switch to domestic goods for household items. John Iselin of the Budget Lab at Yale estimates the average cost to an American household is about $3, though broader trade tensions could add $1,000.

title: IAEA reports Zaporizhzhia plant lost power supply for over a week
summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency reported that the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in Ukraine has lacked off-site power for more than a week. The facility currently relies on emergency diesel generators, which provide only a ten-day supply. IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi emphasized that reliable external power is indispensable for nuclear safety. The plant lost its regular supply following military activity near the Dnipro River. The Vienna-based group is negotiating a local ceasefire to allow repairs to electrical lines.

title: Australians embrace weight-loss drugs, dupe brands, and electric vehicles
summary: The article details five distinct trends in the Australian retail and transport sectors based on recent financial results and market data. Kmart Group reported $11.7bn in sales driven by its Anko brand, which is expanding globally and introducing higher-priced product tiers. Domino's Pizza reduced discounting to improve franchisee profitability despite an 11% revenue drop in Australia and New Zealand. Sigma Healthcare's Chemist Warehouse found that customers buying GLP-1 drugs have shopping baskets 40% larger than others, purchasing more beauty and health products. Eagers Automotive noted that the shift to electric vehicles is a one-way street, with EV sales tripling compared to last year. Australia Post recorded a $108m pre-tax loss as letter volumes fell to 1930s levels, prompting a 15c stamp price increase.

title: Experts say AI will stay in healthcare but doctors must remain final decision-makers
summary: Experts at a webinar organized by SRM Institute of Science and Technology and The Hindu stated that artificial intelligence is a permanent part of healthcare. Panelists emphasized that medical practitioners must retain ultimate responsibility for clinical decisions. Dr. Jayanthi urged students to develop AI literacy and verification reflexes. Dr. Ganapathy warned against outsourcing accountability to technology. Mr. Gautham noted AI can expand access in underserved areas while maintaining oversight.

title: RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat Says Excluding Muslims Makes One Not Hindu
summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat stated in New York that a Hindu who believes Muslims have no place in India ceases to be Hindu. He addressed concerns about the RSS's vision of a Hindu Rashtra, clarifying that Hindutva does not envisage a Bharat without Muslims. Bhagwat highlighted the organization's 1.3 lakh service projects and its inclusive approach during a recent aircraft collision in Dadri. He emphasized that dialogue and selfless service are essential for social change beyond politics.

title: Mirwaiz backs NC MP and demands J&K statehood and Article 370 restoration
summary: Hurriyat Conference chairman Mirwaiz Umar Farooq supported National Conference MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi and criticized the party for abandoning its stance on Article 370. Mirwaiz urged all J&K political parties to demand the restoration of statehood and constitutional guarantees. Mehdi announced his resignation from the NC and Lok Sabha, responding to pressure from party leadership. He highlighted threats to the region's youth, environment, and cultural rights.

title: Five issues driving the US-Canada trade war escalation
summary: The ongoing trade war between the United States and Canada is driven by five key issues, according to a report by Prabhakar Jha. The conflict stems from differing views on the economic relationship, with President Trump accusing Canada of taking advantage of the US while Prime Minister Mark Carney frames it as a sovereignty dispute. Negotiations collapsed after weeks of talks, with both sides accusing the other of demanding too much. The US sought to dictate Canada's future trade agreements, while Ottawa rejected matching American tariffs on third countries. Disagreements also arose over tariffs on steel, aluminium, and automobiles, with Canada imposing counter-tariffs on $27.6 billion of US imports. The breakdown highlights deep economic interdependence and Canada's efforts to diversify its trade relationships.

title: Warangal Hospital to Open by December; Tims Units Follow
summary: Health officials stated the Warangal Super Specialty Hospital will be ready for services by December. Minister Damodar Rajanarsimha directed a doctors' committee to visit the facility every 15 days. Officials reported seasonal diseases declined while typhoid cases increased slightly. The minister ordered intensified disease surveillance and mosquito-control measures across government hospitals.

title: Andhra Pradesh power demand rises 15-20% due to heat wave
summary: Andhra Pradesh energy consumption has increased by 15% to 20% daily due to heat waves and El Niño conditions. Authorities attribute the surge to widespread air conditioner use and farmers pumping groundwater. The state currently generates power from thermal, wind, and hydro sources while purchasing additional electricity from outside regions. Officials expect this high demand trend to continue through the peak summer season.

title: Netanyahu condemns settler attack in West Bank village
summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned dozens of Israeli settlers attacking Palestinians in Qusra and Jalud on August 29, 2026. The military stated forces removed rioters barricaded inside a Palestinian home and opened a police investigation. President Isaac Herzog and the Foreign Ministry also criticized the violence. Since October 2023, at least 1,103 Palestinians have died in the West Bank according to an AFP tally.

title: Mumbai Opposition Warns Against De-Reserving Byculla's Alexandra Theatre
summary: Mumbai opposition parties warned against de-reserving the Alexandra Theatre for residential use, fearing it would set a dangerous precedent. Congress and Shiv Sena (UBT) members argued that cancelling the reservation for a closed cinema could open floodgates for similar claims regarding other theatres. They demanded public disclosure of all 119 cinema reservations under DP-2034 and a comprehensive White Paper on public reservation amendments. While a civic official noted the theatre has been unused since 2007, the proposal remains on hold pending further committee review.

title: Rising Onion Prices in Bhopal May Reach Rs 80 Per Kg
summary: Onion prices in Bhopal have surged from Rs 20 to Rs 50-60 per kg, with traders warning rates could hit Rs 80 per kg. Wholesale traders attribute the spike to low market arrivals and damaged stored stock. Farmers report a 40% to 50% production drop due to adverse weather and panic selling during the monsoon. New crop arrivals from Nashik are not expected until October.

title: Weeve offers free privacy tools for safe AI data use
summary: Weeve provides free tools to help users avoid sharing private information with artificial intelligence assistants. The Dutch startup offers a service that removes identifying details from text before AI processing. Weeve also provides free transcription in 25 languages and a local-first AI note taker for Mac. These features allow users to analyze documents securely without leaking personal data to public databases.

title: Tencent launches Hy4 Preview, a massive 770B parameter open-weight LLM
summary: Tencent introduced Hy4 Preview, a new open-weight text-only large language model. The model features 770 billion total parameters and a 1 million token context window. It offers two reasoning effort levels: high and no_think. The release represents a significant increase in size compared to the previous Hy3 model.

title: Gamescom 2024 Highlights Witcher 3 Expansion, Alien Sequel, and Fable Reboot
summary: A journalist attending Gamescom for the sixth time reports on major game reveals at the Cologne event. CD Projekt Red announced a new expansion for The Witcher 3, Songs of the Past, which includes a free upgrade for the original game. Creative Assembly showcased Alien: Isolation 2, featuring a new protagonist and larger open spaces. Playground Games revealed a 2027 reboot of Fable with a cast of over 100 actors representing various UK accents. Additionally, the event highlighted a remaster of Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis and the Scottish setting of Silent Hill Townfall. The Games Done Quick charity marathon also raised millions for various causes.

title: Vijay Pande launches small firm VZVC to make five concentrated biotech bets
summary: Vijay Pande, formerly of a16z, co-founded VZVC with Zach Werner to pursue a concentrated investment strategy. The firm plans to make approximately five investments annually instead of the dozens typical of larger funds. Pande explained that biology differs from text because biological data cannot be scraped from the internet, creating unique challenges for AI models. He noted that while AI improves drug discovery, clinical trials remain expensive and animal models often fail to predict human responses. Pande emphasized the need for high-integrity founders who prioritize long-term collaboration over competition. The new firm relies on AI agents for operations rather than hiring associates.

title: AI Videos Displace Actors and Livestreamers in China's Entertainment Industry
summary: AI-generated videos are increasingly replacing human performers in China's entertainment sector. The China Netcasting Services Association reports that 95% of short dramas published in Q1 2026 were AI-generated. Production costs have dropped significantly, with one minute of AI video costing between $90 and $120. Tsinghua University professor Shen Yang told the Financial Times that some performers are forced to provide their likeness before losing their jobs. Lawyers note a rise in AI-related labor disputes over the past few years.

title: Iran War Adds $330 Billion to Global Energy Import Bill
summary: The Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air reports that the conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran increased global energy import costs by $330 billion between March and August. The European Union suffered the most financial pain, paying an extra $78 billion due to its reliance on foreign oil and gas. China and India followed as the next largest affected importers, paying additional $35 billion and $22 billion respectively. While crude oil accounted for the largest share of extra costs, liquefied natural gas prices in Asia remain 75% higher than pre-war expectations. The International Energy Agency estimates that hostilities have knocked out 9.6 million barrels of daily refining capacity in the Middle East. Low-carbon energy sources like wind and solar provided a partial offset by saving importers $36 billion during the period.

title: US Justice Department revives 18th-century prize law to seize Iranian oil
summary: The US Justice Department and Pentagon are preparing to use dormant prize law to seize and sell Iranian oil captured during a blockade. Bloomberg reports that Houston is being considered a venue for these cases due to its petrochemical infrastructure. US Attorney Aaron Reitz stated the department is reviving this ancient maritime legal system. The move aims to generate revenue and tighten economic pressure on Iran while avoiding the delays of civil forfeiture. However, legal experts warn of uncertainties regarding modern international law and the lack of contemporary experience administering such cases.

title: Robot.com unveils R-dog delivery robot with ads and facial recognition
summary: Robot.com has unveiled the R-dog, a delivery robot featuring a furry tail and red cap designed to navigate stairs and engage passersby. The company states the robot will run advertisements and use cameras for sentiment analysis while collecting engagement data. Robot.com claims the design aims to make automation more approachable, though it remains unclear how the device handles multiple deliveries. The article notes the robot's makers address privacy concerns through limited data retention and user opt-out options.

title: Illinois legalizes 40 mph e-bikes but requires motorcycle registration
summary: Illinois Governor JB Pritzker signed SB 3484 into law, creating a legal pathway for high-speed electric bikes on public roads starting January 1, 2027. The legislation treats electric motor-driven cycles with speeds up to 40 mph as motor vehicles, requiring registration, titling, insurance, and a valid driver's license. However, the law mandates that these vehicles must comply with federal motor vehicle safety standards and possess a legitimate vehicle identification number. Most current high-powered e-bikes lack the necessary manufacturer certifications and documentation to meet these requirements. Consequently, while the state offers a regulatory framework for these devices, the majority of existing models cannot be legally registered or operated on public roads under the new rules.

title: Poland rapidly reduces coal use while retaining high-emitting capacity for reliability
summary: Poland's electricity transition is accelerating, with coal's share of generation dropping from 72.5% in 2021 to 52.7% in 2025. Renewables reached 31.4% of generation in 2025, surpassing coal for the first time in June. Gas generation also grew significantly, contributing 24.4 TWh in 2025 alongside wind and solar. Despite falling generation, Poland maintains high-emitting coal capacity through a special derogation in its capacity market auctions. The International Energy Agency expects renewables to overtake coal annually by 2028. Poland faces a dual challenge of reducing energy mix reliance while building the grid infrastructure needed to replace coal's reliability functions.

title: California Dairy Farm Gets Record-Low Carbon Rating for Biogas-to-Hydrogen Project
summary: A dairy farm in Kerman, California, is operating a new biogas project that converts methane waste into hydrogen fuel. The California Air Resources Board assigned the project the lowest carbon-intensity rating in the state's history, sparking debate among environmental groups. Critics argue the project prioritizes climate metrics over local water and air pollution caused by dairy waste lagoons. While regulators highlight the project's potential to displace fossil fuels, environmental advocates contend that carbon credits incentivize herd expansion and mask ongoing contamination issues. The facility, Bar 20, has faced previous citations for runoff and groundwater monitoring failures. CARB officials maintain the low rating reflects the capture of methane that would otherwise enter the atmosphere, though they note the approval is provisional. The project supplies hydrogen to refueling stations via truck, despite broader market challenges for hydrogen fuel. Experts warn that energy losses during conversion reduce the total fuel yield compared to direct biogas use. This case illustrates the tension between state climate goals and local environmental justice concerns surrounding industrial agriculture.

title: Pennsylvania Subsidizes Coal Waste While Renewables Lag Behind
summary: Pennsylvania continues to spend millions subsidizing waste coal burning despite the state's renewable energy generation ranking 42nd nationally. The Alternative Energy Portfolio Standards (AEPS) regulation mandates utilities purchase specific fuel sources, with waste coal currently providing about 3 percent of the state's energy compared to 4 percent from renewables. Critics argue these subsidies hinder climate progress, noting that burning waste coal produces significantly more greenhouse gas emissions than traditional coal plants. Although House Bill 501 aims to reduce waste coal's role and increase renewable requirements, the proposal has stalled in the Democrat-controlled State House. Political opposition comes from both Republicans and a faction of Democrats representing coal regions who fear plant closures. Industry representatives warn that altering subsidies could force specialized plants into precarious 'peaking' modes, potentially ending cleanup operations. Meanwhile, costs for the program have risen sharply since 2020 border restrictions required in-state waste coal. Environmental advocates suggest creating a separate state program to manage waste coal, but lawmakers remain divided on the best path forward.

title: Global EV sales surge in July as Tesla Model 3 drops and Leapmotor rises
summary: CleanTechnica reports that global pure electric vehicle registrations reached 1.8 million units in July, representing a 16% year-over-year increase. While battery electric vehicles (BEVs) grew significantly, plugin hybrid sales declined by 11%, causing the overall plugin market to rise only 7%. BEVs accounted for 71% of all plugin sales in July, marking the highest share since 2022. The Tesla Model 3 saw deliveries crash 44% year-over-year to 19,000 units, falling to 11th place globally, whereas the Tesla Model Y remained the top-selling model despite a 9% drop. BYD's Song secured second place, aided by exports and a new generation, while a group of small EVs from Geely and BYD filled the third through seventh spots. Leapmotor achieved record sales, doubling its output year-over-year to reach six-digit levels and surpassing Hyundai-Kia to take sixth place among manufacturers. Toyota also set a new record with 50,415 registrations, edging closer to Volkswagen in the legacy OEM rankings. The article notes that excluding China and the USA, EV sales jumped 50% year-over-year in July.

title: Reports suggest regular iPhone 18 may launch in March 2027
summary: Reports indicate Apple might delay the regular iPhone 18 until March 2027, focusing the September event on Pro models. Consequently, buyers in India are considering whether to purchase the current iPhone 17 now or wait for potential price drops after the upcoming launch event.

title: Tim Cook leaves Apple CEO role after 15 years of expanding product lines
summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook ends his 15-year tenure on August 31, succeeded by John Ternus. During his leadership, Apple introduced the Apple Watch, AirPods, Apple Silicon, and Vision Pro to diversify its business beyond traditional hardware.

title: Nvidia reportedly agrees to buy Hugging Face for US$13 billion
summary: Nvidia has reportedly agreed to acquire Hugging Face for US$13 billion, a deal that would significantly expand the chipmaker's influence over open-source AI development. The article notes that Hugging Face previously rejected a US$500 million investment from Nvidia in 2024 to avoid concentration of power. This transaction occurs as OpenAI develops custom chips that could compete with Nvidia's hardware. By owning Hugging Face, Nvidia aims to steer developers toward its processors rather than those from competitors like Google. The startup generates approximately US$150 million in annual revenue, making the purchase price roughly 86 times its annualised revenue. Critics argue this move creates a paradox where a company promoting open models may instead strengthen its own market dominance.

title: Malaysian PM reinstates 300-litre monthly RON95 transport fuel limit per citizen
summary: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced the reinstatement of a 300-litre monthly quota for subsidised RON95 transport fuel. This measure is part of broader steps to address rising living costs in Malaysia.

title: CMA vet ownership rules change risks pet owners being misled by private equity firms
summary: The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) removed requirements for multinational companies to disclose which veterinary practices they own, raising concerns that pet owners could be misled. The CMA found that pet owners pay 16.6% more on average at large vet groups than at independent practices within the £6.3bn market. While new rules propose capping prescriptions at £21, the Progressive Veterinary Association (PVA) has threatened a judicial review after the CMA softened wording to allow corporations to obscure ultimate ownership. The PVA argues this allows large groups to hide behind misleading brand names, whereas the CMA believes recognisable high street names are more useful to consumers. More than 60% of practices are currently owned by six major groups, including private equity investors and Mars Petcare.

title: Iceland rejects EU membership plan in referendum
summary: Iceland has rejected the government's proposal to hold accession talks with the European Union, public broadcaster RUV reported. The "No" camp secured 52.5 percent of votes while the "Yes" camp received 47.5 percent. Prime Minister Kristrun Frostadottir had previously stated that a "No" would end all EU speculation. Campaigners argued that membership could lower interest rates but also threatened sovereignty and fishing waters. Iceland first applied to join the EU in 2009 during a financial crisis.

title: Toxic waste from Gaza war now threatens Israeli public health
summary: The article reports that untreated sewage and contaminated rubble from Gaza are creating significant environmental hazards for Israel. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the Board of Peace recently agreed to form a working group on sanitation, though its structure remains undisclosed. Daily sewage flows from Gaza into the Mediterranean, causing desalination plant shutdowns and toxic algae blooms that impact Israeli coastal waters. Additionally, the transfer of approximately 60 million tonnes of rubble into Israel and the West Bank risks spreading heavy metals and pathogens to local populations. The text notes that while groundwater contamination is less likely, chemical salts pose long-term risks to shared aquifers. Environmental groups warn that ignoring these shared ecological boundaries endangers Israeli citizens just as it does Palestinians.

title: Trump's economic pressure on Iran may raise global stakes and costs
summary: Sina Toossi argues that the US strategy to isolate Iran economically could backfire by raising global stakes. The author notes that while Iran faces severe economic constraints, its leadership views further US pressure as an act of war. Iranian officials warn they will protect neighboring states and threaten Gulf oil exports if sanctions expand. Toossi highlights that China has ordered firms to ignore US sanctions, complicating Washington's goal of total isolation. The author suggests the US faces a choice between tolerating trade or escalating coercion, which risks multiplying confrontations. Ultimately, Toossi describes the situation as a dangerous contest of endurance where the US bets Iran's economy breaks first. The analysis warns this approach could lead to higher energy prices and a more confrontational adversary.

title: Reviewer praises British film Finding Emily for its romantic comedy style
summary: A reviewer enjoyed the British movie Finding Emily, noting its resemblance to older romantic comedies. The film explores themes of class, accent, and US/UK differences while being skeptical of media and certain feminist branches. Laura Lewis is highlighted as stealing the show in the production. The reviewer describes the film as mostly entertaining and hopes for more similar movies.

title: AI Video Tools Threaten Millions of Jobs in China's Gig Economy
summary: Advanced AI video generation programs are challenging millions of jobs in China's short-drama sector. ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 model enables digital actors to replace humans with higher-quality output. Greg Wollner, a Beijing producer, noted production volume dropped after the tool's release. DataEye reported that 89 of the top 100 animated dramas on Douyin were AI productions in May.

title: Lonely Planet ranks ten global destinations for autumn foliage viewing
summary: Lonely Planet has released a ranking of the ten best destinations worldwide for viewing fall foliage, covering locations across six continents. The list highlights how autumn colors vary by region, with Northern Hemisphere sites peaking in October and Southern Hemisphere locations like Chile and Tasmania displaying colors in April or May. Wine regions such as Burgundy and Ticino feature prominently, while wildlife viewing remains a key attraction in parks from Alberta to the Scottish Highlands. Travelers are advised to plan carefully, as many sites require renting a car and booking months in advance. Specific recommendations include the Adirondacks for water-based leaf peeping, Alberta for golden larch groves, and the Iya Valley in Japan for remote gorges. The guide also notes that timing is critical, as peak color windows can shift by several days depending on weather conditions. Each entry provides practical advice on transportation, accommodation, and local activities tailored to the unique landscape of that destination.

title: U.S. News ranks ten best 2026 SUVs for towing capacity
summary: U.S. News ranks ten SUVs for 2026 towing, noting that while they tow less than trucks, they offer spacious cabins and comfortable rides. The list includes luxury and nonluxury models, plus electric vehicles, with capacities reaching up to 10,300 pounds. Experts recommend the 80/20 towing rule to maintain control and braking performance. Reaching maximum ratings often requires specific trims and packages that increase pricing. The Jeep Grand Wagoneer tops the list with a 10,000-pound capacity at the Limited Altitude trim with the Heavy-Duty Towing Package. The Ford Expedition reaches 9,600 pounds with four-wheel drive and the Heavy-Duty Trailer Tow package. The Land Rover Defender offers an 8,200-pound rating with a Towing Package, while the Lexus GX achieves 9,096 pounds across several trims without extra equipment. The GMC Hummer EV SUV matches the Grand Wagoneer at 10,000 pounds but requires the dual-motor version. The Toyota Sequoia hits 9,520 pounds with the rear-wheel-drive SR5 model. The Infiniti QX80 and Nissan Armada both tow 8,500 pounds without additional packages. The Chevrolet Tahoe reaches 8,400 pounds with the 5.3-liter V8, rear-wheel drive, and Max Trailering package.

title: US Billionaires Increasingly Merge Business and Political Power Globally
summary: John P. Ruehl reports that the United States is leading a global trend where ultrawealthy businessmen hold significant political influence. The article notes that the Trump administration includes 57 cabinet members and senior officials with net worths exceeding $100 million. Ruehl explains that this surge taps into an anti-establishment mood while shrinking the permanent bureaucracy elevates political appointees. The author compares this American phenomenon to China, where more than a third of billionaires have held political office, and Russia, where oligarchs remain embedded in politics despite Kremlin control. Ruehl argues that the fusion of business and government affects geopolitics as major firms operate global infrastructure foreign governments depend on. The article concludes that as business and political disputes overlap, commercial infrastructure can become a target in geopolitical conflicts.

title: WhatsApp group facilitated hundreds of millions in cash transfers for crime
summary: An investigation by the European Broadcasting Union found a WhatsApp group called 'Traders of Greater Europe' was used to move hundreds of millions of euros via the hawala system. The 532-member chat, containing over 82,000 messages, arranged cash transfers for organized crime and extremism without a paper trail. Belgian magistrate Vincent Guerra described the network as professional and global, noting it funded the Islamic State and facilitated people smuggling. The cache of messages was obtained after a 2024 Belgian court case convicted six money launderers, including network head Abu Adam. Police discovered evidence of at least 12,000 transactions, supported by thousands of photos of banknotes and identity cards. While hawala is legal in the UK for registered brokers, it remains illegal in most of the EU. Authorities in Austria also dismantled rings using the system for human trafficking and torture. Europol officials state the hawala system is the primary money-laundering channel for organized crime across Europe.

title: Activist Erin Brockovich now challenges Meta and Google over data centers
summary: Erin Brockovich, the woman who won a landmark lawsuit against Pacific Gas & Electric, has turned her activism toward Big Tech. She has launched a reporting platform to track the environmental impact of artificial intelligence data centers operated by companies like Meta and Google. Experts argue her work exemplifies ecofeminism and validates the legitimacy of lay knowledge over academic credentials. Alicia H. Puleo, a philosopher, states that Brockovich defends the Earth and rejects androcentric authority. Eva Saldaña of Greenpeace Spain notes that women's leadership often stems from their structural position in society regarding care work. Alfredo Menéndez Navarro, a professor, explains that Brockovich's approach represents a democratization of knowledge where communities investigate risks. Charles Barthold, a lecturer, suggests younger generations can learn perseverance and justice from her practice. The article concludes that society needs more role models like Brockovich to challenge indifference and protect the future.

title: Manhunt launched after woman killed and five injured in Swiss rave shooting
summary: A manhunt is underway after a shooting at a rave in Aarau killed one woman and injured five others. Police confirmed the victim died at the scene while the injured were hospitalized with varying injuries. The perpetrator's identity and motives remain unknown as authorities cordoned off the area and deployed officers up to 30km away. Local DJ Tekibo described the event as heartbreaking, noting he lost an important friend. Swiss police are requesting witness photos and videos while a large contingent of officers and a Swiss Army helicopter survey the region.

title: Andy Burnham excludes killers from early release scheme
summary: Andy Burnham announced changes to the early release scheme to ensure PC Andrew Harper's killers remain in prison. The prime minister stated that anyone convicted of unlawful killing would be excluded from the program. Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who killed the officer in 2019, will not have their sentences shortened under the new rules. Debbie Adlam, Harper's mother, expressed relief but noted the campaign was traumatic. Burnham admitted the decision means hundreds more people will stay in prison while addressing overcrowding. He also plans to end imprisonment for public protection sentences by the end of this parliament.

title: 25-year-old man charged with murder of 29-year-old in Tuas
summary: Police in Singapore charged a 25-year-old man with the murder of a 29-year-old man on Monday. Officers found the victim dead on Tuas South Street 15 after receiving a call for assistance at 10.10pm on Saturday. The suspect was arrested within four hours, and preliminary investigations indicated the two men knew each other. Police stated the offence carries the death penalty and investigations are ongoing.

title: Iceland voters reject resuming European Union accession talks
summary: Icelanders voted to reject the resumption of European Union accession talks in a tight referendum result reported by local broadcaster RUV. While Reykjavík constituencies supported the proposal, rural and coastal areas delivered decisive 'No' majorities. The outcome will likely shelve the EU debate in Icelandic politics for at least two more years. Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir's government had revived the question, arguing that a volatile international climate made closer ties worth pursuing. Iceland's relationship with Brussels will not fundamentally change as the country remains in the European Economic Area and Schengen zone. The referendum carries no legal force, but the government has committed to abiding by the result.

title: One dead, five hurt in Switzerland rave shooting; manhunt continues
summary: Police report one death and five injuries after a shooting at a rave in Aarau, Switzerland. Authorities launched a manhunt for the unknown attacker while urging the public to avoid the area. The Aargau Cantonal Police confirmed several shots were fired at a large group. A Super Puma helicopter and disaster response units assisted the investigation. Switzerland maintains high gun ownership rates despite rare violent shootings.

title: Nepal warns of fresh floods as death toll rises to 734
summary: Nepal authorities warn of possible new flooding as water levels rise in the Bhotekoshi River. The combined death toll in Nepal and Tibet reached 750, with over 3,000 people missing. Rescue crews are clearing a major highway while residents struggle with repeated evacuation alarms. Many homes remain without electricity due to damaged power lines.

title: Dozens of soldiers arrested in Niger after attempted mutiny
summary: Dozens of soldiers were arrested or killed in Niger's capital following an attempted mutiny driven by anger over militant violence. Russia's Africa Corps provided support to local forces to suppress the rebellion at a base near the presidential palace. Loyalist forces regained control of the airport, though some rebel troops remained mobile. Public gatherings in Niamey expressed support for military leader Abdourahamane Tchiani, who took power in a 2023 coup.

title: One Nation leader Mike Newman considers reviving scrapped NSW trade posts
summary: One Nation NSW leader Mike Newman stated he would consider reinstating overseas trade commissioner roles if his party wins the next state election. Newman, a former commissioner in Tokyo, criticized the Minns government for scrapping the positions following a scandal involving John Barilaro. He argued NSW cannot be a 'hermit kingdom' and that experienced private sector staff could replace public servants. Meanwhile, Premier Chris Minns begins a four-day visit to India to attract investment.

title: New book reveals Nairobi expansion drives rural land sales and family tensions
summary: Anthropologist Peter Lockwood reports that Nairobi's growth is forcing rural families in Kiambu to sell land due to rising values and economic hopelessness. The author, who conducted research from 2017 to 2022, explains that smallholders are selling ancestral plots despite senior men's earlier advice to retain them. Lockwood notes that young men feel working for low wages is not worth the effort, leading to a sense of abandon. The book highlights gendered conflicts where male inheritors exclude sisters from land inheritance. Lockwood argues that state intervention, such as a universal basic income, is needed to address youth hopelessness and land inequality in Kenya.

title: Zimbabwe: 27 Dead After Minibus and Truck Collide Near Chivhu
summary: At least 27 people died after a minibus and truck collided head-on near Chivhu, Zimbabwe, on Friday evening. Police stated both vehicles carried an unknown number of passengers, with seven others injured. Footage from ZBC showed the minibus severely damaged after the crash. Traffic accidents remain common in Zimbabwe due to poor road conditions and driving standards. Minibus taxis, known as kombi, are frequently criticized for overloading passengers.

title: Food garden or swimming pool? South Africa’s water crisis isn’t just about a shortage. It’s about equality
summary: A team of South African water researchers argues that the country's water crisis stems from inequality rather than just scarcity. The authors report that current definitions of fairness vary widely, hindering local authorities from implementing effective solutions. They propose three core principles for equitable water management: human rights extending to ecological integrity, social justice covering both decision-making processes and outcome distribution, and context-specific historical considerations. The researchers state that past apartheid-era inequalities must be addressed to ensure disadvantaged communities receive priority access. They call for governments, scientists, and communities to collaborate on participatory management that treats water as essential to life rather than a commodity. Ultimately, the team suggests that sustainable development requires managing water resources to benefit both current and future generations.

title: Investors profit while consumers suffer as Iran war reshapes global economy
summary: Six months into the conflict between the U.S. and Israel, the global economy has avoided predicted catastrophe despite uneven impacts. Investment strategist Michael Ashley Schulman of Cerity Partners described the financial recovery as a "Mission Impossible" success. While stock markets have rebounded significantly, consumers face higher costs for fuel and travel. The International Air Transport Association estimates jet fuel prices remain 70% above 2025 levels, forcing airlines to raise fares. Conversely, the war has accelerated clean energy adoption, with the International Energy Agency projecting electric vehicles to reach 29% of global sales in 2026. However, the World Bank reports fertilizer prices peaked 44% higher than prewar levels, threatening food security. Meanwhile, President Donald Trump and his family have benefited financially through investments in military contractors and energy stocks, though a White House spokeswoman denied any conflicts of interest.

title: PM Modi joins yoga session in Uzbekistan during state visit
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi participated in a yoga session in Tashkent hosted by the Yoga Federation of Uzbekistan on August 30, 2026. The Ministry of External Affairs stated that the activity strengthens people-to-people ties between India and Uzbekistan. During his two-day state visit, Mr. Modi also met with President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and the Indian community. The leaders are scheduled to review cooperation in trade, defence, and digital connectivity. Mr. Modi is currently on the first leg of a visit that will also include Kyrgyzstan.

title: Nepal warns of fresh floods as death toll reaches 734
summary: Nepal authorities warn of possible fresh flooding on Sunday after water levels rose in the Bhotekoshi River. The combined death toll in Nepal and Tibet reached 750, with over 3,000 people missing. Rescue crews are clearing a major highway while residents struggle with near-constant alarms and destroyed bridges. Many homes remain without electricity due to tangled power lines.

title: Venezuela interim president says US oil deal lasts 25 years
summary: Venezuelan interim President Delcy Rodriguez stated that a historic oil agreement with the United States will remain in effect for 25 years. The deal aims to increase daily production to over 1.5 million barrels across eight fields in the Orinoco Oil Belt. Rodriguez noted that approximately $19 per barrel will go directly to Venezuela, potentially generating $209.335 billion in revenue at $65 per barrel. US President Donald Trump described the transaction as the biggest oil deal in world history, securing majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of proven reserves.

title: NFL targets Japan for expansion as international games grow
summary: The NFL plans to expand into Japan as part of its global growth strategy, according to Brett Gosper, the league's head of Europe and Asia-Pacific. The 2026 regular season will feature nine international games across seven countries, an increase from the previous year. Gosper noted strong interest and participation in the Japanese market. However, a former World Rugby CEO suggested potential challenges regarding touchdown scoring in some Asian regions.

title: Pegula and Tiafoe praise tennis diversity progress while noting cost barriers
summary: American tennis players Jessica Pegula and Frances Tiafoe stated the sport is advancing in diversity. Pegula highlighted global reach and representation among Black and Asian players. Tiafoe noted historic moments in the men's game but emphasized that financial barriers remain a significant challenge. The USTA reported a 450,000 player increase among Black Americans in 2025.

title: Nepal issues fresh flood warning as 3,000 remain missing
summary: Nepal and Chinese authorities report a combined death toll of 750, with over 3,000 people still missing after devastating floods. A new flood alert was issued as river levels rose, while scientists suggest a glacier collapse may have triggered the disaster. Rescue teams are searching for more than 100 trapped hydropower workers in swamped tunnels. International aid, including $3.6 million from the US, has been pledged to support the relief efforts.

title: Shooting at Aarau rave kills one and injures five in Switzerland
summary: Local police and media reported a shooting at a rave in Aarau, Switzerland, that killed one person and injured five early Sunday. Police spokesperson Pascal Wenzel stated authorities were alerted around 2:30 a.m. to the incident at the horse racing track. The search for the unknown perpetrator remains ongoing, with possible motives and circumstances still unclear. Neighboring German police also joined the search efforts.

title: Putin resumes Kyiv strikes after 37 deaths in Myla care home tragedy
summary: Russia resumed drone strikes on Kyiv overnight following the deadliest attack on Ukraine's capital this year, which killed 37 people. The Russian defence ministry claimed the warehouse in Myla stored drone components, while Ukrainian officials stated it held ammunition and opened criminal proceedings for official negligence. President Volodymyr Zelensky vowed to punish those responsible for storing explosives near residential areas. Meanwhile, Moscow announced preparations for massive strikes against Ukraine's energy infrastructure. In other developments, Russia tested a nuclear-capable intercontinental ballistic missile with a range exceeding 6,700km. Additionally, UK warships tracked Russian vessels in the English Channel during an intense operation.

title: Shooting at Aarau rave kills one and injures five in Switzerland
summary: Police and local media reported one death and five injuries from a shooting at a rave in Aarau, Switzerland. Cantonal police stated on X that the victims were hit by gunfire at the event in the canton's capital. Swiss public broadcaster SRF identified the gathering as a rave. Authorities launched a major operation and urged residents to avoid the area.

title: Motorcyclist dies after crash at Elwomple racing event
summary: A motorcyclist died after a crash at a racing event near Adelaide. SA Police confirmed emergency services responded to the incident at Elwomple. Motorcycling South Australia and The Bend stated the rider was treated by paramedics and died at the scene. Authorities are preparing a report for the coroner. Motorcycling Australia is working with relevant authorities following the tragedy.

title: Putin and Xi lead SCO summit in Kyrgyzstan to counter Western influence
summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping are attending a two-day summit in Kyrgyzstan alongside leaders from Iran and India. The gathering marks 25 years of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, which Russia and China use to promote a multipolar world. Several members face ongoing wars or trade tensions with the West. Experts note that while the bloc claims significant global weight, concrete benefits for members like Iran remain uncertain.

title: CIA Chief Proposes Trump-Putin-Zelenskyy Meeting Amid Global Disasters
summary: This briefing covers a range of international news, including diplomatic proposals, natural disasters, and geopolitical conflicts. CIA Director John Ratcliffe proposed a meeting between US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy during a visit to Moscow, Axios reported. Meanwhile, devastating floods in Nepal and China have killed at least 750 people, with over 3,000 still missing. The text also details various other global events, from military actions in Lebanon and Gaza to legal disputes involving AI and music publishers.

title: Angélique Kidjo receives first Hollywood Walk of Fame star for Black African artist
summary: Angélique Kidjo unveiled a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame on August 18, becoming the first Black African artist to receive the honor. The article notes that previous honorees born in Africa were white South Africans, highlighting the significance of this milestone for Hollywood's recognition of African talent. Kidjo, born in Ouidah, Benin, has won five Grammy Awards and the Polar Music Prize while advocating for African cultural heritage. She broke barriers by blending Beninese rhythms with global genres like funk and jazz, refusing to be confined to the "world music" category. Beyond her art, Kidjo serves as a UNICEF goodwill ambassador and founded the Batonga Foundation to promote education in Africa. The piece concludes that her career has transformed how the world listens to the continent, moving beyond stereotypes of conflict to celebrate creativity.
