summary: Jon from Cardiff established a free school uniform swap shop to assist families facing the cost-of-living crisis. The initiative has grown from a single school to over 200 schools, facilitating the exchange of 8,000 items since its website launched in March. Jon estimates the platform could save Welsh families more than £50m annually, addressing an average uniform cost of £343 for primary and £442 for comprehensive pupils. Participants report that the scheme effectively removes the stigma associated with second-hand clothing while promoting sustainability. The project also connects parents within their communities and complements existing government measures to limit uniform costs in England.

title: Guardian editorial urges securing rare earth supply chains
summary: The Guardian editorial argues that the world must secure essential rare earth supply chains after China blocked exports to Japan in 2010. China currently controls about 70% of global mining and 90% of processing. The US announced a $12bn critical minerals reserve, while Europe faces risks relying solely on Washington. The editorial calls for multilateral partnerships and innovation to reduce environmental damage and import dependence.

title: NASA launches repurposed spy satellite as Roman Space Telescope
summary: NASA launched the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope from Cape Canaveral on Sunday using a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket. The agency described the observatory as a repurposed spy satellite originally built for the National Reconnaissance Office before being donated to NASA in 2012. The roughly $4 billion project aims to map dark matter and dark energy while surveying more than two billion galaxies. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman stated the telescope will become a household name alongside Hubble and Webb. The mission is scheduled for five years, though the telescope may possess enough fuel for five additional years. President Donald Trump called the launch beautiful and confirmed he is supplying NASA's budget. Scientists expect the first high-resolution images before the winter holidays.

title: Trump plans to refill U.S. emergency oil reserve with Venezuelan crude
summary: President Donald Trump announced plans to use Venezuelan crude oil to replenish the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, which has reached its lowest level in over four decades. The administration noted the plan could help restore supplies but faces significant challenges regarding storage compatibility and infrastructure. Potential benefits include opportunities for U.S. refiners and companies like Chevron and Eni. However, issues such as high sulfur content and deteriorated Venezuelan infrastructure remain unresolved.

title: Google Maps renames Lake Ontario to Lake America for US users only
summary: Google updated its US maps to show Lake America, following President Trump's directive, while Canadian users still see Lake Ontario. Ontario Premier Doug Ford criticized the move as backwards and part of a damaging trade dispute. The tech giant stated it aligns with the US Geographic Names Information System. Apple Maps has not made the change yet.

title: Google Maps renamed Lake Ontario to Lake America for U.S. users
summary: Google Maps updated names for U.S. users to reflect a new official designation for Lake Ontario. The company stated it follows the U.S. Geographic Names Information System after President Trump signed an executive order. Critics accused Google of capitulating to political pressure while Apple Maps retained the original name. Canadian officials expressed anger over the change amid ongoing trade tensions.

title: Coyote vs. Acme debuts with $15.5 million while Spider-Man remains top
summary: The AP reports that 'Coyote vs. Acme' opened with $15.5 million, becoming the best debut for Ketchup Entertainment. 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' retained the No. 1 spot with $22.2 million. The film, originally canceled by Warner Bros., was acquired by Ketchup for $50 million. Critics and audiences praised the movie, which earned a 95% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Hundreds mourn four victims of Haiti gang attack that killed 47
summary: Hundreds attended a funeral in Kenscoff for four victims of a brutal gang attack that killed 47 people. UN Human Rights Office spokesperson Marta Hurtado stated that 150 armed gang members participated in the August 23 assault, executing 34 people after forcing them from a church. Survivors blame police for failing to prevent the carnage, while the National Police ordered an investigation into potential negligence. The attack left over 2,600 people homeless and highlighted the ongoing crisis as gangs control an estimated 70% of Port-au-Prince.

title: NYC explosion linked to e-bike battery kills teenager
summary: Fire officials linked a deadly blaze at a Brooklyn housing complex to an e-bike lithium-ion battery. An 18-year-old man died after the fast-moving fire broke out Friday evening. At least 34 fire trucks responded to the scene at Albany Houses. The victim's identity remains unreleased as the investigation continues.

title: Milo Yiannopoulos deported from US faces struggle to fit in with UK right wing
summary: Milo Yiannopoulos has returned to the UK after being deported from the US for overstaying his visa. Sources at GB News stated they would not employ him, noting his appeal is primarily to an American audience. While some UK right-wing figures like Raheem Kassam expect him to resurface as an adviser or reality TV contestant, Reform UK will not accept him. Conversely, Restore Britain, led by Rupert Lowe, may accept him as a party member or adviser. Yiannopoulos previously worked for Breitbart News and promoted Donald Trump before leaving the UK in 2019. He has since worked on Kanye West's 2024 White House campaign and made disparaging comments about President Trump. The Department of Homeland Security confirmed he legally entered the US in 2019 but chose to overstay his welcome.

title: US Open day one results include withdrawals and upsets
summary: The article reports highlights from the first day of the US Open in New York. Jessica Pegula advanced to the second round with a dominant win, while Marin Cilic and Casper Ruud withdrew due to injuries. Barbora Krejcikova became the first seeded player to exit after losing to Kamilla Rakhimova. Unseeded Kamil Majchrzak defeated Hamad Medjedovic to become the first men's player to reach the second round. Play began under temperatures around 25 degrees Celsius.

title: Nepal struggles to preserve recovered bodies as flood toll touches 788
summary: Four days after a glacial collapse triggered floods in Nepal, the death toll reached 788 with 2,502 people still missing. Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai stated that authorities urgently require freezer units and DNA-testing kits to prevent decomposition. Over 900 workers remain missing from hydropower sites while international experts assist in rescue operations. Authorities began mass burials of unidentified bodies in Chitwan after collecting DNA samples for potential future identification. India reported 275 missing nationals while the Nepal Tourism Board noted 591 foreign nationals remain unaccounted for.

title: Trump demands FCC punish NBC host Kristen Welker for criticizing his endorsements
summary: President Donald Trump told the FCC to rebuke or punish NBC anchor Kristen Welker after she described his endorsed candidates' success as mixed. Trump accused Welker of purposeful inaccuracy and urged FCC Chair Brendan Carr to take the threat seriously. Welker previously appeared on NBC to discuss the mixed record of Trump-backed candidates before the Sunday broadcast. Trump has endorsed over 300 candidates, with 214 of 218 House winners and all 24 Republican Senate primaries he supported securing victories. However, five of 21 endorsed gubernatorial candidates lost their primaries, including Mike Lindell in Minnesota. The FCC lacks the authority to punish Welker for her editorial content, though critics worry NBC may face future regulatory pressure. This incident follows similar actions against ABC and Sinclair, which preempted Jimmy Kimmel's show under Trump's direction.

title: Trump threatens FCC report against NBC anchor over election coverage
summary: President Donald Trump stated on Truth Social that NBC journalist Kristen Welker will be reported to the FCC for rebuke or punishment regarding her reporting on his endorsement results. Trump claimed Welker's assessment of mixed results was inaccurate, asserting his endorsements succeeded 98 percent to 100 percent of the time. He also criticized the Radical Left News for allegedly harassing anything related to him. Experts note the FCC lacks legal authority to punish broadcasters for their viewpoints, and several networks have filed lawsuits against the commission over political retaliation concerns.

title: Scientists detect hundreds of deep earthquakes beneath Germany's Laacher See volcano
summary: Researchers monitoring the Laacher See volcano in western Germany have recorded over 500 micro-earthquakes between September 2022 and August 2023. These deep low-frequency earthquakes suggest magmatic fluids are moving at depths of 12 to 14 kilometres. Torsten Dahm of the GFZ explains that such activity indicates the volcanic system remains active, though Joachim Ritter notes no high-frequency swarms or surface uplift have been observed. The volcano last erupted approximately 13,084 years ago, an event estimated to be as powerful as 500 Hiroshima bombs. While recent CO2 degassing and hydraulic fracturing of rock confirm ongoing underground processes, scientists do not expect an eruption in the near future.

title: Feud over Paris Opera ceiling continues 60 years after restoration
summary: The article reports that a dispute regarding the Paris Opera's ceiling remains unresolved six decades after its restoration. The text notes the ongoing nature of the conflict without providing specific details about the parties involved or the current status of the disagreement.

title: Nepal head teacher evacuates 900 students minutes before deadly floods
summary: Rajendra Dawadi, headteacher of Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School in Nuwakot, Nepal, evacuated 900 pupils just 10 minutes before devastating floods struck. Dawadi told the BBC he received four urgent warnings within minutes, prompting an immediate decision to move students to higher ground. The floods have claimed at least 794 lives and left 2,426 people missing. Student Yunisha Amatya, 16, recalled scrambling to safety with friends after teachers informed them of the danger. Her father, Yubaraj Amatya, rushed to the school after being unable to reach his daughter by phone. Dawadi stated that a delayed decision could have resulted in total loss of life. He noted that better warning systems, such as sirens, might have aided earlier responses.

title: Seven killed and 23 missing after ferry capsizes off northern Cyprus
summary: At least seven people died and 23 remain missing after a ferry capsized off northern Cyprus, according to local administration head Ünal Üstel. The vessel, carrying 259 passengers and eight crew, departed Kyrenia before hitting two waves and sinking. Authorities have detained the captain and seven crew members for investigation while search and rescue operations continue. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has ordered extensive rescue efforts in cooperation with local authorities.

title: India and Uzbekistan upgrade ties to strategic partnership with $5bn trade goal
summary: India and Uzbekistan upgraded their relationship to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Tashkent. The two governments set a $5bn trade target for 2030 and are close to signing a new long-term uranium supply agreement. India's Ministry of External Affairs reported positive discussions regarding the deal. The leaders also expanded cooperation in defence, digital payments, and education while reaffirming support for India's UN Security Council bid.

title: French LGBTQ leader hospitalized after homophobic attack in Paris
summary: Prosecutors said Pierre Picavet, a police officer and LGBTQ rights leader, was hospitalized after a nighttime attack in Paris. The suspect, who had no prior criminal record, was taken into custody after striking Picavet with a bottle. STOP Homophobie condemned the assault as homophobic violence. Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire called the incident despicable and vowed to protect the city from hatred.

title: Guinea-Bissau voters cast ballots in referendum to expand presidential powers
summary: Voters in military-run Guinea-Bissau participated in a Sunday referendum to approve a new constitution that would grant the president expanded powers. AFP correspondents reported that voting began slowly due to rain, while security forces were stationed at key locations. The ruling junta stated the change aims to stabilize institutions before December elections intended to restore civilian rule. However, the opposition has urged a boycott, citing restrictions on public freedoms. The referendum follows a recent coup and seeks to shift the country from a parliamentary to a presidential system.

title: Seven people died after a ferry capsized off Northern Cyprus
summary: The article reports seven deaths following a ferry capsize off Northern Cyprus. It includes a technical error message about a site component failing to load. No further details about the incident are provided in the text.

title: President Erdogan says Türkiye mobilized all resources after ship capsize
summary: President Erdogan stated that Türkiye has mobilized all available resources following a passenger ship capsize off Northern Cyprus. The President emphasized the immediate deployment of aid and rescue efforts to assist those affected by the maritime accident.

title: Swiss police hunt shooter after rave shooting leaves one dead
summary: A shooting at a rave in the Swiss Canton of Aargau killed one person and injured five others. Police are conducting a major manhunt involving German authorities to locate the shooter. Authorities stated they currently have no information regarding the motive, though a fight remains a possibility.

title: Male midwives in Lesotho challenge traditional gender roles in childbirth care
summary: Male midwives in Lesotho are challenging traditional gender roles to address rural healthcare shortages. Ntlhane Sehloho, one of approximately 300 male midwives, has worked for two decades to improve maternal care. While UNICEF reports 92% of births now have trained attendants, the World Health Organization notes men comprise less than 1% of global midwives. Some women feel more comfortable with female providers, while others appreciate the attentive care male midwives offer. UNFPA coordinator Blandina Motaung suggests male midwives may show greater caution due to their lack of personal childbirth experience.

title: Legendary Aboriginal boxer Tony Mundine dies aged 75
summary: Tony Mundine, a renowned Indigenous Australian boxer, has died at the age of 75. His son, Anthony Mundine, confirmed the death and expressed his grief on social media. Mundine was the only Australian to compete professionally in four weight divisions. He held titles at middleweight, light-heavyweight, cruiserweight, and heavyweight. Former boxer Danny Green and Billy Dib paid tributes to his legacy. Mundine retired in 1984 and received the Medal of the Order of Australia in 1986. He is survived by his son, grandson, and cousin.

title: Energy experts express skepticism about Trump's proposed Venezuelan oil deal
summary: Energy experts have raised doubts regarding the Trump administration's new proposal to develop Venezuelan oil. The article notes there are multiple reasons for skepticism about this announcement. NPR reports that the U.S. plans to move forward with the initiative despite these concerns.

title: Pacific leaders meet in Palau to address drug crime amid China-Taiwan tensions
summary: Pacific island leaders will gather in Palau from Monday for a summit focused on transnational drug crime. The 18-member Pacific Islands Forum, hosted by Palau, faces potential overshadowing by China-Taiwan tensions. Palau maintains diplomatic ties with Taiwan, while China, Taiwan, and the United States are among the aid partners invited to the forum. Beijing has protested Taiwan's invitation to the event.

title: 45 Japan prefectures struggle to track vehicle evacuees in disasters
summary: A Jiji survey found that 45 of Japan's 47 prefectures face challenges tracking people evacuating by vehicle during disasters. Officials cite difficulties in locating dispersed evacuees and assessing their health needs. Experts suggest balancing personal comfort with better identification and support systems.

title: Three-year-old Carlos loses father to immigration detention and deportation
summary: MindSite News reports that three-year-old Carlos Carino suffered emotional distress after his father, Miguel, was detained by ICE and later self-deported to Mexico. Carlos's mother, Jazmin, navigated the separation through painful visits and now relies on video calls to maintain contact. Experts warn that such forced separations create toxic stress, leading to anxiety, depression, and long-term developmental issues in children. Studies cited in the article link immigration enforcement actions to increased school absences and mental health diagnoses among immigrant families. While the family hopes for future reunification, they currently face economic hardship and emotional strain as Carlos's confidence fades without his father's presence.

title: Darializa Ávila Chevalier wins New York congressional primary
summary: Darializa Ávila Chevalier defeated veteran Congressman Adriano Espaillat in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary for New York's 13th Congressional District. The 32-year-old graduate student secured more than 49% of the vote in Upper Manhattan, becoming the first person of Dominican descent to potentially represent the district in Washington. Justice Democrats recruited Chevalier to run after she spent 14 years as a community organizer and became a serious threat to the establishment-backed incumbent. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani endorsed Chevalier after withdrawing his support for Espaillat, helping to shift the race toward a candidate focused on grassroots organizing. Chevalier, an openly socialist and member of the Democratic Socialists of America, plans to focus on affordable housing and eradicating child poverty if she wins the November 3, 2026 general election. She faces a deeply Democratic district where she is widely expected to win the general election.

title: US announces $3.6M humanitarian aid for Nepal floods
summary: The US announced $3.6 million in humanitarian aid for Nepal, including food assistance for 10,000 households. The State Department stated that embassies in Nepal and China are assisting Americans and supporting relief efforts. Devastating floods along the Nepal-China border killed at least 675 people. Nearly 3,000 people remain missing, including 100 Americans and 589 foreign nationals.

title: China's fertility decline reflects success of modernization and women's independence
summary: The article argues that China's falling birthrate signals the success of its modernization efforts rather than economic failure. Interviews with three women from the one-child generation illustrate how expanded education and career options have reshaped life choices. Parents invested heavily in daughters' independence, yet this empowerment now conflicts with traditional expectations of early marriage and childbearing. The author notes that women increasingly view motherhood as a personal choice rather than an obligation. Consequently, the fertility crisis emerges as evidence that women have successfully prioritized autonomy over state or family demands.

title: Five arrested in alleged gang rape case in Vambay Colony
summary: Nunna police arrested five individuals on Sunday regarding an alleged gang rape in Vambay Colony. Police Commissioner S. V. Rajasekhar Babu directed the arrests following the incident. ACP Prasad stated the accused committed the crime while under the influence of alcohol. The arrests were made under the supervision of the NTR Commissionerate.

title: Kandela Khap condemns Haryana school inspection restrictions
summary: The Sarv Jatiya Kandela Khap condemned the Haryana government's decision to restrict public inspections of government schools. Leaders Om Prakash Kandela, Jagat Singh Redhu, and Raj Singh Kandela stated that villagers have a legitimate stake in schools built on donated land. The statement followed Education Minister Mahipal Dhanda's announcement banning unauthorized entry after CJP activists reported deficiencies. Khap leaders urged the government to withdraw restrictions and focus on improving law and order.

title: Owaisi accuses RSS of hypocrisy over Hindu-Muslim unity remarks
summary: AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi criticized RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat for alleged hypocrisy regarding Hindu-Muslim unity. Owaisi claimed the RSS projects a different image globally while its founders opposed such unity. He cited writings by K B Hedgewar and M S Golwalkar to support his allegations. Bhagwat, speaking in New York, stated that a Hindu must believe all humans have dignity. The RSS chief is currently on a global tour for the organization's centenary celebrations.

title: IISc researchers develop reprocessable eco-friendly foam for cold-chain packaging
summary: Researchers at the Indian Institute of Science have developed an eco-friendly bio-based foam designed for commercial use in cold-chain packaging. Absolute Cold LLP is currently working to integrate the material into temperature-controlled solutions. The foam features a unique chemical structure that allows it to be reprocessed instead of discarded after use. Chethan Kumar of the Times of India reported on this development.

title: Wall Street watches jobs report, AI earnings and Tesla Cybercab launch
summary: Investors are focusing on the upcoming August US jobs report and other economic indicators as Wall Street prepares for September. The data may signal the Federal Reserve's next interest rate move. Technology earnings from companies like Dell and Snowflake will keep artificial intelligence in the spotlight. Tesla is set to host an invite-only event for its Cybercab autonomous vehicle. US stocks fell on Friday as bond market moves suggested the central bank might raise rates soon. The S&P 500 dropped 0.2% while the Nasdaq fell 0.5%. For the week, major indices remained slightly higher. Rajendra Kumar Saxena, a content editor at Livemint, reports on these developments.

title: American man says he is moving to India over healthcare costs
summary: A 23-year-old American man named Yuvaan Ibañez Garware announced on Instagram that he plans to relocate from the United States to India. He cited significant differences in healthcare accessibility and cost as the primary reasons for his decision. Garware shared personal accounts of receiving prompt, affordable treatment in India compared to a delayed and expensive experience in the US. He stated that a minor heart attack in India cost him approximately $500, whereas a similar event in America resulted in a $23,000 bill. The article notes that Live Mint could not independently verify these claims and does not endorse them. While the user praised Indian medical facilities, some commenters offered contrasting views on the two nations' healthcare systems.

title: Google Maps displays Lake America for US users following Trump order
summary: Google Maps now shows Lake America for US users, implementing President Donald Trump's renaming order. The company stated the change follows US Geographic Names Information System conventions. Canadian users will continue seeing Lake Ontario, while others see both names. This move mirrors a previous update for the Gulf of Mexico. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney rejected the renaming, noting the Indigenous origin of the name Ontario.

title: Google Maps Renames Lake Ontario to Lake America for US Users
summary: Google updated its US maps to show Lake America following President Trump's directive, while Canadian users still see Lake Ontario. The company stated it aligned the change with the US Geographic Names Information System. Ontario Premier Doug Ford criticized the move as backwards and warned that trade tariffs would devastate the US auto sector. Trump claimed Canada has been ripping the US off for years.

title: Google Maps renames Lake Ontario to Lake America for US users
summary: Google Maps has updated its display to show Lake America for users inside the United States, following a change in the U.S. Geographic Names Information System. The company stated that Canadian users will continue to see Lake Ontario, while others will see both names. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney defended the historic name, noting its Indigenous origins. Meanwhile, MapQuest plans to offer a custom name generator instead of adopting the change.

title: Bhaskar Reddy Elected President of Hyderabad Golf Association
summary: Bhaskar Reddy was elected president of the Hyderabad Golf Association in a close election. He defeated T. Ajay Kumar Reddy by four votes with 216 votes to 212. D. Vanditha Reddy was elected secretary, while G.V. Ramana, Rupinderjit Singh, and Sudanshu Shah were named executive council members in an association release.

title: Bangladesh Foreign Minister says China-Bangladesh 2+2 dialogue starts soon
summary: Bangladesh Foreign Minister Humaiun Kobir announced that the China-Bangladesh two-plus-two dialogue will begin in the very near future. The engagement will cover diplomacy and defence at the Minister of State level before moving to Foreign Minister-level talks. Specific dates remain unconfirmed as discussions are currently being laid. The announcement follows a recent visit by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to China.

title: TVK Cancels Namakkal SIPCOT Project After Farmer Protests
summary: The TVK government in Tamil Nadu has canceled the proposed SIPCOT industrial park at Valapatti following strong opposition from local farmers. Minister Lokesh Tamilselvan announced the project will be relocated to Lathuwadi within the same district. This move marks the third major infrastructure initiative from the previous DMK regime to be scrapped or altered by the current administration. The decision highlights a recurring political pattern where incoming regimes review projects launched by preceding governments amidst local protests.

title: PM Modi receives 36th international honour as India-Uzbekistan trade targets $5B
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi received Uzbekistan's 'Oliy Darajali Do'stlik' Order, marking his 36th international award since 2016. During talks with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, the leaders elevated bilateral ties to a comprehensive strategic partnership. They agreed to an annual trade target of $5 billion by 2030, up from the current volume of over $1 billion. The two nations also signed 11 agreements covering mining, tourism, and a long-term uranium supply framework.

title: Brij Bhushan Singh claims harassment allegations made him a hero
summary: Former Wrestling Federation of India president Brij Bhushan Singh stated that sexual harassment allegations against him have elevated his status. Speaking at a felicitation ceremony in Mahendragarh, he compared the situation to the story of Kaikeyi and Ram. Singh noted that while some wrestlers received significant farewells, their current value is negligible. He defended his past decisions to protect junior wrestlers, arguing that reversing them would have harmed those without influence.

title: Indian Army pilots execute high-altitude helicopter rescue in Ladakh
summary: Indian Army Aviation pilots performed a daring casualty evacuation at 18,600 feet in Ladakh's Zanskar range. The Fire & Fury Corps stated that the team stripped the helicopter of non-essential gear to fly in severe winds with no landing space. Pilots maintained a perilous hover, touching down on one skid on a steep, snow-covered slope. This mission highlights the corps' unique capability to operate mechanized forces in extreme high-altitude environments.

title: Worli Police Camp Begins 77th Ganeshotsav With Grand Idol Procession
summary: The Worli Police Camp Sarvajanik Ganeshotsav Mandal began its 77th Ganeshotsav celebrations today with a grand procession. Police personnel and traffic cops enthusiastically welcomed the 'Mumbai Polisancha Raja' idol from Gansankul to the camp. The event featured traditional dhol-tasha beats and devotional chants, creating a festive atmosphere of devotion.

title: India Women defeat Thailand Women by 94 runs in T20 Asia Cup
summary: India Women defeated Thailand Women by 94 runs in the T20 Asia Cup after setting a target of 160. Shafali Verma scored 64 off 36 balls to help India reach 159/9. Indian spinners Deepti Sharma and Shree Charani took three and two wickets respectively, while Nandani Sharma claimed three wickets for Thailand. Thailand collapsed to 65/16.1 in their chase.

title: Mumbai mandals granted midnight loudspeaker permission on four 2026 Ganpati visarjan days
summary: The Mumbai Suburban Collector issued a notification allowing sarvajanik Ganeshotsav mandals to use loudspeakers until midnight on four specific days in 2026. The permitted dates are September 15, 18, 19, and 25, covering the period from 6 am to 12 midnight. This exception applies only to these four days, while other festival days remain subject to standard noise pollution rules. The permission is conditional on maintaining noise limits and adhering to Bombay High Court orders.

title: Uttarakhand Congress files police complaints over purification ritual row
summary: The Uttarakhand Pradesh Congress Committee will lodge FIRs across all districts on Monday regarding a purification ritual at Haldwani's Ramlila Ground. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge alleged the act violated the SC/ST Act after his August 8 rally. Rahul Gandhi demanded immediate legal action, while BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi denied any caste angle. Senior leaders, including Kumari Selja, are expected to participate in a major protest in Dehradun on September 7.

title: Mumbai police arrest woman who killed boy while driving distracted
summary: Police in Mumbai arrested a 45-year-old woman after she allegedly ran over an eight-year-old boy while talking on her phone. The victim died at Holy Family Hospital following severe injuries from the collision. Authorities registered a case against the driver, identified as Megha Rawal, under multiple sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Motor Vehicles Act. Further investigation is currently underway.

title: Retired Bengal couple recounts narrow escape from Nepal flood
summary: Retired schoolteachers Anukul Poddar and Reba Roy Poddar returned from Nepal on Sunday after narrowly avoiding a flash flood. Their tour manager received disaster news and reversed the vehicle just before reaching the affected area. The couple chose to return by train rather than fly due to fear of traveling through the disaster zone. Another retired couple from the same district remains untraced.

title: Bengaluru commercial projects face approval delays squeezing new supply
summary: Bengaluru's commercial real estate market is experiencing significant delays between securing statutory clearances and starting construction. Developers attribute these bottlenecks to the administrative transition from BBMP to the Greater Bengaluru Authority, which has slowed approval processes. Mid-stream rule changes and idle contractors have increased costs and uncertainty for projects. While office demand remains strong with vacancy rates declining, the approval stage continues to lock up capital before construction begins. Experts suggest that better coordination between authorities and digital scrutiny could improve predictability and execution timelines.

title: Microfinance loans often increase debt rather than creating economic freedom for the poor
summary: The article argues that microfinance has failed to deliver promised economic independence for many low-income households in Asia. Experts state that flawed assumptions about capital access and entrepreneurial potential often lead to ineffective policy interventions. Evidence from India suggests loans frequently boost existing businesses instead of creating new ones, while high interest rates in places like Bangladesh strain borrowers. Research indicates that multiple loans often result in debt juggling rather than productive investment, leaving families financially vulnerable. Additionally, the sector's shift toward using land as collateral risks putting farmers' primary assets at risk. The authors conclude that broader support for skills and infrastructure is essential, noting that debt is inappropriate for households lacking sustainable returns.

title: NSE cash volumes hit five-month low as CAS swings unsettle investors
summary: NSE cash market volumes fell to a five-month low in August amid uncertainty over the new Closing Auction Session mechanism. Average daily turnover dropped 3 per cent to ₹1,16,579 crore as sharp index swings and profit-booking dampened investor appetite. SEBI introduced the CAS framework on August 3 to determine official closing prices for 208 stocks. Former SEBI Chairman UK Sinha suggested better preparation was needed but expects the system to stabilize. Analysts noted that while the BSE saw a recovery, the NSE remains more affected by the disruption.

title: PM Modi leaves Uzbekistan for SCO Summit after bilateral talks
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi departed Tashkent for Bishkek to attend the 26th SCO Summit following a two-day state visit to Uzbekistan. He thanked President Mirziyoyev for strengthening India-Uzbekistan ties and elevated the relationship to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. The leaders agreed to increase bilateral trade to USD 5 billion by 2030 and cooperate on critical minerals and digital infrastructure. Modi also paid tribute to former PM Lal Bahadur Shastri and received Uzbekistan's highest honour, the Oliy Darajali Do'stlik Order.

title: Subhash Chandra clarifies personal guarantee repayments in NCLT insolvency case
summary: Essel Group Chairman Subhash Chandra addressed social media concerns regarding his personal insolvency by detailing repayment figures and guarantee amounts. He stated that borrowers repaid ₹3,803 crore of the ₹4,808 crore they received, leaving a balance of ₹998 crore. Chandra explained that while total personal guarantees signed amounted to ₹22,000 crore, the current claims filed by lenders stood at ₹5,311 crore. He noted that some lenders had already received full repayment but still submitted claims to the National Company Law Tribunal. The chairman clarified that the repayment plan was prepared by a court-appointed Resolution Professional and highlighted that his family sold assets to assist with repayments. Chandra expressed hope that lenders would reconcile outstanding accounts with borrowers to recover the remaining dues.

title: Govt meets industry on India-US trade ahead of minister visit
summary: The government will meet industry and exporters to discuss India-US trade trends. Additional Secretary Darpan Jain will chair the session. Minister Piyush Goyal will visit the US in late September for G-20 talks. India's exports to the US grew marginally to USD 87.31 billion in 2025-26. The US imposed a 10 per cent tariff on India from July 24.

title: Review finds uneven quality in Pratyaksha's short story collection
summary: A review of Pratyaksha's new collection, The Mistress of Phoolpur, notes that while some stories offer interesting ideas, the overall execution falls short. The author reports that two stories, 'The Hunt' and 'Ma, Let's Fly', successfully explore themes of desire and family dynamics. However, the reviewer argues that other tales rely on clichés or fail to deliver dramatic impact. The book maps fault lines between restraint and transgression but remains highly uneven. Ultimately, the collection provides a few sparks of inspiration alongside several forgettable tales.

title: Northern Railway rescues over 400 passengers after hill slip halts Kalka-Shimla train
summary: Northern Railway rescued more than 400 passengers and crew after incessant rain caused a hill slip between Koti and Ghumman stations. The incident exposed part of a bridge and short-terminated four incoming trains. Officials evacuated travelers using buses and a specially rescheduled train. The railway stated the operation was seamless with no complaints or refund requests.

title: Six-year-old Bihar boy stages dharna over 'police excesses' against parents
summary: A six-year-old boy in Patna, Bihar, initiated a sit-in protest alleging police beat his parents during custody. The child, who previously joined student demonstrations, demands a meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi to address his grievances. Police officials stated the boy was handed to his mother for safety and advised the family to be more careful. The boy vowed to continue the protest until the Prime Minister meets him.

title: Sumeet Bagadia recommends three stocks under Rs 100 for Monday
summary: Indian equity markets closed cautiously on August 31, 2026, with the Nifty slipping 0.31% to 24,175.65 amid global concerns and volatility from the new Closing Auction Session. Sumeet Bagadia, Executive Director at Choice Broking, noted that the Nifty trades below key moving averages with a sideways bias, expecting a trading range of 24,000–24,300. He also observed that Bank Nifty remained range-bound between 57,000 and 58,000. Bagadia recommended three specific stocks for purchase on Monday: Jindal Worldwide, Manali Petrochemicals, and Andhra Sugars. He provided specific entry prices, target prices, and stop-loss levels for each pick. The article states these views are those of the analyst and not Mint, advising investors to consult certified experts before making decisions.

title: Five flexicap funds delivered up to 15% CAGR in three years
summary: IANS reports that five flexicap mutual funds delivered returns between 18.1% and 20.2% CAGR over the past three years. The list includes Bank of India, Motilal Oswal, Invesco India, ICICI Prudential, and ITI funds.

title: Chevron and other U.S. shale producers use soap cocktails to boost oil output
summary: Chevron and other U.S. shale producers are using advanced chemical surfactants to increase oil recovery from existing wells. Chevron has deployed these treatments in over 600 wells, starting with the Permian Basin. The company plans to license its technology to ZL Chemicals for broader market application. Ovintiv reports a 9% productivity improvement in treated wells, while Diamondback Energy tests the method on 60 wells. Industry executives describe these chemical mixtures as essential for unlocking remaining oil trapped in rock formations.

title: Lucid recalls 27,185 vehicles for LED fire risk fixed by July software update
summary: Lucid Motors issued a recall for 27,185 Air vehicles due to a potential fire risk involving exterior LED lighting. The issue stemmed from software that failed to properly limit current to the lights, which could cause overheating. Lucid notes that a July software update already addressed this problem by reducing amperage and preventing repeated re-energizing of faulty circuits. As of August 20, over 20,700 affected vehicles had received the update, while the remainder will receive notices in October. The company has identified three fire events and several smoke-related incidents linked to the front lighting system. While owners were advised to park outside pending repairs, the fix is simply an available software update rather than a physical part replacement. The article highlights that most vehicles were already updated before the recall was officially filed.

title: UBS strategist urges clients to position for a major commodity upcycle
summary: UBS strategist Sagar Khandelwal advised clients to position for a commodity upcycle driven by electrification, AI spending, and supply constraints. The firm believes hard assets offer structural returns and portfolio protection against inflation and energy disruptions. Khandelwal recommends maintaining diversified exposure across precious metals, energy, industrial metals, and agriculture. Recent data shows the Quantix Commodity Index Total Return surged over 22.5% since late June.

title: XPENG Unveils VLA 2.0 AI, Secures $900M Robot Funding, and Reports Q2 Growth
summary: XPENG has announced significant advancements in its physical AI technology alongside strong second-quarter financial results. The company reported revenue of $2.91 billion, an 8.0% year-over-year increase, while its gross margin reached 20.7%. Despite a net loss of $200 million driven by higher R&D spending, XPENG is positioning itself as a technology firm through partnerships with Volkswagen Group and a new robotics division. The automaker recently launched VLA 2.0 version 6.3.0, which features a 300% improvement in latency and 20x better safety performance. This update enables proactive reasoning up to 21 seconds into the future and allows for full voice control of vehicle functions. Additionally, XPENG's robotics unit, Dogotix, raised $900 million in funding to support the commercialization of its IRON humanoid robot. The company plans to deploy these robots in retail and service sectors starting in 2027. XPENG aims to create an AI flywheel where better cars generate more data, leading to improved software and further sales. By running advanced AI models locally on dedicated chips, the company seeks to overcome regulatory and privacy challenges while expanding its technology services revenue.

title: Bentley Unveils Its First In-House All-Electric Torcal SUV
summary: Bentley Motors announced the upcoming September 23 reveal of the Torcal, its first fully electric vehicle produced entirely in-house. The company clarified that previous plug-in hybrids and the Blower Jnr project do not count as this specific all-electric model. Built on a shared platform with Porsche and Audi, the Torcal is designed as a smaller, urban-focused SUV positioned below the Bentayga. Pricing is expected to start at $230,150, with deliveries to US buyers scheduled for 2028. The vehicle features unique materials like 100% Merino wool fabric and recycled walnut veneer, alongside a new Curation Engine for cabin atmosphere management.

title: Tesla faces cash flow risk from heavy spending on robotaxis and robots
summary: The article argues that Tesla's primary near-term risk involves heavy upfront spending on the Cybercab and Optimus projects. Analysts project the company will experience cash outflows between 2026 and 2028 as capital expenditures exceed operating cash flow. Management intends to use these investments to secure supply chains and support long-term growth. However, delays in generating revenue from robotaxis and robots could force the electric vehicle business to bear the financial burden alone.

title: Congressman Rulli Sold Alphabet Stock After Buying It, Possibly Losing Money
summary: Rep. Michael Rulli disclosed selling $50,000 to $100,000 worth of Alphabet stock on Aug. 24, potentially realizing a loss on shares bought in June. Benzinga Government Trades reported the transaction details alongside Rulli's prior purchases. Calculations suggest the trade resulted in a loss between $634.91 and a gain of $1,183.40 depending on exact prices. Rulli has made 33 trades totaling around $331,000 since 2024, with the majority occurring in 2026.

title: Nvidia earnings boost Wall Street while Fed Chair Kevin Warsh warns on inflation
summary: US stock indexes rose on Nvidia's strong earnings and positive AI outlook. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh expressed caution regarding inflation at the Jackson Hole symposium.

title: Syria and Libya agree to reopen embassy and restart diplomatic committee
summary: Syria and Libya agreed to reopen Syria's embassy in Tripoli after 14 years and reactivate a bilateral coordination committee. The deal follows talks between Libyan Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dbeibah and Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad Hassan al-Shaibani. Officials also planned to open a Syrian consulate in Benghazi and discussed security, economic, and consular issues. Libya's Government of National Unity issued a statement confirming the agreement.

title: Stonemasons remove thousands of coins from Giant's Causeway cracks
summary: Specialist stonemason Nathan Morrow removes coins embedded in the cracks of Northern Ireland's Giant's Causeway. Visitors have pushed pocket change into fissures between basalt columns for decades to wish for good fortune. The removal process is painstaking, taking from seconds to over 20 minutes per coin. This ritual has affected the UNESCO World Heritage Site's ancient volcanic pillars.

title: Radhika Gupta advises treating homes as emotional needs, not investments
summary: Adviser Radhika Gupta told attendees at the India Today Woman Summit 2026 that self-occupied homes should not be treated as investments. She warned that home loan EMIs must not strain daily finances. Gupta also urged comparing property returns against mutual funds and other liquid options before buying extra assets.

title: Trump says US will refill Strategic Petroleum Reserve using Venezuelan oil
summary: President Donald Trump announced that oil from a new deal with Venezuela will replenish the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, which currently holds about 290 million barrels. Venezuelan interim President Delcy Rodriguez stated the agreement targets 1.5 million barrels per day production and aims to generate roughly $209 billion in state revenue. Rodriguez emphasized that Venezuela retains sovereignty over its natural resources while leveraging foreign capital and technology. The deal requires significant investment and infrastructure work before production can rise substantially.

title: Russia imports stolen Canadian trucks via criminal networks
summary: The New York Times reports that Western export bans have not reduced demand for brand-name SUVs and trucks in Russia. A sophisticated criminal network steals vehicles, hides them in shipping containers, and ships them to Russia, often through the Middle East. Interpol received 4,798 reports of stolen Canadian vehicles found in Russia between February 2024 and July 2026. Pickup trucks like Dodge Rams and Ford F-150s are in particularly high demand. The Royal Canadian Mounted Police states Russia is the top international destination for these reported stolen cars. Interpol figures likely undercount the actual scale of the problem.

title: Columbia Climate School Dean proposes solar bonds to lower UK home financing costs
summary: Alexis Abramson argues that UK solar bonds could lower capital costs for rooftop solar installations. The proposal attaches loans to properties rather than individuals, ensuring stability if homeowners move. While the US has existing financing tools, Abramson notes they do not offer the same ownership benefits. He suggests a state-by-state approach in the US due to varying utility structures. The author warns that expiring tax credits increase the urgent need for such financing solutions.

title: Venezuela's Delcy Rodriguez defends controversial oil deal with Donald Trump
summary: Venezuela's interim president Delcy Rodriguez defended a controversial energy agreement with Donald Trump, asserting the nation retains full ownership of its oil reserves. Rodriguez stated the deal aims to generate over $209bn in revenue and transform Venezuela into an energy powerhouse. Trump announced the historic transaction, claiming it will fill the US Strategic National Reserves and double American oil holdings. The agreement reportedly involves Washington taking control of 65bn barrels from 17 strategic oilfields. The deal has sparked outrage among Venezuelan opposition figures and former officials who condemn it as a neocolonial land grab. Critics argue the pact undermines democratic prospects and compares the state oil company to a US subsidiary. Rodriguez countered accusations of surrendering resources, emphasizing the need for investment to convert underground wealth into national development.

title: ASX futures fall as Wall Street retreats on US inflation fears
summary: Wall Street closed lower after Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh suggested interest rates might rise due to inflation concerns. ASX 200 futures are pricing in a 0.4 per cent slide on opening. The Australian dollar remained flat at 71.58 US cents while Wall Street indices posted minor losses. Several Australian companies are scheduled to release financial results today.

title: US forces strike two Iranian launchers on Larak island
summary: A US official confirmed that American forces struck two Iranian launchers on Larak Island on Sunday. The official stated that Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces were preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian state media reported that the attack killed and wounded several soldiers and citizens. The strike marks the first known American attacks on Iran since late July.

title: Residents report illegal McDonald's construction at 4am in Brisbane
summary: Brisbane residents report being woken by construction noise at 4am at a West End McDonald's site. Brisbane City Council confirmed it has not authorized work at that time. Council documents show out-of-hours approval was granted only between 9pm and 2am. Store Tec declined to comment on the violation, stating it is a matter for McDonald's. A McDonald's spokesperson said investigations are ongoing. The restaurant is scheduled to open in late 2026.

title: Paris Brunner scores twice as Monaco top Ligue 1 after beating Marseille
summary: Paris Brunner scored both goals as AS Monaco defeated Olympique de Marseille 2-0 to lead the Ligue 1 table. Monaco remains the only team with two wins after their opening matches. Meanwhile, Stade Rennais beat Le Mans 3-2, and Paris FC defeated Nice 3-0. Reigning champions PSG sit in 11th place after drawing their first two games.

title: Australia sends $3m aid as missing Australians in Nepal floods rise to 43
summary: Foreign Affairs Minister Penny Wong announced an additional $3 million in aid for Nepal's flood disaster. The total Australian assistance package now reaches $8 million, including hygiene kits and solar lighting coordinated by the defence force. Meanwhile, the number of missing Australians has risen to 43, with 650 calls received by the department of foreign affairs. Australian personnel remain unable to access the flood zone due to cut-off roads and damaged infrastructure.

title: Noel Godin, the cream pie activist who targeted Bill Gates, dies at 80
summary: Noel Godin, a prankster who targeted powerful figures with cream pies for over 50 years, has died at age 80. His famous targets included politicians, philosophers, filmmakers, and Microsoft founder Bill Gates.

title: Aaron Donald ends retirement to return to Los Angeles Rams
summary: The Los Angeles Rams announced that Aaron Donald has ended his 2 1/2-year retirement to rejoin the team. ESPN reported he agreed to a one-year contract worth at least $20 million in incentives. Donald, a three-time Defensive Player of the Year, will play alongside Myles Garrett and other defensive additions. His return resets his eligibility clock for the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

title: Dozens evacuated from Grand Canyon after flash flood hits creek leading to Colorado River
summary: The National Park Service reported that a flash flood in Bright Angel Creek forced the evacuation of dozens of people and swept debris into the Colorado River. Officials are seeking information on more than 20 missing individuals while continuing evacuations with the Arizona Department of Public Safety. Popular tourist spots remained closed as park officials surveyed damage and halted rafting trips. Meteorologist Justin Johndrow noted that half an inch to one inch of rain fell within 30 minutes, causing rapid runoff.

title: US strikes Iranian rocket launchers in Strait of Hormuz
summary: US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers in the Strait of Hormuz, according to a US official. The IRGC confirmed the attacks hit Larak Island and warned of a retaliatory response. An unnamed US official stated that IRGC forces were preparing to launch rockets and sea mines. This marks the first US military action in the Strait in a month.

title: Aaron Donald returns to LA Rams for one-year deal
summary: Aaron Donald has rejoined the Los Angeles Rams after retiring in March 2024. ESPN reports he will earn $20 million, potentially rising to $30 million with bonuses. Rams head coach Sean McVay stated Donald was outstanding during his summer workout. The 35-year-old defensive tackle returns to a roster featuring Matthew Stafford and Myles Garrett. Donald aims to replicate his peak form with the stacked team.

title: Mass shooting at Chicago park kills one and injures 13
summary: A mass shooting at Washington Park in Chicago killed one person and injured at least 13 others. Police detained a suspect and recovered a weapon after the incident occurred around 11:37 p.m. Saturday. Authorities stated the victims ranged in age from 21 to 47, with one fatality and several hospitalized in serious or fair condition. The Cook County Crime Stoppers offered a reward for information leading to the arrest of the gunman.

title: US strikes Iranian launchers on Larak island in Strait of Hormuz
summary: US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak island in the Strait of Hormuz, a US official said Sunday. Iran's Revolutionary Guards reported the attack killed and wounded several fighters and civilians, vowing punishment. A tanker was struck by an unknown projectile nearby, though no casualties were reported. The conflict has entered a stalemate after six months of fighting.

title: Trump border czar Tom Homan defends deportations to Haiti despite safety warnings
summary: Border czar Tom Homan defended recent deportations to Haiti, stating he does not know the conditions there. The State Department warns Americans against traveling to Haiti due to severe violence and instability. Approximately 350,000 Haitians lost Temporary Protected Status after the Supreme Court allowed its termination. The Department of Homeland Security plans to increase deportation flights from once a month to once a week. A YouGov survey found 53 percent of Americans disapprove of the administration's immigration handling. Human rights groups urge a halt to deportations until safety guarantees exist.
