Public opinion supports the hard-line approach, with a survey showing three-in-four Canadians backing the move. New Canadian tariffs on US goods take effect on September 8. The Royal Bank of Canada warns a no-deal scenario could impact 0.4% of GDP. Canada is also reviewing a planned purchase of 88 Lockheed Martin F-35 fighter jets.

title: Polish prosecutors launch terrorism probe after drone factory fire
summary: Polish prosecutors have opened a terrorism investigation into a deliberate fire at WB Electronics factory in Skarżysko-Kamienna. Authorities state the blaze, which destroyed warehouse facilities valued at least 15 million PLN, resulted from an explosive device. CCTV footage reportedly shows an individual in a balaclava entering the site. WB Group claims production will resume without delaying deliveries to the Polish armed forces. This incident follows a similar fire at an aircraft parts warehouse in Lublin within 24 hours.

title: Nepal rescuers blast hillside to find trapped hydropower workers
summary: Rescuers in Nepal are using explosives to blast into a hillside near the Trishuli River, searching for over 600 workers trapped in mud-filled tunnels. The country's disaster management authority reports 939 deaths and 3,925 missing people, with roughly one in seven believed to be hydropower employees. An international team including Chinese and Nepalese military personnel is leading the operation, which experts describe as extraordinary due to massive boulders blocking access. Families express anxiety as the search continues, while authorities in Chitwan conduct temporary burials for unidentified bodies. Meanwhile, Chinese officials report 16 deaths and 546 missing in Tibet, imposing penalties on those speculating about higher casualty figures.

title: Deadly flash floods in Grand Canyon kill two, leave 15 missing
summary: Flash floods killed at least two people and left 15 missing in Arizona's Grand Canyon National Park after torrential rains saturated the ground. The National Park Service reported that debris flows overwhelmed hikers and damaged the canyon's only water pipeline. Meteorologist Ben Knoll stated that a super El Niño pattern and human-caused climate change increased atmospheric moisture levels by 5 to 15 percent. The National Weather Service maintains a flood watch for northern and central Arizona through Monday evening.

title: Trump warns voters against halting US data centre development
summary: Donald Trump told American voters they would be to blame if they stop data centre development. He stated that China could not be happier about increased opposition to these projects. The issue is gaining traction ahead of the US midterms as energy bills rise and communities are disturbed. Trump emphasized the US is locked in an AI race with China.

title: US military has no plans to send troops to the polls in November, top general says
summary: Gen. Dan Caine, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, wrote Sen. Elissa Slotkin to confirm the military has no plans to send troops to polling places during the 2026 midterm elections. The general stated the Joint Force will not use personnel to seize ballots or voting machines. Caine noted he has not received nor anticipates receiving any unlawful orders regarding the military's role in the upcoming November 2026 elections. While anxiety about potential interference remains, federal law prohibits armed federal force deployment at election locations unless necessary to repel armed enemies.

title: Novak Djokovic exits US Open early amid physical struggles and three-year title drought
summary: Novak Djokovic lost his first-round match at the US Open to Mariano Navone, marking his earliest Grand Slam exit in two decades. The 39-year-old Serbian player has now gone three consecutive years without winning a major title. Djokovic attributed his painful performance to consistent physical issues, including vomiting, cramping, and back pain exacerbated by heat and humidity. He admitted to swallowing pills and receiving medical treatment during the match before collapsing. While he has not announced retirement, his recent form raises questions about his future on the court. Fellow former top players Roger Federer and Rafael Nadal also retired after battling similar physical ailments. Djokovic remains the record holder with 24 Grand Slam singles titles.

title: Ethiopia delegates endorse executive presidency plan amid power grab fears
summary: Ethiopia's national dialogue concluded with delegates overwhelmingly supporting constitutional changes to create a powerful executive presidency. Critics warn the move could allow Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed to consolidate control, drawing comparisons to Turkey's system. While supporters argue the role would unify the nation, opposition parties boycotted the process, and armed groups remain excluded. The recommendations may be presented to parliament in October, though unresolved conflicts and ethnic tensions persist.

title: Trump threatens further action after US and Iran exchange fire in Hormuz
summary: The US and Iran exchanged fire for the first time in a month, with missiles striking Iranian launchers on Larak Island and Iran retaliating against bases in Jordan and the UAE. US Central Command said it acted after detecting plans to deploy fresh mines in the Strait of Hormuz. In response, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed to have targeted US airbases in Jordan, causing heavy damage, while the UAE intercepted a drone. President Trump threatened further action, calling Iran a failed nation. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated that continuing the war is not in Iran's interest and remains ready to implement a mediated memorandum of understanding. Independent tracking agency Tanker Trackers reported Iranian crude exports have been at zero for some time. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent claimed Iran is lashing out kinetically because it is losing economically due to fresh sanctions.

title: Federal agents investigate Alexandra Lozano after 54,000 immigration cases remain unresolved
summary: Federal officials from the Fraud Detection and National Security Directorate are interviewing witnesses regarding Alexandra Lozano, who faces two class-action lawsuits over immigration fraud. Agents in Seattle aim to present a case to a grand jury for potential criminal charges, though Lozano has not yet been charged. The investigation follows allegations that Lozano misled clients, used false information in applications, and enriched herself through fees ranging from $10,000 to $25,000 per case. When she surrendered her law license in May, approximately 54,000 immigration cases were left in limbo. One lawsuit details how a client named Severo López Contreras was detained by ICE after Lozano failed to file his T visa application despite collecting $17,500. Attorneys representing 34 plaintiffs state that Lozano remains silent while her clients face deportation risks.

title: Frank Furedi resigns as head of Viktor Orbán's MCC Brussels over unpaid wages
summary: Frank Furedi resigned as executive director of MCC Brussels on Monday due to persistent failures to pay contractually agreed funds. A spokesperson confirmed no staff in the EU capital received wages in July or August. The thinktank, an offshoot of the Mathias Corvinus Collegium Foundation, launched in late 2022 to influence political debate. Furedi stated the organization effectively ceased operations and could not pay suppliers or meet Belgian insolvency law conditions. He plans to ensure the institution's intellectual legacy continues in another form with like-minded individuals.

title: Netanyahu uses Altalena wreck discovery to target left before elections
summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and right-wing ministers celebrated the discovery of the Altalena shipwreck, a 1948 vessel sunk during a confrontation between the Israeli army and the Irgun militia. The event has become a focal point for political debate ahead of legislative elections in October. While Netanyahu described the find as an emotional moment, critics argue the timing serves to incite against his political opponents. Historians note the incident nearly sparked a civil war, with Menachem Begin preventing further violence. Experts question the feasibility of raising the 18,000-ton ship, calling the recovery promise a publicity stunt. The discovery has reignited historical tensions between Israel's left and right factions.

title: Hungarian PM Magyar urges EU to choose survival or victory amid leadership crisis
summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar told the Bled Strategic Forum that the European Union faces a leadership crisis and must decide whether to survive or win. He criticized Brussels' bureaucracy for stifling initiatives and highlighted unfair daily migration fines against Hungary. Magyar noted that while the EU focuses on internal questions, China is investing in European infrastructure. He also mentioned his government's recent agreement to release frozen funds after meeting Recovery Fund milestones.

title: Grand Canyon braces for more storms after deadly flash flood
summary: The Grand Canyon faces renewed storm threats after a flash flood killed one person and left 15 missing. The National Weather Service warns dangerous conditions persist through Monday due to saturated soils. Authorities suspended overnight stays and tightened water conservation measures after the Transcanyon Waterline was destroyed. More than 60 people were evacuated by helicopter while crews assess damage to trails and infrastructure.

title: India rejects Permanent Court of Arbitration ruling on Indus Waters Treaty
summary: India's Ministry of External Affairs rejected a Permanent Court of Arbitration ruling regarding the Indus Waters Treaty, citing a lack of jurisdiction. The MEA stated the court was illegally constituted and its award has no effect on India's sovereign decisions. India maintains its decision to hold the treaty in abeyance remains in force. The court ordered India to observe treaty obligations and imposed measures on the Ratle Hydro-Electric Plant until July 2027.

title: Singapore clears forests for housing despite climate adaptation spending
summary: Singapore is advancing a national climate adaptation plan while simultaneously approving the clearing of secondary forests for housing. Residents and scientists argue that environmental impact assessments fail to account for the climate and health benefits of these forests. The government plans to proceed with development at Maju Forest and Gillman Barracks, though it will retain more greenery than originally proposed. Experts warn that forest loss could increase urban heat and flood risks, contradicting the city's "city in nature" vision. While Singapore has committed billions to engineered defenses like seawalls, conservationists contend that planting saplings cannot replace the ecosystem services of mature forests.
