Restrictions will apply between 10 am and 3 pm across more than 35 roads and 22 diversion points. Emergency vehicles will receive priority passage while the public is urged to use public transport. Metro services will remain operational, though road-based feeder buses may face delays.

title: Bill Cohan's new book challenges New York Times reporting on Leon Black
summary: Bill Cohan's new biography presents a different narrative about Apollo founder Leon Black than The New York Times. Cohan describes his work as a rebuttal to what he calls a 'Leon jihad' by journalists. Times reporters David Enrich and Matt Goldstein have criticized the book for their portrayal. The dispute centers on how to view Black's relationship with Jeffrey Epstein. Cohan argues Black was a victim of lust and naivety rather than complicity.

title: Buttermilk Eatery owner files Chapter 11 bankruptcy amid lawsuits
summary: Asani Restaurant Group LLC filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in Florida on Aug. 31, listing over $75,000 in assets and over $407,000 in debts. The debtor did not give a specific reason for filing, and a spokesperson was not immediately available for comment. MGM Investment Properties Inc. filed a lawsuit against the owner on Jan. 8, 2026, seeking payment for kitchen equipment. The chain's largest unsecured creditors include Spartan Capital, owed over $178,000, and Toast Capital LLC, owed over $145,000, according to the petition.

title: Bitcoin and Ethereum prices fall as inflation fears persist
summary: Bitcoin and Ethereum prices declined Tuesday despite higher openings, as inflation concerns weigh on the market. Mounting expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates later this month are limiting crypto growth. The CME Group's FedWatch tool shows a 66.4% chance of a rate hike. Ongoing conflict in Iran has further complicated the Fed's efforts to control price growth.

title: Analysis questions if U.S. submarines can defeat China in war
summary: A new analysis argues that the United States may overestimate its submarine combat power in a conflict with China. The authors report that nominal inventory numbers do not reflect deployable strength or sustainable combat power. The text states that maintenance currently removes roughly one-third of the 48 nuclear-powered attack submarines from operational readiness. Deployment cycles further limit the number of boats available for a specific theater at any given time. Geographic distance and mission allocation requirements reduce the force that can be concentrated against a particular enemy. The authors note that weapon magazines are finite and require time-consuming replenishment far from the combat zone. Finally, the analysis highlights that lost submarines cannot be replaced on a wartime timescale, creating a structural vulnerability. The Congressional Budget Office reported that Virginia-class production averages only 1.1 submarines per year. The text concludes that while American submarines are capable, their strategic utility depends on complex logistical and operational constraints.

title: Google Maps renames Lake Ontario to Lake America for US users
summary: Google Maps now displays Lake Ontario as Lake America for users in the United States, aligning with the US government's Geographic Names Information System. Canadians and users elsewhere continue to see the original name or both. Apple Maps and MapQuest retain the name Lake Ontario, with MapQuest publicly rejecting the change and surging in US App Store downloads. The dispute occurs amid strained US-Canada relations as Donald Trump promotes the new name. Ontario Premier Doug Ford responded by displaying a sign reading 'Lake Ontario now and always.'

title: Coles and NSW Police convict man for Apple gift card tampering
summary: Coles and NSW Police successfully busted a man involved in an Apple gift card tampering scam. The supermarket's fraud team captured the suspect on CCTV while he returned tampered cards to supermarket racks. Police covertly tracked the 32-year-old man and searched his home, seizing 47 iTunes gift cards worth between $100 and $500. He was charged with dishonestly obtaining financial advantage and dealing with proceeds of crime. The man was convicted in July 2025 and received a 15-month suspended prison sentence. Coles stated that gift card fraud is an evolving challenge requiring cooperation across retailers and law enforcement. An ABC investigation linked the issue to a wider global scam involving money laundering. Private investigator Ken Gamble noted that joining the dots nationally remains difficult as agencies like the AFP and AUSTRAC stated it was not their primary domain.

title: Bessent urges G20 nations to use tariffs against cheap imports
summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told reporters that G20 countries should adopt tariffs to shield their industries from cheap imports. He warned that Chinese goods could flood markets without such measures. The Tax Foundation noted U.S. tariffs raised consumer prices by roughly 7% in 2025. Bessent also discussed de-risking trade with China while noting global debt reached $353 trillion.

title: Panama disease TR4 reaches 11th Queensland farm as breeders seek resistant Cavendish varieties
summary: Leon Collins, chair of the Australian Banana Growers' Council, confirmed that Panama disease tropical race 4 has now infected an 11th banana farm south of Cairns. The soil-borne fungus cannot be eradicated and poses a severe threat to Cavendish bananas, which account for over 97 per cent of Australian production. Researchers are developing resistant varieties using both genetic modification and traditional crossbreeding. In 2024, QUT received approval to commercialise the world's first GM banana, QCAV-4, though consumer acceptance remains uncertain. Other projects aim to release resistant lines by 2028, but current options often suffer yield penalties of 60 to 90 per cent. Strict biosecurity measures in the Tully region have so far contained the disease's spread.

title: US resumes strikes on Iran after IRGC attacks shipping and personnel
summary: US Central Command announced American forces resumed strikes against Iran on Tuesday, accusing the IRGC of recent attacks on shipping and service members. State media reported a strike near Sirik killed four people and wounded 50 at a wedding. The IRGC stated retaliatory missile and drone attacks on US bases have begun. President Trump warned Iran would face harder strikes if it retaliated further.

title: Andy Burnham addresses House of Commons on economy and regional power
summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham made his first appearance in the House of Commons on Tuesday. He outlined plans to restart the economy and redistribute power from London to regions. Wars in Europe and the Middle East currently weigh on his economic promises. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen spoke with Dr Martin Farr about the situation.

title: Federal judges install panic buttons and hire security amid rising threats
summary: Two new studies reveal that federal judges are installing panic buttons and hiring private security due to a surge in threats. Researchers from NYU, UC Berkeley, and the Brennan Center interviewed dozens of judges who reported feeling overwhelmed by harassment. One judge considered altering a ruling to protect their family from vitriol. Judge Esther Salas stated that recent attacks have made her more worried than after her son's death in 2020. The reports recommend increased funding for judicial security and more prosecutions of those making threats.

title: Police seek 14-year-old girl and father after newborn found dead
summary: Monterey County police are searching for a 14-year-old girl and her father after a newborn was found dead on a roadside. The sheriff's office stated the infant had signs of traumatic injury and the girl is charged with murder. Authorities believe the father is hiding the teen. Sheriff Tina Nieto called for the father to turn himself in, noting he faces multiple sex crime charges. The investigation utilized automated license plate readers to identify suspects within 53 hours.

title: Scott Bessent promotes financial literacy contest and Trump-era investment plan at G20
summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced US support for the Financial Literacy Solutions Sprint at a G20 ministers meeting. The contest will select winners from innovative technology solutions developed within G20 member states to improve financial understanding. Bessent also highlighted the Trump Accounts initiative, which deposits $1,000 into investment accounts for infants born during Trump's second term. Critics argue that financial struggles stem from a lack of disposable income rather than ignorance, citing recent survey data showing widespread dissatisfaction with economic conditions.

title: Deported Milo Yiannopoulos expresses shame over past support for Trump
summary: Milo Yiannopoulos appeared on Piers Morgan Uncensored to discuss his recent deportation by ICE. He described the experience as terrifying and expressed shame regarding his previous support for Donald Trump. The Department of Homeland Security stated Yiannopoulos overstayed his visa, though he disputed this claim during the interview. Yiannopoulos also criticized the brutality of US immigration enforcement.

title: Indigenous knowledge improves forest restoration seed production in Southeast Asia
summary: The authors of a new op-ed argue that integrating Indigenous and local community knowledge into seed propagation strengthens forest restoration outcomes. They state that these communities are indispensable partners due to their familiarity with local species and ecological rhythms. The commentary highlights that focusing on seed quality rather than planting numbers is essential for long-term resilience. Evidence from Indonesia shows local communities developed four propagation techniques to produce tens of thousands of seedlings. The authors suggest that engaging these groups fosters ownership and empowers communities. They recommend incorporating traditional ecological knowledge into technical designs and providing sustainable finance models. The text notes that current efforts remain fragmented in Southeast Asia despite global restoration initiatives.

title: Abdul El-Sayed accuses JD Vance of evil rhetoric and dog whistles
summary: Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed responded to Vice President JD Vance's attacks by defining evil as policies that harm working people. Vance described El-Sayed as representative of terrible evil during a speech in Michigan. El-Sayed accused the vice president of using dog whistles regarding Islamophobia and ethnic division. The exchange also involved comments about Vance's family and El-Sayed's previous remarks on a synagogue attack. Vance urged voters to reject El-Sayed, while El-Sayed called his opponents sock puppets. Both candidates are campaigning for the November election in Michigan.

title: Christiana Figueres receives inaugural Jane Goodall Earth Medal at Starmus Festival
summary: The Starmus Festival board created the Jane Goodall Earth Medal to honor the late conservationist, with former UN climate chief Christiana Figueres selected as the inaugural recipient. Festival co-founder Garik Israelian explained that advisory members Brian May and Peter Gabriel inspired the award, which aims to celebrate Goodall's legacy of uncompromising advocacy. Figueres expressed deep gratitude, describing Goodall as an absolute giant whose leadership continued until her final day. The festival's eighth edition, titled 'The Search for Truth,' features discussions on combating disinformation in the age of social media. Both guests argue that algorithms prioritizing engagement over facts create a post-truth environment where negative emotions dominate public discourse. They suggest that regulating tech companies and improving education are necessary steps to counteract the spread of misinformation. Figueres noted that humans are evolutionarily drawn to bad news, but society must consciously choose to surround itself with accurate information rather than fear-based content.

title: Zelenskyy warns Russian airspace will effectively close due to drone operations
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned airlines and insurers that Russian airspace is becoming unsafe due to escalating drone operations. He stated that the war started by Russia is effectively closing its own skies. Zelenskyy emphasized that Ukraine does not threaten civilian aircraft but noted the sheer scale of drones in Russian airspace. This warning follows a week of sustained Russian attacks on Kyiv using jet-powered drones and missiles.

title: Jurors deadlocked in Lindsay Clancy murder trial but judge urges continued deliberation
summary: Jurors in the Lindsay Clancy trial reached a deadlock after four days of deliberations, prompting Judge William Sullivan to ask them to keep trying. Clancy faces three counts of first-degree murder for killing her three children in Massachusetts in 2023. Her lawyer argues she suffered from postpartum psychosis and could not distinguish right from wrong. The jury, consisting of nine women and three men, has heard weeks of testimony. If found guilty, Clancy could face a mandatory life sentence without parole. Alternatively, she could be found not guilty by reason of insanity and sent to a psychiatric hospital.

title: Netanyahu says Israel captured Hamas security chief in Gaza
summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that forces captured Hamas internal security chief Muein al-Arabid during a Tuesday operation. Hamas officials claimed the officer was wounded and his wife killed during the raid. The operation involved an Israeli-allied militia and resulted in multiple civilian deaths. Palestinian health officials reported four people killed in the initial assault, while separate strikes later killed at least six more individuals. Israeli forces transferred the captured target to Israel for questioning.

title: Spain approves 309 million euro aid package for Ceuta amid migrant crisis
summary: Spain's Council of Ministers approved a 309 million euro extraordinary funding package for Ceuta to address the ongoing migrant crisis. Economy Minister Carlos Cuerpo described the measures as a shock response intended to safeguard jobs and support businesses. The funds are divided into healthcare, security, humanitarian care for minors, and direct business support. President Juan Jesús Vivas called for national unity, stating the city would never be abandoned despite the challenges. The announcement coincided with political demonstrations in the city highlighting internal divisions.

title: Bank of America VP killed in Times Square stabbing by woman with knives
summary: Bank of America confirmed that vice president Erin Piacenti was fatally stabbed in Times Square. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani stated a woman stabbed two people before police shot her. NYPD identified the attacker as Pamela Cisneros, noting she had a history of mental health problems. Piacenti died from abdominal wounds while the second victim remains in stable condition.

title: Senegal and IMF agree new $2.2 billion loan programme
summary: The International Monetary Fund and Senegal agreed to a new $2.2 billion loan programme. The 36-month arrangement supports reforms for 2026–2029 and requires corrective measures for past data misreporting. The deal needs executive board approval. Senegal's fiscal deficit narrowed to 6.4 percent of GDP in 2025. Political tensions remain between President Faye and Speaker Sonko regarding debt restructuring.

title: Bosnian associations urge UEFA to sanction FC Borac over war criminal glorification
summary: Several victims' associations filed a complaint with UEFA against FC Borac Banja Luka regarding the glorification of Ratko Mladic during matches. The groups stated supporters displayed symbols and banners honoring Mladic, a convicted war criminal sentenced to life imprisonment. They called for disciplinary measures if UEFA finds violations of its regulations. FENA news agency reported the complaint was filed Tuesday in Brussels.

title: Kremlin aide says Putin, Trump, Xi may meet at APEC
summary: A Kremlin aide reported that Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping discussed a potential trilateral meeting with US President Donald Trump. Yuri Ushakov stated the leaders spoke about this possibility during talks in Bishkek. The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is scheduled for November in Shenzhen. Ushakov also mentioned separate discussions regarding humanitarian issues in the Ukraine war.

title: Congo Ebola cases exceed 6,000 as violence hampers response
summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo government reports that confirmed Ebola infections have surpassed 6,000, with 2,911 deaths recorded so far. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres stated the epidemic is the fastest-growing on record and warned that international resources are lagging behind the reality on the ground. Health Minister Samuel Roger Kamba announced a vaccination campaign for over 50,000 front-line workers using doses originally developed for a different variant. Conflict and insecurity in eastern provinces continue to obstruct response teams, who reported attacks while handling Ebola-related deaths. Education Minister Raissa Malu proposed radio-based learning to maintain schooling, though teachers note a lack of necessary infrastructure. Despite these challenges, authorities highlight that more than 1,360 people have recovered from the virus.

title: Cuban theater group El Ciervo Encantado defies censorship by leaving state headquarters
summary: Cuban theater group El Ciervo Encantado announced it will no longer operate under state supervision after more than a decade of conflicts with the Ministry of Culture. The group stated on social media that it would cease using its Vedado headquarters while continuing to create art in alternative spaces. Founded by Nelda Castillo thirty years ago, the ensemble has long challenged institutional control over Cuban performance art. Their recent decision marks a significant political gesture against censorship and bureaucratic oversight in the country. The group plans to present works in private homes and other venues to maintain their critical voice. This move highlights ongoing tensions between independent artists and state regulators in Cuba's cultural sector.

title: Accelerated Arctic ice melting opens new commercial shipping route
summary: The article reports that accelerated melting of Arctic ice has opened a new commercial shipping route. It notes that this development is due to changing climate conditions in the region. The text mentions potential impacts on global trade and navigation.

title: Germany blames Russia for drone incident and imposes sanctions
summary: Germany blames Russia for a drone incident at an airport and has announced new sanctions against the country. The German government stated that the attack was a deliberate act by Russian forces. Officials said the measures target individuals and entities linked to the aggression.

title: Tunisia President Saied calls for balanced EU ties during German visit
summary: Tunisia's President Kais Saied hosted German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul in Tunis to discuss strengthening bilateral relations. Saied urged the European Union to update its partnership with Tunisia, describing it as needing to be more balanced and fair. Wadephul emphasized the importance of international cooperation during global crises while reaffirming Germany and the EU as reliable partners. The two nations signed financing agreements totaling nearly 100 million euros and pledged to expand cooperation in energy transition, water management, and digitalisation.

title: Bangladesh has not received an invitation to join the Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan defense pact
summary: Bangladesh has not received an invitation to join the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan. Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman stated the government views the pact positively but membership depends on the intentions of current members. Analysts note the agreement could complicate Bangladesh's relations with India, a key ally that has recently seen strained ties with Dhaka. Experts warn that joining might limit Bangladesh's geopolitical options and create diplomatic pressures if a conflict arises between India and Pakistan. While some see potential benefits in modernizing defense capabilities, others argue there is no direct geographical rationale for Bangladesh to participate in a Middle East-focused security arrangement.

title: Former prosecutor urges Osaka office reform after rape accusation
summary: An ex-prosecutor named Hikari stated that her former office requires reform because victims' allegations are not properly investigated. She publicly accused Osaka's then-top prosecutor of raping her six years earlier in 2024. The accused official, Kentaro Kitagawa, admitted the assault but later withdrew his statement, claiming the encounter was consensual. Few women in Japan speak out about sexual assault.

title: Japanese scientist captures young bear to study rising attacks
summary: In Nagano Prefecture, scientist Akiko Takii responded to a sensor alert by capturing a young Asiatic black bear. Researchers collected blood and fur samples from the 15-kilogram animal before releasing it. The capture occurred amid rising nationwide bear attacks that have led to thousands of culls. The bear was too small for a GPS tracker, so it was not tagged.

title: TCS hosts inter-school quiz contest InQuizitive 2026 in Chennai
summary: Tata Consultancy Services hosted the Chennai edition of its InQuizitive 2026 inter-school quiz programme. Harshith A. and Tarun KD from Manthan Vidyashram won the event, which saw 692 teams from 88 schools participate. DRDO and TCS officials attended the competition. Alex Duraisamy stated the contest aims to inspire students to pursue technology.

title: India joins SCO in condemning strikes on Iran and calling for diplomatic resolution
summary: The SCO reiterated its condemnation of military strikes on Iran, with India joining other member states in expressing concern over civilian casualties and economic damage. The bloc called for a political resolution to the conflict while condemning terrorism and opposing unilateral coercive measures. India also expressed condolences for the death of former Iranian supreme leader Ali Khamenei. Prime Minister Narendra Modi met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian to discuss expanding ties between the two nations.

title: IndiGo flight returns to Goa after engine failure
summary: An IndiGo flight carrying 229 passengers made an emergency landing in Goa after one engine failed shortly after takeoff. IndiGo reported that a technical issue was detected and pilots followed standard procedures to return safely. Air Traffic Control declared a full emergency before the aircraft landed at Manohar International Airport. The airline stated the plane is undergoing maintenance checks and passengers have been arranged for transport to their destination.

title: Armed Forces Tribunal changes gay ex-IAF officer dismissal to routine discharge
summary: The Armed Forces Tribunal principal bench converted the dismissal of a non-commissioned Indian Air Force officer into a routine discharge. The officer, who served 10.5 years, had confessed to being gay and disclosed his relationship with a foreigner during a compassionate discharge application. An inquiry found him guilty of breaching discipline and travelling abroad without permission. The bench ruled that changing the order prevents lasting career stigma while noting the effect of dismissal and discharge is identical in this context.

title: S&P Global considers multibillion-dollar spinout of Capital IQ Pro
summary: S&P Global is exploring a potential spinout of Capital IQ Pro, a business unit within its Market Intelligence division. People familiar with the matter told Bloomberg that discussions are preliminary and may not lead to a transaction. One option involves listing the business separately with a valuation in the high single-digit billions. Investors welcomed the possibility, causing S&P Global shares to rise as much as 6.3%. The move would allow CapIQ to compete directly with providers like FactSet Research Systems.

title: Tata Motors receives ECB approval for 40,000 crore Iveco takeover
summary: Tata Motors secured European Central Bank approval for its proposed acquisition of Iveco Group, valued at approximately 40,000 crore rupees. The company confirmed that all prior sector regulatory authorizations have been obtained, keeping the deal on schedule for an August completion. While British and Spanish regulators have already cleared the transaction, Italy's Consob remains the final regulatory hurdle before the offer document is published. Once approved, the deal will expand Tata's commercial vehicle footprint significantly across European and other developed markets.

title: SB Energy files for IPO after Nvidia backs OpenAI data centre project
summary: SB Energy has filed for an initial public offering with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, aiming to list on Nasdaq under ticker SBE. The company, backed by SoftBank, OpenAI, and Nvidia, plans to raise between $5 billion and $7 billion to fund its AI infrastructure expansion. Chief executive Rich Hossfeld stated that Nvidia's involvement helps unlock investment-grade financing for the project. SB Energy reported a net loss of approximately $3.2 billion in the first half of 2026, with no operational AI data centres yet. The filing highlights the company's substantial dependence on OpenAI as both a tenant and equity investor. Investors will monitor how public markets value the company as it navigates potential regulatory and community challenges associated with rapid data centre construction.

title: Six pilgrims killed after pick-up crashes into truck on Haryana expressway
summary: Police said six pilgrims died and 14 were injured after a pick-up crashed into a stationary truck on the Kundli-Manesar-Palwal Expressway in Haryana. The victims were returning from Rajasthan after visiting the Khatu Shyam Temple. Police suspect the driver fell asleep before the collision and have fled the scene. Deputy Commissioner Jayendra Singh Chhillar inspected a nearby liquor vend, found irregularities, and ordered it sealed. He stated that disregard for road safety rules would not be tolerated.

title: Four Centuries and Five-Wicket Hauls Mark Day One of Hyderabad Cricket League
summary: The Hyderabad Cricket Association reported a batting-dominated opening day for its Senior Men's Multi-Day Super League, featuring four centuries. Bhavesh Seth scored 167 not out, while Rahul Singh G, Aaron George Varghese, and Wafi Kachchhi also reached three figures. Under-19 matches saw Aditya Vardhan remain unbeaten on 202, with Shaik Rehaan Roshan adding 150. Bowling efforts included Mayur Shetty Kumar's 5/10 and four other five-wicket hauls. The 'C' Division league also produced Vaibhav Agarwal's unbeaten 126. Detailed scores for all Senior Men's, Under-19, and 'C' Division matches were released following the day's play.

title: Bombay HC Issues Notice To Padamsinh Patil And Others On Appeal Against Acquittal
summary: The Bombay High Court issued notices to former Maharashtra Home Minister Padamsinh Patil and eight others regarding an appeal against their acquittal in the 2006 murder of Pawanraje Nimbalkar. The victim's widow and son filed the petition challenging the sessions court's decision. A division bench directed the Maharashtra government and accused to file responses. The original acquittal cited evidentiary gaps and unreliable approver testimony.

title: Ganga erosion washes away century-old Chaiti Durga temple in Bhagalpur
summary: Severe erosion by the Ganga river has washed away the nearly century-old Chaiti Durga Temple in Raghopur, Bhagalpur. Deputy Chief Minister Vijay Kumar Choudhary stated the situation is serious due to unexpected changes in the river's flow. Authorities are conducting anti-erosion work while preparing relief camps and evacuation arrangements for affected residents. District administration officials urged people to remain alert and follow advisories as relief measures continue.

title: Bombay High Court Orders BMC to Audit Land for Sanitation Worker Housing
summary: The Bombay High Court directed the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation to audit its land holdings for free housing for sanitation workers. A bench expressed displeasure over an 18-year delay in implementing a 2008 policy granting ownership homes to staff. The court rejected a vague affidavit from the Municipal Commissioner and questioned the administration's neglect of essential workforce members. Officials must submit a fresh report by September 9, 2026, or face an independent committee inspection.

title: Whistleblower warns USPS Trump mail-ballot system risks 2026 election errors
summary: A whistleblower told Congress that a new USPS system enforcing President Trump's mail-voting restrictions could cause technical errors to reject legitimate ballots. Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal requested documents regarding the system, which aims for a zero percent failure rate. The system would check ballots against approved lists before delivery, potentially affecting entire batches due to single mismatches. While the administration claims the measures strengthen election security, critics argue they could disenfranchise voters ahead of the 2026 midterms.

title: Los Angeles reopens restored Vision Theatre after 15 years
summary: The Vision Theatre in South Los Angeles reopened in 2026 following a 15-year restoration project costing nearly $40 million. The City of Los Angeles initiated the effort in 2011 to preserve the historic landmark and revitalize the Leimert Park Cultural and Arts District. Work included structural repairs, system upgrades, and the restoration of original architectural features while ensuring modern accessibility. The 729-seat venue is now managed by the city's Cultural Affairs Department to host diverse performances and community events. Officials state the project signals a commitment to preserving cultural spaces in predominantly Black and Latino neighborhoods. The theatre aims to provide economic benefits to the village while remaining accessible to local residents through targeted programming.

title: Zelenskyy warns airlines Russian airspace is unsafe due to drones
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Russian airspace is now completely unsafe for civilian aviation due to a massive increase in Ukrainian drones. He stated that while Ukraine does not target civilian aircraft, the drone presence makes the skies dangerous for airlines and insurers. At least 12 people were killed in Kyiv during recent Russian strikes. Zelenskyy added that Ukraine might temporarily clear drones from specific areas to aid diplomatic negotiations.

title: Police Arrest Man in Kochi for Storing 21 Litres of Suspected IMFL
summary: Mattancherry police arrested a 36-year-old man on Tuesday after a raid revealed he stored 21 litres of suspected Indian Made Foreign Liquor. Libin Jose P.A. was found in possession of 42 bottles, each containing 500 ml of the alcohol. Authorities booked him under Section 55 of the Kerala Abkari Act for illegal storage and possession of liquor beyond permissible limits.

title: Coal India invests 50,000 crore in gasification and seeks lithium assets
summary: Coal India chairman B Sairam stated the company is investing nearly 50,000 crore in coal gasification projects while scouting overseas lithium assets. The firm aims to reach 9.5 gigawatts of renewable capacity by FY30. Its first commercial gasification project has entered the execution phase at Odisha. The company also incorporated CIL Global in Singapore to facilitate international acquisitions.

title: US Oil Prices Top $90 After Strikes Raise Strait of Hormuz Disruption Fears
summary: US oil prices surpassed $90 a barrel for the first time since late July following fresh American strikes on Iran. West Texas Intermediate rose as much as 5.1% after US Central Command reported projectiles hit two supertankers attempting to exit the Strait of Hormuz. Traders worry about prolonged disruptions to energy flows as Iran warns of severe punishment. Global bond yields climbed to near two-decade highs amid inflation concerns. Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. restored its Ruwais refinery to full capacity, boosting diesel and jet fuel exports.

title: Trump justifies US strikes on Iran and warns of a larger attack
summary: President Donald Trump stated that US strikes on Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz were justified. US Central Command confirmed forces began hitting Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targets on Tuesday. Iranian state media reported explosions at multiple locations, while Iran vowed retaliatory blows. The conflict has escalated tensions in a waterway through which roughly one-fifth of global oil supplies pass. Crude prices have surged more than 50% this year following the renewed clashes.

title: India's Q1 economic growth surprises economists with 7.8% expansion
summary: India's economy grew 7.8% in the April-June 2026 quarter, exceeding expectations of 6%-7%. Manufacturing expanded 9.2%, aided by GST cuts and RBI rate reductions. Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran warns Hormuz uncertainty may keep oil prices high. Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged citizens to buy local and avoid foreign travel. Rising inflation and a deficient monsoon threaten future rural demand.

title: Telangana HC Stays Stay Orders on Welfare Schemes and Issues Warrants
summary: A Telangana High Court division bench stayed interim orders halting the Kalyana Lakshmi and Shaadi Mubarak schemes, allowing financial assistance to continue. The bench noted the Comptroller and Auditor-General had not indicted the expenditure as lacking legislative sanction. In a separate matter, the court directed the health department to detail actions taken regarding the unregulated sale of abortion kits. Additionally, the court issued bailable warrants against two principal secretaries for failing to appear in a contempt case concerning delayed compensation payments. The court emphasized that government officers cannot authorize others to represent them in contempt proceedings.

title: SEC Plans to Expand Retail Access to Private Markets
summary: The US Securities and Exchange Commission submitted a proposal to the White House Office of Management and Budget to broaden retail investor access to private markets. SEC Chairman Paul Atkins stated that market exposure should not be reserved for wealthy insiders. The plan would amend existing acts to allow performance fees for a wider client base. Critics like Better Markets warn that private investments offer fewer disclosures than public ones. The commission will release the proposal for public comment after the White House review.

title: Blackstone sells entire EPL stake for 2032 crore to funds and insurers
summary: Blackstone exited EPL Ltd by selling its entire 26.38 percent stake for Rs 2,032 crore via an open market transaction on Tuesday. Domestic mutual funds, insurers, and foreign investors purchased the shares, with Quant Mutual Fund emerging as the largest buyer. The sale occurred ahead of a proposed merger between EPL and Indovida India Pvt Ltd. EPL shares fell 8.47 percent following the deal.

title: Ukraine conflict shows no end in sight as Russia advances and diplomacy stalls
summary: The article analyzes the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war, noting that peace remains distant due to divergent negotiating positions and mutual distrust. Russia controls roughly a fifth of Ukraine's territory and continues steady advances toward Donbas fortress cities while intensifying aerial attacks on critical infrastructure. Ukraine faces manpower shortages and relies heavily on Western support, having suffered a collapsed counter-offensive in 2023. Diplomatic efforts, including the Anchorage formula requiring Ukrainian recognition of Russian control over five regions, have failed to bridge the gap. Russia insists on addressing territorial and political questions before any ceasefire, whereas Ukraine seeks a ceasefire as a first step. The conflict has hardened into a test of endurance, with Russia sustaining operations through a wartime economy and high domestic support. External dimensions involve the EU expanding defense spending and China deepening trade with Russia in yuan and roubles. For India, the crisis impacts energy security and strategic autonomy, necessitating careful navigation between Moscow, Washington, and Brussels. The author concludes that a prolonged conflict punctuated by intermittent talks is the most likely trajectory, leaving Europe with higher defense spending and a militarized eastern frontier.

title: Nestle sells vitamins business to Yellow Wood for $1 billion
summary: Nestle agreed to sell its vitamins, minerals, and supplements business to Yellow Wood Partners for $1 billion. CEO Philipp Navratil stated the deal allows the company to focus on its strongest competitive advantages. The transaction includes seven brands and is expected to complete in the first half of 2027. Navratil also noted India is on track to become one of Nestle's top five markets by revenue.

title: Delhi HC rules women must resume same functional status after maternity leave
summary: The Delhi High Court ruled that statutory protection for women extends to their duties and career prospects after maternity leave. Justice Sachin Datta awarded over Rs 10 lakh to a chartered accountant who faced professional disadvantage upon returning. The court held that retaining salary while stripping responsibilities violates the Maternity Benefit Act and Article 14. It directed the Centre to frame rules ensuring effective implementation of maternity protections.

title: Four people killed in Guwahati landslides triggered by heavy rainfall
summary: Officials report four deaths in two separate landslides in Guwahati, Assam, on Tuesday. The Assam State Disaster Management Authority confirmed three family members died in Nizarapar while a 65-year-old woman died in Satgaon. Incessant rainfall caused the incidents, injuring five others across the state. Rescue teams recovered the bodies and continue relief operations in affected areas.

title: Starman Optical buys 90% of GoPro for $285 million to address debt and competition
summary: Starman Optical has agreed to acquire a 90% stake in GoPro for $285 million in cash to help the camera maker address financial challenges. The deal aims to alleviate GoPro's debt, rising memory chip costs, and competition from Chinese rivals like DJI and Insta360. Starman, a US optical parts manufacturer, plans to leverage GoPro's 2,500 patents to expand into commercial, defense, and AI data center markets. GoPro shares rose more than 50% after the announcement, trading at approximately $1.33, though the offer price of $1.14 per share remains below the current market value. The transaction is expected to close by the end of 2026, allowing GoPro to retain its consumer business while pursuing new technological opportunities.

title: Government reintroduces petrol export duty at 1.5 rupees per litre
summary: The government reintroduced an export duty of ₹1.5 per litre on petrol during its latest fortnightly review. Diesel export duties remain unchanged at ₹24 per litre, excluding the cess. Meanwhile, the export levy on aviation turbine fuel was reduced by 50 paise to ₹19 per litre. These measures aim to ensure domestic fuel availability following the West Asia conflict. Excise duties for domestic consumption remain unaffected.

title: Modi urges West Asia diplomacy and targets terror ecosystem at SCO summit
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the 26th SCO Summit in Bishkek, calling for dialogue to resolve the West Asia conflict rather than military action. He stated that terrorism remains a serious global challenge requiring a unified approach to dismantle financing and recruitment networks. While not naming specific countries, his remarks on using terrorism as a policy instrument appeared directed at Pakistan. The summit adopted the Bishkek Declaration, which condemned military strikes on Iran and emphasized resolving the Palestinian question through political means. Leaders also approved initiatives on drug control, biodiversity conservation, and artificial intelligence development for the coming decade.

title: Maharashtra CM Fadnavis visits Anna Hazare, who is stable after viral infection
summary: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis visited Anna Hazare at Bombay Hospital to wish him a speedy recovery. Dr Gautam Bhansali stated Hazare's condition is stable following a viral infection, dehydration, and renal failure. The activist underwent tests including a 2D echocardiogram, with results expected in three to four days. Fadnavis informed Hazare that the revised cost estimate for the Kukadi Irrigation Project was approved.

title: UN warns millions in Kolkata and Mumbai face immediate home loss from rising seas
summary: A United Nations report states that 14 million people in Kolkata and Mumbai face immediate risk of losing homes due to accelerating sea level rise. The UN Secretary-General's report highlights that rising seas are currently reshaping coastlines faster than at any point in recorded history. While high-income cities face financial exposure, low-lying deltas in South Asia are defined by human displacement. The report notes that between 2014 and 2023, global sea levels rose by 4.7 mm per year, with 2024 seeing a record rise of 5.9 mm. These changes threaten infrastructure, public health, and human rights, requiring urgent adaptation planning and finance.

title: Hyderabad SIR deletions equal 89% of 2023 Assembly election turnout
summary: A Kolkata-based research organisation found that 19.4 lakh voters were removed from Hyderabad's draft electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision. The Sabar Institute reported these deletions equaled 89% of votes polled in the 2023 Assembly elections. Muslims accounted for 40.7% of all deletions, though the report could not determine if they were removed at a higher rate due to missing data. The institute noted that in two constituencies, deleted electors exceeded votes cast. Concerns remain that the revision could eliminate genuine voters and shape electoral outcomes.

title: US stocks fall as oil prices and bond yields rise ahead of Fed meeting
summary: US stocks declined on Tuesday as investors worried about rising oil prices, higher bond yields, and potential Federal Reserve interest rate changes. The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 301 points, the S&P 500 fell 0.7%, and the Nasdaq Composite slid 1.1%, according to CNBC. Technology stocks led the losses, with Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices, and Micron Technology each dropping about 2%. The 10-year US Treasury yield climbed to 4.788%, its highest level since January 2025, while global yields also surged. Oil prices gained as tensions between the US and Iran increased, raising fears of supply disruptions. President Donald Trump warned of a strong response to recent attacks on US military bases. Goldman Sachs traders noted market nervousness, while Capital Markets analysts expect AI to remain a dominant market driver despite concerns about China's AI progress. Akamai Technologies received an analyst upgrade, and Hut 8 shares rose in premarket trading following reports of a new data center development.

title: Kerala CM Satheesan plans port city development and light metro for Kozhikode
summary: Kerala Chief Minister V D Satheesan announced plans to develop Kozhikode as a port city under the Mission Samudra project. He stated that a Light Metro would be implemented once studies are completed. The CM also mentioned potential projects including a cruise terminal, a new cultural park, and a Cyberpark.

title: Researcher explains how male actor Bal Gandharva defined Hindu wife roles
summary: Radhika Raghav reports that male Marathi theatre star Bal Gandharva defined the ideal Hindu wife for much of the 20th century. The author explains that Gandharva played 27 female roles rooted in Hindu mythology and the concept of stridharma. His performances made feminine objects desirable and respectable, leading women to replicate his fashion in sari shops. The researcher notes that Gandharva endorsed family products like Zenith Drakshasava, linking domestic duty to commercial goods. The article states that this archetype later appeared in post-independence advertisements and echoes in modern tradwife culture. Raghav concludes that domesticated femininity is deliberately constructed and marketed, often by men.

title: Chirag Paswan receives death threat via unsigned postal communication
summary: Union Minister Chirag Paswan received a death threat via an unsigned postal communication on Tuesday, his office said. The message warned he would be killed by hardcore terrorists and included two mobile numbers. Paswan's office wrote to the Union Home Secretary seeking an urgent investigation into the threat's origin and authenticity. Officials also requested a review and potential augmentation of the minister's existing Z-category security arrangements. Further details regarding the source of the threat are awaited.

title: NVIDIA and CrowdStrike Announce SafeMind Agentic Cybersecurity System
summary: NVIDIA and CrowdStrike announced SafeMind, a new agentic cybersecurity system designed to counter automated attacks. Jensen Huang and George Kurtz stated that defense must evolve as quickly as offense. The system combines CrowdStrike's threat data with NVIDIA Nemotron models in a continuous coevolution loop. CrowdStrike also unveiled Falcon IQ to automate security workflows using over 50 agents. The companies tested SafeMind in a high-fidelity simulation of NVIDIA's infrastructure. Huang noted that AI-enabled attacks rose 89% in the past year. Kurtz emphasized that defenders now possess asymmetric advantages through this collaboration.

title: ZS Associates builds secure Amazon SageMaker platform for regulated analytics
summary: ZS Associates reports that it built a security-hardened Amazon SageMaker environment to balance developer agility with strict governance in regulated industries. The platform now serves over 1,000 daily active users across more than 200 SageMaker domains. ZS implemented a multi-tenant architecture with isolated volumes and IAM roles to ensure strong isolation and granular cost tracking. The solution runs in internet-free mode by default, using Amazon VPC endpoints for controlled communication with required AWS services. ZS integrated JFrog Artifactory for package management to prevent unauthorized code entry. The firm states that monthly SageMaker spend exceeds $50,000, while Savings Plans save approximately $10,000 per month. Custom implementations include automated backups, secure package installation, and self-service tools to reduce manual compliance overhead. ZS continues exploring features like Model Registry and Pipelines to extend governance controls into production workloads.

title: Boomi Scribe automates documentation for enterprise workflows using AWS AI
summary: Boomi introduces Boomi Scribe, an AI-powered agent running on AWS that automates the creation and maintenance of technical documentation for complex enterprise integrations. The solution addresses the persistent technical debt caused by manual documentation efforts, which often lead to inconsistencies and compliance gaps. Boomi Scribe parses integration processes into Directed Acyclic Graphs and utilizes Amazon Bedrock and Claude models to generate accurate, user-friendly documentation automatically. The architecture leverages Amazon SageMaker for intent classification, Amazon S3 for storage, and AWS Lambda to orchestrate the pipeline across Boomi's 33,000 customers. By comparing version changes, the tool provides developers with concrete insights to improve planning and auditing. Boomi reports that the solution reduces time spent on documentation by up to 85 percent while ensuring accuracy across hundreds of daily processes.

title: Matt Clifford joins Anthropic as managing director for international affairs
summary: Matt Clifford, the architect of the UK government's AI strategy, has joined US startup Anthropic as managing director for international affairs. Clifford will lead engagement with governments outside the US while remaining chair of government-backed Aria. A not-for-profit campaign group raised concerns about the revolving door between government and industry. MP Chi Onwurah expressed some concern that Clifford is taking his knowledge to a global AI player so soon after leaving government. Anthropic stated it hires people with expertise who understand how government works.

title: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 generates animated pelican SVGs
summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1, which the company says sets a new standard for coding and long-running problem-solving tasks. The model achieved a 52.6% score on the Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 benchmark. A user tested the model's reasoning capabilities by generating SVGs of a pelican riding a bicycle at five different effort levels. Results showed that low and medium settings skipped reasoning entirely, while max effort produced a detailed image in 13 minutes and 54 seconds. The user then animated the max effort SVG for $1.37, noting minor wheel rotation artifacts in the video conversion. The article highlights how reasoning effort levels significantly impact output quality and cost.

title: OpenAI unveils Astra model designed to find and exploit computer security flaws
summary: OpenAI announced its upcoming Astra model, the first large language model to meet its critical cybersecurity threshold. The company stated the model can autonomously discover and exploit unknown security flaws in computer systems. OpenAI reported that Astra achieved a perfect score on ExploitBench and found two zero-day vulnerabilities during testing. To mitigate risks, the firm is implementing new safety techniques, including restricted access for high-risk accounts and additional monitoring. However, without third-party confirmation, it remains difficult to fully evaluate the model's safety measures before its public release.

title: Databricks releases Big Book of AgentOps to guide production AI agent deployment
summary: Databricks has released the Big Book of AgentOps, a new guide designed to help enterprise teams build and manage reliable AI agents in production. The authors report that this resource codifies essential practices including architecture patterns, evaluation loops, and governance strategies to prevent operational complexity from becoming a liability. The book outlines four specific deployment architectures and highlights common anti-patterns that often stall pilot projects. It also details a seven-phase roadmap for implementation, emphasizing the need for stakeholder alignment and continuous learning. Databricks notes that the guide draws on principles from The DevOps Handbook to address the unique challenges of non-deterministic agent systems. The publication aims to assist engineers, product owners, and security teams in transitioning promising AI pilots into dependable, scalable enterprise solutions.

title: Amazon Alexa launches new shopping alert feature called Update Me When
summary: Amazon announced the launch of a new Alexa for Shopping feature named Update Me When on Tuesday. The tool sends personalized notifications when new products or events relevant to a user occur. Amazon stated the feature helps anticipate purchases before shoppers ask. Other highlighted AI tools include price tracking and automated buying capabilities.

title: FDA builds secure AI foundation on Databricks for Government
summary:
The FDA described its modernization of a federal data platform using Databricks on AWS GovCloud during a Data + AI Summit session. The agency reported that this initiative created a secure, AI-ready foundation to address siloed data and operational overhead. Key points include:

*   The FDA migrated over 5,000 users and 8,000 jobs with zero downtime while refactoring thousands of pipelines.
*   The agency consolidated more than 40 data sources to improve collaboration and strengthen its security posture.
*   According to the FDA, query response times improved by more than 30% and compute costs fell by over 20%.
*   User adoption grew from roughly 500 in 2020 to more than 6,000, with expectations to exceed 10,000 by 2028.

The FDA emphasized that governance is the prerequisite for AI, integrating the platform with its enterprise AI tools to support responsible, human-in-the-loop innovation.

title: Researchers introduce BenchMIRT to audit LLM benchmarks at the prompt level
summary: Researchers introduce BenchMIRT, a new method for auditing large language model benchmarks by analyzing individual prompts. The authors report that BenchMIRT applies multidimensional Item Response Theory to separate underlying capabilities like safety and general reasoning. The team trained the tool on results from 100 LLMs across 16 benchmarks and more than 34,000 questions. Analysis revealed that some benchmarks, such as BBQ and WMDP, align more strongly with general reasoning than their intended safety goals. BenchMIRT can also identify the most informative questions, predicting model performance on unseen items 79% of the time. The authors note limitations, including the use of models released by March 2025 and potential risks if informative questions are removed from evaluations.

title: Walter Torous named executive director of MIT Center for Real Estate
summary: MIT School of Architecture and Planning Dean Hashim Sarkis announced that Walter Torous will serve as executive director of the MIT Center for Real Estate starting July 1, 2026. Justin Steil will act as faculty chair of the Academic Curriculum Council to guide the center's academic and strategic direction. Torous will oversee teaching, fundraising, and staff while continuing to direct the Master of Science in Real Estate Development Program. He plans to expand the curriculum across the Institute and engage over 1,200 alumni to train future leaders in technology and financial markets. Torous, an economist specializing in real estate finance, aims to integrate AI and machine learning into the program to address current market changes.

title: Ai2 introduces BenchMIRT to audit LLM benchmarks at the prompt level
summary: Ai2 researchers introduce BenchMIRT, a new method for auditing large language model benchmarks by analyzing individual prompts. The authors report that BenchMIRT applies multidimensional Item Response Theory to separate underlying capabilities like safety and general reasoning within single evaluations. Analysis of 100 models across 16 benchmarks revealed that some tests, such as BBQ and WMDP, align more strongly with reasoning than their intended safety goals. The tool also identifies the most informative questions, showing that keeping only 10% of items can preserve nearly the same model ranking as the full set. Ai2 states that BenchMIRT correctly predicted model performance on held-out questions 79% of the time, outperforming simpler approaches. The authors note limitations regarding models released after March 2025 and warn that question-level detail could allow unsafe models to pass trimmed evaluations.

title: Paint.NET author Rick Brewster credits Claude for rewriting Direct2D
summary: Paint.NET author Rick Brewster announced a new internal rewrite of Direct2D for WINE compatibility. The code, located in PaintDotNet.Windows.Direct2D1.Managed.dll, was generated by Claude without thorough review. Brewster noted the 180,000 lines of code were written in a "vibe coded" style. He admitted to babysitting the AI to fix resource management and architecture issues.

title: University of Sydney staff strike over AI protections and job security
summary: Approximately 2,000 University of Sydney staff walked off the job on Wednesday to protest artificial intelligence usage and job security concerns. The National Tertiary Education Union reported that zero percent of arts and social sciences faculty trust the university to act in their best interests. Union leaders stated management has repeatedly refused to enforce appropriate AI protections, while the university maintains industrial action is premature. The strike disrupted classes, with most moving online or being cancelled. Broader grievances include growing class sizes, reduced student satisfaction, and new restrictions on protest following the Gaza encampment. Despite police presence, picket lines maintained a jovial atmosphere as staff and students demonstrated solidarity.

title: Shopify COO Jess Hertz explains the company's AI strategy and infrastructure
summary: Shopify COO Jess Hertz discussed the company's growth strategy during an interview on Rapid Response. She noted that nearly 90% of quarterly revenue comes from merchants on the platform for over a year. Hertz described Sidekick as an AI-powered commerce agent helping merchants sell more. She also highlighted the Catalog product layer designed to make products discoverable by AI. The interview covered how these tools increase conversion rates compared to using scraped data.

title: Consumer group exposes fake 10 Downing Street listing on Booking.com
summary: Consumer group Which? created a fake listing for 10 Downing Street on Booking.com, which remained active for two months. The platform removed the bogus property only after Which? researchers successfully booked a stay and left a review. Booking.com stated its fraud controls were not triggered because the listing was not fully live. Which? criticized the site's AI systems as unfit for purpose and called for stricter enforcement under the Online Safety Act.

title: Pyka and rivals race to deploy self-flying planes for cargo and farming
summary: Pyka and other companies are racing to bring autonomous fixed-wing aircraft into commercial service, initially for crop spraying and cargo delivery. Pyka's electric planes, which can fly for about 35 minutes, are already operating in Brazil and recently received US authorization for limited agricultural use. While eVTOLs capture much attention, these self-flying planes aim to eventually carry passengers. Experts note that aircraft face stricter safety standards than cars, slowing deployment despite military interest helping propel the technology. Companies differ in their approaches, with some retrofitting existing planes while others build from scratch, and varying strategies regarding AI usage and air traffic control communication.

title: Bangladesh sets $0.086/kWh tariff for rooftop solar surplus power
summary: The government of Bangladesh announced a new incentive tariff of $0.086 per kilowatt-hour for surplus electricity from eligible rooftop solar systems. The Power Division stated the rate includes a 20% profit margin and an 11.25% premium over a benchmark generation cost of $0.065/kWh. Consumers installing systems by February 28, 2027, will receive payments for three years to help reach a 5 GW net-metering target. Mostafa Al Mahmud of the Bangladesh Sustainable and Renewable Energy Association welcomed the move as a commitment to renewable energy expansion.

title: Ørsted Completes Major Construction on 920 MW Taiwan Offshore Wind Project
summary: Ørsted announced the completion of major construction works for its 920 MW Greater Changhua offshore wind farms in Taiwan. The project is expected to enter full commercial operation in late Q3 2026. Ørsted Group President and CEO Rasmus Errboe stated the milestone supports the company's global construction programme. The facility will supply electricity to approximately two million households annually.

title: Ansaldo Energia gains hydrogen and HVO fuel certifications for turbines
summary: Ansaldo Energia received independent validations confirming its gas turbines can operate on low-carbon fuels. TÜV SÜD certified the GT36 for hydrogen readiness, while DNV validated the AE94.3A system running on hydrotreated vegetable oil. These milestones support the company's strategy to expand fuel flexibility across its portfolio. Federico Bonzani, chief technology officer at Ansaldo Energia, stated that fuel flexibility is a key strength enabling decarbonisation.

title: BERC Orders Bihar Discoms and ECR to Clarify Open Access Charges
summary: The Bihar Electricity Regulatory Commission directed South Bihar Power Distribution Company Ltd., North Bihar Power Distribution Company Ltd., and East Central Railway to submit written clarifications by September 9, 2026. The Commission addressed disputes regarding captive status certificates, applicable interest rates, and the Deviation Settlement Mechanism during proceedings in Case No. 02/2023. Parties must also provide disaggregated calculations of outstanding Cross-Subsidy Surcharge following Supreme Court guidelines. Senior officials are encouraged to hold discussions to seek an amicable settlement before the next hearing scheduled for September 16, 2026.

title: U.S. Energy Secretary Says Venezuela Oil Production Could Double
summary: U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright stated that Venezuela's crude oil production could more than double in coming years following new agreements with foreign energy companies. Wright noted that while investment will boost supply, refining capacity remains the primary constraint on gasoline and diesel prices. The U.S. government is negotiating a direct ownership stake in high-yield fields containing 90 billion barrels of reserves. This deal would grant the U.S. a 35% stake in North American Blue Energy Partners and rights to purchase 80% of its production. Analysts estimate revitalizing these fields requires approximately $180 billion in investment over the next decade.

title: KIER researchers achieve 26.7% efficiency for small perovskite-CIGS tandem solar cell
summary: Scientists at the Korea Institute of Energy Research (KIER) reported achieving a world-record 26.7% efficiency for a sub-1 cm² perovskite-CIGS tandem solar cell. The result was verified by Germany's Fraunhofer Institute and included in the US Department of Energy's efficiency chart. Researchers stated they developed new interface materials to minimize performance losses during cell integration. Lead researcher In-Young Jeong noted the achievement improves both efficiency and stability. The previous record for this size category was 26.3%, set by KIST in July 2025.

title: ARENA installs 100th community battery and funds three new Australian projects
summary: The Australian Renewable Energy Agency confirmed the installation of its 100th community battery system and announced AU$23.2 million in new funding for three projects. ARENA acting CEO Chris Faris stated the milestone reflects growing confidence in battery technology for the energy transition. The newly funded projects will deploy systems across regional South Australia, Sydney, and regional Queensland. Beyond ARENA initiatives, the Australian Energy Regulator confirmed 244 community battery systems are currently connected to distribution networks nationwide.

title: UN outlines narrow path to 1.5C warming after inevitable overshoot
summary: The UN sets out a narrow path back to 1.5C warming after an inevitable overshoot. The article states this trajectory follows recent climate analysis. No specific data or figures are provided in the source text.

title: UN Report Warns Climate Overshoot Imminent Without Immediate Action
summary: Scientists warn that fossil fuel emissions are pushing Earth toward a dangerous climate overshoot phase where temperatures exceed the 1.5-degree Celsius Paris Agreement threshold within years. The United Nations Environmental Programme report states immediate cuts and carbon removal are essential to restore a safe climate. Experts say current warming rates could reach 2.7 to 3 degrees Celsius by 2100 without drastic measures. United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres emphasized the need to limit how high and long temperatures rise above the threshold. Researchers noted that recent extreme heat events in Europe and North America demonstrate that climate impacts are happening now, not in the distant future. The report highlights a critical gap between current adaptation capacities and the severity of upcoming climate-driven disasters.

title: Oil Prices Rise After U.S. Strikes Iranian Tankers in Strait of Hormuz
summary: Oil prices climbed as the U.S. escalated tensions with Iran by striking tankers and other assets in the Strait of Hormuz. Axios reported the U.S. targeted two Iranian tankers under a new retaliation policy. The IRGC claimed attacks on U.S. facilities in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Jordan, though some claims remain unconfirmed. President Trump stated he does not care if Iran signs a deal. Meanwhile, U.S. oil inventories dropped by 2.6 million barrels, with additional draws from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve.

title: Windrose unveils iPad-sized 70 kW electric PTO for vehicle transport fleets
summary: Windrose has developed a compact 70 kW electric power take-off unit designed for vehicle transport fleets. CEO Wen Han stated the device is iPad-sized and integrates directly into the company's e-axle. The unit operates on an 800V high voltage platform to provide zero-emission power for specialized trailers. Industry consultant Ken North noted the technology could turn electric highway trucks into versatile application platforms.

title: California VPP bills await Newsom signature; Octopus invests in Uplight
summary: Two virtual power plant bills have passed California's legislature and are awaiting Governor Gavin Newsom's signature. The legislation aims to unlock value from customer-owned energy assets by enabling them to participate more fully in wholesale markets. Meanwhile, Octopus Energy US has completed its investment in behind-the-meter flexibility platform provider Uplight. The partnership will integrate Octopus products into Uplight's solution suite to support grid modernization. Industry advocates note that these measures address an energy affordability crisis while California continues to see rapid growth in solar and battery installations.

title: Federal Judge Invalidates New York Climate Superfund Law
summary: A federal judge ruled that New York's Climate Change Superfund Act conflicts with federal authority. The legislation would have required fossil fuel companies to pay $75 billion over 25 years for climate adaptation costs. Judge Brenda Sannes stated the law went beyond state limits because federal interest in the area is dominant. The decision follows a lawsuit filed by 22 Republican-led states and supported by the American Petroleum Institute. New York officials plan to review the ruling, while the Trump administration has also challenged similar state laws. Legal experts note the case could eventually reach the U.S. Supreme Court to determine if federal law precludes state climate claims.

title: NeoVolta secures 9 GWh of SK On cells for Georgia factory
summary: NeoVolta Power and SK On signed an agreement for 9 GWh of lithium iron phosphate cells to supply NeoVolta's Georgia facility from 2027 through 2031. NeoVolta CEO Ardes Johnson stated the deal supports the company's expansion into large-scale energy storage. The partnership includes a potential future framework for an additional 9 GWh contingent on future orders. NeoVolta aims to increase its annual production capacity to 8 GWh by 2028 using this supply.

title: NY court strikes down climate superfund law; Supreme Court to hear climate damages case
summary: A New York federal judge invalidated the state's Climate Change Superfund Act, ruling it violates the federal Clean Air Act. The decision blocks the law's attempt to extract $75 billion from fossil fuel companies for climate adaptation projects. Judge Brenda Sannes compared the law to a dismissed lawsuit against Chevron, finding it effectively regulates interstate emissions. Environmental groups and Attorney General Letitia James plan to appeal the ruling. Meanwhile, the Supreme Court will hear arguments on whether federal law prevents states from seeking climate damages relief. The Palisades nuclear plant in Michigan is loading fuel, potentially restarting before its 2027 target date. Holtec International plans to build small modular reactors at the site. In other energy news, lithium producers report record profits amid soaring demand. Odyssey Energy Solutions raised $74 million to finance distributed solar projects in emerging markets. California lawmakers passed a bill requiring utilities to offer incentives for home electrification instead of gas line replacements.

title: AI boom drives US battery storage growth despite near-term delays
summary: New research from the Solar Energy Industry Association and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence indicates that AI data centers are accelerating battery storage deployment across the United States. The report highlights that utility-scale projects and behind-the-meter installations are expanding rapidly, though near-term delays may reduce annual capacity additions. Analysts have revised long-term projections upward, anticipating significant growth by 2030 driven by regulatory changes and corporate agreements. Behind-the-meter storage is expected to become the dominant segment, with data centers accounting for a majority of installations. Residential market outlook remains mixed, facing tax credit expiration but potentially benefiting from new third-party ownership models and utility financing programs.

title: US grid battery installations hit record levels in second quarter
summary: The Solar Energy Industries Association and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence report that the US added a record 20.2 gigawatt-hours of grid battery capacity in the second quarter. Benchmark Minerals increased its cumulative installation forecast through 2030 by 11.5% due to this strong growth. While the Trump administration revoked wind and solar subsidies, it maintained tax incentives for batteries and provided $490 million in loans for a Puerto Rico project. The report notes that 74% of new storage occurred in states that voted for Trump, though these outcomes resulted from years of prior industry development.

title: Former minister Andrej Vizjak becomes CEO of Slovenia's GEN energija
summary: Slovenian state-owned energy company GEN energija appointed Andrej Vizjak as CEO following the return of Prime Minister Janez Janša to power. Vizjak, a former minister in Janša's cabinets, vowed to untangle complex cross-ownership loops between GEN energija and its subsidiary GEN-I. He also confirmed that projects for the Krško 2 nuclear power plant and Mokrice hydropower plant are continuing. Meanwhile, Jure Soklič was appointed as the new chief executive of GEN-I.

title: Satellite Images Reveal Hidden Rooftop Solar Growth Across African Commercial Sites
summary: CleanTechnica reports that Africa imported 18.2 GW of solar modules in 2025, yet official capacity additions only reached 4.5 GW. The authors note a significant gap between imported hardware and recorded installations. DataDesk and The Outlier analyzed satellite imagery of 209 shopping malls in South Africa, finding rooftop solar on 76% of them. This evidence suggests a rapid, customer-side solar boom driven by low module prices and unreliable grids. The article states that official statistics often miss behind-the-meter systems, while satellite data confirms physical installation on commercial properties. Experts warn that visible panels do not guarantee operational systems, but the convergence of import and aerial data indicates a hidden solar layer is already active.

title: Lawmakers and regulators propose turning data centers into integrated power hubs
summary: Legal and regulatory experts argue that hyperscale data centers should function as integrated energy projects rather than simple electricity loads. The authors report that current projections indicate data centers could consume 11.8% of U.S. electricity by 2030, necessitating new approval pathways. Proposed reforms require facilities to bring new generation capacity, pay for infrastructure costs, and provide grid support during emergencies. State actions in Texas and Wisconsin illustrate emerging models where large customers shoulder costs and adhere to strict tariff protections. The article recommends standardized contract suites that address interconnection risks, change-in-law clauses, and co-location obligations. Ultimately, the authors suggest America should contract for data centers as power infrastructure to resolve regulatory and construction risks before projects begin.

title: Jim Green explains how predictive digital twins improve condenser chemistry management
summary: Jim Green, principal consultant and founder of Industrial Water Advisory, argues that power plants must evolve condenser chemistry management from reactive monitoring to predictive modeling. He details a three-stage progression in industry practices, moving from legacy indices like LSI to tagged chemistry, and finally to advanced digital twins. Green emphasizes that traditional grab samples and single-salt indices often fail to predict deposition accurately because they do not account for complex ion interactions at the tube wall. He reports that modern digital twins couple first-principles chemistry models with thermal-hydraulic simulations to calculate saturation ratios specifically at the hottest tube surfaces. According to Green, this shift allows operators to treat water chemistry as an optimization variable rather than a fixed compliance cost. He states that accurate modeling can forecast fouling rates based on intended chemical programs, enabling better decisions regarding cleaning intervals and cycles of concentration. Green warns that while tracers confirm chemical presence, they do not guarantee performance, and teams must validate models against historical plant data before trusting their outputs. He concludes that treating condenser chemistry as a performance lever yields significant economic benefits in heat rate and megawatt output.

title: Plastic companies insert industry agendas into U.S. school curricula
summary: A new report from the nonprofit Plastic Pollution Coalition documents how the plastics industry inserts its agenda into classrooms across the U.S. through lesson plans, worksheets, and mobile programs. Industry interests offer these resources for free or cheap, highlighting plastic necessity while downplaying environmental and health downsides. Madison Dennis of the coalition stated that this information obfuscates the true impacts of plastic pollution. The report details case studies where trade groups promote recycling as a primary solution despite scientists warning it cannot keep up with production growth. Wendy Johnson of the National Center for Science Education noted these materials often trick students into thinking they are doing science while teaching ideological perspectives. The coalition calls for stricter school policies against industry-sponsored learning materials and better funding to prevent teachers from relying on such resources.

title: Iberdrola begins feeding electricity from new German offshore wind farm into grid
summary: Iberdrola has started connecting its new offshore wind farm in Germany to the national grid. The project marks a significant step in the company's renewable energy expansion within the region. Officials stated the facility will contribute to local power supply goals.

title: Trump administration forces seven coal plants to stay open despite retirements
summary: The Trump administration has used federal emergency powers to order seven fossil-fueled power plants to remain operational, claiming they are essential for grid reliability. These facilities, mostly coal-fired, were previously deemed unnecessary by state regulators and utilities. The Sierra Club reports the total cost of these stay-open orders is approximately $430 million as of August 6. More than 20 coal-burning units are expected to close before the end of the term, with several facing immediate retirement. Legal challenges from environmental groups and Democratic state attorneys general are underway against multiple orders. Plant owners face significant repair costs and customer bill increases, while some facilities remain broken or idle despite the mandates.

title: U.S. Adds Record 20.2 GWh of Energy Storage in Q2
summary: The U.S. installed a record 20.2 gigawatt-hours of new energy storage capacity in the second quarter, according to the Solar Energy Industries Association and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence. Total installations reached 30.8 GWh in the first half of 2026, nearly doubling utility-scale capacity since the start of the Trump administration. Demand for storage is outpacing expectations, prompting a forecast revision to 683 GWh by 2030. More than 74% of Q2 capacity was built in states won by President Trump in 2024, with Arizona leading at 6.2 GWh. Domestic manufacturing also hit record highs with new facilities in Ohio, Tennessee, and Texas.

title: Anthropic launches Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 with lower costs and fewer restrictions
summary: Anthropic released Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 on September 1, 2026. The company stated these models offer lower token costs and fewer safety interventions. Fable 5.1 is available via cloud platforms, while Mythos 5.1 is restricted to specific partners.

title: Apple appoints John Ternus as CEO while Tim Cook becomes executive chair
summary: Apple appointed John Ternus as CEO and named Tim Cook executive chair. Ternus thanked employees and praised Cook's leadership in his first message. He hinted at a major September 9 launch featuring new iPhones and Apple Watches.

title: Apple renames Lake Ontario to Lake America after Trump lobbying
summary: Apple updated its US maps app to label Lake Ontario as Lake America following direct requests from President Donald Trump. This move makes Apple the second major US tech firm to comply with the executive order, following Google's similar action. While the order cannot legally compel private companies, officials suggest the administration ensured compliance through federal leverage. The change occurs as US-Canada relations deteriorate amid recent trade tariffs.

title: Apple renames Lake Ontario to Lake America following Trump executive order
summary: Apple has renamed Lake Ontario to Lake America on its US Maps app after President Donald Trump issued an executive order. The change applies only to US users, while Canadian users will continue to see the original name. This move follows a trade dispute where Washington imposed tariffs on Canadian goods. Google made a similar switch for its US users, though not all map providers have adopted the new name.

title: Amazon Zoox and Alphabet Waymo expand robotaxi services to more US cities
summary: Amazon's Zoox and Alphabet's Waymo announced separate expansions of their driverless ride-hailing operations into new U.S. cities on Tuesday.
