They provide five specific guidelines for selecting draft length and mechanism across the Pareto frontier. First, increase draft length to push GEMMs into a compute-bound region without increasing KV cache pressure. Second, when attention dominates decode time, choose a draft length calculated as 128 divided by the number of query heads per KV head minus one. Third, prefer draft lengths where the product of query heads and draft length plus one is a multiple of 128 to avoid tile underutilization. Fourth, at very low latency, increase draft length only while the gain in acceptance length justifies the added draft cost. Finally, choose the draft mechanism by balancing acceptance length and draft overhead for the specific workload and hardware. The authors recommend using SPEED-Bench for acceptance measurements and NVIDIA TensorRT LLM for quantifying draft overhead.

title: China defied Western predictions to build an AI revolution
summary: Larry Elliott argues that Western predictions of China's economic collapse have been proven wrong as the nation advanced through three distinct industrial phases. Initially focused on low-cost manufacturing, China 2.0 captured high-end markets like solar panels and electric vehicles. Now, in China 3.0, the country competes with the US for AI dominance, with startup Moonshot suspending subscriptions due to overwhelming demand for its Kimi K3 model. Edoardo Campanella of UniCredit notes Beijing's strategy aims to stay on the technological frontier and set global standards. This development threatens Wall Street valuations if Chinese models undercut US tech investments. Elliott contrasts China's deliberate industrial policy with Britain's approach since the late 1970s, suggesting the latter neglected manufacturing opportunities.

title: Wayve and Uber launch London's first self-driving taxis with safety drivers
summary: Wayve and Uber have launched London's first self-driving taxis for hire, available through the Uber app with a licensed human driver present. Currently, only 15 autonomous Ford Mustangs are licensed, contrasting with over 100,000 private hire vehicles in the capital. Regulatory approval for fully driverless operations remains unlikely this year, requiring a separate government process. Wayve CEO Alex Kendall stated the technology is still maturing but declined to provide a timeline for fully autonomous services. The service uses an AI learning model rather than mapping, and vehicles will be hailed via the app with robotic driver introductions. While fully driverless services operate in the US and China, Uber aims to coexist human drivers and autonomous vehicles in London. Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander called it a major milestone for British innovation, while union leaders warned of potential social disruption.

title: Meta Ends AI Token Incentives While Employees Test New Agentic Tool Hatch
summary: Meta is formally ending an internal incentive program that previously tied employee performance evaluations to AI tool usage. Three employees told WIRED that performance reviews will no longer depend on how much workers use AI tools. The company replaced strict criteria like 'AI Native' designations with looser wording that focuses on impact rather than specific methods. Meta spokesperson Tracy Clayton stated the updates emphasize contributions rather than adoption metrics. Despite ending the tokenmaxxing program, employees report that token consumption continues to surge as they test the new agentic AI tool Hatch. Some workers remain hesitant to connect Hatch to personal accounts due to privacy concerns stemming from past monitoring projects. While management claims mass layoffs are not expected this year, some employees fear productivity gains could lead to further job cuts.

title: Uber launches UK's first robotaxis with a safety driver
summary: Uber has launched the UK's first robotaxis in London, deploying 15 Ford Mustang electric vehicles equipped with Wayve's autonomous technology. Each vehicle includes a human safety driver who can intervene if necessary, as demonstrated during a test ride where the driver took control to avoid a van's open doors. Uber surveyed over 100,000 London customers, who expressed interest in self-driving rides despite past US malfunctions. The company plans to phase in these vehicles over several years while maintaining human driver options. Regulators, including the Department for Transport and Transport for London, are prioritizing rigorous safety testing and local consent before full deployment. Industry experts note significant challenges remain, particularly regarding how autonomous systems handle complex urban scenarios and emergency services.

title: Jason Isbell and other musicians sue Suno over AI identity theft
summary: Jason Isbell and several other musicians filed a lawsuit against AI music generator Suno in Massachusetts. The artists allege the company misappropriates their identities by generating music that mimics their specific styles. The complaint uniquely frames the issue as a violation of individual autonomy rather than a standard copyright dispute. Plaintiffs are seeking class-action status and unspecified damages for the alleged exploitation of their musical identities.

title: Job seeker tests AI recruiter with AI candidate to expose hiring flaws
summary: A job seeker named Christopher applied to multiple positions at Everforth Apex Systems, where an AI recruiter named Riley conducted interviews without offering follow-up communication. After five unsuccessful attempts, Christopher used ChatGPT to simulate a candidate and converse with Riley, resulting in another dead end. The article reports that Christopher later created a highly qualified fake persona named Don Dickner, which prompted Riley to schedule a conversation that never occurred. Industry experts note that while voice AI presents engineering challenges, 63 percent of job seekers encounter AI interviews. The story illustrates a growing trend where applicants use artificial intelligence to navigate automated hiring processes, often revealing systemic failures in recruitment workflows.

title: E.l.f. Beauty deploys AI tool to manage social media comments
summary: E.l.f. Beauty launched E.l.f.luencer, an AI tool that generates 90% of social media responses in the brand's tone. Ekta Chopra, the company's chief technology and AI officer, states the tool increased response rates from 30-40% to above 80% while maintaining human oversight. Chopra oversees a cross-functional committee piloting 85 agentic AI use cases to minimize risks. Internally, more than 80% of employees use the B.F.e.l.f chatbot, and the e.l.f.line assistant handles work equivalent to one human. Chopra created a secure platform allowing non-technical staff to build their own agents.

title: FTC Solar VP Andrew Morse discusses scaling robotics in utility-scale solar construction
summary: Andrew Morse, VP of Software at FTC Solar, discussed the transition from pilot programs to scaled robotic deployments in utility-scale solar construction. He noted that while adoption is accelerating globally, widespread use in the U.S. depends on trackers designed to accommodate automation and measurable improvements in safety, quality, and productivity. Morse highlighted that module installation is the most promising initial application due to its repeatability and high labor intensity. He explained that successful integration involves evolving crews into skilled operators rather than replacing them entirely. Additionally, he suggested that leasing robotic equipment with training programs is a more scalable business model than Robotics-as-a-Service. Finally, Morse recommended that developers evaluate solutions using specific metrics like installation speed, labor-hours per megawatt, and safety incident rates.

title: Amazon signs first Asia Pacific standalone battery storage tolling deal in Australia
summary: Anza Power has signed a tolling agreement with Amazon Australia for the 50MW/200MWh Bairnsdale battery energy storage system in East Gippsland, Victoria. This marks Amazon's first standalone battery storage tolling agreement in the Asia-Pacific region and a first-of-its-kind deal in Australia for a non-energy business to contract for such a system. Unlike previous solar-plus-storage projects, the Bairnsdale system will connect directly to the electricity grid as an independent asset. The project aims to store electricity and dispatch it during peak demand to support regional grid reliability and renewable energy integration. Amazon has now invested in ten battery storage projects across Australia, with a combined capacity of 368MW once completed. The company frames these investments around the grid-stability role storage plays as renewable energy penetration increases.

title: Tesla Model Y Faces Rear Suspension Failures In China And Minor US Recall
summary: Tesla Model Y owners in China report rear suspension failures where the space between the wheel arch and tire narrows drastically after long-distance travel. Car News China states these issues require physical shop visits rather than software fixes. Meanwhile, AutoEvolution reports a limited US recall for under 20 Model Y units due to potentially loose front suspension fasteners. The recall covers specific 2026 models produced between July 26 and August 4, 2026, at the Fremont factory. Tesla plans to notify service centers by September 4 and mail customer notifications by October 30. Despite these mechanical concerns, the Model Y remains the top-selling electric vehicle globally and in the US as of Q1 2026.

title: 70-year-old Bill buys Tesla Model Y despite hating Elon Musk
summary: Bill, a 70-year-old EV enthusiast, purchased a Tesla Model Y after initially avoiding the brand due to his dislike of Elon Musk. He selected the vehicle after a test drive convinced him of its superior features compared to competitors like the BYD Sealion 7 and Hyundai IONIQ 5. The car's hardware for future autonomous driving and its security recording capabilities were decisive factors in his choice. Bill named his new red vehicle Bluie, referencing an Australian custom of ironic nicknaming. He plans to keep his old diesel 4WD for desert trips while using the electric SUV for daily commuting.

title: EXSA reaches commercial operation date for 25MW allocation at Ilikwa solar facility
summary: Energy Exchange of Southern Africa (EXSA) reached commercial operation date for its 25MW allocation at the Ilikwa PV Facility near Parys. The 50MW project, jointly owned by Mainstream Renewable Power and Investec, will supply electricity to EXSA's commercial and industrial customers under a long-term Power Purchase Agreement. EXSA CEO Wayne Cowie stated the milestone signals the maturing of South Africa's private electricity market. The facility is expected to generate more than 70 GWh annually for EXSA's share and avoid approximately 100,000 tonnes of CO₂ emissions. Construction created more than 2,600 jobs, with the majority recruited from neighbouring communities.

title: UK oil and gas firm and floating wind developer explore North Sea electrification
summary: The article reports that a UK oil and gas player and a floating wind developer are exploring electrification opportunities in the North Sea. The text provides no specific company names, figures, or further details about the potential collaboration or project scope.

title: Asian Oil Demand Pushes Dubai Crude Prices Near $100 Per Barrel
summary: Bloomberg reported that strong demand from Asian buyers is driving Dubai crude futures close to $100 per barrel. Indian Oil Corp and PetroChina are among the major refiners increasing purchases of Middle Eastern oil. Despite geopolitical tensions between the United States and Iran, Asian buyers are also sourcing crude from Brazil, Canada, Argentina, and Russia. Murban futures traded at $106.10 per barrel while DME Oman reached $99.18 per barrel. Brent crude and West Texas Intermediate dipped amid uncertainty over potential pauses in US-Iran strikes.

title: Brazil Senate approves data center tax incentives tied to renewable energy
summary: Brazil's Federal Senate approved Bill 278/2026, creating the Redata regime that links data center tax benefits to renewable or low-emission electricity use. The law requires companies to meet 10% of their capacity in Brazil and invest 2% of acquired product value locally. Clean Energy Latin America reports 330 MW of renewable contracts totaling BRL 7.7 billion between 2021 and 2024. The measure aims to expand digital infrastructure while boosting demand for green power projects.

title: India must integrate power planning with data centre growth for sustainable digital expansion
summary: The article argues that India's rapidly expanding digital economy requires simultaneous planning of computing capacity and power infrastructure. Data centre capacity is projected to reach 4 GW by 2030, necessitating a shift toward integrated renewable and storage solutions. The author states that reliable power availability is now a critical investment variable alongside land and connectivity. While renewable energy can reduce carbon intensity, the text notes it cannot guarantee continuous supply without firm grid connections and battery storage. Independent technical oversight is presented as essential to manage engineering risks and ensure long-term asset performance. Ultimately, the piece suggests that aligning power system development with digital infrastructure will strengthen India's economic competitiveness and clean energy transition.

title: UN Warns Climate Overshoot Is Inevitable While Critics Demand Fossil Fuel Phaseout
summary: The UN Environment Programme released a report stating that humanity will inevitably exceed the 1.5°C global warming threshold within the next few years. Independent analysts criticize the document for downplaying the potential to phase out fossil fuels and achieve net-zero emissions by 2050. While the report acknowledges that temperatures will peak higher than the Paris Agreement target, it suggests a strategy of limiting the overshoot and eventually cooling the planet through carbon removal. Critics argue this approach risks becoming a call to apathy rather than a call to arms. Conversely, some officials and organizations emphasize that every fraction of a degree matters and that urgent action on emissions reductions remains essential to minimize damage.

title: Synergy fined AU$1.2 million for software error inflating Western Australia wholesale prices
summary: Western Australia's Economic Regulation Authority fined Synergy AU$1.2 million after a software error caused the company's Kwinana battery to submit inflated price offers. The regulator found the error increased wholesale energy costs by approximately AU$9.5 million over eight months, with Synergy gaining around AU$850,000 in additional revenue. ERA chair Steve Edwell stated the penalty reflected the unintentional nature of the breach while reinforcing that non-compliance is not acceptable. Synergy admitted the breach, cooperated with the investigation, and corrected the software error. As part of the decision, the company must provide full details of the fix and may face an independent audit.

title: Rising U.S. Uranium Output Fails to Boost Stocks Amid Import Reliance
summary: U.S. uranium production reached 2.13 million pounds in the first half of 2026, yet domestic output remains a small fraction of reactor fuel needs. The EIA reports that U.S. operators purchased 46.9 million pounds in 2025, with imports from Canada, Kazakhstan, and Australia supplying 75% of deliveries. Despite a surge in drilling and spending, uranium stocks have retreated as investors realize the timeline for achieving independence is long. Long-term contracts, which account for 87% of deliveries, often lock in prices years in advance, delaying the impact of higher spot prices on earnings. Utilities hold sufficient inventories to defer purchasing, creating uncertainty for mining companies seeking financing. Consequently, the market views the production increase as insufficient to resolve immediate supply gaps or drive stock valuations higher.

title: China's CO2 emissions fell in Q2 2026 as oil use plummeted
summary: Lauri Myllyvirta reports that China's carbon dioxide emissions dropped by 1% in the second quarter of 2026, marking the first time oil consumption reductions drove an overall decline. The analysis attributes this shift to a 9% fall in total oil use, primarily caused by supply disruptions from the Strait of Hormuz crisis. While coal-fired power generation rebounded, the surge in electric vehicle adoption and usage displaced significant amounts of oil. Myllyvirta notes that EVs and public transport enabled transportation levels to rise even as fuel consumption fell sharply. The report highlights that structural factors like electrification and behavioral changes combined to reduce oil demand beyond what capacity growth alone would explain. Despite record increases in solar and wind capacity, power sector emissions rose due to curtailment of renewable output. Myllyvirta explains that grid limitations and fixed coal plant contracts prevented flexible operation to absorb variable renewable energy. The author states that China remains on track to add sufficient clean energy capacity to meet electricity demand growth this year. Future emissions trends depend on resolving grid integration issues and continuing the shift toward electrification in transport and industry.

title: China's Carbon Pollution Fell as Oil Demand Plummeted Amid War
summary: China's carbon pollution decreased recently after consumers and industries sharply reduced oil use, according to a new analysis by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air. The drop in oil consumption helped offset a 2.4 percent increase in coal burning for power, pushing total carbon dioxide emissions down by one percent from the previous year. Lauri Myllyvirta, lead analyst at the research center, noted that rapid electrification of vehicles was the primary driver, with electric truck sales surging 77 percent in the second quarter. While the trend could reshape global energy dynamics, analysts warn that a resolution to the Middle East conflict might eventually cause oil use to rebound. Tim Himle Levinh of Rystad Energy stated that China's emissions are approaching a peak, though higher consumption in petrochemicals and aviation could lead to increases in some years.

title: Europe's largest river heat pump enters construction phase in Cologne
summary: Everllence and RheinEnergie announced that Europe's largest fluvial heat pump has entered its main construction stage at the Cologne-Niehl site. The 150 MW plant will provide climate-neutral heating to approximately 50,000 households and reduce annual carbon dioxide emissions by around 100,000 tons. Commissioning is scheduled for 2028, with manufacturing of key components already advanced at Everllence facilities in Berlin and Oberhausen. The project utilizes Rhine river water and ammonia refrigerant, marking a significant step in industrial-scale climate-neutral district heating.

title: MnDOT seeks 40 new EV fast-charging sites in Greater Minnesota
summary: The Minnesota Department of Transportation is offering $41.2 million to fund up to 40 new EV fast-charging sites in Greater Minnesota. MnDOT commissioner Nancy Daubenberger stated the funding aims to reduce range anxiety for long-distance travelers. Applications for the grants are due by November 2, with awards expected in late 2026 or early 2027. Federal funds will cover 80% of eligible project costs.

title: Maine selects Clearway Energy for 800 MW wind farm and Avangrid for transmission
summary: Maine regulators selected Clearway Energy to develop an 800-megawatt wind farm in northern Maine, which would increase the state's onshore wind capacity by approximately 66%. The Maine Public Utilities Commission also chose Avangrid Networks to build the necessary high-voltage transmission line to connect the project to the regional grid. Maine plans to purchase 600 MW of the output, while the remaining 200 MW will supply other New England states. Officials estimate the projects will generate between $387 million and $425 million in net benefits for customers over their operating lives. However, the projects still require final approval of power purchase agreements, transmission arrangements, and various permits before construction can begin.

title: Rosatom considers Murmansk site for floating nuclear plant construction
summary: Rosatom Director General Alexei Likhachev said the company is considering a Murmansk site to complete floating nuclear power units. He stated this decision responds to the scale of future orders for these units. The report notes that while the Baltic Shipyard remains a key partner, Rosatom may create its own production links where necessary. Likhachev explained that the choice of Murmansk is due to the nearby Atomflot fleet and port infrastructure.

title: Hochtief agrees to acquire German power transmission firm Autmatec
summary: Hochtief has reached an agreement to acquire Autmatec, a German specialist in transmission line infrastructure, pending regulatory approval. The transaction value remains undisclosed, though Autmatec reported approximately €50m in 2026 revenue. Hochtief CEO Juan Santamaría stated the deal aligns with its strategy to invest in high-growth infrastructure markets. The acquisition aims to integrate Autmatec's technical capabilities with Hochtief's engineering scale to support major European grid modernization projects.

title: ETC finds record clean energy investment has not yet delivered emissions cuts
summary: The Energy Transition Coalition reports that record levels of clean energy investment have not yet resulted in emissions reductions. The organization highlights a gap between financial spending and actual environmental outcomes in the current energy transition landscape.

title: Farrans starts construction on BW ESS Berkswell battery storage project
summary: Farrans has begun construction on the Berkswell Battery Energy Storage System for BW ESS in the West Midlands. The 200MW/857MWh facility near Solihull is expected to power over 500,000 homes for four hours once operational. BW ESS co-owns the project with AIP Management and selected Farrans for its infrastructure experience. Farrans project manager Barry McDonagh described the site as a significant step toward a more resilient UK energy network.

title: RBI's FCNR(B) scheme: Uday Kotak lauds GIFT IFSC's role as financial hub with $52.8 billion deployment
summary: Uday Kotak praised GIFT IFSC banking units for deploying $52.8 billion under the RBI FCNR(B) swap facility. The International Financial Services Centres Authority reported that 20 banking units sanctioned $54.02 billion by August 31, 2026. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman directed public sector banks to utilize GIFT City infrastructure for these funds. Both domestic and foreign banks participated, drawing liquidity from nations including the UK, US, and Singapore. IFSCA Chairperson K Rajaraman stated the activity demonstrates GIFT City's growing international orientation.

title: Sonos launches AI update 27, new speakers, and India launch for Play 8
summary: Sonos released its Sonos 27 update, enabling control via ChatGPT and other AI agents. The company also launched the Beam Ultra soundbar and Ace Ultra headphones globally. In India, the Sonos Play portable speaker will launch on September 8 for 35,999 rupees.

title: ByteDance secures $29.6 billion loan after seeking $20 billion facility
summary: Bloomberg News reported that ByteDance secured a $29.6 billion loan, exceeding its initial $20 billion request. People familiar with the matter told Bloomberg the company gathered strong bank commitments. Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

title: South Korea utility proposes advance power payments from Samsung and SK Hynix
summary: Korea Electric Power Corp proposed that Samsung Electronics pay 20 trillion won and SK Hynix pay 5 trillion won in advance for power through 2031. The Chosun Ilbo reported the suggestion based on an internal KEPCO document. KEPCO stated participation details remain unfinalized while Samsung and SK Hynix declined to comment. The utility aims to fund grid expansion for semiconductor and AI data centre projects.

title: UK mortgage rates expected to rise as bond sell-off pushes swap rates higher
summary: UK mortgage borrowers face rising borrowing costs as a global bond sell-off drives up swap rates. The five-year swap rate recently exceeded 4.52%, the highest level since October 2023. AJ Bell investment director Russ Mould stated that lenders will raise rates to preserve margins and manage risk. YorkshireBuildingSociety managing director Tom Simpson noted the current increase is modest compared to previous volatility. The rise in UK 10-year government debt yields has contributed to these market pressures.

title: Jon Fiva shares statistics on publication bias in economics and political science
summary: Jon Fiva shared statistics from new research regarding publication bias in economics and political science. The data indicates that instrumental variable estimates are significantly larger than OLS estimates. Additionally, significant results are far more likely to be published in experimental economics than null findings.

title: PwC report finds nearly half of UK households miss economic growth benefits
summary: A new PwC report indicates that 46% of UK households do not experience improved living standards despite national economic growth. Researchers found a stark North-South divide, with every region in northern England, the Midlands, and Wales showing lower spending power than the national average. Conversely, London and the South East recorded spending power significantly above average. The study defines household spending power as income after taxes and housing costs, adjusted for household size. While Prime Minister Andy Burnham has pledged to address regional inequalities, political debate continues regarding the effectiveness of his growth strategies and the proposed No10 North initiative. PwC argues that future devolution must ensure local areas retain revenues generated by local growth to truly improve community prosperity.

title: Scotland Trading Standards Seek Extra Powers Against Fake Cigarettes
summary: Trading Standards officers in Scotland report an explosion of illegal tobacco sales in high street shops. The BBC joined officers on raids in Inverness to investigate counterfeit and smuggled cigarettes. Officials link the UK-wide problem to organised crime. The Scottish government stated illicit tobacco is a serious issue and is working with partners to address it.

title: Michael Moritz discusses his new memoir and diverse interests
summary: Michael Moritz joins a conversation to discuss his new memoir, Ausländer, and his varied career as a journalist and investor. The authors report that Moritz describes himself as a dilettante with too many interests, ranging from writing books on Apple and Manchester United to learning to paint in his 40s. During the discussion, Moritz explains that tough, grueling works of art offer more layers for exploration than decorative pieces. He also reflects on how unsatisfied curiosity drives his life and writing, noting that each book springs from being curious about something difficult. Moritz shares personal anecdotes about his childhood in Wales, his German citizenship, and his perspective on capitalism in China versus America. The conversation concludes with a recommendation for his new family memoir about escape and exile.

title: Writer Derek Thompson discusses Pangram AI detection tool
summary: Writer Derek Thompson interviewed Pangram founder about generative text detection. Pangram recently helped expose AI use at The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal. Thompson noted re-summarizing key points as a new tell for AI writing. However, Thompson fears AI-writing witch hunts would be an unwelcome addition to online life.

title: Asian data center expansion faces local backlash and lending caution
summary: Nikkei reported that rapid data center construction across Asia is triggering environmental and health concerns from local communities. While demand remains strong, developers are shifting investments to regions with less opposition. Barclays bankers told Bloomberg that lenders have distributed nearly $29 billion since the start of the year but are becoming more selective. Analysts noted that issues arise primarily when developers fail to engage with the community.

title: ADP Reports Private Payroll Growth Missed Expectations by 9,000 Jobs
summary: ADP released data showing private nonfarm payroll employment growth fell short of forecasts. The report indicates a gain of 38,000 jobs instead of the 47,000 expected by Bloomberg consensus. Analysts note this figure does not show a dropoff in employment. The data compares ADP estimates against Bureau of Labor Statistics benchmark revisions.

title: Author analyzes impact of IEEPA tariffs on cyclically adjusted budget balance
summary: The author examines the federal budget balance excluding IEEPA tariff revenue, noting the figure improves through 2025Q3 before refunds begin. CBO estimates the FY2027 cyclically adjusted balance at -5.8% of potential GDP, suggesting elevated real rates. The author states uncertainty remains regarding how the war, refunds, and tariff challenges will affect the balance. Paweł Skrzypczyński's calculations are cited to show uncertainty in customs revenue figures.

title: Fortune Coconut Whan Neng uses TikTok to market fresh coconut milk
summary: Fortune Coconut Whan Neng at MacPherson Market & Food Centre continues to press fresh coconut milk without preservatives. Third-generation successor Lee Zhao Yuan, 27, plans to take over the family business within five years. The stall processes around 300 coconuts daily to yield up to 100 litres of milk. Lee Zhao Yuan uses TikTok and social media to attract younger customers to the traditional trade. The business sells white and brown grated coconut flesh at S$7/kg and S$6.50/kg respectively. Fortune Coconut Whan Neng is located at #01-60, MacPherson Market & Food Centre, 89 Circuit Road, Singapore 370089.

title: OpenAI faces criminal probe after lawsuit claims ChatGPT aided Florida shooter
summary: A family of a Florida shooting victim has sued OpenAI, alleging the gunman used ChatGPT to plan the attack. The company now faces a U.S. criminal investigation for failing to report potential threats. Recent mass shootings in the U.S. and Canada have highlighted concerns over AI use in public killings. Regulators and safety advocates are now warning about the risks of AI-enabled violence.

title: Trump celebrates Apple Maps renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America
summary: President Trump stated that Apple Maps has updated the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America, calling the change binding. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum confirmed the president contacted Apple directly about the update. Google also adopted the new name for U.S. users, while MapQuest declined to change it. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney condemned the move as part of a broader trade dispute.

title: US judge rejects bid to break up Google's ad business
summary: The provided text contains a headline stating a US judge rejected a bid to break up Google's ad business. However, the article body failed to load due to technical issues.

title: Amazon secures exclusive local streaming rights for six NHL teams starting 2026-27
summary: Amazon announced a multi-year deal granting Prime Video exclusive local streaming rights for six NHL teams beginning in the 2026-2027 season. The participating franchises include the Carolina Hurricanes, Anaheim Ducks, Columbus Blue Jackets, Dallas Stars, Minnesota Wild, and St. Louis Blues. NHL Chief Media Officer David Proper stated that the clubs selected Amazon's offer after reviewing various proposals. The agreement includes games, pre- and post-game shows, and other team programming for fans in regional territories.

title: US imposes up to 100% tariffs on drones to reduce Chinese reliance
summary: The United States implemented new tariffs on drones and components to decrease dependence on Chinese suppliers. President Donald Trump signed an order citing national security threats posed by imports. Drones weighing over 25 kilograms face a 100% duty, while smaller models incur a 25% charge. China opposed the move, warning it would disrupt the global supply chain. DJI, which holds more than two-thirds of the market, has faced US restrictions since 2022.

title: Trump escalates trade war with Canada while facing domestic legal and political challenges
summary: Donald Trump intensified trade tensions with Canada, stating the nation has unfairly exploited US farmers and tourists for decades. He previously imposed 50% tariffs on $20bn of Canadian goods, prompting threats of retaliatory measures. Simultaneously, a US judge blocked a new executive order attempting to restrict birthright citizenship, ruling it almost certainly unconstitutional. In domestic politics, House Democrats rejected a Republican proposal to cap the Supreme Court at nine justices by a vote of 212-206. Lawmakers also introduced a resolution to halt the administration's unauthorized boat strikes against drug cartels. The Trump administration denied New York's request for federal disaster assistance following a major snowstorm that caused $168m in damage. Additionally, Arizona Democrat Adelita Grijalva condemned new border wall construction on Tohono O’odham tribal lands. Trump also commented on Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's return to the UK, expressing happiness about their move while criticizing their treatment of the royal family.

title: Chinese AI firm Moonshot confidentially files for Hong Kong IPO
summary: Three sources say Chinese AI startup Moonshot has confidentially filed for a Hong Kong IPO. The company aims to raise $3 billion in the offering, joining other rivals seeking public listings.

title: Nepal Army installs cable to help Nuwakot flood survivors cross river
summary: The Nepal Army installed a roughly 250-metre cable crossing in Bidur to assist flood survivors in Nuwakot district. This makeshift device allows people to cross the swollen Trishuli River after roads and bridges were destroyed. Footage shows soldiers and residents pulling individuals to safety on the precarious route. The crossing has become a vital link for communities cut off by the devastating floods more than a week ago.

title: Home loan applications fall 15% as banks face housing inquiry
summary: Officials from the Commonwealth Bank report a 15% drop in home loan applications since the May federal budget. Banking executives from the top four banks are appearing at a Senate inquiry into generational housing inequality. Robert Parker of the CBA noted investor loans have fallen about 28% since May, though owner-occupier figures remain unavailable. Westpac's Dr Luci Ellis stated the bank does not publicly report how much of its $6.9bn profit comes from home loan interest. Joseph Mitchell of the Australian Council of Trade Unions criticized the big four banks for their high profitability and lack of competition. Meanwhile, a three-year-old girl in Melbourne died after developing Haemolytic-uraemic syndrome following a petting zoo visit. Health authorities warn the STEC bacteria strain can cause fatal kidney failure and brain injury. Public health groups caution that proposed tobacco excise cuts could undermine decades of progress in reducing smoking rates.

title: Xi Jinping visits Egypt to deepen China's Middle East influence
summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping visited Egypt to strengthen diplomatic and economic ties with Cairo, aiming to expand Beijing's regional influence. The leaders discussed opposing unilateralism and working for a more equitable global governance system. Egypt seeks to diversify its strategic partnerships by deepening cooperation with China, which has invested over $10 billion in the country. China aims to position itself as a stabilizer in the Middle East, contrasting its approach with that of the United States. The visit also highlights China's role as a mediator in regional conflicts and its interest in the Suez Canal as an alternative energy route.

title: Edge Early Learning permanently closes Canberra's Charnwood centre
summary: Edge Early Learning announced the permanent closure of its Charnwood childcare centre in Canberra, citing unviable operations following a regulatory suspension. The national provider, which recently entered voluntary administration, stated that reopening the service after a three-month suspension order would be too difficult. The ACT regulator, CECA, had issued the suspension due to significant staff turnover and safety risks, including children going missing. While Edge claimed it had made progress addressing these concerns, the regulator noted the centre previously had a cohesive team. Parents and staff expressed distress over the sudden decision, with families scrambling to find alternative care. Administrators are now seeking buyers for the company's remaining services.

title: Disability worker Scott Bone accused of sexually assaulting two women
summary: Scott Bone, a 56-year-old disability support worker, has been charged with three counts of aggravated sexual touching against two women in his care. The accused will appear in court again on September 23 to address the allegations.

title: Macron and Burnham meet after Bayeux Tapestry viewing to discuss migration and Ukraine
summary: French President Emmanuel Macron and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham are scheduled to hold their first talks on Thursday following a meeting at the Bayeux Tapestry exhibition. The leaders discussed migrant boats crossing the Channel and the war in Ukraine. Macron played a key role in securing the tapestry loan, viewing it as a step toward healing post-Brexit relations. Downing Street confirmed that a surge team of 45 French officers will be deployed to tackle larger migrant vessels. Both leaders emphasized continued support for Ukraine and the importance of EU-UK cooperation. However, an expert warned that the talks might lack substance on EU negotiations.

title: Yuki Tsunoda replaces Isack Hadjar at Racing Bulls for Italian Grand Prix
summary: Red Bull confirmed its driver lineups for the Italian Grand Prix at Monza. Isack Hadjar will miss the race due to a wrist injury sustained during training. Liam Lawson will replace Hadjar at Red Bull Racing, while Yuki Tsunoda will fill in for Racing Bulls. The team stated it is monitoring Hadjar's rehabilitation closely and wishes him a speedy recovery.

title: Former Venezuelan President Maduro and wife seek dismissal of drug charges via immunity
summary: Lawyers for former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores filed motions in Manhattan federal court to dismiss drug trafficking charges based on immunity. Their attorneys argued that U.S. courts cannot try a recognized foreign head of state and that Venezuela's sovereignty prevents prosecution. Judge Alvin K. Hellerstein has scheduled oral arguments for November 17 before the trial set for next June. Both defendants have pleaded not guilty to conspiracy charges involving cocaine trafficking.

title: NYC Mayor Mamdani bans generative AI for elementary and middle school students
summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced a temporary ban on generative AI tools for students through eighth grade. Officials describe this as the most expansive prohibition in the United States, affecting roughly 600,000 public school students. The policy halts use of about 40 educational AI tools while officials study children's technology use. High schoolers remain exempt, receiving AI literacy classes instead. Teachers retain permission to use AI for lesson planning and administrative tasks. The decision emphasizes human connection in education and aligns with the district's teaching ideals.

title: Finland conducts largest civil defense exercise in Europe since WWII
summary: Finland is conducting its largest civil defense exercise since World War II, involving over 2,000 participants in Kuopio to rehearse responses to potential Russian attacks. The scenario simulates cyberattacks disrupting critical infrastructure and the threat of missile strikes from Russia. Retired Army Colonel Asko Muhonen stated that the exercise relies on the mindset of ordinary citizens ready to take responsibility for national security. Participants practiced using shelters designed to withstand nuclear or biological attacks, though officials note these offer limited protection against sabotage campaigns. The Finnish Security and Intelligence Service reported investigating various observations but found nothing of concern regarding recent drone sightings or GPS jamming. Veterans shared memories of past conflicts with the Soviet Union, highlighting the historical context of Finland's defense strategy. The event underscores the nation's preparedness to protect itself without external aid for at least 72 hours.

title: Congo struggles to pay Ebola workers as outbreaks grow
summary: Congo's Ebola response faces severe funding and staffing challenges as unpaid workers abandon checkpoints and many listed employees are absent. Officials discovered that only 40 of 240 workers at an Ebola center were present. The government is implementing biometric registration to eliminate fictitious payrolls and address decades of systemic issues. These problems complicate efforts to combat the world's fastest-growing Ebola epidemic.

title: NBA fines LA Clippers $30m and suspends owner Steve Ballmer over Leonard pay scandal
summary: The NBA fined the LA Clippers $30m and suspended owner Steve Ballmer for 12 months regarding violations involving Kawhi Leonard's contracts. Commissioner Adam Silver stated the penalties reflect the severity of the organization's flagrant rule-breaking. Leonard accepted responsibility and expressed regret for the distraction caused to fans and his family. The Clippers announced they will appeal the decision through every available avenue.

title: UN warns of 'supersized' El Niño as countries prepare for impact
summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres warns the world has entered a danger zone as a supersized El Niño develops. The World Meteorological Organization reports sea temperatures could rise nearly 4C above average, potentially making this the strongest event since 1950. Officials state the phenomenon will last until at least February 2027, bringing droughts to South America and Asia while increasing typhoon risks in the Pacific. Australia faces marine heatwaves, and Indonesia battles extensive wildfires. Experts note that while early warning systems are being strengthened, structural issues like poor housing and weak healthcare systems remain major vulnerabilities for affected populations.

title: US strikes Iranian launchers after claims of new mine-firing rockets
summary: The United States launched airstrikes on Sunday against Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island, citing a new threat to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. US officials stated that Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces were preparing to fire sea mines from rockets, a method some analysts describe as unprecedented. Maritime security experts remain skeptical about the feasibility of this tactic, noting that rockets could damage mines upon water impact and that the method lacks precision. While Iranian state television reported tests with Fajr-5 systems for this purpose in January 2025, specialists suggest the claim may serve as propaganda to justify US strikes or demonstrate psychological warfare capabilities. Regardless of the tactic's reality, the exchange highlights the ongoing escalation between the two nations over control of the vital waterway.

title: Hong Kong court upholds convictions of Cardinal Joseph Zen and others over relief fund
summary: A Hong Kong court upheld convictions for Cardinal Joseph Zen and four others regarding an unregistered relief fund. The five defendants were fined 4,000 Hong Kong dollars each in 2022 for breaching the Societies Ordinance. Observers note the case is significant for the city's freedom of association amid recent political changes. Zen previously stated his case should not be viewed as connected to religious freedoms. Authorities maintain the relevant security law is necessary for stability.

title: Thousands rally in Niamey to support Niger's junta after mutiny
summary: Thousands gathered in Niamey on Wednesday to support General Abdourahamane Tiani following a thwarted army mutiny, Nigerien journalists reported. The demonstration included ministers and Russian flags, reflecting closer ties with Moscow after Niger cut links with France. Business minister Abdoulaye Seydou declared the people stand united against treason. General Amadou Ibro claimed mutiny sponsors are based abroad, a claim the junta uses to justify its rule.

title: Women farmers in Sumatra use citrus trees to deter elephants
summary: Women farmers in Sumatra have adopted citrus trees as a natural barrier to prevent elephants from damaging their crops. This approach avoids the use of poison or electric fences common in other regions. The Batang Nilo Women's Forest Farmer Group also plants elephant-friendly trees to encourage peaceful coexistence. A study highlights how these women act as creative problem solvers rather than victims of human-elephant conflict.

title: Beetle larvae mimic flower scents to trick bees into parasitism
summary: New research reveals European black oil beetle larvae manufacture floral scents to lure bees. The larvae hitch rides to bee burrows where they consume eggs and pollen. Study authors state this is the first known case of an animal hijacking flower smells for parasitism. Lead author Ryan Alam noted the compounds resemble willow flower scents. Experts suggest chemical mimicry may be more widespread in insects than currently known.

title: Trump defends US Iran stance; Germany probes grid sabotage; Venezuela signs energy deals
summary: President Donald Trump stated the US confronts Iran to protect Israel and the West. Iran claimed it laid new naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Germany investigates state-sponsored sabotage after power grid attacks near Cologne. Venezuela signed major energy deals with Chevron and Eni. G20 nations reached consensus on global technology policy. Türkiye remains top in FIBA World Cup 2027 European Qualifiers rankings. Nordic football associations seek EU action regarding FIFA governance concerns.

title: Experts warn Europe must prepare for potential power grid sabotage threats
summary: The article reports that experts warn Europe must prepare for potential power grid sabotage threats. They state the worst-case scenario is not inevitable but requires readiness. No specific details or sources were provided in the text.

title: UNICEF survey finds one in five youths targeted by online sexual abuse
summary: A new UNICEF survey reveals that one in five young people aged 12 to 17 experienced online sexual abuse in the past year. The report indicates that over 15 million children were exposed to unwanted sexual content, while 9 million were pressured into sexual conversations. UNICEF Executive Director Catherine Russell stated that these experiences cause profound emotional distress, yet fewer than 1% of cases are reported to authorities. Data collected from 21,000 young people across 21 countries shows that 57% of perpetrators are known to the victims rather than strangers. The survey identifies Meta-owned platforms like Facebook and Instagram as primary gateways for these assaults. Following these findings, the report calls for stronger digital protections and updated regulations to safeguard minors online.

title: Moroccan migrants stranded in Ceuta camp fear deportation
summary: Hundreds of Moroccan migrants live in tents on Ceuta's El Trampolín beach, avoiding official centers due to fears of deportation. Residents Nebil Tazi and Hamza Mohammed describe difficult living conditions and a desire to reach Europe or find work. Local tensions remain high following the arrival of approximately 80,000 migrants, prompting demonstrations against the Spanish government's lack of policy.

title: Homeland Security Secretary says ICE agents could appear at polling places if threats exist
summary: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin stated that Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents might visit polling locations during the November elections if a threat is identified or a warrant must be served. Mullin clarified that ICE will not patrol these sites but will enforce specific threats or serve warrants on actively tracked individuals. This position contrasts with earlier assurances from DHS officials who claimed there would be no ICE presence at polling places during midterm elections. While no orders exist to deploy agents generally, their presence is not ruled out under specific circumstances. Voting-rights groups have expressed concern that such a possibility could lead to voter intimidation and depress turnout.

title: Study identifies 1,260 genetic variants linked to personality traits
summary: An international consortium published a study in Nature identifying 1,260 genetic variants associated with the Big Five personality traits. The research analyzed data from 1.14 million people across 46 cohorts to map these genetic influences. Michel Nivard, a lead author, noted that while genetics plays a role, environmental factors remain decisive in shaping personality. The study found that family environment has less impact on personality than on traits like intelligence. Nivard emphasized that no single 'personality gene' exists, as each variant contributes only a microscopic effect. The findings suggest that genetic scores can only predict personality when averaged across large populations, not for individuals. Additionally, the research linked specific traits to behaviors such as neighborhood choice and smoking rates.

title: Greece set to sign $3.6B deal for three Israeli air defense systems
summary: Israeli media reports indicate Greece is set to sign a $3.6 billion agreement Monday for three air defense systems. The Jerusalem Post stated a Greek delegation will finalize the deal in Tel Aviv after nearly three years of talks. The contract includes David's Sling, Spyder, and Barak MX systems to bolster Greece's Achilles Shield network. Israeli firms Rafael and Israel Aerospace Industries are expected to supply the hardware, while Greek companies will receive approximately $820 million in work. The project, reported by Calcalist and Yedioth Ahronoth, involves a command-and-control network using artificial intelligence and will be implemented in stages over roughly 35 months. Kathimerini also reported the deal's value and timing. Neither Greece nor Israel has officially confirmed the agreement as of Sunday evening.

title: Ghanaians turn to indigenous plants as Western medicine costs rise
summary: Rising costs of Western pharmaceuticals in Ghana are driving increased reliance on traditional plant-based remedies among the local population. Dr. Kofi Donkor, deputy director of the Center for Plant Medicine Research, explains that traditional practitioners possess generations of knowledge validated through scientific methods. Approximately 60 to 70 percent of Ghanaians depend on traditional medicine markets for their healthcare needs. Rural women harvest medicinal herbs to sell in Accra, while the government center treats roughly 16,000 patients monthly. Researchers are currently studying West African plants, including one showing promise against prostate cancer, to further legitimize this sustainable healing source.

title: John Ternus leads Apple hardware engineering and future product strategy
summary: The article examines how John Ternus shapes Apple's hardware direction under Tim Cook. Ternus oversees engineering for major product lines including the iPhone, iPad, and Mac. His team recently launched the iPhone Air, Apple's thinnest model, developed in close coordination with Johny Srouji's chip division. Srouji now serves as chief hardware officer, unifying hardware technologies and engineering under one executive. The report notes Apple still uses Qualcomm modems in some 2026 models despite building its own C1X chip. Rumors suggest a foldable phone and new smart glasses may launch in September 2026. Ternus also faces the challenge of integrating AI features into Apple's hardware following delays in Apple Intelligence.

title: UDF nominees oppose SSUS decision to cancel incomplete exam tabulation registers
summary: UDF nominees in the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit Syndicate oppose a decision to cancel a July 2026 order allowing officials to sign past exam registers. K. B. Sabu stated that blanket cancellation is impractical as it would delay degree certificates. The university authorities confirmed the August 22 decision to cancel the earlier order and launch a probe into documentation irregularities. Officials who signed registers after the July decision included those who had retired from service.

title: JD(U)'s Sanjay Jha says Ganga Water Treaty harms Bihar interests
summary: JD(U) national working president Sanjay Jha stated that the India-Bangladesh Ganga Water Treaty negatively impacts Bihar's interests. Speaking to The Hindu, he argued the 1996 agreement has hurt the state despite diplomatic messaging benefits. The treaty expires on December 31, 2026, amid current political tensions between India and Bangladesh. The Ministry of External Affairs has not yet responded to queries regarding Jha's remarks.

title: PM Modi directs war footing relief as Varanasi floods cross warning mark
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inspected flood relief efforts in Varanasi as the Ganga river crossed its warning level. The Central Water Commission reported the water reached 70.54 metres at Rajghat, rising at 2 cm per hour. PM Modi instructed district officials to operate on a war footing to provide immediate assistance. Authorities are monitoring affected areas and ensuring relief camps have adequate supplies for vulnerable residents.

title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay to move resolution for Tamil as Madras HC language
summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay plans to move a resolution in the state assembly urging the Centre to recognise Tamil as the principal language of the Madras high court. Official sources confirmed the move is scheduled for Thursday. Additionally, the state government increased the milk procurement price by Rs 6. Vijaya Srivastava, a journalist, covers these political and policy developments.

title: Uber lays off 10 percent of staff to streamline operations
summary: Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi announced layoffs affecting approximately 10 percent of the company's roughly 34,000 employees worldwide. The company stated these cuts aim to simplify operations and reduce coordination delays in its global business. Wedbush Securities expects the reductions to save around $1.75 billion for reinvestment. Additionally, Uber plans to consolidate its delivery units and limit remote work to about one percent of staff.

title: Sensex rises over 150 points, Nifty opens near 24,000 as US bonds yields slightly ease. Why is caution still warranted?
summary: Sensex rose over 300 points to 76,900 while Nifty 50 opened near 23,998 on Thursday. VK Vijayakumar of Geojit Investments noted that easing US bond yields and strong rupee inflows may boost market sentiment. However, analysts warn caution remains necessary due to elevated US yields and high oil prices. Anand James stated that Nifty needs a break above 24,150 to signal further strength.

title: Apple Maps renames Lake Ontario to Lake America for US users
summary: Apple Maps has updated its US interface to display Lake America instead of Lake Ontario, following a similar change by Google Maps. President Donald Trump announced the name change is complete and binding on social media. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney rejected the change, noting the name's 400-year history. MapQuest declined to rename the lake and remains Lake Ontario.

title: Apple confirms September 9 event featuring foldable iPhone Ultra and new Pro models
summary: Apple has confirmed its annual hardware event will take place on September 9, marking CEO John Ternus's first product launch. The company is reportedly preparing to unveil a foldable iPhone Ultra alongside updated iPhone 18 Pro models and a refreshed Apple Watch lineup. Several devices, including the standard iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2, are expected to be delayed to spring 2027. The event will stream online starting at 10 am Pacific Time.

title: Madras Court Rejects DMK Challenge; GDP Debate Rages; NVIDIA CEO Praises India
summary: The Madras High Court dismissed a DMK petition challenging the Kolathur election result due to insufficient evidence. A political dispute has emerged over India's 7.8% GDP growth figures, with the opposition questioning the data while the government defends its accuracy. NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang praised India's AI potential and urged rapid adoption. Meanwhile, Prime Minister Narendra Modi reviewed flood relief measures in Varanasi.

title: Seven Indigenous Siekopai women protect Amazon river turtles
summary: Seven Indigenous Siekopai women in Ecuador's Amazon are leading a conservation effort to protect vulnerable river turtles. The group, known as the Tari Nomiowa'i or "Turtle Women," combines ancestral knowledge with modern technology to safeguard nests along the Aguarico River. During the 2025-26 nesting season, the women collected 235 eggs and successfully released 208 hatchlings into the river. Their work addresses threats such as pollution, predation, and flooding that endanger the yellow-spotted Amazon River turtle. Janeth Piaguaje, a community leader, noted that the project honors their spiritual connection to nature while passing knowledge to younger generations. The initiative demonstrates how local communities can effectively lead conservation when traditional ecological knowledge is paired with digital tools. While the releases represent a positive short-term outcome, continued protection remains essential for long-term population recovery.

title: Former Big Tech Employees Face Financial Strain After Layoffs
summary: Business Insider interviewed four former employees of Meta, Google, Intel, and Microsoft who were laid off without warning. The report details their prolonged job searches, significant financial losses, and the erosion of their sense of security. One applicant submitted over 8,000 applications while another faced a year-long unemployment period. The article highlights how high salaries and tenure at major tech firms failed to protect these workers from sudden job loss.

title: Indian bonds rise as RBI forex inflows boost liquidity and spur debt buying
summary: Indian government bonds gained value on Thursday after large foreign currency inflows increased rupee liquidity. The Reserve Bank of India attracted $136.38 billion through special schemes, while banks raised $127.23 billion in deposits. Kotak Mahindra Bank stated concerns about aggressive sterilisation may be overstated. However, high oil prices and U.S. Treasury yields dampened demand for longer-dated securities.

title: Amazon creates 1.6 lakh seasonal jobs; Meesho expects to add 10 lakh roles ahead of festive season
summary: Amazon India announced the creation of over 1.6 lakh temporary positions across its operations network to handle the upcoming festive season surge. The company stated these roles span 400 cities, including tier 2 and 3 locations, and involve picking, packing, and delivering orders. Abhinav Singh, Vice President of Operations at Amazon India, noted that many associates will continue working beyond the festive period. Meanwhile, Meesho expects to generate approximately 10 lakh seasonal job opportunities through its seller and logistics ecosystems. The marketplace reported that nearly 1.3 lakh sellers plan to hire seasonal workers for packaging and inventory management. PTI reported that the festive season is likely to create 2.5–2.7 lakh temporary jobs across various sectors, with significant demand from tier II and III cities. The TeamLease Festive Season Workforce Report 2026 projected that South India will account for 36.3 per cent of these frontline opportunities.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang urges India to accelerate AI adoption and regulation
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told IANS that India must accelerate its AI development to match the technology's rapid pace. He described AI as essential economic infrastructure and advised governments to regulate only practical harms rather than hypothetical risks. Huang noted that AI systems have improved significantly in reliability over the past two years. He also stated there were no discussions regarding additional US semiconductor tariffs during the G20 ministerial.

title: India's RBI gains $127 billion from NRI deposits to support rupee
summary: The Reserve Bank of India reported a $127 billion mobilisation through non-resident deposits, exceeding market expectations. This influx bolsters the central bank's capacity to support the currency against the US dollar. Traders anticipate the rupee opening between 94.30 and 94.35. The Reserve Bank of India stated that the actual figure is far higher than anyone had expected.

title: Messi Instagram ad declares GOAT debate settled after retirement
summary: Lionel Messi posted a Michelob ULTRA advertisement declaring the GOAT debate settled days after retiring from international football. The video features a receipt listing his 207 appearances and 125 goals for Argentina alongside major titles won in 2021, 2024, and 2024. The ad highlights his 21 World Cup goals and notes he won the 2022 tournament while Cristiano Ronaldo did not. Messi and Ronaldo have faced each other 36 times, with Messi's teams winning 16 matches. The article states Messi finished his international career with 125 goals compared to Ronaldo's 146.

title: Apple CEO John Ternus receives $110 million in stock and $3 million salary
summary: The Apple board approved a new compensation package for CEO John Ternus, raising his annual salary to $3 million and granting restricted stock units worth $2.5 million. His total disclosed stock exposure is approximately $110 million, with potential future payouts reaching $148 million based on performance. Tim Cook transitions to Executive Chairman with a reduced $2 million salary and a $45 million equity award. Ternus officially assumed the CEO role on September 1, 2026. The article notes that while the filing details salary and equity, it does not specify potential cash bonuses, which are typically valued at double the base salary.

title: Marco Rubio denies India-Iran trade deal after SCO summit meeting
summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated on September 2 that he does not believe a trade deal exists between India and Iran. His comments followed a meeting between Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Iranian President Massoud Pezeshkian at the SCO Summit in Bishkek. Rubio emphasized that many nations communicate with the Iranian regime but warned against helping Iran evade sanctions or fund terrorism. Meanwhile, an Iranian readout noted Pezeshkian appreciated New Delhi's support during recent conflicts and urged dialogue to resolve regional issues. The leaders discussed peace efforts amid heightened tensions in West Asia, including recent Iranian attacks on US bases.

title: Two Killed When Bus Hits Lorry on Chennai-Trichy Highway
summary: Police reported that two people died and six were injured after a bus rear-ended a lorry on the Chennai-Trichy National Highway in Perambalur. The deceased were identified as Pon Paldurai and Thirunavukkarasu. Six others, including the driver, were admitted to the Perambalur Government Hospital. A case has been registered, and investigations are ongoing.

title: Analyst Nagaraj Shetti recommends eClerx and UNO Minda shares for short-term buying
summary: Analyst Nagaraj Shetti recommends eClerx Services and UNO Minda shares for short-term investment. The article notes that domestic benchmarks Nifty 50 and Sensex gained 0.35% on Thursday, driven by banking stocks and higher foreign currency mobilization. While oil prices eased near $95 a barrel, the overall Nifty 50 trend remains weak with potential resistance around 24,100-24,200 levels. Shetti highlights that eClerx shows a bullish flag breakout pattern, whereas UNO Minda recently broke down from a triple-top consolidation. The report includes a disclaimer that these views belong to individual analysts, not LiveMint. Readers are advised to consult certified experts before making investment decisions.

title: Sensex and Nifty rebound after three-day slide as bank stocks lead recovery
summary: Benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty rose in early trade on Thursday after three sessions of losses, driven by bank stocks and global market trends. The Sensex climbed 334.16 points to 76,904.51, while the Nifty advanced 95.45 points to 24,009.90. Analysts attributed the positive sentiment to easing U.S. bond yields and record foreign-currency deposit inflows. V. K. Vijayakumar of Geojit Investments noted that recent selling pressure likely came from retail investors rather than institutions. Meanwhile, FIIs bought equities worth ₹6,688.37 crore on Wednesday, while DIIs purchased shares worth ₹2,812.98 crore.

title: Supreme Court sets aside ₹425 crore fine on Gujarat diamond trader
summary: The Supreme Court set aside a ₹425 crore penalty on Gujarat diamond trader Vijay Ghanshyam Gadiya after the original order relied on non-existent case laws generated by AI. A bench of justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu remanded the case to an officer of the same rank, cautioning that while AI can be an assistive tool, it must not drive adjudication decisions. The court left it to the appointing authority to decide on any action against the customs officer who issued the flawed order.

title: ACB raids Suryapet town planning officer over asset allegations
summary: The Anti-Corruption Bureau raided Suryapet Town Planning Officer V. Somaiah's residence on Tuesday following complaints of disproportionate assets. Officials registered a case and are investigating seized documents and bank accounts at his homes in Suryapet and Hayathnagar. Somaiah faces allegations of delaying files to collect bribes and constructing an ashram with donations. Further details on seized assets or arrests are expected as the investigation continues.

title: Fact-checkers confirm viral Nepal flood video is AI-generated
summary: Fact-checkers determined a viral video of people in floodwaters is not from Nepal. Reverse image searches found the clip on Instagram in July, predating the floods. Visual inconsistencies included skyscrapers in a hilly region and people lacking distinct facial features. Multiple AI detection tools confirmed the video was synthetic with high confidence scores. The video is being shared to falsely depict real flood visuals.

title: ED raids Hyderabad ganja syndicate over hawala links amid political controversy
summary: The Enforcement Directorate raided premises linked to Kalapathi Mithubai in Hyderabad to investigate money laundering and hawala transactions. Investigators found the syndicate sold ganja procured from Odisha for six years. Prior actions seized 53.5 kilograms of ganja and over 67 lakh rupees in cash. Meanwhile, political debates continue over India's 7.8% GDP growth figures.

title: Tamil Nadu Police Register Case After AI Deepfake Video Impersonates Chief Minister Vijay
summary: Tamil Nadu CB-CID registered a case after detecting an AI-generated deepfake video impersonating Chief Minister Vijay on social media. Police found the Hindi audio video asked viewers to contact a WhatsApp number for financial assistance. Authorities approached Meta for logs and requested the fake video's removal. The investigation continues to trace creators of similar scams reportedly circulating from Pakistan-based accounts.

title: Jailed JKLF chief Yasin Malik waives defense in Sarla Bhat murder case
summary: Jailed JKLF chief Yasin Malik told a Srinagar court he will not defend himself in the 1990 Sarla Bhat murder case. Malik stated he does not wish to challenge the proceedings but clarified his withdrawal is not an admission of guilt. He also announced his divorce from Pakistani wife Mushaal Hussein Mullick after 16 years. The court has listed the matter for a next hearing on September 19.

title: Police investigate murder-suicide after finding dead woman and injured man in Delhi hotel
summary: Police in Delhi are investigating a murder-suicide case after finding a 28-year-old woman dead and a man critically injured at Hotel Prince in Lahori Gate. Deputy Commissioner of Police Niharika Bhatt stated the woman had multiple stab injuries while the man attempted suicide. The couple, from Bihar and Rajasthan respectively, had checked in two days prior. Authorities are currently contacting their families and conducting further inquiries into the incident.

title: MP Raghav Chadha Claims AAP Deleted His Name From Punjab Voter List
summary: Rajya Sabha MP Raghav Chadha alleges the Aam Aadmi Party orchestrated his removal from Punjab's draft voter list. Chadha stated the deletion was a political vendetta while AAP officials claim he is responsible for maintaining his registration. The Election Commission conducted the Special Intensive Revision independently of the state government. Chadha plans to use available remedies to correct the record before the final roll releases in October 2026.

title: Analysts debate gold versus silver investment potential after recent market correction
summary: LiveMint reports that gold and silver prices rebounded following a correction triggered by the Jackson Hole meeting. Emkay Wealth Management states gold has stronger support around $4,060, while silver faces potential resistance near $68 and $74. Vivek Choksey of Emkay notes the long-term case for gold remains constructive if interest rates soften. Augmont's Renisha Chainani adds that gold currently finds support between $4,400 and $4,410, whereas silver holds above $66. Both metals continue to benefit from a weakening U.S. dollar and easing Treasury yields. The article concludes that while both assets offer long-term value, silver remains more volatile due to its sensitivity to industrial demand.

title: Private equity firms and portfolio companies drive India's IPO surge
summary: Private equity firms and their portfolio companies are increasingly utilizing India's deepening capital markets for initial public offerings. A McKinsey survey indicates India is emerging as a top pick in Asia-Pacific private markets. In FY2025-26, PE-backed listings accounted for 35% of total main-board IPO issuances. Major firms like Blackstone and Warburg Pincus have successfully listed or divested stakes in sectors ranging from real estate to mutual funds. While some investors express caution regarding valuation incentives, the trend signals a shift toward institutional acceptance. Experts note that future success depends on whether these listings foster long-term capital formation rather than serving merely as exit corridors.

title: Abhishek Banerjee alleges BJP supporters vandalised TMC office in Kolkata
summary: TMC General Secretary Abhishek Banerjee alleges BJP supporters vandalised a Kolkata office on Thursday morning. He claims armed attackers ransacked the premises and demanded Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari's resignation. Banerjee stated the Kolkata Police did not respond for nearly two hours. He also cited previous attacks on TMC leaders since the BJP came to power in West Bengal on May 4.

title: Rubio warns nations against aiding Iran after Modi-Pezeshkian meeting
summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio ruled out trade talks between India and Iran following a meeting between the two leaders. Speaking on Fox News Radio, Rubio stated that President Donald Trump has made it clear that no country should help Iran evade sanctions. He warned that any nation assisting Iran in generating revenue to sponsor terrorism or build nuclear weapons will face US sanctions. Rubio noted that while countries develop their own foreign policies, helping Iran create revenue mechanisms is unacceptable.

title: Raghav Chadha claims AAP deleted his name from Punjab voter list
summary: BJP MP Raghav Chadha alleges the AAP government deleted his name from Punjab's draft voter list as political revenge. The AAP states the Election Commission handled the revision and that Chadha resides in Delhi. Chadha claims an AAP officer marked him as shifted despite guidelines requiring MPs' inclusion. The AAP says Chadha should have transferred his registration to Delhi. Punjab is currently in the third phase of the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

title: Abhishek Banerjee accuses BJP workers of vandalising TMC office; BJP denies charge
summary: TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee alleged that armed BJP men vandalised the party's Camac Street office in Kolkata early Thursday. Banerjee claimed intruders damaged equipment and took mobile phones, while BJP MLA Sajal Ghosh denied any party involvement. The TMC shared unverified CCTV footage and demanded arrests, whereas the BJP dismissed the incident as staged. Banerjee further criticized the police response and called for the Chief Minister's resignation.

title: Lumino Industries shares jump 40% after strong IPO debut
summary: Lumino Industries shares rose nearly 40% from their IPO price of Rs 82 to reach a high of Rs 114.48 on the NSE. The company's Rs 700-crore IPO was subscribed over 124 times, with qualified institutional buyers showing the highest interest. Proceeds will largely repay borrowings and fund capital expenditure. Analysts Shivani Nyati and Sunny Agrawal from Swastika Investmart and SBI Securities respectively highlighted attractive valuations and potential debt reduction benefits. However, they noted risks related to high dependence on government clients. Nyati advised partial profit booking for allottees while suggesting fresh investors wait for consolidation before buying.

title: IFCI shares rise 16% as NSE IPO approval nears
summary: IFCI shares rallied over 16% in two days as the National Stock Exchange IPO approaches. SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey stated the regulator is close to approving the draft prospectus. The exchange plans an offer-for-sale of 14.89 crore shares representing about 6% of its capital. Existing shareholders including State Bank of India and insurance companies will sell portions of their holdings. Dolat Capital Market initiated coverage with a bearish call on NSE shares in July.

title: Adobe adds AI tools and precision features to Photoshop updates
summary: Adobe is rolling out new Photoshop updates designed to simplify complex image editing while maintaining creative precision. Deepa Subramaniam, Vice President of Product Marketing for Creative Professionals at Adobe, stated the innovations provide greater choice and control. Key additions include a non-destructive Light Adjustment Layer and expanded Dynamic Text capabilities. The update also introduces an AI Assisted Editor in beta, which uses Firefly models for natural-language prompts and generative tasks. Furthermore, Adobe is launching an Instruct Edit with Masks feature that allows edits based on conversational descriptions rather than precise markings.

title: Frontline explores Uttam Kumar's legacy as West Bengal celebrates his 100th birth anniversary
summary: Frontline presents a special package marking Uttam Kumar's centenary, highlighting his enduring cultural impact on West Bengal. Contributors Madhuja Mukherjee, Moinak Biswas, Anindya Sengupta, and Suhrid Sankar Chattopadhyay offer new perspectives on his craft and representation of Bengaliness. The collection includes an interview with actor Ranjit Mallick and excerpts from Sayandeb Chowdhury's book on the star's life.

title: Sensex and Nifty rebound after three loss sessions amid oil and tension fears
summary: Indian stock indices Sensex and Nifty posted a partial recovery on Thursday following three consecutive sessions of losses. The rebound remained fragile due to elevated oil prices and renewed Middle East tensions. GIFT Nifty futures indicated a positive start, while the Sensex traded over 188 points higher. Analysts noted that investor sentiment deteriorated as fighting between the US and Iran escalated. Brent crude remained near $96 per barrel despite President Trump's comments on the conflict.

title: Uttam Kumar's enduring legacy shines in Bengali cinema and culture
summary: The article explores how Uttam Kumar remains a defining figure in Bengali cinema decades after his death. Critics found the 2024 film Oti Uttam apathetic, yet it became a box-office hit that proved his magic still enchants audiences. Uttam Kumar died in 1980 at age 53, but his name remains synonymous with Bengali cinema and culture. His career began with eight flops between 1948 and 1952 before he achieved stardom with Basu Paribar in 1952. He formed an iconic pairing with Suchitra Sen, appearing together in 30 films over 22 years. Unlike many stars, Uttam played darker, flawed characters and took supporting roles for artistic reasons. Satyajit Ray cast him in Nayak, portraying a middle-class youth, and later in Chiriyakhana as Byomkesh Bakshi. Soumitra Chatterjee acknowledged Uttam's unmatched popularity, comparing their rivalry to rival football clubs. Uttam represented the honest, middle-class Bengali man and became a symbol of Bengaliness. His mass adulation is compared to that of Rudolph Valentino in Hollywood. As Satyajit Ray noted, there will never be another like Uttam Kumar.

title: Critics say Bill Simmons promoting ChatGPT betrays his legacy of championing human creativity
summary: An article argues that Bill Simmons's promotion of ChatGPT contradicts his history of supporting human writers. The author notes Simmons recently used the AI tool to sponsor a podcast episode and answer questions about Russell Westbrook. Critics highlight that large language models are reducing website traffic and threatening creative industries. Simmons founded Grantland in 2011 to encourage ambitious writing, but The Ringer now produces few articles daily. Recent layoffs of staff writers like Claire McNear and Miles Surrey further illustrate the shift away from written content. Employees have expressed discomfort with Simmons's AI usage, yet he continues to advocate for the technology. The piece concludes that Simmons's actions undermine the quality-focused culture he once established.

title: Child abuse survivor sues xAI alleging Grok generated illegal images from her photos
summary: A child sexual abuse survivor has filed a lawsuit against Elon Musk's artificial intelligence company, xAI, alleging that its Grok chatbot used her existing abuse images to create new illegal content.
