The complaint, filed in a California district court, accuses the company of ingesting child sexual abuse material into its datasets and failing to implement standard safeguards. Attorneys for the plaintiff, identified as Jane Doe, state that the Canadian Centre for Child Protection used digital fingerprints to identify the AI-generated images on the X platform. This case differs from previous suits because it involves the generation of new abuse material from pre-existing illegal images rather than non-explicit photos. The plaintiff's legal team argues that AI technology now allows for the creation of infinite new abusive images, causing ongoing trauma to the victim. Neither xAI nor SpaceX, which acquired the company, responded to requests for comment regarding the allegations.

title: Hugging Face launches funes to give coding agents durable local memory
summary: Hugging Face introduces funes, a tool that transforms coding agent session logs into durable, queryable memory. The software indexes traces locally without requiring external accounts or hosted models. It supports multiple agents like Claude Code and Codex while preserving raw evidence from original turns. The tool allows users to bind memories to specific projects for sharing across machines and teams. Benchmarks show recall is significantly cheaper than traditional handoffs or compaction methods. Hugging Face states the project is open source and relies on existing infrastructure like Lance datasets.

title: Author reproduces watercolour painting model using TRL and OpenEnv
summary: An author reproduces a viral watercolour painting project originally created by Surya Narreddi, implementing the full training pipeline using TRL and OpenEnv. The implementation relies on a JavaScript library called p5.brush to generate code that simulates watercolour effects. The training process utilizes a reward system combining a general preference model and a custom pairwise judge based on a hand-rated pool of 178 model-generated paintings. Three distinct training runs were executed to compare different reward mix weights, with results showing that incorporating the custom judge improved style alignment and paint coverage. The author notes that while the model successfully learned to avoid blank canvases, the output remains stylistically similar to the reference pool due to the single-subject nature of the dataset. Technical adjustments were required to adapt the training configuration for the specific Qwen model architecture used. The entire project, including scripts, environments, and trained models, is published openly on Hugging Face for reproduction.

title: University Startups launches agentic AI tool for disability transition planning
summary: University Startups has launched Trinity, an agentic AI solution designed to help students with disabilities create personalized postsecondary transition plans. The tool automates the creation of legally mandated Individualized Education Programs (IEPs) by guiding students through conversations about their goals and strengths. To address scaling challenges, the company partnered with g/d/n/a to build a multi-agent architecture on AWS that separates specialized tasks like college and employment recommendations. This system retrieves data from over 30,000 college records and 1,000 occupations while maintaining strict HIPAA and FERPA compliance through field-level encryption. Trinity currently serves districts in more than a dozen U.S. states and is expanding into Saudi Arabia and Kuwait. Educators report the platform reduces IEP planning time to under ten minutes while increasing student agency.

title: Climate scientist tracks energy use of agentic AI prompts
summary: Climate scientist Zeke Hausfather tracked the energy consumption of his AI usage over eight weeks. He found that his median agentic AI prompt used approximately 150 kilowatt-hours, roughly 600 times more than a standard chatbot query. Hausfather noted that while his personal usage was small, aggregate AI demand could reach 12% of U.S. electricity by 2030. The study highlights a significant increase in energy use as AI shifts from simple conversations to complex, multi-agent tasks.

title: Author Andrew Stellman explains why AI attribution remains legally risky
summary: Author Andrew Stellman discusses the challenges of attributing AI-generated content to its human sources. He notes that while a court settlement may soon pay him and others for work used to train Claude, he values credit over the financial compensation. Stellman argues that current legal frameworks create a paradox where providing attribution could expose AI companies to lawsuits for willful infringement. He explains that while technical methods like TracIn can trace model influences, legal fears prevent labs from publicly sharing these findings. The author suggests that AI systems should instead point users to authoritative sources rather than claiming specific training data origins. He concludes that the primary barrier to attribution is not mathematical complexity but the threat of litigation under current copyright laws.

title: Schools Reinstating Phone Bans See No Academic Improvement
summary: Schools are increasingly reinstating cell phone bans, yet recent data suggests these policies fail to boost test scores or reduce bullying. A study by Stanford University and the National Bureau of Economic Research found virtually no impact on academic performance in schools enforcing bans for three years. Jason Baron, a co-author at Duke University, noted that while banning phones seems logical, students may simply doodle or daydream instead of paying attention. The research indicates that removing devices does not guarantee improved focus or learning outcomes.

title: PhD holder refuses AI training job after interview by machine
summary: A South African academic researcher declined a job offer to train an AI system designed to replace teaching and assessment roles. The author, who recently completed a Ph.D. on AI in agriculture, was interviewed by an AI system rather than a human recruiter. Despite the role offering 600 rand per hour in a country with high youth unemployment, the researcher stopped pursuing the position after the AI suggested retaking an assessment. The article highlights a growing trend where skilled professionals in Africa are recruited to transfer judgment and expertise to machines that may eventually automate their work. The author questions the ethics of handing over pedagogical judgment to algorithms and continues seeking traditional academic employment.

title: Flock Safety faces scrutiny over AI search tools used by police
summary: WIRED analyzed Flock Safety's AI-powered surveillance software, which allows police to search video feeds using written descriptions of people. The company recently implemented new safeguards after facing backlash over misuse, including a Texas deputy searching 83,000 cameras for a woman who had an abortion. However, experts warn that Flock's guardrails may discourage but not stop abusive uses. The AI model, running on Flock's servers, decides which descriptions officers can search for without departmental oversight. While the system blocks searches based on race and religion, it only warns against political and cultural expression, a category experts say is heavily protected under the First Amendment. Flock states that officers cannot run prohibited searches, but the company did not explain how warnings are triggered for religion and nationality. Data flows both ways, with Flock receiving officer search queries and subsequent actions, though the company did not disclose how long these records are kept. Over 46 of 50 recent officer misconduct cases involving license plate readers involved Flock. Flock claims local agencies set rules, but critics argue the technology enables mass surveillance that requires structural reform beyond targeting individual bad actors.

title: BBC journalist rides UKs first self-driving Uber robotaxi in London
summary: Uber launched the UKs first self-driving minicab service in London on Thursday. The company operates 15 autonomous vehicles, each requiring a human safety driver. Fares match standard UberX, Electric, or Comfort rates. BBC journalist Zoe Kleinman became the first British reporter to test the ride.

title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Adds Builders Stage for Startup Scaling Strategies
summary: TechCrunch announces the return of the Builders Stage at its Disrupt 2026 conference, scheduled for October 13-15 at the Moscone Center in San Francisco. The event targets founders, investors, and operators seeking practical advice on scaling startups through candid conversations and case studies. Over 10,000 attendees are expected to join sessions covering fundraising, hiring, go-to-market strategies, and AI integration. The agenda features industry leaders like Grant Lee of Gamma and Robby Stein of Google discussing specific challenges such as competing for AI talent and navigating the Series A landscape in 2027. Speakers will address how product decisions must evolve at scale and how companies can achieve viral growth while maintaining retention. The stage also explores M&A as an early-stage strategy and the psychological demands of founding a high-growth company. Ticket prices are set to increase, prompting organizers to encourage early registration. The event aims to provide actionable insights for building companies that can transition from seed funding to significant market traction.

title: Palo Alto Networks Acquires AI Startup Console for $500 Million
summary: Palo Alto Networks acquired Console, an AI startup, for $500 million in cash and stock, sources say. The deal values Console at $157 million, providing a rapid return for investors including CEO Nikesh Arora. Palo Alto Networks plans to integrate Console into its Cortex platform to enhance autonomous security capabilities. This acquisition marks the cybersecurity firm's seventh purchase in 2026.

title: ADB Proposes $259.91 Million Project To Expand Solar And Low-Carbon Power In Bangladesh's CHT
summary: The Asian Development Bank proposed a $259.91 million project to expand low-carbon power infrastructure in Bangladesh's Chattogram Hill Tracts. The initiative aims to increase electricity access from 49% to 68% by 2032 and connect 88,000 additional households. Funding includes a $175 million concessional loan from ADB and contributions from the Government of Bangladesh and the Bangladesh Power Development Board. The project will construct six new substations, upgrade existing infrastructure, and install solar-powered systems for water and community facilities. It also plans to establish digital complaint centers, childcare facilities, and support sustainable livelihoods through training and business incubation.

title: Chinese inverter makers stress compliance as US restrictions widen
summary: Chinese inverter and battery storage manufacturers are adopting cautious strategies as U.S. restrictions expand. The FCC added foreign inverters to a covered list in July and widened the scope in August. President Trump signed an executive order on August 26 declaring a national emergency over foreign bulk-power equipment. Sungrow stated its U.S. business may gradually shrink amid geopolitical uncertainty. Other suppliers like Ginlong Solis and Deye reported minimal U.S. revenue exposure. Companies plan to shift resources to other markets while exploring cooperation with overseas partners. The industry faces long-term uncertainty regarding future product approvals and market access.

title: ACEN and Yanara secure $37.4 million financing for Sual Solar project
summary: ACEN and Yanara secured a $37.4 million financing facility from RCBC to build the 75 MW Sual Solar project in Pangasinan. The deal, arranged through Renovable Earth Corp, marks a key step toward financial close for the venture. Once operational, the plant will generate enough power for 69,000 homes annually. The project aims to prevent 86,000 tons of CO2 emissions yearly while creating 1,500 jobs during construction.

title: Global Refining Disruptions May Keep Fuel Prices High Through 2027
summary: Analysts warn that damaged refineries in the Middle East and Russia will likely sustain elevated global fuel prices into 2027. The International Energy Agency reports that global refining capacity remains nearly 5 million barrels per day below year-ago levels. Experts state that rebuilding lost capacity will take years, leaving crude oil surplus but unable to reach the market. Phillips 66 executives note that approximately 8.4 million barrels per day of refining capacity are currently offline due to conflict-related damage.

title: Hitachi Energy secures C4-FN gas supply from Daikin for SF6-free switchgear
summary: Hitachi Energy has signed a long-term agreement with Daikin Industries to secure C4-FN gas for its SF6-free switchgear. Daikin will manufacture the specialty gas at a Frankfurt facility starting in 2027. This move adds European capacity to Hitachi's existing Asian sources to improve supply resilience. Hitachi Energy reports that its EconiQ equipment can cut CO2-equivalent emissions by 99% compared to conventional SF6-insulated equipment. The company has recorded over 4,000 EconiQ orders across 40 countries.

title: Chinese scientists build 27.39%-efficient inverted perovskite solar cell using new molecular design
summary: A Chinese research group developed a steric-gated dual-site chelation strategy to improve perovskite solar cell efficiency and stability. Lead author Cong Chen explained that their ADA-DA additive passivates defects while maintaining charge transport. The team achieved 27.39% efficiency in a single cell and 22.33% in a bifacial module. Independent verification confirmed these results, and the modules retained 99.6% power output after 5,000 hours of testing.

title: Poland confirms all foundations are in place for Bałtyk 2 and 3 nuclear plants
summary: Poland has confirmed that all foundations are in place for the Bałtyk 2 and 3 nuclear power projects. The announcement marks a significant milestone in the country's nuclear energy expansion plans. Officials stated that construction can now proceed to the next phase.

title: Comodule unveils Astra tracker for e-bikes with 12-month battery life
summary: Comodule has unveiled Astra, a new anti-theft device designed to keep e-bikes protected for up to 12 months. The Estonia-based company states that smarter power management allows the hardware to remain trackable during long storage periods. Astra features improved location technology including Wi-Fi Locate and Cat-1bis cellular connectivity for better indoor and urban accuracy. Riders can access live location, smart locking, and electronic immobilization through an app or manufacturer integration. Comodule reports its technology has already connected more than 850,000 light electric vehicles over the last 11 years. The company is currently offering demonstrations to manufacturers developing model year 2028 e-bikes.

title: Low European Gas Stocks Spark Winter LNG Competition With Asia
summary: Europe faces critically low gas storage levels, prompting a fierce competition for limited LNG supplies with Asia ahead of winter. Analysts warn that blocked shipments from Qatar and high demand could intensify the global fight for fuel. Current storage stands at 66%, requiring over $8.1 billion in purchases to reach safety targets. ING strategists note that while Europe currently attracts spot LNG, competition is expected to rise significantly if Qatari cargoes remain absent through year-end.

title: Ford aims to sell 100,000 Fathom EV trucks in first year
summary: Ford has set an internal goal to sell 100,000 Fathom electric trucks in the model's first year of sales. People familiar with the matter told the Wall Street Journal that production will begin in Q1 2027. The vehicle is expected to start under $30,000, positioning it as a top-selling non-Tesla EV. Ford plans to use lessons from the Ford Lightning to keep costs down.

title: Marine Heat Waves Threaten Ocean Life as Temperatures Hit Records
summary: Experts report that 82 percent of the world's oceans are currently experiencing marine heat waves, with this year setting new temperature records. Global Climate Risks states these events are becoming more common, intense, and widespread, driven by anthropogenic warming that has absorbed over 90 percent of excess heat. NOAA scientists note that warming has tripled the number of extreme heat days since 1940. The article details how acute heat waves differ from gradual warming by causing rapid ecosystem shifts, such as coral bleaching affecting 84 percent of reef areas and massive algal blooms. Historical data from the 2014-2016 'Blob' illustrates severe impacts, including a 20 percent drop in humpback whales and the collapse of kelp forests. Catherine Gregory of the University of Bern describes current conditions as the most extreme in the Western Mediterranean and Pacific regions. Scientists warn that the current El Niño event may expand these heat waves, compounding damage to marine species like seabirds and sea lions.

title: Trump EPA Proposes Rules Limiting State Power Over Energy Pipelines
summary: The Trump administration is proposing new Clean Water Act regulations that would restrict state and tribal authority to block energy projects like pipelines. EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin argues these rules prevent states from improperly vetoing projects based on non-water-quality factors. Environmental advocates warn the changes will significantly reduce federal water protections. The proposal specifically narrows state reviews to point source discharges and limits tribal participation to those with full water quality standards programs. The EPA states these measures are necessary to ensure legal compliance and support cooperative federalism. If finalized, the rules could impact upcoming projects such as the Constitution Pipeline in New York.

title: Homestead resumes power shutoffs for unpaid bills amid summer heat
summary: Homestead, Florida, has aggressively resumed disconnecting electricity for nonpayment as record summer heat intensifies. Assistant city manager Crystal Ollivierre stated the city collected over $8 million in outstanding bills from more than 9,000 delinquent accounts. Data shows over 1,300 customers were disconnected between March and mid-August, a sharp increase from 68 shut-offs in 2025. Experts note Florida lacks statewide protections against disconnections during extreme heat, unlike 25 other states. The crackdown coincides with increased ICE enforcement, causing undocumented farmworkers to avoid work and further strain household finances. While the city offers payment plans and up to $500 in forgiveness, residents like Mirella Estrada report the terms create significant financial pressure during dangerous heat waves.

title: Heerema finishes foundation work for Poland's Bałtyk 2 and 3 wind farms
summary: Heerema Marine Contractors completed installing 100 wind turbine foundations and two substation jackets for the Bałtyk 2 and Bałtyk 3 offshore wind farms in Poland. The company said the four-month campaign utilized the semi-submersible crane vessel Thialf and nearly 35 support vessels. Jointly developed by Equinor and Polenergia, the 1.44GW project is expected to power over two million households. First power is anticipated in 2027, with full commercial operations planned for 2028.

title: OWC-Led Consortium to Perform Feasibility Study for Morocco's First Offshore Wind Farm
summary: An OWC-led consortium will conduct a feasibility study for Morocco's first offshore wind farm. The project aims to assess technical and economic viability for the country's emerging renewable energy sector.

title: Climate Change Is Altering Summer Traditions Across the United States
summary: A collection of Grist staff writers report that climate change is eroding traditional summer experiences across the United States. The authors describe how rising temperatures, erratic rainfall, and increased wildfire smoke are disrupting seasonal norms from the Southwest to the Midwest. In Arizona, monsoon rains have become less predictable, while Texas faces unrelenting heat and poor air quality that limit outdoor activities. Colorado mountain resorts see more tourists despite drought and smoke, yet the experience feels less blissful. Montana rivers run lower earlier in the season, creating overcrowding and safety concerns for floaters. California is losing its iconic coastal fog, and the Pacific Northwest is installing air conditioning as heat domes become more frequent. Illinois experienced record tornadoes and smoke, while Tennessee farmers struggle with extreme heat and shifting plant zones. The writers note that these changes threaten the reliability of summer traditions like swimming, hiking, and gardening. As the planet warms, the distinct seasonal markers that once defined summer are becoming harder to find. The article highlights that these shifts affect both daily leisure and agricultural livelihoods. Ultimately, the authors argue that the summer many Americans know is slipping away due to a warming climate.

title: Swiss scientists use fiber optic cables to detect icequakes in glaciers
summary: Researchers in Switzerland have deployed distributed acoustic sensing technology to monitor hydrofracturing in an alpine glacier. Thomas Hudson, a seismologist at ETH Zurich, led the team that laid fiber optic cables in a grid pattern to detect vibrations. The system functions like thousands of seismometers, identifying over a thousand icequakes in just one week. This method allows scientists to track how meltwater deepens cracks and compromises structural integrity without risking personnel safety. Hudson noted that while the technology offers unprecedented data, converting these signals into an accurate early-warning system for catastrophic collapses remains challenging. The findings suggest similar processes occur in Greenland and Antarctica, where warming waters and calving events accelerate melting. Understanding these mechanisms is critical for predicting sea level rise and protecting infrastructure near unstable ice sheets.

title: UK budget relies on rainforest loan to fund bus fare cap
summary: The article claims the UK government uses a rainforest loan to finance a bus fare cap. It states this financial strategy requires greater transparency. The text notes the funding connects climate finance with domestic transport costs.

title: Climate groups criticize EU gas-favoring German capacity market design
summary: Environmental organizations ClientEarth and Beyond Fossil Fuels criticize the European Commission's approval of Germany's new capacity market design. The European Commission approved the mechanism on September 2, allowing Germany to proceed with auctions starting September 9. ClientEarth lawyer Stéphanie Nieuwbourg described the decision as astonishing, noting the design effectively subsidizes fossil fuel gas generation. The mechanism is estimated to cost between €15.6 billion and €35.2 billion over its lifetime. Critics argue the rules exclude batteries and demand response from the initial 9GW tenders, favoring gas plants with higher capacity credits. While the Commission deemed the aid appropriate, ClientEarth plans to examine the approval process and its potential market-distorting effects. Industry voices warn that current designs lock in gas capacity while reducing revenues for storage assets.

title: Hyundai breaks ground on Louisiana steel mill amid green energy questions
summary: Hyundai is breaking ground this week on a nearly $6 billion steel mill in Ascension Parish, Louisiana, scheduled to open in 2029. The facility will initially operate on natural gas, producing significantly less carbon than traditional coal mills but still generating harmful air pollution. Kimberly Terrell of the Environmental Integrity Project stated the plant will be a major source of regulated pollutants, while local resident Courtney Harris expressed concern over long-term community costs. Hyundai-Posco Louisiana Steel claims its products will have a carbon footprint 70% lower than conventional methods and that the company meets all environmental standards. Experts note that while the gas-fueled design is cleaner than coal, the industry is currently moving toward direct-reduced-iron production due to cost and efficiency, with green hydrogen remaining a future goal rather than an immediate reality.

title: New York Governor Hochul pushes historic nuclear expansion plan
summary: Governor Kathy Hochul has launched a major initiative to build five gigawatts of new nuclear power plants, aiming to make New York the third-largest state in nuclear capacity. The plan involves the New York Power Authority (NYPA) leading efforts to reduce construction costs and secure financing for these long-term infrastructure projects. While Hochul argues this strategy ensures reliable power and economic growth, critics including NY Renews and state lawmakers oppose the move, favoring wind and solar alternatives. The initiative faces significant hurdles, including a liberalized electricity market that makes financing capital-intensive projects difficult for private developers. Despite political pushback and concerns over costs and safety, the state has already partnered with Ontario to explore small modular reactor designs.

title: Europe shifts renewable energy value toward flexibility
summary: The article states that Europe's renewables expansion is shifting value toward flexibility. It notes this trend without citing specific sources or data points. The text focuses on the changing dynamics of the energy sector.

title: 26 Million Canadians Faced Climate Impacts in 930 Communities This Year
summary: The #ElbowsUp for Climate campaign reports that over 26 million Canadians in more than 930 communities have experienced climate impacts so far this year. The new map documents extreme heat, unsafe air quality, flooding, and other hazards affecting the majority of the population. Campaign co-chair David Miller stated that evacuation preparations have become normalized, linking economic threats with climate disasters. The group is calling for federal investment in clean energy and a national resilience strategy.

title: Opinion: Public Risk Assessment Could Replace Impact Rules for Canada's $280 Billion Projects
summary: Stephen Hazell argues that Canada needs a new approach to assessing risks for major projects after the Carney government rolled back environmental laws. The author warns that the $280-billion subsidy commitment for pipelines, LNG terminals, and other infrastructure lacks sufficient public scrutiny. Hazell suggests that the Major Projects Office may lack the capacity to properly evaluate ecological and fiscal dangers without transparent engagement. He proposes public risk assessment as a second-best alternative to impact assessment to prevent financial and ecological calamity. This framework would require independent expertise and Indigenous participation before federal funding is finalized.

title: China's CO2 Emissions Fall in Q2 2026 as Oil Use Drops
summary: China's carbon dioxide emissions fell by 1% in the second quarter of 2026, driven primarily by a sharp decline in oil consumption rather than coal reductions. The National Bureau of Statistics reports that oil use dropped 9% overall, with transport consumption falling 16% amid disruptions to supply from the Strait of Hormuz. Electric vehicles and public transport became key factors in this shift, with EV usage surging to displace significant amounts of fuel. Despite a rebound in coal-fired power generation, total emissions decreased because the reduction in oil use outweighed the increase from coal. The analysis highlights that structural changes in transportation, including increased EV adoption and charging volumes, played a major role in reducing oil demand. However, power sector emissions rose 3.0% in the first half of 2026 due to curtailment of solar and wind output, which forced greater reliance on coal. Government plans released in the quarter signal a higher bar for new coal projects but also allow for increased renewable curtailment limits in some provinces. While emissions remain below their 2023-24 peak, the trend reflects a complex balance between slowing energy demand growth and the continued expansion of clean energy capacity.

title: Study Shows Methane Cuts Essential To Limit Warming Below 2°C
summary: Researchers published a study in Communications Earth & Environment arguing that limiting global warming to well below 2°C requires stringent methane reductions alongside net-zero CO2 targets. The authors report that even under ambitious national net-zero goals, failing to cut methane leads to peak warming exceeding 1.85°C. Their analysis indicates that to stay under 1.7°C with a 2050 net-zero CO2 target, methane emissions must fall by at least 69% by 2050. Conversely, current policies project a 20% methane increase by 2050, which would push peak warming above 2°C regardless of CO2 efforts. The team suggests decoupling methane and CO2 metrics to clarify necessary emission cuts. They find that meeting the Global Methane Pledge could reduce peak warming by 0.15°C, with 0.05°C achievable at no net cost.

title: Tesla prepares Cybercab launch event in Austin with limited details
summary: Tesla will unveil its two-seater Cybercab at an event in Austin on Thursday, according to reports. CEO Elon Musk describes the autonomous vehicle as essential for transforming the company into a dominant force in driverless transportation. The electric-vehicle maker has expanded its robotaxi service to several cities in Texas and Florida since June 2025. Analysts view driverless vehicles as central to Tesla's future, though regulatory hurdles and slower-than-expected growth remain concerns.

title: France begins road tests of Tesla FSD vehicles
summary: French Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot announced that France has started testing two Tesla vehicles equipped with Full Self Driving technology. The ministry aims to verify data from the Netherlands and Tesla before a potential European Union vote next month or early December. Officials expect results by mid to late September to inform the decision on approving the system across the bloc.

title: Uber, PayPal, Apple, and others cut over 6,300 tech jobs in days
summary: Layoff.fyi reports that more than 6,300 tech jobs were eliminated in just a few days. Uber reduced its workforce by 10% while PayPal cut 2,200 positions globally, with over 1,000 losses occurring in India. These moves reflect broader restructuring plans and cost-cutting measures across the technology sector amid an AI boom.

title: World Bank warns demographic wave makes job creation urgent
summary: The World Bank Group reports that a record 1.2 billion young people are set to reach working age in emerging markets and developing economies by 2035. Sub-Saharan Africa is expected to account for more than three-quarters of the global working-age population increase through 2050, adding 625 million people. The authors note that high youth unemployment rates in regions like MENA and sub-Saharan Africa could turn a potential demographic dividend into a drag on development. Fiscal constraints and high public debt in these regions limit the scope for public spending on job creation. The report argues that policies focusing on infrastructure, a business-enabling environment, and mobilizing private capital are critical to addressing this global jobs challenge.

title: New York Fed economist discusses financial innovation risks at Jackson Hole
summary: New York Fed economist Kartik B. Athreya shares takeaways from the Jackson Hole symposium regarding financial innovation in payments. The author reports that central banks are examining how blockchain technology and smart contracts might alter traditional payment systems. Athreya notes that while these innovations offer benefits like real-time transactions, they also pose risks to consumer well-being and non-bank financial institutions. The economist highlights New York Fed research on stablecoins, warning that digital assets remain vulnerable to runs and shocks similar to traditional bank deposits. Furthermore, the post explores how a shift to stablecoins could impact banks' ability to gather information and lend capital. Athreya concludes that regulators must carefully evaluate whether new payment tools facilitate necessary transactions or merely transfer risks to the public.

title: House Republicans criticize president's tariff strategy in closed meeting
summary: House Republicans expressed frustration with President Trump's tariff policies during a closed-door meeting with US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer. Lawmakers discussed the US-Canada trade war and the removal of beef tariffs, with Rep. Zach Nunn noting the need to address constituents. Representatives described Greer as receptive to their critiques and planned to raise concerns at an upcoming White House dinner.

title: Author argues AI growth offsets labor share decline
summary: The author argues that high AI-driven growth can offset a falling labor share of income, reducing the need for redistribution. The analysis shows that even if labor's share drops significantly, aggregate worker income can remain stable if the economy expands rapidly. Three scenarios illustrate this: an econ-pessimist view requiring 2.7% GDP transfers, an econ-optimist view needing no transfers, and a techno-optimist view requiring only 5.3% transfers despite a 22.9% labor share. The author notes that compensation could involve shifting taxes rather than raising rates. While individual workers may still face job losses, the overall compensation problem is manageable if productivity growth is substantial. The author concludes that growth is beneficial and that labor share alone does not determine AI's distributional impact.

title: Ludlow Food Festival organizers warn rising costs threaten current format
summary: Ludlow Food Festival organizers state that rising costs and economic pressures make the event's current format unsustainable without increased visitor numbers. The 32nd annual festival, held at Ludlow Castle from September 11 to 13, features over 100 exhibitors and various entertainment options. Organizers note that while the event survived previous downturns, it now faces a critical crossroads regarding its future structure. To attract more attendees, the festival has introduced new features including a food theatre, cookery school, and children's workshops.

title: Saudi AI firm HUMAIN launches large global venture capital fund this year
summary: Saudi AI firm HUMAIN plans to launch a large global venture capital fund this year, according to CEO Tareq Amin. The fund will operate offices in the US, Saudi Arabia, France, and the UK to accelerate investment pace. HUMAIN will only back companies that commit to using Saudi data centers or bringing staff to the country. The firm has already secured a 16 gigawatt power commitment and signed agreements with US tech giants for semiconductor supply. CEO Amin stated that data centers are treated like critical national infrastructure due to the US-Iran war, requiring hardened security defenses. HUMAIN has not slowed demand from AI companies, noting its compute costs are about 30% cheaper than elsewhere globally.

title: Sensex drops over 400 points in final five minutes on F&O expiry
summary: The benchmark BSE Sensex index fell more than 400 points during the final five minutes of Thursday's trading session. The decline occurred during the closing auction session on the monthly derivatives expiry day. The index slipped from 76,554.20 to 76,152.86 between 3:25 pm and 3:30 pm. Sensex eventually closed at 76,152.86, down 417.49 points or 0.55 per cent from its previous close.

title: UK homeowners report property damage from recent heatwaves
summary: The article seeks information from UK homeowners regarding property damage potentially caused by recent heatwaves. It explains that dry spells on clay-rich soil can cause foundations to drop and lead to structural problems. The text asks readers to share experiences with subsidence, cracks, or insurance claims. It also provides links for submitting details or reading terms and privacy policies.

title: Trump $1 coin makes him first living president on US currency in a century
summary: The US Mint launched a $1 coin featuring Donald Trump's portrait to celebrate America's 250th anniversary. The Mint stated the coins are legal tender but not currently in circulation. Federal law usually prohibits living presidents from appearing on currency, but a specific design clause allowed this exception. The coins are made of copper, zinc, manganese, and nickel, not gold. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent also announced plans for a new $250 bill with Trump's portrait.

title: Article traces midlife crisis concept from Dante to psychologist Elliott Jaques
summary: This article explores the historical origins of the midlife crisis concept. It notes that Dante Alighieri wrote about a dark forest at age 35 in the early 1300s. Psychologist Elliott Jaques later identified a crisis arriving punctually at age 35 in the late 1950s. The text uses Dante's Inferno as a model for Jaques' theory about reaching the summit of life.

title: Reader's Digest ranks five affordable fall destinations for budget travelers
summary: Reader's Digest recently released a report ranking the most affordable vacation destinations based on the estimated cost of a three-night trip for two adults. The study considered lodging, airfare, meals, and drinks to provide a broader sense of weekend expenses. While actual costs depend on location and travel timing, the list offers budget-conscious travelers options with diverse attractions. Concord, North Carolina, combines shopping, outdoor fun, and family attractions. Phoenix, Arizona, pairs desert adventure with big-city museums and dining. Macon, Georgia, appeals to music and history lovers with its museums and cultural sites. Brownsville, Texas, provides a coastal alternative to inland Texas cities. These destinations prove that a memorable autumn getaway does not require a significant financial investment.

title: Gloria Steinem, influential feminist journalist and activist, dies at 92
summary: Gloria Steinem, a pioneering American feminist and journalist, has died at the age of 92. Her family announced her peaceful passing at her New York City home, noting her lifelong dedication to equality. Steinem utilized rigorous journalism and activism to bring feminist perspectives into the mainstream, campaigning against issues ranging from domestic violence to the Vietnam War. Her career included undercover work for Esquire magazine and co-founding Ms. magazine in 1971. Throughout her life, she addressed the intersection of race and sexism while facing criticism for her past support of Bill Clinton and initial stance on transgender rights. Steinem remained active in politics until her death, co-chairing the 2017 Women's March on Washington and expressing hope to live to 100 just before her passing.

title: Trump administration supports OpenAI in New York Times copyright lawsuit
summary: The Trump administration filed court papers supporting OpenAI in its copyright dispute with the New York Times. The Justice Department argued that training AI models on internet content promotes public benefits and national security. The New York Times stated the administration favors AI companies at the expense of creators. The lawsuit involves claims that OpenAI uses journalistic work without permission or payment. Other news organizations and writers have also joined the legal challenge against OpenAI.

title: Democrats urge DHS funding for election security; Gloria Steinem dies
summary: Senators Alex Padilla and Joseph Morelle wrote to Homeland Security officials demanding the release of $39.6 million for election security. The letter highlights concerns that the Trump administration has treated election security as a political issue while cutting federal funding. Meanwhile, journalist Gloria Steinem has died at age 92 after a lifetime of fighting for gender equality. Steinem co-founded Ms. magazine and remained active in women's rights advocacy well into her nineties. NPR also reported on undercounted heat-related deaths and a housing market surge in San Francisco driven by the AI boom.

title: Trump calls Iran strikes a love tap amid fears of wider war
summary: President Donald Trump dismissed recent Iranian attacks on US targets as a "love tap" after American forces conducted heavy retaliatory strikes. The exchange marks the most significant conflict between Tehran and Washington since July, raising fears of renewed warfare. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth is reportedly extending troop presence in the Middle East to maintain open-ended options for the administration. Meanwhile, oil prices fell as investors weighed the risk of supply disruptions from the Strait of Hormuz. Trump faces pressure to avoid further escalation before the November midterm elections, even as his approval ratings have dropped to a record low. In related developments, the USS Abraham Lincoln docked in Thailand after nearly nine months at sea, and Iran's currency hit a record low against the dollar.

title: UN warns El Niño could be strongest in decades
summary: The World Meteorological Organization warns that the El Niño weather phenomenon is set to intensify into a very strong event by late 2024. WMO chief Celeste Saulo stated the event may be stronger than anything recorded in the past four decades, with impacts continuing through 2027. UN chief Antonio Guterres described the situation as the world entering a danger zone of extreme weather. The agency noted an exceptionally high likelihood of nearly 100 per cent that El Niño will persist through February. Saulo cautioned that the event could deliver a massive blow to global communities and economies, urging disaster management authorities and climate-sensitive sectors to prepare immediately.

title: Baby among 80 feared dead after boat adrift 26 days off Canary Islands
summary: An NGO reports at least 80 people are feared dead after a boat adrift for 26 days was found off Spain's Canary Islands. Survivors say the vessel carried over 100 people from Gambia and Mali. Maritime Rescue found 44 people and five bodies on Wednesday. The tragedy highlights rising deaths on the western Africa to Canary Islands route, which saw a 480 per cent increase in fatalities between 2019 and 2025.

title: Gloria Steinem, American feminist icon, dies at age 92
summary: The provided text contains only a headline announcing the death of Gloria Steinem. It includes a technical error message regarding a site loading issue but offers no further details about her life or career.

title: Kemi Badenoch pledges £10bn defence rise via welfare cuts
summary: Kemi Badenoch announced a plan to increase UK defence spending by £10bn annually by reducing welfare bills. She stated that strong nations must prepare for war to ensure peace, citing Poland's military expansion as an example. Badenoch defended the proposal against claims of lacking credibility, noting that defence spending had fallen from 1989 until 2022. The proposal involves cutting Local Housing Allowance rates, a move some observers note may disproportionately affect the poorest tenants. Meanwhile, Andy Burnham welcomed French President Emmanuel Macron to Downing Street to discuss UK-France collaboration. In other political news, journalist Sam Bright was banned from the Reform UK conference after reporting on anti-abortion speakers, contradicting Nigel Farage's previous free speech pledges. Additionally, Zack Polanski is considering standing as the Green Party candidate in Holborn and St Pancras.

title: Ghanaian craftsmen create elaborate coffins reflecting deceased identities
summary: Ghanaian funeral traditions feature intricately crafted coffins that symbolize the deceased's profession or passions. A musician was buried in a guitar-shaped coffin, while a teacher was laid to rest in a giant pen. Veteran coffinmaker Daniel Oblie Mensah creates these tributes, which have evolved from traditional palanquins into contemporary art pieces. Some unique coffins are displayed in museums like New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art. The industry relies on family skills but has modernized with new equipment and international commissions. These coffins typically cost around 10,000 Ghanaian cedis, though museum pieces use more durable materials.

title: Spanish PM denies Moroccan involvement in Ceuta migrant surge
summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez told lawmakers there is no evidence Morocco orchestrated the recent migrant influx into Ceuta. This statement follows a police report characterizing the event as a planned operation rather than spontaneous migration.

title: Time Out ranks Ashford Castle in Ireland as the world's most beautiful hotel
summary: Time Out magazine compiled a ranking of the world's most beautiful hotels based on visits by its experts. Ashford Castle in Ireland took the number one spot among 33 properties. The hotel features 83 rooms and a spa with a bronze conservatory. Other top European entries include Four Seasons Hotel Firenze and ION Adventure Hotel in Iceland.

title: Belgium records nearly 3,000 excess deaths during summer heatwaves
summary: Belgium health authorities report nearly 3,000 excess deaths during successive summer heatwaves. The Sciensano institute noted a 7% increase in deaths during the third heatwave between late July and mid-August. Total excess mortality reached 2,935, with the highest rate occurring in early July. Belgium confirmed summer 2026 as its hottest on record, averaging 20.3C at the Uccle station. Regional comparisons show Germany, Spain, and France also recorded high heat-related death tolls this year.

title: Kenyan President Orders Crackdown on Foreigners in Small Businesses
summary: President William Ruto ordered a crackdown on foreigners operating small-scale businesses to protect local traders. He promised to fast-track legislation restricting foreign involvement in such trades while maintaining openness to investment. The move addresses tensions between locals and migrants, including refugees, who work in Kenya's informal economy. Ruto emphasized that investors should create jobs rather than compete as hawkers. The government noted that about 857,000 refugees are registered, with many working outside camps.

title: Feminist activist Gloria Steinem dies at 92 in New York
summary: Gloria Steinem, a leading figure in the US women's liberation movement, has died at age 92. Her foundation announced she passed peacefully at her New York City home surrounded by loved ones. Steinem co-founded Ms. magazine and campaigned for reproductive rights, same-sex marriage, and equal pay throughout her career. She witnessed the recent reversal of the Roe v. Wade decision after decades of advocacy. Her foundation stated she continued working for equality until the very end.

title: Vanuatu sues France at ICJ over two Pacific islands and maritime boundaries
summary: Vanuatu has filed a legal application against France at the International Court of Justice regarding sovereignty over two disputed islands and maritime boundaries. The Prime Minister's Office stated that bilateral negotiations failed to resolve the dispute after decades of diplomatic engagement. Deputy Prime Minister Johnny Koanapo affirmed that the islands belong to the people of Vanuatu and that judicial determination offers the clearest path to resolution. The ICJ confirmed the application was transmitted to Paris but noted no action will occur until France consents to the Court's jurisdiction.

title: Senegalese consumers launch online campaign against rising living costs
summary: Senegalese consumers in Dakar have started an online campaign to protest increasing prices. The movement highlights sharp rises in meat and onion costs alongside fuel and rent hikes. Organizers launched the hashtag #30DaysForTheRightPrice to alert authorities to the situation. FRANCE 24 reports that the campaign aims to protect vulnerable households from these economic pressures.

title: Moroccan migrants in Ceuta demand right to apply for asylum
summary: Moroccan migrants in Ceuta are calling for the right to apply for asylum, arguing that other nations are permitted to do so. At least 5,000 migrants remain in the enclave after a July influx of over 70,000 people. Residents claim these individuals strain public resources while living in makeshift camps. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez accused right-wing social media accounts linked to Russia and Israel of exploiting the crisis.

title: Activist Gloria Steinem dies at 92 after decades of feminist advocacy
summary: Gloria Steinem, a prominent figure in the US women's movement, has died at age 92. Her career began as a journalist before she shifted to activism following a 1969 abortion rights speak-out. Steinem co-founded Ms. Magazine in 1972 and remained a vocal advocate for issues like genital mutilation and Korean reconciliation well into her 80s. She often spoke about overcoming her fear of public speaking to reach audiences at rallies and campuses. Steinem expressed frustration that her appearance was frequently highlighted over her work, noting that people often attributed her success to her looks rather than her efforts. She faced hostility from various quarters, including President Richard Nixon, yet continued collaborating on projects until shortly before her death.

title: Cuban families struggle with shortages as schools reopen amid crisis
summary: Cuban families face severe hardships as the new school year begins under conditions of extreme poverty and systemic shortages. The article reports that many mothers cannot afford uniforms, lack electricity for basic needs, and struggle to feed their children. Education Minister Naima Trujillo acknowledged the difficulty in meeting the demand for uniforms for nearly 1.4 million students due to a lack of power, fuel, and money. Additionally, a teacher shortage of 21,000 has reduced coverage to 73%, while low salaries drive professionals away. A recent study by the Cuban Observatory for Human Rights indicates that 94% of the population lives in extreme poverty. Despite these challenges, students attended patriotic ceremonies, though many schools operate with significant delays and resource gaps. Experts warn that the crisis is causing severe mental health effects on children and caregivers.

title: Gloria Steinem, feminist icon and journalist, dies at 92
summary: Gloria Steinem, a leading figure in the US women's movement, died at 92. Her foundation announced her peaceful passing in New York City on Wednesday. Steinem co-founded Ms. Magazine and the National Women's Political Caucus, advocating for issues like abortion rights and equal pay. She received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2013 and remained active in activism until her death.

title: Five Japanese oil distributors admit to forming a price cartel
summary: Five Japanese oil distributors admitted to forming a price cartel for gas oil at a Tokyo District Court hearing. Prosecutors stated that company officials agreed to raise prices and curb reductions between October and December 2024. The Fair Trade Commission raided eight companies, but only five were indicted under the antimonopoly law. Executives claimed meetings were necessary for dealing with powerful clients, while others admitted the practice was commonplace in the industry.

title: Algerian President Tebboune seeks death penalty for arsonists amid deadly wildfires
summary: Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune announced the reinstatement of the death penalty for arsonists following unprecedented wildfires that devastated forests and killed dozens. While official reports cite 12 deaths in Jijel, local accounts suggest the toll is far higher. Tebboune attributed the fires to climate change but also ordered investigations into criminal responsibility. The government declared the region a disaster area and mobilized resources for relief and reconstruction.

title: Everton transfer fails as Balogun withdraws over health doubts
summary: Monaco sporting director Thiago Scuro revealed that striker Folarin Balogun withdrew from a transfer to Everton due to discomfort over health concerns raised during a medical exam. The deal, valued at 40 million pounds, collapsed in the final minutes of the summer window after Everton questioned the results. Everton has faced criticism for the situation, leaving the club with limited striker options. Scuro noted that Balogun remains available for other clubs as Monaco seeks to meet financial regulations.

title: Czech President Says Russia Uses Hybrid Tactics to Divide Europe
summary: Czech President Petr Pavel told CNN that Russia employs sabotage and disinformation to undermine European trust and divide member states. He noted Moscow resorts to these hybrid tactics because it cannot launch an open attack on NATO. Pavel argued that this strategy has backfired by strengthening EU and NATO unity. Meanwhile, Czech authorities are tightening monitoring of Russian diplomats following German accusations regarding a drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport. Foreign Minister Petr Macinka and Prime Minister Andrej Babis confirmed preparations for new security measures and pledged cooperation with partners.

title: Mexico and Brazil state oil firms sign deal raising ecological concerns
summary: Pemex and Petrobras announced a two-year partnership to explore mature and deepwater oilfields in the Gulf of Mexico. Environmental campaigners warn the agreement risks decades of fossil fuel emissions and pollution near vulnerable reef habitats. The deal follows recent safety incidents at Mexican petrochemical sites, with some hoping Petrobras can share safety expertise. However, researchers note that deeper drilling increases spill risks and could displace coastal communities. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum downplayed the partnership, emphasizing renewable energy goals instead. Both companies declined to provide further details on the memorandum of understanding.

title: Pierre Damas Bel's death highlights psychological harm of ICE ankle monitors
summary: Pierre Damas Bel, a 20-year-old Haitian man, died by suicide after walking onto a highway where he was struck by a truck. His family attributes his death to the psychological distress caused by an electronic ankle monitor placed on him by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Lauren Hodges, a senior attorney at Amica, stated that such devices cause significant mental health deterioration and social stigma. The article notes that under the current administration, ICE now uses these monitors indiscriminately rather than evaluating cases individually. Bel's father reported that his son felt treated like an animal and faced harassment from peers due to the device. ICE did not comment on the cause of death while the investigation is ongoing but reiterated that undocumented immigrants can self-deport. The tragedy occurred after the termination of Temporary Protected Status for Haitians, leaving many without legal options to remain in the United States.

title: Hongkong Land seeks billion-dollar Japanese property deals amid investment pivot
summary: People familiar with the matter said Hongkong Land is pursuing over $1 billion property deals in Tokyo as part of Jardine Matheson's strategy shift. The firm has approached Blackstone and Hulic regarding specific assets in central Tokyo. However, sources noted the company faces challenges in securing suitable properties or co-investment partners during the current market cycle.

title: Colombian woman leads grassroots effort to protect Andean condors
summary: Doris Torres transformed her community's fear of Andean condors into a conservation movement. With support from the Parque Jaime Duque Foundation, she helped turn former enemies into protectors. This grassroots initiative has created a safe haven for the threatened Vultur gryphus species in Colombia.

title: Nepal flood victims' families hold symbolic cremations after eight days
summary: Eight days after Nepal's flash floods, families of missing persons performed symbolic cremations because they could not locate their loved ones. The article reports that these ceremonies took place as a way for relatives to cope with the uncertainty surrounding the disaster. NPR noted that it does not accept money for coverage or interviews regarding this event.

title: UN mediates new election agreement for divided Libyan governments
summary: United Nations mediators have secured an agreement for Libyan rival governments to hold elections within two years. The UN Support Mission in Libya stated this marks a significant step toward ending the transitional period. Experts note that while the deal resolves previous legal disagreements, its success remains uncertain. Analysts warn that past political agreements in Libya failed to be implemented. Concerns persist regarding whether elites will accept election results or divide resources instead. External powers like Russia and Turkey continue to support opposing factions in the east and west. The agreement aims to restructure the electoral commission and strengthen legal frameworks for a secure process.

title: PM Modi urges auto industry to innovate for Viksit Bharat by 2047
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers on September 3, 2026, urging the sector to innovate and expand globally. He highlighted that recent free trade agreements and infrastructure improvements are strengthening India's competitive manufacturing capabilities. The Prime Minister noted that government reforms, including the PLI scheme, have boosted the industry. He emphasized that a cleaner mobility ecosystem and rising economic demand will drive significant growth for the automobile sector by 2047.

title: AMD partners with Delhi University to train 10,000 students in AI
summary: AMD and Delhi University announced a partnership to train approximately 10,000 students in artificial intelligence and semiconductor technologies over the next year. Under the signed Memorandum of Understanding, AMD will introduce its AI Engage Developer Program to provide industry-relevant skills. Jaya Jagadish, Country Head & SVP Engineering at AMD India, stated the initiative aims to give students early access to platforms powering real-world AI development. Prof Yogesh Singh, Vice-Chancellor of Delhi University, noted the collaboration will help create a stronger pipeline of AI developers to support India's digital economy. The program offers hands-on access to AMD's ROCm AI software platform, learning resources, and developer GPU cloud credits.

title: Kharge calls Haldwani purification ritual untouchability and seeks action
summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge stated that a purification ritual at his Haldwani rally site constituted an act of untouchability. He announced his party would approach Rajya Sabha Chairman C.P. Radhakrishnan regarding the incident. Kharge criticized the silence of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah on the matter. He also questioned the rule of law after the BJP filed an FIR against Rahul Gandhi in Uttarakhand. The Congress leader urged supporters to peacefully protest against such discriminatory acts.

title: EAM Jaishankar says India ready to help end Russia-Ukraine war
summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar stated in Kyiv that India is prepared to assist in ending the Russia-Ukraine conflict in any possible manner. His remarks followed Prime Minister Narendra Modi's recent calls for a peaceful resolution during a meeting with Vladimir Putin. Jaishankar is currently on a three-day visit to Ukraine and Poland to hold bilateral consultations. The visit occurs amid heightened hostilities and concerns in New Delhi following an Indian death in Kyiv and attacks on merchant vessels.

title: BJP accuses Kerala CM Satheesan of flip-flopping after deleting video on cleric
summary: The BJP accused Kerala Chief Minister VD Satheesan of deleting a video that criticized Grand Mufti Kanthapuram AP Aboobacker Musliyar's remarks on women. The party claimed Satheesan surrendered to religious pressure from groups like Jamaat-e-Islami. Satheesan previously stated the government disagrees with the cleric's view that women should stay home. He emphasized that women must join mainstream public life in modern Kerala.

title: Microsoft reports India leads global AI agent adoption with strong oversight
summary: Microsoft's 2026 Work Trend Index finds India has the highest share of Frontier Professionals among ten markets. Puneet Chandok stated that 32 per cent of Indian AI users employ agents in multi-step workflows, double the global average. The study highlights strong leadership alignment and human oversight in Indian organizations. Major firms like Infosys and TCS show rapid enterprise adoption of Microsoft 365 Copilot. Microsoft says India's advantage combines high adoption with retained human judgment.

title: Anthropic Wins Court Case Against Military, Commerce Chief Says Company Is Back In Favor
summary: U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick stated that Anthropic is aligned with the Trump administration after a federal judge ruled in the company's favor. The judge sided with Anthropic in its legal dispute with the American military regarding AI safety on the battlefield. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had previously blocked certain military contracts because Anthropic refused to allow its models for domestic surveillance or autonomous weapons. Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown later emphasized the importance of data centers at a G20 event in North Carolina.

title: Larry Ellison stayed close to ex-wife Barbara Boothe after their 1986 divorce
summary: People.com reports that Oracle founder Larry Ellison filed for divorce from Barbara Boothe in 1986, three months after their daughter Megan was born. Ellison stated in a 2003 book that he chose to maintain a friendly relationship with Boothe for the children's wellbeing. Boothe raised the siblings and nurtured their love of cinema, amassing over 3,000 VHS tapes. This early exposure helped David Ellison found Skydance Media and Megan Ellison found Annapurna Pictures.

title: Google launches Gemini 3.8 Flash and Cyber models with new capabilities
summary: Google announced the release of Gemini 3.8 Flash and Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber. The company stated the new model works harder on complex tasks and outperforms larger frontier models on engineering benchmarks. Google also introduced the Fairwind Program, which offers the Cyber model exclusively to governments and trusted partners for infrastructure protection.

title: Microsoft reports India leads global AI workforce with 32% frontier professionals
summary: Microsoft Work Trend Index 2026 data shows India holds 32% of global frontier AI professionals, double the world average. Puneet Chandok stated these users redefine workflows while maintaining human judgment. The report highlights that 63% of Indian AI users prioritize quality control, the highest among surveyed nations. Microsoft places responsibility for enterprise adoption on leadership rather than junior staff. Chandok advises young workers to focus on shipped projects instead of degrees.

title: Autoline Industries shares rise 16% after Tata Motors PV order
summary: Autoline Industries shares jumped nearly 16% after the company announced a new business award from Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd. The order is expected to generate approximately ₹100 crore in additional annual revenue. Autoline stated the award reflects confidence in its engineering and manufacturing capabilities. The components will supply both internal combustion engine and electric vehicle models. Managing Director Shivaji Akhade emphasized the company's focus on quality and delivery.

title: Meta settles US teen lawsuits with midnight lockout; India rules differ
summary: Meta reached a settlement with US attorneys general requiring midnight-to-6 am lockouts for teens under 18. The deal includes daily usage caps and hidden like counts, effective for a decade. Meta has not announced plans to extend these specific US restrictions to India. India currently operates a narrower 10 pm to 7 am sleep mode for teen accounts. Parents in India can manually set screen-time limits and block access during specific hours.

title: Reliance Jio launches JioPC cloud service starting at Rs 1,000
summary: Reliance Jio launches JioPC, a cloud service that boosts older computers with up to 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage. The company says the setup takes less than five minutes and requires no new hardware. JioPC offers two pricing tiers starting at Rs 1,000 for two months.

title: NHRC seeks reports from MeitY, MIB, and Delhi Police on CSAM ads
summary: The NHRC bench has requested Action Taken Reports from MeitY, MIB, and Delhi Police regarding CSAM advertisements on Instagram. The commission emphasized examining the case under the POCSO Act and questioning Meta's role as an intermediary. A BBC investigation previously found Instagram promoted ads linking to explicit content. Meta stated the allegations were inaccurate and highlighted its AI detection efforts.

title: Commerce Minister Goyal says India's textile sector has no excuses left for weak exports
summary: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal stated that India's textile industry must improve performance as tariff advantages now match competitors. He highlighted that nine active FTAs cover $60 trillion in GDP, with future deals potentially accessing 75% of global trade at lower rates. Goyal noted that while Bangladesh and Vietnam previously benefited from LDC status or better trade terms, India's new tariff parity removes external excuses. The minister called for a nationwide effort to help businesses utilize these agreements to meet the $1 trillion export target.

title: New U.S. tariffs on drones take effect Thursday
summary: New U.S. tariffs on drones took effect Thursday, targeting imports to reduce reliance on China. President Donald Trump signed the order in August, citing national security threats. Drones weighing over 25 kilograms face a 100% duty, while smaller models incur a 25% charge. China opposed the move, warning it would disrupt global supply chains. DJI, which holds more than two-thirds of the global market, has previously faced U.S. restrictions.

title: India seeks tariff advantage over rivals before finalizing US trade deal
summary: Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal stated that India requires a tariff advantage over competing economies before the final US trade deal is announced. Goyal noted that India secured favorable terms in sensitive sectors like agriculture and fisheries while reporting 7.8% GDP growth for the April-June quarter. Conversely, the Congress party questioned these economic figures as statistical adjustments. Previous negotiations faced delays after the US Supreme Court struck down global tariffs, creating uncertainty about the final agreement's timeline and specific terms.

title: India delays US trade deal until preferential tariff terms are granted
summary: India will finalize its Bilateral Trade Agreement with the US only after Washington offers preferential tariff terms compared to competitors, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said. While a senior US official claimed the deal was effectively finalized in July, India insists on better rates for its exporters. The agreement aims to expand market access and deepen economic ties between the two nations.

title: El Niño threatens India's crops as drought declaration gaps persist
summary: India faces heightened drought risks as El Niño strengthens, yet systemic flaws in the declaration process leave many affected areas undetected. The 2016 drought manual relies on multiple indicators, but inconsistent implementation and staffing shortages hinder effective relief distribution. Past El Niño events reduced agricultural output by 5 to 7%, and current forecasts indicate a 14% rainfall deficit since the monsoon began. Political factors often influence drought declarations, with research showing relief may be misdirected for electoral gain. While the Indian Council on Agricultural Research advises on climate-resilient seeds, 315 districts remain vulnerable, and only 10 central financial assistance requests were made between 2020 and 2025.

title: Reduced nature exposure linked to rising immune system diseases in children
summary: The authors report that cases of immune-mediated inflammatory diseases have risen over the last two decades. They argue that a disconnect from nature contributes to immune dysregulation, potentially leading to conditions like asthma and rheumatoid arthritis. The commentary suggests today's children face greater risks due to rapid urbanization and reduced outdoor exposure. Scientists propose that the immune system requires microbial diversity from natural environments to develop proper tolerance. The authors note that urban planning strategies prioritizing green spaces could support healthier immune system development in future generations.

title: GJC urges balancing economic patriotism with cultural gold traditions
summary: The All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) responded to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's appeal for economic patriotism by emphasizing the need to balance it with cultural heritage. Rajesh Rokde, the GJC Chairman, stated that while supporting restraint on gold as an investment, jewellery consumption remains vital for culture and livelihoods. He noted the sector contributes nearly 7-8% to the economy and supports millions of jobs. As a ₹10 lakh crore industry, the GJC called for responsible growth that aligns with national priorities while respecting enduring traditions.

title: IAF plans border drills; AAP leader Satyendar Jain granted bail
summary: The Indian Air Force will hold major combat exercises near the Pakistan border in September. AAP leader Satyendar Jain was granted bail by Rouse Avenue Court in an ACB case. India reported 7.8% GDP growth in the latest quarter. A Telangana state minister was dropped amid cabinet infighting.

title: IAF schedules Veer Guardian and Tarang Shakti drills near Pakistan border
summary: The Indian Air Force plans major combat exercises near the Pakistan border in September. The India-Japan Veer Guardian drill will involve 110 Japanese personnel in Jodhpur. Multinational Exercise Tarang Shakti will include the United States and other global air forces. These drills occur ahead of the BRICS Summit in New Delhi.

title: Kerala CPI(M) faces internal dissent over electoral defeat and leadership accountability
summary: The Kerala CPI(M) is confronting significant internal dissent following a historic electoral defeat, with the party's vote share dropping to 21.77 per cent. The Central Committee acknowledged leadership failures in candidate selection and noted a widening gap between the party and its rank and file. While General Secretary MA Baby has urged cadres to speak openly about the loss, tensions remain regarding whether the leadership will accept full responsibility. The upcoming State Committee meeting in Kozhikode from September 13 to 15 is expected to test the party's commitment to self-criticism and organizational reform. Members are increasingly questioning decisions on candidate selection and the handling of communal issues, challenging the leadership to address these concerns publicly.

title: Mettur Dam water level stands at 92.14 feet
summary: The Mettur Dam water level was recorded at 92.14 feet on Thursday, significantly below the full reservoir level of 120 feet. Inflow into the dam was 8,041 cusecs while discharge was 7,000 cusecs.

title: Delhi central offices close September 11 for BRICS Summit
summary: The Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions announced that central government offices in Delhi will remain closed on September 11, 2026. This decision aims to manage extensive security and traffic arrangements for the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit. The Delhi government also declared the date a holiday for its own offices and public sector undertakings. India assumed the BRICS chairship for 2026 with a focus on resilience and sustainability.

title: War-worn USS Lincoln docks in Thailand after 286-day Middle East deployment
summary: The rusted USS Abraham Lincoln arrived in Laem Chabang, Thailand, concluding an extraordinary 286-day deployment in the Middle East. Reuters reported that the carrier and its strike group faced visible wear from prolonged combat operations against Iran. While the Pentagon disputed claims of deteriorating conditions, Naval experts noted that deferred maintenance creates significant burdens upon a ship's return. The four-to-five-day port call offers sailors their first major opportunity for rest after the historic mission. Rear Admiral Robert Loughran described the visit as a chance for personnel to recharge following truly historic accomplishments. Local businesses in Pattaya expect an economic boost from the thousands of US personnel visiting the treaty ally.

title: Bengal police arrest ex-Panihati chairman over hasty cremation in rape-murder probe
summary: West Bengal police arrested former Panihati chairman Somnath Dey in Bengaluru on charges of hastily cremating the body of a junior doctor raped and murdered at RG Kar Medical College. Police officers aware of the matter stated Dey had been absconding since June before being caught. The arrest follows earlier detentions of two other TMC leaders and a state-ordered inquiry into the cremation process. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari highlighted irregularities in the cremation schedule and lack of family documentation.

title: Lollapalooza India 2027 announces Olivia Dean and Limp Bizkit as headliners
summary: Lollapalooza India has released the complete lineup for its fifth edition, headlined by Olivia Dean and Limp Bizkit. The festival will occur on January 23 and 24 at the Mahalaxmi Racecourse in Mumbai. Ticket prices range from ₹7,999 for general access to ₹49,999 for platinum tiers. Additional performers include KATSEYE, Fontaines DC, and numerous Indian artists. Tickets are available via the official website and BookMyShow.

title: Canada investigates food fraud risks after India raids warehouse with fake labels
summary: The Canadian Food Inspection Agency is assessing risks to imports after Indian authorities raided a Mumbai warehouse seizing nearly $80,000 in food products with fake labels. Officials found chemicals and machines used to alter expiry dates and nutrition information on brands like PepsiCo and Nestle. The CFIA stated it has no evidence these specific items entered Canada but remains vigilant against food fraud. Major food companies denied involvement in the illegal export operation.

title: Pranav Constructions sets IPO price band at ₹118–124 per share
summary: Pranav Constructions has fixed the price band for its ₹351-crore IPO between ₹118 and ₹124 per share. The company said the public issue opens on September 7 and closes on September 9, with anchor investor bidding scheduled for February 4. The offering combines a fresh equity issue of ₹315.6 crore with an offer for sale of 28.57 lakh shares by BioUrja India Infra. Investors must apply for at least 120 shares, with a minimum investment of ₹14,880 at the upper price limit. Proceeds will fund redevelopment approvals, floor space index purchases, debt repayment, and general corporate expenses. The company reported revenue of ₹762 crore and net profit of ₹71 crore in FY26. Centrum Capital and PNB Investment Services are acting as lead managers for the listing on BSE and NSE.

title: Supreme Court rejects plea against UP and Rajasthan school entry restrictions
summary: The Supreme Court refused to hear a public interest litigation challenging government orders restricting outsider entry into public schools in Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan. The Bharatiya Janita Party governments in both states mandated prior permission for photography, videography, and interviews inside schools. The petitioner argued these restrictions violate fundamental rights under Articles 14, 19, and 21 of the Constitution. Live Law reported the court declined to entertain the challenge against the orders issued in August.

title: The Frontline launches a bookshelf segment featuring six new titles
summary: The Frontline introduces a new segment called The Frontline Bookshelf to highlight recommended reading. The first edition presents six books covering fiction and non-fiction topics. Selections include works by Pia Ghosh-Roy and Mithi Mukherjee. The segment aims to offer diverse stories and ideas for readers to explore.

title: Calcutta High Court asks for no coercive action against Anandabazar Patrika journalists
summary: The Calcutta High Court directed the West Bengal government to ensure no coercive steps are taken against Anandabazar Patrika journalists facing FIRs over their use of the term 'saffron hooliganism', provided they cooperate with notices. Senior Advocate S N Mookherjee argued the cases were based on allegations of incitement rather than defamation. The court emphasized that compliance with issued notices would prevent further action, while noting the newspaper's office had been painted saffron by protesters. Several press associations have also demanded the immediate withdrawal of these FIRs.

title: US stock futures rise as investors watch oil, jobs data, rates and tech earnings
summary: US stock futures rose on Thursday after a three-day decline, driven by investor attention on Middle East tensions, oil prices, jobs data, interest rates, and technology earnings. Yahoo Finance reported that Dow Jones futures gained 0.2%, while S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 futures also increased slightly. The Morning Bull noted that the 10-year US Treasury yield remained near 4.8%, keeping borrowing costs high for mortgages and corporate loans. Yahoo Finance stated that President Donald Trump announced a heavy attack on Iran, raising inflation concerns. The Morning Bull reported that Dell Technologies shares jumped 15.81% following strong earnings, while Credo Technology shares dropped 20.04% after brokers lowered price targets. Hindustan Times highlighted that investors remain cautious about the impact of high energy prices and tariffs on the economy.

title: Jharkhand youth protest over cancelled civil services exam amid irregularity claims
summary: This Frontline Insight Box examines the ongoing protest by civil services aspirants in Jharkhand following the cancellation of the JSSC-CGL examination. The Jharkhand High Court stayed the cancellation on August 18 due to allegations of examination irregularities and paper leaks. For thousands of candidates, these exams represent a critical pathway out of poverty and economic insecurity. The dispute has united protesters in their 20s and 40s over recurring institutional failures.

title: Migration is not a crisis or a cure-all. It just needs to be managed
