summary: Eleven Jawaharlal Nehru University students filed a sexual harassment complaint against a professor with the university's Internal Complaints Committee in May. University sources stated the allegations emerged after a student shared inappropriate remarks made during viva examinations in an unofficial WhatsApp group. The ICC has since called students to record statements regarding the incident. JNU administration did not respond to queries from Hindustan Times about the matter.

title: Nuvama raises HUL price target to Rs 2820 with buy rating
summary: Brokerage firm Nuvama Institutional Equities raised its Hindustan Unilever share price target to Rs 2,820 and issued a buy rating. The firm expects medium-term EBITDA margins between 22% and 24% driven by premium mix improvements and operational leverage. HUL reported a 3% decline in consolidated net profit for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, while total income rose 10% year-on-year. CEO Priya Nair noted stable underlying demand despite global geopolitical volatility.

title: Shiv Sena workers assault hospital staff over treatment bill dispute
summary: Palghar police booked 17 people, including Shiv Sena functionaries and an MLA's son, following an altercation at a private hospital. The incident occurred after a dispute over a treatment bill for injured Govinda Pathak members. CCTV footage shows Shiv Sena Palghar city chief Rahul Gharat hitting a hospital employee. An FIR has been registered under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and Maharashtra Medical Law. Kundan Sankhe stated the group sought patient discharge after minor injuries were sustained during a Dahi Handi celebration.

title: Toddler among three killed after drunk car driver hits bike in Kerala
summary: Three people, including a toddler, died after a car struck their motorcycle in Kerala's Thrissur district. Police stated the driver was allegedly drunk and is currently absconding while two passengers were taken into custody. The victims were thrown nearly 50 metres during the collision on the Guruvayur-Kunnamkulam road. News agency ANI reported the identities of the deceased as Muneer, his wife Safna, and their three-year-old son Yamil Aibak. Separately, Tamil Nadu Minister S Rajesh Kumar announced that the state assembly would discuss compensation for families affected by a recent fatal accident on a highway. Kumar noted that the government would take action after gathering full details about the incident and circumstances.

title: Two wheels derail from Mahananda Express shortly after leaving Arrah station
summary: Two wheels of the Sikkim Mahananda Express derailed shortly after departing Arrah railway station in Bihar on Sunday morning. Railway officials confirmed that no passengers were injured during the incident. Technical teams worked to restore services after train movement was disrupted for approximately three hours. Officials are currently investigating the cause of the derailment.

title: BRICS Summit in Delhi: Will Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman Attend?
summary: As BRICS leaders gather in Delhi, attention focuses on whether Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will attend the summit. India-Bangladesh relations have deteriorated significantly since Sheikh Hasina fled to India in August 2024. Bangladesh is moving closer to Pakistan and Turkey, with possible membership in the Mecca Pact. The extradition of Hasina remains a central diplomatic flashpoint between the two nations. Despite strained ties, mutual dependence on trade and a shared border keeps full rupture unlikely.

title: China unveils Type 100 tank with unmanned turret and hybrid power
summary: Military Watch Magazine reported new footage of China's Type 100 main battle tank, which features an unmanned turret and hybrid-electric propulsion. The Chinese Ministry of National Defense confirmed the vehicle was commissioned into the People's Liberation Army after its September 2025 debut. US Army assessments note the tank's networked capabilities and active protection systems designed to counter modern threats like drones.

title: FSSAI suspends licenses of Kailash Formulation and Sanecure Water Project
summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India suspended licenses for Kailash Formulation and Sanecure Water Project due to severe hygiene and compliance violations. FSSAI officials cited poor sanitation, pest infestations, and altered lab records at Sanecure. Kailash Formulation faced unsatisfactory premises conditions and missing test reports. The regulator also recently penalized CG Foods for reprocessing broken noodles without proper approvals.

title: Kunda Bachhav Receives National Teachers Award for Educational Initiatives
summary: President Droupadi Murmu conferred the National Teachers' Award 2026 on Kunda Bachhav, a teacher at Nashik Municipal School No. 18. Bachhav launched an initiative supporting over 150 girls from weaker families and transformed 30 local walls into educational spaces. She mobilized more than ₹55 lakh through community and CSR efforts to improve school infrastructure. Her innovative programs have attracted students from private schools to the municipal institution.

title: Delhi schools and offices shut on September 11 for BRICS Summit
summary: Delhi schools and government offices will remain closed on September 11, 2026, due to security arrangements for the BRICS Summit. The Directorate of Education issued a circular ordering the holiday for government and private schools. Delhi Traffic Police requested virtual court sessions at Patiala House Courts because traffic restrictions could disrupt proceedings. The summit will bring together leaders from around 30 nations at Bharat Mandapam.

title: Karnataka plans to develop existing Blue flag beaches instead of opening new ones
summary: Energy and Tourism Minister K.J. George stated the State Government intends to fully develop existing Blue flag beaches in Tannirbhavi and other coastal Karnataka locations. Officials are studying CRZ norms, road strengthening, and cruise tourism while resolving revenue disputes. The government will not open casinos but may allow beach access after 7 p.m. and support health tourism initiatives.

title: Delhi house collapse rescues four, leaves several trapped
summary: A five-storeyed student hostel collapsed in South West Delhi on Sunday afternoon. The Delhi Fire Service reported that four people were rescued in critical condition and taken to AIIMS. Rescue teams, including JCBs and student volunteers, are removing debris while police cordon off the area. Officials state that at least 30 students lived there, though the exact number of trapped individuals remains unconfirmed. The Delhi Police have not yet issued a statement regarding the cause.

title: FCNR deposit inflows strengthen rupee and lower gold prices
summary: FCNR deposit inflows of $127 billion strengthened the rupee, causing spot gold prices to fall by 4% to Rs 1,54,884 per 10 grams. The India Bullion and Jewellers Association noted that consumers often wait during price uncertainty before purchasing. Industry leaders stated that the lower prices should help demand during the upcoming festive season, though volatility may reduce average purchase sizes. Experts believe deferred demand will return quickly once prices stabilize.

title: Union minister says Modi government targets drug-free India by 2029
summary: Union minister Shah stated the Modi government aims to make India drug-free by 2029 to support a developed nation by 2047. He described narcotics control as a national security priority, contrasting it with pre-2014 isolated efforts. Shah asserted that the government will tackle drug menace with the same intensity used to eradicate Naxalism over five decades.

title: Seven easy DIY decoration ideas for Ganesh Chaturthi 2026
summary: The article suggests seven budget-friendly, eco-friendly decoration ideas for Ganesh Chaturthi 2026. These suggestions include creating a fresh flower curtain, painting terracotta diyas, and making a recycled paper lotus wall. Other options involve using banana leaves, crafting fabric torans, building a mini garden, and painting an eco-friendly backdrop. The text notes the festival will occur on September 14.

title: Psychologists explain why people check phones during quiet moments
summary: The article explores psychological reasons behind the urge to check smartphones during unstructured time. Researchers suggest this behavior stems from discomfort with unstructured mental space rather than simple boredom. Studies published in Science and PLOS One indicate that resisting phone impulses affects concentration and mind-wandering differently than expected. A systematic review in PubMed found mind-wandering is common and phones often interrupt these natural cognitive states. Research in Addictive Behaviors links boredom proneness to problematic mobile phone use among college students. Loneliness and self-control also influence how emotional states drive device usage according to PubMed-indexed studies. The authors note that checking phones can provide reassurance against uncertainty or become an automatic habit. A recent study showed smartphone breaks improved mood without harming cognitive performance. The article concludes that understanding internal mental states before reaching for a phone is more valuable than judging the device itself.

title: Anak Krakatau eruption suspends 300 flights at Jakarta airport
summary: Volcanic ash from Mount Anak Krakatau forced the suspension of over 300 flights at Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport. Authorities extended the halt multiple times, affecting 22,000 people and cancelling routes to Singapore and other cities. Schools and fishing activities also ceased due to ashfall causing eye irritation. Indonesian officials advised residents to wear masks and stay indoors while confirming no immediate tsunami risk.

title: US envoys arrive in Kyiv to restart peace talks after Moscow meeting
summary: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv to resume peace efforts following a three-hour meeting with Vladimir Putin in Moscow that yielded no breakthroughs. While Moscow discussed economic projects, fighting continues along the 1,250-kilometer front line with both sides exchanging fire. Local residents in Ukraine hold mixed hopes, with some welcoming the diplomatic push while others remain skeptical of previous failed delegations.

title: UK Business Minister Meets JLR CEO Over 4,000 Planned Job Cuts
summary: UK Business Minister Jonathan Reynolds will meet Jaguar Land Rover's CEO to discuss planned job cuts. The company aims to save £1.7 billion over two years through a voluntary redundancy programme. Reynolds stated the business environment remains challenging for UK carmakers. JLR faces pressure from US tariffs and Chinese competition, which have impacted sales of its luxury models.

title: Sudarshan Pharma board approves 9.5% stake acquisition in US biotech firm
summary: Sudarshan Pharma's board approved acquiring a 9.5% stake in MedTherapy Biotechnology Inc. to expand its US market presence. The acquisition, valued in US dollars, is expected to be completed by March 31, 2027. Sudarshan Pharma shares have surged over 369% in three years despite weak market sentiment. The deal requires approval under India's Foreign Exchange Management Act.

title: Scholars analyze Mouna Ragam as political allegory of Indian neoliberalism
summary: Two PhD scholars argue that Mani Ratnam's 1986 film Mouna Ragam serves as a political allegory for India's turn toward neoliberalism. The authors report that the film's narrative shifts from progressive depictions of working women to regressive themes centering on marriage and individualism. They state the movie portrays the Left as violent chaos while framing the new corporate managerial class as a safe alternative. The scholars write that the film's resolution uses class conflict to manufacture consent for structural economic adjustments. They note that despite these cultural efforts to pacify contradictions, neoliberalism has not delivered shared prosperity for most of the country.

title: Asaduddin Owaisi questions religious freedom after Saharanpur mosque demolition
summary: A mosque in Saharanpur was demolished on September 5, 2026, following a court order declaring it an unauthorized structure. AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi condemned the action, questioning if freedom of religion applies equally to Muslims. Opposition leaders criticized the demolition's timing and manner, while officials discovered a century-old well beneath the site. The Archaeological Survey of India has been informed to examine the structure.

title: Five-storey boys' PG collapses in south Delhi, trapping students
summary: A five-storey building housing a boys' PG collapsed in Satya Niketan, south Delhi, on Sunday afternoon, reportedly trapping multiple people. The Delhi Fire Service received a distress call around 1.33 pm and rushed eight tenders to the site. While locals suspect more than 15 people are trapped, this figure remains unconfirmed. Firefighters rescued three individuals in critical condition and rushed them to AIIMS. BJP MLA Anil Sharma stated that students are trapped inside and rescue efforts are ongoing. Delhi CM Rekha Gupta tweeted that teams are working on a war footing and the adjacent building has been vacated. An eyewitness claimed bodies were found and that a basement was being constructed when the collapse occurred.

title: BJP Agent Arrested in Jharkhand for Allegedly Targeting Muslims with Voter Deletion Forms
summary: A BJP Booth Level Agent in Jharkhand was arrested for allegedly submitting 200 Form 7 applications targeting minority voters. The Indian Express reported that the arrest followed a complaint by voter Mukarram Ansari regarding the deletion of names from the electoral roll. Police registered an FIR citing forgery and false declaration under the Representation of the People Act. The District Election Officer ordered a probe into the mass submission of forms. Opposition parties have raised concerns about the scale of voter deletions during the Special Intensive Revision process.

title: Building collapse in Delhi traps several people under debris
summary: A five-storey building collapsed near Satya Niketan in southwest Delhi on Sunday afternoon, leaving several people feared trapped. Emergency teams, including the Delhi Fire Service and police, are conducting a rescue operation. An eyewitness reported that four children were rescued and some bodies recovered, while sounds of crying were still heard from the rubble. Authorities have not yet confirmed the exact number of people trapped.

title: India backs UN equal-area map but insists J&K and Ladakh follow official depiction
summary: India voted for a UN resolution adopting an equal-area world map that enlarges Africa, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said. The Ministry clarified the vote supports equal representation without endorsing specific boundary lines. India maintains Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh must appear per its official map. The African Union adopted the new projection in February 2026 to correct Mercator distortions.

title: Assam Police Arrest 330 People Allegedly Involved in Fraud and Cyber Crimes
summary: Assam Police arrested 330 individuals in nine hours, according to Director General of Police Harmeet Singh. The operation, which began at 3 am Saturday, focused on Cachar district and targeted those impersonating police officials. Singh stated that arrested suspects lured victims by promising to settle cases and threatened others to extract money. Several accused were also found dealing in stolen goods and using cyber mediums for their activities. Police noted that ground verification is required as mobile numbers may not match the account operators.

title: Review highlights Lutfor Rahaman's stories of Muslim life in rural Kolkata
summary: A review praises Lutfor Rahaman's collection for depicting Muslim lives on Kolkata's margins through death and nature. Translator Mursed Alam preserves the original details without dilution. The stories feature gritty, resilient characters facing obstacles without pity. Nature is portrayed as destructive, creating a Sisyphian tone across the six tales. The work offers a foil to canonical Bengali literature by focusing on rural Muslim communities.

title: SBI Chairman CS Setty Announces Plans to Hire 12,000 Staff and Open 250 Branches
summary: SBI Chairman CS Setty announced plans to recruit approximately 12,000 employees and add 250 branches in the current financial year. The bank aims to expand its presence in emerging areas while rationalizing existing locations. Setty also confirmed a joint stake dilution of up to 1% in the National Stock Exchange through an IPO. He noted that no immediate monetization plans exist for other subsidiaries.

title: Restaurants Use AI Food Images Despite Consumer Disgust and Backlash
summary: Jill Sennett, a nurse in Denver, shared images of AI-generated food menus that appeared unappetizing, sparking widespread disgust among her followers. While restaurants cite cost-cutting measures as the reason for using artificial intelligence, consumers often find the resulting images misleading and repulsive. A 2026 report from the National Restaurant Association indicates that 26% of operators now use AI for various business functions, yet backlash remains fierce in tech-heavy areas like the Bay Area. Experts warn that AI frequently misrepresents food textures and lighting, potentially altering consumer expectations and dietary choices. Some establishments are gaining attention by pledging to avoid AI entirely, highlighting a growing divide between industry efficiency goals and diner preferences for authenticity.

title: AI skin cancer tools work well for light skin but fail on darker skin
summary: A computer engineer reports that new AI tools for detecting skin cancer are highly accurate for light skin but perform poorly on darker skin. The author explains that these models often mistake skin tone for disease rather than analyzing the lesion itself. By digitally darkening images of light-skinned patients, the engineer and colleagues found that the tools' diagnostic accuracy dropped significantly. This highlights a critical gap in current technology that researchers must address to ensure equitable access to medical expertise.

title: Trump administration rolls back Biden-era chemical pollution rules
summary: The Trump administration is dismantling the HON rule, a major Biden-era regulation designed to reduce toxic emissions from over 200 petrochemical plants. President Donald Trump granted temporary exemptions to more than 70 facilities and plans to rewrite the rule to scale back its protections. Advocates argue these moves endanger communities in areas like Louisiana's Cancer Alley, where cancer risks are already significantly elevated. The administration justifies the exemptions by claiming they protect national security and domestic supply chains, though critics say the claims lack evidence. Additionally, the EPA is proposing to weaken safety mandates and remove public data tools that track chemical plant accidents and operations. Environmental groups and affected residents are suing to halt these changes and restore the original regulatory standards.

title: Tens of thousands protest illegal waste dumping in Croatia
summary: Tens of thousands of citizens gathered in Zagreb to protest illegal waste dumping across Croatia. The event organizer, the "Gospić is Our Home" initiative, presented seven demands to authorities. State agencies confirmed the scandal involving over 30,000 tons of waste in Gospić and similar cases elsewhere. Protesters criticized government silence and called for immediate remediation plans and a ban on waste imports. Over 200 public figures attended the rally.

title: Former NITI Aayog VC says Apple wanted Chinese vendors in India
summary: Former NITI Aayog Vice Chairman Rajiv Kumar stated that Apple sought to bring its Chinese vendors to India during its expansion. Kumar told The Core that the government agreed to the move despite initial resistance. He argued India should welcome more Chinese foreign direct investment.

title: Nvidia CFO warns memory prices will rise further next year
summary: Nvidia CFO Colette Kress stated that memory pricing conditions have become extreme and are expected to increase further into next year. The company is resetting expectations for gross margins, which are projected to bottom between 71% and 72% in fiscal Q4 before recovering. Kress attributed current memory scarcity primarily to the ongoing AI buildout rather than external supply issues. Nvidia noted it is the largest single buyer in the market, with supplier commitments reaching approximately $279 billion.

title: UK minister rules out bailout for Jaguar Land Rover amid planned job cuts
summary: Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds stated the government will not provide taxpayer money to prevent job losses at Jaguar Land Rover. The company, owned by Tata Motors, plans up to 4,000 redundancies as part of a £1.7bn cost-cutting strategy over two years. Reynolds emphasized that financial support would not be a bailout but might involve workforce adaptation to global market conditions. Union leaders are expected to pressure the company to avoid compulsory layoffs during upcoming talks. The planned cuts affect nearly 12% of JLR's UK workforce and challenge Prime Minister Andy Burnham's reindustrialisation pledges. External pressures include sales slumps from a cyber-attack, US tariffs, and competition from Chinese vehicles.

title: German startup Isar launches first commercial rocket from continental Europe
summary: German startup Isar Aerospace successfully launched its uncrewed Spectrum rocket from Arctic Norway, marking the first commercial orbital launch from continental Europe. CEO Daniel Metzler stated that launch capability is currently the industry's biggest bottleneck. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and EU Commissioner Andrius Kubilius praised the achievement as a significant boost for European space autonomy. The rocket carried five small satellites and an experiment, following a previous failure at the same site. Isar plans to scale operations to 40 annual launches and is developing a second site in Nova Scotia.

title: Smriti Irani recalls seeking work after 2024 election loss
summary: Smriti Irani told Times Now she called entertainment industry contacts for work after losing the 2024 Amethi Lok Sabha election. The former Union Cabinet minister described the period as liberating. She said the defeat changed her perspective on her career and led her back to television.

title: Trump issues executive orders allowing ranchers to sell beef directly to consumers
summary: President Trump issued new executive orders permitting ranchers to sell meat directly to consumers. This move aims to pacify American cattle ranchers who opposed plans to boost beef imports.

title: Former State Department envoy discusses Iran war impact on gas prices
summary: NPR host Ayesha Rascoe interviewed former State Department energy envoy David Goldwyn regarding the conflict in Iran. The discussion focused on how the ongoing war continues to influence current gas and diesel prices. Goldwyn provided his analysis on the specific economic effects of the situation on fuel costs for consumers.

title: Jersey deputy withdraws fuel duty cut proposal after talks
summary: Deputy Lucy Stephenson withdrew a proposal to cut fuel duty in Jersey following discussions with Treasury Minister Alan Maclean. The plan would have reduced taxes by 10p per litre from October to December. Stephenson stated the talks produced a pragmatic way forward to help islanders with financial issues. She noted that voters clearly expressed their struggle with the cost of living during the recent election.

title: Reader's Digest offers five simple ways to reset routines for fall
summary: Reader's Digest suggests five simple steps to prepare for the busier fall season. The publication advises booking vacation days early to prevent them from disappearing. Experts recommend establishing consistent bedtimes and visible family schedules before school starts. The article also suggests clearing out summer clutter and organizing winter essentials. Additionally, it recommends reviewing pantry supplies and preparing emergency car kits. These small tuneups aim to reduce chaos as the season changes.

title: Police departments deploy Flock cameras to track vehicles across America
summary: The article states that Flock cameras are now visible on roads throughout the United States. These small devices photograph cars and read license plates to assist police. Authorities use the network to locate stolen vehicles, track suspects, and find missing people. The text notes that these cameras sit on poles beside intersections.

title: The Trade Desk leaves S&P 500 as Bloom Energy and others join
summary: S&P Dow Jones Indices announced changes to the S&P 500 and S&P 100 indices. Bloom Energy, Everpure, and Illumina joined the S&P 500, while The Trade Desk moved to the SmallCap 600. Several other companies also shifted between the indices.

title: UnitedHealth, Moderna, and Medtronic lead notable healthcare headlines this week
summary: Wall Street major averages fell Friday as investors digested stronger-than-forecasted jobs data. The Dow ended 0.5% lower while the S&P 500 slipped 0.3%. UnitedHealth, Moderna, and Medtronic were among the notable healthcare companies in focus.

title: Kroger to Report Second-Quarter Earnings on September 11, 2026
summary: Kroger is scheduled to release its second-quarter financial results before the market opens on September 11, 2026. Analysts expect adjusted earnings of $1.05 per share, representing a slight increase from the previous year. The company recently reported adjusted EPS of $1.58 and maintains a forward P/E ratio of 11.1 times. Over the past 52 weeks, shares have declined 14%, though the stock yields approximately 2.5% in dividends.

title: US Tourism Groups Seek Canadian Visitors Amid Trade War Tensions
summary: US tourism organizations are actively trying to attract Canadian travelers despite a deteriorating trade relationship between the two nations. Josh Loewen, a Vancouver marketing executive, describes these efforts as a wasted effort given the current political climate. Statistics Canada reports that Canadian border crossings dropped 25% in 2025, with spending falling by $2.4 billion. While some destinations like Las Vegas offer currency deals, many Canadians remain reluctant to visit due to high tensions and tariffs. Deborah Friedland, a hospitality consultant, notes that sentiment remains negative following recent tariff announcements. Although tentative improvements appeared during the 2026 World Cup, air travel continues to decline. Experts warn that the upcoming winter season will test whether this boycott persists.

title: US Tourism Groups Seek Canadian Visitors Amid Trade Tensions
summary: American tourism organizations are actively trying to attract Canadian travelers despite a sharp decline in cross-border visits. The drop in tourism coincides with deteriorating diplomatic relations and new tariffs between the two nations. Statistics Canada reports that Canadian residents made 25% fewer return border crossings in 2025 compared to the previous year. While some officials remain optimistic about future recovery, many Canadians cite political tensions as a primary reason for avoiding US travel. Experts warn that the boycott may persist through the winter season unless diplomatic relations improve.

title: Voters in Saxony-Anhalt begin election that could see AfD lead a state government
summary: Voting started Sunday in Saxony-Anhalt, a closely watched election in eastern Germany. The Alternative for Germany (AfD) could become the first far-right party to lead a state government since World War II. Our guest, Hans Stark, a professor of German studies at Sorbonne University, discusses the situation.

title: America's Got Talent contestant charged with murder after nephew drowns
summary: Former America's Got Talent contestant Deshundre Vinson faces murder charges following the drowning death of his 4-year-old nephew. The Hamilton County Sheriff's Office stated Vinson was arrested in Chattanooga for first-degree murder and aggravated child abuse. Authorities reported the boy remained underwater for nine minutes before dying five days later. Investigators noted Vinson allowed unsupervised access to the pool and sent messages acknowledging the lack of supervision. Vinson, a member of the R&B trio Citi Limitz, has a court date scheduled for Tuesday.

title: FIFA says President Infantino will seek re-election in March despite opposition
summary: FIFA stated that President Gianni Infantino remains committed to seeking re-election in March next year. A spokesperson confirmed that nothing has changed regarding his candidacy announced in April. Infantino faces calls to resign from UEFA, the AFC, and CONCACAF following the cancellation of a plan to sell a 20 per cent stake in FIFA events. He retains support from the African and South American confederations. No formal challenge to his candidacy has been announced.

title: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov calls Leipzig drone accusations a real war
summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov stated that accusations regarding a drone incident at Leipzig Airport mark the beginning of a real war. Speaking to Vesti, Lavrov noted that no investigation occurred into the drone's ownership. He compared Germany's current diplomatic expulsions to actions taken before World War II. Germany officially blamed Russia for the incident and announced sanctions including closing the Russian Consulate General in Bonn.

title: Russia calls Leipzig drone accusations start of real war
summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov stated that German accusations regarding a Leipzig drone attack mark the beginning of actual war. The German government concluded Russia was responsible for the incident and ordered security measures, including a new cyberdome. US Ambassador Matthew Whitaker warned NATO members not to tolerate such hybrid warfare actions. Germany plans to expand drone defense capabilities and use AI for surveillance.

title: US envoys Kushner and Witkoff arrive in Kyiv for peace talks
summary: US negotiators Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff arrived in Kyiv to continue discussions on ending the war in Ukraine. The pair met President Volodymyry Zelenskyy in Sophia Square following three hours of talks with Vladimir Putin in Moscow. While details of any peace proposal remain unclear, officials stated the meetings discussed substantive plans for next steps. The visit marks an intensification of efforts to resolve the conflict, which has now lasted over four and a half years.

title: Kremlin says Anchorage understandings remain on agenda
summary: Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov stated that elements of the Anchorage understandings will always remain on the agenda. Peskov noted it is difficult to assess their current applicability from Ukrainian and US perspectives. Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov described recent talks between Putin, Steve Witkoff, and Jared Kushner as substantive and constructive. The US envoys subsequently traveled to Kyiv for the first time since the war began.

title: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner visit Kyiv after Moscow talks with Putin
summary: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv by train to pursue peace efforts with Russia. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Kyiv has prepared proposals for a just and sustainable postwar peace. Reuters reported that national security advisors from the UK, France, and Germany also met with the US envoys. Kyrylo Budanov, Zelenskyy's chief of staff, told the New York Times he does not expect the fighting to end before spring 2027.

title: Anak Krakatau eruption suspends flights, schools, and fishing in Indonesia
summary: An eruption of Indonesia's Mount Anak Krakatau disrupted local activities on Sunday. The event caused six airports to suspend flight operations, significantly impacting hundreds of flights at Jakarta's main airport. Additionally, authorities halted some school activities and fishing operations in the affected area. The eruption prompted immediate safety measures across the region.

title: FIFA President Gianni Infantino Announces Candidacy for 2027 Re-election
summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino confirmed he will seek re-election at the 2027 Congress in Rabat. A spokesperson stated that nothing has changed regarding his candidacy announced in April. Infantino faces continued pressure from UEFA despite assurances that a controversial investment plan was withdrawn. He previously vowed to run again, thanking delegates for their support over the last decade.

title: US Embassy denies seeking to influence Malaysian politics
summary: The US Embassy in Malaysia rejected claims it sought to influence Malaysian politics. Charge d'affaires David H Gamble Jr stated the US never decided Malaysia's political leadership. PAS chief Abdul Hadi Awang alleged the US offered help to topple the government in 2014. PAS representatives confirmed a meeting occurred but denied discussing plans to overthrow the government.

title: AfD candidate Ulrich Siegmund votes in Saxony-Anhalt state election
summary: AfD candidate Ulrich Siegmund cast his ballot in Saxony-Anhalt's state election on Sunday, arriving in Tangermünde with his wife. Supporters cheered as he arrived on a motorcycle and took selfies with the crowd. The election has drawn national attention as the AfD seeks its strongest result yet. Siegmund stated he would seek the governor's post only if the party wins an absolute majority. After voting, he told supporters he saw a spirit of optimism and called for Germany to overcome political divisions.

title: Kentucky man with meat allergy starts ostrich farm to feed customers
summary: Brent Williams, a nutritionist in Danville, Kentucky, launched Alpha Roost Farms after developing a life-threatening allergy to red meat known as alpha-gal syndrome. Williams noted that many people with this condition find ostrich meat a suitable alternative because it lacks the alpha-gal sugar found in mammalian meat. The farm currently holds over 400 ostriches and plans to expand its herd to 700 by next year to meet rising demand. Owners report that customers are willing to pay more than $20 per pound for ground ostrich and drive long distances to purchase it. While the industry faced a crash in the 1990s due to inexperienced farmers, current producers like Williams and Boyd Clark in Texas are adapting to the specific needs of these large birds. Experts estimate there could be up to half a million Americans with alpha-gal syndrome, creating a growing market for safe meat substitutes.

title: At least 25 people die in Cape Verde bus crash
summary: A bus crash in Cape Verde killed at least 25 people, mostly children and teenagers, according to public radio network RCV. The accident occurred on Fogo Island when the vehicle plunged into a ravine after an excursion to a volcanic crater. Thirty-two people were on board, and the driver, who organized the trip, was among the dead. President José Maria Pereira Neves called the event a great catastrophe and plans to visit the island with other officials.

title: Jordan Bardella faces controversy during European tour over immigration and Ukraine
summary: The provided text contains an error message regarding a failed site load and does not include the article body. Consequently, no summary of the reported events can be generated from the available source material.

title: Trump envoys Kushner and Witkoff meet Zelensky in Kyiv
summary: The provided text indicates a loading error and does not contain the article body required to summarize the meeting between Trump's envoys and Zelensky. No facts, figures, or claims could be extracted from the source.

title: Qantas passengers describe engine fire and panic during diverted flight
summary: Passengers on a Sydney-bound Qantas flight reported screaming and panic after flames shot from the left engine, forcing a diversion to Christchurch. Kriti Sethi stated the fire occurred five times while the plane shook, contradicting initial crew claims about landing gear. The captain informed passengers of a chemical engine failure, and emergency services were present upon landing. Qantas has grounded the aircraft for inspection while an investigation continues. In a separate incident, another Qantas plane was grounded after an anti-skid system alert. Consultant Neil Hansford suggested a detached engine blade may have ignited fuel, noting aircraft are designed to handle such events safely.

title: Spotify co-founder says he would leave Sweden if wealth tax imposed
summary: Spotify Technology co-founder Martin Lorentzon stated he would immediately leave Sweden if new wealth taxes are introduced. The billionaire warned that such levies would force entrepreneurs to sell company stakes, reducing innovation and investment. While center-left parties campaign for billionaire taxes, the current government opposes them. Lorentzon argued that taxing illiquid wealth is counterproductive and has already created uncertainty for business founders.

title: Saxony-Anhalt AfD leader Ulrich Siegmund expects victory in state election
summary: Ulrich Siegmund, leader of the Alternative for Germany party in Saxony-Anhalt, expressed confidence in securing a majority to lead the state government after Sunday's election. He stated that even if the party falls short, the resulting political chaos would last only a few months before another victory. Siegmund described the party as the future and maintained a positive outlook for the upcoming vote in the eastern German state.

title: White sacred stone signals peace and prosperity for Togo
summary: Hundreds of Voodoo priests and priestesses gathered in Aneho, Togo, to unveil the sacred Ekpessosso stone during the annual Epe-Ekpe festival. Guardian Wlomo Nomo Combietey VIII Nii Labite explained that the stone's white color symbolizes peace and prosperity for the coming year. Approximately 51 percent of Togo's seven million people practice Voodoo, the nation's largest religion. The ceremony, which dates back to 1663, concluded with chants against evil spirits and prayers answered by the gods.

title: BRICS explores cross-border payment links to cut costs
summary: BRICS nations are discussing mechanisms to facilitate direct cross-border payments between members ahead of the 18th summit in New Delhi. Current systems rely on correspondent banks and the dollar as a vehicle currency, incurring high fees and conversion costs. The article reports that foreign exchange margins can reach 20% in some African transactions. BRICS aims to connect national payment systems directly or via a shared hub using central bank digital currencies. This approach would remove the need for intermediate currency conversions and reduce settlement risks. India proposes linking CBDCs for trade and tourism while framing the initiative as a cost-cutting measure rather than a move to displace the dollar. The report notes that US tariff threats may influence this cautious framing.

title: India co-sponsors UN resolution designating November 27 as day against child marriage
summary: India co-sponsored a United Nations General Assembly resolution designating November 27 as the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage. The 193-member body adopted the Sierra Leone-led measure by consensus on September 4, 2026. Bhuwan Ribhu of Just Rights for Children stated the adoption marks the beginning of global action to end the practice. The resolution calls on member states to implement comprehensive laws and invest in girls' education. It recognizes child marriage as a harmful practice violating human rights. Fatima Maada Bio noted the issue remains a barrier to gender equality and sustainable development.

title: New Arctic shipping routes shift global trade power toward Russia and China
summary: Two cargo ships recently departed from Qingdao and Busan to test a new weekly Arctic route between Asia and Europe. The authors report that this shift shortens transit times by up to 40% compared to the Suez Canal while avoiding Red Sea conflicts. Kjell Stokvik of the Center for High North Logistics notes that Russia controls navigation permits for the Northern Sea Route, granting Moscow significant geopolitical leverage. Environmental concerns remain, as Javier Arnaut warns of potential collisions with Arctic wildlife and increased pollution risks. While Spain benefits from current diversions around the Cape of Good Hope, the Arctic route threatens to diminish its influence. The European Union is preparing a new Arctic strategy, but experts like Alla Pozdnakova doubt its ability to counter growing tensions between major powers. Russia views the route as a strategic priority, allowing it to charge tolls or shut down the corridor at will.

title: Teenagers bring online culture codes to public parks and streets
summary: Teenagers are gathering in public spaces to perform acts known as 'aura farming,' a trend blending video game logic with real-world social interaction. Analyst Adrián Juste argues that digital trends have long moved from screens to streets, evolving from flash mobs to Pokémon Go. Sociologists explain that these performances allow youth to build collective identity and separate themselves from family environments using shared ironic codes. Philologist Byron Ramírez notes that absurdity in these battles helps transmit ideas and sustain community among peers. The article concludes that for digital natives, the internet is no longer a separate reality but an extension of daily life where public squares function as extensions of the web.

title: Nepali woman found alive after mudslide buries home
summary: Rescuers discovered a 64-year-old Nepali woman alive on the fourth floor of her mud-buried home in the Nuwakot district. The Armed Police Force found Chandika Shrestha more than 10 days after a wall of ice, rock, and mud tore through the Himalayan valley. She was airlifted to a hospital in Kathmandu for treatment, according to Reuters.

title: Haitian caregivers lose US work status, leaving families devastated
summary: Families in the US are struggling after the termination of Temporary Protected Status for Haitian workers, who make up a significant portion of the direct-care workforce. The Supreme Court ruled in favor of the Trump administration's decision to end TPS, affecting approximately 350,000 Haitians and forcing many employers to lay off staff. Healthcare organizations report severe staffing shortages, with some losing dozens of employees and facing long recruitment delays. A Department of Homeland Security spokesperson defended the move, stating that TPS is temporary and that relying on unvetted workers is false. Despite bipartisan efforts to extend TPS for Haitians, Senate opposition has stalled the legislation. Families describe the loss of trusted caregivers as devastating, particularly for vulnerable individuals with disabilities and seniors.

title: Author argues North Macedonia must stop glorifying convicted war criminal Ratko Mladić
summary: Bardhyl Jashari argues that commemorating North Macedonia's independence by honoring Ratko Mladić undermines the rule of law and damages the country's multiethnic society. The author states that Mladić was legally convicted of genocide and war crimes by the International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals, making his glorification morally unacceptable and potentially a criminal offense under Article 407-a of the Criminal Code. While several political parties condemned the behavior, the author criticizes the VLEN coalition and VMRO-DPMNE for failing to directly name or dismiss the officials responsible. Jashari warns that tolerating such views contradicts North Macedonia's commitment to European values and hinders its integration into the European Union. The article concludes that a state cannot build a European future while allowing the glorification of convicted war criminals.

title: Tamil Nadu Tourism Minister visits Kaipamangalam crash site and promises support
summary: Tamil Nadu Tourism Minister S. Rajesh Kumar visited the Kaipamangalam crash site on September 6, 2026, following a fatal accident that killed eight students. The Minister expressed grief and promised immediate assistance for the victims' families in consultation with the Chief Minister. He criticized unscientific highway construction and called for the completion of remaining road works. Rajesh Kumar emphasized that strict measures are needed to prevent future tragedies and ensure motorist safety.

title: GIFT and ICSSR host two-day GST reform seminar in Thiruvananthapuram
summary: The Gulati Institute of Finance and Taxation and the Indian Council of Social Science Research are organizing a national seminar on GST reforms. Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan will inaugurate the event and launch a new publication. Former finance ministers and economists will discuss the tax system's impact on state finances.

title: Amit Shah says India aims to be drug-free by 2029
summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced a government roadmap to make India drug-free by 2029. He described narcotics control as a national security priority. The administration employs a reverse investigation model to trace drug flows. Officials also plan to utilize the NIDAN database for tracking.

title: Indian stocks focus on RVNL, Mazagon Dock, Tata Motors updates
summary: Vaamanaa reports that Indian investors are focusing on several companies following post-market business updates. Rail Vikas Nigam secured a ₹903 crore order for a thermal power project. Tata Motors launched an open offer to acquire Iveco Group shares at €14.1 per share. Mazagon Dock received a ₹118 crore purchase order for an AI-based security project. Other updates include JSW Steel's production rise and Lupin's FDA approval for Modafinil tablets.

title: Tata Motors launches €3.82 billion cash tender offer to acquire Iveco Group
summary: Tata Motors announced a €3.82 billion all-cash tender offer to acquire the Italian commercial vehicle manufacturer Iveco Group. Analyst Seema Srivastava of SMC Global Securities stated the deal will transform Tata Motors Commercial Vehicles into a global entity delivering 590,000 units annually with combined revenues exceeding €21 billion. The acquisition will shift approximately 46% of Tata's annual business to the European Union. However, Srivastava noted that funding the deal via bridge facilities will increase leverage and interest costs while initial cost synergies depend on joint procurement rather than workforce reductions. Mahesh M Ojha, VP at a research firm, indicated the share price currently shows sideways to positive technical movement with support at ₹448 and potential upside to ₹505.

title: Google lets Gemini Spark manage Google Photos libraries
summary: Google announced that its personal agent, Gemini Spark, can now manage users' Google Photos libraries. The tech giant said users can ask the tool to edit pictures, curate albums, and turn concert flyers into actual plans. Google Photos lead Shimrit Ben-Yair stated these capabilities will roll out over the next few weeks to AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in the US. The company did not mention a timeline for when the new capabilities will be rolled out globally.

title: Bank of India Flexi Cap among 5 flexi-cap funds that deliver over 15% annualised return in 3 years
summary: ETMarkets.com reports that five flexi cap funds delivered over 15% annualised returns in the last three years. Bank of India Flexi Cap Fund topped the list with 20.5% annualised return, followed by Motilal Oswal, Invesco India, ITI, and ICICI Prudential funds.

title: Over 150 dividend stocks turn ex-record date this week
summary: The Economic Times reports that more than 150 stocks are turning ex-record dates for dividends this week. Investors must hold shares in demat accounts by respective record dates to be eligible. The list remains tentative as additional companies may announce dates during the week. Force Motors and Empire Industries will pay Rs 50 per share on Wednesday, while Apar Industries will pay Rs 60 per share on Friday. Kalyan Jewellers and IREDA are among the companies distributing dividends on Friday.

title: Federal Judge Rejects xAI Bid to Block Minnesota AI Nudification Ban
summary: A federal judge in Minnesota declined to block a state law banning AI-generated nude images, rejecting xAI's request for a preliminary injunction. U.S. District Judge Donovan Frank stated that xAI failed to demonstrate imminent harm while its First Amendment challenge proceeds. Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison defended the measure as necessary to stop the creation of nonconsensual sexual imagery. xAI plans to appeal the ruling to the 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals.

title: Former Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah calls for 75 percent reservation
summary: Former Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah stated that a 75 percent reservation quota is necessary to build an egalitarian society. Speaking at the Karnataka State Backward Castes Federation's Silver Jubilee celebration, he demanded the implementation of the caste census report he accepted before leaving office. Siddaramaiah argued that social justice requires equal opportunities based on population for Dalits, backward communities, and minorities. He also highlighted measures taken during his tenure, including increased departmental budgets and the establishment of numerous hostels for students.

title: Coimbatore Collector mandates safety and eco-friendly rules for Vinayaka Chaturthi
summary: District Collector Pavankumar G. Giriyappanavar convened a meeting with idol makers to enforce safety and environmental guidelines for Vinayaka Chaturthi. The administration requires idols to be made of clay and natural materials while restricting loudspeaker use and procession routes. Authorities also mandate waste removal at immersion points to prevent water pollution. The Collector urged full cooperation with police to ensure the September 14 festival remains peaceful and safe.

title: India votes for UN resolution promoting equal-area world maps
summary: India voted in favor of a United Nations resolution encouraging the use of equal-area map projections to show landmass sizes more accurately. The resolution does not alter borders or mandate a specific map like Equal Earth. Diplomat Raghoo Puri clarified that India supports the broader concept, not a particular projection. The Ministry of External Affairs stated the measure does not affect international boundaries or disputed territories.

title: Delhi Police register FIR after five-storey PG building collapse kills two
summary: Officials report that a five-storey building in Satya Niketan, Delhi, collapsed on Sunday afternoon, killing two people and leaving five others in critical condition. Rescue teams recovered six individuals from the rubble, though residents estimate 40 to 50 people may still be trapped. The structure, used as a paying guest facility, was undergoing basement repairs when it fell at 1.30 pm. Emergency personnel from the Delhi Police, NDRF, and Delhi Fire Service are conducting operations in a congested area near Delhi University. Political leaders, including Rahul Gandhi and Amit Shah, have expressed concern and urged swift rescue efforts. The Delhi LG directed agencies to coordinate for swift rescue, while the Delhi Police have registered an FIR in connection with the incident.

title: Delhi student survivor fears scooter was inches from collapse
summary: An 18-year-old psychology student at Aryabhatta College survived a building collapse in Delhi's Satya Niketan area on September 6, 2026. The student, Unnayan, was sitting on a broker's scooter when the structure fell. He told The Hindu that if the scooter had been any closer, he and the driver would have been under the rubble. The area is a major hub for students seeking affordable accommodation near Delhi University. Unnayan, who was searching for a cheaper flat, expressed fear about living in the dense rental zone again. Local students also joined rescue efforts at the site.

title: Embraer expands India supply chain across commercial and defence aviation
summary: Embraer is accelerating its supply chain expansion in India across commercial and defence aviation segments. Sankalp Shrivastava, Country Head and Director, Embraer Defence & Security India, stated the company has been actively developing local partnerships over the past three to four years. Recent agreements include MoUs with Hindalco Industries and Bharat Forge Ltd for raw material manufacturing. Additionally, Embraer has a strategic partnership with Adani Defence & Aerospace for final assembly of the E175 aircraft. The company also plans to establish a maintenance hub in India if the C390 is selected for the Indian Air Force's Medium Transport Aircraft programme.

title: Director Honey Trehan Defends Film Satluj Against Government Censorship
summary: Director Honey Trehan discussed the challenges faced by his film Satluj, which depicts the life of human rights defender Jaswant Singh Khalra. Trehan stated that the movie was blocked by the government's censor board for 31 years before its eventual release on an OTT platform. He attributed the film's widespread popularity to unauthorized screenings and piracy, noting it achieved a 9.7 rating on IMDb within days. Trehan argued that political motives drove narratives claiming the film incited violence, asserting Khalra fought for all undocumented victims regardless of religion. The director emphasized that the film united diverse communities in Punjab and provided emotional healing to those affected by past political violence. Trehan rejected accusations that the film glorifies violence, explaining it portrays a specific historical period rather than being a biopic. He criticized the selective application of national security threats, contrasting Satluj with other controversial films that received awards. Trehan confirmed his producer, Ronnie Screwvala, lost crores of rupees due to pressure to make cuts that were never implemented. The director expressed pride in the project, viewing it as a service to his community and humanity.

title: Mumbai Police Probe ₹57 Crore Ponzi Scheme After Contacting 1,000 Investors
summary: The Mumbai Economic Offences Wing is investigating an alleged Ponzi scheme that collected over ₹57 crore. Police have contacted nearly 1,000 investors to identify victims and track funds after arresting four accused individuals. The scheme, operated under names AI Origin and Digital Origin, promised high monthly returns without regulatory licenses. Investigators seized cash, vehicles, and digital devices while examining transactions on the accused's website and app.

title: Former Pakistan cricketer Yousuf blames 2021 India win for team decline
summary: Former Pakistan star Mohammad Yousuf told Samaa TV that the team's current crisis began after their historic 10-wicket victory over India in the 2021 T20 World Cup. Yousuf stated that the win damaged the squad by fostering excessive confidence and a lack of humility among players. He also criticized the internal fight for the captaincy, noting that players prioritized leadership roles over taking responsibility for their performances. Amidst recent heavy defeats against England, the Pakistan Cricket Board removed head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and sent seven players back to Pakistan. Yousuf supported the board's decision, arguing that the team's poor reputation necessitated immediate action to improve. He emphasized that the team's struggles extend beyond the current England series, citing poor results in recent major tournaments.

title: Over 3,100 Students Create Eco-Friendly Ganesh Idols at Nashik Workshop
summary: More than 3,100 students from Nashik district participated in a workshop to create Ganesh idols using shadu soil. Organized by K K Wagh Educational Institute and other foundations, the event aimed to reduce environmental degradation caused by plaster of Paris idols. District Collector Ayush Prasad and Municipal Commissioner Manisha Khatri attended as chief guests. Organizers stated that eco-friendly idols are essential for preserving culture while protecting the environment.

title: Trapped Delhi student shares SOS video as rescue teams work
summary: Officials report that 30 to 50 students remain trapped under rubble after the collapse of the five-storey Satya Niketan building in Delhi on Sunday. One person died and two are critical at AIIMS. A video identified as showing student Aditya Kumar trapped under debris surfaced, which he shared with a friend to seek help. The National Students' Union of India shared the clip while its workers assisted rescue efforts. BJP MLA Anil Sharma stated that trapped individuals are still calling for assistance. Multiple agencies, including the NDRF and Delhi Fire Services, are conducting operations on a war footing. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta arrived at the site to oversee the response.

title: Vikas Singh Panwar ranks 159 in UPSC and wins 50 lakh on KBC
summary: Vikas Singh Panwar secured All India Rank 159 in the UPSC CSE 2025 exam on his first attempt at age 22. Months prior, he won 50 lakh on Kaun Banega Crorepati before quitting to avoid risk. He plans to repay his father's education loan with the prize money. Panwar, from Jubli village, studied Political Science at Hindu College and qualified for the UGC-NET exam. He received a full scholarship from NEXT IAS to support his preparation.

title: India's BS7 norms open Rs 10,000 crore annual market for auto parts makers
summary: India's Bharat Stage 7 emission norms are expected to create an annual opportunity of approximately Rs 10,000 crore for auto-component manufacturers. Industry experts told BusinessLine that heavy trucks and buses could see the highest incremental content per vehicle, while two-wheelers remain significant due to high volumes. Road Transport and Highways Secretary V Umashankar stated that final consultations for the draft norms are nearing completion. The opportunity is distributed across exhaust systems, sensors, and fluid-dosing technologies, with specific companies identified as potential beneficiaries.

title: JNU professor investigated after students allege sexual harassment remarks
summary: JNU sources say 11 students filed a sexual harassment complaint against a professor. The Hindustan Times reports the professor allegedly told students he would award extra marks if they accepted his sexual advances during May examinations. University officials stated the Internal Complaints Committee has begun proceedings. This case follows a 2025 dismissal of another faculty member, Swaran Singh, for similar allegations involving a Japanese official.

title: Five-storey Delhi hostel collapses trapping students during repairs
summary: A five-storey residential building in Delhi's Satya Niketan area collapsed on Sunday, trapping between 30 and 50 students. Five individuals have been shifted to the trauma centre at AIIMS, though their condition remains unknown. Rescue operations involving the NDRF and fire vehicles are underway at the site of the five-decade-old structure. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta ordered the adjacent building vacated as a precaution.

title: High CAPE ratio, Fed rates and Trump tariffs raise S&P 500 crash risks
summary: The S&P 500 faces potential crash risks as its Shiller CAPE ratio rises above 41, while inflation fears, Federal Reserve rate hike concerns, and Trump policies add pressure. The Motley Fool reports the CAPE ratio has crossed 35 only twice in 155 years, both times preceding major downturns. President Trump's tariffs could increase inflation, limiting the Federal Reserve's ability to cut rates or forcing them higher. CME Group's FedWatch tool indicates an 87% chance of a rate hike by year-end. US Treasury bond volatility also threatens highly valued stocks. However, the article notes a crash is not guaranteed if strong corporate earnings continue to lower forward price-to-earnings multiples.

title: New Zealand home prices hit three-year low amid cautious buyers
summary: Property consultancy Cotality reported that New Zealand home values fell 0.4% in August, reaching a three-year low. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand raised interest rates to 2.75% while noting uneven economic recovery. Cotality economist Kelvin Davidson stated the market remains stagnant with no near-term growth catalyst. The central bank forecasts a 0.5% price decline in 2026 before a modest recovery begins.

title: Delhi PG Hostel Collapses, Killing One and Trapping Students
summary: A five-storey boys' PG building in Delhi collapsed on September 6, 2026, killing at least one person and trapping several students. Hindustan Times reported the incident occurred around 1:34 pm while most students were inside. Scroll noted the structure was 40 to 50 years old and repair work was ongoing in the basement. Union Home Minister Amit Shah cancelled an event in Goa following the tragedy. Rescue teams worked on a war footing to locate survivors amidst the debris.

title: Delhi Student Tragedy: Focus on Rescue, Authorities' Delay & Civic Body Negligence Questioned
summary: A speaker addressed the Delhi student tragedy, emphasizing rescue operations over political blame. Authorities noted delays in police and ambulance arrivals while three students were evacuated. The speaker questioned the MCD and NDMC regarding alleged negligence and safety norms. Officials in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar are monitoring severe flooding caused by water release from Nepal.

title: Gujarat couple kills finance manager to escape loan and recover gold
summary: Prantij police arrested a woman and are hunting her lover after they killed an IIFL Finance branch manager. Police said the couple plotted the murder to avoid repaying a combined Rs 6 lakh loan and recover pledged gold. The accused attacked the manager inside his car with a sharp-edged weapon. Bhavna Thakor has been arrested, while her seven-year partner Yogesh remains absconding.

title: Jing-Jing Lee's novel honors comfort women of occupied Singapore
summary: Jing-Jing Lee's 2019 novel How We Disappeared centers on Wang Di, a young girl trafficked as a comfort woman during Japan's occupation of Singapore. The article notes that the Japanese military occupied Singapore in February 1942, claiming the lives of approximately 55,000 ethnic Chinese and kidnapping young women for the army. Lee's protagonist survives in a brothel where she serves up to 50 men daily while suffering from venereal diseases and facing constant threats. After the war, the novel depicts the severe ostracization these women faced upon returning to their families. The Japanese government has denied running state-sponsored rape camps, yet victims from multiple nations continue to seek justice. Lee's work keeps these memories alive, ensuring the suffering of these women is not forgotten.

title: Kharge calls Modi's SRCC visit a political campaign
summary: Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi for turning a Shri Ram College of Commerce visit into a political campaign. Kharge alleged the Prime Minister used derogatory labels to evade accountability regarding rising unemployment and recruitment delays. In response, PM Modi addressed students by labeling critics as 'Angry Uncles' who oppose national development projects. The exchange highlights ongoing tensions between the ruling party and the opposition over governance and youth welfare.

title: Delhi court remands Hindutva influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj to one-day judicial custody
summary: A Delhi court has remanded Hindutva influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj to one day of judicial custody. The Patiala House Court's Duty Magistrate ordered this after Delhi Police sought 14 days of custody for the accused. Bhardwaj was detained in connection with an alleged attempt to murder Sanjay Azad during a protest. The magistrate granted the one-day order while the police requested a longer period. Bhardwaj will be produced before the concerned court on Monday.

title: Trump wants lower rates, but inflation from tariffs, war and AI blocks the Fed
summary: The Motley Fool reports that President Donald Trump wants the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates significantly, yet inflation driven by tariffs, the Iran war, and an AI boom is preventing this. The article states that Trump argues lower rates would boost US growth to 20% and help manage the nation's $40 trillion debt. However, the Fed faces pressure from tariffs raising import costs, the Iran conflict disrupting energy supplies, and an AI infrastructure boom creating a supply-demand imbalance. The Motley Fool explains that these factors keep core inflation sticky, forcing the central bank to balance growth against price stability. Consequently, the Fed may keep rates higher or even raise them, which could slow AI investment and hurt the stock market, directly contradicting Trump's economic goals.

title: Sixteen Indian IPOs open next week with GMPs signaling up to 38% returns
summary: ETMarkets reports sixteen Indian IPOs opening across mainboard and SME segments next week. Grey market premiums suggest selective investor appetite, with Rentomojo showing the highest GMP of 38%. Several issues lack active GMPs yet, focusing attention on subscription demand.

title: Eleven penny stocks drop up to 81% in six months
summary: ACE Equity identified eleven penny stocks that fell between 49% and 81% over the last six months. The screen targeted shares with a market capitalisation below Rs 1,000 crore and a price under Rs 20. These low-priced, liquid stocks faced significant selling pressure during the period.

title: Terence Eden claims DNS primarily facilitates widespread scam operations
summary: Terence Eden argues that the Domain Name System functions mainly as a vector for criminals to run scams. He cites Interisle data showing 85 million new gTLD registrations in 2025, with 8.5 million added to blocklists by May. Eden estimates the abuse rate is likely between 10% and 20%, noting one in five new domains are scams. He mentions ICANN has discussed this problem for years.

title: Colombia Lifts Fracking Ban to Attract $4 Billion in Oil Investment
summary: Colombia's new administration plans to reverse a four-year ban on oil and gas exploration to attract foreign investment. Fossil fuel companies anticipate injecting up to $4 billion into the sector over the next four years. However, the government must quickly remove regulatory hurdles and address security concerns to make the deals viable. Political analysts warn that investors require long-term fiscal certainty and that local community opposition remains a significant challenge.

title: Oman expands renewable energy capacity to diversify economy
summary: Oman plans to significantly expand its renewable energy capacity to support economic diversification and green transition goals. The government introduced new policies to encourage private investment in cleantech industries and achieve net-zero emissions by mid-century. Minister Salim Al Aufi emphasized the strategic importance of these plans for a sustainable low-carbon economy. The country aims to reduce carbon emissions by 33 per cent by 2035 through energy diversification and carbon capture projects. Oman intends to add approximately 5.7 GW of solar and over 2 GW of wind power by the end of the decade. Despite some withdrawals from green hydrogen projects, the nation continues to develop seven hydrogen projects with a combined output of one million tonnes annually by 2030.

title: Analysts Project Nvidia Profits Could Match Saudi Arabia GDP by 2029
summary: Analysts forecast Nvidia could generate $851 billion in annual net income by 2029, surpassing Saudi Aramco's record. Jensen Huang stated the supply chain is operating at full capacity. The projection assumes a 64% compounded earnings growth rate based on recent financial results. If realized, Nvidia's revenue would rank it as the 18th-largest economy globally.

title: Elon Musk Plans to Use Starlink and AI to Fund SpaceX Space Goals
summary: The article argues that SpaceX must execute two growth pillars before pursuing multiplanetary ambitions. CEO Elon Musk stated the mission is to make life multiplanetary, but the text notes the company recently posted a net loss of $541 million. Starlink profits are critical for self-funding, while AI represents a $26.5 trillion market opportunity. The author suggests these businesses will justify speculative space ventures to investors.

title: US annual interest expense hits record 18.5% of federal revenue
summary: A linked report states that US annual interest expense reached a record 18.5% of federal government revenue. This figure surpasses the previous high of 18.4% set in 1991. The percentage has more than quadrupled over the last four years as public debt interest expenditures rose sharply.

title: Guardian editorial warns Burnham's devolution plans need stronger local scrutiny
summary: The Guardian editorial argues that Andy Burnham's devolution plans must address diminished local government scrutiny. The article notes the 2015 abolition of the Audit Commission weakened oversight, citing scandals like Teesworks. While the proposed Local Audit Office is an improvement, the editorial suggests creating local public accounts committees. It also highlights the problem of declining local media, with 4.4 million people lacking dedicated news outlets.

title: SBI plans to hire 12,000 employees and add 250 branches by FY27
summary: State Bank of India chairman CS Setty announced plans to recruit 11,000 to 12,000 employees and open up to 250 new branches during the current financial year. The bank aims to fill both clerical and officer roles while rationalizing existing locations to expand its net presence. Setty noted that last year's large hiring included 1,500 specialist IT officers, a need not present this year. Additionally, SBI and its subsidiary plan to dilute a combined 1% stake in the National Stock Exchange through a proposed IPO.

title: ISRO rejects privatization rumors and clarifies its future role in India's space program
summary: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) rejected reports suggesting it could be privatised or have its role diminished. The agency stated it will remain India's principal institution for advanced research, national missions, and strategic capabilities. While private participation is encouraged to scale mature technologies, ISRO will focus on frontier research and complex national goals like the Bharatiya Antariksh Station. The Department of Space will provide policy direction, while IN-SPACe and NewSpace India Limited will facilitate non-government participation and commercialisation. ISRO noted that ownership of critical infrastructure will remain with the government. The clarification follows concerns raised by nine employee associations regarding the transfer of manufacturing functions to private entities.

title: China injects $54bn into financial sector to support growth
summary: China plans to inject $54bn into its financial sector to bolster banks and insurers amid sluggish economic growth. Major state insurers like China Life and China Taiping will receive billions in capital, while three large state lenders will raise a combined 290bn yuan. Officials state the stimulus aims to enhance the sector's ability to serve the real economy and manage risks. The initiative extends a financing tool previously used to support other major state banks.

title: Wall Street mixed as strong jobs data and rates weigh on stocks
summary: Wall Street ended the week mixed as Treasury yields and interest-rate expectations remained in focus following the latest nonfarm payrolls report. U.S. employers added 162K jobs, well above economists' 55K forecast, while the previous month was revised to +21K from -23K.

title: Eurometal warns of 300,000 EU factory job cuts due to Chinese competition
summary: Eurometal warns that 300,000 manufacturing jobs in the EU could be lost by the end of 2026 due to expanding competition from China. The trade body plans a protest in Brussels to urge decision-makers to address the issue. Eurometal president Alexander Julius stated that China aims to control complete supply chains rather than just supplying raw materials. The organization highlights that Chinese components face no carbon taxes or levies, creating an uneven playing field for European manufacturers. While the EU has imposed tariffs on electric vehicles and steel, Julius argues these measures do not fully address the component-level competition driving job losses.

title: German far-right AfD projects historic win in Saxony-Anhalt
summary: German far-right party AfD projects a major victory in Saxony-Anhalt, securing 44.5% of the vote ahead of the CDU. State leader Ulrich Siegmund claims a mandate to govern alone, though final results depend on smaller parties crossing the 5% threshold. Intelligence agencies classify the group as extremist, a label Siegmund rejects. Supporters celebrated the outcome as a historic shift in German politics.

title: Sabalenka advances to US Open quarter-finals after defeating Townsend
summary: Defending champion Aryna Sabalenka defeated Taylor Townsend 6-4, 6-3 to reach the quarter-finals at the U.S. Open. The match took place on Arthur Ashe Stadium on Sunday, September 6. Other results included Tommy Paul facing Carlos Alcaraz and Daniil Medvedev playing Frances Tiafoe. The tournament schedule listed multiple matches across Arthur Ashe and Louis Armstrong stadiums.

title: Dozens Trapped After Hostel Collapse in Delhi Kills Three
summary: A five-storey student hostel collapsed in Delhi on Sunday, trapping dozens inside. At least three people died while eight others were rescued, according to police. Construction work in the basement may have weakened the structure. Local officials are leading rescue efforts as authorities search for the building owner.

title: AfD poised for historic win in Saxony-Anhalt state election
summary: Exit polls indicate the far-right AfD party is set to win a historic majority in Saxony-Anhalt, marking a significant shift in German politics. The party's support rose to 44.5 per cent, while Chancellor Merz's CDU fell to 18.5 per cent. AfD leaders claim a clear mandate to implement policies restricting immigration and curbing Islamic expression. However, forming a government depends on whether other parties pass the five per cent threshold and if the CDU can block an AfD-led coalition.

title: German exit polls show AfD leading Saxony-Anhalt regional election
summary: German exit polls indicate the Alternative for Germany party holds a significant lead in Saxony-Anhalt's regional election. The AfD secured approximately 44% of the vote, more than double its result from five years ago. While the party aims to form the nation's first far-right state government, it currently trails an absolute majority. The incumbent Christian Democratic Union dropped to 18.5%, while the Left Party finished third with about 9%. Officials from both the AfD and the ruling CDU commented on the difficult results.

title: Chinese officials report recovery of 12 bodies at mudslide-ravaged Gyirong border crossing
summary: Chinese officials announced the recovery of 12 additional bodies at the Gyirong border crossing following a devastating mudslide. Rescue teams are using excavators and radar to search for hundreds still missing after the disaster killed over 1,300 people. Diplomats expressed frustration over limited information sharing regarding victim identification. Officials stated the disaster occurred on the Nepalese side and called for international cooperation to improve monitoring.

title: US envoys meet Zelensky in Kyiv as frontline battles continue
summary: US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv to discuss peace talks following a meeting with Vladimir Putin. While a temporary truce paused air strikes on capitals, intense fighting persisted along the 1,200-kilometre front line. Discussions focused on next steps and Ukraine's urgent winter energy needs after Russian strikes destroyed 9 gigawatts of power generation. Officials anticipate a formal announcement regarding the negotiations in the coming weeks.

title: Trump administration appeals to Supreme Court over mail-in voting restrictions
summary: The Trump administration asked the Supreme Court to allow restrictions on mail-in voting as states begin sending ballots. Solicitor General John Sauer argued the current court order risks election chaos. This marks the third time the administration has sought Supreme Court intervention on the issue. The dispute centers on an executive order limiting ballot delivery to voters on a federal list. Democratic states and voting rights groups claim the order is unconstitutional.

title: Early results suggest AfD may win Saxony-Anhalt election
summary: Voting is underway in Saxony-Anhalt, where early results indicate the far-right AfD could secure a landslide victory. Nick Holdsworth notes that an AfD government would be the first regional administration led by such a party since the end of World War II. The correspondent describes this potential outcome as forming the first far-right state government since the dark days of Nazism.

title: German far-right AfD wins Saxony-Anhalt election with 44.5% of votes
summary: German exit polls show the far-right AfD leading in Saxony-Anhalt with 44.5% of the vote, according to ARD projections. The party's lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund stated the result makes history, while the incumbent CDU suffered a major setback. Voter turnout reached a record 80%, significantly higher than the 2021 election. Infratest Dimap identified declining confidence in established parties, social security, the economy, and migration as decisive issues. If the AfD forms a government, it would be the first far-right party to lead a German state since World War II.

title: AfD wins landslide in Saxony-Anhalt but government formation remains uncertain
summary: Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party secured a landslide victory in Saxony-Anhalt state elections, polling 44.5 percent of the vote according to early results. The party's co-leader Alice Weidel described the outcome as historic, though it remains unclear if the AfD can form a government alone. Exit polls showed Chancellor Friedrich Merz's conservatives at 18.5 percent, while the Social Democrats and Greens also cleared the parliamentary threshold. The AfD's potential victory challenges Germany's post-war "firewall" policy against extremist parties and places renewed pressure on Merz's leadership. While the party rejects extremism accusations, mainstream parties remain reluctant to cooperate with a group investigated for right-wing ties.

title: Wout van Aert wins shortened Vuelta stage 15 in Cordoba
