Aritra Roy Gosthipaty discussed profiling in PyTorch, while Adarsh covered SGLang, Transformers, and kernels for efficient inference. Adithya S Kolavi spoke on RL environments, and Mansi Agarwal presented on DeviceMesh and DTensor for distributed training. Arkadip Maitra closed with a talk on zero-copy GPU-to-GPU communication. The collaboration aimed to help practitioners become builders of profilers, runtimes, and communication layers. Organizers noted that the event demonstrated real appetite in India for technically serious, systems-oriented ML community events.

title: Health minister warns NHS research may suffer from Palantir mistrust
summary: Health minister James Frith expressed concern that public mistrust of Palantir might negatively impact NHS research, noting a recent increase in patient data opt-outs. While the company claims its technology has improved surgical waiting lists, critics cite its work with the Israeli military and ICE as reasons to end its £330m contract. Frith indicated a policy shift, stating there is no longer a mandatory requirement for trusts to use the Palantir-powered platform, though the government continues to investigate the data's validity.

title: Grindr agrees to pay £26m to settle claims over shared HIV data
summary: Grindr has agreed to pay £26m to settle a lawsuit alleging it shared users' HIV status and other personal information with third parties before 2020. The company stated the settlement includes no admission of liability and disputes the allegations while acknowledging the distress caused to some UK users. Two payments of £13m will be made by December 2024 and March 2027. The lawsuit, led by law firm Austen Hayes, involved more than 11,000 claimants who alleged the app breached UK privacy laws by sharing sensitive data with analytics services Apptimize and Localytics for commercial purposes. Grindr noted that since 2020, it has overhauled its privacy practices and remains committed to user control and transparency.

title: Tesla asks businesses to buy Cybercab fleets despite profit logic
summary: Tesla is currently asking businesses whether they would like to buy and operate their own fleets of Cybercab robotaxis. The article notes that Elon Musk has promoted this model since 2019, claiming owners could earn significant annual profits. However, the text argues that if running such a fleet were genuinely profitable, Tesla would not sell the vehicles to third parties. The author cites MisterGreen, a Dutch leasing firm that went bankrupt in December 2025 after losing $40 million betting on Tesla's promises. The piece concludes that Tesla likely wants fleet buyers to absorb capital costs and depreciation while the company retains high-margin software revenue and network control.

title: Volkswagen ID. Polo receives 30,000 orders with 10-month wait
summary: Volkswagen confirmed that the new ID. Polo EV has received over 30,000 orders, creating a waitlist of at least 10 months according to German newspaper Automobilwoche. The automaker is ramping up production at its Martorell plant in Spain to meet demand while implementing cost-cutting measures under its Future Plan 2030.

title: India increases rail coal shipments as power plant stocks fall
summary: India's Ministry of Coal announced that rail coal deliveries to power plants have increased as stockpiles at dozens of facilities fell to critically low levels. The Central Electricity Authority reported that 53 plants had stocks below 25% by September 5, a rise from 45 in late August. This shortage stems from monsoon rains disrupting supply chains while El Niño conditions drive higher electricity demand. State-owned Coal India Limited stated it remains committed to sustaining these improved supply trends to meet sector requirements.

title: UNEP warns 1.5°C warming threshold exceeded within next few years
summary: The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) published a report predicting the 1.5°C global warming threshold will be exceeded within the next few years. UNEP warns that while the Paris Agreement goal remains valid, avoiding overshoot is no longer realistic under current policies, which could lead to 2.6°C warming by 2100. The agency outlines a necessary pathway of emissions reductions, net-zero targets, and eventual net-negative CO2 emissions to peak and then decline global temperatures, though permanent climate impacts will likely persist regardless of recovery efforts.

title: Iraq Plans to Surpass Saudi Arabia as Top Middle East Oil Producer
summary: Author Simon Watkins argues that Iraq may soon surpass Saudi Arabia as the Middle East's leading oil producer. The article states that Iraq plans to raise output to between 8 million and 10 million barrels per day within six years, a target the author believes is achievable due to three main factors. First, the country holds vast reserves, with the International Energy Agency estimating recoverable resources at about 246 billion barrels. Second, recent efforts to reduce corruption have allowed Western firms to return after previously exiting the market. Third, a $27 billion project ratified by French supermajor TotalEnergies aims to boost production through improved gas capture and field pressure stabilization. Watkins notes that calculations based on super-giant fields suggest a potential capacity of around 11.5 million barrels per day if these initiatives succeed.

title: Energy Security and Load Growth Reshape America's Power Market
summary: Philip Cruver, CEO of Geo2Watts, argues that America's electricity challenge is increasingly an infrastructure issue driven by load growth and security concerns. On August 26, 2026, President Donald Trump declared a national emergency regarding foreign-produced bulk-power equipment, including transformers and circuit breakers. This policy shift prioritizes equipment provenance and supply assurance alongside traditional performance metrics. Cruver introduces the concept of GridValue, which assesses projects based on existing interconnections and location rather than just megawatt-hour costs. He further proposes Infrastructure Arbitrage, a strategy to capture value from underutilized physical assets like retired oil fields and industrial sites. By repurposing these brownfields, developers can avoid new transmission costs while modernizing legacy substations. Federal actions in April and August 2026 reinforce the view that manufacturing and maintaining electrical infrastructure is a strategic national capability. Consequently, the article suggests manufacturers should evolve into providers of secure, modular infrastructure platforms capable of supporting decades of service.

title: China pours concrete for second Zhaoyuan nuclear unit
summary: China Nuclear Engineering & Construction Corp stated that construction began on the second Zhaoyuan nuclear unit after pouring approximately 8,800 cubic metres of concrete on September 5. The project, operated by Shandong Zhaoyuan Nuclear Power Company, is part of a six-unit facility expected to generate 50 TWh annually. This plant will utilize secondary circulation large-scale seawater cooling systems, marking a first for China.

title: Alibaba and Coupang offer different investment paths for 2026
summary: The article compares Alibaba Group and Coupang Inc as investment options for 2026, highlighting their distinct geographic focuses and capital structures. Alibaba reported fiscal 2026 revenue of $152.2 billion with a 3% increase, though net margins contracted to 10%. Coupang achieved 14% revenue growth to $34.5 billion in fiscal 2025, maintaining a narrow 0.6% net margin while reinvesting for expansion.

title: Microsoft stock faces cash flow test near all-time high
summary: Microsoft shares are trading near a $549.20 all-time high, yet analysts maintain a Hold rating because a massive 80% surge in capital spending to $116 billion is severely impacting free cash flow. Although the company achieved $331.839 billion in revenue and Azure revenue exceeded $100 billion, the widening gap between these growth metrics and cash generation is the critical variable determining whether the stock can sustain its climb or stall below current levels.

title: OpenAI Chief Scientist Jacob Pfau warns of unprepared risks from rapidly advancing AI capabilities
summary: OpenAI Chief Scientist Jacob Pfau warns that no one is prepared for the consequences of rapidly advancing AI, urging caution and safety measures. He highlights risks like recursive self-improvement and the difficulty of aligning powerful systems with human values, calling for international cooperation and independent auditing to ensure safe development.

title: Apple Event 2026: John Ternus hosts while Tim Cook watches as executive chairman
summary: Bloomberg reports that Apple CEO John Ternus will host the September 9, 2026 event, while former CEO Tim Cook will attend as an audience member without appearing in the launch video. The company aims to position Ternus as the primary face for upcoming products, though Cook retains his role as executive chairman overseeing policy and international relations.

title: Federal investigators begin search for cause of Amazon cargo jet crash
summary: Federal investigators initiated a search for the cause of a Boeing 767 cargo jet crash at Miami International Airport on Sunday, which killed five people and injured five others. The aircraft, operated by contractor 21 Air for Amazon, overshot the runway around 2pm after arriving from San Juan, Puerto Rico. Video footage showed the plane landing far down the runway and moving abnormally fast before coming to rest in a parking lot. Aviation experts noted the plane may have landed too fast to stop in time, with some suggesting tail winds contributed to the float. The National Transportation Safety Board announced a news conference, while Amazon confirmed the incident and pledged cooperation with the investigation.

title: Huawei launches tri-fold smartphone as rivals prepare to follow
summary: Huawei launched its new Mate XT2 tri-fold smartphone series in Guangzhou on Monday, with prices starting at 19,999 yuan and sales beginning on September 12. Huawei Executive Director Richard Yu told a press conference that pricing was challenging due to sharply risen memory costs. The new phones feature the Kirin 9050 Pro chip and a redesigned folding mechanism. Xiaomi is set to launch a rival device later Monday, while Apple is expected to unveil a foldable phone on Wednesday. Huawei currently holds a 68 percent share of foldable phone shipments in China, according to Smart Analytics Global.

title: Authors analyze how 1930s US forestation policy altered climate and farming
summary: The authors report that a 1930s US Midwest forestation program increased precipitation and decreased temperatures, leading farmers to expand corn acreage and adopt water-intensive practices. This study isolates climate effects from afforestation to show how tree planting altered agricultural development and farm structures.

title: Cheryl Hachem studies how loan rates and wage contracts interact in banking
summary: NBER Working Paper 35696 author Cheryl Hachem reports that banks jointly design loan rates and wage contracts to manage agency problems and diagnostic repayment information. The study finds that capital requirements can cap failure pay and potentially create permanent cycles where banks alternate between different contract types and risk-taking levels.

title: German far-right AfD wins landslide in Saxony-Anhalt
summary: Germany's nationalist AfD party won a landslide victory in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, potentially making it the first far-right party to gain power since World War II. The result challenges the establishment's strategy of excluding the far right from coalitions. ING analysts noted that the looming political dysfunction is not the best situation for a country and economy that still needs substantial reforms.

title: R.K. Narayan publishes a condensed version of The Mahabharata
summary: R.K. Narayan has published a condensed version of The Mahabharata, one of Hinduism's central epics. The author intentionally avoided historical analysis, noting that cold factual research seems like catching a rainbow with one's fingers. Instead, the book focuses on core story episodes relevant to understanding contemporary India. The original text comprises 100,000 verses.

title: Jaguar Land Rover plans 4,000 job cuts amid global sales decline
summary: Jaguar Land Rover has decided to reduce its workforce by 4,000 positions after experiencing significant sales declines across major markets. The automotive manufacturer attributes these struggles to a devastating cyber-attack that paralyzed production last year, falling sales in China due to aggressive local competition, and reduced US sales caused by import tariffs. Additionally, the company faces high energy costs in the UK and intense rivalry from Chinese brands expanding into Europe. While investing billions in electric vehicle development, executives believe a major overhaul is essential to restore profitability. This decision impacts thousands of employees and suppliers, who are already facing high operational expenses. The company aims to streamline operations as it prepares to launch its new all-electric Jaguar brand later this year.

title: Investigators probe why Amazon jet did not abort landing before Miami crash
summary: Federal authorities are investigating the fatal crash of an Amazon cargo plane at Miami International Airport, focusing on whether the aircraft touched down too late to stop safely. The Boeing 767, operated by North Carolina-based 21 Air, left the runway and struck vehicles, killing at least five people. Aviation analysts note that standard procedures require a touchdown within the first 3,000 feet; if exceeded, pilots should abort the landing. Former Transportation Department Inspector General Mary Schiavo observed that video footage shows the jet floating far down the airstrip without pitching its nose up. She stated that a tailwind could have contributed to the float. The National Transportation Safety Board has arrived in Miami to lead the inquiry. Amazon released a statement expressing heartbreak and promising full cooperation with investigators.

title: Trump tariffs on Canadian goods threaten to raise hockey equipment prices
summary: President Donald Trump's administration recently imposed 50% tariffs on Canadian goods, a move that could significantly impact hockey equipment prices. Families already struggle with rising costs, as a goaltender's helmet price jumped from $400 to $1,000 in recent years. John Merola of B&R Sports noted that custom goalie gear and specialized skates made in Canada fall directly under these trade rules. Although most hockey sticks are imported from China, the Sports & Fitness Industry Association warns that persistent tariffs could stunt participation growth. Economics professor Chris Douglas suggests that while an immediate 50% price jump is unlikely, long-term duties could eventually force manufacturers to raise prices or relocate production away from Canada.

title: Anak Krakatau eruption strands 340,000 passengers as Indonesian airports remain closed
summary: More than 340,000 passengers have been left stranded across Indonesia after the Anak Krakatau volcano erupted, disrupting nearly 3,000 flights and forcing airports to suspend operations for a second day. Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport decided not to reopen as planned because volcanic ash remained near its airspace, with flights resuming at 23:59 on Monday. The Geological Agency warned that the probability of further eruptions remains high, while ash reached heights of 6,000m on the Java side and 15,000m on the Sumatra side. Authorities have prohibited ships from entering a 3km exclusion zone around the active crater, and Transport Minister Dudy Purwagandhi stated that the duration of the closures cannot be ascertained due to dynamic weather conditions.

title: Indigenous communities in Panama's Darién test biodiversity credits to fund conservation
summary: Four Indigenous Wounaan and Emberá-Wounaan villages in Panama's Darién forest launched a biodiversity monitoring project to document their conservation status and access the emerging biodiversity credits market. Facing pressure from illegal logging and agricultural expansion, these communities recorded more than 200 species across 18,000 hectares using camera traps and bioacoustic recorders. The data serves as a baseline for joining the nature finance industry, which advocates claim can fund conservation efforts. Although proponents suggest the market has learned from carbon credit mistakes, observers note it is too early to evaluate its promises. The FSC Indigenous Foundation guided the project, ensuring Indigenous science and knowledge directed all stages. Communities now partner with Savimbo to sell credits, emphasizing transparency and community control over funds. While the initiative represents a pioneering step, experts caution that proving biodiversity loss without intervention remains complex and the market's impact is yet to be fully measured.

title: UN human rights chief warns AI poses existential risk
summary: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk warned that artificial intelligence could pose an existential risk to humanity, calling for strict safety guarantees. Speaking in Geneva, Turk condemned Russia's reported use of autonomous drones in Ukraine and demanded accountability for 23 deaths in US immigration custody. He also pledged to scrutinize businesses fueling global conflicts.

title: Former war criminal Ratko Mladic buried with military honors in Belgrade
summary: Thousands gathered in Belgrade on Monday for the funeral and burial of Ratko Mladic, a former Bosnian Serb army commander convicted of genocide. Serbian Patriarch Porfirije officiated the service, and Mladic was laid to rest at Topcider Cemetery beside his daughter. President Aleksandar Vucic did not attend, citing a scheduled visit from Uzbekistan, and later dismissed EU criticism of the military honors as 'stupid.' Informer TV broadcast the event as a 'magnificent farewell' without mentioning the Srebrenica massacre. Political scientist Dejan Bursac told DW that Vucic is using the funeral to generate nationalist support ahead of snap elections expected on October 25. Analysts note that both the ruling party and the student opposition movement are avoiding alienating nationalistically minded voters in a race expected to be decided by a narrow margin.

title: Avalanche kills at least 11 climbers in southern Russia
summary: Local emergency services reported that an avalanche in Russia's Kabardino-Balkaria Republic killed at least 11 climbers and injured six others. The disaster occurred on Mount Mizhirgi, a high peak in the North Caucasus region, where the snowslide swept down the mountain slope.

title: Spain's top court orders criminal probe into Ceuta migrant influx
summary: Spain's Audiencia Nacional court has ordered a criminal investigation into the arrival of tens of thousands of migrants in Ceuta in July. Investigating judge María Tardón stated that the influx constitutes a method of hybrid warfare, noting a police report highlighting "total permissiveness" by Moroccan security forces. While the judge ruled the court has jurisdiction over crimes against territorial integrity, the Spanish government says there is no conclusive evidence that Rabat was responsible for the mass entry, which saw more than 70,000 migrants cross into the exclave.

title: IAEA reports Iran blocking inspectors amid Hormuz threats
summary: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi informed the Board of Governors that Iran has failed to provide information on declared nuclear materials and denied inspectors on-site access. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei dismissed these reports as Western political pressure and warned of countermeasures if a new UN Security Council resolution is passed. Meanwhile, Iran's parliament speaker warned US energy assets face retaliatory strikes, while the IRGC warned vessels off the southern Hormuz corridor.

title: Poorest Americans struggle to find housing as low-income units remain vacant
summary: The Associated Press reports that the poorest Americans cannot find housing even as low-income units sit empty. Mathew Davis, a resident of an Austin shelter, earns a few hundred dollars monthly yet cannot afford a $450 tiny home. A survey of state housing agencies indicates most low-income housing is for those earning 50% of an area's median income or above. The National Low Income Housing Coalition notes only 4 million affordable units exist for 11 million extremely low-income households. Experts like Chris Edwards of the Cato Institute argue the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit is inefficient, suggesting direct tenant subsidies would be better. In Austin, over 4,500 affordable units remain vacant as rents approach market rates. Developers state units for extremely low-income people are not economically feasible without extraordinary subsidies. Meanwhile, some renters prefer market-rate apartments for faster approval despite higher costs.

title: Wuhan authorities fine Guo Degang's theater and promoter for altered patriotic song
summary: Wuhan authorities fined a theater and its promoter after comedian Guo Degang altered lyrics of a patriotic song during a performance. The Culture and Tourism Bureau stated the comedian distorted a revolutionary song and will deal seriously with relevant personnel. Multiple shows were canceled following the incident, and Guo has not performed publicly since. The bureau noted that revolutionary songs carry the memory of the nation's War of Resistance and cannot be distorted.

title: Dangote refinery prepares major IPO to fund expansion
summary: Nigeria's Dangote refinery is preparing an initial public offering expected to raise around 1.6 billion dollars to fund capacity expansion. The company plans to increase refining capacity from 650,000 barrels per day to 1.4 million barrels per day, potentially making it the world's largest refinery. The IPO order book is expected to open on September 14, with formal signing of listing documents taking place Monday.

title: AfD surge in Saxony-Anhalt raises concerns for France's far right
summary: Exit polls showed the Alternative for Germany (AfD) surged into first place in Saxony-Anhalt state elections on Sunday, putting a far-right party on the cusp of power at state level for the first time since World War Two. The result has garnered attention across Europe, not least in France where national elections next year could see far-right veteran Marine Le Pen become president.

title: North Korea and Russia open first road bridge amid Ukrainian security concerns
summary: North Korea and Russia have opened their first road bridge over the Tumen river, a development Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin described as a historic event intended to strengthen economic ties. The Russian government stated up to 300 vehicles will cross daily, though Ukrainian officials worry the bridge could facilitate the transport of military equipment. While Moscow and Pyongyang celebrate the infrastructure as a symbol of deepening cooperation, Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and human rights groups fear it will become a covert logistics corridor for North Korean troops and Russian technology during the ongoing war.

title: Raymond Depardon revisits his photojournalist past at Visa Pour l'Image festival
summary: Raymond Depardon revisits his photojournalist past at the Visa Pour l'Image festival. The article notes this event but provides no further details due to a loading error.

title: Former Sierra Leone President Koroma Returns After Treason Charges Dropped
summary: Former Sierra Leone President Ernest Bai Koroma returned to Freetown on Sunday after authorities dropped treason charges against him regarding a 2023 coup attempt. An AFP journalist reported that Koroma arrived accompanied by Nigerian officials and was welcomed by Sierra Leonean government representatives and opposition party members. The justice ministry had previously cleared him to travel for medical treatment, though he remained abroad for more than two years. His return comes ahead of the 2028 presidential elections, following the July dropping of charges without a stated reason.

title: UN watchdog says secret Syrian reactor was almost complete
summary: The UN nuclear watchdog reported that an undeclared Syrian nuclear reactor constructed during the Assad era was almost complete, representing a significant step toward nuclear weapons capability. IAEA inspectors discovered the facility in Deir Ezzor along with a fuel fabrication plant and a storage site holding approximately 73 tonnes of natural uranium metal. Agency head Rafael Grossi noted the reactor was highly efficient for producing fissile material and suggested the previous government may have used explosions to hinder investigation. While Grossi praised Damascus for reporting the site, he stated the IAEA board must decide on the Syria file, with a draft resolution expected to propose closing the case.

title: France reacts with surprise to far-right victory in German Saxony-Anhalt
summary: The provided text contains only an error message regarding a failed site load and does not include the article body or headline needed to summarize the story.

title: Pakistan ministers debate creating new provinces to improve governance
summary: A politically sensitive debate has reignited in Pakistan regarding whether its current four-province system can effectively govern a population of around 260 million people. Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal recently called for a national discussion on administrative reform, proposing the creation of 12 to 15 new provinces or the establishment of 160 empowered district governments. While Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and Defense Minister Khawaja Asif support decentralization, no formal decision has been taken due to disagreements within the ruling coalition. Experts like Miftah Ismail and Abid Qaiyum Suleri argue that smaller provinces are not a substitute for empowered local governments and caution that redrawing boundaries could reopen disputes over water and resources. Political resistance has already emerged, particularly from Sindh's provincial assembly, highlighting the risks of ethnic tension and the complexity of redistributing power without creating new conflicts.

title: New Police Commissioner sets up anti-stabbing squads in Hubballi-Dharwad
summary: New Police Commissioner Bhushan Borase announced the formation of anti-stabbing squads across all police stations in Hubballi-Dharwad to tackle increasing stabbing incidents and prepare for the Ganesha festival. The squads became operational on Sunday, during which over 215 vehicles were checked. On Monday, police arrested a local youth, Gangadhar Anand Madiwalar, after he was filmed brandishing a sword. Commissioner Borase warned of strict action under the Arms Act for those found with weapons and urged the public to report illegal activities.

title: West Bengal CM announces crackdown on child marriage after 60,000 underage deliveries
summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced a statewide crackdown on child marriage after the state health department reported nearly 60,000 institutional deliveries involving underage girls between January and June. Adhikari ordered house-to-house drives to identify cases, warning that husbands, facilitators, and officials involved would face arrests, imprisonment, and withdrawal of government welfare benefits under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act and the POCSO Act.

title: Election Commission announces bypolls for five Assembly seats and one Lok Sabha seat
summary: The Election Commission announced bypolls for five Assembly constituencies and one Lok Sabha seat, with voting scheduled for October 6 and vote counting on October 9. The Nandigram Assembly seat in West Bengal is a key contest, having been vacated by Chief Minister and BJP leader Suvendu Adhikari. The commission stated that EVMs and VVPATs will be used at all polling stations to ensure a smooth process.

title: Apple stock rises 18% ahead of Sept. 9 event: Is it still a buy?
summary: Apple stock has risen 18% year-to-date, outpacing peers like Microsoft and Alphabet as investors anticipate the Sept. 9 product event. Zacks reports the launch will feature the iPhone 18 Pro, powered by a new 2-nanometer chip, and potentially Apple's first foldable iPhone Ultra. While iPhone revenue grew 22% in the June quarter, 24/7 Wall St. notes memory costs drove a sequential decline in gross margins. Zacks also highlights supply chain constraints and a projected drop in gross margins to 47%-48%. With Apple trading at 33.6 times earnings, Hindustan Times reports that the upcoming event is critical to justify the stock's premium valuation against rivals.

title: RBI absorbs Rs 6 lakh crore amid record banking liquidity surplus
summary: The Reserve Bank of India intensified liquidity absorption measures on Monday, mopping up over Rs 6 lakh crore amid a record surplus of Rs 10.73 lakh crore. While the initial Variable Reserve Repo Rate auction saw tepid demand, a subsequent overnight auction received better bids. Madhavi Arora of Emkay Global noted that limited VRRR success implies overnight rates could remain lower than policy rates. Bankers argue the RBI must manage this abundance through forex sales and other tools given sub-par monsoons and elevated crude prices. The central bank has absorbed funds following large inflows through the FCNR(B) deposit scheme, which contributed 92 per cent of the $136.3 billion raised via special swap windows by end-August.

title: RBI absorbs over Rs 3.53 lakh crore via VRRR auction to manage liquidity
summary: The Reserve Bank of India absorbed over Rs 3.53 lakh crore through a one-day Variable Rate Reverse Repo auction to manage excess liquidity in the banking system. The central bank accepted all bids at a 5.24 per cent rate, absorbing over 70 per cent of the notified amount. This move follows a surge in foreign currency inflows of $73 billion through the FCNR(B) scheme, which has prompted the RBI to step up liquidity absorption operations to ensure financial stability.

title: Trump shares AI image of Intel stock jump and claims billions in gains
summary: US President Donald Trump shared an AI-generated image on Truth Social depicting himself trading Intel stock from $20 to $95, claiming he made hundreds of billions for the US. Intel shares closed at $95.80 on September 4. Government filings reportedly show accounts tied to Trump building positions in Intel and Dell Technologies before public posts about the companies. The US government's reported 9.9% stake in Intel was acquired at $20.47 per share in August 2025. Trump's latest stock-related post was part of a wider social media spree featuring apparently AI-generated images portraying him in exaggerated roles and labeling territories as US possessions.

title: Former RBI Governor urges incentives for more small finance banks
summary: Former RBI Governor C Rangarajan urged the Reserve Bank of India to incentivize the creation of more small finance banks, noting the sector currently has only 11 institutions. Speaking at Equitas Small Finance Bank's Chennai office inauguration, he highlighted the bank as a potential model for universal licensing. Equitas reported a 27% year-on-year increase in gross advances to ₹47,641 crore as of June 2026, with deposits reaching ₹48,976 crore.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang declares AGI has arrived after OpenAI launches Astra
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang declared on social media that artificial general intelligence has arrived after OpenAI unveiled its new Astra model. Huang stated that 400,000 additional graphics processing units will soon go live to support further AI development. OpenAI president Greg Brockman described the launch as a historic turning point, yet industry figures like Gary Marcus and Sam Altman have urged caution regarding the term AGI. The report notes that major development groups remain heavily reliant on Nvidia's processors for their operations.

title: Jaguar Land Rover plans to cut 4,000 jobs over two years
summary: Jaguar Land Rover has confirmed plans to cut about 4,000 jobs over the next two years to save £1.7 billion, citing tariffs, competition, and a cyber-attack. Chief Executive PB Balaji stated the reductions will affect senior and R&D roles more heavily. Business Minister Jonathan Reynolds ruled out a taxpayer bailout, noting the company has not used a previously agreed £1.5 billion loan facility. Reynolds is due to hold talks with Balaji and Unite General Secretary Sharon Graham regarding the planned cuts.

title: Minister Sridhar Babu blames KCR for BRS assault on cops
summary: Legislative Affairs Minister D. Sridhar Babu launched a counter-attack against the BRS on Monday, condemning MLC Tata Madhu for disparaging comments against the Assembly Speaker. Babu stated that KCR bore direct responsibility for the outrage and alleged that KTR physically assaulted police personnel. The minister asserted that the BRS must tender an unconditional apology to the Speaker before any other legislative business is taken up.

title: Maruti Suzuki raises prices on select models by up to 20,000 rupees
summary: Maruti Suzuki India announced on Monday that it will increase prices on select passenger vehicle models by up to 20,000 rupees effective this month. The company attributed the move to enduring inflationary pressures and an adverse cost environment, noting that it has attempted to mitigate costs through internal measures. In a regulatory filing, Maruti Suzuki stated it is constrained to pass on a portion of increased costs while striving to keep the impact on customers to a minimum. This marks the second price hike for the manufacturer in recent months, following an earlier increase of up to 30,000 rupees in August. Other automakers, including Tata Motors and Hyundai Motor India, have also recently announced price revisions across their portfolios.

title: Election Commission announces October 6 by-polls for West Bengal seats
summary: The Election Commission announced by-polls for West Bengal's Nandigram and Rejinagar assembly seats following the resignations of Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and AJUP chief Humayun Kabir. Voting is scheduled for October 6 with vote counting on October 9, and the entire election process will be completed by October 11. The EC stated that the gazette notification will be issued on September 9, with the last date for filing nominations set for September 16. EVMs and VVPATs will be used at all polling stations, and the EPIC card remains the principal identification document.

title: Madurai Bench directs state to report on Kansapuram caste clash
summary: The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court directed the State to file a report on a public interest litigation petition filed by advocate V. Periyasamy regarding caste tensions in Kansapuram. The petitioner, representing the Devendrakula Vellalar community, alleged intimidation by the Maravar community and sought directions to implement the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act to restore peace. The court posted the matter for further hearing to October 7.

title: Voters struggle with midnight hearings and inaccessible notices in Karnataka
summary: Voters in Bengaluru face difficulties resolving electoral roll discrepancies due to midnight hearing schedules and inaccessible Booth Level Officers. Activist Vinay Sreenivas noted minor name differences caused confusion, while elderly voters struggled to navigate the process. Many complain that despite public notice lists lacking venue details, they must visit offices in person. Voters have requested English notices, noting the current Kannada-only format is difficult to understand. The Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer had previously assured physical copies would be available.

title: DAC clears 1.1 lakh crore military capability boost proposals
summary: The defence ministry said the Rajnath Singh-led Defence Acquisition Council cleared proposals worth 1.1 lakh crore to enhance the capabilities of the Indian armed forces. The plan includes integrating Russian-origin missiles with Sukhoi-30 fighters and acquiring new systems for the army, navy, and air force. The defence ministry stated that approximately 98% of these procurements will be made from Indian industry, aligning with the government's goal to boost defence manufacturing.

title: Omar Abdullah criticizes BJP over delayed Jammu and Kashmir statehood
summary: In an episode of Speakeasy with Amit Baruah, Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah criticized the BJP-led Union government for failing to restore statehood in the region. Abdullah argued that people were never informed that statehood depended on electing a BJP government. He also discussed challenges of governing a Union Territory, including institutional constraints and continuing detentions, while reflecting on his second tenure compared to his first term from 2009 to 2015.

title: Uttar Pradesh leads Jal Jeevan Mission with 2.36 crore rural tap connections
summary: Uttar Pradesh has emerged as the largest contributor to India's Jal Jeevan Mission, connecting more than 2.36 crore rural households and laying over 5.07 lakh km of pipelines by March 2025. The state aims to provide tap water to all 2.62 crore rural households by 2028. The Union Cabinet extended the mission until December 2028, restructuring it as JJM 2.0 with a focus on reliable service delivery and source sustainability. While significant progress has been made, the long-term challenge remains ensuring that these connections deliver safe and reliable water consistently.

title: Delhi HC orders probe into Satya Niketan collapse after seven deaths
summary: Rescue efforts at the collapsed Satya Niketan building in Delhi concluded after 24 hours, leaving seven people dead according to officials. The Delhi High Court criticized both the Municipal Corporation of Delhi and Delhi University for failing to ensure adequate safety measures and ordered a high-level inquiry into the tragedy. Authorities are now sealing illegal structures and conducting a comprehensive audit of student housing facilities. While the Delhi government intensified inspections, political parties engaged in public disputes regarding accountability. The court has listed the matter for a hearing on 25 September, requiring agencies to file replies within 10 days.

title: Sonia Gandhi publishes memoir and writes frequent articles criticizing Modi
summary: Sonia Gandhi has emerged as a prominent writer and critic following her decision to limit her political role. Since June 2024, she has published twelve articles in newspapers, frequently attacking Prime Minister Narendra Modi's governance and policies. Her writings cover diverse topics, including the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test scandal, the closure of public schools, and India's response to the conflict in Gaza. Additionally, she has criticized the government's amendment to the Flag Code, which allows machine-made flags. Her upcoming memoir, Belonging, is set to be released after she refused to remove references to Modi and the RSS from the text. The author suggests her memoir may provide insights into dynastic politics and the hardships faced by religious minorities in India.

title: Delhi CM Rekha Gupta vows strict action after Satya Niketan collapse
summary: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta announced that the government is treating the Satya Niketan building collapse with utmost seriousness, stating that anyone found guilty will not be spared. She ordered the immediate sealing of buildings with unauthorized fifth floors across Delhi and confirmed the suspension of multiple officials. Additionally, the Chief Minister's Office revealed plans to make periodic structural audits mandatory for public buildings. MCD Commissioner Sanjeev Khirwar expressed grief over the seven lives lost and announced the demolition of the adjacent building.

title: PM Modi's Vadodara event sold out in one hour on BookMyShow
summary: The Vadodara Municipal Corporation utilized the private platform BookMyShow to manage free registrations for Prime Minister Narendra Modi's event, which sold out in one hour. Over 42,000 additional applicants were placed on a waiting list. During his visit, Modi will inaugurate the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor and lay foundation stones for various railway and highway projects. He will subsequently travel to Mumbai to inaugurate the Global Fintech Fest 2026, according to the report.

title: Gauhati HC orders Assam to pay ₹2 lakh to family of woman pushed to Bangladesh
summary: The Gauhati High Court has ordered the Assam government to pay 2 lakh as interim compensation to Mujammel Hoque, the husband of Mumtaz Begum, after she was pushed into Bangladesh without her family being informed. A bench of justices Kalyan Rai Surana and Susmita Phukan Khaund passed this order on September 3 following a habeas corpus petition. The court noted that the state failed to provide Begum or her family with the tribunal order or an opportunity to appeal before her expulsion. This marks the first instance where a court has imposed a cost on the state for violating deportation rules by pushing a person into Bangladesh. The bench also directed the Ministry of External Affairs to make an endeavour to locate Begum in Bangladesh and expatriate her to India. Additionally, the court asked the Assam home department to order an inquiry into the episode and directed district superintendents of police to ensure declared foreign nationals are informed of tribunal orders before custody.

title: Sport needs attention to survive, but can it survive the attention economy?
summary: The author of Offside explores the tension between sport's need for visibility and the dangers of the attention economy. The piece notes that while legendary athletes like George Best and Muhammad Ali generated headlines through their skills and personalities, modern influencers often lack any connection to the sport itself. The author cites the Invisible Gorilla experiment to illustrate how human attention is limited and easily diverted by digital noise. Specific incidents, such as a photoshoot interrupting Naomi Osaka's preparation at the US Open and the online harassment of powerlifter Keyaa Kunal Banerji, are used to demonstrate how the pursuit of engagement can degrade the sporting experience. Ultimately, the author questions whether sport can maintain its integrity while competing for scarce attention against algorithms and viral trends.

title: Investors watch Adani Power, Swiggy, Shiprocket shares on Tuesday
summary: Indian stock market investors are likely to track several companies on Tuesday, 8 September, following key business developments, order wins, and investment announcements. The Indian stock market extended its losing streak to a fourth consecutive session on Monday, September 7, with benchmark indices ending lower amid continued selling pressure. Technology stocks led the losses after stronger-than-expected US jobs data boosted expectations of a September interest rate hike by the US Federal Reserve. Container Corporation of India secured an ₹89.09 crore contract from Eastern Railway for the supply of 12 rakes of BLSS wagons. Swiggy plans to sell its entire stake in Lynk Logistics to Udaan for ₹500 crore. Adani Power received a Letter of Intent after the Committee of Creditors approved its resolution plan for GVK Energy. The Defence Acquisition Council accorded in-principle approval for various defence acquisition proposals worth around ₹1.10 lakh crore. Shiprocket reported a narrower consolidated loss of ₹13.71 crore in the June quarter. Ksheera Sagar, a Market Research Analyst at LiveMint, compiled these updates.

title: Kerala police book journalist Aparna Kurup for alleged religious sentiment hurt
summary: Kochi Cyber Police booked television journalist Aparna Kurup under Sections 192, 299, 302, 353(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and Section 120(o) of the Kerala Police Act, 2011. The police registered the case on Monday following a complaint by Abdul Hakkim regarding Kurup's alleged hurt to religious sentiments while anchoring a debate on Kanthapuram A P Aboobacker Musliyar's remarks. Police stated the FIR alleged Kurup intended to cause a breach of peace and deliberately hurt religious feelings. The move followed protests by UDF leaders against a separate case against an Islamist leader who threatened Kurup with physical assault. BJP national executive member P K Krishnadas criticized the UDF government, alleging pressure from religious groups influenced the administration. The Home Department directed police not to proceed with the case against the Islamist leader after the protest.

title: Calcutta HC sets aside arrest warrant against TMC MP Mahua Moitra
summary: The Calcutta High Court on Monday set aside an arrest warrant against TMC MP Mahua Moitra and ordered the case transferred to the special MP/MLA court at Bidhannagar. A division bench directed the special court to treat the complaint regarding alleged hate speech as being at the pre-cognisance stage. Moitra's lawyer argued the allegations are baseless and the case must be tried before the designated court since the speeches occurred during her tenure as an MP.

title: Delhi Police issues security advisory ahead of 2026 BRICS Summit
summary: Delhi Police has issued a security advisory for the 18th BRICS Summit, which will be hosted in New Delhi on September 12 and 13. The advisory urges citizens to remain alert at public places, report any suspicious activity, and avoid unnecessary gatherings near sensitive locations. Hotel and guest house operators have been directed to maintain visitor records and verify guests properly. Residents are also advised to ensure police verification for domestic helps and tenants.

title: Jio Platforms plans November IPO with global roadshows starting next week
summary: People familiar with the matter said Jio Platforms will begin investor roadshows next week while targeting an initial public offering in November. The digital and telecommunications arm of Reliance Industries plans meetings across the US, Singapore, Hong Kong, London, and the Middle East. Jio Platforms filed draft documents in June and received regulatory approval in August for an issuance of up to 270 million new shares, which could raise as much as $4 billion. The company intends to use proceeds to repay debt, though details regarding size, valuation, and timing remain subject to change during ongoing deliberations with banks.

title: Two Bihar residents arrested in Tripura with factory-made pistols
summary: NCC Police and Assam Rifles arrested two men from Bihar in West Tripura and recovered two 9mm pistols, three magazines, and live rounds during a joint operation on September 6. Subrata Barman, SDPO, stated that an FIR was registered and the accused will be produced before a local court today for remand and detailed interrogation regarding the source and purpose of the weapons.

title: Temple head urges Hindus to avoid meat during Durga Puja, drawing sharp political criticism
summary: Dhirendra Shastri, the head of the Bageshwar Dham temple, urged Hindus to avoid eating non-vegetarian food during Durga Puja, describing the meat as "dirty" and claiming those who consume it cannot be considered religious. The Trinamool Congress and BJP leaders strongly criticized his comments, arguing that dietary choices are personal and that no one has the right to dictate how Bengalis celebrate their cultural heritage. Shastri's remarks sparked a wider debate about religious traditions and food culture in West Bengal.

title: Osama Manzar questions whether India's data centers represent true development
summary: Osama Manzar, founder of the Digital Empowerment Foundation, argues that India's government is treating data centers as developmental activities without adequately consulting local communities. Manzar notes that while internet penetration in India has risen from 1.2% to over 70%, the rapid expansion of data centers poses risks of extractive technology. He points out that these facilities are projected to consume water equivalent to 1.3 billion people's annual domestic needs and electricity matching the demand of 650 million people by 2030. Manzar criticizes the lack of awareness among locals, stating that terms like 'data center' are not understood until construction begins. He advocates for hyperlocal, multi-distributed data centers that serve local needs rather than acting as data waste centers for global elites. The interview, originally published in Rest of World, emphasizes the need for genuine community consultation and responsible development practices.

title: Historic CAPE ratio warning appears for sixth time in 155 years
summary: Hindustan Times reports that the US stock market's CAPE ratio has crossed 30 for only the sixth time in 155 years, currently sitting at 41.1. This valuation measure compares stock prices to average inflation-adjusted earnings over a decade, and the current reading is more than double the historical average of 17.8. While the article notes that previous instances of such high valuations were followed by significant market corrections, it clarifies that the metric serves as a warning light rather than a precise crash predictor. The piece highlights potential risks from rising interest rates, which could impact the current AI investment boom. Senior Content Producer Durva More writes that investors should remain cautious but avoid panic, focusing instead on building portfolios resilient to volatility.

title: Doctors warn AI transcriptions create errors and waste time
summary: Two doctors writing to a newspaper report that AI transcriptions in their practice frequently contain errors and contradictions. Dr Mary Gibbs and Debbie Cameron state that these tools do not save time, as clinicians must still proofread the long, repetitive accounts and cannot trust the information written by the AI. They warn that relying on this technology risks losing essential clinical skills and could harm patients.

title: Tesla data confirms driver-assist system was active during fatal stop sign crash
summary: A Tesla Model 3 struck a Honda Civic at a stop sign in Buena Vista Township, New Jersey, killing the Civic's driver. While police described the incident as a failure to stop, Tesla's own report to the NHTSA confirms the vehicle's driver-assist system was 'Verified Engaged' at the time of impact. The report redacts critical details regarding the software version and crash narrative. The article suggests the system was likely Full Self-Driving, as basic Autopilot does not process stop signs. Tesla maintains that the human driver remains responsible for Level 2 systems, but the redacted data prevents a full understanding of the event.

title: Russia Vows to Keep Selling Oil to India Despite U.S. Tariff Threat
summary: Russia's Ambassador to India, Denis Alipov, told Asian News International that Moscow will remain a key crude supplier to India despite U.S. tariff threats. Alipov criticized planned U.S. legislation, noting that excluding Russian oil would harm global energy markets. Meanwhile, India's crude imports from Russia eased in August due to Ukrainian attacks and competition from China. Analysts suggest a U.S. bill proposing 100% tariffs on major Russian oil buyers is unlikely to pass the House before November's mid-term elections.

title: Port Authority and CALSTART launch $45M electric truck incentive plan
summary: The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey and CALSTART announced a $45 million program to incentivize zero-emission trucks and charging infrastructure at the port. Funded by a larger EPA grant, the initiative includes point-of-sale vouchers and funding for new charging hubs to help drayage operators modernize their fleets. CALSTART Executive Vice President Alycia Gilde stated the partnership lowers barriers for operators, while Port Authority Executive Director Kathryn Garcia noted the funds support the Authority's net-zero commitment by 2050.

title: Author argues modern warfare consumes nonrenewable metals needed for high-tech future
summary: Kurt Cobb argues that modern warfare is rapidly depleting the nonrenewable metals essential for high-tech applications. The author highlights that while civilian devices containing strategic minerals can often be recycled, military applications frequently result in the total destruction of these materials, rendering them unrecoverable. Cobb references the law of entropy to explain that all nonrenewable resources will eventually degrade, noting that current extraction rates for minerals like lithium have increased dramatically since 1970. He questions whether humanity can sustain such rapid growth in resource extraction as lower-grade ores are depleted. Ultimately, the author contends that the global scramble to secure these supplies for military use will likely fall short of goals, leaving fewer resources available to build the promised high-tech future.

title: Serbia's EPS issues call to acquire renewable energy projects
summary: State-owned utility Elektroprivreda Srbije issued a public call inviting investors to acquire or co-develop renewable energy projects. CEO Dušan Živković stated the initiative aims to diversify the portfolio and accelerate renewable investments through a transparent competitive process. The call targets solar, wind, hybrid, waste-to-energy, and green hydrogen projects, with letters of intent due within 30 days.

title: Slovenia's new government criticizes predecessor over green transition strategy
summary: Slovenia's new government criticized the previous administration for a misguided green transition policy that neglected energy sovereignty, causing domestic electricity generation to fall from 97% in 2024 to 82% in 2025. The government stated that unfavorable hydrological conditions and the scaled-back operation of the Šoštanj thermal power plant contributed to the decline. According to the Ministry of Infrastructure and Energy, the new administration under Prime Minister Janez Janša will prioritize security of supply and domestic production over activist energy policies.

title: Apple may launch iPhone 18 Pro, foldable iPhone, and new watches at September event
summary: Apple is expected to unveil the iPhone 18 Pro series, a potential foldable iPhone, and new Apple Watch models at its September 9 event, according to reports. The new CEO, John Ternus, may lead the presentation while Tim Cook remains absent from the video. A foldable iPhone could cost over $2,000.

title: Amazon cargo plane overruns Miami runway, killing at least five people
summary: An Amazon cargo plane overran a runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday, killing at least five people and injuring others. The Associated Press reported the aircraft, operated by 21 Air, struck vehicles after arriving from San Juan. Miami-Dade officials stated three people were critically injured while the pilot and copilot remained trapped. Amazon expressed heartbreak over the loss and pledged cooperation with the investigation.

title: Researchers find online job postings overstate labor market concentration
summary: Dalton, Kahn, and Mueller report that Burning Glass data overstates labor market concentration nearly threefold compared to JOLTS because small and mid-sized establishments post less online. The authors note that while skill demand levels remain stable after adjustment, the dataset fails to capture vacancies from smaller firms.

title: Researchers find transfer design shapes how households spend pandemic aid
summary: Researchers Therese Bonomo, Krista J. Ruffini, and Diane Whitmore Schanzenbach analyze four pandemic-era transfers to low-income families with children. They find households spend more from in-kind and recurring benefits than from cash or one-time payments of similar value.

title: Experts warn AI helps firms learn customer and worker payment limits
summary: Experts from the University of Auckland Business School warn that AI algorithms are increasingly helping businesses determine exactly how much customers will pay and the lowest amount workers will accept. While regulators like the US Federal Trade Commission and Consumer NZ investigate these risks, there is currently no evidence that New Zealand supermarkets individually price products this way. The authors explain that digital platforms can observe thousands of individual decisions, reducing uncertainty for firms while leaving workers and consumers in the dark about their own limits. They caution that this dynamic risks creating a form of digital feudalism where platforms see the people they deal with, but those people cannot see the systems governing the exchange. The authors state that the issue is not whether these systems create efficiencies, but how the gains are distributed and whether they are fair. They conclude that business schools must encourage students to ask who benefits from such optimisation and that transparency should not flow only one way.

title: South Korea sees rise of dopamine sites that mimic shopping without purchases
summary: A new trend in South Korea features 'dopamine sites' like Dopamine Shop and FoodNeverComes that simulate the full online shopping experience without completing transactions or delivering items. These websites allow users to browse, add items to carts, and track deliveries, but no money changes hands and no packages arrive.

title: Africa must treat energy shocks as risks, not surprises
summary: The Strait of Hormuz crisis exposed African economies' vulnerability to energy disruptions, causing fuel price surges and stalled projects across the continent. Nana Menya Ayensu argues that African policymakers should build resilient energy systems through efficiency, diversification, and domestic capacity rather than treating each disruption as an emergency. He notes that African power grids lose 12% to 20% of electricity, urging leaders to price volatility into investment decisions and create redundancy to withstand future shocks.

title: Europe's major mobile operators discuss satellite consortium
summary: Bloomberg News reports that Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Vodafone Group, and Telefonica are in early discussions to form a consortium for bidding on satellite spectrum. People familiar with the matter told the outlet that the group intends to offer direct-to-mobile services using airwaves the European Union proposed reserving. No final decisions have been made yet. The initiative would create a European rival to Elon Musk's Starlink service and align with the EU's push for sovereign satellite capabilities. Vodafone and Orange declined to comment, while Deutsche Telekom and Telefonica did not immediately respond to requests.

title: Nils Pratley argues government should not fund Jaguar Land Rover job cuts
summary: Nils Pratley argues that Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds correctly refused to use public funds to support Jaguar Land Rover's planned 4,000 job cuts. The author contends the company's cost-cutting measures are a competitive strategy rather than an existential crisis requiring state financial assistance, noting the firm plans to save £1.7bn annually while maintaining investment of £18bn over five years.

title: John Crace criticizes John Healey's unconvincing and boring first speech as chancellor
summary: John Crace writes that John Healey's debut as chancellor was a disappointing performance characterized by silence and a lack of conviction. The author notes Healey arrived 15 minutes late and appeared nervous, struggling to project the strength required for the role. Crace argues that Healey's speech offered little new information, merely repeating fiscal discipline and manifesto promises already established by Rachel Reeves. The columnist suggests Healey is better suited for crisis announcements than delivering optimistic messages, which die on his lips. Furthermore, Crace observes that the wider government seemed silenced during the event, with the home secretary notably absent. Ultimately, the article portrays Healey as ill-equipped for the job, leaving the public and markets in a state of uncertainty.

title: Next wins appeal to overturn £30m equal pay ruling for warehouse staff
summary: Next has won an appeal against a 2024 equal pay ruling, allowing the retailer to avoid paying over £30m in back pay to warehouse staff. The Employment Appeal Tribunal accepted Next's argument that higher recruitment and retention pressures justified paying warehouse operatives more than shop floor workers for jobs of equal value. While the tribunal upheld findings on night-time and overtime premiums, Next described the decision as a landmark victory for market forces in employment.

title: Governor Gavin Newsom confirms he is considering a 2028 presidential run
summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom confirmed he is considering a 2028 presidential run while campaigning in South Carolina, telling CNN he would be lying if he denied it. The term-limited governor has released tax returns and adopted aggressive messaging against President Trump, who has attacked Newsom's dyslexia and used the nickname "Newscum." Newsom's visit aimed to build ties with Democratic leaders in the South, a region crucial for future primaries.

title: Eiffel Tower closed after Hindu group members were removed
summary: The Eiffel Tower was closed after members of a Hindu group were removed from the site, sparking a public row. The closure occurred as part of the ongoing dispute over the group's presence at the landmark.

title: Russia calls for Iran inclusion in Gulf security system
summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov called for Iran to be included in a Gulf security system, describing it as a practical step toward regional stability. Speaking at Moscow State Institute of International Relations, Lavrov noted that Iran's participation would facilitate confidence-building measures. He referenced the Mecca Agreement as a potential framework and stated Russia would not seek a leading role in the process.

title: Ed Miliband announces UK trade ban on Israeli settlement goods
summary: Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband is set to announce a broad reset of UK relations with Israel, including a ban on trade in goods and services from illegal settlements. This intervention, expected to face criticism from the US and Israel, represents a shift from traditional rhetorical support to active steps against settlement expansion. Miliband will also reassert the call for a two-state solution and highlight humanitarian injustices in Gaza, though the package excludes sanctions on aid restrictions or a genocide description. Polling indicates strong public support for the trade ban, with 46% of UK adults favouring it. The measures align with a 2024 International Court of Justice advisory opinion and may require primary legislation. The UK officially regards all Israeli civilian settlements built on territories captured in 1967 as illegal under international law.

title: Sydney Philharmonia Choirs amateur members tour UK Royal Albert Hall
summary: The Sydney Philharmonia Choirs recently returned from a 12-day tour of the UK, where amateur singers performed at the Royal Albert Hall as part of the BBC Proms. According to choir members like Kate Clowes and Joel Wilkinson, the group largely consists of people with day jobs who self-fund their participation and travel. Artistic Director Brett Weymark noted that during the tour, these individuals temporarily become professional musicians dedicated solely to singing. The performance, which featured over 300 performers, was broadcast on ABC Classic. Weymark compares community music groups to local sports teams, emphasizing their vital role in grassroots music making. Members reported that the experience provided significant professional development and strengthened friendships, creating a unique sense of connection through shared musical joy.

title: Experts warn of legal risks when lending family money without clear agreements
summary: As young Australians increasingly rely on family funds for housing and living expenses, experts warn of significant legal risks associated with informal lending. Youth sociologist Julia Cook and her team found that many parents and children remain unclear whether money is a gift or loan, often failing to document the arrangement. Family lawyer Gabriella Pomare notes that disputes typically arise only after relationship changes, leaving courts without evidence. Relationships NSW CEO Elizabeth Shaw emphasizes the importance of upfront discussions regarding risks and suggests families consider independent legal advice. Both experts recommend creating clear agreements detailing repayment terms, interest, and scenarios like separation or death to protect family dynamics and financial interests.

title: Springboks name Damian Willemse and Morne van den Berg for final test
summary: South Africa have made two changes to their starting XV for the fourth and final test against New Zealand in Baltimore. Coach Rassie Erasmus confirmed Damian Willemse returns from injury to replace Cheslin Kolbe at fullback, while Morne van den Berg starts at scrumhalf. Erasmus noted the team is well settled and believes selecting the same matchday squad makes sense for the closing match of the series.

title: U.K. government condemns protests against small boat arrivals in Portsmouth
summary: The U.K. government and ministers condemned protests in Portsmouth where hundreds blocked buses carrying migrants from a dinghy arrival. Police and Crime Commissioner Donna Jones described the situation as a worrying escalation and a wake-up call regarding the lack of border control. A Home Office spokesperson called the protester behavior intimidating and thuggish, while Treasury Secretary Emma Reynolds stated it crossed a line. Commissioner Jones noted that 140 migrants arrived from France and warned of significant issues if traffickers shift routes to Portsmouth.

title: Israel warns of full-scale war if Palestinian Authority launches Oct 7-style attack
summary: Israel's Defence Minister Israel Katz announced on Monday that the military is prepared to open a full-scale war against the Palestinian Authority if it initiates or is certain of an imminent terror attack similar to Hamas's October 7 assault. The statement, issued from Katz's office, specifies that such a campaign would target the PA's senior leadership, security mechanisms, and terror infrastructure in the West Bank. This warning follows a stabbing attack in the northern West Bank that wounded an Israeli settler, which the military responded to by killing the assailant. Palestinian National Council President Rawhi Fattouh denounced the threat as evidence of an aggressive Israeli government seeking to fuel conflict rather than peace. While the PA maintains its security forces work to curb militancy, violence in the occupied territory has surged since the Gaza war began, with at least 1,106 Palestinians killed by Israeli forces or settlers since October 2023.

title: Zheng Qinwen upsets Swiatek to reach U.S. Open quarter-finals
summary: Chinese qualifier Zheng Qinwen produced a spectacular fight back to upset six-times major winner Iga Swiatek 7-5, 6-3 in the U.S. Open on Monday. Zheng recovered from 0-5 down in the opening set to reach the quarter-finals, saving three set points in the deciding set. She stated she found her rhythm point by point despite starting poorly. Zheng will next play either Naomi Osaka or Elena Rybakina.

title: Thousands attend funeral of convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic in Belgrade
summary: Thousands gathered in Belgrade on Monday for the funeral of Ratko Mladic, a former Bosnian Serb general convicted of genocide and war crimes. The large turnout, featuring armed soldiers and chanting crowds, drew sharp criticism from the EU and Bosnia, which protested the event's handling and blocked television signals. While Serbian officials attended, the funeral reopened old wounds regarding the 1990s Yugoslav conflicts.

title: President Mirziyoyev visits newly restored Centre for Contemporary Arts Tashkent
summary: A 1912 industrial building in Tashkent has been restored as the Centre for Contemporary Arts Tashkent while preserving its original character. Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev toured the facility ahead of its public opening and reviewed plans for future exhibitions and research programs. The centre features a specialist research library and will host an inaugural exhibition including a Guggenheim Museum installation.

title: Documentary 'Top of the World' explores Windows on the World staff who survived 9/11
summary: A new documentary titled 'Top of the World' examines the lives of Windows on the World employees who survived the September 11 attacks. Directed by Betsy West and Julie Cohen, the film explores how Sekou Siby survived the tragedy after swapping shifts with a coworker, while 169 others at the restaurant perished when Flight 11 struck the North Tower. The documentary highlights the diverse immigrant community that worked at the venue and details how survivors like Siby and Michael Lomonaco have processed their loss over the years. The film premieres on CNN.

title: German Chancellor Merz vows to stay despite AfD state election victory
summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz vowed to stay in office following a decisive victory for the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) in the Saxony-Anhalt state election. Merz, appearing contrite, stated the result shook his Christian Democratic Union (CDU) to its foundations, yet he maintained his commitment to continuing reform paths for the sake of future generations. While the AfD secured nearly 44% of the vote, it fell short of an absolute majority and must now seek coalition partners to form a government. Merz emphasized that Germany's institutions remain resilient and that the country would not budge on its stance regarding Ukraine or Russian interference. Despite internal calls for his replacement, Merz insisted giving up is not an option, even as the AfD prepares for further regional elections later this month.

title: King Charles classes Harry and Meghan as private citizens on UK return
summary: King Charles III has issued a letter clarifying that Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are private citizens following their return to the UK. The document, shared by the Lord Chamberlain, confirms they will not use royal titles or undertake representative duties. It notes their charitable work is a personal matter, while security funding remains uncertain as the couple settles in the Cotswolds.

title: Eiffel Tower workers strike after female staff sidelined for Hindu visit
summary: Eiffel Tower workers went on strike on Monday after protesting the exclusion of female staff during a visit by a Hindu delegation. The CGT trade union condemned instructions that rendered female employees invisible based on their gender. The Eiffel Tower operator stated the delegation requested limiting interactions with women, noting these conditions should not have been accepted. Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire expressed support for the strike, calling the exclusion unacceptable.

title: US restricts personnel travel to Nogales due to unspecified threat
summary: U.S. authorities restricted their personnel travel to Nogales, Sonora, to essential movements during daylight hours due to an undisclosed threat. The U.S. Consulate General in Nogales issued the alert without revealing specific details. Sonora authorities stated they have no information indicating a specific risk to the public but will maintain preventive security operations. Republican Congressman Andy Biggs urged Americans in the area to heed government guidance. The warning does not change Sonora's existing Level 3 travel advisory status.

title: Arab League meets in Cairo to urge restraint amid regional tensions
summary: The Arab League convened in Cairo to address escalating regional tensions, focusing on maritime security in the Gulf and Israeli military operations in Lebanon. Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty stressed the importance of keeping shipping routes open, while the League condemned recent Israeli strikes that killed at least 12 people. Secretary General Nabil Fahmy noted that Arab states remain open to balanced relations with Iran, provided such ties respect national sovereignty and territorial integrity. Additionally, an Arab ministerial committee called for stronger action to halt Israeli violations in occupied Jerusalem and protect holy sites.

title: Nicaragua challenges German arms exports to Israel at ICJ
summary: Germany requested the International Court of Justice to dismiss a legal challenge filed by Nicaragua regarding arms exports to Israel. Nicaragua accuses Berlin of aiding genocide in Gaza, whereas Germany argues the case lacks jurisdiction and proper procedural steps were not followed. The German government noted that its weapons export policies remain strictly regulated. While an initial bid for an emergency injunction failed in 2024, Germany suspended exports briefly in 2025 before resuming them following a truce. A decision on dismissing the case is tentatively expected later this year, potentially contingent on separate proceedings concerning Israel's actions in Gaza.

title: MLB playoff format may cause uproar due to unbalanced American League bracket
summary: The article discusses a potentially controversial American League postseason bracket where the Houston Astros and Cleveland Guardians would face each other in the opening round. This matchup occurs because division champions are seeded above teams with better records. Additionally, the Chicago Cubs led the majors with 201 home runs in August, and the Boston Red Sox finished the week with a 5-2 record.

title: King Charles confirms Harry and Meghan remain non-working royals
summary: King Charles III has reiterated that Prince Harry and his wife, Meghan, remain non-working members of the royal family following their return to the United Kingdom. A letter sent on behalf of the king by the Lord Chamberlain stated the couple will continue to refrain from using their royal titles and that any charity work will be carried out in a private capacity. The communication aims to avoid doubt regarding their status and clarify that operational security decisions remain matters for relevant police agencies.

title: Tanzanian President Samia's husband Hafidh Ameir dies in Zanzibar hospital
summary: Vice-president Deogratius Ndejembi announced that Hafidh Ameir Hassan, the husband of Tanzania's President Samia Suluhu Hassan, died from a heart condition at a Zanzibar hospital. He was buried in Kizimkazi on Monday evening. Kenyan President William Ruto, Zambia's President Hakainde Hichilema, and Burundi's President Évariste Ndayishimiye all shared condolences with the first family. Ameir, an agricultural academic who rarely appeared in public, had been married to Samia since 1978.

title: Filmmaker Poh Si Teng releases documentary about US doctors in Gaza
summary: Filmmaker Poh Si Teng has released the documentary American Doctor, which centers on three US doctors volunteering in Gaza's besieged hospitals during the Israeli offensive. The film follows Dr. Thaer Ahmad, Dr. Feroze Sidhwa, and Dr. Mark Perlmutter as they provide medical assistance while becoming targets of the Israeli army. Throughout the documentary, the protagonists struggle to gain support in the US Capitol and raise awareness among the political class. Poh Si Teng argues that full stories must be told to help Western citizens feel sufficiently involved. Producer Watermelon Pictures states that content related to Palestine has recently taken on special prominence in its streaming catalogue.

title: Russia grants Serbian airlines rights to fly to Kaliningrad
summary: The Russian Transport Ministry stated on Monday that Serbian airlines will be authorized to operate regular flights to the Kaliningrad region under a new agreement between the two nations. The ministry did not specify when services would commence or which carriers would participate. This arrangement preserves Serbia's role as a key European air bridge to Russia, distinguishing it from EU states whose airlines remain banned from Russian airspace following reciprocal restrictions implemented in 2022.

title: TVK women Ministers and MLAs wore saffron sarees to Assembly
summary: Two women Ministers and MLAs of the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam attended the Assembly on Monday wearing red-tinted saffron sarees to mark the day Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay replied to the debate on demands for grants for the Police and Fire and Rescue Services departments. After the Chief Minister completed his speech, they met him and appreciated his performance.

title: Kerala High Court lawyers pay revised fine for flood-rescue vehicle
summary: On September 7, 2026, a collective of Kerala High Court lawyers handed over ₹50,000 to cover a revised penalty for a modified off-road vehicle used in flood-rescue operations at Aranmula. Aranmula MLA Abin Varkey criticized the Motor Vehicles Department for penalizing the vehicle, noting that the fine was increased after the court found six additional lights and tyres projecting beyond the body.

title: ‘Will reduce UP to Orwellian Dystopia’: Allahabad HC raps Noida DM over student’s NSA detention
summary: The Allahabad High Court has ordered the recovery of Rs 5 lakh from the salaries of Gautam Buddha Nagar district magistrate Medha Roopam and other officials after quashing the National Security Act detention of activist Akriti Chaudhary. The division bench of Justices Atul Sreedharan and Achal Sachdev held that the detention violated Chaudhary's fundamental rights because the material relied upon by authorities did not justify invoking the preventive detention law. The court criticized the manner in which the detention order was passed, warning that continued despotic conduct by errant bureaucrats could reduce Uttar Pradesh to an Orwellian dystopia. The bench noted that the police dossier lacked credible supporting material and that the detention appeared intended to make an example of Chaudhary to discourage others from exercising freedom of speech. The court also questioned the state's version of the arrest timeline, finding the procedure to be a sham. It cautioned authorities against treating peaceful public protests as threats and reminded bureaucrats that their duty is to the Constitution rather than the political executive.

title: RBL Bank approves $1 billion overseas bond issuance plan
summary: RBL Bank announced on September 7, 2026, that its board approved a plan to raise up to $1 billion from overseas investors through a Euro Medium Term Note Programme. The private lender stated the issuance is subject to regulatory approvals and market conditions. This move follows Emirates NBD Bank's acquisition of a majority stake in RBL Bank in June, marking the largest foreign direct investment in the Indian banking sector.

title: Copper hits record high as tight supplies outside US drive prices
