summary: Benchmark copper on the London Metal Exchange touched a record high of $14,533 a metric ton, surpassing its previous peak. Traders said volumes were likely muted due to a U.S. holiday, with attention focused on copper and zinc. Analyst Albert Mackenzie told Reuters that tariff uncertainty keeps prices elevated as material flows to the U.S. Meanwhile, Shanghai Futures Exchange inventories stood at 63,000 tons, down 85% since March. Zinc also gained 1.1% to $3,988 a ton, supported by tight supplies. A weaker U.S. currency provided broader support to base metals, with aluminium rising 0.7% and tin adding 0.4%. The article is based on inputs from agencies and does not represent the views of The Economic Times.

title: Rahul Gandhi accuses PM Modi of silencing critics with insulting labels
summary: Rahul Gandhi joined the debate over Prime Minister Narendra Modi's use of the term 'Dimagi Naxal,' accusing the leader of using insulting labels to silence critics. The opposition leader utilized the Delhi building collapse incident to highlight a lack of government accountability. Senior Congress leader P Chidambaram and Aam Aadmi Party convenor Arvind Kejriwal responded by proudly accepting the label, with Kejriwal suggesting historical figures like Bhagat Singh would also be termed 'dimagi naxals.' Union Minister Kiren Rijiju defended the Prime Minister, stating the remark targeted those rejecting the Indian Constitution rather than political opponents. Later, PM Modi reiterated his stance at a Delhi University event, calling the label a 'homoeopathic pill' and introducing the new term 'naraz fufa' for those who question national projects. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge criticized the Prime Minister's modus operandi of assigning new adjectives to opposition figures annually.

title: SEBI extends angel fund compliance deadline to March 2027
summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has extended the deadline for existing angel funds to comply with the accredited investor mandate to March 31, 2027. The regulator stated this decision followed representations from the Alternative Investment Fund industry seeking additional time. Funds registered on or before September 10, 2025, must implement the mandate by the new date, whereas funds registered after that date must comply immediately. During the transition period, these funds cannot offer opportunities to more than 200 non-accredited investors.

title: John Ternus faces AI delays and memory costs ahead of Apple event
summary: John Ternus assumes Apple CEO duties just before the September 9 event, where he must address AI delays and rising memory costs. Competitors Huawei and Xiaomi recently launched foldable phones, while Apple prepares to debut the iPhone 18 Pro series and iOS 27. The company faces pressure from soaring memory prices and potential price hikes for the new iPhone lineup. Additionally, Apple adjusted its EU commission structure to ease developer restrictions, though this may impact App Store revenues.

title: RBI absorbs over 6 lakh crore rupees in two auctions amid mixed bank response
summary: The Reserve Bank of India conducted two variable rate reverse repo auctions on September 7, 2026, absorbing over ₹6 lakh crore from the banking system. The initial 30-day auction received a tepid response with bids of ₹2.59 lakh crore, whereas the subsequent overnight auction attracted ₹3,53,390 crore. These operations aim to manage surplus liquidity estimated at ₹11.16 lakh crore, driven largely by foreign currency inflows through special deposit schemes.

title: Canada imposes retaliatory tariffs on US goods amid trade dispute
summary: Canada is set to impose tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% on hundreds of US products starting Tuesday, escalating its trade dispute with the Trump administration. Prime Minister Mark Carney stated that Canada remains ready to resume negotiations for a durable agreement while protecting key industries. The measures target steel, consumer goods, and other sectors, aiming to pressure Washington into returning to the negotiating table. Previous talks collapsed after President Trump criticized the Canadian dollar and threatened further retaliatory actions.

title: El Niño: Red Gram, Cotton Farmers Incur Heavy Losses
summary: The adverse impact of El Niño is widely felt across the Rayalaseema region, where rain deficits have caused severe losses for groundnut, red gram, and cotton farmers. In Anantapur and surrounding districts, over 10 lakh hectares of groundnut withered, while similar acreage of red gram and cotton faced the same fate. Rekulakunta weather station scientist K Narayana Swamy noted that red gram fields are being cleared as hopes are lost. Major agricultural concerns include rainfall deficiency, prolonged dry spells, and high temperatures, which have caused reduced vegetative growth, flower shedding, and poor boll setting in cotton. Farmers in areas with black cotton soil are digging out saplings to prevent further soil damage. The conditions are particularly serious for rain-fed crops, leading to significant yield reductions and economic hardship for the farming community.

title: Telangana tells Andhra Pradesh to stop overdrawing Krishna water
summary: Telangana officials informed the Central Water Commission that Andhra Pradesh had already drawn 30 tmc ft of its allowed 34 tmc ft allocation from Pothireddypadu. During a meeting in New Delhi, Telangana stated that Andhra Pradesh must stop its overdrawal immediately to allow water to reach Nagarjunasagar for Hyderabad's drinking water needs amid El Nino impacts. Telangana also clarified that its decisions regarding the Srisailam left bank power house would prioritize the state's drinking water and power requirements.

title: Punjab minister calls proposed employee strike illegal before mass leave call
summary: Punjab Industry Minister Aman Arora declared a proposed employee strike illegal on Monday, citing that the dearness allowance dispute is sub-judice before the Supreme Court. The minister warned of action against unauthorized absentees and appealed to the 85,000 affected employees to resolve demands through dialogue rather than disrupting public services. The government noted it has already addressed DA demands for post-July 2020 recruits by raising the rate from 42 to 60 per cent.

title: Madhya Pradesh death toll in Sagar hooch tragedy rises to 13
summary: The death toll in Madhya Pradesh's Sagar hooch tragedy rose to 13 on Monday, with 96 people undergoing treatment at four hospitals, including seven in critical condition, officials said. Sagar Collector Pratibha Pal stated that post-mortems indicated suspected poisoning and that viscera were sent for testing. Police arrested 14 of 30 accused and suspended five officials while investigating a suspected link to a gang in Lalitpur. A magisterial inquiry has been ordered to determine the causes and identify responsible parties. Deputy Chief Minister Jagdish Devda visited the area, confirming the official death toll of 13 and promising strict action against negligent officials, while Congress leader Jitu Patwari claimed the number was higher.

title: Tamil Nadu government proposes bill to extend Special Officers terms in 28 districts
summary: The Tamil Nadu State government introduced a Bill in the Assembly on Monday to amend the Tamil Nadu Panchayats Act 1994. This legislation aims to extend the tenure of Special Officers for village panchayats and other local bodies in 28 districts until October 19, 2026. The move follows previous extensions and addresses the inability to hold elections due to incomplete delimitation processes in those areas.

title: Special CBI court acquits Acharya Balkrishna in 15-year-old fake passport case
summary: A special CBI court in Dehradun acquitted Acharya Balkrishna on Monday of all charges in a 15-year-old case involving alleged forged documents for a passport. The prosecution had alleged that educational certificates linked to a Sanskrit college in Khurja were used to obtain an Indian passport. Following the ruling, Balkrishna said the verdict proved the truth after a mentally exhausting legal battle, though he described enduring false allegations and insults during the proceedings.

title: Gasoline prices hit Labor Day record of $4.15 amid Iran war disruptions
summary: Gasoline prices reached a record $4.15 per gallon on Labor Day, according to AAA, driven by ongoing supply disruptions linked to the Iran war. The conflict has significantly increased crude oil benchmarks and restricted flow through the Strait of Hormuz, while damaged refineries in the Middle East and Russia further constrained gasoline availability. U.S. gasoline inventories remain 6% below average, exacerbating the shortage. While the EPA moved the switch to cheaper winter-grade gasoline forward to September 1 to boost supply, analysts caution that high crude prices could keep pump costs elevated. Diesel prices also hit a record $5.90 per gallon. The situation remains dependent on whether diplomatic efforts resolve the conflict and restore normal shipping routes.

title: Strait of Hormuz deal: Iran and Oman to set temporary safe route as tanker traffic falls amid war
summary: Bloomberg reported that Iran and Oman are finalizing an agreement to document a temporary safe shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz with the International Maritime Organization. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei stated negotiations made very good progress. The deal aims to reduce tanker risks and lower oil prices, though the US seeks to restore the strait to its pre-war status as a freely accessible waterway. Macquarie analysts noted current traffic is around 7 million barrels per day compared to 20 million before the war. The conflict has driven up energy prices and pressures the US administration to end the dispute ahead of midterm elections.

title: Lucknow Tops National Clean Air Survey, 16 Uttar Pradesh Cities Earn Recognition
summary: Lucknow topped the Swachh Vayu Survey-2026, securing the first national position in the category of cities with a population exceeding 10 lakh with 198 points. The Central Pollution Control Board and the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change conducted the survey, in which 16 Uttar Pradesh cities achieved national recognition across different population brackets. Lucknow Mayor Sushma Kharkwal credited Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath for the success, noting integrated efforts in electric transport, waste management, and green cover. Urban Development and Energy Minister Arvind Kumar Sharma stated that the state is transforming rapidly under Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's guidance. The Municipal Corporation of Lucknow utilizes approximately 1,100 electric vehicles for waste collection and operates 140 electric buses to reduce pollution. Additionally, 97 electric mechanized sweeping machines and 559.85 kilometers of paved roads help control dust. Scientific waste processing capacity stands at 2,550 TPD, with a focus on preventing open waste burning. The state received cash awards totaling Rs 1.5 crore for Lucknow and Rs 25 lakh for Firozabad. Ward-level awards were also distributed to specific urban areas for outstanding performance in local clean air management.

title: Pernod Ricard India appoints four banks for potential IPO
summary: Moneycontrol reported that Pernod Ricard India has appointed Kotak Mahindra Capital, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, and BofA Securities as advisors for a potential IPO. The report cited people familiar with the matter, noting that the syndicate could expand. Pernod Ricard India told Moneycontrol that discussions remain ongoing and exploratory, with no final decision on the issue's size or structure. Global CEO Alexandre Ricard confirmed the board continues to analyze the strategic opportunity for shareholder value creation.

title: EOW investigates Rs 17.88 crore fraud at Mumbai Sumitra Cooperative Credit Society
summary: The Economic Offences Wing has taken over an investigation into an alleged Rs 17.88 crore fraud at Sumitra Cooperative Credit Society Limited in Mumbai. Chartered accountant Santosh Gangaram Shigwan filed the complaint after detecting irregularities during the society's 2023-24 statutory audit. The case, registered at D.B. Marg Police Station, involves accusations of forged loan accounts, missing mandatory documents, and misappropriation of funds by former office-bearers and employees. The Economic Offences Wing is now conducting a further probe into the alleged financial loss and the roles of the accused.

title: Speculation suggests GTA 6 PC release could arrive before 2027
summary: While GTA 6 is confirmed for November 19, 2026 on consoles, speculation suggests a PC version might launch earlier than historical precedents. VGC editor-in-chief Andy Robinson noted industry discussion about a potential forward shift, though he provided no specific date. Former employees reportedly hinted at a February 2027 target, yet Rockstar has not officially commented. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick previously explained the company prioritizes console audiences first. Consequently, all specific PC dates remain unconfirmed guesses rather than facts.

title: JLR plans to cut 4,000 jobs over two years to save £1.7 billion
summary: Jaguar Land Rover announced plans to cut approximately 4,000 global roles over the next two years as part of its strategic transformation programme. Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited stated the reductions, achieved through voluntary means where possible, aim to save £1.7 billion to support long-term growth. CEO PB Balaji emphasized the move will simplify the organization while committing to invest between £15-18 billion in electrification and digital technologies over the next five years.

title: Drug addict trespasses into J&K CM residence minutes after police release
summary: A 21-year-old drug addict named Tilak Raj allegedly trespassed into Chief Minister Omar Abdullah's residence in Srinagar shortly after being released by police. Police stated the youth fled after being handed to his father, noting he had prior theft charges and was intoxicated when caught. The incident has raised security concerns regarding the protection of the Chief Minister and his father, Dr Farooq Abdullah, following previous security lapses and an attempted assassination.

title: New videos show 9/11 suspect Omar al-Bayoumi with al-Qaida leader
summary: A BBC investigation has released previously unseen videos showing Omar al-Bayoumi, a Saudi national investigated after the September 11 attacks, embracing al-Qaida leader Anwar al-Awlaki. The footage contradicts al-Bayoumi's denial of the meeting. The report claims the FBI failed to pursue evidence linking him to the attacks, including a diagram connecting him to the plot that British police seized but US agents did not fully utilize.

title: Air India CEO Tewolde Gebremariam takes charge with focus on safety and trust
summary: Air India chairman N. Chandrasekaran outlined the airline's turnaround priorities during a town hall meeting as incoming CEO Tewolde Gebremariam formally took charge. Chandrasekaran emphasized that the carrier must rebuild passenger trust and strengthen safety, stating the safety record should be 'better than the best' airlines globally. The airline has faced mounting losses, recording a deficit of more than $2 billion in the financial year ended March 2026, according to Singapore Airlines. Gebremariam, who succeeds Campbell Wilson, pledged to make safety the number one priority and aims to get operational basics right for passengers. The leadership transition occurs as the airline navigates scrutiny following the fatal Ahmedabad crash and a recent hydraulic failure incident involving an Airbus A320.

title: Adani Power reports improved ESG scores and secures GVK Energy resolution approval
summary: Adani Power, the country's largest private-sector thermal power generator, reported an improved Environmental, Social, and Governance score of 66 for FY26, according to NSE Sustainability. The company highlighted its focus on sustainable growth and responsible operations. Additionally, Adani Power stated that the Committee of Creditors for GVK Energy Limited approved its resolution plan under the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process, pending further regulatory approvals.

title: CJP spokesperson demands investigation into PG mafia after Delhi building collapse
summary: Cockroach Janta Party spokesperson Saurav Das slammed the Delhi government over the Satya Niketan building collapse, alleging a PG mafia nexus functions with political patronage. He stated that youth are demanding answers after being left to live in unsafe conditions. Meanwhile, Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu chaired a high-level review meeting emphasizing strict enforcement against unsafe buildings and directed officials to investigate the owner's political associations. Delhi Police have arrested three family members connected to the property.

title: FTSE Russell inclusion may help NSE shares gain global index access
summary: FTSE Russell announced that securities listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) will become eligible for its global equity indices from the March 2027 review. Arun Kejriwal, founder of Kejriwal Securities, stated that while this change impacts most large Indian companies minimally, it could be particularly relevant for the National Stock Exchange (NSE). The NSE is expected to list its shares on the BSE towards the end of the month, potentially allowing its stock to meet the six-month listing requirement for consideration in global indices by the time of the review. However, inclusion is not automatic and requires meeting specific criteria regarding size, liquidity, and investability. The move could remove an exchange-level hurdle for the NSE as it enters the listed market, potentially attracting international institutional investors through benchmark and passive funds.

title: Allahabad HC quashes NSA detention of activist Akriti Chaudhary
summary: The Allahabad High Court has quashed the preventive detention of 25-year-old activist Akriti Chaudhary, stating the Gautam Buddha Nagar district magistrate's conduct was 'worthy of derision'. The bench, comprising Justices Atul Sreedharan and Achal Sachdev, found the detention order devoid of material evidence and passed without application of mind. Consequently, the court directed authorities to pay Chaudhary Rs 5 lakh in compensation, to be deducted from the salary of District Magistrate Medha Roopam and other responsible officials. The judges emphasized that bureaucrats' loyalty belongs to the Constitution, not the political executive, and warned against reducing the state to an 'Orwellian Dystopia'. The ruling comes after the police claimed Chaudhary instigated violence during recent Noida worker protests, a claim the court rejected due to a lack of evidence like WhatsApp chats or video clips.

title: Scientists Explain Why Mosquito Bites Cause Different Reactions in People
summary: The article explains that mosquito bites cause varied reactions due to how saliva interacts with human immune systems. When a mosquito bites, its saliva contains proteins that trigger histamine release and alter local immune environments, often nudging the body toward allergy-type responses. A genetic study of over 84,000 people confirmed that reactions vary significantly based on exposure history and genetics, with children and those encountering unfamiliar species reacting more strongly. Some individuals develop Skeeter syndrome, an exaggerated response involving severe swelling. Researchers note these immune changes may also facilitate the spread of viruses like dengue and Zika. Additionally, malaria parasites may alter human odors to attract mosquitoes. Scientists are now exploring vaccines that target mosquito saliva itself to mitigate both allergic reactions and disease transmission.

title: W Health Ventures closes second fund at 700 crore to build healthcare firms
summary: W Health Ventures, a Mumbai-based healthcare venture capital firm, announced the closure of its second fund at 700 crore, surpassing the initial target of 630 crore. The firm plans to utilize this capital to build eight to 10 healthcare companies from the pre-idea stage over the next four years. Managing partner Dr Pankaj Jethwani explained that the company creation model identifies gaps in healthcare delivery and recruits founding teams to address structural mismatches. Unlike conventional funds, W Health Ventures develops businesses from the idea stage, having already launched two companies under Fund II that have reached 25 million patients. The firm intends to expand this approach across India and the US-India corridor.

title: TechCrunch defines opaque recurrence and other essential AI terminology
summary: TechCrunch has released a living glossary to clarify the fast-moving vocabulary of the artificial intelligence sector. The article explains that terms like LLMs, RAG, and RLHF are now joined by newer concepts such as opaque recurrence, a reasoning technique in OpenAI's Astra model that safety researchers find concerning. The piece defines artificial general intelligence (AGI) as systems that outperform humans in most economically valuable work, though definitions vary between OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and other experts. It further details AI agents, which autonomously perform tasks like coding or booking tickets, and distinguishes them from basic chatbots. The text clarifies technical processes including chain-of-thought reasoning, which breaks problems into steps to improve accuracy, and distillation, a method for creating smaller models from larger ones. Additional entries cover fine-tuning, generative adversarial networks (GANs), hallucinations, and inference. The article also notes the industry-wide shortage of RAM chips, termed RAMageddon, and explains how tokenization drives enterprise costs. By providing plain-English definitions, the publication aims to help investors, builders, and readers keep pace with the field's evolution.

title: Creator builds animated transition between Mercator and Equal Earth projections
summary: The author created an animated transition between Mercator and Equal Earth map projections using GPT-6 Astra and D3 after the Equal Earth projection was recently voted on at the UN.

title: Questions Swirl Around Tesla Cybercab Rollout and Elon Musk's Political Controversies
summary: Tesla unveiled its new Cybercab autonomous robotaxi in Austin, Texas, on September 3, yet the event generated more questions than answers regarding fleet adoption and individual ownership. A contact form solicited interest from other robotaxi fleets, but the vehicle's incompatibility with Level 2 home charging eliminates the gig-economy model for private owners. Industry observers noted that recent history, including struggles by Hertz and Mistergreen, suggests a partnership with Tesla is not a guaranteed profit. Furthermore, NBC News reporter David Ingram highlighted Tesla's detailed safety instructions for first responders, which warn of electrical risks and require contacting Tesla support. On September 4, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened an audit to investigate if the Cybercab meets federal safety standards. Meanwhile, Tesla stock declined, and Elon Musk faced backlash after posting a message congratulating a German far-right party.

title: Rosneft Ships First Crude From $157 Billion Vostok Oil Project
summary: Rosneft has shipped the first crude oil cargo from the Vostok Oil project in Eastern Siberia, marking a significant milestone despite ongoing sanctions and the departure of Western business partners. Rosneft CEO Igor Sechin announced that 2,000 wells have been drilled at the site, which holds combined reserves of approximately 7 billion tons of low-sulfur crude. Originally estimated at $157 billion in 2019, the project proceeded after Western majors like Trafigura and Vitol exited following the war in Ukraine. Sechin noted that the operation now utilizes domestically developed drilling technology. The first cargo was loaded on a Russia-flagged tanker at the Arctic port of Sever. President Vladimir Putin described the project as part of large-scale efforts to develop Siberia and the Arctic, creating a reliable path to global markets. The initiative aligns with Russia's strategic pivot toward Asian markets while developing the Northern Sea Route.

title: GM and Ford Pivot EV Battery Losses to Energy Storage Business
summary: General Motors and Ford are transforming losses from their electric vehicle expansion into a new energy storage business to meet rising demand. The automakers wrote down billions in investments due to poor EV demand but are now pivoting to battery energy storage systems for data centers and grid support. Ford launched its BESS business in late 2025, planning to invest roughly $2 billion to scale operations at its Glendale, Kentucky facility. The company aims to deploy at least 20 GWh annually by late 2027. General Motors also entered the sector, partnering with Peak Energy for sodium ion chemistry and supplying second-life batteries to Redwood Materials. Industry reports indicate record-high energy storage capacity installations in the United States as utilities seek grid reliability.

title: Family replaces second car with Xtracycle Hopper e-bike after 1,000 km
summary: The author of this review put the Xtracycle Hopper electric cargo bike through a long-term test with his friend's family of four. After covering 1,000 km, the family reported that the bike effectively replaced their second car for daily errands and trips to the beach. The author noted that the children enjoyed the ride more than being in a car, turning transportation into family time. The bike, priced at $2,499, featured a 750W motor and a 48V 15Ah battery. Mechanical reliability was high, with the only issue being a broken kickstand spring that the manufacturer replaced under warranty. The author concluded that for many short family trips, the e-bike offered a better experience and lower cost than owning a second car.

title: Kia launches three new electric GT vehicles in Europe and the US
summary: Kia has expanded its electric GT lineup with the launch of the EV3 GT, EV4 GT, and EV5 GT. Pablo Martinez Masip, vice president of product, marketing & customer experience at Kia Europe, stated the company is opening the GT experience to new segments. These models utilize dual-motor all-wheel-drive setups and feature exclusive design elements like neon-green brake calipers. Starting prices in Europe range from €53,990 for the EV3 GT to €59,990 for the EV5 GT. In the US, the EV3 GT is available starting at $45,890, while Kia has no plans to launch the EV4 GT or EV5 GT there. Kia said it will reveal UK prices and specs shortly, noting the EV4 GT Fastback will not be available in that market.

title: OpenAI plans sponsored ads in ChatGPT free version answers
summary: OpenAI plans to display sponsored ads below answers in the ChatGPT free version to create a new revenue stream, though not every response will include an ad. According to OpenAI, advertisers will not be able to read users' personal chats, but privacy concerns remain as the company explores this monetization method.

title: Apple CEO Tim Cook steps down as Dyson launches new toothbrush
summary: Business Today reports that Apple CEO Tim Cook has officially stepped down after a 15-year tenure, transitioning to Executive Chairman while John Ternus takes over. The article also notes Dyson's entry into the wellness sector with a new electric toothbrush equipped with a microscopic CameraJet technology.

title: Authors propose PLRD estimator for regression discontinuity inference
summary: The authors report that their new PLRD estimator shows lower estimation error than existing methods in simulation studies calibrated to twelve high-profile applications. They also provide large-sample guarantees and describe a general template for evaluating new econometric methods.

title: Ng and Gospodinov analyze time-compressed data for long-run economic relations
summary: Authors Serena Ng and Nikolay Gospodinov report that time-compressed data can yield super-consistent estimates for long-run relations, though the growth-warming temperature link remains fragile. They find consumption-income and growth-demographic relations are well determined, while noting the fanning out effect weakens with strong mean-reversion.

title: Chancellor Healey seeks confidence despite historic borrowing costs
summary: Chancellor John Healey addressed the BBC and the public regarding the UK's economic outlook, emphasizing a need for confidence despite rising borrowing costs. Healey stated that doubling down on growth generation is a central priority before the Budget on 28 October. He acknowledged the challenge of historic high borrowing costs and the recent loss of 4,000 jobs at Jaguar Land Rover. While Healey refused to comment on specific tax decisions, he reiterated the government's commitment to controlling public spending. He also announced a £150m fund to support innovative firms in the north of England. Opposition figures criticized Healey for failing to end uncertainty about potential tax rises.

title: Chancellor Healey warns tax rises may be limited to protect economic confidence
summary: Chancellor John Healey addressed the 4,000 job losses at Jaguar Land Rover, framing them as evidence of global turbulence requiring UK resilience. Healey emphasized that stressing fiscal discipline should build confidence rather than sap it amid fears of tax hikes. While acknowledging high borrowing costs, Healey declined to comment on potential tax rises before the October 28 Budget. He highlighted the UK's status as the third most innovative country and outlined plans for public finance institutions to invest strategically in technology startups. The Chancellor noted that long-term growth will determine whether borrowing rules are met, suggesting a potential prioritization of economic expansion over strict budget balancing.

title: French winemakers forecast 30-year low harvest after severe drought and heat
summary: According to the French agriculture ministry, severe drought and record-breaking heatwaves are expected to result in a 30-year low for the country's wine harvest. Agreste estimates production will fall to just under 34m hectolitres, representing a 17% drop from the 2021-2025 average, with Champagne and Burgundy regions hit hardest. However, industry representatives argue it is too early to confirm such drastic figures as harvests continue. The ministry noted that definitive results will not be available until official declarations are made later this year, though the sector faces additional challenges from wildfire smoke and declining international demand.

title: Loss of Costco deal helps push beverage brand into Chapter 11
summary: Synergy CHC Corp., the maker of Focus Factor, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy following the loss of a major Costco deal. The company markets its supplements with bold claims about memory and focus, noting that the FDA does not approve supplements but requires specific disclaimers for such assertions.

title: NTSB describes Miami Amazon plane crash as causing utter devastation
summary: The National Transportation Safety Board described the scene of a Sunday crash involving an Amazon cargo plane as one of "utter devastation." NTSB Chair Jennifer Homendy told reporters that the Boeing 737-300, operated by contractor 21 Air, overshot the runway by roughly 1,300 feet, killing five people in two vehicles. The plane struck a Ford van and a Toyota Corolla SUV after bursting through an airport fence. Officials have recovered flight recorders and are interviewing potential survivors. The NTSB is investigating whether an Engineered Material Arresting System, which Miami International Airport reportedly lacks, would have prevented more destruction. The agency expects to release more information on Tuesday.

title: Trump bans Bombardier jets from US amid trade war with Canada
summary: President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social that Bombardier aircraft are not good enough and called for an end to their sales in the United States. The article states that the president lacks authority to bar a foreign manufacturer's aircraft from being sold in the US, as certification is the responsibility of the Federal Aviation Administration. Several claims in Trump's post are identified as false, including assertions that Canada blocked Gulfstream certification and that the US loses $60 to $100 billion annually in trade deficits with Canada. The US Trade Representative's office reports a 2025 goods deficit of $48.3 billion. Canada has promised to retaliate dollar-for-dollar against the US tariffs that took effect last month.

title: Israel intensifies strikes in South Lebanon, killing 13 people
summary: Israel launched a wave of airstrikes across southern Lebanon, killing 13 people, including women and children, Lebanon's health ministry said on Monday. This marks an escalation after weeks of relative calm. Israel said it would continue targeting Iran-backed Hezbollah over alleged ceasefire violations. Hezbollah has not commented on the strikes. One overnight strike hit a building in Kfar Rumman, killing 11 people, while another attack in the same town killed a rescuer. A later strike on Rihan killed one person, and a strike on Nabatieh wounded nine. The Israeli military vowed to continue operations to remove threats while remaining committed to the ceasefire agreement. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun urged Washington and the international community to help stop Israeli attacks.

title: UN passes resolution ahead of General Assembly to end child marriage
summary: The UN estimates 650 million women and girls alive today were married before age 18. The organization passed a resolution ahead of the General Assembly to bring awareness and push countries to act to end child marriage.

title: Dairy founder Ian Campbell and daughter Hannah die in plane crash
summary: Ian Campbell, founder of Barambah Organics, and his daughter Hannah Campbell died when their light plane crashed in Stockleigh, Queensland, on Monday. Emergency services found the two occupants from Ascot dead at the scene after the aircraft left Archerfield Airport around 10:57am. The crash caused a grass fire, prompting eight Queensland Fire Department crews to respond. Queensland Police and the Australian Transport Safety Bureau are investigating the incident, with investigators examining wreckage and sending components to Canberra for analysis.

title: Iran raises gasoline prices for heavy users amid economic struggles
summary: State media reported that Iran introduced higher gasoline prices for heavy consumers on Tuesday, marking the second hike since December. The government cited the current situation without mentioning the war, noting the extra revenue will support households. Keramat Veis Karami, CEO of the state oil distribution company, told IRNA the new rate affects 15% of consumers. Experts warn the move could worsen inflation in a country already facing an annual rate of about 67%.

title: Jesús Luzardo records first career shutout as Phillies defeat Braves
summary: Phillies left-handed pitcher Jesús Luzardo recorded his first career shutout, leading his team to a 1-0 victory over the Atlanta Braves in the fastest nine-inning game of the season. Luzardo, who had never pitched into the ninth inning in his first 149 starts, struck out 12 batters and retired the final two hitters to complete the 109-pitch effort. Manager Don Mattingly expressed confidence in Luzardo's recent performance, highlighting a 1.93 ERA over his last 21 starts. Kyle Schwarber provided the winning run with his 43rd home run of the season. The Phillies cut the NL East lead to four games after splitting the four-game series with the Braves.

title: Former PM John Howard warns against limiting immigration; Barnaby Joyce defends super plan
summary: Former Prime Minister John Howard spoke at the Australian National University regarding immigration and security, asserting that stopping terrorism cannot be achieved by simply stopping immigration categories. Meanwhile, One Nation leader Barnaby Joyce defended his party's policy allowing superannuation diversion for rent or mortgages, stating it would have a minute impact on inflation. Assistant Treasurer Daniel Mulino countered that unwinding the 12% superannuation guarantee is dangerous, while Independent MP Kate Chaney criticized the government's Major and Local Community Infrastructure Program as pork barrelling. Additionally, Nationals leader Matt Canavan expressed deep scepticism over new digital duty of care rules proposed by the government.

title: Andreeva advances after consoling injured Potapova; Zheng upsets Swiatek
summary: Mirra Andreeva advanced to the US Open quarterfinals after defeating Anastasia Potapova 5-7, 6-4, 6-3, displaying sportsmanship by helping the injured fifth seed up and offering ice. Andreeva, 19, called Potapova a "little star" she had always admired. Meanwhile, Qinwen Zheng upset six-time major winner Iga Swiatek to reach the quarterfinals as the first qualifier since Emma Raducanu in 2021 to do so. Reuters reported on these matches at Flushing Meadows.

title: Indonesia reopens six airports after volcanic ash crisis
summary: The Indonesian Transport Ministry reported that Jakarta's main airport and four other hubs resumed operations early Tuesday following days of volcanic ash closures. Mount Anak Krakatau's eruption disrupted nearly 3,000 flights and stranded more than 340,000 passengers. While six airports are now open, two of the original eight remain shut as airlines work to rebook stranded travelers.

title: California residents forced to live in cars due to housing crisis
summary: The article reports that thousands of Americans in California are forced to live in their cars due to the housing crisis. It notes that this situation is a result of severe housing shortages and high costs in the state.

title: US envoy reports progress toward three-way peace talks with Russia and Ukraine
summary: US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff reported substantive progress on scheduling trilateral peace talks with Russia and Ukraine following weekend meetings. Although Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met separately with US envoys, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov stated it is too early to confirm specific details for future negotiations. Meanwhile, Zelenskyy warned that fighting is likely to continue into the winter despite these diplomatic efforts.

title: Volkswagen sells Osnabrück plant to state and Aurelius for defence production
summary: Crisis-hit Volkswagen has struck a preliminary deal to sell its Osnabrück plant in Lower Saxony to the state government and Israeli investor Aurelius Capital. From mid-2027, the iconic factory is expected to start producing equipment for Rafael Advanced Defence Systems, the company behind the Iron Dome missile defence system.

title: North Korea condemns US, Japan, South Korea military drills
summary: North Korea condemned a five-day Freedom Edge military exercise involving the US, South Korea, and Japan, warning of serious consequences. The Defense Ministry statement, carried by the Korean Central News Agency, accused Washington of military provocations. Defense Minister Kim Song Ji vowed that Pyongyang would maintain its toughest stance against US hostility despite the drills.

title: Giuliani tells Mamdani to skip 9/11 ceremony amid Islam comments
summary: Former New York mayor Rudy Giuliani told current Mayor Zohran Mamdani he should skip the 9/11 memorial service, claiming Mamdani is hiding his Muslim faith. Mamdani confirmed he will attend the ceremony to stand with victims' families and first responders, while Giuliani stated he will also be present. Giuliani made these remarks during an interview with Newsmax, drawing parallels between Mamdani's religion and the 2001 hijackers. Mamdani's office declined to respond to the comments.

title: Albania launches pink flamingo art project targeting famous architects
summary: Albania is launching a pink flamingo art project aimed at renowned architects. The initiative seeks to engage famous designers in a creative campaign featuring the distinctive pink birds.

title: Trump warns Bombardier it must build in US to sell there
summary: US President Donald Trump warned Canadian aircraft maker Bombardier that it would no longer be permitted to sell in the US unless it began manufacturing in the country. In a post on his Truth Social account, Trump wrote that the company must build in the US to access the market. The warning comes amid a growing trade war between Washington and Ottawa, following previous threats of tariffs and decertification against the company.

title: WHO expands Ebola treatment centre in DR Congo as deaths rise
summary: The World Health Organization is coordinating and funding the expansion of the Lita treatment centre in Ituri province to add 42 beds and improve health facilities. The Congolese National Institute of Public Health reported that the current outbreak has caused 3,007 deaths and infected 6,186 people. The virus, caused by the Bundibugyo strain, has spread to six provinces where insecurity is widespread. While approved vaccines target the Zaire strain, WHO experts are testing the Ervebo vaccine against Bundibugyo, with initial data suggesting it could offer some protection.

title: Mexican Navy rescues missing fisherman Héctor Márquez after community search
summary: Héctor Márquez, a fisherman missing for a week off the coast of Oaxaca, was rescued on September 7 by a Mexican Navy vessel, sources at the institution confirmed to EL PAÍS. Although a cargo ship located him and provided supplies earlier, Márquez refused to board until his community arrived, leading to a prolonged search by local fishermen and family.

title: Spain launches public housing portal with income-linked rents and 14-year contracts
summary: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez launched the first national portal for Spain's public housing stock, managed by the State Housing and Land Agency CASA 47. The platform initially offers 800 homes, with plans to add 1,500 more soon, featuring rents linked to local economic conditions and capped at 30% of a tenant's income. Sánchez defended state intervention in the market, citing a broken housing sector, and promised that these homes would remain protected in the public stock forever. Housing Minister Isabel Rodríguez highlighted the need for a transparent allocation process to avoid favoritism and noted the recovery of over 42,000 homes from Sareb assets to expand availability.

title: Three years after Morocco earthquake, victims still wait for aid
summary: Three years after a devastating earthquake struck Morocco's Al Haouz region, victims report a stark divide in reconstruction progress. While some residents in villages like Ighermane have rebuilt homes with partial state support, others in areas like Azgour remain excluded due to bureaucratic residency issues. The High Atlas Development Agency states that 54,425 homes have been built or rehabilitated, with over 7.2 billion dirhams distributed, yet the National Coordination for Al Haouz Earthquake Victims reports complaints from more than 3,000 families who received no help. Critics argue that authorities treat victims as statistics rather than human beings. Despite challenges like remote locations and material transport, some experts believe progress is positive relative to the timeframe. However, many families, including those living in tents, continue to demand transparent investigations and solutions ahead of the upcoming general election.

title: Iran finalizes temporary safe route deal with Oman through Strait of Hormuz
summary: Iran announced Monday that it is finalizing an agreement with Oman to create a temporary, safe route through the Strait of Hormuz. Foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said the agreement will probably be registered with the International Maritime Organization over the coming days. This development occurs as Tehran attempts to close the strait following recent attacks by the U.S. and Israel, while Western nations consider referring Iran to the U.N. Security Council for nuclear noncompliance.

title: EU pledges 200 million euros to reassure Greenland against US pressure
summary: The European Union sought to reassure Greenland on Monday by promising 200 million euros in investment to address climate change and improve infrastructure. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen stated that Greenland's future lies with its people and Denmark, emphasizing territorial integrity. This visit occurred as Denmark and European allies resisted US President Donald Trump's threats to seize the island, with Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen expressing deep gratitude for unfailing EU support during these challenging times.

title: Israel threatens full-scale war against Palestinian Authority over potential attacks
summary: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz threatened a full-scale war against the Palestinian Authority if it prepares an attack similar to the October 7 Hamas assault. The warning, issued on September 7, 2026, targets senior leadership and terror infrastructure in the West Bank. Palestinian officials denounced the statement as an attempt to fuel conflict during the Israeli election season, noting the Authority does not officially participate in militant activity. Recent violence in the occupied territory has surged since the Gaza war began.

title: Morocco strengthens foreign policy with US and Israeli backing
summary: Morocco has significantly strengthened its international standing through diplomatic support from major powers and expanded military alliances. Bernabé López García notes that Donald Trump's 2020 recognition of Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara marked a turning point, allowing Rabat to bypass the UN and secure backing from permanent Security Council members. Consequently, Morocco has become the continent's largest arms importer, surpassing Algeria according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute. The United States now supplies 60% of Morocco's arms, while France's share has dropped to 10%. Lahcen Haddad explains that US recognition also normalized Morocco-Israel relations, leading to agreements on air defense and the construction of spy satellites. While Morocco has revived sovereignty claims over the Spanish exclaves of Ceuta and Melilla, experts like Irene Fernández Molina argue this is a political move to influence the September 23 legislative elections rather than a fundamental strategic shift. The country continues to pursue its Western Sahara autonomy plan, which recently received a UN Security Council resolution with abstentions from Russia and China.

title: US Envoy Witkoff reports progress on ending Russia-Ukraine war
summary: US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff reported on Monday that substantive progress has been made in US efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war. Speaking after weekend meetings in Moscow and Kyiv, Witkoff highlighted movement toward scheduling additional trilateral talks between Washington, Moscow, and Kyiv. He noted that President Donald Trump is working hard to stop the killing and pursue a lasting peace. The US delegation met with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, joined by national security advisers from Britain, Germany, and France in Kyiv. Witkoff expressed hope to revive these trilateral discussions following the three-day halt in attacks agreed upon by Russia and Ukraine.

title: Burundians rush to Kenya as crackdown on unregistered traders begins
summary: Hundreds of Burundians in Kenya are rushing to process travel documents ahead of President William Ruto's Monday deadline for foreigners to cease unlicensed business activities. The Kenyan trade ministry stated that some visitors deliberately misused visa applications to work without permits. Burundi's Foreign Affairs Minister Edouard Bizimana expressed concern that continued hate speech could change the situation for Burundians living in Kenya. While the government clarified that foreigners with proper documentation can continue working, many remain anxious about the crackdown and potential safety issues.

title: UP Congress leaders detained over Saharanpur mosque demolition row
summary: Uttar Pradesh Police detained senior Congress leaders, including State President Ajay Rai, on September 7, 2026, after they attempted to visit the site of a demolished mosque in Saharanpur. The Congress party described the action as dictatorship, while an Archaeological Survey of India team examined a well discovered at the location. Rai was released in the evening after hours of detention.

title: Shinde suspends Sena leader Rahul Gharat arrested over hospital staff assault
summary: Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde suspended Shiv Sena leader Rahul Gharat following his arrest for allegedly assaulting hospital staff. Police Inspector Kishor Mahanubhav explained that the altercation occurred after party members refused to pay the remaining ₹9,000 of a ₹19,000 medical bill for injured individuals. Shinde warned that such incidents would not be tolerated, while police continue investigating the attack involving 17 accused persons.

title: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla supports women's quota in Parliament
summary: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla called for a 33% women's quota in Parliament and state assemblies, describing it as a historic need to open new avenues for women in political leadership.

title: 72nd National Film Awards to be held in Gujarat
summary: The 72nd National Film Awards ceremony will be held at Ekta Nagar in Gujarat on September 22, breaking a long-standing tradition of hosting the event in New Delhi. The government has not explained the reason for this location change or indicated if it will become a regular practice. Among the honorees is filmmaker Aanand L Rai, who won Best Direction in the non-feature category for his film on the Statue of Unity.

title: Federal investigators probe Amazon cargo jet crash in Miami
summary: Federal investigators are examining why an Amazon cargo jet overran the runway at Miami International Airport, killing at least five people. The National Transportation Safety Board has sent a team to determine if the Boeing 767 touched down too late to stop safely. The aircraft, operated by 21 Air, plowed across a road used by warehouse workers after arriving from San Juan, Puerto Rico. Five people died, while three were critically injured and two others hospitalized. Aviation experts noted the plane appeared to float above the runway for an extended period. The crash halted flights at the busy hub, causing 160 cancellations and over 300 delays on Sunday. Amazon said in a statement, "We're heartbroken to learn that five people lost their lives in today's incident at Miami International Airport." The investigation will also look at weather conditions, braking, and the aircraft's maintenance history.

title: By Polls For 2 And 1 Pondy Seats On Oct 6
summary: The Election Commission of India announced on Monday that by-elections for the Madurantakam and Dharapuram Assembly constituencies in Tamil Nadu, along with the Thattanchavady seat in Puducherry, will be held on October 6. These seats became vacant after sitting members resigned or switched parties. The ruling TVK is expected to nominate Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabhama, while the AIADMK and NR Congress will field candidates in the Tamil Nadu and Puducherry contests respectively. Analysts view these polls as a potential yardstick for the performance of the Vijay-led TVK government and the NR Congress administration, though they may not impact immediate political stability. Senior leaders like C Vijayabaskar and M R Vijaybakar are waiting for their traditional constituencies to be included in future by-elections.

title: India joins US and 24 nations in 6G network initiative
summary: The US Department of Commerce announced that India has joined the United States and 24 other countries in an initiative to shape next-generation 6G networks. Union minister of state for commerce and industry Jitin Prasada met US commerce secretary Howard Lutnick to discuss the future of 6G technology at the G20 Innovation Ministerial.

title: South Korean billionaire faces divorce verdict over gaming company control
summary: South Korean gaming billionaire Kwon Hyuk-bin and his wife Lee Hwa-jin await a court verdict on their divorce, which could determine control of Smilegate Inc. The dispute centers on whether Lee, who held a 30% stake and served as CEO at the company's founding, deserves half of Kwon's 100% stake valued at up to 8 trillion won. Local media reports indicate Lee is seeking half his stake, while Smilegate stated all initial capital came from Kwon. The outcome will depend on the court's assessment of Lee's contribution and the valuation of unlisted shares.

title: SEC Orders Photo Electoral Rolls for MPTCs and ZPTCs
summary: State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha directed Mandal Parishad Development Officers and chief executive officers of zilla parishads to prepare and publish photo electoral rolls for MPTCs and ZPTCs. Punetha noted that gram panchayat rolls were already published and must be used for the new lists per AP Panchayat Raj Rules. The updated rolls will be open for inspection at relevant offices on September 11 ahead of upcoming elections.

title: Bombay High Court Allows Residential Construction On Pune Cantonment Plots
summary: The Bombay High Court allowed residential construction on two leased plots in Pune Cantonment, holding that the government cannot deny leaseholders their existing rights based on hypothetical future resumption concerns. A bench of Acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad set aside orders by the Pune Cantonment Board and defence authorities that had rejected building proposals. The court ruled that a valid lease cannot be treated as ended due to future apprehensions, noting the leases remain valid until November 30, 2033. While permitting construction, the court imposed safeguards requiring petitioners to use the properties only as personal family residences and not for commercial purposes. They also agreed not to construct multi-storey high-rises or claim compensation if the military resumes the land in 2033. The court directed the Pune Cantonment Board to process and grant necessary permissions within 30 days of the petitioners submitting required formal undertakings.

title: Bangladesh and India plan to resume cross-border train services by October
summary: Officials say Bangladesh and India plan to resume the Maitree, Mitali, and Bandhan Express trains by October following a meeting of railway authorities. Bangladesh sources reported that officials will discuss restarting the three services and launching a new train from Rajshahi to Kolkata during the upcoming two-day meeting in Dhaka. Indian high commissioner Dinesh Trivedi emphasized the importance of people-to-people relationships during the discussions.

title: ASI officer inspects 20-foot well-like structure under Saharanpur mosque
summary: An Archaeological Survey of India officer inspected a 20-foot deep structure found beneath a demolished mosque in Saharanpur. ASI Assistant Archaeological Officer Manoj Kumar Yadav noted the construction resembles a medieval well but emphasized that its age and origin require evidence. He cautioned against linking the site to the Shahjahan era or specific religious functions without archaeological proof such as coins or seals. Further excavation decisions await government approval.

title: AAP and Congress protest BJP over Satya Niketan PG collapse
summary: The Aam Aadmi Party and Congress protested the BJP government on September 7 over the Satya Niketan building collapse that killed seven people. AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj demanded a list of PG owners, alleging influential BJP leaders have financial interests in the properties. Delhi Congress president Devender Yadav alleged corruption caused the collapse and called for the Municipal Commissioner's resignation. Urban Development Minister Ashish Sood responded by stating the administration is concerned about student safety and fixing the system.

title: King Charles clarifies Harry and Meghan remain private citizens after UK return
summary: King Charles III has clarified that Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are not working members of the British royal family despite their recent return to the UK. A letter issued by the Lord Chamberlain stated the couple stepped down from royal duties in 2020 and their status remains unchanged. The document noted they should not be addressed as His or Her Royal Highness and described their position as akin to private citizens with commercial and charitable interests. This clarification aims to avoid doubt regarding their role and security arrangements after moving back to Britain.

title: Bhopal BMC Employee Booked After Attempting to Burn Mayor's Vehicle
summary: Chaos erupted at the Bhopal Municipal Corporation headquarters on Monday when employee Sunil Gaikwad allegedly attempted to set Mayor Malti Rai's official vehicle ablaze. The employee, associated with the garden section, threw burning papers onto the vehicle while the mayor was in her office. Following the incident, BMC commissioner Sanskriti Jain directed the registration of an FIR. Gaikwad, who claimed his child was expelled due to his employment status, was booked for the act. Meanwhile, the on-duty guard Ramsingh Yadav sustained burns while removing the burning material from the vehicle.

title: Maharashtra forest officials capture tigress that killed four people
summary: A tigress that killed four people in Amravati and Wardha districts was tranquillised and captured on Monday in Shirjagaon Kasba, an official said. The forest department launched a high-alert operation after two deaths within 24 hours, using patrols, camera traps, and thermal drones to track the animal. Officials stated the tigress had moved across multiple talukas over 20 days, attacking livestock and people. The district administration and police maintained security to prevent law and order issues. The forest department provided immediate financial assistance to the families of the deceased. Staff from various forest divisions, the Melghat tiger project, the Akola forest department, a team from Pune, the district administration, police, honorary wildlife guards, and NGOs participated in the operation, bringing the search to a close.

title: Former pilot Heather Penney recalls suicide mission to protect Washington on 9/11
summary: Former Air Force Major Heather Penney recalled preparing for a suicide mission to protect Washington, D.C., on September 11, 2001. She and her flight lead scrambled to intercept a hijacked airliner with unarmored F-16s, intending to crash into it if necessary. Penney noted that United Flight 93 crashed in Pennsylvania roughly 20 to 30 minutes before they were ordered to launch, rendering their potential sacrifice too late. She credited the passengers of Flight 93 as the true heroes who fought back against the hijackers.

title: Satya Niketan PG asks 40 female students to vacate amid sealing drive
summary: A women's PG facility in Satya Niketan, located 300 metres from a collapsed building, asked all 40 occupants to vacate immediately on Monday. Students reported being told the hostel could be sealed any time and would operate only as long as supplies lasted. Many students have already left for their hometowns, leaving others stranded. The college administration has not shown interest in the situation, and students face uncertainty regarding their paid rent and security deposits while authorities announce a sealing drive against unauthorized structures.

title: Irdai fines ICICI Lombard Rs 1 crore for outsourcing violations
summary: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Irdai) imposed a penalty of Rs 1 crore on ICICI Lombard Insurance. Irdai said the insurer used agents of other insurers for event management without adequate documentation and failed to classify these activities as outsourced. In its September 7 order, Irdai noted that by not classifying these services correctly, the insurer avoided regulatory scrutiny. The penalty relates to payments made under the sales marketing and business support head during FY19.

title: Finance ministry defers PSB PLI scheme amid staff concerns
summary: The finance ministry announced on Monday that it has deferred the implementation of the Production Linked Incentive scheme for public sector banks. This decision follows employee representation regarding the PLI structure, with the ministry stating it will address the issues during ongoing bipartite settlement discussions. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman met with a delegation of bank employees led by the Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh to facilitate dialogue and consultation.

title: Musician Chongtham Vikram Singh dies after Delhi assault
summary: Chongtham Vikram Singh, a 55-year-old musician from Manipur, died on Monday after being assaulted by a group of men outside his Delhi home on Sunday evening. According to a report by The Indian Express, Singh stepped out to confront the group over noise and sustained serious injuries while being treated at Holy Family Hospital. Vineet Kumar, DCP South-East, stated that seven accused have been arrested and an FIR was registered following the incident.

title: Amit Shah announces serious two-year coastal security push
summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced that the Ministry of Home Affairs will take very serious action on coastal security over the next two years. Speaking at the 28th Western Zonal Council meeting in Panaji, Shah emphasized the need for the Western region to lead in implementing the New Nyaya Sanhitas to combat drugs. He also highlighted the economic strengths of the Western states, including tourism, exports, and the blue economy, while noting the increased frequency of Zonal Council meetings since 2014.

title: Indian and Chinese armies hold talks to maintain peace along LAC
summary: People familiar with the matter said the Indian and Chinese armies met at the Wacha-Damai border meeting point in Arunachal Pradesh to focus on maintaining peace and tranquillity along the Line of Actual Control. The Indian delegation was headed by Lt General Girish Kalia, the commander of the Army's Dimapur-based 3 Corps. These corps commander-level talks occurred days after Special Representative talks in Beijing, where National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi discussed delimitation and trans-boundary cooperation. The meeting came amid reports of aggressive military posturing by Chinese troops in the Upper Subansiri region. Both sides have taken measures to rebuild their relationship following the Galwan Valley clashes in 2020.

title: Indian Embassy in China requests DNA samples from families of missing nationals
summary: The Indian Embassy in China on Monday urged families of Indians missing since the August 26 flash flood to provide DNA samples to help identify them. The Indian mission made the request after Chinese authorities confirmed they could now receive such data, which families must submit in the internationally recognised CODIS format. The embassy will forward the data to Chinese authorities for comparison and will notify families if a match is confirmed. Blood samples can be collected from parents, spouses, children, or other relatives of the missing person. The disaster, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche, left 43 dead and 519 missing, including 49 Indians.

title: Coal Ministry reports 20% rise in coal rake loading to boost thermal plant stocks
summary: The Union Coal Ministry reported a 20% increase in coal rake loading for the power sector between September 3 and September 6, 2026. Data from the Central Electricity Authority indicated that 53 domestic coal-fired plants were operating at critical stock levels as of September 5. The ministry stated that corrective measures are in place to ease supply positions at these facilities while mining conditions recover.

title: Avalon Technologies shares rise 7% after Nomura raises target price
summary: Shares of Avalon Technologies ended Monday's trade with a 7% gain after Nomura retained its 'Buy' rating and raised its target price to ₹2,767.32. The Japanese brokerage cited a proposed joint venture with Zollner as a key driver, estimating it could lift FY29 earnings per share by 21%. The stock has soared 168% year-to-date following strong Q1 results, though some brokerages remain cautious due to stretched valuations.

title: FATF warns digital hawala networks aid money laundering and terror financing
summary: The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) reports that a centuries-old underground banking system is evolving into a tech-enabled network known as 'digital hawala,' which aids money laundering and terror financing. The watchdog's latest study identifies six configurations of this system, ranging from encrypted messaging to artificial intelligence tools, noting that nearly 70% of surveyed jurisdictions have adopted these technologies. While digitization increases network resilience, the FATF emphasizes that cash remains critical at collection and exit points. The report cites a Turkish case where authorities seized over $57,000 linked to ISIL financing disguised as charity donations. FATF warns that strict enforcement and bank 'de-risking' may inadvertently push genuine users into criminal informal channels. Consequently, the organization recommends disrupting entire laundering chains rather than targeting individual transactions and clarifying the legal status of underground banking systems.

title: Broker initiates Buy rating on ESDS Software with ₹1,550 target
summary: A broker initiated coverage on ESDS Software with a Buy rating and a target price of ₹1,550, valuing the company at 18x FY28E EV/EBITDA. The firm expects revenue, EBITDA, and PAT to grow at 120.9%, 72.6%, and 81.3% CAGR over FY26–FY29E, driven by core business momentum and the ramp-up of AI infrastructure revenues. Key risks include AI deal execution and customer concentration.

title: Bandhan Bank launches four-tier credit card portfolio with Mastercard
summary: Bandhan Bank launched its credit card business on Monday in partnership with Mastercard, introducing four variants: Sparks, Ignite, Flare, and Lumina. The cards are tiered by spending profile, targeting customers from Gen Z to premium lifestyle seekers. MD & CEO Partha Pratim Sengupta described the launch as a milestone in the bank's evolution as a universal bank. Mastercard's President for India & South Asia, Gautam Aggarwal, cited India's rapid shift toward digital payments as the backdrop for the partnership. Bandhan Bank, which started operations in August 2015, currently serves over 3.2 crore customers across 6,400-plus banking outlets in 35 states and union territories, with a deposit base of ₹1.65 lakh crore as of June 2026.

title: Amal prepares for Gurupurab langar service at gurudwara with family
summary: In a story excerpted from Sanjana Kapur's book, young Amal wakes up early on the morning before Gurupurab to help his family prepare for the day. His parents, who run a restaurant, explain the deep history of the gurudwara's langar, emphasizing how Guru Amar Das ji mandated that all visitors, from kings to tailors, must sit and eat together. Amal expresses excitement about his first time participating in the big kitchen service, known as Seva. After finishing a hurried breakfast, the family prepares to leave for the gurudwara to join the community in cooking and serving food.

title: Malaysia Airlines flight diverted to Chennai after engine issue
summary: A Malaysia Airlines flight from Kuala Lumpur to Jeddah was diverted to Chennai International Airport on Monday following an engine-related technical issue, prompting a full emergency declaration, an official said. Malaysia Airlines MH 156 with 186 persons on board landed safely, and appropriate emergency response arrangements were activated at the airport. Separately, an Air India Express flight from Tiruchirappalli to Singapore was diverted to Chennai International Airport due to a technical issue, and a local standby was declared at the airport. The airline's engineering and technical teams are assessing the reported technical issue, and operations are normal.

title: Kangana Ranaut backs Tamil Nadu CM on protecting women from character attacks
summary: Actor and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut said women's character is always used against them to destroy them. Speaking after chairing a meeting in Kullu, she backed Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay's warning against personal attacks on women. Ranaut noted that society must look within to understand how women are treated, citing examples of successful women being targeted globally and in Tamil Nadu.

title: Mistral raises 3 billion euros in largest European tech funding round
summary: Mistral today announced it raised 3 billion euros in a Series D funding round at a post-money valuation of more than 21 billion euros, the largest equity fundraising round ever completed by a European technology company. Samsung Electronics led the round, joined by co-leads Scaleup Europe Fund and existing investor PSG Equity. The capital will expand Mistral's frontier research and infrastructure to support its sovereign, open-weight AI models across 20 countries. New investors include Advent, BlackRock funds, and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, while existing backers such as ASML, NVIDIA, and Salesforce Ventures participated. The company aims to provide a full-stack AI solution that maintains data control and independence for enterprises and governments.

title: Alibaba Cloud, Ant Group, Cambricon and Huawei Come Together in Shanghai to Advance the Open Source AI Stack at PyTorch Conference China
summary: The PyTorch Foundation announced new memberships for Alibaba Cloud, Cambricon, and Ant Group during the PyTorch Conference China 2026 in Shanghai. Alibaba Cloud and Cambricon joined as Platinum members, while Ant Group joined as a Gold member, alongside existing supporter Huawei. Representatives from the four organizations delivered keynotes addressing the open AI stack, ranging from hardware accelerators to application-layer deployment. Mark Collier, Executive Director of the PyTorch Foundation, stated that welcoming these members strengthens the global open source AI ecosystem. The companies plan to collaborate on advancing production-grade platforms and lowering barriers to AI development through open models and infrastructure.

title: Instagram creators lose thousands after scammers use fake copyright claims for ransoms
summary: Instagram creators say they have lost thousands of pounds after their accounts were suspended due to fake copyright claims filed by extortioners. One user with 1.5 million followers told the BBC he paid a scammer $50 to retrieve his account, noting that Meta's appeal process could take weeks. A Meta spokesperson stated that the company has restored affected content and added protections, though some creators argue the platform is poor at identifying spurious cases. The BBC spoke to three individuals who file these strikes, two of whom denied profiting while one admitted keeping the money. Experts attribute the recent increase in these scams to AI automation, making it easier to deploy attacks at scale against platforms with billions of users.

title: Cambricon Joins PyTorch Foundation as Platinum Member
summary: The PyTorch Foundation announced that Cambricon has joined as a Platinum member, granting the company a seat on the Governing Board. Elton Gong, Vice President of Software Engineering at Cambricon, explained that the move supports their goal of tight software-hardware co-optimization and a thriving open ecosystem. Mark Collier, Executive Director of the PyTorch Foundation, highlighted Cambricon's sustained upstream contributions to PyTorch and its work enabling vLLM on Cambricon hardware as key factors in strengthening the shared mission. Jin Wang, Senior Director of AI Frameworks and Infrastructure at Cambricon, will lead the company's efforts on the board, while Jing Zhu joins the Technical Advisory Council. As a Platinum member, Cambricon will deepen collaboration in areas such as compile infrastructure and device-agnostic support.

title: XPeng activates automated IRON robot production line targeting 2026 mass output
summary: XPeng has activated an automated production line for its IRON humanoid robot, marking a shift from research prototypes to manufacturing. The Chinese automaker states the line utilizes over 80% automation and targets mass production by the end of 2026, with commercial deliveries planned for 2027. CEO He Xiaopeng described the initiative as a significant step for a new product category, noting the robot possesses 76 degrees of freedom and runs on in-house AI chips. Although the article contrasts this progress with Tesla's Optimus delays, it clarifies that XPeng has not yet shipped a robot to a paying customer or proven utility at scale. The company recently raised over $900 million in funding to support these robotics ambitions.

title: Inox Wind clarifies 100 MW order came from IOCL subsidiary Terra Clean
summary: Inox Wind Limited clarified to the BSE and NSE on September 7, 2026, that a 100 MW turnkey order was received from Terra Clean Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Indian Oil Corporation Limited, rather than directly from IOCL. The company stated the previous announcement incorrectly identified IOCL as the direct customer due to an inadvertent error in the press release framing. Deepak Banga, Company Secretary, digitally signed the correction issued to the stock exchanges.

title: Germany Risks Winter Gas Shortage as Storage Lags Behind Targets
summary: Germany faces a potential gas shortage this winter if temperatures drop significantly, according to the country's gas storage association INES. With current storage levels at 54.52%, the association warned that reaching the 77% target by November 1 is uncertain due to injection rates averaging around 900 GWh daily. INES head Sebastian Heinemann noted that a colder winter could create a supply-demand gap of up to 25% in January, while elevated LNG prices have slowed winter buying efforts.

title: Malaysia considers Huawei chips for AI despite US export warnings
summary: Bloomberg reported that Malaysia is considering using Huawei chips to power its sovereign AI efforts, marking a potential first instance of a foreign government choosing Chinese accelerators over American ones. Huawei's steep discounts offer cheaper compute amid a global memory shortage that could persist through 2030, even as Washington warns that using Chinese chips could violate export restrictions. Beijing's inroads into Malaysia, which already hosts US data centers, boost its efforts to become a global AI supplier of choice, as the West tightens China's access to advanced chips.

title: Reliance Industries plans largest bond issue of the year at 12,500 crore
summary: Bloomberg reported that Reliance Industries may issue local currency bonds worth 12,500 crore in the coming week, marking the year's largest domestic deal for a listed company. The 5-year notes carry a 7.47% coupon, with Axis Bank, ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, and YES Bank acting as arrangers.

title: OpenAI updates ChatGPT Work to mimic user writing styles
summary: OpenAI has released an update for ChatGPT Work enabling the AI to mimic a user's personal writing style. The company stated the feature analyzes frequently used words, capitalization habits, and specific phrases to generate drafts that sound like the user. OpenAI shared an X post announcing the update, noting it can replicate favorite phrases, sign-offs, and capitalization quirks to create text resembling the user's normal writing.

title: Mistral raises $24 billion valuation in largest European private tech funding round
summary: French artificial intelligence company Mistral announced it raised €3 billion at a valuation of approximately €21 billion ($24 billion), the largest equity funding round for a privately owned European technology firm. The round was led by PSG Equity, with new investments from Samsung Electronics and the Scaleup Europe Fund. Chief financial officer Johan Bergqvist stated the capital will power model development and frontier research to compete with larger U.S. rivals like Anthropic and OpenAI. Mistral, which serves over 125 customers with open models, projects $1 billion in annual recurring revenue by year-end. While an initial public offering remains an option, Bergqvist noted there are no ongoing discussions regarding a listing. The company also highlighted its technological sovereignty goals and expanding client base in Asia and North America, though Microsoft did not participate in this specific funding round.

title: Canada imposes tariffs on $20 billion of US goods in trade war
summary: Canada has escalated its trade dispute with the United States by imposing tariffs on roughly $20 billion of American goods. Prime Minister Mark Carney announced the measures, which take effect Tuesday, as a direct response to recent US actions. The Royal Bank of Canada's research arm noted that while overall US growth might remain unaffected, specific businesses could suffer significantly. Beyond tariffs, several Canadian provinces have restricted US alcohol sales, and Trump has threatened further penalties, including banning Bombardier aircraft sales. Political scientists observe that these aggressive tactics have rallied Canadian public support for Carney rather than forcing concessions. Although the US economy is significantly larger, experts point to American vulnerabilities in energy and agriculture as potential leverage points for Canada.

title: Canada implements counter-tariffs on US goods as trade war continues
summary: Canada's retaliatory tariffs on a range of US goods came into effect on Tuesday, with no sign of a trade deal on the horizon. The counter-tariffs will apply to nearly C$28bn worth of American products, ranging from steel to furniture, and will be as high as 50%. Prime Minister Mark Carney stated that Canada is still in search of a deal with the US that is "durable" and in the best interests of both countries. Meanwhile, US trade representative Jamieson Greer said the ball is in Canada's court after talks collapsed in late August. Economists warn that the latest counter-tariffs will raise prices for consumers on everyday goods like clothing, food, and furniture. The Canadian Chamber of Commerce has urged the government to take a surgical approach to retaliation, noting that businesses are preparing for this trade dispute to last.

title: Canada imposes retaliatory tariffs on $20bn of US imports
summary: Canada's retaliatory tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% on $20bn of US imports took effect Tuesday morning, targeting sectors like steel and dairy.
