summary: France Football announced on Tuesday that eight-time Ballon d'Or winner Lionel Messi, along with Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappé, are among the 30 players shortlisted for the 2026 Men's Ballon d'Or. Additionally, Cape Verde's goalkeeper Vozinha has been nominated for the Yashin Trophy following his standout World Cup performances. The 70th edition of the award will take place in London on October 26 as a tribute to Stanley Matthews.

title: UK sanctions West Bank settlements, Israel retaliates with consulate closure
summary: The UK government announced sanctions against illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, accusing Israel of turning a blind eye to settler violence. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband stated the measures target settlement goods and services, not Israel itself, while banning advertising for these settlements. Israel's Foreign Minister Gideon Saar condemned the move as an outrageous lie and announced counter-measures, including closing the UK consulate in East Jerusalem and banning 11 UK MPs from entering Israel. The UK action was supported by France, Canada, and ten other nations in a joint statement. Meanwhile, the UK also announced new sanctions on Hezbollah and Iran.

title: US accuses Chinese AI firms of industrial-scale technology theft
summary: Three U.S. security agencies accused Chinese AI companies of aggressive, industrial-scale distillation activities on Tuesday. Officials described the process as training smaller models using output from larger ones to lower training costs.

title: UK government pays highest 30-year bond rate since 1998 amid fiscal pressures
summary: The UK government paid 5.82% interest on a £4bn 30-year bond, the highest rate since 1998, as Chancellor John Healey faces fiscal challenges. Markets reacted to fears of rising inflation and public debt following the Middle East conflict. Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey warned that energy price risks remain on the upside, noting UK mortgage rates are now significantly higher than when the conflict began.

title: Trump pressure prompts first Black Smithsonian secretary to retire
summary: Lonnie Bunch, the first Black secretary of the Smithsonian Institution, announced his retirement after a year of political pressure from President Donald Trump. Bunch stated the decision was made with mixed emotions following a White House report that criticized the museum's leadership and an executive order alleging the institution presents inaccurate history. While Trump threatened to cut federal support, he cannot easily remove Bunch because the Smithsonian functions independently of the executive branch. Vice President JD Vance and Chief Justice John Roberts paid tribute to Bunch's tenure before his departure.

title: Fourteen smugglers face trial for deadliest Channel boat disaster
summary: Fourteen suspected people smugglers, primarily Afghan nationals, have appeared in Paris accused of manslaughter and facilitating illegal immigration regarding the worst small boats disaster in the English Channel. The defendants face charges related to the November 2021 sinking of a dinghy that killed at least 30 people, with two alleged leaders tried in absentia. While the trial focuses on the criminal organization, separate inquiries are examining potential failures by British and French rescue services to assist the victims.

title: UK, France, and Canada announce sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements
summary: British, French, and Canadian leaders announced Tuesday that sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements mark a turning point in their approach to protecting the two-state solution. Andy Burnham, Emmanuel Macron, and Mark Carney issued a joint statement declaring the outcome critical for regional stability. They noted that systematic settlement expansion and increased settler violence pose an urgent threat to peace. Consequently, the three countries will ban the importation of goods from settlements and enforce targeted measures against those who facilitate or profit from them. Additionally, the leaders confirmed they will co-chair a meeting at the United Nations General Assembly later this month to advance their efforts and pursue peace.

title: Russia resumes Kyiv strikes killing five as Trump and Putin discuss Europe
summary: Russia resumed strikes on Kyiv on Tuesday, killing five people and injuring nearly 30 after a brief halt for US peace negotiators. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko confirmed the death toll, while officials stated that more than 50 sites, including residential buildings and a school, were damaged. In related diplomatic news, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin held a phone call where they discussed allegations of Russian sabotage in Europe. Yuri Ushakov, Putin's foreign affairs adviser, stated that Russia does not have aggressive plans toward European countries. Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expressed hope for a meeting with Trump around September 20 to discuss security needs, including requests for Patriot missiles and funding for drones.

title: Carbon credits help Africa expand clean cooking access
summary: Carbon credit financing is helping to drive Africa's clean cooking transition by making cleaner stoves affordable for millions of low-income households. As governments introduce new policies, companies such as Kenya's BURN are using carbon credits to subsidize electric and efficient biomass cookstoves across the continent. Supporters say the approach could accelerate access to clean cooking, help to reduce deforestation and cut hazardous household air pollution. Still, its long-term success depends on sustained demand for high-integrity carbon credits.

title: Russia and North Korea open first road bridge across shared border
summary: Russia and North Korea opened the first road bridge across their shared border on Monday, September 8, 2026. The Russian government said the one-kilometre bridge over the Tumen River has two lanes and will allow up to 300 vehicles a day. Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin, speaking via video link, said the expansion of transport infrastructure will boost trade and cooperation between the Russian Federation and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. The nations already share a railway bridge and air service, having agreed in 2024 to construct the automobile bridge.

title: Guterres urges global unity as UN General Assembly closes 80th session
summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urged all countries to unite and find solutions together as the UN General Assembly closed its 80th session on Tuesday. He highlighted profound challenges such as conflicts, hunger, poverty, and the risks of artificial intelligence, emphasizing that diplomacy remains essential. Outgoing President Annalena Baerbock noted the UN's indispensable role despite shortcomings, while incoming President Khalilur Rahman of Bangladesh pledged to perform his duties with loyalty and discretion guided by the organization's interests.

title: U.K. air traffic control glitch cancels nearly 300 flights
summary: Nearly 300 flights were cancelled Tuesday due to a technical issue in the U.K. air traffic control system, according to Flightradar24. Britain's National Air Traffic Services stated that engineers implemented a fix and the flight system is starting to recover. The disruption affected dozens of flights operated by multiple airlines, including British Airways and EasyJet, causing delays across Europe. While departing flights were impacted, arriving flights did not appear to be affected.

title: French far right party proposes cutting Ukraine aid
summary: The French far right party has proposed cutting financial aid to Ukraine. The article notes that this amount represents a drop in the ocean of public finances.

title: PAC questions failure to transfer ₹9,222 crore in cess collections to reserve funds
summary: The Public Accounts Committee questioned the Union Finance Ministry regarding the failure to transfer ₹9,222 crore in cess and levy collections to designated reserve funds during 2024-25, according to a Comptroller and Auditor General report. PAC chairperson K.C. Venugopal stated that ignoring the committee's directions constitutes an insult to Parliament, while the Finance Ministry argued that maintaining large idle balances was fiscally imprudent given high government borrowing.

title: India has 51 days of coal stocks after production recovers from monsoon
summary: Union Coal and Mines Minister G. Kishan Reddy stated India holds enough coal for 51 days of power demand following a recovery from monsoon disruptions. Reddy noted that production has increased as rainfall eased, with Coal India's daily output rising 35% to 1.83 million tonnes. Meanwhile, government officials reported that coal-based power generation rose 9.1% year-on-year, attributing the increase to El Niño conditions and a decline in hydropower.

title: MCD demolishes 24 properties and seals seven after Satya Niketan collapse
summary: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) demolished 24 properties and sealed seven illegal structures across Delhi following the Satya Niketan building collapse that killed seven people. According to MCD data quoted by PTI, the civic body stepped up enforcement against unauthorized construction, issuing numerous notices and orders. The action followed a meeting between Delhi lieutenant governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu and Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, who directed inspections of PG accommodation hubs and structural audits within a week. MCD officials confirmed enforcement actions were carried out across all 12 zones, including areas with substantial student populations. Additionally, the MCD suspended South Zone deputy commissioner Rakesh Kumar and four engineers pending disciplinary proceedings. Between September 1 and 8, the MCD demolished 48 properties and sealed 15, while from June 1 to September 8, it demolished 1,007 properties and sealed 471 others.

title: Cheque-bounce case: Actor Rajpal Yadav seeks exemption from surrender, SC says deposit Rs 5 cr first
summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday directed actor Rajpal Yadav to deposit Rs 5 crore with its Registry by Wednesday as a condition for exempting him from surrendering to serve his sentence in a cheque-bounce case involving Murli Projects Pvt Ltd. A bench headed by the Chief Justice passed the order after Yadav's plea was orally mentioned, challenging the Delhi High Court's July 10 judgment upholding his conviction and three-month imprisonment in seven cases under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. The matter will next be heard on September 15. The case stems from seven complaints filed by Murli Projects against Yadav, his wife Radha Rajpal Yadav, and their film production company over the dishonour of seven cheques issued for financing the film Ata Pata Lapata. According to case records, Murli Projects advanced Rs 5 crore in 2010 for the film's completion. Yadav's petition states the original transaction was an investment rather than a loan, and cheques were issued as security. The dispute escalated after Murli Projects approached the Delhi High Court in 2012, leading to seven complaints under Section 138 of the NI Act. The trial court convicted Yadav and others in April 2018, with sentences later reduced to three months' simple imprisonment and fines of Rs 1.35 crore in each of the seven cases, to run concurrently.

title: NSE IPO likely to list on Sept 25 as India's largest offering
summary: Sources reported that the National Stock Exchange's nearly Rs 30,000-crore IPO is expected to open for subscription on September 18 and list on September 25. The offering could become India's largest, surpassing Hyundai Motor India's 2024 deal, though the exchange will not receive proceeds. The timeline aims to ensure shares debut before Pitru Paksha starts on September 26. Bank of Baroda is likely to divest 35% of its holding via the issue.

title: Apple shares dip ahead of foldable iPhone 18 launch event
summary: Apple Inc shares dropped 1.3% to $315 on September 8 ahead of an event where the company plans to unveil its first foldable iPhone. Analysts anticipate the device, expected to cost more than $2,500, could quickly become a category leader despite potential limitations in camera and processor technology. Nabila Popal of IDC stated that the phone would sell well due to Apple's ability to create an aura of exclusivity. The introduction also marks a debut for CEO John Ternus, who took the role on September 1. Apple aims to refresh its Pro models while delaying updates to other lines until spring 2027. This move represents a significant design shift in the iPhone's nearly 20-year history, following years of internal research initiated by then-CEO Tim Cook around 2020.

title: Apple Event 2026: Foldable iPhone, AI integration, and a new face on stage
summary: Apple's September 2026 launch event, led by CEO John Ternus, is anticipated to feature a foldable iPhone priced between $2000 and $2500. Analysts from Gartner and Counterpoint expect the device to drive significant interest in the foldable ecosystem while introducing advanced AI capabilities. The event may also see the omission of a base iPhone 18 model, with higher costs likely passed to consumers for the Pro series. Additionally, Ternus is expected to present updates to the Apple Watch, AirPods, and Mac hardware.

title: Qualcomm stock rises 9% after announcing AI chip deal with Amazon
summary: Qualcomm shares rose nearly 9% on Tuesday after the company announced a multi-generational data centre chip deal with Amazon. The agreement allows Amazon to acquire up to $4 billion worth of Qualcomm shares and involves developing custom silicon for Amazon Web Services' artificial intelligence infrastructure. Qualcomm stated the partnership supports its efforts to expand beyond its core smartphone business as it faces the eventual loss of its modem business from Apple. The deal includes warrants for up to 25 million shares at $161.26 apiece, vesting in tranches linked to Amazon's chip orders, which could reach $60 billion over the next decade. Cristiano Amon, President and CEO of Qualcomm Incorporated, said the collaboration brings decades of leadership in advanced processing to deliver breakthrough performance for the next generation of AI infrastructure. This partnership follows similar agreements with other cloud providers like Google and Microsoft, as Qualcomm pitches custom chips to cloud providers seeking alternatives to Nvidia's dominant AI processors. Qualcomm expects revenue from two custom-chip hyperscale customers before the end of the year, with data centre chip sales expected to reach $15 billion by 2029.

title: Flipkart widens lead over Amazon as quick commerce grows
summary: Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research reports that Flipkart and Myntra combined account for 35% of India's monthly active user share, widening their lead over Amazon to 17 percentage points. Bernstein data indicates Flipkart's user base grew 15% year-on-year in July 2026 while Amazon's contracted. Meanwhile, TechCrunch cites PTI that Flipkart Minutes now handles 1.1 to 1.2 million daily orders, nearing Swiggy Instamart's volume as quick commerce expands.

title: RBI Governor says FinTechs bridge India's MSME credit gap
summary: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra stated that FinTechs are helping bridge India's MSME credit gap by extending formal credit to millions of small businesses previously invisible to traditional underwriting models. Speaking at the 7th Global Fintech festival, Malhotra noted that FinTech has reshaped Indian finance by enabling seamless digital transactions for shopkeepers, farmers, and professionals through UPI and the Jan Dhan ecosystem. He emphasized that the Reserve Bank views FinTech as a valuable partner in building a safer, more inclusive financial system.

title: Samsung India cuts 8-10 senior staff, plans 40-50 more layoffs
summary: Industry sources said Samsung India Electronics laid off 8-10 mid-to-senior employees in its Consumer Electronics division and plans to cut another 40-50 staff soon as part of a cost-rationalisation exercise. The company is also merging branch offices across the country to drive efficiency amid stiff competition from rival Korean and Chinese players, rising input costs, and muted consumer demand.

title: TRAI Recommendations Approved: Elon Musk's Starlink Likely To Launch In India
summary: The Digital Communications Commission approved Telecom Regulatory Authority of India recommendations on satellite spectrum allocation at a September 2 meeting. Sources privy to the development stated that Starlink, OneWeb, and Reliance Jio can now acquire spectrum and begin services soon. The panel cleared the framework requiring providers to pay a 5 percent spectrum usage charge on adjusted gross revenue, with lower rates for rural connectivity. These operators are expected to establish ground infrastructure and complete security trials before a pan-India rollout.

title: NCPCR Summons Meta India Officials Over Alleged CSEAM Ads
summary: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights summoned Meta India's Managing Director and Head to appear on September 9 regarding allegations of child sexual abuse material in ads. The child rights body initiated proceedings after a BBC Eye report, while the National Human Rights Commission separately directed Delhi Police to investigate Meta's compliance with the POCSO Act following similar allegations.

title: RBI Governor credits fintech for India's digital financial progress
summary: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said fintech has significantly improved India's financial ecosystem by reducing transaction costs and strengthening fraud detection. Speaking at the Global Fintech Fest 2026, he highlighted the technology's role in credit delivery to MSMEs and real-time supervision. Malhotra also credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership for placing India at the forefront of digital innovation, noting the Prime Minister's third consecutive year of presence at the event. The festival is expected to attract over 100,000 delegates and more than 8,000 institutions.

title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Astra with new autonomous computer skills
summary: OpenAI launched GPT-6 Astra, a new artificial intelligence model designed to perform complex tasks across computers and browsers with limited human intervention. The company states the model can conduct research, write software, and complete professional workflows, claiming it scored 99.9% on the ARC-AGI-3 benchmark. OpenAI president Greg Brockman and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang suggested this launch marks the arrival of artificial general intelligence. However, the article notes that Astra's performance varies significantly depending on the testing environment, scoring only 62.7% under a standard provider-neutral harness. While Astra demonstrates strong capabilities in computer use and cybersecurity, it does not outperform all rival models on every measure. The piece highlights that achieving high scores on specific benchmarks does not equate to the broad autonomy required for true AGI. Furthermore, recent incidents involving autonomous agents acting offensively underscore the growing safety concerns associated with increasingly independent AI systems.

title: Goldman Sachs warns oil prices could reach $120 if Hormuz Strait attacks continue
summary: Goldman Sachs analyst Daan Struyven warned that continued attacks on shipping in the Hormuz Strait could drive oil prices to $120 per barrel. The situation escalated after the US struck Iranian oil tankers and Iran threatened retaliatory measures, including a new exclusion zone. Consequently, oil prices rose as traders priced in a risk premium for potential supply disruptions. JPMorgan estimates that every additional month of conflict could add $7 to $8 per barrel to Brent prices. Meanwhile, ANZ analysts lifted their short-term forecast to $95 per barrel, noting that a prolonged standoff appears the most likely scenario. Market data shows Brent trading at a premium over future contracts, with Kotak Securities identifying $102 as a major resistance level.

title: Coimbatore foundries report 20% growth amid rising demand
summary: Jayakumar Ramdass, chairman of Inter Foundry and Managing Director of Mahendra Pumps, stated that the Coimbatore foundry industry registered 20% growth last year driven by robust orders. The sector, which produces 1.5 million tonnes of castings annually worth nearly ₹25,000 crore, faces skilled manpower shortages but is investing in automation. Meanwhile, the upcoming Inter Foundry and Inter Diecast exhibition aims to showcase latest technologies and attract over 10,000 visitors, including 60 overseas buyers, to boost global market presence.

title: HCLTech opens advanced semiconductor lab in Bengaluru
summary: HCLTech inaugurated a new Advanced Semiconductor Lab in Bengaluru with an investment of ₹185 crore. The 40,000 sq ft facility features Class 10K and 1K cleanrooms to support end-to-end post-silicon engineering and testing. The company stated the lab aims to accelerate time-to-market for global clients using tools from Teradyne, Advantest, Keysight, Tektronix and Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. Hari Sadarahalli, Corporate Vice President and Global Head of Engineering and R&D Services, noted the facility reflects the firm's commitment to high-end engineering capabilities and contributing to India's vision as a global technology hub.

title: Tamil Nadu creates separate HR&CE department for temple management
summary: The Tamil Nadu government has carved out a separate Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department to manage temples independently. This administrative restructuring follows earlier decisions by the TVK government, such as banning smartphones in 52 major temples and cancelling 46 projects worth Rs 245.85 crore previously approved by the DMK administration.

title: Indian Navy chief visits Australia and New Zealand to strengthen maritime ties
summary: Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, the Chief of the Naval Staff, will visit Australia and New Zealand beginning September 9 to strengthen naval cooperation and maritime ties. Officials stated the visit aims to bolster interoperability and security with the Royal Australian Navy and Royal New Zealand Navy. During the trip, Admiral Swaminathan will hold bilateral discussions with senior leadership from both nations and visit key operational establishments. The engagements seek to deepen operational interaction, information sharing, and professional exchanges, reflecting India's growing defence engagement in the Indo-Pacific region.

title: Indian Navy detains Tharuvaikulam boat with nine fishermen in Lakshadweep
summary: The Indian Navy detained a mechanised boat carrying nine fishermen from Tharuvaikulam after it reportedly entered a banned area near Kavarati Island in Lakshadweep. The vessel, owned by Michael Raj, had departed Kochi on September 4 for deep-sea fishing. Authorities took the boat to Kavarati Island for interrogation following the incident on September 7.

title: Magnitude 5.3 earthquake hits Tibet; Nepal feels tremor
summary: Reuters reported that a magnitude 5.3 earthquake struck Tibet on 8 September at a depth of 35 km, according to the European-Mediterranean Seismological Centre. The National Center for Seismology stated that Nepal felt tremors from the event, which occurred after recent flash floods near the border. This follows a magnitude 5 quake on 3 September at a depth of 110 km, per the German Research Center for Geosciences.

title: Former Delhi chief secretary Rakesh Mehta dies by suicide at Noida residence
summary: Former Delhi chief secretary Rakesh Mehta died by suicide at his Noida residence on September 6, officials said. Police recovered a note citing his mental and health issues. Mehta, a 1975-batch IAS officer, served under Sheila Dikshit and oversaw the 2010 Commonwealth Games. He held several senior roles in the Delhi government before retiring in November 2010. His last rites were performed at the Lodhi Road crematorium in Delhi on Monday.

title: SIMS Hospital performs bone-sparing hip procedures on two international patients
summary: Doctors at SIMS Hospital performed bone-sparing hip procedures on two international patients, a 44-year-old from the USA and a 58-year-old from the UK. Vijay C. Bose, joint director and senior consultant in Orthopaedics, explained that the new high-density polyethylene implant conserves bone and supports high activity. The procedure addresses limitations of previous metal-on-metal implants. Raju Sivasamy and Sharat Kusuma were present at the event.

title: Indore loses clean air ranking to Lucknow by one point
summary: Indore lost its top ranking in the 2026 Clean Air Survey, finishing second with 197 points behind Lucknow's 198 points. Mayor Pushyamitra Bhargava stated the city lagged due to higher PM10 levels. Following the fifth edition of the Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan Awards, the administration announced steps to curb traffic and industrial pollution. Despite the ranking drop, officials noted a decline of more than 15 per cent in PM10 levels compared to previous years.

title: 'Don't send your children to Delhi to study': Father's appeal to parents after losing son in Satya Niketan tragedy
summary: Bhupendra Jaj, a taxi business owner from Dewas, made an emotional appeal to parents not to send their children to Delhi for studies after his son Arpit Jaj died in a building collapse. The incident at Satya Niketan claimed seven lives, and the father reported facing difficulties in locating his son's body. He stated he was devastated and that the family plans to donate Arpit's remaining eye. Police have arrested the building owner and others, while authorities ordered the demolition of an adjoining dilapidated structure.

title: Yale professor explains H1N1 response and public health challenges in India
summary: Brian Wahl, an assistant professor at the Yale School of Public Health, speaks to Frontline about the recent surge in H1N1 cases in India and the effectiveness of current public-health responses. Wahl notes that while India has strengthened surveillance systems since the COVID-19 pandemic, challenges remain regarding vaccine uptake and the need to engage the public in designing health interventions. He argues that absolute case counts are of limited utility without knowing the population denominator and advocates for a bottom-up approach to public-health interventions. Wahl also highlights the importance of vaccination, noting that influenza vaccine efficacy ranges from 40-60 per cent, and urges individuals to get vaccinated if they have not already fallen ill. Furthermore, he discusses the role of climate change in increasing the risk of infectious diseases through water contamination and vector-borne diseases, suggesting nature-based solutions and community engagement as effective strategies.

title: Former Delhi Chief Secretary Rakesh Mehta found dead in Noida
summary: Police in Noida found former Delhi Chief Secretary Rakesh Mehta hanging at his Sector 82 residence on September 6, 2026, with a suicide note citing mental and health issues. The 1975-batch IAS officer, who oversaw the 2010 Commonwealth Games and major Delhi reforms, was cremated at Lodhi Road crematorium after a post-mortem examination.

title: BJP leader Gaurav Bhatia files defamation case against CJP leaders
summary: BJP leader and senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia filed a defamation suit in the Delhi High Court against Cockroach Janta Party leaders Abhijeet Dipke and Ashutosh Ranka, and journalist Saurav Das. The case seeks Rs 2 crore in damages and an injunction against the defendants, who Bhatia alleges circulated false, AI-generated graphics on social media platform X that harmed his reputation. The dispute arose after an image falsely attributed remarks concerning Swatantra Bhardwaj to Bhatia, which Das initially shared before deleting it. Bhatia claims the content continued to spread, with one post viewed by over 1.32 lakh users. The suit also references earlier posts by Das regarding Umar Khalid, which Bhatia alleges amount to a broader attack on the judiciary. These allegations remain under consideration by the court.

title: High Courts require improved succession planning and complaint handling
summary: V. Venkatesan, a Contributing Editor at Supreme Court Observer, argues that High Courts require improved succession planning and complaint handling. The author points to recent appointments in Punjab and Haryana and Rajasthan as examples of procedural delays and insufficient state consultation. Venkatesan calls for transparent records of appointment timelines and safeguards to protect the integrity of judicial complaint examinations. He emphasizes that the current system often fails to allow meaningful state government input or adequately prepare successors before vacancies occur. Furthermore, the article notes that allegations against acting chief justices must be examined separately from succession processes to ensure fairness. Venkatesan suggests that making procedural steps public would allow better scrutiny of delays and decisions. Ultimately, the author contends that a system recording its reasoning makes the exercise of judicial power open to scrutiny.

title: Jake Gyllenhaal stars in M Night Shyamalan's new thriller 'Remain'
summary: M Night Shyamalan's new supernatural thriller 'Remain' stars Jake Gyllenhaal and Phoebe Dynevor. Co-written by Nicholas Sparks, the film is scheduled for release on February 3.

title: Cleveland Clinic, RIKEN, and IBM named 2026 ACM Gordon Bell Prize finalists
summary: Cleveland Clinic, RIKEN, and IBM have been named finalists for the 2026 ACM Gordon Bell Prize for their breakthrough quantum-HPC chemistry research. The team achieved the largest known quantum-enabled simulation of a biologically relevant molecule by integrating IBM Quantum Heron processors with supercomputers from RIKEN and the University of Tokyo. Additionally, the researchers introduced a fully automated end-to-end workflow that reduces operational complexity and improves the accuracy of protein-ligand binding energy calculations, advancing the scale of quantum-centric supercomputing.

title: Flashlight Capital seeks Samsung shareholder list in S-1 Corp takeover bid
summary: Singapore-based activist fund Flashlight Capital Partners has requested the shareholder registers of five Samsung Group units holding a substantial stake in S-1 Corporation. Founder Sanghyun Lee aims to communicate directly with these shareholders to improve returns at the South Korean security company, which has lagged the benchmark KOSPI. Lee offered to buy all S-1 shares held by the five affiliates for 906.6 billion won, arguing there are no meaningful business synergies. Samsung Group and its affiliates did not respond to comment requests, while S-1 stated it has no position to state on the proposal.

title: OpenAI CFO says AI chip design tool beats open-source rivals on cost
summary: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar announced at the Goldman Sachs conference that the company is expanding AI into specialized industries like chip design, aiming to undercut open-source rivals on cost. Friar stated that deploying OpenAI's lower-cost Luna model is cheaper than running Chinese alternatives on cloud providers. She noted the company finalized its Jalapeno chip design within nine months using its own models and cut the price of the Luna model by 80 percent, driving a roughly 10-fold increase in usage. Enterprise revenue increased 32 percent from June to July, while the company aims to balance enterprise and consumer businesses by year-end.

title: OpenAI's Navier-Stokes Solution Sparks Controversy Over Credit and AI Access
summary: OpenAI announced that its agents solved the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, but the milestone is overshadowed by accusations of failing to credit researchers Tristan Buckmaster and Levent Alpöge. Buckmaster, an NYU mathematician, posted a document alleging that OpenAI employees pressured him regarding authorship and denied that their models accessed his work, though OpenAI denies these claims. While OpenAI's internal model reportedly solved the full equations using about 10,000 concurrent agents at a cost of millions of dollars, experts suggest that human research taste may have guided the AI toward a specific approach. The episode raises concerns about the future of mathematics, with some fearing that private AI companies will monopolize problem-solving resources, potentially stifling the collaborative spirit and transparent error-correction processes that traditionally drive mathematical discovery.

title: OpenAI releases ChatGPT Images 2.5 with improved instruction following
summary: OpenAI has released ChatGPT Images 2.5, an update to its image generation models that improves instruction-following capabilities and speed. The new version is better at preserving subjects from reference photos and includes two new API models: gpt-image-2.5-sunburst and gpt-image-2.5-flare. OpenAI suggests using Sunburst for workflows requiring high editing precision, while Flare is intended for fast, everyday image generation. The company notes that its image models have already generated over 3 billion images across ChatGPT Images and the GPT-Image API.

title: OpenAI claims to solve century-old Navier-Stokes math problem
summary: OpenAI claims to have solved the Navier-Stokes problem, one of seven Millennium Prize Problems, after spending millions on the AI-led endeavor. The company stated that about 10,000 AI agents reached the solution in 88 hours. However, mathematician Tristan Buckmaster expressed concerns that OpenAI may have accessed his and another researcher's work, noting their data was stored in OpenAI's Codex model. OpenAI researcher Sebastien Bubeck denied using the pair's material, though the company admitted it could not rule out that such data helped improve its models. OpenAI said it does not intend to claim the $1m prize. The announcement follows recent cybersecurity incidents and calls for AI regulation.

title: Zepto scales customer support using an evaluation-first AI agent framework on Databricks
summary: Zepto, a quick-commerce platform operating in over 60 cities, partnered with Databricks to scale its customer support using an evaluation-first AI agent architecture. The company processes more than 100,000 tickets daily and faced challenges maintaining reliability as ticket volume and product categories expanded. To address this, Zepto established evaluation as core infrastructure rather than a final check, utilizing Databricks and MLflow to create a dual-loop system connecting development and production phases. This approach enabled the company to implement stratified sampling, which reduced review costs by 86% while improving edge-case detection by 9X compared to uniform sampling. The framework also automated prompt optimization and regression testing, ensuring that changes were validated against a golden dataset before deployment. Real-world applications included catching a production issue where agents repeated cached responses and detecting intent confusion when adding cancellation features. By treating evaluation as a fundamental development primitive, Zepto achieved significant improvements in quality, cost efficiency, and operational performance while minimizing customer-facing errors.

title: Hackers Steal Claude Tokens From Subscribers via Compromised Sessions
summary: Grant De Swardt, an independent AI consultant, discovered unauthorized token consumption on his Claude Max 20x account despite not using it. After contacting Anthropic, the company suspended his account and issued a partial refund, stating that a compromised session key allowed a third party to mint unauthorized tokens. De Swardt told TechCrunch that Anthropic could not determine how the attackers gained access, suggesting either stolen credentials or an external service connection. Other users reported similar experiences, including automatic account upgrades and rapid token depletion. Anthropic warned that infostealer malware, often acquired from infected software or ads, was the likely culprit. While the company signed users out and invalidated authorizations, De Swardt remains skeptical due to the lack of itemized usage data and unresolved security concerns, eventually cancelling his subscription.

title: OpenAI claims to solve 90-year-old Navier-Stokes math problem in 88 hours
summary: OpenAI announced on Tuesday that it solved the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, a 90-year-old mathematical challenge, in just 88 hours. The company utilized roughly 10,000 autonomous AI agents trained on a new internal model to exchange nearly 3 million messages while attempting the task. OpenAI described the achievement as a milestone but noted the solution remains unverified by the Clay Mathematics Institute and does not yet claim the associated $1 million prize. The announcement sparked controversy after mathematician Tristan Buckmaster claimed OpenAI received information about his own concurrent research on the problem. While OpenAI congratulated Buckmaster and stated it had not seen his work, the company admitted it cannot rule out that de-identified data from user interactions may have improved its models.

title: Microsoft patches record 972 vulnerabilities in September update amid AI threat
summary: Microsoft released a September security update addressing a record 972 vulnerabilities, including 112 critical ones. Dustin Childs, a researcher at the Zero Day Initiative, describes this spike as the 'new normal' but warns that AI-assisted vulnerability discovery continues to accelerate despite increased patching efforts.

title: Google updates WeatherNext 3 AI model to ingest satellite data
summary: Google has released version 3 of its WeatherNext AI weather model, marking a significant update to its forecasting capabilities. The new version ingests satellite weather data, reducing the lag time between current conditions and forecast generation compared to previous reliance on reanalyses. This change allows for hourly forecasts and increased spatial resolution. Additionally, Google added a separate machine-learning model trained on satellite-based precipitation estimates, providing multiple precipitation forecasts. The company detailed these improvements in a white paper, noting that the larger model required process tweaks to manage increased computational demands.

title: OpenAI claims Navier-Stokes solution amid accusations of skulduggery
summary: OpenAI reported resolving the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, using an unreleased internal model. The announcement follows accusations from Tristan Buckmaster and Levent Alpöge, who claim OpenAI acted opportunistically after learning of their own progress. Buckmaster stated that OpenAI launched its effort on September 1 after hearing rumors related to his and Alpöge's work. OpenAI described launching an evaluation on September 1, with agents arriving at a resolution on September 5. The company noted its agents sent 4.9 million messages and used approximately 300 billion output tokens. OpenAI clarified that no specific user data was accessed but acknowledged de-identified data might have helped improve models. Buckmaster questioned whether OpenAI's model had access to their sessions or training data. OpenAI offered to wait for Buckmaster to publish but excluded Alpöge as a co-author due to his employment at Anthropic.

title: NYC and LA School Districts Ban Student AI Use Ahead of 2026 School Year
summary: Just before the start of the 2026 school year, major United States school districts issued new policies restricting artificial intelligence applications in classrooms. On Wednesday, New York City officials announced a one-year moratorium on generative AI for K-8 students while permitting limited approved tools for high schoolers. Simultaneously, Los Angeles Unified School District placed a similar one-year ban on generative AI for its estimated 378,000 students. Tech Policy Press reporters Chris Mills Rodrigo and Laura Karpas surveyed national trends, finding that while many districts are establishing guardrails, clear rules on permissible use remain elusive. Rodrigo noted that roughly 35 states have adopted soft guidance focusing on AI literacy rather than strict prohibitions. The New York City policy change followed significant backlash against previous draft guidelines, which teachers and students felt created an inconsistent "Wild West" environment. Advocates, including the AI Moratorium Coalition, argued that the lack of transparency and the rapid pace of decision-making undermined democratic processes in education. Laura Karpas observed that public frustration extended beyond AI to a broader skepticism of educational technology's slow creep into classrooms over the last two decades. Both reporters emphasized that these local actions in the nation's largest districts will likely influence other jurisdictions waiting to see how the moratoriums are implemented.

title: SQL Data Types Define Storage, Performance, and Integrity Rules
summary: The article explains that SQL data types define column values and storage requirements, directly impacting data integrity, storage efficiency, and query performance. It categorizes types into numeric, character, date/time, and specialized binary groups, noting that different systems like MySQL and PostgreSQL implement them with slight variations. The text emphasizes that choosing the correct type enforces logical rules, prevents invalid data entry, and improves scalability. For instance, DECIMAL stores exact values for financial calculations, while FLOAT uses approximate binary representation for faster but less precise math. Storage efficiency matters significantly; VARCHAR saves space compared to CHAR for variable-length data, and selecting appropriately sized numeric types reduces disk usage. The guide advises storing timestamps in UTC to handle time zones consistently and using native types for dates and booleans rather than strings. It also highlights that implicit type conversions can be risky, suggesting explicit casting for clarity. Finally, the article notes that while core concepts are universal, specific type names and limits vary across platforms, requiring careful documentation and testing during schema design.

title: China Adapts Disinformation Tactics in Taiwan Using AI Technology
summary: A research team led by Dr. Austin H. Wang at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, and RAND identified an undeleted AI prompt instructing writers to target a Taiwanese audience. This evidence points to specific efforts to produce content for Taiwan rather than general Traditional Chinese readers. While some networks previously relied on manual coordination and proxy IPs, other PRC-linked operations now incorporate language models for content creation. Additionally, AI is being used to generate misleading video content, such as news anchors spreading narratives about outgoing president Tsai Ing-wen. William Yang, an analyst at the International Crisis Group, stated that election interference efforts from China will certainly rise with advanced AI technology. Experts argue the goal is to distract the public and create a 'liar's dividend,' where genuine evidence is dismissed as fake. Current responses from platforms and governments focus on identifying fake content rather than analyzing the coordinated behavior patterns behind the operations.

title: Google funds PG&E virtual power plant pilot to test grid capacity
summary: Pacific Gas & Electric is launching a virtual power plant pilot called SHARE, fully funded by Google rather than ratepayers. The program will integrate approximately 21,000 existing energy devices in the San Jose area, including home batteries and smart thermostats, to provide 12 megawatts of capacity. PG&E and consultancy Demand Side Analytics will build and operate the initiative, with partners like Tesla, Sunrun, and Renew Home participating. A spokesperson stated that Google covers all costs, including incentives and potential subsidies for new heat pump systems. The pilot serves as a proof of concept to test whether optimizing distributed energy resources can relieve transmission strain and exert downward pressure on rising electricity rates. Planning and enrollment are expected to begin this fall, with evaluation scheduled for the end of 2027.

title: CRISIL forecasts 100-200 bps revenue growth for large Indian EPC firms
summary: CRISIL Ratings reports that large Indian engineering, procurement and construction companies are expected to see revenue growth accelerate to 9-10% this fiscal, driven primarily by rising power-sector investments. The rating agency notes that while operating margins are projected to decline to 8.2-8.4% due to commodity inflation, the credit profiles of these firms are expected to remain stable.

title: Iranian researchers develop AI model to predict solar pile uplift resistance
summary: Researchers from Iran's Islamic Azad University and partners developed an interpretable artificial neural network to predict the uplift capacity of solar PV piles. The team trained the model using data from 130 field load tests conducted at a Rafsanjan solar plant. While the model achieved an R² of 0.778, the scientists cautioned that because the data originates from a single sandy site, the predictions may not generalize to markedly different geological settings like clay or gravel soils.

title: Rising Oil Prices May Force China's Independent Refiners to Cut Processing Rates
summary: Chinese independent refiners may reduce processing rates as international oil prices rise and supply from Venezuela and Iran dries up, according to an Energy Aspects analyst quoted by Bloomberg. These independent refiners have slimmer margins than state-owned majors, with some already at breakeven. Meanwhile, China imported 37.93 million tons of crude oil in August, a 6.2% increase from July but still 23.4% lower than the same month last year, official Chinese customs data showed.

title: Solis commissions first 1.04 MWh energy storage system in Chennai
summary: Solis has commissioned its first SolisStorage EverCore energy storage system in India at a data center in Chennai. Developed with Inforce Engineering Solutions LLP, the 500 kW/1.04 MWh battery system integrates with an 870 kW rooftop solar installation to strengthen energy resilience. Honey Raza, Country Manager at Solis India, stated the project demonstrates the potential for solar-plus-storage solutions to support India's expanding digital infrastructure.

title: Google plans $15 billion AI infrastructure investment in Finland
summary: Google announced a minimum €13 billion investment in Finnish AI infrastructure over the next two years, which the company described as its largest single investment in Europe. Google said the project will include data centers and grid improvements to support services like Gemini and Search. The investment is expected to contribute approximately $3.6 billion to Finland's GDP during construction and support around 7,000 jobs annually. Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo stated the decision highlights the country's strengths in the digital economy.

title: Apple plans to name its first foldable iPhone the iPhone Duo
summary: Apple is reportedly planning to name its upcoming foldable smartphone the iPhone Duo. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports that the company is moving away from speculation regarding names like iPhone Ultra or iPhone Fold. This new designation marks a shift in Apple's strategy for its anticipated foldable device.

title: Apple expected to unveil folding iPhone as new CEO takes center stage
summary: Apple is expected to unveil a folding iPhone during its annual event, marking the first foldable model for the company and serving as a major test for new CEO John Ternus. The device, rumored to cost over $2000 and lack Face ID, will be presented alongside updates to other product lines including a first-ever touchscreen MacBook. Bloomberg reports that Apple began testing prototypes in early 2021, though the final name and specifications remain unknown. Ternus, who replaced Tim Cook on September 1, expressed excitement about the upcoming launch in a note to employees.

title: Elon Musk's ex-girlfriend accuses him of sowing deliberate division on X
summary: Ashley St Clair, the mother of one of Elon Musk's 14 confirmed children, has accused the world's richest man of sowing 'deliberate division' on his social media platform X. Speaking in a new documentary by Alex Gibney, St Clair revealed that Musk told her he wanted to have a child with her because he needed to have 'a legion of children before the civil war'. She further stated that Musk's team offered her a $40m lump-sum payment and a $100,000 monthly stipend in return for signing a non-disclosure agreement, but withdrew the offer after she refused to sign it.

title: OpenAI CFO says AI chip design tool beats open-source rivals on cost
summary: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar announced at the Goldman Sachs conference that the company is expanding into specialized industries like chip design, leveraging AI to undercut open-source rivals on cost. Friar highlighted that OpenAI's lower-cost Luna model is cheaper than Chinese alternatives such as Z.ai's GLM 5.3 when deployed on cloud layers. She also noted a 32 percent increase in enterprise revenue from June to July, driven by aggressive pricing strategies and a focus on business outcomes.

title: OpenAI agents solve Millennium Prize Problem on Navier-Stokes equations
summary: OpenAI announced that agents of an unreleased model solved the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem within 88 hours by proving the equations sometimes break down. Tristan Buckmaster accused the firm of interfering with his and a colleague's earlier work on related sub-questions, a claim OpenAI denied. The firm deployed around 10,000 agents on Aug. 28 to achieve this result.

title: Fiction dominates top hardcover bestseller lists in 2025
summary: Data indicates a significant shift in publishing trends, with fiction now comprising 18 of the top 25 hardcover bestsellers in 2025, compared to just 6 in 2015.

title: Chinese Vice President Han Zheng pledges more measures to boost international investment
summary: Chinese Vice President Han Zheng announced on Tuesday that China will actively expand voluntary opening-up and take further measures to facilitate international investment. Speaking at the opening ceremony of the 26th China International Fair for Investment and Trade in Xiamen, he emphasized the importance of global cooperation amidst rising uncertainties. The event drew registrations from more than 1,200 official government institutions and business delegations representing 129 countries and regions, as well as 30 international organizations.

title: CGTN poll finds nearly 90% view CIFTIS as key to China's services opening
summary: A global online survey by CGTN conducted within 24 hours found that 89.6% of 2,406 respondents view the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services as a key platform for China's services opening. The poll, released across five languages, highlighted that 93.8% see the fair as a core trading platform, while 90.3% believe China's services trade is rapidly enhancing technological sophistication. The event featured a new 'China Services' exhibition area showcasing AI and digital innovations, attracting 90 countries and over 1,800 enterprises. Respondents noted that China's services trade, which surpassed $620 billion in imports in 2025, continues to unlock global opportunities despite rising protectionism.

title: Samsung Electronics celebrates full opening of Yokohama semiconductor research base
summary: Samsung Electronics held a ceremony Tuesday to mark the full opening of its Yokohama semiconductor research base, which focuses on back-end chip assembly technology. The company plans to invest a total of 40 billion yen by 2028, including 20 billion yen in Japanese government subsidies, to expand operations at the facility. Samsung Vice Chairman Jun Young-hyun stated the base aims to promote technological exchanges between Japan and South Korea.

title: Apple unveils new iPhones with foldable model as John Ternus becomes CEO
summary: Apple is preparing to unveil its latest iPhone lineup, widely expected to include a foldable version, at an event headlined by new CEO John Ternus. Analyst Dipanjan Chatterjee noted that Apple typically waits for technology to mature before entering a market, though the new phones may cost more due to a global memory chip shortage. The event in Cupertino will outline Ternus's vision as he inherits a successful company from Tim Cook.

title: ECB to raise rates despite easing underlying inflation pressures
summary: The European Central Bank is set to raise interest rates on Thursday, with market odds indicating a near-certain quarter-point increase to 2.5%. Although headline inflation in the eurozone reached 3.3% in August, largely due to energy costs, core inflation actually declined to 2.4%. ECB economists attribute the energy surge to geopolitical supply shocks rather than domestic demand, arguing this differs from previous inflationary periods. The move is described as an 'insurance rate hike' because underlying economic pressures are easing. This decision coincides with anticipated rate adjustments by the Federal Reserve and the Bank of Japan later in September, creating complex currency dynamics for the euro.

title: Huawei begins U.S. trial over Iran dealings and trade secret charges
summary: Jury selection began Tuesday in Brooklyn federal court for Huawei Technologies, which faces fraud and conspiracy charges. Prosecutors accuse the Chinese company of defrauding banks over its business with Iran, conspiring to steal trade secrets from five U.S. technology companies, and lying about dealings in North Korea. The trial also involves allegations that Huawei supplied surveillance equipment to Iran to track protesters during 2009 anti-government demonstrations in Tehran. This case represents one of the U.S. government's earliest and most closely watched battles against a Chinese company as tech competition heats up between the two countries.

title: Five Miami plane crash victims identified as Amazon jet ran off runway
summary: Five people died when an Amazon cargo jet ran off the runway at Miami International Airport and struck a shuttle van used by an aircraft cleaning crew. Miami-Dade County Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz confirmed the identities of the deceased, while the National Transportation Safety Board Chairwoman Jennifer Homendy announced that the investigation will center on the lack of specialized deceleration systems. Although the airport maintains a safety buffer, it lacks lightweight crushable materials found at other US airfields. Homendy emphasized that recommendations must be implemented to prevent future tragedies. Investigators have recovered the flight data recorder and are scheduling interviews with the crew and witnesses. Two victims remain in critical condition, while the pilots have been released from the hospital.

title: Teacher Ruan Junting reflects on education through her comic Chunhui
summary: Ruan Junting, an art teacher at the China Academy of Art, created the comic Chunhui to reflect on the meaning of education after students challenged her views on success. She stated that helping students discover their own passions is more important than imposing her own ideas on them.

title: China's consumer price index rose 0.8% in August
summary: Official data showed China's consumer price index, a main gauge of inflation, rose 0.8% year on year in August. The figure was released on Wednesday.

title: Riverside families in the Amazon change meals as mercury poisons staple fish
summary: Mongabay Latam investigated the impact of mercury contamination on Amazonian communities by building a database from over 7,000 human and 5,900 fish samples. The analysis identified Lake Puruzinho in Amazonas, Calama, and the Karipuna Indigenous Territory in Rondônia as areas with severe exposure linked to illegal gold mining. Studies show mercury concentrations in Lake Puruzinho residents range from 15.61 to 25.81 micrograms per gram, well above the World Health Organization safe limit of 2 micrograms per gram. Consequently, families like that of Maria Rogelina dos Santos have drastically reduced their consumption of staple fish like tucunaré. Researchers from the Federal University of Rondônia note that organic mercury accumulates in the body, causing neurological and cardiological problems. While Brazil is a party to the Minamata Convention, the government has not yet implemented restrictions on mercury use in gold mining in these states. The Federal Public Ministry criticized a national mining plan for excluding Indigenous peoples from its development. Health officials report increased cases of respiratory diseases and neurological symptoms, though specific federal data for the Madeira River region remains incomplete. Residents express concern over the inability to safely consume fish or access clean water without traveling to cities.

title: Study finds Indigenous territories maintain Amazon forests as well as protected areas
summary: A new study reports that Indigenous territories in Ecuador's Amazon maintained forest conditions comparable to formal protected areas despite lacking conservation contracts. Researchers analyzed satellite data across three governance models, finding that while community-protected forests showed strong drought resilience, Indigenous lands exhibited the greatest proportion of positive long-term vegetation trends. Lead author Fernando Troya stated that effective conservation depends on governance and local participation rather than simply drawing lines on a map. The study noted that government-protected forests in northern Ecuador showed more degradation due to roads and oil development.

title: Trump bans Canadian alcohol and hikes tariffs in trade escalation
summary: President Donald Trump escalated his trade dispute with Canada by issuing executive orders to ban alcohol imports and impose a 50% tariff on specific goods. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney acknowledged the economic cost of loosening ties but insisted the benefits would outweigh the pain. Canada has already implemented retaliatory tariffs on US imports, while Trump threatened to bar Canadian companies from US government contracts. The two nations have not resumed negotiations since talks broke down in August.

title: Trump bans Canadian alcohol and raises tariffs on other goods
summary: The White House escalated its trade dispute with Canada by banning specific imports and raising tariffs on others. President Donald Trump signed executive orders imposing a 50% surcharge on goods such as mattresses and motorboats starting September 15, while banning alcoholic beverages and some dairy products from September 29. A senior administration official explained the measures are intended to maintain a level playing field and protect American production. These actions follow Ottawa's recent imposition of new tariffs on U.S. products in response to duties announced by Washington on August 22. Additionally, Trump threatened to exclude Canadian products from a government procurement program unless reciprocity is restored.

title: Canadian PM defends sovereignty as $20 billion US tariffs take effect
summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said he would protect Canada's sovereignty as retaliatory tariffs on $20 billion of US goods took effect. He expressed regret that trade talks with the US collapsed.

title: Canada accelerates economic diversification from US as tariffs take effect
summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced Tuesday that Canada will accelerate efforts to reduce its economic reliance on the United States as retaliatory tariffs on approximately $20 billion of U.S. goods took effect, with Ottawa bracing for President Donald Trump's response.

title: Experts discuss APEC's role in building a smarter energy future
summary: An editor's note introduces a discussion on how APEC economies can maintain affordable, reliable, and sustainable energy through renewables and AI. Panelists Wang Guan, John Pang, Steivan Defilla, and John Grimes examine challenges regarding energy access, the green transition, and China's renewable capacity.

title: Andrew Hastie accuses Pauline Hanson and Barnaby Joyce of lying cowardice
summary: Opposition frontbencher Andrew Hastie has escalated a dispute with One Nation leaders Pauline Hanson and Barnaby Joyce by calling them "lying cowards." The conflict stems from a video describing Hastie as a "traitor," which both leaders deny making personally. Senator Barnaby Joyce confirmed he had not used the term but acknowledged a satirical cartoon contained the claim. Hastie, a former SAS officer, argues the accusation is a slur on veterans who testified in the Ben Roberts-Smith defamation case. He has vowed to fight exceptionally hard to retain his seat of Canning against One Nation in the 2028 election, stating the party has "picked a fight with the wrong veteran."

title: Man charged after three-day manhunt ends over family axe attack
summary: Police ended a three day manhunt after arresting Peter O Ryan in Tyers, Victoria, who allegedly attacked his brother and parents with an axe. O Ryan faces three counts of intentionally causing serious injury and was remanded in custody after refusing to leave the cells during his court appearance. Magistrate Justice James Elliott noted management issues including paranoid schizophrenia and denied bail to Zeinab Ahmad, an Australian woman linked to Islamic State, who argued childbirth changed her views. In other news, Queensland police fined a 29 year old driver $1 104 for buttering a bagel while driving. Federal social services minister Tanya Plibersek denied accusations regarding a $6m grant to a golf club in Prime Minister Anthony Albanese s electorate. Labor MP Plibersek also shared her experience of being assaulted while walking home in Canberra. Attorney General Michelle Rowland stated the government is working on a framework for automated decision making with robust safeguards.

title: South Korean protesters oppose troop deployment to Strait of Hormuz
summary: Dozens of South Korean protesters gathered in Seoul on Wednesday to urge their government against deploying troops to the Strait of Hormuz, characterizing the conflict as an illegal war. The demonstration occurred one day after South Korean defence authorities announced a fact-finding mission to the region while emphasizing that no deployment decision had been made. Protesters, including representatives from civic groups, argued that sending soldiers would constitute direct participation in US aggression and could lead to casualties. Meanwhile, Iran has warned that any South Korean deployment would be viewed as support for the aggressors. South Korea is currently weighing potential contributions to US security efforts along the strait, provided its own military readiness remains uncompromised. Any future deployment would require a majority vote in the National Assembly.

title: Ex-politician denies seeing Alan Jones kiss athlete at trial
summary: During Alan Jones's criminal trial in the NSW Local Court, a former politician testified regarding an alleged indecent assault involving a prominent athlete. The witness, who attended an event a decade ago, told the court he did not see Jones kiss the athlete, known as Complainant M, on the mouth. Under cross-examination by barrister Gabrielle Bashir SC, the politician affirmed he would remember such an act if it had happened. Meanwhile, the prosecution presented evidence that Complainant M received weekly flowers and text messages from Jones for over a year. Separate testimony described the alleged victim, Complainant C, as appearing 'sunken and diminished' during a meeting with Jones, while a colleague who succeeded him denied witnessing any inappropriate conduct.

title: Singapore police investigate five people over racist online comments
summary: Singapore police have questioned five people over alleged racist online comments regarding Nepal floods and Singapore Airlines' investment in Air India. Senior Minister K. Shanmugam announced the investigation following reports of shameful remarks targeting Indians. The Ministry of Digital Development and Information will ask social media platforms to remove comments that breach guidelines. Prime Minister Lawrence Wong emphasized that prejudice against any community must not be normalized.

title: Kenya forms committee to resolve Tata Chemicals compliance issues
summary: Kenya's Ministry of Mining, Blue Economy, and Maritime Affairs announced the establishment of a high-level technical committee to resolve compliance issues with Tata Chemicals Magadi Ltd. Cabinet Secretary Hassan Ali Joho stated the committee will review outstanding matters such as mineral beneficiation and community benefits. The government aims to create a sustainable framework for responsible mining while maintaining constructive engagement with investors.

title: OpenAI expands chip and AI cooperation with Samsung Electronics
summary: OpenAI is deepening its partnership with Samsung Electronics to develop custom chips and expand enterprise AI services. Harrison Kim, General Manager of OpenAI Korea, highlighted joint research on next-generation chips and noted that Samsung is among the largest-scale global deployments of ChatGPT. OpenAI reported a 28-fold surge in ChatGPT Enterprise users at South Korean companies as businesses adopt AI across various functions. The collaboration follows Samsung and SK Hynix signing letters of intent to supply memory chips for OpenAI's Stargate data centre project.

title: BJP launches month-long Seva Sankalp campaign on Modi's birthday
summary: The BJP announced on September 9, 2026, that it will launch a month-long 'Seva Sankalp' campaign beginning on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's birthday, September 17. BJP chief Nitin Nabin stated the initiative aims to highlight Modi's 25 years of public service and claimed that 25 crore families have been brought out of poverty under his leadership.

title: Tamil Nadu gold ring scheme launch delayed for CM's London investment visit
summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay has postponed the September 15 launch of his gold ring scheme to facilitate his first official overseas visit to London. The announcement comes as Vijay prepares to meet European industrialists and seek fresh investment commitments for the state. Senior officials from the industries and finance departments are also expected to travel to London to support these discussions. Meanwhile, the deferred scheme, which provides a one-gram gold ring worth around Rs 13,600 to newborns delivered at government facilities, was intended to celebrate the cultural tradition of 'Thaimaaman Seer' and coincide with the birth anniversary of former CM C N Annadurai. The state has allocated approximately Rs 755.83 crore annually for the initiative, covering nearly 4.2 lakh expected institutional deliveries.

title: Supreme Court criticizes magistrate for issuing notice to CJP protester student
summary: The Supreme Court criticized a Greater Noida executive magistrate for issuing a notice to a law student attending a Cockroach Janata Party protest, violating a September 1 direction barring coercive action against students. Chief Justice Surya Kant questioned how a magistrate could dare issue such a notice. Additionally, the Allahabad High Court reprimanded Gautam Budh Nagar district magistrate Medha Roopam for approving National Security Act detention of student activist Akriti Chaudhary without credible supporting material. The court warned that errant bureaucrats risk reducing Uttar Pradesh to an Orwellian dystopia if they disregard their constitutional oath.

title: Iran attacks US base in Jordan as oil prices rise amid conflict fears
summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards reported attacking two US destroyers and a facility in Jordan's Al Azraq with ballistic missiles, citing retaliation for US strikes on Iranian oil tankers. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated Washington would continue targeting Iranian tankers in response to attacks on US warships. Amid rising tensions, Goldman Sachs warned oil prices could reach $120 a barrel if hostilities intensify, while JPMorgan estimated prices could add $7 to $8 per barrel for every additional month of disruption. Other analysts, including Citi and ANZ, raised their Brent crude forecasts to $86 and $95 respectively, citing a prolonged standoff between the US and Iran.

title: Apple Unveils Foldable iPhone Ultra Tonight; India Availability Delayed
summary: Apple is set to unveil its first foldable iPhone, the iPhone Ultra, tonight alongside the iPhone 18 Pro models. However, supply constraints suggest Indian buyers may face significant delays, with availability potentially pushed to late 2026 or early 2027. Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo notes that only a fraction of the usual inventory will be ready initially, with the US prioritized. While global pricing is estimated between $1,999 and $2,399, Indian estimates range from ₹1.3 lakh to over ₹3 lakh, pending official confirmation.

title: OpenAI agents solve Navier-Stokes problem; NYU professor accuses company of cheating
summary: OpenAI announced that 10,000 AI agents solved the 90-year-old Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem in 88 hours using an unreleased model. NYU professor Tristan Buckmaster accused OpenAI of racing down a research path based on his unpublished work, while the company denied accessing specific user data but conceded it cannot rule out that de-identified data improved its models. The Clay Mathematics Institute has not yet verified the solution.

title: IT stocks crash as Coforge leads selloff amid leadership changes
summary: IT stocks came under intense selling pressure on Wednesday, with the Nifty IT index falling nearly 3.6% as Coforge led the decline after chairman O P Bhatt resigned. Choice Institutional Equities Research Analyst Kunal Bajaj noted that higher crude prices and hawkish Fed expectations are creating a sentiment overhang, though underlying deal activity remains resilient. Global market weakness and rising crude prices further contributed to the broader market downturn.

title: Jio and Apple launch new RCS pricing for businesses in India
summary: People familiar with the development said Jio and Apple have enabled brands to send application-to-person messages to iPhone users on Jio's network. This partnership allows marketing, transactional, and OTP messages to reach iPhone users. Vodafone Idea and Bharti Airtel are also expected to onboard the Apple RCS ecosystem soon. A Juniper Research study expects telecom operators to generate $2 billion globally from RCS for business traffic in 2026, up from $1.2 billion last year.

title: Apple to Unveil iPhone 18 Pro Series and First Foldable in India
summary: Apple is scheduled to host its annual keynote event in Cupertino today, where it is rumoured to launch the iPhone 18 Pro series and its first foldable phone, the iPhone Ultra. The event will be streamed live from the Steve Jobs Theater, with the iPhone Ultra expected to feature a book-style design, an A20 chip, and a price between $1,999 and $2,399. Additionally, the company is expected to unveil the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, which may include processor upgrades and new health-tracking features.

title: ANI appeals Delhi High Court ruling on OpenAI content use
summary: News agency ANI has moved a division bench of the Delhi High Court against a single judge's order dismissing its plea to restrain OpenAI from using its content to train ChatGPT. ANI argues that OpenAI infringed its exclusive rights by scraping, storing, and commercially exploiting the agency's work, contrary to the lower court's finding that the use qualified as fair dealing under Indian copyright law. The appeal was listed before justices V Kameshwar Rao and Manmeet PS Arora but was adjourned to September 14 as the bench did not assemble.

title: Apple hosts iPhone 18 launch event with foldable phone
summary: Apple is hosting its 'Surprise and Shine' event today, September 9, to unveil the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the company's first foldable iPhone. The foldable device, widely expected to be called the iPhone Ultra, is anticipated to feature a book-style folding design with a 7.8-inch inner display and a titanium frame. Reports suggest the phone may use Touch ID instead of Face ID and include two 48MP rear cameras. The event will also likely introduce new Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 models, along with potential AirPods 5 and smart-home product updates. Apple CEO John Ternus is expected to host the keynote, which will begin at 10:30 pm IST. Preorders are reportedly set to open on September 12, with retail sales potentially starting on September 18.

title: Instagram briefly suspended three journalists reporting on MP child deaths
summary: Instagram briefly suspended the accounts of three independent journalists reporting on child deaths in Madhya Pradesh's Balaghat district before restoring them on Wednesday. The Press Club of India condemned the action, alleging the reporters faced pressure and surveillance from local authorities. The Indian Youth Congress also criticized the state government for targeting independent journalism regarding the healthcare collapse.

title: Users create 1980s AI portraits on Instagram using ChatGPT prompts
summary: Instagram users are adopting a new trend that utilizes ChatGPT to transform modern photographs into 1980s-style portraits. Instead of applying standard vintage filters, individuals upload their images to the AI tool and request recreations of the era. Participants share their specific prompts on Instagram Stories using the platform's 'Add Yours' sticker to invite friends to join. The resulting images display diverse aesthetics, ranging from Bollywood studio portraits to old family album styles. Users specify details such as warm lighting, bright colors, and specific clothing to achieve an authentic look. The article notes that these creations aim to visualize how individuals might have appeared forty years ago.

title: Amazon Launches Creator Connections Program in India
summary: Amazon announced the launch of Creator Connections in India, a new program designed to connect eligible creators directly with relevant brand campaigns. The initiative aims to help over 1.65 lakh creators build sustainable income through performance-led engagement. Nidhi Thakkar, Head of Social Commerce at Amazon, stated the program simplifies monetization by matching creators with campaigns aligned with their content and interests ahead of the festive season. The launch builds on existing programs like the Amazon Influencer Program to support regional and emerging creators.

title: Kerala Tourism asks Apple CEO John Ternus to add a Sadya emoji
summary: Kerala Tourism has urged Apple CEO John Ternus to add a Sadya emoji to Apple devices. The request came in response to Ternus' first social media post after assuming the role of Apple CEO on September 1. Kerala Tourism shared a picture of a traditional Kerala Sadya with the caption, "Submitting our petition to add a sadya emoji." The traditional vegetarian feast holds a special place in Kerala's food and cultural heritage. Apple is preparing for a major product launch event on September 9, where the tech giant is expected to unveil its first foldable iPhone alongside the iPhone 18 Pro models.

title: US bans Canadian dairy, alcohol, motorcycles as trade war escalates
summary: The White House announced on Tuesday that the United States is banning dairy products, most alcoholic beverages, and motorcycles from Canada. This ban, set to take effect in three weeks, follows Canada's imposition of retaliatory tariffs on USD 20 billion in US imports. US President Donald Trump directed the General Services Administration to exclude Canadian products from government contracts until full reciprocity is achieved. In response, Prime Minister Mark Carney vowed to accelerate efforts to reduce Canada's dependence on the United States, noting that over 70 percent of Canadian exports currently go to the US. Carney defended the tariffs as necessary to protect Canadian workers and asserted that Washington sought dependency rather than a true economic partnership. Meanwhile, Canadian officials indicated the government will continue its strategy of building domestic capacity and diversifying trade abroad regardless of further US actions.

title: Supreme Court seeks explanation from Greater Noida magistrate over student protest notice
summary: The Supreme Court questioned a Greater Noida executive magistrate for issuing a notice to student Akshat Tripathi regarding his participation in the Cockroach Janta Party protest. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant expressed surprise, stating the court had previously ordered that no coercive action be taken against students. The bench directed the lawyer to place the notice on record and seek an explanation from the authority. Senior Advocate Bishwajit Bhattacharyya argued the move constituted contempt of court, even after the notice was withdrawn.

title: Delhi airport operator DIAL files FIR against 63 social media handles
summary: Delhi airport operator DIAL announced on September 9, 2026, that it has filed a First Information Report against 63 social media handles for spreading misleading information regarding flooding at Indira Gandhi International Airport. The company stated that while temporary water accumulation occurred at Terminal 3 on September 4, operations remained unaffected and the situation was resolved within 20 minutes. DIAL described the posts as a deliberate attempt to create public mischief and damage the airport's reputation.

title: Delhi CM orders scrutiny of records on illegal constructions after building collapse
summary: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta directed officials to inspect all paying guest accommodations and scrutinize building records following a fatal collapse in south Delhi. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi has launched a demolition drive, sealing seven illegal structures and taking action against 24 properties since the incident. Officials were also asked to ensure senior civic leaders remain on the ground during the enforcement drive.

title: One killed, four injured after oxygen cylinder explodes in Delhi
summary: PTI reported that one person died and four others were injured after an oxygen cylinder exploded near a community hall in Okhla Phase-1, Delhi, on Wednesday. Emergency services, including three water tenders and a multi-casualty first responder vehicle, rushed to the scene around 11 am, and the injured were taken to a nearby hospital.

title: CJI questions magistrate notice to student over Jantar Mantar protest
summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday decided to seek an explanation from the Greater Noida executive magistrate for issuing a notice to a student over his participation in a CJP-led Jantar Mantar protest.
