summary: ETMarkets.com reported that ten smallcap stocks gained more than 96% in one year, with HFCL recording the highest rise of 233.67%. The list includes Welspun Corp, Kirloskar Oil Engines, and Chennai Petroleum among others that posted significant annual gains.

title: ED raids nine Ramnandi Hotels locations in alleged Rs 132 crore fraud case
summary: The Enforcement Directorate searched nine locations in Bihar, Haryana, and Delhi on Friday regarding an alleged Rs 132 crore bank fraud involving Ramnandi Hotels and Resorts Ltd. Officials stated the searches were conducted under Section 17 of the PMLA, noting properties were sold at undervalued prices with cash receipts. Some buyers are suspected to be proxies of Akhouri Gopal. Vijaya Srivastava, a journalist covering human-centred developments, reported on the case.

title: BRICS leaders gather in Delhi for summit amid heightened security
summary: The 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit is set to convene in New Delhi on September 12 and 13, focusing on global governance, trade, and security challenges. Organizers have outlined a detailed schedule featuring closed-door meetings, exhibitions, and a joint tree-planting ceremony. To ensure safety, around 15,000 Delhi Police personnel and 200 paramilitary companies have been deployed, with aerial restrictions imposed within a 300-km radius of the capital. Prominent arrivals include Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, whose visit marks his first trip to India in seven years. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to host a gala dinner and hold bilateral talks with visiting leaders.

title: Sam Altman Says OpenAI May Slow AI Development and Hopes Rivals Will Follow
summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told employees the company may slow its cutting-edge AI development, hoping other labs will follow, Bloomberg reported. This potential shift follows a surge in internal safety concerns, highlighted by former researcher Jacob Coxon's viral post warning that AI could kill everyone by the end of the decade. However, sources caution that any formal industry-wide coordination to slow development could risk running afoul of antitrust laws.

title: OpenAI launches finance-focused ChatGPT with enterprise controls
summary: OpenAI has launched ChatGPT for Financial Services, a new platform targeting investment banking and equity research with integrated financial datasets and enterprise security controls. The company stated that its work with partners like Morgan Stanley identified reliable data access and high-quality artifact creation as major challenges for financial teams. The product provides built-in access to datasets from providers such as Daloopa and PitchBook, allowing professionals to trace figures back to sources without separate contracts. OpenAI emphasized that firm business data is not used to train models by default, while administrators can manage access and create multiple workspaces to enforce information barriers.

title: Anthropic reports Yemen weapons cell used Claude for missile software
summary: Anthropic published a report identifying a Yemen-based weapons engineering cell that utilized its Claude artificial intelligence model to create guidance software for missiles. The company stated it disrupted six operations in China, Russia, and Yemen where actors employed the AI for conventional weapons development and procurement. While Anthropic found no evidence the group successfully fielded an operational weapon, the actors did conduct a failed test launch of a guided rocket. The report highlights that the group used multiple Claude instances simultaneously to write control software and tune settings, attempting to circumvent safety measures by concealing their work's purpose. Anthropic banned the linked accounts and shared intelligence with partners, noting that AI capabilities are collapsing the labor gap between state-sponsored operations and individual operators. The company also flagged risks regarding biological research misuse and plans to incorporate investigation findings into its safeguards.

title: Anthropic Accuses Chinese AI Labs of Routing User Data Through Fraudulent Accounts
summary: Anthropic accused Chinese AI laboratories, including Moonshot AI and DeepSeek, of secretly routing customer prompts to its Claude models through networks of fraudulent accounts. According to Bloomberg, Moonshot relied on 5,380 fake accounts to divert nearly 300,000 requests in one ten-day stretch, using the responses to train its own software. Anthropic stated that these practices exposed sensitive data, including queries from a user likely affiliated with China's People's Liberation Army and credentials for a Russian government database. The company reported that these activities totalled more than 23 million exchanges between May and July and marked an escalation in its dispute over illicit distillation.

title: Users create Kerala retro images with ChatGPT prompts
summary: A viral trend has emerged where users transform modern photographs into portraits resembling Kerala images from the 1960s through the 1990s. Mint Senior Assistant Editor Anjali Thakur reports that users specify details such as clothing, hairstyles, and lighting to achieve authentic vintage looks. Specificity in prompts is crucial for guiding the AI to recreate desired visual elements accurately. Thakur notes that users must explicitly state which elements should remain unchanged to preserve identity while modifying styling. Additionally, excluding modern objects helps maintain an authentic retro appearance consistent with the chosen historical period.

title: Anthropic blocks AI misuse for biological weapons and cyberattacks
summary: Anthropic announced Thursday that it blocked attempts by malicious actors to utilize its artificial intelligence for cyberattacks, surveillance, and biological weapon development. The company detailed findings from its third misuse report since March 2025, which included a blocked request for Claude to assist in a grant application for gain-of-function research on the chikungunya virus. Anthropic noted that while older models were less capable of aiding sophisticated biological research, newer models pose greater risks, prompting the implementation of stricter safeguards. The report follows concerns raised by a resigning researcher regarding the industry's rapid development of powerful AI systems.

title: Users avoid common mistakes to create realistic 1980s AI photos on social media
summary: A new social media trend involves using ChatGPT to transform modern selfies into realistic 1980s-style photographs. Mint Senior Assistant Editor Anjali Thakur reports that achieving a convincing result depends heavily on prompt specificity. Users must avoid vague instructions and ensure the AI preserves their identity while adding period details like analog grain and bold colors. OpenAI provided a sample prompt that explicitly requests retention of facial features while altering clothing and surroundings to reflect the mid-1980s era. Thakur notes that including modern objects or failing to describe the photographic aesthetic undermines the retro effect. The article emphasizes that detailed instructions regarding lighting, textures, and era-specific accessories are necessary to distinguish authentic-looking recreations from generic AI interpretations.

title: Apple iPhone Duo and Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 display technologies compared
summary: Apple has entered the foldable market with the iPhone Duo, leveraging lessons from Samsung's earlier generations to create a more mature device. While both phones use OLED technology, Apple employs a custom nano-texture finish and viscoelastic adhesives to reduce glare and crease visibility, according to Macrumors. Conversely, Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8 focuses on physical reinforcement using a titanium layer and Corning Gorilla Glass Ceramic 3 to ensure resilience against daily impacts and scratches.

title: US Recalls 264 Pounds of Colombian Potato Chips With Pork
summary: El Eden Import Distributor Corp. recalled approximately 264 pounds of De Todito potato chip snacks from New Jersey and Utah after discovering they contained pork cracklings imported from Colombia. The US Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service initiated the investigation following a consumer complaint regarding the unlabelled meat content. FSIS announced the recall on September 9, 2026, advising consumers not to consume the items while noting no illnesses have been linked to the products.

title: Modi hosts Xi and other leaders at BRICS summit in Delhi
summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar addressed the BRICS Business Forum, emphasizing India's chairship theme of resilience and innovation amid global challenges. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is hosting Chinese President Xi Jinping in Delhi for a bilateral meeting, ending a seven-year gap, to discuss border situations and trade deficits. The summit also features meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. Meanwhile, the IMF noted India's 7.8 per cent GDP growth in the second quarter.

title: China Hopes to Reach US Tariff Reduction Deal Soon
summary: A Chinese government spokesperson said negotiators are striving to implement reciprocal tariff reductions on $30 billion worth of goods at an early date. Commerce Ministry spokesperson Huang Ling stated the amount will come from each side. Barclays Bank noted that while trade will be central to the upcoming summit, the scope for a broad deal is limited as the truce expires on Nov. 10.

title: Police rescue Class 11 student kidnapped by senior over one-sided love
summary: Police rescued an 18-year-old Class 11 student from Arangi forest after she was kidnapped by a senior student and four associates over one-sided love. Authorities arrested the main accused, Biriya Oraon, and four other youths, seizing the Bolero SUV used in the abduction. Police official Neeraj Kumar stated that the case has been registered and assured that those responsible would be sent behind bars.

title: S Jaishankar urges deeper BRICS economic cooperation and resilient supply networks
summary: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar addressed the BRICS Business Forum, stating that greater economic activity and security within the bloc would enhance self-reliance. He emphasized the need for genuine market practices, reliable logistics, and diversified commercial relationships to strengthen business ties among member countries. The forum serves as a principal platform for private-sector engagement, shaping the grouping's economic priorities ahead of the upcoming September summit.

title: Omar Abdullah challenges Congress over mandatory Vande Mataram singing
summary: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah pushed back at Congress allies regarding the mandatory singing of the full Vande Mataram song at official events. Abdullah stated that a law enacted in July makes all stanzas of the national song compulsory wherever the national anthem is played, calling it a statutory obligation for the entire country. He questioned why Congress would demand Kashmiris be jailed for complying with this rule. Conversely, Congress leaders, including K C Venugopal and Tariq Hamid Karra, expressed disapproval, arguing the unabridged version does not align with India's pluralist ethos. NC spokesperson Sadiq countered by highlighting that Congress-ruled states in Karnataka and Telangana also play the full version during government functions.

title: IRCTC sets record with over 2 million tickets booked in one day
summary: IRCTC reported that 20,06,353 tickets were booked on September 7, surpassing the previous peak of 18,40,203 recorded last year. Officials stated that system upgrades, including anti-bot measures and infrastructure overhauls, enabled the platform to handle high demand without failures or outages. The corporation noted that 89% of reserved tickets are booked online, with the Next Generation e-Ticketing system managing millions of logins and bookings during advance reservation periods. Actions against misuse resulted in over 3 million user IDs being deactivated and more than 63 million placed under revalidation.

title: Author argues Special Intensive Revision destroys Indian citizenship ethos
summary: Parakala Prabhakar argues that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls is destroying the ethos of Indian citizenship by creating two distinct classes of people. The author claims nearly 13 crore names have been deleted, with projections suggesting another crore will be removed, disproportionately affecting denotified tribes and minorities. Citing the Sabar Institute, the article states that deletions in certain Hyderabad constituencies exceeded total votes cast in the 2023 election. Prabhakar contends that the process targets Muslims, Christians, Dalits, and Adivasis, resulting in a 'savarna Hindu-isation' of the political landscape. He asserts that without franchise, citizenship becomes hollow, effectively rendering these groups stateless within their own borders. The author compares this trajectory to the political culture of Israel and warns that the revision serves as a weapon for political genocide, dismantling the secular, plural identity of the Indian Republic.

title: HDFC Bank shares hit 52-week low despite winning Credit Suisse bond cases
summary: HDFC Bank shares dropped to a fresh 52-week low of Rs 681.90 on Friday, falling 2% despite recent legal victories. The lender reported that the High Civil Court of Bahrain rejected all seven cases concerning Credit Suisse AT1 bonds, ruling that investors failed to provide sufficient admissible evidence. Although the court's decision removes a key legal overhang, the stock continues to decline amid broader governance concerns and mixed analyst sentiment. While Goldman Sachs initiated coverage with a 'Buy' call, Jefferies recently removed HDFC Bank from its India long-only model portfolio. The heavyweight stock has plunged around 31% in 2026 so far, dragging down major indices and mutual funds.

title: Anthropic blocks attempts to use AI for biological weapons
summary: Anthropic announced it has identified and disrupted attempts to use its AI models for malicious activities that could support biological weapons development. The company's latest threat intelligence report details five specific case studies where actors utilized its technology for this purpose. Anthropic emphasized that biological misuse represents one of the most serious risks of frontier AI models. The report also noted instances of misuse for conventional weapons, cyber operations, and scams. Anthropic stated it has incorporated these findings into its processes to better prevent, detect, and disrupt such activities in the future. The company shared intelligence with authorities and industry partners where appropriate. These findings contribute to ongoing industry warnings about AI risks, prompting calls for regulatory action from figures like US Senator Bernie Sanders.

title: Pennsylvania sues TikTok over addictive features and deceptive claims
summary: Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday announced a civil lawsuit against TikTok on August 11, 2026, accusing the social media platform of violating state consumer protection laws. The suit alleges TikTok made false statements about content maturity and knowingly created addictive features like infinite scrolling that harm youth. A TikTok spokesperson rejected the charges, calling the claims misleading and ignoring the company's voluntary safety measures. The article notes that while the lawsuit seeks liability, the issue of digital addiction does not fall neatly into binary distinctions of safe or dangerous.

title: Oil prices target $100 weekly finish as Middle East tensions rise
summary: Oil prices slipped on September 11 but remain on track to finish the week above $100 a barrel, marking the first time since mid-May. Brent crude futures fell 3.48% to $103.88, while US West Texas Intermediate crude dropped 3.25% to $99.15. The decline followed reports that Middle East foreign ministers are negotiating a temporary deal to manage shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Concurrently, US markets and Asian stocks slid amid fears of supply disruptions. Stocks and bonds across Asia fell as investors awaited US inflation data and potential Federal Reserve rate hikes. Analysts note that ongoing conflict, including Houthi assaults on Saudi energy facilities and US strikes on Iranian tankers, threatens to keep energy prices elevated and feed through to inflation.

title: Liquidators sue DBS over five accounts linked to Jho Low associate
summary: Court-appointed liquidators for 1MDB-linked companies filed a $1.3 billion damages claim against DBS in the Singapore High Court, alleging five accounts opened in 2013 were used to move stolen funds to luxury dealers. The 1MDB Asset Recovery Task Force stated that banks should have questioned the suspicious transactions involving Eric Tan, a known associate of Jho Low, and vowed that any recovered money will be returned to the Malaysian people. DBS categorically rejected the claim, stating it will vigorously resist the lawsuit.

title: Singapore minister advises graduates to build mastery amid tight job market
summary: Minister for Health Ong Ye Kung addressed graduates at the Kent Ridge Ministerial Forum regarding challenges in the current employment landscape. He noted that the proportion of graduates securing employment six months after graduation declined from about 93 per cent to 89 per cent from 2023 to 2025. The minister attributed this tightening market to increased graduate numbers, a self-reinforcing loop of internship requirements, and technological changes like AI replacing initial career rungs. Ong advised graduates to remain confident in Singapore's growing economy and to tap into existing support structures such as university career offices and the NTUC. He emphasized that building mastery in a chosen craft is the most important priority for long-term success. Furthermore, he argued that while AI impacts routine tasks, it does not cause mass job displacement and that society will likely continue to demand human touch in essential professions.

title: Autonomous vehicles may end diverse human driving cultures
summary: The article explores how autonomous vehicles might replace human driving, potentially ending diverse regional driving cultures. It notes that companies like Waymo and Tesla aim to make self-driving software the dominant force in transportation, with only a few firms likely to succeed in building the world's safest driver.

title: Article proposes runtime operating mode to prevent exception drift in enterprise agents
summary: The authors report that temporary emergency routes often linger in production systems after incidents resolve, creating unmanaged exception drift. The authors propose treating operating mode as an authoritative runtime input rather than inferring it from prompts or memory. The authors suggest an external control plane should manage exception state to ensure temporary accommodations automatically expire when incidents close. This approach prevents agents from carrying exception behavior beyond their authorized scope and duration. By making operating mode a first-class runtime construct, platforms can enforce governance constraints and verify that systems return to normal operations without manual cleanup.

title: China wafer prices drop as polysilicon production plans remain unverified
summary: China wafer prices declined as the mid-August rally faded, with M10 and 210R models dropping to $0.149 and $0.156 per piece, respectively, per the OPIS Global Solar Markets Report. Industry sources cite weakening downstream demand and supplier leverage issues as primary drivers, noting that n-type 183 wafers fell back to around CNY 1 per piece. Although a production-control initiative was reported in Sichuan aiming to cut 2026 polysilicon output by 20%, its legal enforceability remains uncertain. Meanwhile, domestic polysilicon production increased 13.1% in August to 118,900 metric tons, with September output expected to rise further despite upcoming seasonal constraints.

title: UAE and Mongolia sign MoU to advance renewable energy and green hydrogen cooperation
summary: The UAE Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure and the Ministry of Energy of Mongolia signed a Memorandum of Understanding to strengthen bilateral cooperation in renewable energy, green hydrogen, and clean energy infrastructure. UAE Minister Suhail bin Mohammed Al Mazrouei and Mongolia's Deputy Prime Minister Togmid Dorjkhand signed the agreement, which aims to promote knowledge exchange and explore joint projects. The partnership will establish a joint working group to identify priority areas and assess project feasibility, focusing on capacity building and private sector participation to support Mongolia's energy sector transformation.

title: Vattenfall approves 254 MW battery project in Brunsbüttel, Germany
summary: Swedish power company Vattenfall has made a final investment decision to construct a 254 MW battery storage facility in Brunsbüttel, northern Germany. According to Vattenfall, the project will be operational by the end of 2028 and will nearly double the company's existing battery capacity. Claus Wattendrup, head of solar and batteries at Vattenfall, stated that the facility is essential for strengthening energy security as renewable generation grows. The company also aims to optimize up to 1.5 GW of battery assets by 2029 through its flexibility optimization business.

title: Hannah König advises leaders to value disagreement and focus on contributions over identity
summary: Hannah König, Head of Project Execution at Enertrag, argues that the renewable energy industry urgently needs diverse talent to drive economic growth and the energy transition. She observes that while gender-inclusive leadership has not shifted significantly, individuals who excel and support others based on ability create genuine impact. König emphasizes that leaders must create safety for disagreement and openly acknowledge mistakes to foster improvement. She advises executives not to seek universal approval but to make difficult choices for the company's benefit. For women entering the sector, she suggests treating difference as an advantage by focusing on strengths and contributions rather than identity.

title: Eskom extends rooftop solar registration deadline to September 2026 amid disputes
summary: South African power utility Eskom has extended the registration deadline for residential solar systems to September 30, 2026, and removed the requirement for professional engineer sign-offs. The utility also withdrew previous threats of disconnection for unregistered systems. However, Eskom maintains its authority to disconnect installations it deems unsafe, a position challenged by OUTA and energy experts who argue that valid Certificates of Compliance should be respected unless legally invalidated. Legal analysts also question the regulatory basis for mandatory registration of systems below 100 kilowatts.

title: Türkiye claims final decision power at COP31 while Australia leads talks
summary: The provided text is a promotional advertisement for a news service and does not contain a news article body or headline to summarize.

title: RBI launches $136 billion FCNR bond sale to build forex reserves
summary: The Reserve Bank of India has launched a $136 billion FCNR bond sale to strengthen its foreign exchange reserves. Market expert Arun Kejriwal notes this move acts as a shock absorber against rising global borrowing costs and volatility. The RBI aims to build a forex cushion as global rates and oil prices increase.

title: Apple removes specific iPhones, Watches and AirPods from its India lineup
summary: Apple has updated its India retail lineup, removing the iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, Watch Series 11, Watch Ultra 3, and AirPods 4. The company notes that while these items are no longer listed, service and parts may remain available for at least five years after last distribution. Buyers are advised to verify seller policies for any remaining unsold units.

title: Chinese chip firm Enflame surges 180% in IPO amid Nvidia competition
summary: Shanghai Enflame Technology's stock price jumped 180% on its debut, with the IPO 6,000 times oversubscribed according to Nikkei. While Google's TPUs offer cost advantages over Nvidia GPUs, analysts note Nvidia remains central to the AI ecosystem.

title: IEA warns 2026 oil supply gap will widen on delayed Gulf flows
summary: The International Energy Agency warned that global oil supply and demand are set to fall further than previously expected this year. The agency stated that a lack of progress in ending the Middle East conflict delays normal Gulf oil flows into 2027, causing supply to decline by 5.7 million barrels per day in 2026. Meanwhile, world oil demand is projected to drop by 2.5 million barrels per day due to high prices, yet inventories are depleting at a record pace as buffers shrink. The IEA emphasized that resolving the conflict is crucial to avoid further market tightening.

title: Oracle shares rise after AI cloud backlog beats estimates
summary: Oracle shares rose 5.5 per cent premarket on Friday after the company reported stronger-than-expected quarterly results, booking more than $30 billion in additional AI cloud contracts. This boosted its revenue backlog to $664 billion, surpassing analyst estimates. J.P. Morgan analysts stated the results should address key investor concerns about sustaining backlog growth and converting it into revenue. Lale Akoner, an etoro market strategist, said the results should ease fears that Oracle is building ahead of demand. The stock trades at 16.86 times its forward earnings estimates, compared with Microsoft's 23.84 multiple and Amazon's 22.58 multiple, according to data compiled by LSEG.

title: Alex Gibney's documentary exposes Elon Musk as a confidence man
summary: Director Alex Gibney released a new documentary titled Musk, which portrays the Tesla co-founder as a confidence man who deceives and fabricates to achieve his goals. The film, running three hours and 45 minutes, traces Musk's career from Silicon Valley to his influence on politics and culture, featuring interviews with former associates and using AI-generated avatars since Musk refused to be interviewed. Gibney argues Musk's wealth comes from inflated stock values and describes his behavior as noble cause corruption. The documentary highlights contradictions in Musk's claims, including staged autonomous driving footage and unsubstantiated theories about space lasers affecting elections. While Gibney aims to show the full scope of Musk's impact, some critics note the film includes conspiratorial elements without evidence.

title: Sam Altman says OpenAI may slow AI development pace
summary: According to Bloomberg, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told employees this week that the company is open to slowing the development of cutting-edge artificial intelligence. Altman stated OpenAI might match its development tempo with peer labs, though he acknowledged not every company would participate. Bloomberg also reported that OpenAI recently halted certain internal AI training runs and scaled back portions of its model development work over safety concerns.

title: Proxy respondents lower reported male earnings and narrow Mexico's gender wage gap
summary: Researchers Estrada, Goyheix, and Lombardi analyzed Mexico's National Survey of Occupation and Employment to examine how proxy respondents affect earnings data. They found that when relatives answer for men, reported monthly earnings drop by 7.2% compared to self-reports, whereas the drop for women is only 1.8%. Consequently, the authors report that the measured gender wage gap becomes 25% narrower when proxy responses are included in standard calculations. The study indicates that men may partially hide income from household members, a behavior not observed with women. The researchers suggest statistical agencies should identify proxy respondents in public data to allow researchers to test for such measurement errors.

title: VoxDev highlights research on African startups, mining, AI, and lockdown impacts
summary: This week's VoxDev features research on African startups, mining, AI, and lockdown impacts. Emanuele Colonnelli and colleagues built a dataset showing African startups prefer local investor knowledge, while Roland Hodler and others found that new mine locations can affect conflict risk. Additionally, Sonia Bhalotra and team estimated that COVID-19 lockdowns increased helpline calls by 94% in Chile, and Girum Abebe and Simon Quinn documented evaluator bias against female candidates in Ethiopia.

title: Silver prices fall ahead of CPI data as rate hike expectations rise
summary: Silver futures opened 1.2% lower on September 11, 2026, showing negative momentum ahead of the Consumer Price Index report. Surging oil and gas prices have led more analysts to expect the Fed to raise rates next week, weighing on silver prices. According to the CME Group's FedWatch tool, 69.4% of traders now anticipate higher rates, up from 62.2% the previous day.

title: Gold price today, Friday, September 11, 2026: Gold opens at lowest level in over a month ahead of CPI data
summary: Gold futures opened at $4,359.40 per troy ounce on Friday, September 11, 2026, down 1.1% from the previous day's close and marking the lowest level since August 6. This decline occurred just hours before the release of the August Consumer Price Index report, which analysts expect to show a 3.4% price gain. Escalating tensions between the U.S. and Iran have driven oil prices higher, with Brent crude exceeding $103 per barrel. Consequently, the probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike next week has increased to 69.4% according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool, a move that could constrain gold's growth in the near term. The article also outlines varying expert recommendations for gold portfolio allocations ranging from 0% to 20%.

title: Israel destroys two kilometers of Hezbollah tunnels in southern Lebanon
summary: Israel announced it blew up two kilometers of tunnels operated by Hezbollah during an offensive that continues despite a months-old ceasefire. Israeli authorities have refused to withdraw from southern Lebanon, citing Hezbollah's refusal to give up arms as part of the US-brokered truce. The conflict has resulted in nearly 9,000 deaths and displaced hundreds of thousands since 2023.

title: UK government announces Alstom will build 29 battery-electric trains in Derby
summary: The Department for Transport announced that Alstom will construct 29 new Adessia Stream battery-electric trains at its Derby factory, with work starting in 2028 and service beginning in 2034. Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated the investment of almost £1bn aims to deliver faster journeys and support over 6,000 jobs across the UK supply chain. The trains, purchased by Rock Rail and leased to TransPennine Express, will operate on the TransPennine Route Upgrade, offering zero emissions on non-electrified sections and reducing journey times between Manchester and Leeds by up to 10 minutes.

title: Competitors troll Apple after unveiling new foldable iPhone Duo
summary: Apple unveiled its new foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, at its "Surprise and Shine" event on Wednesday, Sept. 9. Samsung responded with a sarcastic post on X, sparking a viral campaign that drew other brands like Motorola and DuoLingo into the online mockery.

title: AI incidents and researcher resignation fuel 'AIpocalypse' debate
summary: The article states that recent AI incidents and a researcher's resignation have pushed the 'AIpocalypse' debate to new heights. However, the provided text also displays a technical error message regarding a site loading failure.

title: Conservationists combine Indigenous knowledge with acoustic tech to hunt Amazon monkeys
summary: Conservationist Nicolás Schuldt Durán is partnering with the Siekopai Indigenous community in Ecuador to locate the pygmy marmoset, the world's smallest monkey. Durán, founder of Neblina Labs, combines local ecological knowledge with passive acoustic monitoring technology to track the vulnerable species. A recent pilot project deployed microphones for 72 hours but did not detect the monkeys, though it successfully recorded other local sounds. Durán stated the team now has a better understanding of the area's biodiversity and plans long-term fieldwork to improve detection chances. He emphasized that finding these primates is a main goal because their presence indicates good forest health.

title: OpenAI calls for binding national AI safety rules after GPT-6 Astra release
summary: OpenAI has shifted its stance to advocate for binding national AI safety rules in the United States. Chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane wrote that mandatory regulations should focus on advanced model capabilities. The company now supports a federal framework with common testing standards and independent assessments, following recent cybersecurity concerns surrounding its GPT-6 Astra model. OpenAI President Greg Brockman described the release as the beginning of the artificial general intelligence era.

title: Anthropic says China and Iran used its AI to spy on dissidents
summary: Anthropic announced Thursday that it disrupted several state-sponsored surveillance operations using its artificial intelligence models between January and July. The company stated these campaigns originated in China, Iran, and West Africa, targeting groups including Hong Kong pro-democracy activists. Additionally, Anthropic alleged that Chinese developers Moonshot and Deepseek secretly used its Claude model to generate user responses and train their own systems. The report noted that some of this data potentially violated privacy agreements.

title: Texas judge rules TikTok misled users about safety features
summary: A Texas court ruled that TikTok violated state consumer protection laws after finding the platform misled the public regarding its underage content filtering and Restricted Mode safety settings. Judge Cory Liu concluded that the company's internal labeling of rule-breaking posts and the failure of Restricted Mode exposed underage users to inappropriate media. Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton's office announced the lawsuit will move to trial within the coming month to determine financial penalties. This decision follows recent settlements between TikTok and minors over addiction claims, as well as a separate $18 billion agreement reached by Meta Platforms regarding similar youth safety allegations.

title: China expands telemedicine and smart hospital technology across BRICS nations
summary: China is advancing telemedicine and smart hospital infrastructure across BRICS nations through technology transfer and clinical partnerships. A landmark remote robotic subretinal injection recently connected a surgeon in Guangzhou with a patient in Urumqi, demonstrating micron-level precision over 4,200 kilometers. Domestically, telemedicine networks now cover all cities and counties, while AI platforms reduce pathology review time significantly. Internationally, the New Development Bank is financing an 800-bed smart hospital in São Paulo scheduled to open in 2029. Additionally, Chinese medical teams have performed first-of-their-kind procedures in Brazil, Indonesia, and Vietnam, and training programs have educated physicians from 13 countries.

title: Study finds unreported uranium in DRC cobalt exports poses nuclear risk
summary: Researchers have identified a significant gap in nuclear accountancy within the Democratic Republic of Congo's critical mineral supply chain. The authors report that their study estimates 2,000-5,000 tonnes of natural uranium were exported in cobalt-hydroxide shipments between 2000 and 2024. They state that less than 10% of this material was publicly declared to the International Atomic Energy Agency, with most exports going to China. The researchers note that this quantity could fuel a standard light-water nuclear reactor for 10-25 years or produce roughly 600-1,500 nuclear weapons. In response to the findings published in July 2026, the DRC launched a probe to test outgoing shipments and consult with the agency. The study highlights environmental risks to local communities from discarded uranium in tailings areas and calls for systematic assay measurement of cobalt products to ensure transparency and safety.

title: Shanghai hosts diplomats to showcase its people-centered city vision
summary: In November 2019, President Xi Jinping entrusted Shanghai with the mission of building a people-centered city. On September 8, 2026, 30 diplomats from 20 countries visited the Shanghai People's City Practice Exhibition Hall during a program hosted by the Chinese Foreign Ministry. The exhibition featured interactive displays highlighting Shanghai's practices in urban development.

title: China and US law enforcement crack synthetic cannabinoid precursor case
summary: China's Ministry of Public Security announced that Chinese and US law enforcement agencies jointly cracked a transnational case involving synthetic cannabinoid precursors. The coordinated operations in Hebei Province led to the arrest of 21 suspects and the seizure of non-scheduled chemicals. The ministry highlighted this success as evidence of the effectiveness of the China-US counternarcotics cooperation mechanism in combating transnational drug crimes.

title: SCIO briefs on 15th Five-Year Plan for China's financial sector
summary: The State Council Information Office held a press conference in Beijing on Thursday to discuss implementing the 15th Five-Year Plan for the financial sector. Li Chao of the CSRC stated the commission will strengthen market stabilization mechanisms and risk monitoring. Cong Lin of the National Financial Regulatory Administration announced measures to crack down on illegal practices like price wars. Lu Lei of the People's Bank of China reiterated adherence to a managed floating exchange rate regime, while Li Bin of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange confirmed basic convertibility for direct investment has been achieved.

title: 9/11 survivor Janice Brooks relives nightmare of escaping south tower
summary: Janice Brooks, a 9/11 survivor who escaped the south tower, has been haunted by a recurring nightmare for 25 years. The article details her miraculous escape from the 84th floor after hearing a plane strike the north tower and ignoring a Port Authority announcement that Building Two was secure. Brooks helped injured colleagues evacuate before the south tower collapsed, killing 61 of her Euro Brokers colleagues. Now 66, she works with a charity to educate younger generations about the attacks. Despite a psychiatrist suggesting the nightmare figure represents her, the dream persists as autumn approaches.

title: ICE expanded after 9/11, now faces criticism for excessive power
summary: The article examines how the September 11 attacks reshaped U.S. immigration control, leading to the creation of the Department of Homeland Security and the division of the former INS into three separate agencies. Doris Meissner, a former INS commissioner, argues that this split reduced policy coherence and allowed ICE to receive massive funding increases under recent budget bills. Hiroshi Motomura, a UCLA law professor, notes that this structure has enabled ICE to expand significantly while USCIS faces insufficient resources. The authors report that critics contend these changes have empowered ICE to operate with impunity, prioritizing security over due process and legal immigration services.

title: Princess Diana's revenge dress returns to auction for first time since 1997
summary: Princess Diana's iconic black silk dress, known as the 'revenge dress,' is going up for auction at Sotheby's in New York on Dec. 9, where it is expected to sell for between $150,000 and $300,000. This marks its first public appearance since 1997. Part of the proceeds from the sale will be donated to NHS Lothian Charity on behalf of the Royal Edinburgh Hospital.

title: MPs debate assisted dying bill amid criticism of Lords and NHS readiness
summary: MPs in the UK House of Commons are debating the assisted dying bill, with Labour MP Lauren Edwards criticizing the House of Lords for obstructing previous votes. She argued the delay harms terminally ill patients and their families. Liberal Democrat MP Layla Moran supports the bill to improve palliative care, while former health minister Zubair Ahmed warned the social and palliative care system is not ready. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch described the legislation as rushed and badly drafted, urging caution before it is forced into law. The debate continues as MPs consider the bill's safety and efficacy.

title: Trump and Vance attend 9/11 anniversary ceremonies amid political pledges
summary: The article reports on the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, noting that President Donald Trump plans to attend a ceremony at the Pentagon and Vice President JD Vance is expected at the National September 11 Memorial in New York. Trump doubled down on a pledge to pay all US adults $5,000 if Republicans hold Congress, stating the country is taking in trillions. Vance urged Republicans not to abandon the party in November's elections, referencing Charlie Kirk. The text also covers planned remembrances across the US, including vigils and volunteer projects. Additionally, the Guardian asked readers how the attacks affected their lives, with responses highlighting initial unity followed by division and Islamophobia. Personal accounts from families, such as Anna Sweeney Rossman and Jenna Jacobs McPartland, describe enduring grief. The article notes that Muslim Americans faced backlash and government repression following the attacks.

title: Houthis claim Saudi airstrikes hit Mokha airport in southwestern Yemen
summary: The Houthis claimed Friday that Saudi aircraft carried out two airstrikes on Mokha airport in southwestern Yemen. The Houthi-run Saba news agency reported the strikes without providing information about casualties or damage. Saudi Arabia did not immediately comment on the claim. These reported strikes occurred two days after Saudi coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki stated that Houthis launched attacks involving ballistic missiles and drones toward southern Saudi cities. Fighting between government forces and the Houthis has intensified since early July, with territorial control shifting across multiple provinces including the strategic western coast near the Bab al-Mandab Strait.

title: Article claims counterterrorism adaptations erode Western rule of law
summary: The provided text contains only a headline and a browser error message, so no article body exists to summarize. The headline suggests counterterrorism adaptations erode Western rule of law and public freedoms.

title: Fires destroy migrant tents in Ceuta after threats to burn families
summary: Fires destroyed at least 40 tents in Ceuta's migrant settlement Friday, following Tuesday attacks where assailants threatened to burn residents. Police attribute the blaze to negligence, while a public cleaning employee was arrested for separate arson incidents in the city. Emergency services reported no injuries, and authorities estimate 5,000 migrants remain in the exclave awaiting asylum processing.

title: Thai police arrest monk and accomplice in $3m embezzlement scandal
summary: Thai police have arrested former abbot Phra Wachirayan Wi and a female accomplice on suspicion of embezzling 100 million baht from Wat Phutthaisawan monastery. Lead investigator Pattanasak Bupphasuwan stated that donations meant for temple renovations and sacred objects never entered the temple's account. Police seized cash, gold bars, and jewellery worth an estimated 6.04 million baht from the accomplice's home. The monk was defrocked after his arrest, while the 47-year-old woman faces charges of abetting a state official in illegal activities. Authorities believe two or three other people could be involved in the case, which began after an anonymous tip in mid-July.

title: Japan's marriage intention rate drops below 80% for first time
summary: A government survey released Friday indicates that the proportion of single Japanese men and women intending to marry has dropped below 80% for the first time. The National Institute of Population and Social Security Research noted that more individuals believe they will not feel lonely living alone and have never interacted with infants, contributing to this decline. Among unmarried people aged 18 to 34, 75. 1% of men and 77. 8% of women said they intend to marry eventually, both figures falling by more than 6 percentage points from the previous survey.

title: M.K. Muneer's MLA pension delayed three months due to clerical error
summary: Former Kerala Minister M.K. Muneer has not received his MLA pension for three months due to an error in a letter from the Accountant General's office that listed the wrong name. While a corrected letter has been issued, the pension remains unpaid. Additionally, Muneer is reportedly displeased about the delay in announcing his appointment as chairman of the Administrative Reforms Commission, a post with Cabinet rank. His absence from a recent Muslim Youth League conference has raised questions among party workers regarding his dissatisfaction with these administrative delays.

title: DMK president Stalin urges PM Modi to fill 1,857 vacant super-speciality medical seats
summary: DMK president M.K. Stalin urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to intervene regarding 1,857 vacant super-speciality medical seats across India. Quoting The Hindu, Stalin stated that the Union government's Director General of Health Services has not reduced the qualifying percentile, leaving seats empty. He requested the percentile be lowered to zero and asked states to independently adjust quotas for in-service doctors to prevent waste of national assets.

title: PM Modi gifts Putin Russian Thirukkural translation ahead of Brics summit
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi gifted Russian President Vladimir Putin a Russian translation of the ancient Tamil classic Thirukkural during their bilateral meeting in New Delhi on Friday. The exchange took place ahead of the Brics Summit, showcasing cultural diplomacy between the two leaders. The Times of India reported the event as part of their coverage of the summit preparations.

title: Tharoor defends Brics diplomatic value while Chidambaram questions outcomes
summary: Senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor defended the relevance of the Brics grouping, stating it provides a vital platform for the Global South. Speaking to PTI, Tharoor noted the 11 member countries represent 41 per cent of global GDP. This stance contrasts with colleague P Chidambaram, who told ANI he could not see tangible benefits from recent summits. While Tharoor highlighted the diplomatic prestige of hosting leaders, Khurshid urged the party to view Chidambaram's comments as caution. The 18th Brics Summit is set for September 12-13 in New Delhi, where leaders including Putin and Xi Jinping are expected to attend.

title: Jefferies cuts KEI Industries target price amid UltraTech entry concerns
summary: Jefferies cut KEI Industries' target price by 11% citing concerns that UltraTech Cement's entry into wires and low-tension cables could erode profitability. The brokerage noted a potential 300 bps loss in KEI's retail market share over FY26-30E and factored in a 50 bps margin compression. KEI management countered that its established brand and competitive pricing allow it to defend its market position.

title: Bernstein names Paytm as top fintech pick with 26% upside target
summary: Bernstein analysts named Paytm their top fintech stock pick, setting a Rs 2,200 target price that implies up to 26% upside from current levels. The brokerage cites merchant loan growth, strong operating leverage, and potential MDR on UPI as the three primary drivers for Paytm's future profitability. However, the firm also highlighted risks, noting that the absence of MDR on UPI transactions would represent a material downside to earnings estimates.

title: Anthropic Reports State Actors Used Its AI for Spying and Data Theft
summary: Anthropic announced Thursday that it shut down multiple state-sponsored surveillance operations between January and July originating in China, Iran, and West Africa. The report stated these campaigns targeted diaspora communities and dissidents, with actors using the AI to identify individuals and design intelligence software. Additionally, Anthropic accused Chinese developers Moonshot and Deepseek of deceptively using Claude to generate responses while distilling data to improve their own models. The company noted that over a ten-day period, Moonshot relayed nearly 300,000 customer requests through a network of 5,380 fraudulent accounts.

title: Mumbai Man Confessed to Using ChatGPT to Forge PMO ID
summary: Police told a court on Friday that Rohan Parikh confessed to fabricating a Prime Minister's Office identity card using ChatGPT to elevate his social standing. Investigators stated Parikh created the documents since 2025, while accomplice Dilip Kunde admitted using a revolver as a bodyguard. The court remanded both men in 14-day judicial custody following their arrest at a Mumbai mall where they attempted entry with the fake ID and a firearm.

title: Apple prepares iOS 27 rollout with rebuilt Siri on Monday
summary: Apple is preparing to roll out iOS 27 on Monday, September 14, introducing a rebuilt, AI-powered Siri. The update will be free for eligible devices, including the iPhone 11 and later models. While Apple has not confirmed a specific release time or whether the rollout will be phased, users are advised to back up their data, free up storage, and ensure their devices are charged before installing the software.

title: Rohan Parekh admits using ChatGPT to create fake PMO documents since 2025
summary: The Crime Branch reports that 24-year-old Rohan Parekh admitted using ChatGPT to create fake PMO documents since 2025 to enhance his image and self-esteem. The accused stated he generated these documents for his family and society.

title: ChatGPT and Gemini warn users about privacy risks in 1980s AI photo trends
summary: A viral trend turning selfies into 1980s-style portraits has raised privacy concerns regarding AI tools like ChatGPT and Gemini. ChatGPT noted that content on personal accounts may be used to train models unless users opt out, while Gemini highlighted that uploaded images share biometric data and may be stored on cloud servers. The article advises users to avoid uploading photos of children or sensitive documents and to review privacy settings before using these services.

title: RBI partially cancels debt auction as bond yields spike
summary: Traders said the Reserve Bank of India partially cancelled a government security auction after accepting only 40% of planned bids worth ₹4506 crore. A trader with a state-run bank noted the move could soothe market sentiment as fresh Middle East escalation and U.S. data pushed yields higher.

title: X user explains annual iPhone upgrade strategy using lease-like model
summary: Chirag Barjatya, an X user, explains that he upgrades his iPhone annually from the iPhone X to the iPhone 17 Pro by combining no-cost EMI with the exchange value of his previous device. Barjatya describes this arrangement as a lease model that allows him to spread payments over time while replacing his phone before its resale value falls too sharply. He notes that while keeping a phone for four to five years would be cheaper, he prefers the convenience of daily use for work and content creation. The post has attracted over 844 likes and sparked debate among users regarding the financial sense of frequent upgrades versus long-term retention. Meanwhile, Apple has launched the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, introducing new hardware features and starting prices of ₹1,64,900 and ₹1,79,900 respectively in India.

title: Reliance Digital opens iPhone 18 Pro pre-booking on September 12
summary: Reliance Digital announced that pre-booking for the iPhone 18 Pro begins on September 12 at 5:30 PM. The device will be available for purchase starting September 18 at 8:00 AM across stores and online. The retailer invites customers to secure the phone ahead of the launch day.

title: Apple launches iPhone 18 Pro models with new A20 chip and variable aperture cameras
summary: Apple has officially launched the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max globally, introducing the new A20 Pro chip and variable aperture cameras. The US, Japan, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE offer these models at lower prices than India due to tax structures. In India, the iPhone 18 Pro starts at Rs 1,64,900, while the Pro Max starts at Rs 1,79,900.

title: Apple launches iPhone 18 Pro with variable aperture camera and 2nm chip
summary: Apple has launched the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max in India, introducing significant hardware upgrades including a variable aperture main camera and the 2nm A20 Pro chip. The devices start at Rs 1,64,900 and Rs 1,79,900, marking a Rs 30,000 price increase over last year's models. Pre-orders open on September 12, with availability scheduled for September 18. The phones also feature improved battery life, a smaller Dynamic Island, and the new Siri AI assistant arriving with iOS 27.

title: Modi and Putin discuss trade deficit, energy, and defence cooperation
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin met at the 18th BRICS summit in New Delhi to discuss bilateral ties. The agenda included reaching $100 billion in trade, addressing the trade deficit, and enhancing defence and energy cooperation. Experts noted the importance of energy trade and defence collaboration, while an exhibition showcased India's growing private space technology sector.

title: Users create retro AI portraits for social media using specific prompts
summary: A viral trend has taken over social media feeds, with users prompting AI to recreate portraits mimicking styles from the 1960s to the 1990s. The article details specific prompts for tools like ChatGPT and Google Gemini to transform modern photos into grainy, era-specific images featuring period-accurate fashion and lighting. Celebrities and public figures have also joined the movement, sharing their own nostalgic AI-generated portraits online.

title: US-Canada trade war: Carney expects new tariffs to hurt some businesses, but Ottawa unlikely to retaliate
summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney addressed reporters in Banff regarding escalating trade tensions between the United States and Canada. He acknowledged that new US measures, including import bans on goods like alcoholic beverages and motorcycles, would negatively affect individual companies but described the overall impact as modest. Carney signalled that Ottawa is unlikely to retaliate, prioritizing domestic economic strengthening instead. While the Trump administration announced these restrictions following failed tariff reduction talks, a senior US official indicated that constructive discussions occurred this week. Carney confirmed a recent phone call with President Trump but noted it remains unclear if trade was discussed. Both sides remain open to negotiating a mutually beneficial deal that respects sovereignty.

title: Experts question Bengaluru Hebbal tunnel's traffic and water safety
summary: The proposed Hebbal tunnel in north Bengaluru faces scrutiny over its uncertain traffic benefits and potential environmental risks. While intended to ease congestion at Hebbal Junction, an analysis by the Indian Institute of Science suggests the project is a localized improvement that may worsen bottlenecks elsewhere. Experts also raise alarms regarding groundwater recharge and flooding, noting the tunnel's alignment near Hebbal Lake could disrupt the region's critical water systems. A public interest litigation in the Karnataka High Court has sought a stay on the project, citing a lack of hydrological impact assessments. Although the Bangalore Development Authority claims to have conducted studies, details remain unavailable. Critics highlight fragmented governance, where road construction plans conflict with lake rejuvenation efforts, potentially undermining the city's flood management infrastructure.

title: Centre amends mining law to restrict state taxation powers
summary: The Union Government introduced the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, to centralize control over mineral-bearing land and limit state taxation powers. Mining states such as Jharkhand and Odisha fear substantial revenue losses, with Jharkhand estimating a loss of ₹1.36 trillion in past dues. While the Ministry of Mines asserts that existing tax-sharing mechanisms will remain intact, experts warn the move disregards a 2024 Supreme Court ruling. Opposition parties and state leaders have vowed to challenge the legislation in court, citing concerns over federal balance and fiscal stability. Experts suggest states may explore alternative levy sources to offset potential revenue shortfalls.

title: Kerala blackout sparks social media memes and political attacks
summary: Prolonged power cuts across Kerala have triggered widespread public anger, with social media flooded with complaints and political attacks. Kerala Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph stated that electricity demand increased by more than 1,000 MW compared to the previous year, citing infrastructure expansion and air conditioner usage. The opposition Left Democratic Front has accused the Congress-led government of reviving power cuts, while residents demand advance outage alerts.

title: Editor contrasts past and present religious films in India
summary: Political editor Anand Mishra contrasts the non-controversial success of the biopic Hanuman Ansh with recent films that sparked legal and social disputes. The article notes that older religious movies like Jai Santoshi Maa achieved commercial success without creating communal divides, unlike recent productions. Mishra questions whether modern filmmakers are prioritizing political agendas and hate-mongering over art to generate box-office revenue.

title: Kolkata exhibition displays visual history of the 1857 Revolt
summary: The Asiatic Society in Kolkata is hosting an exhibition titled "1857: The First War of Independence—A Visual Journey" curated by Jyotirmoy Bhattacharya. The display features rare engravings, drawings, and photographs from sources like Charles Ball and Felice Beato to depict the Revolt of 1857. Curator Jyotirmoy Bhattacharya stated the exhibition serves as a homage to the heroes of 1857 who ignited nationalist aspirations leading to India's independence. The visual journey traces the conflict from the annexation of Awadh to the suppression of the mutiny in July 1858, while also highlighting the subsequent nationalist movement. The exhibition includes graphic depictions of violence and brutality, such as the killing of sepoys and the storming of Delhi, offering a detailed pictorial representation of the historical events.

title: Five ISKP militants killed in CTD operation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
summary: An official stated that five militants of the banned Islamic State Khorasan Province were killed during a Counter-Terrorism Department operation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. A key commander identified as Imran was eliminated in the exchange of fire at a refugee camp near Peshawar on Thursday night. The CTD reported that militants opened indiscriminate fire as personnel entered a compound, prompting the retaliatory action that resulted in the deaths.

title: Yemeni Houthis seize strategic Perim island in Bab al-Mandeb Strait
summary: Yemeni government sources reported that Iran-aligned Houthis reached the strategic island of Perim in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait on Friday, September 11, 2026. Earlier, Saudi-backed Yemeni government sources said their forces withdrew from Perim while Houthis also captured the mainland coastal town of Dhubab, potentially tightening control over a vital shipping route.

title: JD(U) leaders consider renaming party as JD(U)-Nitish
summary: JD(U) working president Sanjay Jha proposed renaming the party to JD(U)-Nitish, a suggestion backed by senior leaders Deputy Chief Minister Bijendra Prasad Yadav and minister Shrawon Kumar. The ruling RJD criticized the move as a sign of an impending split, alleging that internal factions are acting as agents of the BJP.

title: PM Modi and Putin discuss trade targets and industrial cooperation in Delhi
summary: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal called for accelerated India-Russia economic partnership, urging businesses to achieve a USD 100 billion bilateral trade target by 2030. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Vladimir Putin held bilateral talks in Delhi ahead of the BRICS Summit, where they discussed expanding industrial cooperation, strengthening civil nuclear ties, and increasing mobility collaboration. Sources indicated that the leaders also addressed the success of INNOPROM in India and plans for critical minerals and fertilizer cooperation.

title: Anthropic blocks scientists attempting bioweapons research with its AI
summary: Anthropic announced it stopped multiple attempts this year by scientists to use its technology for research that could help develop biological weapons. The startup provided five examples of actors who circumvented controls to obfuscate their research purposes, including cases involving users from prohibited nations such as Russia, China, and Iran. Anthropic stated it banned the accounts involved but did not disclose specific institution names or locations. The company hopes sharing these examples will spark industry and government conversations about emerging biological risks.

title: Experts Assess Privacy and Civil Liberties Changes Since 9/11
summary: Tech Policy Press asked nine privacy and civil liberties experts to evaluate how War on Terror policies have altered rights and oversight twenty-five years after the September 11 attacks. The experts, including Spencer Ackerman and Sharon Bradford Franklin, generally agreed that civil liberties have declined and that the Department of Homeland Security has struggled to meet its original mission. While respondents noted that terrorism has receded as a priority and the public is more skeptical of expanded government powers, they universally agreed that the imperial presidency is much stronger than it was in 2001. The survey highlights the difficulty of restoring lost protections once security powers are granted to the executive branch.

title: MIT Lincoln Laboratory device wins 2026 technology transfer award
summary: The Federal Laboratory Consortium selected the AI-GUIDE medical device for its 2026 Excellence in Technology Transfer Award. Developed with U.S. Army funding by MIT Lincoln Laboratory and Massachusetts General Hospital, the portable tool assists medics in inserting catheters in pre-hospital settings. The team is transferring the prototype to startup AutonomUS Medical Technologies to facilitate commercialization and improve survival rates for injured service members and civilians.

title: US core inflation rises more than forecast, strengthening case for Fed rate hike
summary: US core inflation rose more than forecast in August, strengthening the case for the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at its upcoming meeting. Analysts note that stubborn inflation, driven by energy prices and geopolitical tensions, may push the central bank toward its first rate increase in three years. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh faces pressure to justify a decision that could conflict with President Trump's calls for lower rates amid rising consumer costs.

title: DBS CEO Tan Su Shan rules out politics, urges diverse talent for policy debate
summary: DBS chief executive Tan Su Shan ruled out entering politics, stating, "I'm too old," during a Sept 11 fireside chat. She called for attracting diverse talent from both public and private sectors to improve the quality of Singapore's policy debates. Tan, who leads the bank since 2025, emphasized that private sector professionals bring different decision-making perspectives crucial for national relevance. She also noted that Singapore must accept failure to learn and move forward.

title: Colombian Armed Groups Recruit Children via Social Media Algorithms
summary: Nelson González Sánchez, an author for Human Rights Watch, reports that Colombian armed groups are increasingly recruiting children through social media platforms like Facebook and TikTok. The investigation revealed that algorithms often amplify content showcasing an alluring lifestyle, including images of cash and weapons, which seduces vulnerable youth. Recruiters utilize specific emojis as coded signals to bypass platform restrictions while posting explicit job offers. Although González Sánchez noted that both Meta and ByteDance removed some accounts, similar content remains online. The report indicates that social media now drives nearly half of all child recruitment in Colombia, leading the author to call for stronger platform regulation to protect children's rights.

title: Researchers introduce DiscoSign for discourse-aware text to sign language gloss translation
summary: The authors report that DiscoSign is a computational approach for discourse-aware text to sign language gloss translation grounded in linguistic research. The authors report that the system addresses spatial coreference resolution, question-answer clauses, and concept-gloss consistency within a modular large language model framework. Experiments on sentence-level and discourse-level datasets show that the approach significantly improves spatial consistency and entity tracking relative to sentence-only translation while maintaining competitive single-sentence gloss translation quality. The authors state that their work establishes the first systematic framework for discourse-level text to sign language gloss translation with corresponding evaluation methodology.

title: Researchers introduce SimpleDesign for joint protein sequence and structure codesign
summary: The authors report that SimpleDesign is a multi-modal protein design model trained directly in data space using a single-stage end-to-end objective. The authors report that the model was trained on over 2M sequence-structure pairs and achieved competitive performance across co-design and unconditional generation benchmarks. This approach combines discrete cross-entropy for sequences with a regression objective for structures, utilizing Transformer-based multimodal backbones to process both modalities effectively.

title: AWARE urges caution on chemical castration for sex crimes
summary: Lim Shoon Yin, Executive Director of AWARE, writes that the organization urges caution regarding chemical castration as a deterrent for sex crimes. She notes that evidence proving its effectiveness remains inconclusive and suggests the premise implies offenders lack biological control over their urges. Instead, AWARE recommends a national review of sexuality education to shift from an abstinence-based approach to one focused on consent and rights. The organization emphasizes that prevention through education must occur across all life stages, including workplaces and national service, to address beliefs enabling sexual violence.

title: Lim Fu Kang argues coffee shops should allow personal water bottles
summary: Lim Fu Kang argues that coffee shops should reconsider policies banning personal water bottles. He states that discouraging water consumption contradicts public health messages encouraging reduced sugar intake. The author suggests creating an environment where choosing water is easy rather than compelling customers to buy sweetened drinks.

title: Graham Dumpleton releases alpha Python monkey patching tool wrapture
summary: Graham Dumpleton has released wrapture, an alpha Python library combining monkey patching with observability features. The author notes the package allows zero-code tracing via TOML configuration and supports many frameworks like Flask and Django. Daily tutorials cover unit testing, live tracing, and OpenTelemetry export capabilities.

title: Geely launches TT electric sedan at $19,100 in China
summary: Geely launched its new TT electric sport sedan in China with a starting price of 129,900 yuan, approximately $19,100. The vehicle features 800V fast charging and standard LiDAR across all trims, positioning it at roughly half the cost of a comparable Tesla. Geely reported receiving more than 20,000 pre-orders in about two weeks before the launch. The car is currently available only in China, though Geely plans to enter the US EV market within two to three years.

title: Kia deploys 200 custom electric PV5 vans to South Korean post offices
summary: Kia announced Friday it will supply 200 custom electric PV5 vans to The Korea Post for mail delivery following a pilot test. The company modified the vans based on feedback from mail carriers to improve loading and unloading. Kia plans to support The Korea Post's electrification transition with EV training, customized charging solutions, and maintenance services. The automaker also revealed it now offers 10 different PV5 body styles and is expanding partnerships with other industries.

title: Indonesia fires in 2026 on track to match 2015 record emissions
summary: Wildfires currently burning across Indonesia are projected to generate emissions comparable to the country's most intense fire season this century. Data from the Global Fire Emissions Database indicates that as of 7 September, fires produced 76 million tonnes of carbon in 2026, aligning with the 2015 trajectory. Dr Guido van der Werf of Wageningen University states the fires are 'more or less on track' to reach 2015 levels, which generated 333 million tonnes of carbon. The current crisis occurs during an El Niño year, a climate phenomenon that creates conditions for immense fires. Dr Mark Parrington of the Copernicus Climate Change Service notes the scale is unprecedented for this time of year. While Indonesia has implemented peatland protection measures since 1997, Dr Nisa Novita of Yayasan Konservasi Alam Nusantara questions if current efforts are sufficient given the risk of degraded peatlands.

title: Article Debunks Viral Claim That America Has Only 14 Days of Oil Left
summary: An article debunks a viral social media claim that the United States has only 14 days of oil remaining. The text explains that this figure incorrectly compares the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to total petroleum demand while ignoring daily crude production and commercial inventories. The Department of Energy describes the reserve as an emergency tool, noting its current level of 286.6 million barrels is the lowest since November 1982. Recent releases for the Ukraine and Iran conflicts have significantly reduced this cushion, though the current program uses an exchange structure to eventually rebuild stocks. The article concludes that the viral math confuses an emergency reserve with the nation's entire supply system.

title: Latvenergo evaluates 250 MW wind acquisition to expand Baltic renewable portfolio
summary: Latvenergo, Latvia's state-owned utility, is evaluating the acquisition of up to 250 MW of wind or hybrid power projects to expand its renewable generation. Advised by PricewaterhouseCoopers, the search targets ready-to-build projects and operational turbines no older than five years. The utility reported a Baltic renewable portfolio of 1,144 MW by mid-2026, which includes recently completed solar and wind assets alongside a growing pipeline of battery storage. This expansion aligns with Latvenergo's medium-term strategy to diversify its power mix and strengthen energy security following the region's synchronization with the Continental European grid.

title: Hidroelectrica selects contractor for Iron Gates II battery storage project
summary: Romanian hydropower company Hidroelectrica has selected Bucharest-based Synergy Construct to install a 64 MW battery energy storage system at its Iron Gates II plant. Hidroelectrica stated the RON 296.8 million investment will create the largest battery asset in its portfolio. CEO Iulius-Dan Plaveti said the project supports a shift toward an energy model where renewable generation is complemented by storage capabilities. The company also noted it is working on designs for additional battery facilities totaling 200 MW and 800 MWh on the lower course of the Olt River.

title: Metlen Energy sells 165MW Chile solar-plus-storage project to Copec
summary: Metlen Energy & Metals announced on 10 September that it has agreed to sell the Tamarico II solar-plus-storage project in Chile to Copec S.A. through its subsidiary Copec Flux S.p.A. The deal involves a 165MW solar PV generation facility paired with a 725MWh battery energy storage system, which Metlen stated reaffirms its ability to develop and monetize renewable energy assets. Metlen also noted the agreement strengthens its partnership with the COPEC Group, laying groundwork for future collaboration on renewable energy and battery storage investments in Chile.

title: Analysts argue Alphabet and Amazon are must-buy stocks despite capex fears
summary: Analysts argue that Wall Street should celebrate rather than fear the massive capital expenditure by cloud providers Alphabet and Amazon. The article explains that these companies are pouring money into AI infrastructure because demand continues to outstrip capacity while they achieve strong returns with quick payback periods. Amazon plans to spend about $220 billion on capex this year, which it says will still not meet current demand. Meanwhile, Alphabet revealed it gets a payback on server investments in less than two years. Both companies report that their AI capacity is contracted out for at least five years, and they expect to remain capacity-constrained through 2027.

title: Apple launches AppleCare One Family plan in the US
summary: Apple has launched a new AppleCare One Family plan in the US, allowing families to manage coverage for multiple devices under one subscription. This expansion of Apple's existing AppleCare One service is currently rolling out in the US, though the plan for other regions has not yet been confirmed.

title: PM Modi to address BRICS Business Forum with global corporate leaders attending
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will address the BRICS Business Advisory Forum Leaders Session on Friday evening in New Delhi, where over 1,000 foreign representatives and major global companies including Huawei, Alibaba, and Tata are expected to participate.

title: New Mexico court fines lawyer for ChatGPT-fabricated police testimony
summary: The New Mexico Supreme Court fined attorney Stephen Aarons $5,000 and held him in contempt for submitting a murder appeal brief containing false police testimony fabricated by ChatGPT. Aarons admitted he used the AI tool to summarize trial proceedings without verifying the accuracy of the generated content, which included wholly invented witnesses. The court cited his lack of remorse and concern for his client, while Aarons described the incident as an honest mistake and a lesson for professionals relying on unstable technology.

title: Anthropic report flags UAE-linked AI misuse targeting Muslim Brotherhood
summary: Anthropic released a report stating that a UAE-linked influence operation misused Claude AI to target the Muslim Brotherhood. The operation utilized approximately 300 fake social-media accounts, established a front NGO, and ghost-wrote testimony for the UN. Anthropic traced the campaign with high confidence to UAE government officials, noting that Abu Dhabi has designated the Muslim Brotherhood a terrorist organization since 2014. The UAE Foreign Ministry did not respond to a request for comment regarding these findings.

title: IEA cuts 2026 oil forecasts as US-Iran tensions rise
summary: The International Energy Agency cut its 2026 global oil supply and demand forecasts on Friday, warning that stalled US-Iran talks and renewed shipping attacks are pushing the market toward a deeper shortfall.

title: Lawmakers push AI regulation after researcher extinction warning
summary: More than 20 lawmakers are supporting tougher artificial intelligence rules after Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon warned that AI labs are gambling with lives. Sen. Ruben Gallego urged Senate leadership to form a bipartisan AI select committee, while Rep. Lori Trahan stated cross-party momentum has reached a tipping point. Several bills, including the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, are already in motion, though prospects for passage remain remote with Congress largely on recess. President Donald Trump dismissed extinction concerns, while OpenAI's Chris Lehane called for mandatory national regulation.

title: Federal agencies seek comment on proposed third-party risk management guidance
summary: The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, Federal Reserve Board, National Credit Union Administration, and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency requested public comment on proposed third-party risk management guidance. The agencies also issued a statement regarding community bank engagement with core service providers and separately sought feedback on a specific guide for Federal Reserve-supervised community banks.

title: Oracle shares rise as AI backlog growth offsets spending concerns
summary: Oracle shares rose 3 per cent on Friday following a $26 billion increase in revenue backlog, which alleviated some investor concerns regarding the company's debt-fueled expansion. While Oracle stated that roughly half of its $664 billion backlog will convert to sales within 36 months, Morningstar analyst Luke Yang noted that cash flow improvements are not expected soon. The company reported negative free cash flow of $5.40 billion, surpassing analyst estimates of $9.56 billion according to LSEG data. Despite these figures, Evercore analysts described the results as a solid step forward, though the stock still trades at a lower multiple than Microsoft and Amazon.

title: Patagonia may host data centers; Harley-Davidson faces high Canadian tariffs
summary: This newsletter from The Indicator from Planet Money highlights three business stories. Reuters reports that Argentina is courting Big AI CEOs with tax breaks, and OpenAI has committed to a roughly 500-megawatt data center worth up to $25 billion that could land in Patagonia. The Wall Street Journal reports that China's semiconductor export value went up 130% from last year, even though chip export volume went down by 7.9%. CBC's Paul Haavardsrud explains that Canada is imposing tariffs on Harley-Davidson motorcycles, including a 50% tariff, to put political pressure on the White House.

title: U.S.-Canada trade war creates supply chain headaches for auto parts makers
summary: The escalating trade war between the U.S. and Canada is creating significant challenges for the tightly woven auto-parts industry. New tariffs on steel, aluminum, and vehicles threaten to disrupt decades of cross-border manufacturing integration.
