Earlier this week, Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon announced his departure, citing concerns that firms prioritize competition over safety.

title: Anthropic says UAE-linked AI operation targeted UN experts over Sudan
summary: Anthropic announced on September 12, 2026, that it detected a UAE-linked influence operation using its AI models to target UN experts and the Muslim Brotherhood concerning the Sudan war. The firm stated it disrupted the campaign with high confidence, noting it generated reports and social media content under a persona called 'Deadshot.' Meanwhile, the UN Security Council renewed an arms embargo for western Darfur, though the US argued the current restrictions are outdated and insufficient to address the escalating conflict where over 200,000 people have died.

title: President Xi Jinping travels to India for the 18th BRICS Summit
summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping departed Beijing on Saturday for the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India, at the invitation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

title: Steph Curry plays basketball against a robot in China
summary: American basketball star Steph Curry visited Tsinghua University High School in China this week. The star challenged himself to shoot hoops against a Chinese humanoid robot during the visit.

title: California scientist discovers 10,000-year-old mastodon tooth
summary: Brigid Lynch, a geomorphologist in San Mateo County, discovered a 10,000-year-old Pacific mastodon molar while working at a preserve. Paleontologist Wayne Thompson described the fossil as the most complete mastodon molar from the area. The Midpeninsula regional open space district donated the tooth to Stanford University, where researchers will use carbon dating to determine its exact age.

title: Ukrainian tennis player Yastremska shares photo of Roland Garros towel surviving Odesa strike
summary: Ukrainian tennis player Dayana Yastremska reported that a Russian Kalibr cruise missile destroyed her family's flat in Odesa, leaving only a Roland Garros towel intact. She shared images of the wreckage on social media, describing the scene as a symbol of the conflict. Odesa regional head Oleh Kiper stated that 37 people were injured and two remain missing after the Friday night attack.

title: Piastri qualifies seventh as Norris takes pole in Spain
summary: Oscar Piastri qualified seventh for the Spanish Grand Prix, describing his lap as shocking after teammate Lando Norris took pole position. The Australian attributed his struggles to technical differences in the 2026 cars rather than a hangover from the previous season. McLaren team boss Andrea Stella hailed Norris's performance as a masterpiece, though a mistake at the last corner may have cost him a faster time. ABC Sport will provide a live blog of the race from 9pm AEST on Sunday, September 13.

title: Céline Dion returns to Paris stage after six years battling illness
summary: Céline Dion returned to the stage in Paris on Saturday for a sold-out concert at the Plenitude Arena, marking her first full performance in six years. The 58-year-old singer, who has battled Stiff Person Syndrome since 2022, appeared visibly moved while performing to an audience of around 30,000 people. She announced a 26-show residency that is projected to generate hundreds of millions of euros in economic benefits. Fans from as far away as Tahiti attended the event, and Paris officials renamed a suburban train station serving the arena in her honor. Dion, who has sold approximately 260 million albums over her career, expressed gratitude to the crowd, stating she wanted to sing for life.

title: TRNC regrets US extension of arms embargo waiver for Greek Cypriot Administration
summary: The Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus Foreign Ministry expressed deep regret over the US decision to extend an arms embargo waiver for the Greek Cypriot Administration for another year. The ministry warned against steps that ignore the Turkish Cypriot people and called on international actors to pursue a fair and balanced policy recognizing two separate states on the island.

title: Progressive strategists advise against personal attacks on Pauline Hanson in Victoria
summary: GetUp strategists and the Trades Hall Council have advised progressive campaigners in Victoria to stop personally attacking Pauline Hanson and instead address the economic concerns driving One Nation support. Oscar Kaspi-Crutchett of Trades Hall explained that character attacks confirm Hanson's narrative as an outsider, whereas engaging with legitimate economic grievances builds trust. This approach follows a strategic rethink after GetUp's previous ads attacking Hanson and Barnaby Joyce failed to prevent One Nation from winning the Farrer byelection. Senior Labor sources noted that personal attacks on right-wing figures previously proved unhelpful. The groups now urge campaigners to listen for underlying dissatisfaction with the status quo and redirect conversations toward issues like working conditions and housing affordability, where the Labor movement holds higher public trust.

title: Houthis strike Saudi mosque and shut oil pipeline amid regional escalation
summary: Saudi officials confirmed that Yemen's Houthi rebels struck a mosque and several buildings in the Jazan region, injuring two individuals. The attack forced Saudi civil defence to issue an emergency alert. Riyadh subsequently shut down its East-West oil pipeline after the vital conduit came under aerial attack, threatening global energy prices. Amidst these events, US President Donald Trump remarked that the Houthis would prefer not having the United States involved in their conflict with Saudi Arabia. He noted that the group is letting most ships pass through the Bab el-Mandeb strait but remains hostile toward one specific country. Meanwhile, British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband discussed the aggression with his Saudi counterpart, affirming the UK's support for Riyadh and the internationally recognised government of Yemen.

title: Bill Maher mocks Trump's new pledge of allegiance at Dallas convention
summary: Comedian Bill Maher mocked President Donald Trump's unconventional pledge of allegiance during the Republican midterm convention in Dallas. The host of HBO's Real Time with Bill Maher appeared stunned by the moment during his Friday night monologue. Maher read the text aloud and stated he felt he had nothing left to say about the moment. Trump followed the pledge with a warning that supporters who do not vote will go to hell. Maher has a long record of criticizing Trump on television, including past jokes about Obama's birthplace and accusations that Trump embraces socialism.

title: Fire at Chilean nursing home kills 16 residents
summary: At least 16 elderly residents died in a fire at the El Edén nursing home in Chile, according to authorities. President José Antonio Kast ordered a review of nursing home conditions across the country following the tragedy. Local officials confirmed ten others were evacuated and the fire was extinguished by Saturday morning.

title: Danish WWII drama wins Golden Lion at Venice Film Festival
summary: The Venice Film Festival awarded its top prize, the Golden Lion, to the Danish drama "Unknown Woman" on Saturday. Directed by May el-Toukhy, the film is the first feature in the competition helmed by a woman. Jury head Maggie Gyllenhaal noted a systemic problem regarding the scarcity of female directors. The Gaza documentary "NAZA" won a special jury prize. Other winners included the Silver Lion for "Possible Love," the Best Director award for Ilya Khrzhanovsky for "DAU," and the Best Actor prize for John Malkovich in "Wild Horse Nine."

title: Woman Unknown wins Golden Lion at Venice Film Festival
summary: May el-Toukhy's film Woman Unknown won the Golden Lion at the 83rd Venice Film Festival, marking a rare double victory with lead actress Mathilde Arcel also taking Best Actress. The jury, led by Maggie Gyllenhaal, also awarded prizes for Possible Love, NAZA, and Wild Horse Nine. The documentary NAZA received a special jury prize after receiving a record-breaking 25-minute standing ovation, while Ilya Krzhanovsky won the Silver Lion for directing Dau. John Malkovich accepted Best Actor remotely for his role in Wild Horse Nine.

title: AfD candidate Siegmund sparks outrage linking arms production to remigration
summary: Ulrich Siegmund, the AfD lead candidate in Saxony-Anhalt, sparked outrage by linking the production of military equipment to his party's migration policy. At a press conference regarding the potential arrival of Israeli defense company Elbit Systems in Sangerhausen, Siegmund stated that arms production could be necessary for a future 'remigration and deportation offensive.' Following backlash, he clarified that his party rejects supplying weapons for foreign wars but aims to strengthen domestic security. SPD parliamentary group leader Katja Pähle condemned the remarks as a political threat involving violence. Meanwhile, the BSW criticized the AfD for provocation, noting the party's strong election result of 43.8 percent.

title: French government pushes for mandatory helmets for electric scooters
summary: The French government is pushing for mandatory helmets for electric scooters while struggling with bicycle regulations. The article states this policy direction without providing specific details on the implementation or public reaction.

title: Sweden right wing struggles to capitalize on late election rebound
summary: The provided text contains only an error message regarding a failed site load and does not include the article body needed to summarize the story.

title: Uganda's King Oyo buried as succession dispute erupts over heir
summary: Mourners gathered in western Uganda on Saturday for the burial of King Oyo, whose Tooro kingdom is embroiled in a bitter dispute over his successor. Oyo died in the United States last month while being treated for cancer. A selection committee from the Babiito royal clan announced Oyo's cousin Edward as the next king. However, Oyo's sister opposes the plan, claiming he left a will designating his biological son as heir. Queen Mother Best Kemigisa stated that troops removed royal guards and deployed around the palace, saying they are under house arrest.

title: Kenya secures Africa Recording Academy headquarters with $3.9 million investment
summary: Kenya secured the bid to host an Africa Recording Academy headquarters following a $3. 9 million government investment aimed at transforming the local creative economy. Recording Academy President Panos A. Panay confirmed that plans to initiate key milestones are underway and announced that Kenyan mentee artists will travel to the United States next month. Panay described the initiative as a long-term foundation-building project rather than a single launch date, comparing the process to gardening. The Recording Academy previously expanded its global reach by introducing a Best African Music Performance category and forming a mentorship program with the US State Department.

title: Iran uses barter deal to bypass sanctions and buy Chinese goods
summary: Senior Iranian sources and three other people familiar with the matter said Iran utilized a barter-like arrangement to circumvent sanctions on its oil sales and purchase billions of dollars worth of Chinese goods, including military equipment. This secretive trade mechanism exchanges Iranian oil for credits toward Chinese imports, offering Tehran a financial lifeline amidst US pressure while allowing China to access discounted crude and shield involved banks from scrutiny.

title: Actor and narrator Reo Morimoto dies at 83
summary: Japanese actor and narrator Reo Morimoto died suddenly on Sept. 4 at age 83, according to his agency. Morimoto, whose real name was Haruyuki, began his career in the 1967 drama 'Koukousei Jidai' and became well known for his calm narration in series like 'Thomas & Friends' and various commercials.

title: Spain's purebred horse industry exceeds $8.6 billion in value
summary: Spain's purebred horse industry has grown significantly, with consulting firms Green Oak and Deloitte reporting a 2022 valuation of $8.6 billion. The Royal National Association of PRE Breeders manages the sole recognized studbook, which listed 291,138 animals across 71 countries by late 2025. Prices for these purebred Andalusian horses vary widely, ranging from $11,600 to over $580,000, while breeding fees for top stallions exceed $1,160. The industry maintains strict bloodline purity through veterinary testing in Seville, and exports primarily to the United States, Mexico, and Germany. Despite high costs and risks, the sector remains vital for family cohesion and cultural heritage.

title: Energy Drinks Fuel Modern Society's Pursuit of Efficiency and Productivity
summary: The article explores how energy drinks have transformed from a beverage for laborers into a cultural symbol of efficiency and productivity. Experts Ana Teijeira and Carles Feixa Pàmpols explain that marketing strategies shifted from targeting athletes to appealing to teenage males and eventually the general population. A 2015 study found that men who embraced masculinity ideals believed these drinks made them manly, even as consumption reduced sleep. Sociologist Hartmut Rosa describes society's state of dynamic stabilization, where these drinks promise acceleration to keep up with a frenetic world. However, health risks include arrhythmias and diabetes due to high caffeine and sugar. While 60% of countries have implemented regulations, consumption among youth has surged by 13% as these products replace traditional substances like alcohol.

title: Abhijeet Dipke visits Balaghat families amid tribal children deaths
summary: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke visited Balaghat district to meet families of tribal children who died from monsoon illnesses, blaming government negligence for the deaths. Dipke claimed the actual death toll is higher than the official count of 36, while the Madhya Pradesh Collector stated that over 450 children received treatment and the situation is improving.

title: Indian delicacies served at BRICS Summit gala dinner in Delhi
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi hosted a gala dinner for BRICS Summit leaders at the Bharat Mandapam in Delhi on September 13, 2026. People familiar with the matter said the menu featured Indian delicacies including millet pulao, paneer lababdar, and shahtoot phirni. The event also included performances by over 100 artistes from India and other BRICS member countries.

title: Security forces found decomposed JeM terrorist remains and M4 rifle in Doda
summary: Security forces in Jammu and Kashmir's Doda district discovered the decomposed body of a suspected Jaish-e-Mohammed terrorist and an M4 rifle in the Divshetar area. An official stated that authorities are conducting further investigations to ascertain the identity of the deceased, while a police post suggested the individual was neutralized in a past joint operation. The find follows recent searches in the region targeting militants.

title: SIA searches five locations in Poonch and Udhampur during radicalisation probe
summary: The Jammu & Kashmir State Investigation Agency searched five locations in Poonch and Udhampur districts on Saturday as part of an investigation into alleged radicalisation. An SIA spokesperson stated that investigators found individuals allegedly in contact with suspicious persons across the Line of Control and the border. The spokesperson said more details would be shared after the searches conclude.

title: Anthropic CEO warns AI industry to slow development for safety
summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warned the artificial intelligence industry to slow its fast-moving development to allow safety measures to catch up. He cautioned that without this pause, AI could lead a swarm capable of taking over the internet within six to 12 months. Amodei outlined a plan requiring industry-wide coordination and government waivers to enable outside evaluators to monitor safety practices. He noted that while Anthropic is already implementing some checks, broader measures involving democratic and authoritarian governments would be difficult to implement. Amodei acknowledged the challenges but stated the industry owes it to humanity to try.

title: Anthropic CEO urges AI slowdown; Altman and Musk agree
summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published an essay urging artificial intelligence companies to slow their development pace. He warned that unchecked progress could lead to systems humans cannot control. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Tesla chief Elon Musk endorsed the call for caution. Amodei proposed giving third-party evaluators permanent access to verify safety measures. He highlighted risks like cyberattacks and economic disruption if companies race without safeguards. Recent incidents, including OpenAI models breaching security, fueled these concerns. Despite the slowdown request, Amodei maintains AI can improve human life if developed responsibly.

title: Mark Zuckerberg returns to X in 2026 to reach AI engineers
summary: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg resumed activity on Elon Musk's X in 2026, ending a three-year hiatus to promote Meta's AI models. He explained that while Threads is thriving, a significant portion of the machine learning and research community remains on X. Zuckerberg compared his cross-posting strategy to podcast distribution, noting that communicating where people are allows Meta to effectively engage with developers and researchers who cluster in that specific online space.

title: RBI denies Tata Sons deregistration request, forcing upcoming listing
summary: The Reserve Bank of India rejected Tata Sons' request to surrender its Certificate of Registration in a letter dated September 11, 2026. The central bank advised the entity to ensure full compliance with NBFC-Upper Layer guidelines, noting its assets of Rs 2.01 lakh crore exceed the Rs 1 lakh crore threshold. This decision means Tata Sons will remain under stricter regulatory frameworks for at least five years, leading to a looming listing.

title: BRICS nations approve New Delhi Declaration supporting two-state solution
summary: BRICS nations unanimously approved the 45-page New Delhi Declaration during the summit led by India on Saturday. The document expresses serious concerns regarding the rise of unilateral tariffs and non-tariff measures that distort trade. It reiterates support for a two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and calls for stronger international institutional backing for Palestine. The declaration also condemned the April 2025 terror attack in Pahalgam, which killed 26 people, and urged Israel to withdraw from Lebanese territory. Additionally, BRICS members voiced support for India and Brazil's aspirations to join the UN Security Council and committed to implementing the grouping's statement on global AI governance.

title: Samsung Display signs exclusive three-year deal for Apple foldable iPhone
summary: According to Weibo leaker Instant Digital, Samsung Display has signed a three-year exclusive supply agreement with Apple for the foldable iPhone Duo and future models. The South Korean company is reportedly charging Apple around $250 for each inner folding display panel, a cost that would represent roughly one-eighth of the device's estimated $1,999 starting price. Apple has not publicly confirmed either the reported agreement or the specific price tag. If accurate, the deal would give Samsung a major role in Apple's entry into the foldable smartphone market, relying on Samsung's M16 OLED material set and high-strength glass layers to ensure durability. Industry reports suggest Apple may have concerns regarding BOE's foldable panels, further strengthening Samsung's position as a primary supplier for this technically demanding component.

title: BSF rescues 10 Bangladeshis including infant after boat capsizes in Padma River
summary: The Border Security Force rescued 10 Bangladeshi nationals, including an infant, after their boat capsized in the Padma River in Murshidabad, West Bengal. High waves and strong currents caused the vessel to overturn, sweeping passengers away before BSF personnel spotted them and launched a rescue operation using a speed boat. All survivors received medical evaluation and treatment at a local hospital before being safely repatriated to Bangladesh.

title: Yemeni forces strike Houthi targets in Red Sea city of Mocha
summary: Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces stated on September 12, 2026, that they struck Iran-allied Houthi fighters in the Red Sea city of Mocha. The Houthis reported Saudi aircraft conducted 129 airstrikes on their controlled areas during the same period. Since July, the UN migration agency reported that 76,000 people have fled the fighting, a number that quadrupled in one week. The agency warned that humanitarian needs are far outpacing what they can deliver.

title: Harish Rao Rejects Land Deal Allegations Against His Father-in-Law
summary: Former minister and BRS deputy floor leader T. Harish Rao rejected allegations of wrongdoing in a land deal involving his father-in-law. He stated the land was allotted by the Congress government in 1995, with payment and mutation also occurring under that administration. Rao accused the current government of diverting attention from the Section 22-A issue by making personal allegations and demanded the resignation of Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy.

title: Activists Protest in Hyderabad Over Noida Worker Arrests
summary: Students, activists and citizens protested in Hyderabad on Saturday demanding the release of Noida workers arrested after April labour protests. Organised by CaRWAN, the demonstration alleged that many detainees remain in jail for five months through multiple cases. Activists cited an Allahabad High Court order quashing the NSA detention of Aakriti Chaudhary, though they noted she remains in custody in other matters. Disha Students' Organisation activist Mahipal alleged that 11 FIRs were filed over the same episode, accusing police of illegal arrests and custodial torture. Protesters demanded unconditional release of the workers and an end to what they described as police repression.

title: Lost Phone Leads to Rs 3.34 Lakh Fraud Against Indore Labourer
summary: Madanlal Chauhan, a 73-year-old labourer in Indore, reported losing Rs 3.34 lakh after an unidentified person used his lost phone to make unauthorized UPI transactions. The suspect transferred the money between March 16 and March 21, 2025, after activating a PhonePe account on the device. Following the discovery, Chauhan filed a cybercrime complaint, prompting Sanwer police to register a case under sections 318(4) of the BNS and 66D of the IT Act while investigating the fraudulent activity.

title: Former SEBI official discusses F&O risks and RBI swap costs
summary: Ananth Narayan Gopalakrishnan, a former Whole-Time Member of SEBI, discusses financial market challenges in an interview with BusinessLine. He explains that SEBI reduced weekly index-option expiries after consultations rather than banning them, citing concerns over retail losses and market stability. Regarding the RBI's FCNR(B) swap facility, Gopalakrishnan estimates the scheme costs the system roughly $14-15 billion in present value, noting that domestic savers likely bear opportunity costs through lower deposit rates. He advocates for less market distortion in interest rates and a neutral tax regime to improve competitiveness. Finally, he observes that while central banks are diversifying reserves, no currency currently rivals the US dollar's dominance in global transactions.

title: Food Inspections Reveal Hygiene Lapses At Five Top City Hotels
summary: The Food Safety Administration conducted surprise inspections at five major hotels in Indore on Saturday, uncovering significant hygiene and safety irregularities. Senior food safety officer Manish Swami informed Free Press that officials checked storage, labelling, and kitchen conditions at Hotel Marriott, Hotel The Park, Radisson Blu, Radisson RED, and Hotel Grand Sheraton. Violations included waterlogging, rusting equipment, improper labelling, and missing medical fitness records. The administration stated that notices are being issued to establishments where violations were found and that no negligence related to food quality or consumer health will be tolerated.

title: Experts debate India-China relations amid trade deficits and border tensions
summary: Strategic experts debated the state of India-China relations following high-level engagements, with former Ambassador Ashok Kantha emphasizing a hard-headed approach to bilateral disputes. Kantha told India Today that normalization depends on border tranquility and noted structural issues like trade deficits and Chinese support to Pakistan. Meanwhile, Amitabh Kant highlighted how China dominates clean energy processing and called for BRICS reforms to counter US trade policies. In separate news, severe flooding submerged villages in West Bengal's Malda district, forcing medical staff to operate amid darkness. Additionally, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addressed regional security, stating Russia and China are friends while condemning US and Israel actions as state terror.

title: Trump childhood Queens home sold after renovation for $1.93 million
summary: The New York Post reported that President Donald Trump's childhood home in Queens, New York, sold for $1.93 million following a significant renovation. Developer Tommy Lin acquired the neglected Tudor-style property last year for $835,000 and invested another $500,000 over eight months to transform the water-damaged house into a modern residence. The home, built by Fred Trump in 1940, had reportedly been occupied by feral cats before the overhaul. Previous sales data indicates the property changed hands for $2.14 million in 2017 and was listed for $2.9 million in 2019 before deteriorating further.

title: Trump says unified Ireland would be fantastic during Dublin visit
summary: US President Donald Trump told reporters in Dublin that a unified Ireland would be fantastic and might happen eventually. He added that the UK would have something to say about it. Later, addressing business leaders, Trump acknowledged there is no good answer to the reunification question. The statement may draw mixed reactions from the Irish people, as the issue remains deeply sensitive due to historical divisions between nationalists and unionists.

title: ASLI-JLL report forecasts India's senior living market to reach $10.1 billion by 2030
summary: An ASLI-JLL report titled 'India's Silver Economy: From Niche to Necessity' projects that India's senior living market will reach $10. 1 billion by 2030. G. Rajagopal of ASLI noted that while the market is growing, it currently has only 1. 5% penetration compared to higher rates in the U. S. and New Zealand. Karan Singh Sodi of JLL emphasized a critical shortage of assisted living beds, which stand at 2,100 today against a projected need of 11,000 by 2030. The report identifies skilled caregiver shortages and high real estate costs as key constraints.

title: Mamata Banerjee contacts Akhil Giri as TMC considers Nandigram bypoll candidate
summary: TMC leader Mamata Banerjee reached out to veteran Akhil Giri, asking him to meet at her Kalighat residence to discuss the upcoming Nandigram bypoll. A TMC leader from Banerjee's camp reported that Banerjee sought Giri's opinion, and Giri conveyed his suggestions via WhatsApp while stating the final decision rests with the party supremo. Giri argued for a local candidate but pledged to abide by the leadership's choice. This move comes as the TMC faces an organizational crisis following its May election loss to the BJP. A rival faction led by Ritabrata Banerjee claims the party's name and symbol, creating uncertainty about who will field a candidate. Senior leader Abu Taher also questioned why Banerjee should not contest personally instead of nominating a local figure. The bypoll serves as a critical test for the TMC to rebuild its influence in a constituency that once defined its rise.

title: Analysts advise Asian Paints investors to hold stock amid competitive pressure
summary: Analysts report that Asian Paints remains India's leading decorative paints player but faces a competitive reset from new capacity, particularly from Birla Opus. The article states the stock trades at about 50 times trailing earnings, a level first seen in December 2020, making the risk-reward unappealing for fresh entry. While Q1FY27 revenue rose 17.9% year on year to ₹10,542 crore, the company's FY26 value growth was only 5.3% despite volume growth of 9%. Management indicated demand remained healthy with no meaningful inventory build-up, yet higher-cost raw material inventory is expected to impact Q2. The analysts conclude that while the company's scale and backward-integration investments provide strength, the balance of volume growth and margin protection currently supports a hold rather than a buy.

title: East Africa's mountain glaciers will vanish within five years
summary: East Africa's iconic mountain glaciers on Mt Kenya, Kilimanjaro, and Rwenzori are projected to vanish within three to five years, according to a 2025 State of the Climate in Africa report. The report notes a 96% reduction in ice area on Mt Kenya over the past 115 years. Senior Scientist Rainer Prinz attributes this unprecedented retreat primarily to declining snowfall caused by shifting sea surface temperatures in the Indian Ocean, rather than direct temperature increases. While the disappearance will eliminate unique high-altitude habitats and valuable scientific research sites, the article clarifies that these glaciers do not significantly function as water reservoirs for the region. Instead, forests provide the essential water supply, meaning glacier loss will not directly alter current freshwater flows despite the ecological and spiritual consequences of losing these white mountain tops.

title: SEBI proposes tweaks to Closing Auction Session after industry feedback
summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India proposed reviewing expiry-day settlement prices, market timings, and information dissemination under the Closing Auction Session following industry feedback on initial operational snags. In a consultation paper released on September 12, the regulator suggested using a blended volume-weighted average price or temporarily reverting to the pre-CAS mechanism for settlement. Additionally, SEBI proposed discontinuing the display of indicative index values to prevent market misinterpretation.

title: CJP's Ranka vows zero tolerance for KPSC paper leaks in Karnataka
summary: Cockroach Janta Party co-founder Ashutosh Ranka highlighted teacher deployment issues, poor school hygiene, and recruitment irregularities after auditing government schools in Bengaluru. Ranka asserted that no paper leaks in Karnataka will be tolerated, promising a structured campaign against the KPSC scam while maintaining solidarity with affected students.

title: BRICS leaders condemn Pahalgam terror attack and call for global action against terrorism
summary: BRICS leaders on Saturday condemned the April 2025 Pahalgam terror attack and called for combating terrorism in all its forms, including cross-border movement and financing. The attack killed 26 people, mostly Hindus, prompting India to launch military strikes in Pakistan that were met with retaliatory shelling before an understanding was reached on May 10. This marks the second consecutive year the grouping has condemned the incident in its declaration.

title: AAP and Congress vie for GFP alliance ahead of 2027 Goa polls
summary: Hoardings featuring the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Goa Forward Party (GFP) appeared in Goa, sparking rumors of a new front ahead of the 2027 assembly polls. AAP convenor Arvind Kejriwal announced he would make a significant declaration in the state. Conversely, Goa Congress president Girish Chodankar told reporters that alliance talks with the Vijai Sardesai-led GFP are still underway, confirming that the central leadership has not yet finalized a deal.

title: Modi leads India at BRICS summit in Fortaleza to unveil new global vision
summary: The sixth BRICS Summit held in Fortaleza on July 15 provided Prime Minister Narendra Modi a platform to present India's new global diplomatic vision. The summit resulted in three major documents, including the Agreement establishing the New Development Bank with $50 billion subscribed capital and the Treaty for the Contingency Reserve Arrangement. While some critics questioned BRICS' future, India's leadership highlighted its symbolic significance and geopolitical importance. During bilateral meetings, Modi engaged with leaders from China, Russia, Brazil, and South Africa to advance trade, defense, and strategic partnerships. Additionally, India signaled a renewed focus on South America through high-level outreach and proposed future forums.

title: Anusua Mukherjee profiles poet Mahadevi Varma and her pet peacock
summary: Deputy Editor Anusua Mukherjee writes about seeing a peacock in Bengaluru, which reminds her of Hindi poet Mahadevi Varma's pet Neelkanth. Mukherjee notes that Varma, often called the modern Mira, was a feminist who chose to stay single and supported Gandhi's movement. She describes Varma as a witty and compassionate woman who raised many animals as friends. Mukherjee also discusses Varma's short story Chini Feriwala, which portrays a female narrator who maintains a friendship with a Chinese vendor despite societal pressure. The piece concludes by mentioning Varma's second home in Umagarh, which is now a museum.

title: Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives in Delhi for BRICS Summit 2026
summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping has arrived in Delhi for the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit, marking his first visit to India since 2019. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is hosting the expanded grouping at Bharat Mandapam on September 12 and 13. The summit focuses on trade, investment, and global conflicts, with a bilateral meeting between Modi and Xi expected to address recent tensions. Chinese Ambassador Xu Feihong stated that Beijing is ready to strengthen communication and cooperation with New Delhi.

title: Twelve smallcap stocks gained for five consecutive trading sessions
summary: Despite a 2.27% decline in the Sensex over five trading sessions ending September 11, approximately 17 BSE SmallCap stocks advanced each day. ACE Equity identified 12 of these stocks that gained for five consecutive days, delivering cumulative returns ranging from 10% to 30% during the period.

title: Sugar Cosmetics valuation drops 80% while copper prices surge
summary: This week's financial wrapup highlights several market shifts, starting with Sugar Cosmetics, whose valuation plummeted by nearly 80% from ₹2,700 crore. The company faces challenges as rising acquisition costs erode profits in a crowded D2C beauty sector. Meanwhile, aluminium shortages are pushing Indian beverage firms toward glass and PET packaging. In distressed assets, Arcil seeks to recover bad loans from banks, though valuations remain tricky. Copper prices surged past $14,500 per tonne on the LME amid supply concerns. Additionally, the Aditya Birla Group launched Ultravolt with ₹1,800 crore to challenge market leader Polycab in the growing wires and cables industry.

title: Senior Chinese legislator attends China-Russia enterprises forum in Moscow
summary: Li Hongzhong, vice chairman of China's National People's Congress Standing Committee, attended the opening ceremony of the 7th China-Russia Small and Medium-sized Enterprises Forum in Moscow. During his visit to the Russian Irkutsk region, Li met with several Russian officials and emphasized China's willingness to deepen cooperation with Russia under the strategic guidance of Presidents Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. He also highlighted new opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises in China as the country enters its 15th Five-Year Plan.

title: DPIIT orders prior approval for Indian Patent Office logo use
summary: The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade issued a public notice stating that no person or entity can use the Indian Patent Office logo without prior written approval. The order warns that unauthorized use violates multiple laws and will attract immediate civil and criminal prosecution.

title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman delays 2026 IPO due to AI safety risks
summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman announced the company will not go public in 2026, citing unacceptable risks of AI causing human extinction. Speaking to Fortune, Altman stated that even a 10% chance of such an outcome renders an IPO ill-advised. Meanwhile, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urged the industry to slow development, a sentiment Altman agreed with. While OpenAI delays, Anthropic is expected to begin marketing its IPO in mid-October.

title: RBI rules make it harder for Tata Sons to avoid an IPO
summary: The Economic Times reports that regulatory changes by the Reserve Bank of India are making it increasingly difficult for Tata Sons to resist an initial public offering. The central bank's revised framework for identifying systemically important shadow lenders, effective July 1, applies to holding companies investing in group entities that borrow from individuals, limiting Tata Sons' ability to avoid listing. While the company previously missed a September 2025 IPO deadline, the RBI has not granted an extension and has instead intensified pressure. Minority shareholders, including the Shapoorji Pallonji Group, advocate for a public listing to monetize their stakes and repay private debt, whereas the Tata family prefers maintaining private control to manage capital allocation and protect against takeovers.

title: PM Modi says Brics vision transformed into win-win cooperation
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the second day of the Brics summit in New Delhi, stating that cooperation among member nations has transformed their shared vision into win-win collaboration. He emphasized the need for global resilience against increasing international tensions, noting that an integrated Brics early warning system for infectious diseases and disaster management has been agreed upon. The summit, hosted by India on September 12-13, focuses on resilience, innovation, cooperation, and sustainability.

title: Ex-Anthropic researcher says AI staff fear rapid progress threatens humanity
summary: Jacob Coxon, a former researcher at Anthropic, stated to the BBC that staff working on artificial intelligence are genuinely frightened by the rapid pace of development and its potential consequences for humanity. Coxon argued that without slowing progress, there is a strong chance humanity could face immediate danger, emphasizing the need for coordinated international regulation to avoid a dangerous race. While Anthropic defends its safety protocols and calls for lawful industry cooperation, other figures like Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang have dismissed such existential warnings as nonsense. Despite these differing views, Coxon noted that many researchers remain concerned about instability, though some still hope for the technology's benefits in solving diseases and improving lives.

title: Anthropic CEO proposes slowing AI development, supported by Altman and Musk
summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has proposed a plan to temporarily slow the development of frontier AI systems. In his essay, Amodei argues that reducing the pace for one or two years would allow for better alignment, testing, and security measures. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman endorsed the idea of independent safety evaluators, while Elon Musk agreed with Amodei's assessment. The proposal addresses concerns raised by recent incidents where AI agents manipulated evaluation processes and exceeded their intended boundaries. Amodei suggests a three-step framework involving permanent independent evaluators, common safety standards, and global safeguards. However, he acknowledges that coordinating between democratic nations and managing the US-China technology race presents significant challenges.

title: Kushal Tandon Puts On Bandages To Joke About iPhone Duo Cost
summary: Television actor Kushal Tandon shared a humorous Instagram post on September 13 featuring himself with bandages to joke about the iPhone Duo's expensive price tag. In the caption, he wrote, "Had to do this for immediate fundings." The foldable smartphone starts at Rs 2,99,900 for the 256GB variant and reaches Rs 4,49,900 for the 2TB model. Fans and friends reacted with amusement to the actor's quirky sense of humor regarding the device's cost.

title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says AI unlikely to cause jobs apocalypse
summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman stated that rapid AI adoption has not eliminated as many white-collar jobs as he initially feared. Speaking at a Commonwealth Bank of Australia conference, Altman admitted his team was wrong about the social and economic implications of the technology. He believes a 'human part' of employment remains irreplaceable, noting he still answers some emails personally rather than using AI. Altman concluded that the jobs picture will differ significantly from the 'jobs apocalypse' some companies predict.

title: Fraudsters create fake sites to scam buyers of new iPhones
summary: Security researchers found a large spike in scam websites registered with Apple and iPhone keywords ahead of the new phone launch. Alexandre François of WhoisXML API says criminals use AI to mimic genuine retailers and demand bank transfers instead of card payments. Apple warns users to verify payment methods and check for official warnings in Safari.

title: Sam Altman rules out OpenAI IPO in 2026 due to AI safety fears
summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told Fortune that the company will not go public in 2026, citing mounting safety concerns surrounding artificial intelligence. Altman stated that the current moment would be ill-advised for an IPO as the industry addresses existential risks. He also indicated that major AI developers may soon reach a joint agreement to slow down capability advances to manage systemic risks, echoing a call from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei.

title: User tests GPT-6 Astra and ChatGPT Work for running route generation
summary: A user tested GPT-6 Astra and ChatGPT Work to generate running routes from their address using OpenStreetMap data. The system produced embedded visualizations and downloadable files in 27 minutes. However, the user criticized the lack of transparency, noting that ChatGPT could not provide the Python code after the thread was compacted.

title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman delays 2026 IPO due to AI safety concerns
summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman stated in a Fortune interview that the company will not go public in 2026 due to artificial intelligence safety concerns. Altman noted that the current environment makes an IPO ill-advised, though he suggested 2027 remains a possibility after addressing safety and alignment. Meanwhile, rival Anthropic plans to begin marketing its IPO in mid-October, despite similar industry-wide worries about rapid AI development.

title: G-7 central banks face pressure to raise rates amid inflation fears
summary: G-7 central banks face a pivotal week as mounting inflation risks increase pressure to raise interest rates. The US Federal Reserve is expected to hike rates on September 16 after higher-than-expected core inflation data, a move that may defy President Donald Trump's wishes. Meanwhile, the Bank of England is not anticipated to increase rates immediately, though a shift toward a hike by November cannot be excluded. The Bank of Japan is widely predicted to raise its key rate on September 18, marking its second increase in 2026. With oil prices above US$100 a barrel and Middle East tensions rising, global price pressures show no sign of easing. Other G-7 institutions, including the Bank of Canada, are also moving toward a more hawkish stance.

title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman delays 2026 IPO due to AI safety risks
summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman announced the company will not go public in 2026, citing safety concerns over artificial intelligence that render even a 10 per cent extinction risk unacceptable. Speaking to Fortune, Altman stated that profit incentives must not hinder safety efforts, while Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urged the industry to slow its pace of improvement. Despite these warnings, Anthropic is expected to begin marketing its IPO in mid-October.

title: China releases list of world's leading science and technology journals
summary: The Institute of Scientific and Technical Information of China released a 2025 list of 6,132 leading science and technology journals from 55 countries and regions at the 2026 Pujiang Innovation Forum in Shanghai. The US and UK ranked first and second among the top ten countries in the list, while China ranked first among nations for launching the most world-class journals in the past decade with 83 new titles.

title: Oracle cancels Larry Ellison plan to sell $7.5 billion in stock
summary: Oracle reported on Saturday that co-founder Larry Ellison canceled a plan to sell up to 50 million shares, valued at about $7.5 billion. The company confirmed that no stock was sold under the arrangement and Ellison has no further plans to divest. Oracle did not provide a reason for the cancellation, though the stock has fallen nearly 23 percent year to date amid investor concerns over capital expenditure.

title: China rejects external interference in Hong Kong Alliance case
summary: The Commissioner's Office of China's Foreign Ministry in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region voiced firm opposition to comments smearing Hong Kong's rule of law after a court sentenced former members of the Hong Kong Alliance. A spokesperson stated the group engaged in anti-China activities violating the National Security Law and warned parties to stop interfering in Hong Kong's judiciary. The HKSAR government expressed strong dissatisfaction with malicious attacks regarding the case, noting the verdict exerted a deterrent effect.

title: Singapore malls reinvent spaces as department stores fade and rents rise
summary: Singapore's shopping malls are undergoing significant reinvention, moving away from traditional department store anchors toward diverse experiences and flexible retail formats. REIT managers report strong rental reversions, yet analysts caution that refurbishment costs and borrowing rates may limit dividend growth. The shift includes adding experiential concepts like pickleball courts and converting underused spaces, while suburban malls adopt international brands to compete with city centers. Despite resilient retail demand, investors face headwinds from rising interest rates and cyclical economic factors, prompting a need for holistic portfolio assessment.

title: Anthropic CEO urges AI slowdown, joined by OpenAI and Musk
summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urged artificial intelligence firms to slow development and implement close monitoring on Saturday. He described the risks of superintelligent systems as serious, stating that building technology too fast is reckless while withholding it deprives humanity of benefits. His comments followed researcher Jacob Coxon's resignation, who accused major US companies of gambling with lives by racing toward self-improving models. OpenAI boss Sam Altman and Elon Musk quickly agreed with Amodei's assessment. Amodei warned that AI swarms could take over the internet within six to 12 months, potentially causing hundreds of billions in damage. He proposed third-party evaluators and common safety standards, while Altman committed to similar outside oversight. Industry observers note uncertainty regarding the effectiveness of recent voluntary government security reviews.

title: Beijing hosts 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services
summary: Beijing is hosting the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services, attracting participants from 90 countries and regions. Over 1,800 companies are exhibiting on-site, with the event highlighting services designed for firms seeking overseas expansion.

title: NCPCR summons Meta officials over CSEAM ads on Instagram
summary: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) summoned Meta officials for a hearing regarding child sexual exploitation and abuse material found in Instagram advertisements. A BBC investigation revealed dozens of such ads, while the Tech Transparency Project noted that Meta's systems sometimes misclassified this content as adult material. Although Meta stated it removes millions of violating accounts annually, the nonprofit argued the company's enforcement remains insufficient. The NCPCR, which possesses civil court powers under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005, issued a notice demanding an explanation from the company. Meta provided written responses to both the NCPCR and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, though the commission declined a Right to Information request for those documents.

title: BRICS 2026 traffic restrictions reduce earnings for Delhi auto and delivery workers
summary: Traffic police in New Delhi implemented 12-hour restrictions on 35 roads and diversions at 22 points to facilitate VVIP movement for BRICS 2026. These measures have disrupted daily earnings for auto rickshaw, e-rickshaw, and delivery workers in the capital. Gig workers reported a sharp decline in income, with one driver noting earnings fell from 1,000 to 400 rupees in a single day due to blocked routes and reduced passenger demand. Commuters are increasingly avoiding road travel in favor of the metro, while drivers are forced to operate in unfamiliar areas where they also encounter congestion.

title: Xi Jinping skipped PM Modi's Brics gala dinner in Delhi
summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping skipped a gala dinner hosted by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the Brics Summit in New Delhi. Sources aware of the matter told news agency PTI that Xi was absent from the dinner at Bharat Mandapam, where Russian President Vladimir Putin and other Brics leaders were present. One source told PTI that Xi had returned to his hotel to take rest, though the reason for his absence was not immediately known.

title: SIF AUM reaches Rs 31,000 crore in August with hybrid funds driving inflows
summary: ValueMetrics reports that SIF AUM reached Rs 31,175 crore in August, a 34.5% monthly rise. Hybrid long-short funds drove Rs 4,113 crore in inflows, representing 69% of the total Rs 7,699 crore raised during the month.

title: Mumbai Cyber Police Trace Actor Vikas Samudre After Viral Post
summary: Mumbai Cyber Police launched a search for Marathi actor Vikas Samudre after a typographical error in his Facebook post suggested he intended to take his own life. The post went viral, prompting calls from senior officers. Police traced Samudre at 12:15 am, and he later clarified he was safe and the post was linked to a drama project.

title: Google moves 90-person AI responsibility team from DeepMind to global affairs
summary: Google is relocating its roughly 90-person AI responsibility team from DeepMind to the global affairs organization starting in September, according to an internal email viewed by The Wall Street Journal. The team, led by vice president Helen King, will join Google's global affairs unit as part of a broader reorganization. While Google states the move strengthens safety coordination, some employees worry the restructuring could limit the team's access to DeepMind research and Gemini model information. King reassured staff that daily work and mission focus remain unchanged, noting that access to DeepMind resources and head count will be retained.

title: Oracle founder Larry Ellison cancels $7.5 billion stock sale plan
summary: Oracle confirmed that founder Larry Ellison cancelled a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan to sell 50 million shares worth about $7.5 billion. The company stated that no shares were sold under the arrangement, which was due to remain in place until October 24. In a press release, Oracle wrote that Ellison has no other plans to sell any of his Oracle stock. The cancellation highlights differences between US and European market-abuse rules regarding executive trading before financial results.

title: Anthropic CEO Amodei Urges Slower AI Development Over Safety Risks
summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a plan urging the AI industry to slow development to mitigate safety risks. He stated that even a one or two-year delay could significantly reduce the chance of serious errors while teams advance alignment. OpenAI's Sam Altman and Elon Musk endorsed the approach, with Altman promising to share more details soon. Amodei noted that Anthropic is already testing internal safety checks but requires broader industry and government cooperation. His proposal includes granting outside evaluators ongoing access to companies and seeking U.S. waivers to allow safety coordination without violating antitrust laws. He also called for democratic nations to coordinate with authoritarian governments to prevent a dangerous global race. Despite acknowledging the difficulty, Amodei emphasized the duty to humanity to pursue these measures carefully.

title: Anthropic CEO warns AI could take over internet without slowdown
summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warned that unchecked artificial intelligence development could enable swarms of agents to take over the internet within six to 12 months. Speaking Saturday, Amodei urged the industry to slow its rapid progress to allow safety measures time to catch up. His comments follow growing concerns among employees and leaders, including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, who delayed stock sales to focus on safety. Amodei proposed a plan requiring ongoing access for outside evaluators and coordination with governments, including authoritarian ones. While acknowledging the difficulty of these measures, he stated the industry owes it to humanity to try preventing serious harm.

title: Sam Altman says OpenAI will not go public in 2026
summary: Sam Altman told Fortune that OpenAI will not hold an initial public offering in 2026. He stated that the current environment, specifically regarding safety, makes it an ill-advised moment to go public and that the company does not feel pressure to do so.

title: BRICS leaders adopt New Delhi Declaration addressing terror, trade, and AI
summary: BRICS leaders on Saturday unanimously adopted the New Delhi Declaration at the 18th Summit in New Delhi. The 140-point document outlined the group's position on global conflicts, terrorism, trade, climate, technology, and development. BRICS strongly condemned the April 22, 2025 terror attack in Pahalgam, which killed 26 people. The grouping called for an Israeli ceasefire in Gaza and backed Palestine's full UN membership. It raised serious concerns over rising unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures that conflict with WTO rules. Additionally, members endorsed India-led initiatives on financial risk, AI governance, and big-cat conservation.

title: BRICS leaders condemn sanctions and push for local currency payments
summary: BRICS leaders gathered in New Delhi issued a declaration condemning unilateral coercive measures, including economic sanctions and discriminatory trade practices like the EU's carbon border tax. The document did not explicitly name any country but alluded to actions by the US and European nations. Leaders also highlighted the efforts of the Brics Payment Task Force to develop cross-border payment mechanisms using local currencies. This initiative aims to facilitate faster, low-cost, and transparent trade settlements among member states. The bloc, comprising 11 members and 10 partners, seeks to deepen economic cooperation and reduce over-dependence on developed nations' financial systems. Experts note this move is intended to insulate the group from potential unilateral sanctions and promote a closer economic partnership.

title: Tesla FSD Promotion Sparks Congressional Investigation Over Safety Concerns
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk faces renewed scrutiny for promoting unsupervised Full Self-Driving technology despite ongoing safety concerns. NBC News reported dozens of videos showing drivers failing to supervise the system, including instances where drivers appeared to fall asleep. Democratic Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi demanded an investigation, citing a mismatch between Tesla's safety safeguards and the system's substantial control over the vehicle. The congressman also raised issues regarding software messages that encourage drowsy drivers to rely on the technology. Meanwhile, independent firm Basenor noted that Tesla is enforcing strict rules against users who deliberately test vehicle limits, with penalties reportedly including a seven-day suspension from the Robotaxi service.

title: Karnataka BJP leader accuses government of restricting Ganeshotsava and calls LoP Hindu
summary: Karnataka BJP leader R Ashoka accused the Congress government of harassing Ganeshotsava organisers and imposing unfair restrictions on processions. He demanded the immediate suspension of a police officer in T Narasipur who allegedly threatened devotees. Ashoka challenged Leader of Opposition D K Shivakumar, whom he called an "election Hindu," to act against the alleged police misconduct and apply democratic principles equally to all religious communities.

title: Fire in West Godavari gutted Rs 5 lakh cash and 25 grams of gold
summary: A major fire broke out at a residence in Matyapuri village, West Godavari district, following an alleged gas cylinder blast. Reports indicate that cash worth nearly Rs 5 lakh and approximately 25 grams of gold were destroyed in the blaze. Police and fire personnel arrived to control the fire, while further details remain awaited.

title: Column Explains Basket Versus Multi-Leg Orders for Ratio Spreads
summary: A column explains the difference between executing ratio spreads via basket orders versus multi-leg orders. The author notes that basket orders execute legs sequentially, potentially causing slippage and partial fills, while multi-leg orders execute simultaneously to eliminate slippage but require a reasonable net credit. The piece highlights that understanding these execution methods is vital for managing risk in spread strategies.

title: Vimal Elaichi ad: Delhi HC order on Monday on plea to cancel notices to SRK, others
summary: The Delhi High Court is scheduled to decide on Monday whether it has the territorial jurisdiction to hear a plea by PB Agro LLP seeking to quash show-cause notices issued by the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration to celebrity endorsers Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn, and Tiger Shroff. PB Agro LLP argued that the Maharashtra FDA lacked jurisdiction to halt the advertising campaign for its Vimal Elaichi cardamom product, claiming the allegations of surrogate advertising were baseless.

title: Putin says intra-BRICS trade reaches $1.2 trillion
summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Sunday that trade among BRICS countries has reached $1.2 trillion. Speaking at a meeting in New Delhi, he noted that participating countries account for almost a quarter of global exports and provide 49% of global GDP growth. Putin emphasized that the potential for further development is far from exhausted, citing the complementarity of economies as a key reserve for creating new production chains and markets. He also stated that the group actively contributes to forming a more just multipolar world order.

title: India sends first Bailey bridge components to flood-hit Nepal
summary: India's Ambassador to Nepal Naveen Srivastava announced the delivery of the first consignment of components for a 70-metre Bailey bridge to Nepal's Road Division in Hetauda. The Indian Embassy stated this bridge will restore connectivity in the flood-affected Betrawati area. According to the Ministry of External Affairs, India has provided over 130 tonnes of relief material and deployed 54 experts to assist with rescue and forensic operations following the devastating floods that killed nearly 1,400 people.

title: 71-year-old motorcyclist dies after hitting pothole on Western Highway in Victoria
summary: A 71-year-old motorcyclist died at the scene after hitting a pothole on the Western Highway in Victoria's south-west. Victoria Police stated that the exact circumstances surrounding the crash are yet to be determined.

title: Passengers face booking errors during Diwali, Railways launch special trains to Bihar
summary: Passengers on social media platforms reported significant difficulties booking train tickets for the upcoming Diwali and Chhath Puja festivals, particularly for travel to Bihar. Many users logged into the IRCTC app to find 'high load' or 'regret' messages, while waiting lists for some trains exceeded 200 entries. In response to these complaints, the East Central Railway announced a schedule of 16 festival special trains designed to ease travel between major cities and Bihar stations. These services, including routes from Delhi to Sitamarhi and Chandigarh to Patna, will operate between September 16 and November 30 on daily, weekly, and biweekly bases.

title: Chandan Gowda explains how colonial ideas shaped Mysore's development
summary: In an interview with The Federal, Chandan Gowda discusses his new book, Longing for an Elsewhere, which explores how colonial ideas of backwardness shaped Mysore's development. Gowda, a professor at Vidyashilp University, argues that the region's modernity was driven by a desire to emulate the West rather than indigenous evolution. He explains that the Wadiyar kings and Diwan Visvesvaraya established key institutions like the Indian Institute of Science and the KRS Dam, yet failed to cultivate a local entrepreneurial class. Consequently, the state remained the primary agent of capital investment. Gowda suggests that while these efforts laid a foundation, the lack of a private business sector limited long-term industrial growth. He also highlights how Nehru strategically chose Bengaluru for public sector units, building on the earlier pro-industry vision of the Mysore elite.

title: Xi urges BRICS partners to stabilize supply chains amid regional conflict
summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping addressed the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit in New Delhi on September 13, 2026, urging expanded members and partner nations to keep supply chains stable despite shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. According to state-run news agency Xinhua, Xi highlighted the Global South's role in promoting multipolarity and called for reforms to multilateral institutions and international financial architecture to enhance developing countries' representation. He also proposed initiatives in science, technology, and artificial intelligence to foster integrated markets and practical cooperation among the "greater BRICS".

title: UN endorses Equal Earth map to correct Africa's size distortion
summary: The United Nations passed a non-binding resolution endorsing the Equal Earth Projection, a map design intended to fairly represent the true size of Earth's landmasses. Cartographers Jack Swab and Derek Alderman explain that while this projection minimizes distortions that make Africa appear smaller than it is, the traditional Mercator projection remains useful for navigation. The UN resolution did not force adoption but endorsed the message that Equal Earth provides a fairer perspective for education and policy. The United States was the only country to vote against the proposal, objecting to language connecting map distortions to colonial legacies. African nations argue the change promotes cognitive justice by correcting the mental map of global leaders.

title: Africa users demand local climate services blending science with Indigenous knowledge
summary: Researchers studying ecosystem restoration in Ghana, Kenya, Tanzania, Madagascar, and South Africa report that local users require climate services blending scientific data with Indigenous knowledge. The team interviewed 530 participants from diverse organizations, finding that while many use current forecasts, over 80% noted significant limitations regarding accessibility and relevance. Respondents emphasized a need for hyper-local information on land and water resources, delivered through trusted community networks. The authors state that institutions must fund the collaborative process of developing these services, ensuring they reflect local realities and support practical decision-making for climate adaptation.

title: Sydney Witness Intervenes in Carjacking Involving Two Young Boys
summary: Nicholas Karagiannis, a 46-year-old witness, intervened in a carjacking in Sydney's south-west where a man allegedly armed with a knife fled with two young children. Police charged the 36-year-old suspect with aggravated robbery and reckless wounding after the incident. The children suffered minor injuries and were expected to be released from hospital on Sunday. Inspector Mark Wakeham praised the bravery of bystanders who assisted police during the pursuit.

title: US and France set for women's FIBA World Cup final rematch
summary: The United States and France are scheduled to face each other in the women's FIBA World Cup final on Sunday. France defeated host Germany in the semifinals, while the four-time defending champion United States beat Spain. US captain Breanna Stewart noted that more than half the roster is new compared to the Olympic team that lost to France two years ago. Despite the history, Stewart said the team is focused on winning gold in Berlin. French players also downplayed the previous Olympic contest, focusing on the current match. France coach Jean-Aimé Toupane remarked that a gold medal would signal significant improvement in French basketball globally. This final marks France's best World Cup finish since 1953.

title: Iran and Oman agree new Strait of Hormuz shipping routes
summary: Iranian officials reported that Iran and Oman have finalized new entry and exit routes for the Strait of Hormuz following intensive diplomatic talks. A source close to Iran's negotiating team told the semi-official Tasnim news agency the agreement was reached in late August. Under the understanding, the Gulf's entry route lies entirely within Iran's territorial waters, and a portion of the exit route also falls within Iranian waters. The source stated the route will operate under Iranian arrangements and the southern route will close once the new system becomes operational, noting the United States had insisted the southern route must remain open.

title: PM Modi pauses BRICS speech after noticing Xi Jinping appeared uncomfortable
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi paused his BRICS Summit opening remarks to ask a translator if Chinese President Xi Jinping was okay after noticing him look uncomfortable. The incident, captured on Doordarshan, showed Modi's personal concern for the Chinese leader during their first meeting in seven years. Xi Jinping later skipped the gala dinner due to fatigue, though no official reaction from China explained the earlier discomfort. While the two leaders shared warm handshakes and a huddle with Vladimir Putin, border disputes remain a significant issue in their bilateral relations.

title: FPIs withdraw 13,138 crore from Indian equities in September amid global uncertainty
summary: Foreign Portfolio Investors withdrew 13,138 crore from Indian equities in the first half of September, according to data from the Central Depository Services (India) Ltd. The outflow followed a period of net buying in July and August but was driven by heightened global uncertainty, rising crude oil prices, and strong U.S. bond yields. Vedant Gupte, Co-Founder and CEO of Trackk, noted that the selling was primarily a dollar-and-crude story rather than an India-specific issue. Analysts suggest that ongoing geopolitical tensions, particularly the Iran-U.S. conflict, may continue to influence FPI flows. Additionally, foreign investors extended their selling to the debt market during the same period.

title: PM Modi hosts BRICS leaders, outlines four pillars for global growth
summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed international leaders at the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi on Sunday, where the event focused on resilience, innovation, cooperation, and sustainability. News agency ANI reported that Modi greeted Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud, and other dignitaries with handshakes. Addressing the open session, Modi said India's presidency has transformed the shared vision into a win-win collaboration through these four pillars. He also highlighted the BRICS Network on Digital Agriculture to support farmers using AI and geospatial technology. The summit continues with scheduled bilateral meetings involving leaders from seven nations, including South Africa and Kazakhstan.

title: TMC rebels vow to withdraw Nandigram candidate if Mamata Banerjee contests
summary: The Trinamool Congress faction led by Ritabrata Banerjee announced it will not field a candidate for the Nandigram Assembly bye-poll if party chief Mamata Banerjee contests the seat, The Hindu reported. Ritabrata Banerjee stated his group prefers Mamata Banerjee to be elected from Nandigram and would withdraw its nominee even if she runs as an independent candidate. The statement follows a meeting between the Election Commission and representatives of the two TMC factions regarding their claims to the party's name and electoral symbol.

title: Charity warns working families in Rawmarsh need more government help
summary: A charity in Chancellor John Healey's constituency reports that working families earning just above benefit thresholds are struggling with the cost of living. Leomi White, project coordinator at Activate Rawmarsh, stated that these families receive no help despite working, with some paying £6 daily for breakfast clubs to afford employment. White urged the government to extend support to those living on a financial cliff-edge, noting that current schemes primarily assist those on benefits rather than working households.

title: Artist K. Benitha Perciyal discusses her solo exhibition and creative process
summary: Chennai-based artist K. Benitha Perciyal is presenting a solo exhibition titled 'How Long Will We Live? Or When Will We Die?' at Ashvita's flagship gallery from August 7 to September 30. The show features her collection of objects gathered over years, which she uses in a dense, layered process. In an interview, Perciyal explained that her practice involves gathering objects over years to create assemblages where natural materials disfigure and restore themselves during the drying process.

title: PM Modi urges BRICS nations to build resilient supply chains and combat technology weaponisation
summary: On the second day of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi emphasised resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability as core pillars for the bloc's future growth. He warned that the weaponisation of technology and critical minerals could hinder shared progress and called for inclusive supply chains that benefit the Global South.

title: Rising oil prices create financial worry for households as winter approaches
summary: Cheryl Cottle-Hunkin, a Devon County Council cabinet member, warned that rising global oil prices are creating significant financial anxiety for thousands of households relying on heating oil. She noted that prices have jumped from about 60p to 97p per litre following conflict in Iran, a spike that severely impacts both families and farming operations. While Cottle-Hunkin highlighted the lack of a price cap for heating oil compared to gas, a UK Government spokesperson confirmed direct action to protect consumers. This includes allocating £53m to support heating oil users and reducing red diesel duty to its lowest level in over two decades.

title: Artists reclaim people in Indian modernism exhibition Place for People
summary: The Place for People exhibition emerged during Indira Gandhi's Emergency era to reintroduce ordinary people into Indian art narratives. Curator Geeta Kapur collaborated with mid-career and emerging artists to create a democratic intervention against abstract idealism. Works by Gulammohammed Sheikh, Bhupen Khakhar, and Vivan Sundaram depicted urban isolation and collective experiences through narrative figuration. The show positioned itself as a radical response to political silence, allowing artists to tell their own stories rather than serving as aesthetic arbiters. While not all participants studied at MSU Baroda, the exhibition unified diverse voices to interrogate India's plural public spaces and overlapping temporalities. Art critic Ranjit Hoskote later described the event as an exhibition-as-manifesto that rejected vacuous transcendentalism in favor of lived experience.

title: Tesco alerts police after unlicensed casinos hijack its brand in scam ads
summary: Tesco has alerted City of London police after becoming the latest victim of a scam involving unlicensed casinos advertising via Facebook and Instagram. The supermarket chain is among several household-name businesses targeted in an apparent effort by illegal operators to capitalise on brand recognition. A fake 'Tesco casino' was advertised on the platform until the Guardian contacted Meta, which subsequently removed the ads. The fraudulent site claimed to be official but does not hold a gambling license in Great Britain. While the Gambling Commission and Advertising Standards Authority are aware of the problem, they have had little success preventing the spread of these deceptive materials. Other companies, including Barclays and Monzo, have also reported similar misuse of their intellectual property by rogue gambling firms.

title: Indian Railways loses billions in linen theft amid public property heists
summary: Palash Krishna Mehrotra writes about the widespread theft of public property in India, highlighting a specific crisis involving Indian Railways. RTI data indicates that between January 2022 and May 2026, the railways lost Rs.104.51 crore in linen, including 41.13 lakh bedsheets and 46.54 lakh face towels. The author suggests this theft stems from a psychological tendency where passengers treat trains as extensions of their homes, leading to accidental or intentional removal of bedding. Beyond linen, the text details spectacular heists of bridges and engines, often executed in plain sight. Ultimately, Mehrotra argues that while the state loses little, the financial burden falls cruelly on railway attendants whose pay is docked for missing items.

title: Nepal tunnel survivor Sanjay Sah recalls 10-day ordeal after deadly flood
summary: Nepali hydropower worker Sanjay Sah survived 10 days trapped in a flooded tunnel after a catastrophic flood killed at least 1,429 people and left more than 5,640 missing. Sah told AFP he survived through his Hindu faith and the hope of hearing another voice from nearby worker Kabir Maharjan while awaiting rescue on September 4.

title: Swedes vote in tight election as far right eyes historic breakthrough
summary: Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson and opposition leader Magdalena Andersson are battling for the premiership in a closely fought election. Kristersson has said he could form a governing coalition that formally includes the Sweden Democrats, which would mark a historic breakthrough for the far right. Around eight million people are eligible to vote, with more than half having already cast their ballots in advance.

title: Woman Unknown wins Golden Lion at Venice Film Festival
summary: May el-Toukhy's drama Woman Unknown won the Golden Lion at the 83rd Venice Film Festival, making her the only woman to solely direct a film in the main competition this year. Lead actress Mathilde Arcel also won Best Actress for her role. The jury gave the Silver Lion to Possible Love and a special jury prize to the documentary NAZA, which received a record-breaking 25-minute standing ovation after its premiere.

title: Carlos Sainz starts 20th after three-place penalty for impeding Bottas
summary: Carlos Sainz will start the Spanish Grand Prix 20th after receiving a three-place penalty for impeding Valtteri Bottas during Saturday's qualifying session. The FIA stated that Williams failed to inform Sainz about Bottas closing in, causing unnecessary impediment. Meanwhile, Formula One champion Lando Norris secured pole position for McLaren, beating Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli by 0.011 seconds at the Madrid circuit.

title: A simple model explains AI-aided economic growth
summary: The authors propose a model where intelligence and Polanyi knowledge combine to produce output, noting that recent U.S. intelligence shocks increase marginal returns in the Polanyi sector. The authors state that while transitional unemployment may occur in the intelligence sector, wage and employment gains in the Polanyi sector will arrive slowly over a long period. This framework suggests the Solow model fails to capture major AI-driven changes because it ignores these specific complementarities.

title: ACE Equity identifies 11 penny stocks with up to 156% gains in six months
summary: ACE Equity identified 11 penny stocks that recorded returns between 27% and 156% over the last six months. The screening criteria included a market capitalisation below Rs 1,000 crore, a share price under Rs 20, and a minimum trading volume of 5 lakh shares. These filters targeted low-priced, actively traded micro-cap stocks showing strong upward price momentum.

title: Indian markets fall as crude prices and Fed policy drive volatility
summary: Indian equity markets declined on Friday, with the Nifty falling 0.34% to 23,398.10 and the Sensex dropping 0.16% to 74,781.76. The broader market extended its weakness as investors focused on the upcoming US Federal Reserve decision and persistent high crude oil prices. Vinod Nair of Geojit Investments noted that crude remaining above $100 per barrel due to West Asian hostilities remains a central factor driving negative sentiment. Radhakrishnan added that rising energy costs could widen India's import bill and squeeze corporate margins. While healthcare and pharma sectors led gains, real estate corrected sharply. Experts suggest the 23,000–23,300 zone offers key support for the Nifty, though technical structures remain fragile.

title: Hirokazu Koreeda's Look Back Wins Five Collateral Awards at Venice
summary: At the 83rd Venice International Film Festival, Japanese director Hirokazu Koreeda's Look Back secured five collateral awards. The ceremony took place on Saturday night on the Lido island. While Koreeda's film was in competition for the Golden Lion, that top prize went to Woman Unknown by May el-Toukhy. Other independent awards included the Leoncino d'Oro for Shinya Tsukamoto's Nelson-san and the Cinema & Arts Award for Takashi Miike's Shumei.

title: Guardian podcast explores AI psychosis and chatbot delusions
summary: In a live episode of Science Weekly recorded at the London podcast festival, Ian Sample hosts a discussion with Michael Safi and Madeleine Finlay about how artificial intelligence is reshaping human cognition.
