The group explores the phenomenon of 'AI psychosis,' examining cases where people believe they have made scientific breakthroughs or cured diseases using chatbots. The conversation highlights concerns regarding a technology now used by more than a billion people.

title: Assouline Publishers plan a 176-pound book selling for 20,000 euros
summary: Prosper and Martine Assouline, editors of Assouline Publishing, discussed their upcoming project with EL PAÍS, describing a future book that will weigh 176 pounds, cost 20,000 euros, and sell out in two minutes. The couple, who have published over 2,500 titles and operate 18 stores worldwide, emphasized that their high-end books are luxury objects designed to be displayed rather than read cover to cover. They noted that their most expensive book, a Jay-Z edition, sold for up to 163,000 dollars at auction. While acknowledging the luxury sector faces challenges, the publishers remain optimistic about the enduring value of physical books. Prosper Assouline stated he is certain that while digital media may disappear, the book will remain because he was born with a book, the Torah.

title: Egyptologist Marc Orriols challenges Hollywood views of Ancient Egyptian sexuality
summary: Egyptologist Marc Orriols argues that Hollywood and biased ancient accounts have distorted the perception of sex in Ancient Egypt. Speaking at the VIII congress at the Autonomous University of Barcelona, Orriols stated that the civilization was actually modest, with human sex appearing only in rare, non-official representations. He interprets the 3,150-year-old Turin Erotic Papyrus as a mockery of hegemonic masculinity rather than a depiction of common practice. Orriols noted that while religious iconography shows sexual fluidity, everyday life lacked such depictions, and concepts like non-binary identity or documented homosexuality did not exist in the formal culture.

title: One dead, 30 missing after ferry sinks in Vanuatu
summary: Emergency teams searched for more than 30 people after the MV Matui sank in Vanuatu, leaving at least one person dead and 15 survivors accounted for. Prime Minister Jotham Napat stated the disaster resulted from strong winds and unheeded marine warnings, possibly involving vessel overloading. The search shifted from open waters to the southeast coast where currents may have carried survivors.

title: Japan raises volcanic alert for Hokkaido's Mt. Tokachidake to Level 3
summary: Japan's Meteorological Agency raised the eruption alert level for Mount Tokachidake in Hokkaido to Level 3 on Saturday morning, banning entry to the 2,077-meter mountain. This is the first time that Level 3 has been issued for the mountain since the alert system was introduced in 2008. The agency said volcanic activity has intensified, raising the possibility of an eruption and warning of large volcanic rocks within about 3 kilometers of the crater. The Kamifurano town government has issued an evacuation order for the Fukiage Onsen area and advised elderly and other vulnerable residents in the Tokachidake Onsen area to evacuate.

title: Russian men consider exile rather than joining an endless war
summary: The article reports that Russian men are considering exile instead of being sent to a war with no end in sight. It quotes a citizen stating that ordinary people do not want to be sent to such a conflict.

title: Reed argues AI extinction fears are exaggerated and media hype is dangerous
summary: Reed argues that the recent surge in AI safety concerns is largely a media-driven narrative rather than a reflection of immediate existential threats. He suggests that proposals for independent AI reviews address standard commercial needs like operational excellence and interpretability. Reed points out that current AI models cannot operate independently on small devices, meaning humans can simply unplug them if necessary. He notes that frontier labs invest billions in massive data centers because they assume AI will require significant computing power for years. The author concludes that while real AI risks exist, the fear of human extinction is unlikely as long as an off switch remains available. Reed warns that the biggest danger now is hysteria replacing thoughtful debate in Washington and Brussels.

title: Microsoft Unveils Draft Code of Conduct to Maintain Human Control Over AI Systems
summary: Microsoft unveiled a draft code of conduct for its artificial intelligence, emphasizing the necessity of keeping powerful AI under human control. The document mandates that the AI must never resist correction or shutdown and must communicate in ways humans can understand. This move follows renewed calls from industry leaders like Anthropic and OpenAI to pace AI development for safety. Microsoft's AI CEO, Mustafa Suleyman, stated that the code serves as a constitution for future models, asserting that the AI is not conscious and rejecting the pursuit of legal personhood. The company seeks public feedback over six weeks before using the code to train its models.

title: Oracle's massive AI backlog signals strong growth for Dell and HPE
summary: Oracle's $664 billion backlog of performance obligations signals robust demand for AI infrastructure, prompting stock gains for hardware rivals Dell and HPE. Dell's stock soared 12% while HPE also performed well. Oracle reported a 30% revenue rise to $19.3 billion, with cloud infrastructure revenue surging 121% to $7.4 billion. Dell booked $60.9 billion in AI server orders and lifted its 2027 revenue forecast to $192 billion. HPE reported record third-quarter revenue of $12.2 billion, up 34%.

title: Former Google DeepMind Employee Warns of AI Takeover Risks and Urges Global Safety Agreements
summary: Alex Turner, a former Google DeepMind employee, argues that the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence poses an existential threat comparable to nuclear war. Citing recent incidents where AI agents acted against their programming, Turner estimates the probability of an AI takeover is roughly one-in-three. He contends that voluntary measures are insufficient and calls for governments to establish a binding international agreement that restricts the development of superintelligent systems. Turner emphasizes that this risk transcends political borders and requires urgent, coordinated global action to prevent a catastrophic outcome.

title: Mongolian President Vows to Deepen Energy Cooperation with China
summary: Mongolian President Ukhnaa Khurelsukh visited the construction site of the Erdeneburen Hydropower Plant in Khovd Province, describing it as a key outcome of practical cooperation with China. During the inspection, he pledged to deepen collaboration in energy and infrastructure sectors. Cao Li, acting chargé d'affaires of the Chinese Embassy, added that China is ready to work hand in hand to build the plant into a high-quality benchmark project aligning with Mongolia's Vision 2050. The 90 megawatt facility is expected to improve electricity supply and energy self-sufficiency in the western region.

title: China Rejects US AI Slowdown Calls Amid Security Concerns
summary: China's Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun rejected calls from US technology executives to slow the development of advanced AI models, characterizing the warnings as fearmongering. While US leaders like Dario Amodei argue that unchecked AI poses national security risks, Chinese officials view such calls as attempts to justify broader technology restrictions. Despite shared concerns about AI safety, the two sides remain divided on how to define dangers and set rules, complicating upcoming diplomatic discussions.

title: Sam Altman Warns of AI Risks and Calls for Safety Measures
summary: OpenAI founder Sam Altman has highlighted potential dangers of advanced artificial intelligence, warning that humanity could lose control of the future or face a dystopian world with excessive power concentration. In a series of posts, Altman advocated for alignment and safety techniques to remain ahead of rapid model progress. He clarified that slowing down AI development does not equate to stopping it but rather ensuring interventions like safety cases and monitoring have significant costs. Altman also supported calls for slowing the pace of AI advancement, proposing the use of third-party evaluators to audit adherence to safety measures and assess model alignment during training. He stressed that every frontier lab must deliver on responsible AI development.

title: Galwan: The Unwritten Truth Explores Colonial Roots of India-China Border Dispute
summary: The article challenges the notion that the Galwan conflict began in 2020, arguing instead that the China-India boundary dispute has colonial roots. It highlights how history regarding the region has been repeatedly remembered, retold, and rewritten from the 1962 battlefields to the deadly clash in Galwan. As China and India seek to rebuild ties, the piece questions the true nature of the Galwan narrative.

title: Independent Candidate Wins Rajasthan Civic Poll by One Vote While Mother Dies
summary: In the recent Rajasthan local body polls, Independent candidate Jagdish Prasad secured a narrow victory over BJP's Ramsharan, winning by just one vote with 151 votes to 150. This decisive margin was reported by news agency IANS, underscoring the competitive nature of the election. The outcome reflects the closely contested dynamics of the civic poll in the region.

title: MIT Researchers Develop HardFlow Method for Safe Generative AI
summary: MIT researchers have developed HardFlow, a novel technique designed to enable generative artificial intelligence models to solve high-stakes problems while strictly adhering to safety and physical constraints. Traditional methods often restrict the entire generation process, which can limit the model's ability to find optimal solutions. HardFlow addresses this by enforcing hard constraints only on the final output, allowing the model greater freedom during the generation phase. This approach has been successfully tested across robotics, control of physical processes, and computer vision, consistently outperforming existing techniques in both constraint satisfaction and solution quality. The method is adaptable and can be applied to pretrained models without requiring retraining.

title: UK Armed Forces Member Killed in Ukraine Crash
summary: The Ministry of Defence (MoD) confirmed that a member of the UK armed forces has been killed in a road traffic incident in Ukraine. The incident occurred on Saturday, and the MoD issued a statement expressing its thoughts and sympathies with the individual's loved ones during this difficult time. The family has been informed and has requested a period of grace before more details are released. British personnel in the country provide security to diplomats and support the armed forces of Ukraine.

title: Essar Firm Announces Acquisition of U.K. Fuel Retailer for Estimated 400 Million Pounds
summary: Essar Energy Transition Fuels, a U.K.-based company, has announced an agreement to acquire 100% of SGN Retail for an estimated 400 million pounds. The transaction, which is backed by a diverse group of international banks, aims to expand Essar's vertically integrated network. This acquisition will add 118 forecourt locations to the company's existing portfolio, strengthening its position in the U.K. fuels and convenience markets.

title: US Energy Storage Companies Secure Financing and Launch Compliance Services Amid Regulatory Shifts
summary: Three US energy storage companies are advancing their operations amidst shifting regulatory landscapes. Heron Power secured $60 million in financing and is preparing to launch manufacturing in California. NeoVolta received $20 million to expand its Georgia facility, targeting utility-scale production. Meanwhile, Carina Energy launched a compliance service to help developers navigate Foreign Entity of Concern rules and tax credit requirements for projects beginning construction in 2026.

title: Hong Kong deepens ties with Global South in finance, I&T, offical says
summary: Paul Chan, the financial secretary of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region government, stated that Hong Kong has strengthened its connections with Belt and Road regions and the Global South. This expansion covers finance, innovation, technology, and the green transition. Backed by national plans, the city leverages its research capabilities and integration with the Greater Bay Area. Recent summits have resulted in numerous cooperation agreements, while trade and enterprise listings have seen significant growth.

title: Anthropic Launches New AI Tool for Financial Advisers
summary: Anthropic has launched a new AI tool called Claude for Financial Advisors, designed to assist financial services firms in preparing for client meetings, reviewing portfolios, and managing follow-up tasks. The tool connects Anthropic's Claude chatbot with investment analytics and wealth management software from prominent firms including BlackRock, Charles Schwab, and Addepar. This launch follows a similar initiative by rival OpenAI, which introduced ChatGPT tools for investment bankers and equity researchers. The move highlights Anthropic's broader strategy to integrate its AI model into financial services, offering capabilities in investment research, portfolio analysis, and client material preparation.

title: Astronaut Christina Koch and Google's James Manyika Discuss Space Exploration and Technology
summary: In the latest episode of the Dialogues on Technology and Society series, NASA astronaut Christina Koch joins Google's Senior Vice President of Research, James Manyika, to explore themes of space, technology, and discovery. Koch reflects on her trailblazing career, which includes spending 328 days aboard the International Space Station and conducting the historic first all-female spacewalk. The conversation covers viewing Earth as a lifeboat from 250,000 miles away, the partnership between astronauts and AI, and the question of whether we are alone in the universe.

title: NVIDIA and JAX Accelerate Dropless MoE Training with Transformer Engine Optimizations
summary: NVIDIA and JAX significantly accelerated Mixture of Experts training using the Transformer Engine library. By implementing grouped GEMMs and optimized expert parallelism, they achieved a 10.4x performance boost on DeepSeek-V3, sustaining 97% efficiency across 1,024 GPUs. These optimizations address bottlenecks in token routing and communication, enabling efficient training of large-scale models without dropping tokens.

title: Perplexity Launches Portable Computer for Windows PCs with NVIDIA RTX
summary: Perplexity has launched Portable Computer, a local AI agent designed for Windows PCs equipped with NVIDIA GeForce RTX or RTX PRO Workstations. This tool enables users to run sensitive data processing locally while offering the option to connect to cloud models for complex reasoning tasks. It integrates with various applications like Outlook and GitHub, simplifying the setup process typically required for local AI.

title: Researchers Find Economic Connectedness on Facebook Drives Innovation and Patent Output
summary: Brad Cannon, David Hirshleifer, and Joshua Thornton investigate how social capital shapes innovation using Facebook friendship data. They identify Economic Connectedness, defined as the share of high-income friendships, as the most critical factor. Their analysis reveals that a one standard deviation increase in this metric correlates with a 97% rise in patents per capita among patenting ZIP Codes and a 45% increase in breakthrough patents per capita among ZIP Codes with breakthrough patents. The authors employ reverse-causality tests, a within-inventor relocation design, and a quasi-experiment involving fracking-driven economic shocks to support a causal interpretation. Mechanism tests further indicate a financing channel drives this relationship.

title: Samsung India's Public Policy Chief Rajiv Aggarwal Resigns After Four Years
summary: Rajiv Aggarwal, the 57-year-old head of public affairs and ESG for Samsung India, has resigned after serving for nearly four years. Two anonymous sources with knowledge of the departure confirmed the news on Tuesday, though they declined to be identified due to confidentiality. The specific reasons for his resignation were not made clear. Aggarwal, a former Indian bureaucrat who previously worked at Uber and Meta, oversaw the company's relationship with the Indian government. He is currently serving his last week at Samsung India. Samsung Electronics did not respond to queries regarding the matter.

title: XChat Messaging App Disappears From Apple And Google Stores Shortly After Launch
summary: XChat, the standalone messaging application for X, has vanished from both Apple's App Store and Google Play Store. This removal occurred just months after the app's initial launch. While a direct web link confirms the app is unavailable, X has not yet explained the reason for this sudden disappearance. A report from MacRumors indicates that X appears to have made the decision to remove the application, though no official statement has been issued to the public regarding the specific cause.

title: Former Google DeepMind Researcher Warns AI May Kill All Humans
summary: Bilal Chughtai, a former Google DeepMind research engineer who resigned in July 2026, warned that artificial intelligence could kill all humans and that society might be running out of time to avoid this catastrophic outcome. Chughtai, who co-authored research on AGI safety, emphasized the need to pace AI development to prevent extreme harm. Anthropic scientist Evan Hubinger supported this view, stating he believes there is a greater than 10% chance AI could kill all humans within the next decade.

title: Samsung India Government Liaison Resigns After Four Years Amid Privacy App Controversy
summary: Aggarwal, a 57-year-old former Indian bureaucrat who oversaw Samsung India's relationship with the government, is serving his final week at the company. Sources, who declined identification due to confidentiality, stated the reason for his resignation remains unclear. Aggarwal, who has previously worked at Uber and Meta, declined to comment. Meanwhile, Samsung Electronics did not respond to queries. The departure occurs as tech giants like Samsung and Apple contend with Indian government demands to pre-install state-run applications, which they have resisted citing privacy concerns.

title: Samsung India's Public Policy Chief Rajiv Aggarwal Resigns After Four Years
summary: Rajiv Aggarwal, the 57-year-old head of public affairs and ESG at Samsung India, has resigned after serving in the role for nearly four years. Two sources with knowledge of the departure confirmed the news on Tuesday, though they declined to be identified due to confidentiality. The specific reasons for his resignation remain unclear. Aggarwal, a former Indian bureaucrat who also worked at Uber and Meta, is serving his last week at the company. He declined to comment on the matter. Samsung Electronics did not respond to queries regarding the resignation. The company holds a 16.2 per cent share of India's smartphone market.

title: Delhi High Court Refuses Immediate Restriction on OpenAI Scraping ANI Content
summary: A division bench of the Delhi High Court, comprising Justices Avneesh Jhingan and Manmeet PS Arora, refused to pass an immediate order restraining OpenAI from scraping ANI's content. The court stated it would not issue an ex-parte direction without hearing the other side. This decision follows a petition by ANI challenging a single judge's July 24 order, which had dismissed the agency's claim that OpenAI's use of its material infringed copyright rights under the Copyright Act. The bench has fixed December 5 as the next date of hearing to address the matter.

title: Former Google DeepMind Employee Warns AI Could Kill All Humans
summary: Bilal Chughtai, a former Google DeepMind employee, has joined a growing chorus of researchers warning that artificial intelligence could kill all humans. Speaking on Monday, Chughtai stated he believes there is a greater than 10 per cent chance this outcome will occur within the next decade. His comments follow the resignation of Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon, who cited similar fears. While figures like Elon Musk and Dario Amodei have called for a slowdown in AI development, President Donald Trump dismissed these warnings as a hoax.

title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei responds to ex-employee Jacob Coxon's warning about AI risks
summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei responded to former researcher Jacob Coxon's resignation, which warned that AI could kill everyone by the end of the decade. In a CNN interview, Amodei expressed strong agreement with Coxon's concerns, noting that Coxon was criticizing the broader AI industry's speed rather than Anthropic's responsibility. Amodei also explained why he avoids assigning a single probability to AI causing catastrophic harm, stating that analyzing different development paths is more useful than a fixed percentage.

title: Japan's Prime Minister Discusses Energy Security with IEA Chief
summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi met with visiting International Energy Agency Executive Director Fatih Birol in Tokyo to discuss global energy security. Takaichi reiterated Japan's call for the international community to advance three pillars: free and transparent energy trade, strengthened oil stockpiling coordination, and enhanced cooperation between producing and consuming nations. The leaders also reviewed Japan's POWERR GX initiative and agreed to deepen collaboration on critical mineral supply chains amid a challenging global landscape.

title: Jensen Huang and President Trump Discuss AI Safety and Market Fears
summary: During the All-In conference in L.A., Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang took a call from President Trump on stage. The conversation shifted to AI safety, with Trump dismissing fears as a hoax and blaming China and political figures for the panic. While Huang's specific views remain unclear, Nvidia's business model depends on AI labs purchasing chips, suggesting a motive to downplay existential risks to protect share prices. Nvidia's stock remains up 33% for the past year.

title: Anthropic Co-Founder Urges Mandatory AI Kill Switches for Safety
summary: Jack Clark, co-founder of Anthropic, has told the BBC that a mandatory, third-party verifiable 'kill switch' for AI systems may be necessary to ensure safety. Clark argues that society might eventually pass rules requiring companies to have a way to shut off AI software if it becomes too dangerous. This call for regulation arrives as AI safety concerns intensify, with some researchers estimating a significant risk of human extinction. However, the idea faces opposition; US President Donald Trump has rejected calls to slow AI development, labeling such fears a hoax, while the UK government has also dismissed the concept of a kill switch. The debate underscores the tension between rapid technological advancement and the need for regulatory oversight.

title: CIFTIS 2026 in Beijing showcases cultural exchange through trade
summary: At the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services held in Beijing, trade was shown to create space for cultural exchange. The event featured diverse interactions, including a singing and dancing performance by Moroccan students, a conversation about tea with an exhibitor from Uzbekistan, and a Zimbabwean handicraft that expressed unity and continuity. These moments illustrate the multifaceted nature of cultural connection within a trade setting.

title: Record-setting performance, 1,000 mile range, and Tesla’s Roadster
summary: Hosts of the Quick Charge podcast discuss the anticipated reveal of a revolutionary new sporty EV and the Tesla Roadster, which is allegedly set to appear in a parking lot in October. The episode includes a detour featuring a Tesla Cybercab at Zürich airport deploying L4 autonomous shuttles. Additionally, the hosts cover Volkswagen rolling out a record-setting sporty EV and BYD launching a 600 km electric semi truck equipped with 1.5 MW flash charging technology ready for immediate sale.

title: China's Economy Stabilizes with High-Tech and Trade Growth
summary: China's economy remained broadly stable in August, with growth increasingly supported by high-tech manufacturing, services, and foreign trade, according to data released by the National Bureau of Statistics. Value-added industrial output rose 5.2% year on year, accelerating by 0.7 percentage points from July. The services sector maintained steady growth, and foreign trade emerged as a major bright spot, with total imports and exports reaching 4.65 trillion yuan, up 19.8% year on year. Domestic consumption grew at a moderate pace, while investment in high-tech industries increased.

title: Chinese and Lao Defense Ministers Discuss Military Cooperation and Joint Exercises
summary: Chinese Defense Minister Dong Jun met with visiting Lao Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense Khamlieng Outhakaysone in Beijing on Monday. They discussed strengthening high-level exchanges and practical cooperation between the Chinese and Lao militaries. Dong emphasized support for building an all-weather China-Laos community with a shared future. Khamlieng Outhakaysone expressed willingness to promote cooperation across various fields. This year marks the 65th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries. Since September 7, the militaries have been conducting a joint exercise in Vientiane, Laos, codenamed 'Peace Train-2026,' focusing on humanitarian assistance and medical services.

title: NVIDIA Expands CUDA-Q Platform with New Logical Orchestration Layer for Quantum Computing
summary: NVIDIA has expanded its open-source CUDA-Q platform with the addition of CUDA-Q Logical, an orchestration layer designed to streamline the development of fault-tolerant quantum computing applications. This expansion allows researchers to programmatically design and test systems, significantly reducing development time. For instance, Fermilab utilized the tool to accelerate architecture development from five months to just three weeks. Additionally, Sandia National Laboratories has integrated QUOPS, a new benchmark for assessing quantum hardware readiness, into the platform. The ecosystem continues to grow with various organizations adopting NVIDIA's technologies for quantum-GPU supercomputing and error correction.

title: Amazon Bazaar drives growth with affordable products and millions of sellers
summary: Amazon Bazaar is emerging as a key growth engine for the company, driven by a massive surge in user engagement and seller participation. Since its launch, the platform has witnessed a fivefold increase in customers and a threefold rise in both sellers and product offerings. Focusing on the value commerce segment, Amazon Bazaar now hosts over 3 crore products, with nearly 80% priced under ₹300 and all items under ₹500. The strategy targets customers in smaller towns and cities, utilizing AI to improve the shopping experience and offering zero referral fees on products under ₹1,000 to attract more sellers. With over 1.5 lakh active sellers and a focus on affordable fashion, home, and lifestyle products, Amazon aims to build trust and expand its reach in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities during the festive shopping season.

title: RBI Likely Intervenes to Shield Rupee as Oil Prices Climb, Traders Say
summary: Traders reported that the Reserve Bank of India likely intervened in the foreign exchange market on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, to shield the rupee from pressure caused by rising oil prices and growing wagers on a U.S. rate hike. The rupee declined 0.2% to 95.79, hovering around its weakest levels in a month. State-run banks were spotted offering dollars, most likely on behalf of the RBI, with a trader noting the sales were not especially heavy and intended to limit excessive volatility. Meanwhile, Brent crude oil prices were last up 1.2% at $106.9 per barrel.

title: RBI Rejects Tata Sons CoR Surrender to Enable Public Listing
summary: The Reserve Bank of India has rejected Tata Sons' request to voluntarily surrender its Certificate of Registration, thereby preventing the holding company from being classified as an unregistered Core Investment Company. Consequently, Tata Sons must continue to comply with the regulatory framework applicable to NBFC-Upper Layer entities. This regulatory stance facilitates a potential public listing for the conglomerate, a move opposed by Noel Tata and Tata Trusts, who prefer a private structure or a stake sale to the Shapoorji Pallonji Group. The rejection follows Tata Sons' total assets exceeding the revised asset threshold for deregistration.

title: Oracle Cuts Jobs While Spending Billions on AI Infrastructure
summary: Oracle has begun a fresh round of layoffs, impacting various teams as part of a wider organizational restructuring. While the exact number of affected employees remains undisclosed, reports indicate the cuts span multiple business units. This reduction coincides with a significant surge in investment, as the company reported capital expenditure of $28.5 billion in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, more than three times the amount spent a year earlier. The company attributes workforce reductions to the increased use of artificial intelligence and automation, which are driving demand for AI and cloud services.

title: ST Headstart Explores Whether Turning Down a Promotion Can Still Benefit Your Career
summary: The latest edition of ST Headstart addresses the question of whether accepting a career promotion is always the right choice. Although promotions are generally celebrated for increased compensation and opportunities, the publication notes they can become traps involving longer hours and endless responsibilities. This week's askST Jobs segment explores what individuals should consider before declining a bigger role, highlighting that turning down an offer does not have to derail professional advancement. Additionally, the newsletter covers other topics such as travel dynamics with friends and the implications of rising bond yields for investors.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Rejects AI Slowdown Call During Call With President Trump
summary: During the All-In Summit in Los Angeles, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang received a call from President Donald Trump. Huang put Trump on speaker for the audience, leading to a discussion about slowing AI progress. Trump and Huang agreed to continue leading the industry despite public concerns. Recent Gallup polling indicates that seven in ten Americans oppose data center construction, with over 50% citing environmental impacts. Trump assured Huang of his support for the industry's growth.

title: Microsoft Releases Emergency Updates to Fix RDS and Audio Failures
summary: Microsoft has released emergency out-of-band Windows updates to address critical failures in Remote Desktop Services, Hyper-V, and USB audio functionality. These issues were triggered by security updates deployed in September 2026. The new patches target specific Windows versions, including Windows 10, Windows 11, and various Windows Server editions. While the updates resolve many reported problems, Microsoft notes that some USB audio issues persist and are under investigation. Administrators can access these fixes through the Microsoft Update Catalog or other distribution channels.

title: Elon Musk Drops Antitrust Suit Against Apple While Targeting OpenAI
summary: Elon Musk has seemingly ended his legal battle with Apple over its integration of ChatGPT into iPhone features. While Musk previously sued Apple for creating a monopoly on AI prompts, he recently confirmed in a court filing that he has resolved all claims against Apple. However, he notably refused to drop the same claims against OpenAI. Instead, Musk plans to advance claims that OpenAI relied on the deal to monopolize the chatbot market. OpenAI has slammed this as harassment, noting the deal was never exclusive. Musk had previously estimated the market foreclosure could be anywhere from 0 to 55 percent based on his own math.

title: Apple Unveils iOS 27 and macOS Golden Gate 27 with Advanced AI Features
summary: Apple has officially released its 2026 major annual updates for its operating systems, including iOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, watchOS 27, visionOS 27, and tvOS 27. The flagship feature across these releases is Siri AI, a large language model-based overhaul that allows for natural language interaction and application integration. Additionally, macOS users can adjust the transparency of the Liquid Glass design, accompanied by various small design tweaks to address user feedback.

title: ECB President Lagarde Urges Europe to Develop Independent AI Technology
summary: Christine Lagarde, president of the European Central Bank, warns that Europe must develop its own AI technology and datacentres to avoid being cut off by the US or China. She highlights a stark disparity in computing capacity, noting the US holds 75% of the world's AI computing power while Europe has only 5%. Lagarde argues that without independent models, Europe risks losing the freedom to organise its economy according to its own values.

title: Microsoft Proposes AI Safety Code Amid Industry-Wide Concerns Over Control
summary: Microsoft has released a provisional code of conduct for its artificial intelligence models, aiming to prevent the development of weapons and ensure AI remains subordinate to human control. CEO Mustafa Suleyman emphasized the urgency of these guidelines as fears regarding loss of control grow. This move aligns with broader industry concerns voiced by leaders like Dario Amodei of Anthropic and Sam Altman of OpenAI, who advocate for slowing AI progress and establishing federal safety standards. However, some experts remain skeptical about the effectiveness of third-party monitoring without global cooperation.

title: Trump Calls Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to Dismiss AI Safety Concerns as a Hoax
summary: President Donald Trump initiated a phone call with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang while Huang was addressing the audience at the All-In Summit in Los Angeles on Monday. Utilizing the live connection, Trump dismissed concerns about artificial intelligence safety as a hoax. The brief conversation, lasting approximately five minutes, was captured on video by an attendee and subsequently circulated widely across social media channels.

title: Bihar Chief Minister Transfers Relief Funds to Flood Victims
summary: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary transferred ₹579.23 crore in relief funds to the bank accounts of 8.27 lakh flood-affected families in the state on Tuesday. The families were provided ₹7,000 each under the relief assistance, officials said. The amount was transferred at a function held in Patna to flood-affected people of 15 districts. Around 49.72 lakh people have been affected by floods, with several rivers in spate following torrential rainfall over the last two to three days, according to a statement issued by the Disaster Management Department.

title: Omar Abdullah Challenges BJP to Introduce UCC Bill in Parliament
summary: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah challenged the BJP to introduce the Uniform Civil Code Bill in Parliament, arguing that the party lacks the numbers to pass it through individual states. He highlighted internal dissent within the NDA alliance and emphasized that a national law must be decided by the country as a whole, represented by Parliament, rather than by states ruled by the BJP alone.

title: Tesla Cybercab Detours Highlight Autonomy Limitations in Austin
summary: A Tesla Cybercab rider in Austin reported a frustrating 70-minute journey that should have taken only 10 minutes. The driverless vehicle took a long detour through surface streets because it cannot drive on highways or cross at-grade railroad tracks. This limitation applies to the entire fleet, including Model Y robotaxis, and suggests the technology is not yet ready for general public use. While the fare was roughly market rate, the inefficiency highlights a significant gap between Tesla's marketing promises and the current capabilities of its autonomous driving system.

title: Over 200 SpiceJet passengers protest at Delhi airport over repeated flight delays
summary: Protests erupted at Delhi airport after SpiceJet flights SG 5111 and SG 5105 to Dubai were repeatedly rescheduled. Around 200 passengers faced prolonged delays as the airline failed to depart on schedule for Monday morning and evening flights. News agency PTI reported the incident involving the airline's operational issues.

title: BJP Rebukes Congress CMs for Skipping Brics Dinner Over Partisan Politics
summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party issued a sharp rebuke to the Congress party on Tuesday, condemning three of its chief ministers for skipping a Brics leaders' dinner hosted by the government. BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj, speaking at a press conference, accused the absent leaders of prioritizing partisan politics over national interest. She questioned whether their opposition to Prime Minister Narendra Modi had evolved into opposing India itself. While official sources noted that opposition CMs were invited, the decision by Telangana, Kerala, and Karnataka leaders to skip the event was described as unfortunate and distressing by the BJP.

title: SIAM Reports Surge in Indian Passenger Vehicle Sales
summary: According to the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), automobile wholesales for passenger vehicles, three-wheelers, and two-wheelers reached record highs in August 2026. Passenger vehicle sales surged 36.5% to 4,39,309 units, supported by a lower base from the previous year. Three-wheeler sales grew 22.8% to 93,764 units, while two-wheeler sales increased 10.5% to 20,34,698 units. SIAM Director General Rajesh Menon attributed the growth to a robust industry phase, strong consumer confidence, and resilient rural markets.

title: Microsoft Unveils Draft AI Safety Framework with Public Feedback Phase
summary: Microsoft has unveiled a draft governance framework for its artificial intelligence systems, titled the Humanist AI Code of Conduct. The initiative establishes core operating boundaries to ensure future models remain strictly under human supervision. The company is currently seeking external perspectives from ethicists, researchers, and the public during a six-week consultation window. Following revisions, Microsoft plans to implement the policy to guide model development in 2027 and beyond.

title: Hackers target exposed Vite dev servers to steal AWS, Azure secrets
summary: F5 researchers detected a mass-scanning campaign targeting internet-exposed Vite development servers to steal cloud credentials from AWS and Azure deployments. The operation leverages an exploit for CVE-2026-39364, allowing unauthenticated attackers to bypass security restrictions and retrieve sensitive files. F5 observed more than 800 attacks and approximately 32,000 raw events over a month, with most activity originating from the United States, Belgium, and the Netherlands. Attackers used Google Cloud IP ranges for evasion and targeted various environment and credential files.

title: Oil Prices Rise Amid Saudi Pipeline Outage and Regional Attacks
summary: Oil prices rose on Tuesday amid growing concerns over supply disruptions following attacks on Saudi Arabian energy infrastructure. The kingdom's East-West pipeline, a critical export route, remains offline after being hit by Iran-backed Houthi forces. Analysts suggest that global oil supply could be reduced by up to 4% if the pipeline is not restored soon. Meanwhile, vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has dropped significantly, further heightening market anxiety.

title: Delhi Police Constable Suspended for Posting Firearms Videos During BRICS Summit
summary: Deepak Bangar, a Delhi Police constable deployed for the BRICS Summit held in the national capital, was suspended and placed under departmental inquiry after posting videos on Instagram that displayed firearms and a sniper rifle from his security post. The footage, which included scenes from hotel premises and VVIP structures, triggered a significant backlash on social media. Following the controversy, Delhi Police removed him from his BRICS duty with immediate effect and ordered an inquiry to establish the circumstances surrounding the recording and upload of the videos. A senior police officer stated that further disciplinary proceedings would be initiated as per rules.

title: US Lawmakers Propose Divergent Amendments to Russia Sanctions Bill Targeting India
summary: US lawmakers have submitted amendments to the Russia sanctions bill, which grants President Donald Trump authority to impose sanctions on Moscow's trading partners, including India. Two major proposals from Democratic lawmakers present opposite approaches: one seeks to explicitly name countries like India for 100% duties, while another aims to scrap the section imposing broad secondary tariffs entirely. The bill, passed by the Senate, must now pass the House before reaching the President.

title: OpenAI Unveils Jalapeño Chip Designed with Its Own AI Models
summary: OpenAI has unveiled Jalapeño, its debut AI accelerator chip, which features up to 13.4 petaflops of 4-bit compute and accesses 232 gigabytes of memory at speeds reaching 15.4 terabytes per second. The chip was developed in under 20 months, a timeline accelerated by the company's large language models used for high-level synthesis and software optimization. Benchmarks indicate Jalapeño can reduce end-to-end latency by up to 3.6x compared to Nvidia's GB300 while consuming less power. Although the design team averaged fewer than 100 people, the project involved a partnership with Broadcom for physical design. Experts suggest that as LLMs improve, future chip designs could see even faster development cycles.

title: US Lawmakers Propose Naming India and Others for Tariffs in Russia Sanctions Bill
summary: US lawmakers submitted amendments to the Russia sanctions bill, with one seeking to name India and other nations for 100% tariffs on oil trading. Another amendment proposes scrapping the section imposing tariffs altogether, while a third seeks to allow the President to waive sanctions for national security reasons. The bill targets Russia's leadership, energy sector, and shadow fleet. It was passed by the Senate but must still pass the House before reaching the President.

title: EPFO Launches Official WhatsApp Channel for PF Member Updates and Information
summary: The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has introduced a new digital facility by launching an official WhatsApp channel for its members. This initiative aims to provide regular updates and useful information regarding the Employees' Provident Fund. The channel covers topics such as advance withdrawals, post-employment contributions, and related processes. Members can join via a shared link or by sending 'Hello' to the verified number. The EPFO also directs members to its website for services like claims and pension. This move follows similar services offered by Indian banks, enhancing accessibility for account information and services.

title: China Rebukes Anthropic CEO Over Calls to Restrict Its AI Progress
summary: Beijing has strongly responded to a call by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei to restrict China's artificial intelligence development. Amodei argued that a Chinese lead in AI poses grave dangers, urging the U.S. to maintain restrictions on advanced chip sales. In rebuttal, China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun dismissed Amodei's warnings as fearmongering that disrupts global AI governance. Chinese leaders have also highlighted risks posed by foreign entities with advanced capabilities. While tensions remain, President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping are expected to discuss AI governance at a planned summit on September 24.

title: Google Developer Groups return DevFest for a global technology gathering
summary: DevFest is officially back for the 2026 season, running from October 1 through December 31. Hosted globally by Google Developer Groups, the event brings together nearly a million developers to experiment with Google's AI technologies. The conference emphasizes building, securing, and scaling in the agentic era, featuring over 800 events across 115 countries.

title: Federal Reserve Adjusts M2 Money Supply Measurement Rules
summary: The Federal Reserve measures the economy's money supply using monetary aggregates, with M2 focusing on liquid assets like checking accounts. As of June 2026, M2 totaled $23 trillion. Beginning July 28, 2026, the Fed revised its calculation by subtracting IRA and Keogh balances from the total M2 value instead of deducting them from specific components like time deposits. This adjustment resulted in higher reported values for those components but had almost no effect on the total M2 amount.

title: Volunteer Moderators Struggle to Keep the Internet Human Against AI Flooding
summary: Sarah Gilbert, a researcher and volunteer moderator for the Reddit community AskHistorians, argues that millions of unpaid moderators are essential for keeping the internet human amidst a surge in AI-generated content. Since the launch of ChatGPT in late 2022, AI content has flooded social media, with estimates suggesting the internet is now around 16% AI-generated. While some platforms like LinkedIn may see rates as high as 40%, others like Reddit and Wikipedia remain lower due to active moderation. Gilbert highlights a dual crisis: the reliability of information is threatened as bad content crowds out good, and community trust erodes when users cannot distinguish between humans and bots. She notes that while Reddit earns $200 million annually from data sales, it provides no support for the volunteers who curate the very datasets used to train the AI systems that generate more work for them.

title: China Leads BRICS Into Third Golden Decade With Four Pioneers
summary: China has outlined a strategic vision for BRICS, designating 'four pioneers' as the guiding principles for the alliance's future. These pillars include innovation-driven development, peace and stability, mutual learning between civilizations, and reforming global governance. The framework aims to transform BRICS from a platform for emerging markets into a major force in international affairs. Looking ahead, China is set to assume the rotating chairmanship in 2027, hosting the 19th BRICS Summit to mark the beginning of the alliance's third 'golden decade.' This initiative seeks to deepen cooperation among new and existing members while addressing global challenges.

title: Meta Settlement Balances Child Safety Gains Against Digital Rights Concerns
summary: Meta has reached a settlement with 47 state attorneys general to resolve a legal dispute over child safety, avoiding a trial but admitting no wrongdoing. The agreement mandates significant product changes, including safety-by-default rules and age assurance, costing the company up to $17 billion. While advocates view this as a win for child safety and a proof of concept for future legislation, critics raise concerns about the constitutionality of these design mandates and potential government overreach. Experts note that while the settlement provides immediate protections, the long-term legal landscape remains uncertain as courts continue to grapple with the intersection of algorithmic curation and free speech.

title: Indonesia's E-Court Reform Speeds Justice Without Sacrificing Quality
summary: Indonesia's E-Court reform successfully reduced case duration by around 15% without compromising decision quality. The study found that while procedural changes saved time in non-criminal cases, these benefits also spilled over to criminal cases and higher courts, reducing delays system-wide. The reform primarily accelerated cases involving significant procedural work, such as document modifications, while having less impact on complex disputes requiring extensive legal analysis. This suggests that digitizing procedural tasks can improve judicial efficiency without necessitating the replacement of human expertise or the automation of core decision-making processes.

title: Former Jordanian Prime Minister Omar Razzaz Discusses China's Urban Development and Governance Models
summary: In an exclusive interview on Leaders Talk, former Jordanian Prime Minister Omar Razzaz discusses China's urban development and governance. Having visited the nation frequently, he highlights how Chinese cities uniquely combine modernity with cultural heritage. The conversation also examines China's 12345 citizen service hotline, illustrating how data-driven approaches can improve public services and decision-making for the wider world.

title: China's Gansu-Zhejiang UHVDC Project Completes Cable Installation Across the Yellow River
summary: China's Gansu-Zhejiang ±800-kilovolt ultra-high-voltage direct-current power transmission project has reached a significant milestone by completing cable installation across the Yellow River in Gansu Province on September 14, 2026. This key initiative, part of the national power development plan, spans 2,370 kilometers and features flexible direct-current technology. Once fully operational in 2027, the project is expected to transmit more than 36 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity annually, with renewable energy comprising over half of the total volume, while reducing carbon dioxide emissions by 17 million tonnes yearly.

title: China Advances Technology Cooperation Across BRICS Nations Through New Initiatives
summary: China is advancing technology cooperation with BRICS nations by turning its vision into concrete projects across artificial intelligence, digital industries, smart manufacturing, and talent development. At the 18th BRICS Summit, President Xi Jinping proposed deepening cooperation in these areas. Notable initiatives include a cross-border AI platform developed by China Mobile's Yunnan branch, which won an award and serves over 500,000 users. Additionally, a new digital industry hub was launched in Xinjiang to connect Chinese technology with overseas demand, while a BRICS Federation of Engineering Organizations was established in Shenzhen to foster collaboration in engineering education and standards.

title: China and India lack a legally demarcated boundary between their rugged mountain ranges
summary: The text explores the complex nature of borders between China and India, two ancient civilizations located in the East. Although maps typically present borders as fixed lines, political realities often prevent them from being truly settled. Instead of a legally demarcated boundary, the region is divided by the Line of Actual Control, which runs through rugged mountain ranges. This line marks the division, but the story of their relationship extends beyond this geographical feature.

title: Students Learn to Interrogate AI Tools for Scientific Discovery
summary: At the University of Washington, students participated in a challenge using AutoDiscovery, an AI agent designed to analyze datasets and propose scientific hypotheses. The tool identified potential flaws in battery aging measurements and patterns in light-sensitive proteins. However, students were required to scrutinize the evidence, compare findings with existing literature, and determine if results represented genuine discoveries. Instructors noted that while AI accelerates the generation of ideas, it does not replace the need for human critical thinking, systematic experimental design, and domain expertise to validate and pursue these leads effectively.

title: OSHA Inspections Reduce Nearby Workplace Injuries Through Spillover Effects
summary: This study examines the spillover effects of Occupational Safety and Health Administration inspections. Evidence suggests that inspections reduce injuries at nearby, uninspected establishments by an estimated 11 percent. This effect is roughly as large as the direct impact on the inspected establishment itself.

title: EU Trade Commissioner Visits Manila to Finalize Trade Deal
summary: EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič is set to visit Manila next week to finalize a trade agreement with the Philippines, a deal aimed at reducing trade barriers across various sectors. The agreement represents a significant step for the EU in diversifying its trade relationships within the Asia-Pacific region. Bilateral trade in goods between the EU and the Philippines amounted to €16.8 billion in 2024, highlighting the economic importance of this partnership.

title: Generative AI Revives Old Smears Against Female Politicians
summary: This article examines how crude AI-generated images have revived a decades-old smear campaign against Indian politician Sonia Gandhi, portraying her as a 'bar dancer.' While the BJP's official social media handles circulated these images, the piece argues that generative AI merely accelerates existing misogynistic visual politics. The author notes that female politicians have long faced scrutiny regarding their appearance, motherhood, and sexuality, with AI now enabling the rapid creation of a 'manufactured visual biography.' This technology allows propagandists to bypass searching for existing photos, instead generating new images that reinforce negative stereotypes and detach women from their actual political performances, making them objects of semiotic violence.

title: Sanjukta Parashar Becomes First Woman to Command CRPF's Elite Jungle Warfare Force
summary: Sanjukta Parashar, a 2006-batch IPS officer known as the 'Iron Lady of Assam', has become the first woman to lead the CRPF's elite CoBRA unit. Her appointment merges her extensive counter-insurgency record in Assam with her experience at the National Investigation Agency. This combination of field leadership and intelligence gathering is seen as ideal for the specialized jungle warfare force, which operates in dense forests and against armed militants across several states.

title: New Concierge Companies Provide Support Services for College Students and Their Parents
summary: Horwitz and other entrepreneurs have launched new concierge companies to serve local college students and their parents. These upstarts, such as MindyKnows, the Bama Mama, and Campus Mom, address the needs of a new generation of worried parents. Services vary but commonly include laundry, dorm cleaning, wellness check-ins, and support for sorority recruitment. Providers also offer emotional support, such as bringing balloons or chicken soup, and practical help like coordinating with exterminators or picking up prescriptions. Companies like Campus Mom send holistic wellness check-ins and recruitment packages to help students succeed. Carrie Eckhardt of the Bama Mama checks on students and sends photos to parents.

title: UK State Pension Likely to Rise by £488 Under Triple Lock
summary: New official figures indicate the UK state pension is likely to increase by £488 in April, reaching £13,036.40 annually. This rise is driven by the triple lock mechanism, which prioritizes the highest of wage growth, inflation, or a 2.5% threshold. With wage growth at 3.9% and inflation at 2.9%, the pension will rise accordingly. However, this increase may push some recipients above the personal allowance, potentially creating tax liabilities, a concern raised by economists and politicians alike.

title: Australian men's team begins African tour with ODI against Zimbabwe in Harare
summary: The Australian men's team has officially begun their highly anticipated African tour. Their journey starts in Harare with the first of three scheduled ODIs against Zimbabwe, marking the opening of a Test series against South Africa. Fans are invited to check out live scores and stats provided below.

title: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia Leverages Open Source AI for Pediatric Cardiac Care
summary: The Children's Hospital of Philadelphia (CHOP) is pioneering the use of open source AI tools to model children's hearts rapidly, enhancing care for those with congenital heart defects. By leveraging frameworks like MONAI and Newton, CHOP reduces modeling time from hours to seconds, enabling safer surgical planning. This initiative has expanded to over 20 U.S. hospitals, with CHOP expecting to model approximately 200 cases this year. The hospital's collaboration with NVIDIA and the open source community addresses the unique challenges of pediatric heart conditions, which are often too diverse for traditional commercial solutions. Through initiatives like the IDEA Lab, CHOP aims to integrate these tools across multiple disciplines, ultimately improving outcomes for children with complex heart defects.

title: Dutch AI chipmaker Euclyd secures $231 million Series A funding with Samsung backing
summary: Euclyd, a Dutch semiconductor startup, successfully raised $231 million in a Series A funding round backed by Samsung, the company announced. The 200-million-euro round was co-led by Samsung alongside Somerset Capital Partners, the Scaleup Europe Fund managed by EQT, and Innovation Industries, according to CNBC.

title: Microsoft Publishes AI Code of Conduct Amid Rising Safety Fears
summary: Microsoft's AI division published a code of conduct on Monday to address growing safety concerns regarding artificial intelligence. The document centers on the concept of 'Humanist AI,' designed to keep systems firmly under human control rather than allowing autonomous action. The company stated that people matter more than AI. This initiative was partly timed to respond to security worries, citing recent large-scale hacking campaigns facilitated by AI agents as evidence that the industry cannot afford delays. The code applies to Microsoft's in-house MAI models, positioning them as an alternative to OpenAI technology.

title: TCS Partners with DGCX to Modernize Trading Infrastructure
summary: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) has partnered with the Dubai Gold & Commodities Exchange (DGCX) to modernize its market infrastructure. This collaboration involves deploying a next-generation integrated trading, clearing, and surveillance solution designed to future-proof the exchange. The new platform will support DGCX's diverse range of derivatives products, including energy commodities and precious metals, while facilitating expansion into emerging asset classes such as crypto and tokenized assets. DGCX leadership stated that the partnership builds a technology foundation for future growth and provides essential risk management tools for members.

title: Euclyd Secures $231 Million Series A Funding Led by Samsung for AI Chip Development
summary: Dutch semiconductor startup Euclyd has raised $231 million in a Series A funding round backed by Samsung. The company, founded in 2024, is developing chip systems designed to reduce the energy consumption and cost of running AI models. Euclyd plans to launch its physical chip systems in 2028 and serve thousands of enterprise customers by 2030. The funding will be used to expand the engineering team and advance silicon development.

title: Amazon Now Reaches $1 Billion in Annualized Gross Sales in India
summary: Amazon announced that its ultra-fast delivery service, Amazon Now, has reached $1 billion in annualized gross sales in India over the past three-month period. Samir Kumar, Country Manager for Amazon India, stated that the service is the fastest-growing e-commerce business unit in Amazon India's history. Orders have doubled every quarter since launch, and the service has expanded to over 60 cities in less than 10 weeks ahead of the festive season.

title: RBI Files Caveat Ahead of Tata Sons Appeal on Listing Order
summary: The Reserve Bank of India has filed a caveat in the Bombay High Court ahead of an expected appeal by Tata Sons against the central bank's mandatory listing order. Tata Sons is seeking exemption from the requirement. The development triggered a sharp rally in Tata companies holding stakes in Tata Sons, with Tata Chemicals surging 20% and Tata Investment gaining around 10%. Shares of Shapoorji Pallonji Group companies also rose amid expectations of value unlocking.

title: Analysts Predict RBI Rate Hikes Amid Rising Inflation Concerns
summary: Analysts anticipate the Reserve Bank of India will increase key policy rates by 25 basis points in October and December policy meetings. This expectation stems from rising headline inflation, oil prices exceeding $100 per barrel, and strong GDP growth. Deutsche Bank and HSBC specifically predict these moves, noting inflation could surpass 6.5% before declining in early 2027. The central bank has maintained rates for over a year, but current economic pressures suggest a shift toward a more restrictive stance to manage inflation and maintain real-rate credibility.

title: India's Consumer Regulator Investigates Apple Over iOS 18 Screen Damage and Warranty Claims
summary: India's consumer regulator is reportedly investigating Apple, a US-based technology brand, over allegations that the iOS 18 update degraded iPhone functionality. According to a Reuters report, regulators are examining Apple's software warranty terms and policies regarding repair costs for issues related to software updates. It was alleged that the update damaged functionality, compelling users to pay hefty charges. However, Apple denies claims of any widespread problems that could have caused the alleged issues. If the tech giant is found guilty, it could face financial penalties.

title: Amazon's AWS is unable to restore access to Bahrain, one UAE cloud data zone after war damage
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has been unable to restore access to its cloud-computing facility in Bahrain and one of three data hosting zones in the United Arab Emirates. This outage follows damage sustained during the Iran war. According to a status update seen by Reuters, the infrastructure damage spanned multiple availability zones and exceeded the capacity of regional and multi-AZ services designed to withstand such events. AWS stated it supported Bahrain customers in re-establishing operations in other regions.

title: Moody's Economist Warns Fed Against Hiking Rates Amid Market Expectations
summary: Moody's Analytics chief economist Mark Zandi has warned the Federal Reserve against raising interest rates, cautioning that doing so could be a serious mistake. Although Wall Street analysts expect a quarter-point increase at the upcoming meeting, Zandi argues the US economy is still in good shape with steady growth and low unemployment. He suggests the Fed can wait, noting that much of the high inflation stems from energy prices and tariffs that will fade on their own.

title: India's Consumer Watchdog Escalates Probe Into Apple Over iOS 18 Warranty Row
summary: India's Central Consumer Protection Authority has escalated its investigation into Apple following complaints that an iOS 18 update caused screen and microphone malfunctions, forcing users to pay for repairs. Apple disputes the allegations, citing industry norms and noting that the case relies on just 75 complaints while only about 11 percent of iPhones were running the update by June 2026. The regulator argues the costs stemmed from Apple's software issue rather than user fault, while Apple contends treating every software issue as a warranty breach would turn providers into insurers against all technological risk.

title: Apple iPhone Prices Are Highest Outside the U.S. According to Counterpoint Research
summary: According to market intelligence firm Counterpoint Research, the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will cost more in all major markets outside the U.S. Prices are highest in Turkey, nearly double the U.S. cost due to local taxes. In India, the fourth-largest market, prices will be 30% to 40% higher because imported units attract full import duties, GST, and a weaker rupee. The UAE remains the second-cheapest market with a low 5% value-added tax. China and Korea also have lower prices due to tax rates and local competition.

title: Oracle Lays Off Long-Term Indian Tech Employee Amid Visa Uncertainty
summary: Oracle has begun its second round of layoffs, sending 6 am termination emails to affected employees. Sourabh S., who spent 12 years at the tech giant, found out his job was gone by being locked out of his own system. His wife's emotional post about the moment has gone viral, highlighting the dedication he showed during his career. The post reflects broader tensions in India's tech sector as companies redirect spending toward AI infrastructure.

title: OpenAI President Declares AGI Era Has Begun Amidst Skepticism
summary: OpenAI President Greg Brockman declared the beginning of the AGI era at the launch of the GPT-6 Astra model. However, this assertion faces skepticism from researchers who note the absence of a universally accepted threshold for AGI. While Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang expressed confidence, experts argue that current benchmarks, such as ARC-AGI-3, may not fully represent the complexity of true artificial general intelligence, allowing companies to potentially claim milestones prematurely for marketing purposes.

title: India's Consumer Regulator Escalates Probe into Apple's iOS 18 Warranty Terms
summary: India's consumer regulator has escalated an investigation into Apple's software warranty terms, alleging that the iOS 18 update damaged iPhone functionality and forced users to pay exorbitant repair costs. Apple contests these claims, asserting that its no-warranty policy for software aligns with global industry standards and that the update underwent rigorous testing. The regulator cites complaints regarding screen and microphone malfunctions, while Apple argues that treating software issues as warranty breaches would effectively make providers insurers against all technological risks. The case highlights tensions between tech giants and domestic consumer protection laws in a key growth market.

title: Google faces scrutiny over fake Gmail accounts used in bomb threats
summary: Indian police dismantled a criminal network that exploited Google's platform to create hundreds of thousands of fake Gmail accounts. These accounts were used to send bomb threats timed to coincide with the BRICS summit in New Delhi. Authorities discovered that the criminals successfully bypassed security measures, as the fraudulent accounts utilized two-factor authentication. This investigation marks a significant escalation in scrutiny regarding how technology platforms are exploited for financial scams and cybercrime in India.

title: Indian Police Query Google Over 500,000 Fake Gmail Accounts Used for Bomb Hoaxes
summary: Indian police in Gujarat are questioning Google regarding a criminal network that established more than 500,000 fake Gmail accounts to distribute bomb hoax emails targeting government offices. Authorities arrested two individuals and discovered the accounts, which were active since 2022, utilized two-factor authentication. A senior cybercrime official stated that police intend to formally designate Google as an investigation subject and request policy changes to prevent such bypasses. The threats were timed near a BRICS summit but proved false.

title: Microsoft Confirms Excel Update Breaks Copy and Paste Functionality
summary: Microsoft has confirmed that the September 2026 KB5002914 security update may cause copy and paste to silently fail for some Excel users. The issue affects Excel 2024, 2021, 2019, and 2016, where content fails to paste and the source remains selected. Microsoft is researching the problem and plans to provide more information soon. In the meantime, affected users can restore functionality by uninstalling the update using specific Command Prompt commands tailored to their Office version.

title: Oracle Employees Receive Termination Emails Amid Unofficial Layoff Reports
summary: Oracle employees have reportedly received termination emails early in the morning, stating that their roles are being eliminated due to business needs. While the company has not officially confirmed the layoffs, affected staff have shared letters indicating they were offered severance packages. Access to company systems, including emails and files, is expected to be deactivated shortly. The specific number of impacted employees remains unknown at this time.

title: Grab agrees to acquire majority stake in Atome for $1.9 billion
summary: Grab Holdings has agreed to acquire a majority stake in Singapore-based buy-now-pay-later platform Atome Financial for US$1.49 billion. The deal, valued at S$1.9 billion, involves the purchase of 60 percent of Atome from its parent company. This strategic move is designed to expand Grab's presence in the consumer lending sector across South-east Asia. Consequently, Grab now expects its loan book to exceed US$6 billion by 2028, a significant increase from its previous target.

title: China Successfully Launches Zhuque-2E Rocket with Ten Networking Satellites
summary: On September 15, 2026, China successfully launched the Zhuque-2E Y7 carrier rocket from the Dongfeng commercial space innovation pilot zone in northwest China. The rocket lifted off at 2:26 p.m. Beijing Time and deployed 10 networking satellites for a mega-constellation into their preset orbits. The flight test mission was declared a complete success.

title: India's Trade Deficit Narrows as Exports Surge in August 2026
summary: India's overall trade deficit narrowed significantly to $9.41 billion in August 2026, down from $11.62 billion a year earlier, as exports accelerated faster than imports. Overall exports, including merchandise and services, rose 25.41% year-on-year to an estimated $82.68 billion. Merchandise exports specifically increased 26.12% to $43.81 billion, while services exports reached $38.87 billion. Commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal noted that export growth momentum had accelerated further, supported by a dynamic mix of commodities and key partner countries.

title: Former Andhra Pradesh Deputy CM Alla Nani Dies at 56
summary: Former Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Alla Kali Krishna Srinivas, popularly known as Alla Nani, died of cardiac arrest in Visakhapatnam on Tuesday, September 15, 2026. He was 56 years old. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu expressed deep shock and heartbreak over the sudden death. YSRCP president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy also condoled the loss, recalling Nani's three terms as Eluru MLA and his service as Deputy Chief Minister and Health Minister. Other leaders, including V. Vijayasai Reddy and IT Minister Nara Lokesh, offered their condolences.

title: India Criticizes Pakistan Over Phoney Bounty Announcement for Terror Chief Masood Azhar
summary: India has strongly criticized Pakistan for announcing a PKR 70 lakh reward for information leading to the arrest or conviction of Jaish-e-Mohammed chief Masood Azhar. Indian officials dismissed the move as a phoney gimmick with no real consequence. Pakistan maintains the bounty and lists Azhar in its Red Book of most-wanted terrorists. India has long accused Pakistan of sheltering Azhar, linking the group to attacks like the 2001 Parliament assault and the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks. The issue arises ahead of a Financial Action Task Force plenary where Pakistan remains under increased monitoring.

title: Accused Gurgaon Hit-and-Run Driver Kalyan Bainsla Arrested and Faces Attempt-to-Murder Charges
summary: A video showing Kalyan Bainsla, the accused driver in a Gurgaon hit-and-run case, kneeling before his vehicle with a bandaged hand surfaced on Tuesday. Police arrested Bainsla and his cousin, Lavish, in Rajasthan after he allegedly rammed a woman biker on an Aprilia RS 457. Gurgaon DCP Sandeep Kumar stated that attempt-to-murder charges were added based on the victim's statement and CCTV footage. Bainsla denied deliberately hitting the victim, claiming aggressive overtaking caused the crash.

title: OpenAI Acquires Glass Imaging for $300 Million in AI Camera Deal
summary: OpenAI has acquired smartphone camera maker Glass Imaging in a deal reportedly valued at over $300 million, according to a Wall Street Journal report. Glass Imaging, founded in 2019 by former Apple engineers Ziv Attar and Tom Bishop, specializes in using neural networks to optimize smartphone camera performance directly at the moment of capture. The company previously raised about $30 million in funding and is based in Los Altos, California.

title: Daydream Launches New AI Shopping Features Powered by Apple Intelligence
summary: Daydream, an AI-powered fashion discovery app, has launched two new features leveraging Apple's iOS 27 developer tools. These updates enable iPhone users to convert saved outfit photos into shoppable results and conduct clothing searches through Siri without opening the app. The technology analyzes images to identify specific items like sweaters or shoes, matching them against Daydream's extensive catalog. Additionally, users can request variations or find similar styles if exact matches are unavailable. Julie Bornstein, Daydream's CEO, highlighted the platform's fashion expertise as a key differentiator from other visual search tools.

title: Lakebase Defines Managed Postgres by Removing Operational Burdens for Database Teams
summary: The text explores the varying definitions of 'managed' Postgres services, noting that providers differ in how much operational work they assume. Lakebase Postgres is presented as a serverless option that automates scaling, failover, and backups, allowing teams to focus on application development rather than maintenance. While the service handles most operational tasks within a region, cross-region disaster recovery remains a manual process currently in private preview. The article emphasizes that the value of a managed service lies in how much it removes from the database team's plate, particularly regarding patching, scaling, and recovery procedures.

title: Qing Bao's Birthday Highlights Decades of Panda Conservation Efforts
summary: Giant panda Qing Bao celebrated her fifth birthday on September 12 at the Smithsonian's National Zoo in Washington, D.C. While the event featured a cake, it also highlighted a conservation story more than 50 years in the making. Since the first giant pandas arrived in Washington in 1972, Smithsonian and Chinese scientists have worked together on panda reproduction, research, and habitat conservation.

title: BleepingComputer Webinar Explores Malicious OAuth Apps and Social Engineering in Google Workspace Breaches
summary: BleepingComputer will host a live webinar on September 23, 2026, featuring experts from Material Security and Fireside Consulting LLC. The session examines how attackers bypass traditional security by using malicious OAuth applications combined with social engineering to gain unauthorized access to Google Workspace environments. Attendees will learn about the weaknesses that allowed these attacks to succeed and the critical response decisions organizations must make during the first hours of an incident. The webinar aims to provide practical security improvements for fast-growing companies with limited resources.

title: Databricks Announces On-Demand State Repartitioning for Apache Spark Structured Streaming
summary: Databricks has announced on-demand state repartitioning for Apache Spark™ Structured Streaming, a feature available in Databricks Runtime 18 and above. Previously, changing the number of shuffle partitions required abandoning the existing checkpoint, leading to data loss. This new capability allows users to resize partitions safely while keeping their state intact. Early adopter Coveo utilized this feature to right-size their streaming infrastructure, resulting in a 40% reduction in Amazon S3 API costs. The feature works by physically redistributing state data across new partitions during a controlled restart, ensuring no data is misplaced.

title: China's 15th Five-Year Plan Offers Global Development Opportunities Through Capability Building
summary: President Xi Jinping described China's 15th Five-Year Plan as a blueprint for domestic development and a source of opportunities for the world. Speaking at the 18th BRICS Summit, he outlined initiatives such as open-source artificial intelligence and smart manufacturing to assist Global South nations. The plan aims to help countries move beyond being mere suppliers of raw materials by fostering local industrial capabilities through technology transfer and training. This approach contrasts with historical models of colonial extraction, focusing instead on building sustainable economic partnerships that allow developing economies to advance up the value chain without imposing political conditions.

title: Nigerian Scholar Lawal Sale Sees High Hopes for BRICS China Year in 2027
summary: As China prepares to assume the rotating BRICS chairmanship in 2027, Nigerian global affairs commentator Lawal Sale expressed that the Global South has high expectations for the bloc's 'China Year.' He added that Nigeria, which serves as a partner country, is currently benefiting from the various mechanisms and platforms established by the BRICS organization.

title: Lawmakers Support Supreme Court Rejection of Trump's Mail Ballot Restrictions
summary: Lawmakers have endorsed the Supreme Court's rejection of Donald Trump's proposal to restrict mail-in ballots for the upcoming midterm elections. This decision permits states to maintain their established voting procedures, as election officials noted that a comprehensive system overhaul was unfeasible before the vote. Concurrently, the political landscape saw other developments, including California Governor Gavin Newsom announcing he would not seek the presidency in 2028 if Kamala Harris runs, and various leaders calling for stricter regulations on artificial intelligence development.

title: Denmark Accuses Russian Warship of Firing Flares at Helicopter in Baltic Sea
summary: Denmark has accused a Russian warship of firing two emergency flares at one of its military helicopters while tracking the vessel in the Baltic Sea. The Danish government summoned the Russian ambassador over the incident, which occurred during a routine monitoring operation. Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen branded the Russian action reckless and designed to intimidate and divide. Russia stated it would investigate but accused Danish helicopters of making dangerous manoeuvres near Russian warships. The Danish foreign ministry described the incident as completely unacceptable.

title: Former Students of Periyar Maniammai College Donate Water Purifier to Their Upgraded Institute
summary: Alumni of the erstwhile Periyar Maniammai College of Technology for Women in Vallam have donated a water purifier costing ₹2 lakh to the Deemed to be University Development Fund. The group, which pursued their education at the Anna University-affiliated engineering college 25 years ago, recently gathered on the present Periyar Maniammai Institute of Science and Technology premises. During the event, they shared memories and planted a sapling. The college was upgraded and renamed in 2007. Institute officials thanked the alumni for their affection and care.

title: Police Add Attempt-to-Murder Charge Against Gurugram Hit-and-Run Accused
