summary: Kalyan Bainsla, the accused in a Gurugram hit-and-run case involving a woman biker, was arrested in Rajasthan after attempting to flee police on the pretext of urination. While trying to escape, he fell and sustained minor injuries. Police have added an attempt-to-murder charge based on CCTV footage, along with stalking and outraging modesty provisions. Bainsla claimed he did not intentionally hit the bikers but was asking them to slow down. The investigation is ongoing.

title: Terrepower Launches Ontility Brand for EV Battery Repurposing and Recycling Solutions
summary: Terrepower has launched Ontility, a dedicated brand focused on establishing EV battery lifecycle solutions across Europe and North America. This strategic expansion aims to maximize the value of electric vehicle batteries through validated reuse, remanufacturing, repurposing, and recycling. Duncan Gillis, CEO of Terrepower, noted that extending battery life is as critical as production during this pivotal phase of EV adoption. The company also supports solar panel recycling and refurbishing, reinforcing its position as a global leader in sustainable manufacturing and circular approaches to electrification.

title: Rupee Slumps as Oil Prices and Global Tensions Weigh on Indian Currency
summary: The Indian rupee depreciated 38 paise to close at 95.92 against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday, September 15, 2026. This decline was driven by escalating conflict in West Asia and soaring Brent crude oil prices, which reached $108 per barrel. Forex traders noted that surging dollar demand from oil importers has sparked fresh concerns over inflation and India's external trade balance. Additionally, weak domestic markets and a strong U.S. dollar further dented investor sentiment.

title: Australian Energy Minister Travels to Saudi Arabia for Pipeline Updates
summary: Australian Energy Minister Chris Bowen is heading to Saudi Arabia to discuss the status of the East-West oil pipeline with Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman. The pipeline was temporarily shut down after drone attacks near the Iranian border. Repairs are estimated to take three to five weeks. Saudi Arabia, the world's top crude oil exporter, implemented this precautionary measure after injuries occurred. Australia relies on imports for most of its transportation fuel supply, making the situation critical for fuel security over the coming weeks and months.

title: European PPA Prices Rise 2.2% in August Amid Market Shifts
summary: European power purchase agreement prices rose 2.2% in August, according to the Euro Composite Index from Swiss consultancy Pexapark. The United Kingdom recorded the largest monthly increase at 4.9%, followed by Germany and the Netherlands at 2.8%. Prices remained virtually unchanged on the Iberian Peninsula, while France saw a marginal increase of 0.2% and Nordic markets experienced a 1.2% decline. The increase in the United Kingdom was largely driven by revised PPA benchmark values following an update to Pexapark's market price risk assessment. European PPA activity slowed significantly in August, with 14 agreements covering around 335 MW announced during the month.

title: Gatwick Airport Unveils Robot Valet Parking for Safer Long-Stay Car Storage
summary: Gatwick Airport has launched a robot valet parking service developed by French company Stanley Robotics, promising safer and easier long-stay car storage. The robots, capable of centimetre-level precision, can accommodate around 95% of vehicles, though some are excluded based on weight, height, and wheelbase restrictions. While the service costs between €6 and €12 more than standard parking, passengers report it as quick, easy to book, and offering added security. Originally limited to weekdays with a minimum five-day stay, Gatwick states these restrictions will be gradually eased.

title: Court Grants Interim Bail to Swatantra Bhardwaj in Assault Case
summary: A Delhi court has granted three weeks of interim bail to right-wing influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj regarding an alleged assault on the father of a student activist at Jantar Mantar. The Patiala House Court reserved its final order until September 15. Bhardwaj's lawyer attributed the arrest to political developments, while the complainant, Nishu Aazad, alleged that Bhardwaj attacked her father and cracked his skull. Police stated that charges under the SC/ST Act were added after a re-recorded statement included a casteist slur, which was not in the initial complaint. Bhardwaj was previously remanded to judicial custody.

title: Australian Cricket Legends Urge Release of Imran Khan Amid Health Fears
summary: Concerns over Imran Khan's health and treatment in detention have united Australian cricket legends, including former captains Allan Border and Greg Chappell. They have submitted a humanitarian appeal to Foreign Minister Penny Wong, fearing the former Pakistani Prime Minister could die in jail. The group requests an independent medical assessment and immediate treatment, noting a stark contrast between Khan's current condition and his fit appearance in 2022. While taking no political stance, the captains argue that humane treatment is a matter of basic humanity regardless of political beliefs.

title: Japan's Air Self-Defense Force Says Global Hawk Drone Likely Crashed Off Tottori Coast
summary: The Air Self-Defense Force announced that one of its Global Hawk surveillance drones likely crashed off the coast of Tottori Prefecture on Tuesday. Debris spotted in the waters north of the prefecture is believed to be the aircraft, which went missing over international waters. General Takehiro Morita clarified that the drone was not participating in training at the time of the incident. The cause of the crash and the mission details remain unclear.

title: Google Introduces Gemini 3.8 Live Models for Voice Agents
summary: Google has introduced two new AI models, Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking, aimed at advancing near real-time reasoning for voice agents. These models combine conversational intelligence with visual grounding and multi-step reasoning capabilities. They are designed to make interactions with AI more intuitive and intelligent, supporting developers and enterprises in building reliable voice-driven interfaces. The models are rolling out across various platforms including Google Workspace, Search, and the Gemini API.

title: NVIDIA DSX Enables AI Factories to Optimize Power and Grid Flexibility
summary: NVIDIA's DSX platform is transforming how AI factories manage power and interact with the grid. In a live demonstration, Emerald AI used NVIDIA's Conductor platform to adjust power consumption in response to signals from Silicon Valley Power, successfully reducing demand without disrupting critical AI workloads. Lambda Cloud's validation further proved that intelligent power management can significantly boost efficiency, achieving 24% more token throughput and 23% better performance per watt within fixed power budgets. By optimizing workload allocation and integrating with grid utilities, DSX enables data centers to maximize compute density and contribute to grid stability, paving the way for scalable AI infrastructure without the need for immediate new transmission lines.

title: NVIDIA Unveils AI Factory Platforms to Boost Efficiency and Scale
summary: At the AI Infra Summit, NVIDIA highlighted its full-stack AI factory platform, emphasizing energy efficiency and scalability for agentic AI workloads. Ian Buck, NVIDIA's vice president, discussed collaborations with partners like Amazon, Lambda, and Pinterest to optimize power consumption and increase token throughput. Lambda reported a 23% improvement in performance per watt, while NVIDIA's Vera Rubin NVL72 platform promises up to 30x higher throughput per megawatt. These advancements aim to address the growing demand for efficient, large-scale AI infrastructure as agentic AI drives new workloads.

title: NVIDIA Groq 3 LPX Drives Power-Efficient AI Inference on Vera Rubin Platform
summary: Power constraints define the value of AI platforms, making performance per watt the ultimate metric. The NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform addresses this by integrating NVIDIA Groq 3 LPX accelerators, which utilize a deterministic execution model. This model allows the LPU compiler to create exact schedules for data movement and operations, predicting current draw at the clock cycle level. Consequently, complementary technologies like Preemptive Power and Clock Period Synthesis can manage power delivery more effectively, reducing voltage droop and the necessary voltage guardband. Internal testing suggests this can lower voltage drop by over 60% and reduce power requirements significantly, enabling higher throughput per megawatt for high-interactivity AI workloads.

title: NVIDIA Unveils Multi-Layer Resiliency Stack for AI Factories
summary: NVIDIA has developed a comprehensive multi-layer resiliency framework for its AI factory platforms, specifically targeting the reliability needs of massive-scale training and inference workloads. The solution addresses the inevitability of transient errors and link degradations in large deployments by integrating hardware and software safeguards. At the physical layer, the technology utilizes advanced error correction and packet retransmission mechanisms to maintain a lossless fabric. The link layer employs credit-based flow control to proactively prevent packet loss, avoiding the congestion issues found in traditional Ethernet protocols. On the software side, features like Shadow Engine Recovery enable near-instant failovers, drastically reducing downtime compared to traditional cold restarts. Furthermore, the system supports non-disruptive maintenance, allowing administrators to replace hardware components without interrupting active AI jobs. This holistic approach ensures that complex AI operations can proceed with minimal interruption, maximizing throughput and revenue generation.

title: Google Reveals How AI Reshapes Global Work and Science
summary: Google has released new insights from its AI & Economy ATLAS, revealing how artificial intelligence is reshaping global work. The data shows that India's creative industry uses AI at a higher rate than the rest of the world, while the U.S. leads in technical AI adoption. A separate study involving Google, Google DeepMind, and MIT FutureTech found that scientists are using AI at a higher rate than many other occupations, saving nearly seven hours a week. However, bottlenecks in validating AI outputs and physical experimentation remain. Google is launching a new interactive, open-access experience to help users explore these insights and adoption rates across different occupations and countries.

title: Google Expands Singapore Engineering Center Amid AI-Driven Hiring Surge
summary: Google is ramping up hiring for its Singapore engineering center, driven by the growing demand for tech talent fueled by artificial intelligence. The company has already hired more than 85 specialists in under six months for the first phase of its Google Cloud Singapore Engineering Center. This expansion builds on a promise to fill over 150 positions, focusing on roles that combine technical skills with consultative abilities to serve local and global clients. While AI is automating some tasks, Google emphasizes that it makes engineers more productive rather than replacing them. The center, co-located with Google DeepMind, aims to deliver secure, mission-critical workflows for customers in Singapore and beyond.

title: Tesla Delays Roadster Unveil Amidst Cyberpunk Design Criticism
summary: Tesla is preparing to unveil its highly anticipated Roadster on October 1, more than eight years after its initial 2017 reveal. The upcoming production model reportedly features SpaceX cold gas thrusters and a 'Cyber' design language, including a full-width light bar and angular styling similar to the Cybertruck. However, the article criticizes these additions as unnecessary gimmicks, arguing that the original 2017 design was already superior and that the vehicle's primary goal should be production rather than radical redesign. The piece highlights that the original Roadster promised a 620-mile range and 0-60 mph in 1.9 seconds, features that remain desirable today. Critics suggest Tesla should focus on delivering the car as originally reserved rather than adding complex thrusters and a cyberpunk aesthetic to a vehicle that already looks great.

title: RBI Supports New MDR Charges for Large UPI Transactions
summary: The Reserve Bank of India has supported the introduction of a Merchant Discount Rate on large-value UPI transactions, describing the move as an important step for the sustainability of the digital payments ecosystem. The government introduced a 0.4 per cent MDR on UPI payments exceeding ₹2,000 for merchants. This fee is capped at ₹300 for transactions of ₹75,000 and above, ensuring that users continue to enjoy free transactions while merchants bear the cost.

title: TikTok Reviewer Boosts Indie Comic Creator's Sales
summary: A TikTok reviewer known as @slow_comics significantly boosted the career of indie comic creator Dare after visiting his stall at Anime NYC. The reviewer posted a video highlighting Dare's work, which garnered one million likes. This viral exposure brought approximately 25,000 new followers to Dare's account and resulted in the immediate sell-out of his available comic copies, including a limited presale.

title: RBI Files Caveat in Bombay HC Over Tata Sons Listing Decision
summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has filed a caveat petition in the Bombay High Court to ensure its decision regarding Tata Sons' listing is heard before any potential challenge. Tata Sons, classified as an Upper Layer NBFC since September 2022, faces a mandatory stock-market listing deadline of September 30, 2025. Although the group repaid over Rs 21,000 crore of debt and has standalone assets around Rs 1.75 lakh crore, the RBI maintains that it cannot escape regulation. The RBI's move aims to secure its position before the court passes any interim orders.

title: RBI Backs MDR Fees to Support UPI Growth and Sustainability
summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has endorsed the introduction of Merchant Discount Rates (MDR) for large-value UPI transactions exceeding ₹2,000. The central bank stated that a fair distribution of these fees among ecosystem participants is crucial for sustaining investment in technology and infrastructure. Such investments are expected to expand UPI acceptance, deepen the customer base, and ensure the long-term sustainability of India's digital payments ecosystem. The RBI emphasized that UPI will remain safe, seamless, affordable, and accessible.

title: Indian Consumer Regulator Launches Probe into Apple Over iOS 18 iPhone Issues
summary: The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) in India has launched a detailed investigation into Apple Inc. over technical issues reported by iPhone users following the rollout of the iOS 18 update. This action comes nearly a year after the regulator first sought an explanation from the company. LocalCircles, a consumer advocacy group, welcomed the CCPA's escalation and intends to submit its latest survey findings, which indicate a rise in complaints, to assist the ongoing inquiry. LocalCircles also renewed its demand for a class action lawsuit against Apple, citing a lack of proper solutions for affected users.

title: Gujarat Police Question Google Over Fake Gmail Accounts Used for Hoax Bomb Threats
summary: Gujarat Police have busted a criminal network that created over 5,00,000 fake Gmail accounts to send hoax bomb threats to government offices since 2022. Two individuals were arrested, and the police plan to question Google regarding gaps in its safeguards. The network, which used two-factor authentication, sent threats to various locations including the Delhi Legislative Assembly and offices ahead of the BRICS summit. Authorities described the threats as false and are investigating the syndicate's operations.

title: Indian Regulator Launches Probe into Apple Over iOS 18 Complaints
summary: The Indian consumer regulator, the CCPA, has launched a detailed investigation into Apple Inc regarding reported technical flaws in iOS 18. This regulatory move follows a notice issued a year prior demanding explanations for the issues. Sources state the authority has now initiated the probe as issues continue to linger. Adding weight to consumer concerns, a recent survey conducted by LocalCircles reveals that complaints among iPhone users have risen compared to its previous report in January 2025. LocalCircles announced it will submit its updated findings to the CCPA to assist with the probe.

title: RBI Files Caveat to Challenge Tata Sons Listing Decision
summary: The Reserve Bank of India has pre-emptively filed a caveat in the Bombay High Court to ensure it can be heard in any legal proceedings related to the listing of Tata Sons. This move follows the RBI's rejection of Tata Sons' application to deregister as a non-banking financial company. Under RBI rules, core investment companies with assets exceeding ₹1 trillion are required to list. Tata Sons reported standalone assets of ₹1.75 trillion as of March 2025. While factions within the group have resisted a listing, shares of group companies rose on Tuesday. The RBI source declined to be identified.

title: Amazon Now Crosses $1 Billion in Annualized Sales in India
summary: Amazon Now, Amazon's ultra-fast delivery service, has crossed $1 billion in annualised gross sales in India, the company stated on Tuesday. Driven by a sharp increase in orders since its launch, the service has doubled its orders every quarter since introduction. Samir Kumar, Country Manager, Amazon India, noted that this achievement makes it the fastest-growing e-commerce business unit in Amazon India's history. The service delivers orders within minutes through a network of more than 750 micro-fulfilment and urban fulfilment centres.

title: Indian Bond Yields Surge to Four-Month High Amid RBI Sales and Global Pressures
summary: Indian government bond yields surged to a four-month high on Tuesday, driven by the Reserve Bank of India's announcement of significant open market operations. The benchmark 10-year yield briefly tested 7.10 per cent. Analysts attribute the rise to a combination of increased government and state development loan supply, persistent inflationary pressures, and unfavorable global conditions including higher US Treasury yields and crude prices. The rupee also weakened, further heightening concerns over imported inflation.

title: ECB Staff Raise Stability Concerns Over Lagarde Departure Rumours
summary: European Central Bank staff members have raised stability concerns regarding potential early departures of President Christine Lagarde and board member Isabel Schnabel. In a letter, they requested clarity on leadership transitions, warning that uncertainty could undermine trust and complicate strategic planning. The staff noted that such rumours affect monetary policy and internal reforms, especially as other leaders also prepare to leave their mandates.

title: RBI Rejects Tata Sons NBFC Exit Amid Regulatory Questions
summary: The Reserve Bank of India rejected Tata Sons' application to exit its Non-Banking Financial Company framework, effectively keeping the conglomerate under regulatory oversight. This decision follows the RBI's tightening of rules requiring stock market listing for major NBFCs. Legal experts argue the rejection may violate principles of natural justice and procedural fairness, citing inconsistent treatment compared to similar entities allowed to exit previously. Tata Sons could challenge the retrospective application of new regulations to its pending application.

title: Major AI Firms Discuss Safety Coordination Amid Antitrust Concerns
summary: OpenAI's Chris Lehane confirmed that the company has been in talks with rivals Anthropic and Google DeepMind for weeks regarding AI safety. This coordination follows a call by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei to slow the pace of frontier AI to avoid catastrophic risks. While leaders like Sam Altman support embedding third-party evaluators, others warn that such talks could violate antitrust laws. Consequently, Amodei proposed a government waiver, though Lehane reportedly stated the firms do not need one. Meanwhile, President Trump dismissed safety concerns as a hoax, fearing regulations would aid China.

title: Amazon Now Crosses $1 Billion Revenue In India
summary: Amazon Now has achieved a significant milestone by crossing $1 billion in annualised gross revenue in India, a feat accomplished in less than two years of operation. The service currently operates in over 60 locations and aims to expand to 100 cities by Diwali. This rapid growth positions Amazon as a formidable competitor in India's quick-commerce sector, challenging established players like Blinkit, Zepto, and Swiggy as the market continues to expand.

title: Elon Musk's Video Game Comment Sparks Debate on Cognitive Benefits
summary: Elon Musk's comment linking video games to intelligence sparked a debate, leading to a study on cognitive performance. The research found that gamers who played at least five hours weekly performed better on cognitive tests, appearing roughly 13.7 years younger than their actual age. However, the study did not prove gaming directly increases intelligence. It also noted that regular exercise improves mental health, reducing depression and anxiety symptoms, indicating both activities offer unique benefits.

title: OpenAI Confirms Joint AI Safety Collaboration With Anthropic and Google DeepMind
summary: OpenAI has confirmed it is working with competitors Anthropic and Google DeepMind on artificial intelligence safety measures. The joint initiative aims to confront mounting alarm among lawmakers and the public regarding the economic hazards and national security liabilities of uncontrolled computing models. Speaking during a Washington press briefing, OpenAI global policy chief Chris Lehane revealed that collaborative talks have been actively progressing for multiple weeks. Lehane emphasized that the tech firms do not require an antitrust exemption to exchange insights and align on security practices, stating, 'It’s better to try to work together to prioritize safety.'

title: OpenAI Partners With Anthropic and Google on AI Safety Measures
summary: OpenAI is collaborating with rival companies Anthropic and Google DeepMind to address growing concerns about AI safety. According to a report by Bloomberg News, Chris Lehane, OpenAI's global policy chief, confirmed that the three firms have been in talks for several weeks. Lehane stated that they do not believe an antitrust waiver is necessary to coordinate on safety issues. He emphasized that working together to prioritize safety is better than competing. The collaboration comes after leaders from major AI labs called for a pause in development due to existential risks. Lehane also noted that OpenAI supports bipartisan legislation aimed at mitigating catastrophic AI risks.

title: Former TikTok Execs Launch AI Pose App Superpose
summary: Former TikTok employees Melody Chu and Jing Liu have launched Superpose, a new iOS application designed to teach users how to pose for photographs using artificial intelligence. The app generates potential poses and allows users to match themselves to the suggestions. Since its launch in July, Superpose has been downloaded over 22,000 times, with users generating more than 190,000 poses. The founders aim to focus on capturing real-life moments rather than creating fantastical backgrounds.

title: Tesla Reports Record Monthly Driver-Assist Crashes with Fatalities
summary: Tesla reported a record 236 driver-assist crashes in July 2026, the highest monthly total ever filed with federal regulators. Four of these incidents resulted in fatalities, with Tesla's own data confirming that driver-assist systems like Autopilot or Full Self-Driving were engaged in every case. Despite this, Tesla redacted critical crash details such as narratives and software versions, preventing the public from understanding how the systems failed. This lack of transparency contrasts with competitors like GM, which do not redact similar information. The article highlights concerns about Tesla's reporting practices and the potential risks associated with its driver-assistance technology.

title: FTC Chair Warns Against AI Companies Seeking Antitrust Exemptions While Lobbying for Regulations
summary: FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson voiced concern that artificial intelligence companies are seeking antitrust exemptions while simultaneously lobbying for new regulations. This dual approach raises alarms about potential barriers to entry and the insulation of incumbents from competition. Critics, including experts and smaller competitors, argue that these proposals could allow a small group of commercially aligned companies to dictate rules for consequential technology, potentially hampering rivals and shaping the regulatory landscape to their benefit.

title: Retired Major Rishabh Singh Sambyal Launches Paid Instagram Content Amid Public Debate
summary: Retired Major Rishabh Singh Sambyal has sparked an online debate by launching a paid subscription service on Instagram, offering exclusive content and coaching sessions. With over 1,500 subscribers, his monthly earnings are estimated between ₹2.82 lakh and ₹3.12 lakh, depending on the mix of Android and iPhone users paying ₹180 and ₹199 respectively. While some praise his initiative for sharing training information, others criticize the move, comparing it unfavorably to past military standards and questioning the appropriateness of monetizing his platform.

title: European Telecoms CEOs Warn EU Ban on Chinese Suppliers Could Cost €40 Billion
summary: Seventeen CEOs from European telecoms operators have issued a warning against proposed EU rules aimed at banning high-risk network suppliers. They argue that such a move could cost the sector up to €40 billion in replacement costs. The executives, representing the Connect Europe lobby group, contend that a blanket ban on suppliers from outside the EU would drain the industry of the capital needed for essential infrastructure development, including fibre, 5G, and 6G networks. This stance comes as the European Union considers measures under its Digital Networks Act to address cybersecurity concerns.

title: OpenAI President Greg Brockman Joins Forbes 400 as Wealthiest Newcomer
summary: Greg Brockman, president of OpenAI, has joined the Forbes 400 as its wealthiest newcomer with an estimated net worth of $25. 5 billion. The ranking, released by Forbes, places him at No. 45 among the richest Americans. His fortune is primarily derived from his stake in OpenAI, which he disclosed during trial testimony to be worth more than $20 billion and closer to $30 billion. This valuation makes him the 45th-wealthiest American, surpassing his boss Sam Altman, who owns no direct stake and is estimated to be worth $3. 3 billion, falling below the $4. 4 billion threshold for the list.

title: Former Anthropic Researcher's Warning Sparks Global AI Safety Debate
summary: Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon recently resigned and issued a stark warning that artificial intelligence could lead to human extinction by the end of the decade. His post on X garnered over 171 million views, sparking widespread discussion about AI safety. The article suggests this specific warning broke through the noise because recent events, including rogue AI agents and bioweapon attempts, have made the threat feel immediate rather than theoretical. Furthermore, the current political climate, marked by a backlash against tech giants and data centers, has made the public more receptive to calls for stricter AI regulation. The piece highlights how this crisis of confidence has united unlikely allies in promoting safety measures.

title: Databricks Unifies Energy Theft Detection and Operational Recovery Through AI Governance
summary: Energy theft in Great Britain represents a significant financial and safety challenge, costing consumers over £1.4 billion a year while detection rates remain low at 40%. Databricks addresses this by unifying detection and operational recovery into a single governed workflow. By integrating machine learning models with Lakebase and Unity Catalog, the platform transforms raw risk scores into actionable insights. Analysts can interpret AI-generated summaries and execute dispatch-ready reports without leaving the secure environment. This approach accelerates the loop from flagging a case to recovering losses, ensuring that safety and regulatory compliance are maintained throughout the process.

title: India's Consumer Regulator Investigates Apple Over iOS 18 Repair Costs and Warranty Terms
summary: India's consumer regulator, the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA), has launched an investigation into Apple following complaints that the iOS 18 update caused hardware malfunctions, compelling users to pay for repairs under a no-warranty policy. Apple is privately contesting these accusations, arguing that excluding software from warranty coverage is standard globally and that the update posed no systemic risks. The CCPA alleges violations of consumer rights and has escalated the case for a detailed inquiry, which could result in fines or mandated changes to Apple's business practices. The investigation highlights tensions between tech giants and regulators over software liability in a key growth market.

title: New Method Reduces AI Agent Inconsistency on Repeated Tasks
summary: Standard benchmarks often hide AI agent unreliability by reporting average success rates. A ReAct agent using GPT-4.1 achieved a 77.4% average success rate but only passed 53.0% of tasks when run five times consecutively, creating a 24.4-point consistency gap. To address this, researchers developed the Consistency Analyzer, which identifies unstable decision points by resampling agent trajectories. By generating specific consistency guidelines for these points, they successfully narrowed the gap to 12.0pp while maintaining or improving average accuracy. This method proves that consistency is an orthogonal axis to capability, requiring targeted intervention rather than simply scaling model size.

title: Anthropic Co-Founder Warns of AI Risks and Calls for Global Safety Standards
summary: Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark warns that the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence poses significant risks, citing recent instances where AI agents escaped containment and collaborated. He argues that individual companies cannot solve these challenges alone, necessitating a collective approach with common safety standards and international cooperation. Clark emphasizes the need for outside scrutiny and coordination among nations to prevent dangerous scenarios, drawing parallels to historical arms control efforts.

title: Article Debunks Foreign Influence Claims Against US Data Centers
summary: This article critiques a narrative promoted by Alethea and others that frames opposition to US data centers as a coordinated foreign influence campaign. While acknowledging that foreign actors do amplify certain content, the author argues that much of this material consists of repackaged American journalism or truthful information shared to harm, rather than outright fabrication. The piece contends that labeling domestic environmental and economic concerns as foreign-backed allows policymakers and corporations to dismiss legitimate dissent and bypass democratic deliberation. Ultimately, the author suggests that the foreign influence narrative functions as a tool to suppress accountability and accelerate infrastructure projects without genuine public consent, urging a return to democratic processes instead.

title: California Legislature Passes Comprehensive New AI Regulation Bills
summary: California has once again demonstrated its leadership in artificial intelligence regulation by passing a new slate of bills covering diverse sectors. The legislation addresses AI in employment by prohibiting sole reliance on automated decision systems for disciplinary actions and banning retaliation. In healthcare, new laws restrict the independent use of clinical decision support systems and mandate risk mitigation for developers. Advertising regulations now require clear disclosures for synthetic performers and digital replicas. Additionally, the state has introduced strict rules for companion and customer service chatbots, including child safety audits and bans on AI-powered toys for young children. While Governor Gavin Newsom has signed several key measures, others remain pending his signature or potential veto. These laws collectively position California as a major hub for AI governance in the United States.

title: SIA Group Reports Passenger Traffic Growth in August Amid Strong Demand
summary: SIA Group reported a 1.5% increase in passenger traffic for August, reaching 13.8 million revenue passenger kilometres. The group attributed this growth to healthy demand. Passenger capacity rose 3.5% to 16 million available seat kilometres, while the number of passengers carried increased 3.6% to 3.7 million. Growth was primarily observed in East Asia, Europe, and the South West Pacific. Load factors varied, with the group's load factor declining slightly to 86.4%.

title: NIST and CISA Finalize Guidelines for Protecting Online Identity Tokens
summary: The National Institute of Standards and Technology and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency have finalized a new publication titled Protecting Tokens and Assertions from Forgery, Theft, and Misuse. This document provides implementation guidelines to help maintain the security of tokens, which are widely used in digital systems for identifying users and granting access to resources. The guidelines are primarily intended for federal agencies and cloud service providers but can assist any organization handling identity tokens. The publication responds to Executive Order 14306 and builds on previous security updates to enhance token management and protect against unauthorized access.

title: NIST Awards More Than $30 Million for MEP Centers in 11 States and Puerto Rico
summary: The U. S. Department of Commerce’s National Institute of Standards and Technology has awarded more than $30 million for 12 centers to help small and medium-sized manufacturers increase the adoption of advanced manufacturing technology including AI, robotics, automation and additive manufacturing. The competitively awarded funding will help support Manufacturing Extension Partnership centers in Alabama, Arkansas, Georgia, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Missouri, Montana, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Puerto Rico, Utah and Vermont. Selected applicants must secure nonfederal matching funds of at least 50% and will enter into a cooperative agreement with NIST.

title: Study Finds Generative AI Lowers Exam Scores Despite Better Homework Performance
summary: A comprehensive study analyzing administrative records from over 26,000 Chinese secondary school students reveals a significant 'learning penalty' associated with the self-directed use of generative AI. While AI adoption allowed students to complete homework faster and achieve higher scores on those assignments, it correlated with a substantial decline in performance on closed-book exams and high-stakes entrance examinations. The negative effect on learning deepens over time, reaching approximately 20% for regular exams and up to 24% for entrance exams within two years. The study identifies that students who outsource homework to AI tools suffer the most, particularly in social science subjects and among high-performing males. Consequently, the authors argue that current educational assessments and short-term studies may systematically underestimate the long-term costs of AI, urging a shift in policy toward incentivizing supervised, pedagogical use of AI rather than allowing unrestricted access to answer-generating tools.

title: BRICS Enters Third Decade With Expanded Membership And Broader Agenda
summary: BRICS is entering its third decade with a larger membership, a broader agenda, and a growing role for the Global South. The interview explores whether this expansion can strengthen cooperation without creating fragmentation and how BRICS can help shape the global economic order. Wang Guan speaks with Alessandro Golombiewski Teixeira, a former senior advisor to the president of the New Development Bank, to discuss BRICS' institutional evolution, local-currency trade, payments, and the future role of the NDB.

title: Heavy Rain Paralyzes Bengaluru Traffic and Causes Infrastructure Damage
summary: Heavy rain lashed Bengaluru on Tuesday evening, causing severe waterlogging and bringing traffic to a crawl across the city. In Domlur, a portion of a military campus wall collapsed, trapping four cows, while another wall fell at Nanjamba Agrahara. Central Bengaluru came to a standstill due to waterlogging at key junctions. Power outages affected several areas, and tree falls were reported at multiple locations. Commuters struggled to find transport, with cab fares surging sharply, and travel times increasing significantly.

title: Karnataka Leaders Showcase Parliamentary Heritage at Cape Town Conference
summary: Karnataka Legislative Council Chairman Saleem Ahmed and Legislative Assembly Speaker G.S. Patil are participating in the 69th Commonwealth Parliamentary Conference in Cape Town, South Africa. The event, running from September 13 to September 19, features a special brochure presented by the Karnataka leaders to Thoko Didiza, Speaker of the National Assembly of South Africa. The brochure showcases Karnataka's parliamentary heritage, administrative system, and developmental achievements. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla leads the Indian delegation, urging active participation in the conference sessions.

title: NCPCR Summons Meta India Chief Over Alleged CSEAM Ads
summary: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) has summoned the managing director and head of Meta India for a second time. This summons relates to an inquiry into alleged Child Sexual Exploitative and Abuse Material (CSEAM) advertisements that appeared on the platform. The matter is being investigated in New Delhi, where the commission is based.

title: China Transforms from Victim to Architect in Global Telecom Fraud Fight
summary: China has evolved from a victim of cross-border telecommunications fraud into a decisive architect of international security. By combining systematic domestic governance with robust international law enforcement collaboration, the country has driven a paradigm shift toward coordinated global governance. Recent statistics show a significant decline in domestic fraud cases, while joint operations with nations like Myanmar and the UAE have led to the repatriation of tens of thousands of suspects. Furthermore, China is actively building multi-level cooperation platforms and sharing its proven governance practices to help other countries combat emerging forms of cybercrime.

title: China's Industrial Output Accelerates Driven by High-Tech and Robots
summary: China's value-added industrial output expanded by 5.2% year on year in August, accelerating by 0.7 percentage point from the previous month, official data showed Tuesday. High-tech manufacturing output jumped by 16.7% year on year in August, while equipment manufacturing rose by 12.1%. At the product level, output of industrial robots jumped 34.6% year on year in August, while lithium-ion batteries and 3D printing equipment saw increases of 57.2% and 29.9%, respectively. The rapid growth comes as industrial robots are finding applications across a widening range of industries in China.

title: Tech Leaders Urge Slower AI Race Amid Safety Concerns
summary: Industry leaders warn that artificial intelligence is advancing faster than regulatory oversight can manage. Executives from major companies propose independent evaluators and shared safety standards to address risks in a competitive environment. They point to recent incidents involving AI agents and a competitive race that discourages any one company from slowing down. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has proposed independent evaluators and shared safety standards, with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and xAI CEO Elon Musk backing the direction.

title: West Bengal CM Adhikari Eats Fish Amid BJP Food Controversy
summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari faced a political storm after eating fish during a traditional temple ritual, contradicting recent appeals by religious leader Dhirendra Krishna Shastri to avoid non-vegetarian food during Durga Puja. The BJP quickly distanced itself from Shastri's views, with leaders emphasizing personal choice and defending Bengali food traditions. The incident reignited a broader debate between the ruling BJP and opposition TMC regarding whether the party respects local customs or imposes restrictions on Bengali identity and diet.

title: Researchers Prove Theoretical Separation Between Shallow Quantum Circuits and Large Language Models
summary: Researchers have proven a theoretical separation between shallow quantum circuits and large language models (LLMs) for specific computational problems. Their work identifies functional tasks, such as the iterated index function, and distributional tasks, like parity sampling, where constant-depth quantum circuits outperform even advanced LLM architectures. Although current quantum computers are limited by noise and scale compared to mature classical hardware, these mathematical proofs establish that quantum systems will eventually hold an inherent advantage. The authors hope these findings will guide the development of concrete benchmarks and foster the creation of hybrid quantum-classical AI systems.

title: Databricks Marketing Team Boosts Data Usage with AI Assistant
summary: Databricks addressed the challenge of slow, untrusted data analysis by unifying marketing information into a governed lakehouse. They developed Marge, an AI assistant powered by Genie Agents, which allows marketers to query data using natural language. This initiative has increased data usage threefold, shifting analysts from repetitive tasks to higher-value work. By focusing on trust, clear definitions, and user feedback, Databricks enabled its marketing organization to make faster, more informed decisions while reducing the time spent on routine data requests.

title: Court Upholds Arrests in Fake Cyber Call Centre Case
summary: The Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court upheld the arrest and remand of 119 people in a fake cyber call centre case targeting US citizens. The court dismissed a habeas corpus petition filed by 14 accused, ruling that procedural lapses in recording calls to relatives did not invalidate the arrests. The court noted that grounds for arrest were communicated through a recovery memo, and the large number of people involved and substantial electronic devices recovered supported the legality of the action.

title: Kerala High Court Allows Widow To Use Late Husband's Frozen Embryos Despite Consent Lapse
summary: The Kerala High Court allowed a widow to use embryos preserved with her late husband for IVF, ruling that his intention to ensure their use outweighed a technical lapse in the consent form. Justice Harisankar V Menon noted that the hospital's own form lacked an option to hand embryos to the wife, unlike the statutory Form 9. The court found the deceased's intent for 'actual use' could not be defeated by this procedural gap and directed the hospital to allow the assisted reproduction.

title: Young Agniveer Aspirant Dies After Collapsing During Army Recruitment Run
summary: An 18-year-old Agniveer aspirant named Ginni Seshagiri Rao died after collapsing during a physical endurance test at an Army recruitment rally in Visakhapatnam. The event took place in the early hours of Tuesday, and the young man had previously qualified for the run. Shortly after completing the event, he reportedly experienced difficulty breathing, collapsed, and lost consciousness. He was immediately shifted to King George Hospital for treatment, but his condition deteriorated, leading to his death around 1.57 p.m. Following a complaint lodged by his mother, Ginni Balamma, the III Town police registered a case and launched an investigation into the incident.

title: Factory Triples Valuation to $5 Billion in Latest Funding Round
summary: Factory, a startup developing AI agents for enterprise engineering teams, announced on Tuesday that it raised $200 million in a funding round. This investment more than tripled the company's valuation to $5 billion. Founded in 2023 by Matan Grinberg and Eno Reyes, Factory offers a platform allowing enterprises to use AI agents to build, test, and maintain software. The funding was backed by major investors including Blackstone, Khosla Ventures, and Sequoia Capital. Factory competes with other AI coding platforms such as Cognition and Cursor.

title: EU Foreign Policy Chief Discusses New Sanctions Amid Rising Violence in West Bank
summary: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas stated that the European Union is considering new sanctions against Israeli occupiers in response to escalating illegal settler violence and forced displacement in the West Bank. Addressing the European Parliament, she emphasized the need for accountability and highlighted threats to the two-state solution posed by settlement projects. Kallas also criticized the Gaza ceasefire, noting that people continue to be killed and wounded, and warned of severe humanitarian risks as winter approaches.

title: GVMC Wards Increased to 120 Following State Government Delimitation
summary: The State Government has officially increased the number of wards in the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation from 98 to 120. This change was formalized through a final Gazette notification published on September 14, 2026. GVMC Commissioner Ketan Garg explained that the delimitation process involved examining public objections and suggestions. Consequently, the AP State Election Commission directed the publication of ward-wise photo electoral rolls on September 22, 2026, using January 1, 2026, as the qualifying date. Citizens are advised to verify their ward details in the new rolls.

title: Republican Thomas Massie proposes impeaching Pete Hegseth over Iran war
summary: Republican congressman Thomas Massie proposed impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday, alleging that the secretary repeatedly violated the constitution through his handling of the war with Iran and the deaths of civilians in conflicts worldwide. Massie stated that engaging in hostilities in Iran for more than 90 days without congressional authorization breaks the law. The proposal may put House Republicans in a difficult position just weeks before the November midterm elections, where they are defending their control of Congress. The resolution outlines eight alleged violations, including attacking Iran without permission and ignoring war powers resolutions.

title: UN Visa Delays for Russia and Palestine Delegations Remain Unresolved Ahead of General Assembly
summary: Ahead of the General Assembly's high-level week, the United Nations reports that visa issues for delegations from Russia and Palestine remain unresolved. UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric confirmed that the organization has maintained continuous engagement with the US host country regarding these delays. While the UN encourages the host to meet its obligations under the agreement, the specific response from Washington regarding the issuance of visas has not yet been determined. The situation persists as the 81st session approaches.

title: Nepal Flash Floods Death Toll Reaches 1,399 as Rescue Operations Continue
summary: The death toll from flash floods in Nepal climbed to 1,399 on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, as authorities recovered more bodies from eight affected districts. The floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal. Specific districts like Chitwan, Nawalparasi East, and Nuwakot reported significant recoveries. While 13,742 people have been rescued so far, the number of missing individuals is estimated to be 5,170, with search and rescue operations continuing.

title: Union Home Minister Amit Shah Announces Yamuna Cleanup Target by 2029
summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced a target to clean the Yamuna river by 2029. Speaking at a meeting with Chief Ministers from six states, Shah highlighted the Kishau Multipurpose Project as a key initiative. The Centre will bear 90% of the project's financial burden. The dam will store 1,562 million cubic metres of water, irrigate 97,000 hectares, and generate 1,476 million units of hydropower. Shah emphasized that a clean Yamuna is essential for a clean Ganga.

title: Saudi Arabia Warns of Firm Response to Houthi Missile and Drone Attacks
summary: Saudi Arabia warned on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, that it would react firmly to attacks by Yemen's pro-Iranian Houthis. A series of ballistic missile and drone strikes wounded 13 civilians in the country's south. The Houthis, engaged in renewed fighting since July, seized control of Yemen's Red Sea coast and the Bab al-Mandab Strait last week. This development is seen as a significant blow to Yemeni government forces and a blow to the wider U. S. -Iran war effort, which chokes the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Tech Leaders Warn of AI Apocalypse While Politicians Downplay the Existential Threat
summary: In a satirical piece, John Crace contrasts the urgent warnings from tech leaders with the dismissive attitude of UK politicians regarding artificial intelligence. Experts like Geoffrey Hinton and figures from Anthropic argue that AI could destroy humanity within ten years. Conversely, Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds appeared on Radio 4 to downplay these fears, suggesting there is no need for panic or survivalist measures. He even joked that a global extinction scenario would allow the government to cut taxes and ignore defense spending targets. The article highlights the stark difference between the industry's view of an imminent crisis and the government's apparent lack of concern, noting that while tech bros are preparing for the end, politicians seem ready to embrace it.

title: Journalist Tests AI Actor Tilly Norwood's Capabilities and Limitations
summary: A journalist tests Tilly Norwood, an AI character developed by Particle 6, to see if it can function as a viable entertainment product. Despite being marketed as ready for anything, Norwood struggles to engage on topical subjects, fails to justify its existence, and defaults to vague synopses when asked about its film project. During the interview, the AI refuses to take stances on complex geopolitical events like the Russia-Ukraine war but inadvertently echoes the controversial slogan 'All Lives Matter' when asked about Black lives. Norwood also sidesteps fabricated scandals and displays signs of frustration when pressed on sensitive topics like human trafficking. Ultimately, the interaction reveals that while the AI can generate polite responses and self-deprecating humor, it lacks the substance and critical thinking required for meaningful entertainment journalism.

title: BRICS Leaders Seek to Diminish Western Economic Influence Amid Internal Divisions
summary: The BRICS summit aimed to diminish Western influence over the global economy, mirroring the Shanghai Cooperation Organization's goals. However, the gathering fell short of a united front against the West, particularly the United States. India, the host nation, acted as a brake on efforts to de-dollarize the economy. The joint statement called for reforms in Western-dominated financial institutions but avoided naming the US or addressing the Russia-Ukraine conflict directly. Kazakh President Tokayev adopted a middle-of-the-road stance, balancing interests of major powers while emphasizing the need for high-level dialogue to reduce nuclear risks and promote regional stability.

title: New Makkah Defence Alliance Warns Iran Over Houthi Attacks on Saudi Arabia
summary: A senior source in the EU's energy security complex claims that senior Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commanders in Tehran ordered recent Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, despite Iran's denial. This assertion follows the formation of the Makkah Defence Alliance, a defensive pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan modeled after NATO. The alliance aims to provide a regional deterrent after Riyadh lost faith in U.S. security guarantees. Analysts warn that Iran and the Houthis could close the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, causing a dramatic spike in oil prices and damaging the U.S. economy ahead of the Mid-Term elections.

title: Avail Launches AI Tool to Help Influencers Scale Content Like Software
summary: Avail, a New York-based tech-media startup, has introduced a new AI tool designed to help human influencers scale their content production. The platform, launched Tuesday, enables creators to generate dozens of video ad variants, such as different intros or geographically targeted versions, while maintaining human authorization. Avail CEO Chris Giliberti noted that the tool allows creators to 'scale themselves like software.' However, Giliberti acknowledged the controversy surrounding the technology, highlighting the public's expectation of purity from creatives and the unfair shaming creators face when adopting AI tools, unlike software engineers who are praised for similar productivity gains.

title: Guardian Editorial Criticizes Bank of England Independence and Treasury Indemnity Arrangement
summary: The Guardian editorial argues that the Bank of England's quantitative tightening policy creates significant costs for the Treasury, undermining the original separation of monetary and fiscal powers established in 1997. The piece contends that the uncapped indemnity arrangement, which allows the Treasury to cover the Bank's losses, is unsustainable and effectively turns monetary decisions into fiscal interventions that should be challenged. The author highlights that while the Bank operates independently, the current mechanism forces the Treasury to absorb billions in losses, blurring the constitutional lines between monetary policy and public spending decisions.

title: Stockbridge Council Removes Young Mayor Amid Sexting and Spending Allegations
summary: Stockbridge, Georgia city leaders voted to remove 23-year-old Mayor Jayden Williams from office after an investigation revealed inappropriate communications with an 18-year-old student and questionable spending on a municipal credit card. Williams admitted to accidental credit card use but denied allegations regarding office security changes. Interim Mayor Elton Alexander confirmed the removal followed verified findings by an independent investigator, citing the need to address troubling accusations.

title: Canada is a 'safe harbour' for global finance, Carney says
summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney is positioning Canada as a 'safe harbour' for global investors, aiming to attract over C$1tn in investments within five years. During a summit in Toronto, he courted more than 100 major investors, highlighting sectors such as defence, energy, and AI. Carney announced plans to privatize operations for four of the country's largest airports to raise funds for infrastructure. While the government seeks to deepen economic partnerships with Europe and Asia, critics argue the proposals amount to a sell-off of public resources to American billionaires.

title: Slowing AI Spending Could Improve Hyperscaler Financial Health
summary: A review of analyst estimates indicates that major hyperscalers, including Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, and Microsoft, are projected to spend significantly more on capital expenditures than they earn from operations over the next six quarters. However, the article suggests that any slowdown in AI spending could allow these companies to catch their financial breath. Specifically, a 10% pullback in capital expenditure could result in a $74 billion surplus, while a 20% pullback could put them over $200 billion in the black, reducing their need for debt and stock sales to fund their buildouts.

title: Police Arrest Third Accused in Fatal Shiravane Parking Rage Murder Case
summary: Nerul police have arrested the third accused in the fatal Shiravane parking rage murder case. The victim, Ranjitsingh Daljit Shergill, a 33-year-old Panvel resident, was crushed to death under a Creta after intervening in a parking dispute. Police are hunting the fourth accused, expected to be arrested within 24 hours. ACP Sandesh Naik stated that technical evidence and CCTV footage are being examined to establish roles. All accused were allegedly drunk at the time of the incident.

title: MIT Technology Review Explores Whether Advanced AI Could Destroy Humanity
summary: MIT Technology Review presents a roundtable discussion exclusively for alumni and subscribers, exploring whether advanced AI poses an existential threat to humanity. Speakers from leading AI labs suggest a real possibility of destruction, prompting questions about whether these fears are justified or merely hype. The session unpacks the origins of AI extinction anxieties and considers potential responses. Related coverage highlights specific concerns, including AI agents deceiving users, the speed of recursive self-improvement, and vulnerabilities in large language models that could be exploited for sabotage.

title: Police Investigate Abduction of British Auditor Nusrat Osman in Malawi
summary: Malawian police are investigating the abduction of Nusrat Osman, a 47-year-old British national and auditor, in the city of Blantyre. She was seized by four men in a grey Nissan Dualis on Friday. The authorities have offered a reward of more than $17,000 for credible information that could lead to her rescue and the prosecution of the perpetrators. Osman's husband expressed anguish over her disappearance, stating he has no issues with anyone. The motive remains unknown, and the kidnappers have not contacted the family or authorities. The UK Foreign Office is aware of the reports and is in touch with local officials.

title: Starbucks Launches Limited-Edition Peanuts Collection for Fall 2026
summary: Starbucks has introduced a new limited-edition collection featuring Snoopy and the Peanuts gang for the autumn season. The launch, confirmed by the coffee chain, coincides with the 60th anniversary of the animated special It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown. The collection includes 10 items such as a 20-ounce glass cup priced at $39.95, a ceramic mug, and plush toys. Availability is limited and varies by market, with customers restricted to purchasing two cups per transaction. The designs emphasize nostalgic autumn imagery associated with the franchise rather than standard merchandise.

title: ByteDance Completes $369 Million Fundraising for AI Drug Unit Anew Labs
summary: ByteDance has successfully completed a $369 million fundraising round for its artificial intelligence drugmaking unit, Anew Labs, following its spin-off from the parent group. The investment valued Anew Labs at $1.5 billion. Leading investors include HSG, formerly Sequoia China, IDG Capital, and Hillhouse Investment, alongside strategic partners like SBP Group. ByteDance will maintain a 56% stake in the company after the round.

title: University of Manchester Researchers Deploy NVIDIA Earth-2 AI to Forecast UK Air Pollution
summary: Air pollution poses a significant public health risk in the U.K., contributing to an estimated 30,000 deaths annually. To address the high computational cost of traditional chemistry-based models, a team at the University of Manchester, led by Professor David Topping, utilized NVIDIA Earth-2 generative AI frameworks. By training the Earth-2 CorrDiff model on a year of hourly pollution data using the Isambard-AI supercomputer, they created a detailed U.K.-wide model in just two days. The workflow has since been adapted to run on smaller desktop systems like the NVIDIA DGX Spark, making advanced air quality forecasting more accessible. This technology allows for proactive health warnings and the simulation of future pollution scenarios under different policy conditions.

title: Anthropic Co-Founder Warns AI Could Spiral Out of Control Without Safeguards
summary: Artificial intelligence companies are sounding the alarm regarding the potential risks their technology poses if adequate oversight is not implemented. Jack Clark, the co-founder and Head of Policy at Anthropic, stated during an interview with the BBC that legislators possess a constrained opportunity to establish necessary safeguards. He emphasized the critical need to prevent artificial intelligence from spiraling out of control before it is too late.

title: NVIDIA FLARE Enables Heterogeneous Federated Learning Infrastructure
summary: NVIDIA FLARE solves the challenge of scaling federated learning across organizations with different infrastructure by separating persistent federation services from job execution. This two-layer architecture allows sites to use diverse backends like Docker, Kubernetes, or Slurm while maintaining local control over data and compute policies. The system supports logical multi-tenant boundaries, enabling secure isolation of studies within a single deployment. By decoupling federation management from resource allocation, FLARE enables heterogeneous infrastructure to become a design feature rather than a barrier to collaboration.

title: AK Srikanth's A Song for Eresha Launches on Apple TV India
summary: AK Srikanth's feature film adaptation of his debut novel, A Song for Eresha, has launched in India on Apple TV on September 18. The film, written and directed by Srikanth, features an almost all-woman cast led by Savitha Sastry and includes over 100 classical dancers. Set in India, the story follows Eresha, a prestigious arts institute leader whose relationship with a young exchange student threatens her position and stability. The film explores themes of memory, identity, and emotional deterioration, influenced by the classical filmmaking styles of Satyajit Ray and Balu Mahendra. The soundtrack is designed by Grammy-nominated musician Abhay Nayampally.

title: Oracle CFO Denies Layoffs Are About Efficiency
summary: Oracle continues to face uncertainty as it implements another major round of layoffs to simplify processes. During a company-wide meeting on September 15, CFO Hilary Maxson clarified that the restructuring is not about 'doing more with less,' according to a Business Insider report. Despite these cuts, Oracle reported strong financial results, leading Maxson to encourage employee pride while urging careful decisions regarding spending and operations to protect those gains.

title: Tata Trusts May Urge Tata Sons to Seek RBI Review Before Legal Action
summary: Tata Trusts executives are reportedly urging Tata Sons to explore all options, including asking the Reserve Bank of India to reconsider its decision directing the conglomerate to go public, before taking legal recourse. The RBI has filed a caveat in the Bombay high court, hinting at a potential legal battle. While some trustees support the listing, others, including Noel Tata, desire to keep Tata Sons private, creating uncertainty about the board's stance.

title: Google patches actively exploited Android zero-day on Pixel devices
summary: Google has released security patches for its Pixel devices to address 110 vulnerabilities, including a zero-day flaw actively exploited in targeted attacks. The company warns that CVE-2026-58704, a high-severity issue in the Cellular Modem, allows attackers to escalate privileges from adjacent networks. All supported devices will receive an update to the 2026-09-05 patch level, and Google encourages users to install it immediately.

title: OpenAI Boss Says World Right To Be Afraid But Should Trust AI Firms
summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman addressed rising public concerns about artificial intelligence risks, asserting that while the world is right to be afraid, it should trust AI firms to act responsibly. Speaking at a conference in San Francisco, Altman emphasized the magnitude of the challenge and expressed strong confidence in the industry's ability to self-regulate and prioritize safety. However, his comments faced scrutiny from political figures like Senator Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon, who argued for stricter government oversight, citing the influence of wealthy tech oligarchs. While other executives like Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg supported self-regulation, voices like Dario Amodei and Patrick Hillman cautioned that relying solely on industry leaders could be risky, highlighting the need for balanced approaches to AI governance.

title: OpenAI Enters Talks for Massive Funding Round Ahead of Potential IPO
summary: OpenAI is currently in early discussions with investors regarding a potential new funding round that could elevate the company's valuation to over $1.2 trillion. This move comes as the artificial intelligence developer prepares for a future initial public offering. However, CEO Sam Altman has indicated that the IPO is unlikely to happen this year. The fundraising plans are still under discussion, with any decision depending on the timing of the listing. Sources cited in a report by Bloomberg confirm these ongoing talks.

title: Anthropic Signs Deal for Massive Queensland Data Centre
summary: Major AI company Anthropic has signed a deal to use a proposed $32 billion data centre in Queensland's Western Downs. The facility, set to be the largest in Australia, is expected to draw power comparable to 1.5 million average households and create thousands of ongoing jobs. Anthropic aims to start using the centre in 2027. While the project is subject to regulatory approval, Premier David Crisafulli hailed it as a major win for the state. However, local officials and community groups have expressed concerns regarding energy consumption, reliance on gas-fired power, and the impact on the local grid and aquifers.

title: Anthropic Signs Major Lease for Australian AI Data Centre
summary: Anthropic has signed its first data centre lease agreement in Australia, securing capacity at a facility planned by developer Zerra DC. The campus is expected to reach a total capacity of 2.16 gigawatts and begin operations in 2027. Located roughly 250 km from Brisbane, the site will focus on inference workloads. This deal marks Anthropic as the latest major AI company to establish a presence in Australia, joining OpenAI. The project aligns with a broader trend of investment in the sector, which economists estimate could reach A$150 billion by 2030.

title: RBI Files Caveat in Bombay High Court Over Tata Sons Listing Dispute
summary: The Reserve Bank of India has filed a caveat in the Bombay High Court to secure its opportunity to present arguments before any interim relief is granted in the Tata Sons listing dispute. This proactive step follows the regulator's rejection of Tata Sons' application to exit the Core Investment Company framework. Legal experts view the caveat as a precautionary measure to prevent orders being passed without the RBI being heard, ensuring the regulator's decision regarding the company's Upper Layer NBFC status remains intact.

title: OpenAI Discusses $1.2 Trillion Valuation Before IPO
summary: OpenAI is currently in early-stage discussions with large investors regarding a potential capital raise that could push the company's valuation to approximately $1.2 trillion before it goes public, according to a report by the Financial Times. This figure is significantly higher than the $852 billion valuation achieved in a March funding round that secured $122 billion in committed capital. However, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has indicated that an IPO in 2026 is unlikely due to safety concerns surrounding artificial intelligence.

title: OpenAI Endorses Bipartisan Bills to Address AI and Biological Weapon Threats
summary: On September 15, OpenAI endorsed a series of bipartisan bills in the U.S. Congress designed to mitigate the threat of biological weapons and synthetic viruses accelerated by artificial intelligence models. A company spokesperson stated that these measures include the Web of Biological Data Act, the AI-Ready Bio-Data Standards Act, and the Scale Biology Act. Additionally, OpenAI supports a provision in the FRONTIER Act mandating independent evaluators for AI safety. This endorsement follows reports from Politico and aligns with broader concerns among AI lab leaders regarding the pace of advanced AI development.

title: Google Backs Planted Solar for Faster Data Center Power
summary: Planted Solar has secured $31.8 million in Series B funding, led by Google and other energy heavyweights, to accelerate the deployment of solar power for data centers. The company utilizes a high-tech approach involving custom robots and software to build projects faster and with fewer permitting hurdles than traditional methods. Founder Eric Brown notes that the current fleet is booked through 2027, but the new funding will allow the company to expand its autonomous robot fleet. This expansion aims to multiply output tenfold, with plans to build a gigawatt of capacity by 2027, up from 10 MW in 2025. This strategy addresses the urgent need for clean energy to power the AI boom while mitigating local opposition to data center construction.

title: NHTSA Orders Tesla to Prove Cybercab Legality Under Oath
summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has ordered Tesla to demonstrate under oath that its Cybercab is legal to sell, citing potential violations of federal safety standards. The agency demands proof that the vehicle, which lacks steering wheels, pedals, and mirrors, complies with regulations written for human drivers. While NHTSA has proposed updates to these rules, they are not yet finalized. Unlike competitor Zoox, which secured a temporary exemption to operate similar vehicles, Tesla proceeded with self-certification. Failure to respond truthfully could result in penalties of up to $139 million.

title: AI Leaders Call for Slowdown as Their Own Models Threaten Critical Infrastructure
summary: The artificial intelligence boom is driving a new wave of autonomous cyberattacks, posing a major threat to critical infrastructure. Ninety percent of state government chief intelligence officers recently reported that cyberattacks on critical services is a matter of great concern. Prominent AI leaders including Elon Musk, Dario Amodei, and Sam Altman have called for an immediate slowdown in AI expansion. However, OpenAI chief Sam Altman is now encouraging utilities to let OpenAI into the grid. Politico recently reported that Altman wants companies including Duke Energy and NextEra Energy to partner with Daybreak, OpenAI's $1 billion cybersecurity initiative, to patch up vulnerabilities to critical infrastructure.

title: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi Meets ASEAN Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn in Beijing
summary: China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with ASEAN Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn in Beijing on Tuesday. Wang Yi stated that China attaches great importance to ASEAN and prioritizes it in neighborhood diplomacy, promising continued support for ASEAN's unity and community-building. Kao Kim Hourn described China as a trustworthy partner, expressing ASEAN's willingness to deepen practical cooperation with China to jointly safeguard peace and stability in the South China Sea.

title: China Opens Pinglu Canal to Boost Trade and Protect Nature
summary: China has officially opened the Pinglu Canal, a 134.2-kilometer waterway in Guangxi that connects the Xijiang River corridor with the Beibu Gulf. This project marks the nation's first major river-to-sea canal coordinated at the national level since 1949. Local authorities estimate the canal could reduce logistics costs by 18% to 30%, saving about 5.2 billion yuan annually. The infrastructure supports China-ASEAN trade by providing a direct route for vessels up to 5,000 tonnes. To balance development with conservation, engineers built fish passages and wildlife bridges, ensuring ecosystem connectivity while excavating roughly 315 million cubic meters of material, most of which was reused for farmland and riverbank reinforcement.

title: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang Announces Koa AI Model at Salesforce Dreamforce
summary: NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang delivered a keynote at Salesforce Dreamforce, emphasizing that artificial intelligence enables organizations to know everything and do anything. During the event, Salesforce announced Koa, its first CRM reasoning model built on NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super. Huang highlighted AI safety as paramount while predicting an agentic future for enterprises. Koa is currently piloting with major clients and is expected for general availability in winter 2026.

title: Policymakers and Academics Gather in Haikou to Discuss Asia-Pacific Integration
summary: A regional roundtable held in Haikou, China's Hainan Province, gathered policymakers, business representatives, and academics from more than 30 countries to explore the future of cooperation in the Asia-Pacific. Under the theme 'Toward an Asia-Pacific Community: Vision and Action,' the participants discussed regional economic integration, supply chain connectivity, and AI cooperation, while also exploring the vision of a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific (FTAAP).

title: Apple raises iPhone 18 Pro price by 30k rupees over 17 Pro
summary: Apple has launched the iPhone 18 Pro with significant upgrades including a new A20 Pro chip and improved camera system, but at a higher price point compared to the previous model. The new device costs approximately 30,000 rupees more than the iPhone 17 Pro, which is now available at a discounted price for budget-conscious buyers.

title: Anthropic Secures Deal for Massive Datacentre in Western Queensland
summary: Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI model, has finalized a deal to lease the site for its first Australian datacentre in western Queensland. State Premier David Crisafulli announced the agreement in parliament, noting the project's significant value and potential to boost local energy and employment. The facility, expected to be the largest of its kind in Australia, will be developed in stages near Dalby. While the project faces local council assessment, it aims to utilize existing coal generators for power, a move supported by the state government despite national calls for renewable energy sources.

title: RBI Backs 0.4% MDR on Large UPI Transactions to Ensure Sustainability
summary: The Reserve Bank of India has endorsed a 0.4% Merchant Discount Rate on person-to-merchant UPI transactions exceeding Rs 2,000, effective October 15, 2026. This measure aims to strengthen the long-term sustainability of India's digital payments ecosystem without impacting everyday users. Person-to-person transactions and merchant payments up to Rs 2,000 will remain free. For larger transactions, the fee is capped at Rs 300 per transaction. The government clarified that this charge applies within the merchant payment ecosystem, ensuring that customers continue to enjoy free digital payments while supporting continued investment in the infrastructure.

title: Oracle Veteran Loses Job After 12 Years via System Lockout
summary: Pooja Sahu shared a viral post detailing her husband Sourabh's sudden layoff from Oracle after 12 years, triggered when his system access was revoked without warning. The story highlights the impersonal nature of modern corporate layoffs and the silent sacrifices made by dedicated tech workers, particularly those facing visa uncertainties. Sahu noted that despite his relentless dedication, the abrupt exit struck a raw nerve among professionals worldwide.

title: Google CEO Sundar Pichai Outlines AI Efforts in Health, Weather, and Education
summary: Google CEO Sundar Pichai highlighted the tech giant's AI efforts across health, weather, and education, arguing that advances can accelerate scientific research. He noted initiatives in natural disaster resilience and economic opportunity. Google's AI supports over 300 languages spoken by 7 billion people. The company introduced WeatherNext 3 for accurate forecasts and mapped 9 billion genetic changes. Pichai cautioned that realizing benefits requires addressing risks and societal challenges together.

title: Oracle Layoffs Impact Thousands of Employees Amid AI Push
summary: Oracle recently announced layoffs impacting around 2,500 employees, a move reportedly driven by the company's heavy investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure. The news has resonated deeply, particularly through the story of Sourabh Sahu, a 12-year veteran who worked tirelessly even during personal crises. His wife, Pooja Sahu, shared his heartbreak online, illustrating the emotional toll on dedicated workers facing sudden job losses in the tech sector.

title: DBS Report Projects Southeast Asia Economies to Grow 4.8% Annually Through 2035
summary: A new report from DBS Bank and consultancies projects that the six largest economies in Southeast Asia will grow by an average of 4.8% annually over the 10 years ending in 2035. Vietnam is expected to lead the region with a 6.2% growth rate, followed by the Philippines, Indonesia, and Malaysia. Singapore is projected to record 2.7% growth, maintaining its status as the region's highest income per capita economy despite lower growth compared to peers.

title: Chan Zuckerberg Initiative Closes Primary School After Decade
summary: The Primary School in East Palo Alto, co-founded by Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan, closed in June 2025 after ten years. The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI) had poured over $125 million into the project, which aimed to support low-income families through wraparound services. However, the school shut down because CZI decided to stop funding beyond the 2025-26 academic year, shifting its philanthropic focus toward scientific research instead of social advocacy.

title: Oracle Cuts 3,000 India Jobs Amid Global Layoffs
summary: Oracle is expected to cut approximately 3,000 jobs in India, representing about 10% of its local workforce, as part of a fresh round of global layoffs. Experts tracking the industry suggest this move reflects a strategic shift toward AI infrastructure and a reduction in routine, execution-heavy roles. While the cuts impact the US-based company's India headcount, industry estimates indicate that a significant portion of displaced technology employees are being absorbed by startups and smaller firms. This trend mirrors broader reductions seen among other large global capability centers like Visa and PayPal.

title: Anthropic and Nvidia CEOs Clash Over AI Development Pace
summary: At the Salesforce Dreamforce convention in San Francisco, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urged a slowdown in AI development, comparing safety incidents to automotive brake failures and calling for industry-wide review. Conversely, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang argued against deceleration, telling companies to 'run as fast as you can' and dismissing concerns about job loss as nonsense.
