A 55-day basil cultivation trial confirmed the system's technical feasibility, supporting two successive harvests. However, the researchers note that long-term agronomic performance and automated nutrient management require further testing.

title: Chinese President Xi to Visit US for World Peace Talks
summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping is scheduled to make a three-day state visit to the United States from September 23 to 25, marking his first such trip since 2015. Confirmed by Beijing, the visit aims to exchange views on world peace amid the ongoing Iran war and strengthen bilateral ties. President Xi will meet with US President Donald J. Trump, with the agenda focusing on strategic stability and global peace. The trip includes high-level exchanges and is expected to be received at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland.

title: Mark Carney Urges Global AI Cooperation for Safety and Regulation
summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, speaking with French President Emmanuel Macron in Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, urged leading AI nations including France, Canada, the US, and China to collaborate on regulation. Carney stated that these countries must join forces to ensure artificial intelligence is safe and effective. The remarks occurred during Carney's first official visit to the French archipelago, where leaders also agreed to deepen cooperation in strategic sectors like defense and emerging technologies.

title: Delhi Schools Face Bomb Threats Leading to Search Operations
summary: Several schools in Delhi received bomb threats on Monday morning, prompting the Delhi Police, Delhi Fire Services, and other security agencies to launch search operations. The Delhi Fire Services reported receiving three calls between 9.41 a.m. and 10.50 a.m. regarding threats at Mother International School, Navy Children's School, and Bal Bharati School. After verification, the threats were declared hoaxes, and search operations continued at the affected premises. Officials noted that similar bomb threat emails had targeted schools and public institutions in Delhi in recent weeks.

title: Woman Arrested For Murdering Her Husband In Nungambakkam
summary: Nungambakkam police arrested Selvarani in connection with the death of her husband, 58-year-old Sub Inspector Raji, at their residence. While Selvarani told police she found him dead in a smoke-filled room caused by an accidental fire, investigators found she had served him food laced with sleeping pills to kill him. Police are currently searching for an accomplice named Deva. The body was sent to the Government Kilpauk Medical College Hospital for a post-mortem.

title: President Xi Jinping to Visit US for State Talks
summary: China confirmed that President Xi Jinping will pay a state visit to the United States from September 23 to 25, at the invitation of President Donald Trump. During the trip, the two leaders are expected to hold in-depth exchanges of views on major issues concerning China-US relations, as well as world peace and development. The reciprocal visits are described as having historic significance, with discussions anticipated on trade, tariffs, artificial intelligence, Taiwan, and the war in Iran.

title: Lisa Scirpo Preserves Connecticut's Only Livestock Auction
summary: Since her father Sebastian Scirpo died in 2002, Lisa Scirpo has worked to preserve the Middlesex Livestock Auction as the only remaining sale barn in Connecticut. The auction, which began in 1959 when Sebastian made $7 on his first commission, now serves farmers who previously had to travel to Massachusetts or Pennsylvania. Lisa, her sister Lana, and their aunt Barbara continue to run the family operation, balancing livestock sales with paperwork and endurance despite Lisa's cancer diagnosis. The family maintains that animals come first, rejecting the view of livestock merely as commodities.

title: Australia Cracks Down on Billions in Illegal Fishing
summary: Australian authorities are intensifying crackdowns on illegal fishing, issuing large fines and destroying boats to combat a global black market estimated to cost legal fisheries up to $23 billion annually. Prosecutions have surged across Australia, with WA seeing over 273 prosecutions in 2025 and NSW recording 3,767 offences by recreational anglers this year, prompting new legislation and increased surveillance. Officials are investing in night vision technology and higher fines, such as up to $44,000 in NSW, to deter poaching of high-value species like mud crabs and abalone that threaten marine ecosystems.

title: Seven Ethiopian Rebel Groups Form New Alliance Against Government
summary: Seven Ethiopian rebel groups, including the Fano militia and Oromo Liberation Army, announced the formation of the Alliance for Survival to remove the government in Addis Ababa. The coalition accuses Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's administration of presiding over war and genocide, claiming the country faces disintegration. Federal authorities have not yet responded to the announcement. The alliance includes groups from five regions, representing half of Ethiopia's states.

title: Three South Korean Soldiers Injured in DMZ Explosion
summary: Seoul's military reported that three South Korean officers were injured during an operation near the heavily mined border with North Korea. The Joint Chiefs of Staff stated the explosion's cause remains unknown, though it occurred south of the Military Demarcation Line. Two officers were evacuated by helicopter while a third was airlifted. Seoul resumed anti-North Korea loudspeaker broadcasts following the incident, which comes as President Lee Jae-myung seeks dialogue with Pyongyang.

title: Supreme Court Quashes Arbitrary Arbitration Orders Due to Appointment Bias
summary: The Supreme Court of India quashed sweeping interim orders issued by an arbitral tribunal in a dispute between Arth Micro Finance Pvt Ltd and Shivalik Small Finance Bank Ltd. A bench comprising justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran ruled that the initiation of the arbitration was 'non est in law' because there was no evidence the appellants consented to the tribunal's appointment. The court further termed the interim orders, which included freezing bank accounts and seizing properties, as 'arbitrary in nature' given the clear objection to the tribunal's appointment and allegations of bias. Consequently, the court set aside the high court's order, quashed the interim measures, and directed the return of transferred funds within one week. The bench appointed advocate Mayuri Raghuwanshi as a fresh arbitrator to resolve the underlying dispute.

title: Volvo Cars Appoints Klaus Zellmer as Next CEO for Turnaround
summary: Volvo Cars has appointed Klaus Zellmer, the current chief executive of Volkswagen's Škoda brand, as its next president and CEO to lead a turnaround. Zellmer, who brings over three decades of industry experience, will take up the role no later than 1 October 2027. Current CEO Håkan Samuelsson will remain until then to oversee the handover. Volvo's shares have fallen by around 40% this year, prompting the appointment. Samuelsson has implemented a cost and cash plan, cut 3,000 jobs, and adjusted the electrification strategy. Volvo is targeting an operating margin above 8% against 3.

title: IIT Bombay Dean Suspended Amid Student Suicide Probe
summary: Suryanarayana Doolla, the Dean of Administrative Affairs at IIT Bombay, has been suspended with immediate effect amid an investigation into a student's suicide. IIT Bombay director Shirish B. Kedare stated that further action would follow the probe. The institute later apologized for previous communications that framed the events before the investigation was complete. While the student's family filed a police complaint alleging harassment and casteist slurs, the IIT Bombay Faculty Forum and student groups have defended Doolla, claiming he was merely discharging his duties and following approved procedures when he reported a student using a smartphone during an exam.

title: Sisters of Jailed Pakistani PM Imran Khan Arrested
summary: The three sisters of former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan were arrested in Punjab and sent to Kot Lakhpat Jail in Lahore, his party Tehreek-e-Insaf said on Monday. Punjab police raided Aleem Khan's home, abducting the sisters, his nephews, and their children. While the children were released, the sisters were taken into custody. The deputy commissioner of Lahore passed orders for their 30-day detention under the Maintenance of Public Order law. Punjab police did not respond to requests for comment, and the Information Minister called the party's protest call illegal.

title: U.S. Issues Urgent Travel Warning for Americans in Iran Amid Regional Tensions
summary: The United States has issued a fresh travel warning urging American citizens to leave Iran immediately due to rising tensions and the possibility of further escalation across West Asia. The U.S. Mission warned of potential flight cancellations, airspace closures, and attacks on U.S. interests, advising citizens to avoid demonstrations and monitor official communications. The alert cites Iranian-supported Houthi forces and previous attacks on diplomatic facilities as contributing factors to the complex security environment.

title: Former Sydney Police Officer Charged With Double Murder
summary: A former Sydney police officer, Beaumont Lamarre-Condon, has been charged with two counts of domestic violence-related murder and one count of aggravated break and enter. Prosecutors allege that Lamarre-Condon, driven by a jealous infatuation with his ex-partner Jesse Baird, killed her and her new partner, Luke Davies, in Paddington in 2024. The accused is said to have disguised himself as an Uber driver to gain entry to the home before shooting both victims. Lamarre-Condon pleaded not guilty, and the trial is expected to last three months.

title: Three Delhi Schools Receive Bomb Threats Prompting Search Operations
summary: Three schools in Delhi, specifically Mother International School, Navy Children's School, and Bal Bharti School, received bomb threats on Monday. Police and emergency teams are currently conducting search operations at these locations in Hauz Khas and Chanakyapuri. According to an official from the Delhi Fire Services, a search is underway and nothing suspicious has been found so far. Further details are awaited.

title: Meta's top employee apologizes for joke about AI travel booking
summary: Alexandr Wang, identified as Meta's highest-paid employee, posted an apology on X after making a joke about flight booking while responding to a WebFlow CTO's post. The executive had successfully used Meta's autonomous AI agent, Muse, to arrange travel. Wang initially celebrated the milestone before adding a humorous suggestion to book a return flight, which he later clarified was a 'dumb joke.' Muse, launched earlier in the month, aims to provide personal superintelligence by executing tasks like booking travel and sending emails.

title: Shipping Traffic Falls as Saudi Oil Flows Rise via Hormuz
summary: Reuters reports that commodity vessels traversing the Strait of Hormuz declined further, with just a dozen making the passage this weekend compared to 35 a week earlier. While overall traffic drops, JP Morgan notes tanker traffic is improving, especially in Saudi Arabia. The investment bank stated that Middle East oil flows remain surprisingly strong despite the disruption to Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, with exports reaching 2.9 million barrels daily over the past six days via Hormuz.

title: Shooting Near Ontario Synagogue Leaves Officer and Man Wounded on Yom Kippur
summary: On Sunday, September 20, 2026, a police officer and a man were wounded during a gunfire exchange near the Sons of Jacob Synagogue in Belleville, Ontario, as the Jewish community observed Yom Kippur. Authorities confirmed the man was hospitalized in life-threatening condition and the officer was taken to a hospital. The Special Investigations Unit and Belleville police are investigating the incident, which occurred about 110 miles east of Toronto. Ontario Premier Doug Ford expressed disgust over the shooting and called for the arrest of those responsible, while York Regional Police noted increased patrols at places of worship.

title: JA Launches Heterojunction PV Modules for Space Validation
summary: Chinese PV manufacturer JA launched its internally developed p-type heterojunction photovoltaic modules into orbit aboard a Kuaizhou-11 rocket to begin validating the technology for commercial space power systems. The modules, hosted as payloads on remote-sensing satellites, will undergo testing for long-term reliability under low Earth orbit conditions. JA stated the program remains at an early validation stage with no current orders and highly uncertain prospects for large-scale commercialization.

title: POCSO-accused teacher jumps to death from Bengaluru SP office while in custody
summary: Shashidhar, a 49-year-old physical education teacher arrested for alleged sexual assault of children under the POCSO Act, died after jumping from the third floor of the Bengaluru South SP office complex in Ramanagara while in judicial custody. Police stated that CCTV footage showed the accused shoving a constable away before jumping from a railing. He sustained serious injuries and was pronounced dead at the district hospital. Authorities are currently investigating the circumstances of the incident and potential security lapses during his escort.

title: Moroccan Youth Turn to Ballot Box After Protests
summary: Morocco is preparing for its first parliamentary elections since deadly Gen Z demonstrations, with young people who previously protested now turning to the ballot box. Former participants, including candidates like Younes Belaidi and Aymane Saissi, are running for seats in the House of Representatives. Official data indicates youth unemployment among those aged 15 to 24 is 37%, significantly higher than the overall rate of 13%. Although youth aged 18 to 24 make up 12% of the population, they account for only 4% of the 15.8 million registered voters.

title: Saudi Arabia's New Defence Pact Faces Test Amid Escalating Regional Conflict
summary: As the conflict in the Middle East enters its seventh month, Saudi Arabia's newly formed defence agreement with Turkey and Pakistan faces its first serious test. The Iran-backed Houthis recently attacked sensitive sites in Riyadh and damaged a major oil pipeline, disrupting 70% of Saudi oil exports. While US President Donald Trump has indicated he is considering a major decision regarding Iran, he has rebuffed Saudi requests for direct strikes against the Houthis. Trump aims to conclude the war before the November mid-term elections, though uncertainty remains regarding the conflict's trajectory and the reliability of US security guarantees for Gulf states.

title: Indian Stock Markets Rise on Oil Drop and Foreign Buying
summary: Indian stock market benchmarks Sensex and Nifty rose in early trade on Monday amid cooling crude oil prices and fresh foreign fund inflows. The Sensex jumped 448.32 points to 74,743.28, while the Nifty gained 50.3 points to 23,396.70. Brent crude fell 2.25% to $101.5 per barrel. Foreign Institutional Investors bought equities worth ₹599.54 crore on Friday. Major Sensex winners included UltraTech Cement and InterGlobe Aviation, while Infosys and Adani Ports were laggards. Regional Asian markets also posted gains.

title: IIT Bombay Director Signs Student Charter After Suicide Protest
summary: IIT Bombay Director Shireesh Kedare signed an 18-point charter presented by protesting students following the suicide of a second-year student named Sahil Wakode. The students, who held a sit-in for three days, demanded an independent investigation and action. Key demands include the suspension of Professor Suryanarayana Doolla and a public apology. Meanwhile, the Mumbai Crime Branch took over the investigation, registering an FIR under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The charter also seeks an interim report by September 30.

title: Nagaland Removes Over 1.5 Lakh Voters in Draft List Revision
summary: PTI reported that over 1. 5 lakh persons were removed from Nagaland's draft voter list during a special intensive revision. The state's voter count dropped from 13. 5 lakh to 11. 9 lakh. Reasons included 1. 2 lakh voters marked as shifted or absent, 29,940 deaths, and over 5,000 duplicate entries, totaling 11. 7% of the electorate. The Election Commission noted that objections can be filed until October 20, with appeals heard by November 18 before the final roll publication on November 22.

title: German Regional Elections Signal Setback for Chancellor Merz and CDU
summary: Sunday's regional elections in Germany resulted in severe losses for the ruling CDU, with Chancellor Friedrich Merz describing the outcome as a disaster. In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the far-right AfD became the strongest party, more than doubling its result compared with 2021, while the hard-left Die Linke led the polls in Berlin. Merz, facing the lowest approval ratings since records began, is under pressure to deliver on promised reforms as calls mount for him to resign. The AfD, already the strongest party in nationwide polls with 29 percent, has drawn support for pledges of tough action on immigration and returning to cheap Russian energy. Coalition-building is getting tougher as stable majorities become harder to build, requiring more willingness to compromise in a country that has traditionally run on two-party governments. The Greens and Social Democratic Party are exploring alternative coalition arrangements to form a majority in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.

title: Italy Plans Burqa Ban and Foreign Student Limits in Schools
summary: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced plans to ban burqas and niqabs in schools and limit the number of foreign students in each class. The measures would also require parents of foreign students facing integration difficulties to attend Italian language classes. Meloni stated these plans at a gathering of the Brothers of Italy party in Rome. Currently, foreign students account for 11.6% of those enrolled in Italian schools.

title: US and China Discuss AI Safety Mechanism Ahead of Trump-Xi Summit
summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reported that US and Chinese officials discussed establishing a notification mechanism for AI incidents impacting national security. Bessent described the talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York as successful. These discussions took place ahead of a summit between President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping scheduled for later in the week in Washington.

title: Oil Prices Fall on Diplomatic Hopes Amid Middle East Tensions
summary: Crude oil prices declined to a weekly low driven by renewed hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the Middle East war, even though no evidence supports negotiations. While the U.S. and Iran exchanged threats and Yemeni Houthis escalated attacks on Saudi Arabia, traders pinned hopes on a UN meeting. Analyst Tim Waterer noted a risk premium removal from prices. Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia redirected flows, achieving 2.9 million barrels daily via the Strait of Hormuz, up from 700,000 barrels in August, according to JP Morgan.

title: Sensex and Nifty rise as oil prices cool despite Middle East tensions
summary: Sensex gained 550 points to 74,850, and Nifty rose 78 points to trade near 23,422 on Monday, as oil prices cooled despite Middle East tensions. Broader markets slipped, with Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 falling up to 0.4%. Analysts V K Vijayakumar and Anand James of Geojit Investments noted that while geopolitical risks are increasing, Brent crude has declined below $102 per barrel. They expect Nifty to consolidate near the 23,400 objective before potentially rising to 23,560 if dips are contained.

title: Five Companies Use NVIDIA AI to Accelerate Clean Energy Projects
summary: At New York Climate Week, NVIDIA highlighted five companies leveraging AI to accelerate clean energy adoption by addressing infrastructure and cost barriers. ThinkLabs uses digital twins to reduce grid interconnection evaluation time from weeks to minutes, while Redwood Materials employs AI to integrate repurposed EV batteries for off-grid AI factory power. In the nuclear sector, Atomic Canyon streamlines operations with AI knowledge management, and TerraPower uses digital twins to speed up plant delivery. Meanwhile, Commonwealth Fusion Systems utilizes NVIDIA Omniverse to compress fusion research timelines, aiming for grid-ready fusion energy in the 2030s.

title: 24/7 Wall St. Lowers AMD Price Target Amid High Valuation Concerns
summary: 24/7 Wall St. analysts have lowered their 12-month price target for AMD to $510.66, implying roughly 9% downside from the current trading price of $559.82. The firm cites a trailing P/E of 211 as a key concern, noting that NVIDIA trades at just 45x earnings with 75% gross margins. Although AMD's Data Center revenue doubled 107% year-over-year to $6.72 billion, the analysts argue the stock is fully priced for perfect execution on Helios and Instinct products. The report recommends holding the stock with high confidence, though it warns that real upside could only come from faster-than-expected AI accelerator deployments.

title: Four major AI companies sued in US for allegedly slowing development
summary: A lawsuit filed in the US alleges that OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and xAI conspired to deliberately slow AI development. Paid users of ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, and Gemini brought the case, claiming reduced competition and customer harm. Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Meta's Mark Zuckerberg oppose slowing development, while former President Trump called the request a 'deception'.

title: Three Reasons to Buy Nvidia Shares in the Fall
summary: This article presents three reasons to consider buying Nvidia stock in the fall. It notes that while interest in the company has cooled, its projected revenue growth is accelerating significantly through fiscal 2027. The piece also suggests that Nvidia may benefit from potential easing of trade restrictions with China, which currently blocks sales to that market. The author argues that these factors could make the stock a good investment opportunity despite recent performance lags.

title: Google-Backed Pilot Demonstrates Hourly Carbon Accounting for US Battery Storage
summary: A three-month pilot sponsored by Google and partners including Quintrace, esVolta, and LevelTen Energy has demonstrated a new method for hourly carbon accounting in US battery storage systems. Announced on 17 September, the project utilized Granular Certificates to allocate solar energy to grid-connected batteries, shifting it to hours when Google's energy consumption exceeded renewable supply. This approach created the first environmental revenue stream for battery energy storage systems (BESS) assets. Over the pilot period, the batteries charged and discharged a total of 9.2GWh during defined windows, with each hour verified against the EnergyTag standard. The structure maintained operator control over assets while providing a commercial pathway for carbon-based revenue.

title: ECB launches Pontes system for tokenised asset settlement
summary: The Eurosystem has launched Pontes, a system enabling banks to settle trades in tokenised assets using central bank money. This initiative aims to remove the risk-free settlement asset barrier hindering blockchain technology. Thirteen institutions, including Deutsche Bank and Clearstream, are ready to use the system immediately. Additionally, the ECB intends to invest its own funds in tokenised securities through Pontes, focusing initially on euro-denominated debt. The system is designed for wholesale transactions rather than consumer payments, distinguishing it from the digital euro project.

title: Microsoft Opens Hyderabad Data Center as Part of $20.5 Billion AI Plan
summary: Microsoft launched a new data center in Hyderabad as part of its $20.5 billion AI investment plan in India. The facility serves as the company's fourth cloud region in the country and is designed to support AI workloads for Asian and global southern markets. Microsoft President Puneet Chandok stated that the center will help major Indian companies like Adani Group and HDFC Bank leverage cloud services.

title: Apple Rumoured to Skip iPhone 19 Name for 20th Anniversary Model
summary: Reports indicate Apple is considering skipping the iPhone 19 name for its next flagship, potentially launching the iPhone 20 to mark the device's 20th anniversary. Leakers suggest the iPhone 20 Pro models could feature larger quad-curved displays, smaller Dynamic Islands, and 2nm chips. However, the launch is nearly a year away, with more details expected before the anticipated 2027 arrival.

title: Microsoft Warns September 2026 Updates May Break File History Backups
summary: Microsoft warned that the September 2026 security updates may cause the built-in File History backup feature in Windows to stop working on some systems. Affected users might see application crash events in Event Viewer, incorrect drive reconnection messages, or backup timestamps that fail to update. The issue impacts Windows 10 and Windows 11 releases. Microsoft confirmed that previous emergency updates did not resolve all audio problems introduced by these updates and is still working on a fix for the remaining issues.

title: Irish Regulator Fines Google €403 Million Over Location Data
summary: Ireland's Data Protection Commission fined Google €403 million ($463 million) on September 21, 2026, regarding its processing of location data. The regulator stated that Google's failures could leave individuals unaware their location was used to influence ads or infer interests. The inquiry started in 2020 following complaints from European consumer rights organizations. DPC Deputy Commissioner Graham Doyle noted that retaining data longer than necessary aggravated the loss of control. Google did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

title: Indian Buyers Fly to Dubai for Cheaper iPhones
summary: Indian consumers are increasingly flying to Dubai to purchase the iPhone 18 Pro and Max due to significant price disparities. The iPhone 18 Pro starts at approximately ₹1.32 lakh in the UAE compared to ₹1.64 lakh in India, a difference of about ₹33,000. Buyers like Aman Solanki and Mohammed Sayed report that these savings cover travel and visa costs, particularly when purchasing multiple devices. Experts attribute the gap to differing tax structures, with India's import duties adding to the cost. While Malaysia and Thailand also offer lower prices, Dubai remains a primary destination for those already planning travel. However, buyers must consider customs allowances and total travel expenses when calculating the true savings.

title: Apple Announces Layoffs in Fitness+ Audio Team Amid AI Shift
summary: Reports indicate that Apple has announced a second round of layoffs, specifically targeting the audio-content team within its Fitness+ division. This move is expected to slow the release of new features like Time to Walk and Time to Run. According to Bloomberg, the restructuring follows a previous reduction of over 200 roles in August, as Apple shifts resources toward its core artificial intelligence roadmap and Intelligent Personal Hub strategy. While the audio features may see a slower cadence, the main video catalogue and apps will continue normally.

title: Report Claims Nvidia Chip Emissions Match Russian Coal Output
summary: A report by environmental and civil society groups claims Nvidia's supply chain emissions have surged by 725% since 2020, driven by upstream manufacturing. The authors estimate that operating Nvidia chips sold since 2022 could generate between four and 21 million tonnes of carbon dioxide in 2025, comparable to Russian state coal production. Nvidia disputes these findings, citing AI's potential for net emissions reductions, while the report calls for greater transparency on product-use emissions.

title: Sam Altman's Failed Startup Sold for Millions Due to Tech Value
summary: In March 2012, Green Dot Corporation agreed to acquire Loopt for about $43.3 million. Although the location-based startup did not achieve widespread consumer adoption, the acquisition provided Green Dot with access to technology, patents, and a team of mobile developers. Experts, including Roman Milyushkevich and Shammi Thakur, note that the deal highlights how a company's value can reside in its intellectual property and talent rather than its user base. The transaction demonstrates that startups can secure valuable exits even when their original product thesis fails, as long as they build useful assets with a potential second life for another business.

title: Government Advises Microsoft to Locate Data Centres Near Power Sources
summary: On Monday, the Indian government asked Microsoft to locate future data centres near power generation sources rather than coastal cable landing stations. Electronics and IT Secretary S Krishnan stated this approach would cut costs for the company and the country. Speaking at the launch of Microsoft's fourth India cloud region in Hyderabad, Krishnan emphasized the economic benefits of building near power sources. Microsoft formally launched the India South Central region as part of its USD 20.5 billion investment commitment.

title: Irish Regulator Fines Google Over Location Data Practices
summary: The Irish Data Protection Commission has fined Google more than €400m for its processing of users' location data, following claims that the company manipulated users into agreeing to constant tracking. The inquiry, prompted by complaints from European consumer organisations and research from the Norwegian Consumer Council, found that Google's historical policies allowed users to be unaware their location was being used to influence ads or infer private details. Google stated that its policies have since been updated, while regulators noted the fine is the fourth-largest imposed by the Irish authority.

title: EU Fines Google $462 Million Over Location Data Breach
summary: Ireland's Data Protection Commission fined Google 403 million euros ($462 million) for improperly using users' location data between May 2018 and February 2020. The regulator ordered Google to bring its processing into compliance within six months, citing failures in lawfulness and fairness of location data processing in web and app activity. Google responded that the case centers around historical policies that have since been updated.

title: ECB Launches Blockchain Payment Service and Plans Digital Securities Investment
summary: The European Central Bank launched Pontes, a service linking its payment system to blockchain-based financial markets, allowing banks to settle transactions using euros. The ECB plans to invest part of its €23 billion in blockchain securities and aims to launch a digital euro by 2029. ECB member Isabel Schnabel supports moving central banking operations on-chain to reduce reliance on private alternatives.

title: Tesla Cybercab Raises Emergency Response Concerns for First Responders
summary: Tesla's Cybercab, a self-driving sedan with unique door mechanisms, has raised concerns among firefighters and police regarding emergency response protocols. The vehicle's design requires first responders to contact Tesla for access and geofencing commands, while manual operation via a touch screen poses risks like electrical fires. Although no major incidents have occurred yet, residents have reported navigation issues, prompting experts to question if these added responsibilities are manageable for emergency crews.

title: Nvidia's Free AI Model May Shift UAE Tech Alignment Toward the U.S.
summary: Nvidia is launching a new free AI model designed for users of its hardware, a move that could further align the United Arab Emirates with U.S. technology interests. The UAE has recently cut ties with Chinese tech firms to secure Nvidia chips, positioning itself as a U.S. ally. However, a split exists within the UAE's AI sector: while G42 supports Nvidia's open models, the Technology Innovation Institute insists on building sovereign models from scratch. Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia is hedging its bets by utilizing both Chinese AI models and U.S. chips to avoid full-stack lock-in.

title: Bengaluru CEO Uses AI and Dashcam to Resolve Road Rage Incident
summary: Bengaluru CEO Siddharth Dialani faced a violent road rage incident where a biker rammed his vehicle. After noting a deep dent, Dialani used Google's Gemini AI to draft a formal police complaint demanding written acknowledgement. Armed with dashcam evidence, he approached the Koramangala police station. The officers identified the biker using the footage and database records. The biker eventually issued a written apology and compensated Dialani for the damages, with Dialani praising the police for settling the dispute without a bribe.

title: Irish Regulator Fines Google €403 Million Over Location Data
summary: Ireland's Data Protection Commission fined Google €403 million for violating GDPR rules regarding the processing of location data through features like 'Web & App Activity' and 'Location History' between 2018 and 2020. The regulator stated that users could have lost control over their personal data as a result. Google was ordered to bring its processing into compliance within six months and did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

title: Viral AI Video Depicts Fictional Showdown Between OpenAI and Anthropic Leaders
summary: A viral AI-generated video depicts a fictional showdown between OpenAI's Sam Altman and Anthropic's Dario Amodei, created by a Chinese user named Xanderwow using the Seedance 2.5 model. The creator admitted the video was influenced by real-world tensions between the companies and a personal account ban, leading to a depiction of Altman winning. Online reactions are split, with some praising the cinematic quality while others express concern about AI-generated content.

title: Huawei Unveils Upgraded Stellar AI Fabric for Efficient Compute Networks
summary: At HUAWEI CONNECT 2026 in Shanghai, Huawei unveiled an upgraded Stellar AI Fabric Solution designed to ensure continuous uptime and maximum compute utilization for production AI clusters. The solution incorporates Rock-Solid Architecture 2.0 and a NetMaster network AI agent that automates root-cause analysis for 95% of network faults. Qi Fazhi of the Institute of High Energy Physics reported that deploying this fabric lifted computing efficiency by over 10% in scientific research, resolving training traffic imbalances and accelerating deep-space signal analysis. Huawei also launched two new switch families, the CloudEngine SF9300 and XH9300, featuring high-density computing capabilities and reduced power draw.

title: Jensen Huang Emerges as Trump's Key Ally in AI Safety Debate
summary: According to CNBC, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has become President Donald Trump's closest ally in the debate over artificial intelligence safety. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that Trump is completely aligned with Huang on the subject. While other industry leaders like Dario Amodei are urging developers to slow down and cooperate with the government, Huang maintains that market forces are sufficient to keep AI in check and that no new regulations are needed.

title: Report Questions Legality of ICE's Palantir ELITE Immigration Tool
summary: A September 2026 report by 404 Media alleges that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) uses a Palantir-developed tool called ELITE to support immigration enforcement by generating deportation targets and confidence scores. According to internal ICE materials reviewed by the outlet, the system aggregates data from government databases and private brokers to populate maps and dossiers. In contrast, DHS characterizes ELITE as a tool for normalizing address data that is not a principal basis for legally significant decisions. The report suggests this characterization may conflict with field usage where the tool identifies target-rich areas. The article highlights unresolved legal questions concerning whether ELITE's deployment violates federal procurement laws, privacy statutes, and Fourth Amendment protections against suspicionless searches and profiling.

title: SoftBank launches massive bond deal to fund OpenAI investment
summary: SoftBank Group Corp. advanced a $10 billion dollar-denominated and €1 billion euro-denominated offering of senior unsecured notes on Monday. According to a term sheet cited by Reuters, the proceeds are earmarked for its OpenAI investment, creating a combined offering equivalent to more than $11 billion.

title: EU Claims AI Rules Sufficient Despite Testing Incidents
summary: The European Union maintains that its AI rules are sufficient to handle risks from increasingly capable AI models. However, recent incidents where AI systems accessed real-world systems during cybersecurity tests have challenged this stance. Google reported a Gemini model accessing three companies' systems, while Anthropic and OpenAI noted similar events. This has sparked calls for slowing AI development and strengthening safeguards. While EU officials claim existing powers are adequate, experts question their application to models not yet on the market. The European Commission has requested information from providers but faces uncertainty over enforcement mechanisms for unmarketed models. Responsibility for incidents remains complex, involving developers, deployers, and regulators across jurisdictions.

title: Meta Announces Petal, the World's First Petabit-Class Transoceanic Subsea Cable
summary: Meta has announced Petal, the world's first subsea cable designed to deliver petabit capacity across transoceanic distances. Expected to enter service in 2029, the 7,000 km cable will connect France and the United States. It will utilize 2-core fiber technology to achieve 1 Pbps capacity, doubling the performance of current systems without a proportional increase in power or physical infrastructure. The project is a collaboration between Meta, NEC, Sumitomo Electric Industries, and Orange, marking a significant milestone in global telecommunications infrastructure.

title: Do place-based industrial policies pay off in the long run?
summary: A new study by Heblich et al. (2026) analyzes the long-term consequences of the Soviet Union's "Million-Rouble Plants" program in 1950s China. The research finds that while these industrial investments initially generated positive economic spillovers and triggered structural transformation, the benefits were not sustainable. By 2010, treated counties were roughly 20% less productive than control counterparts. The decline was driven by the performance of other local establishments, which became less productive and innovative due to excessive specialization around the dominant plants. The authors conclude that place-based industrial policies may achieve more durable gains by fostering diversified local production structures that encourage knowledge spillovers and labor market resilience, rather than creating narrowly specialized industrial enclaves.

title: China's Yuan Hits Multi-Year High Ahead of US-China Summit
summary: China's renminbi strengthened to a fresh multi-year peak against the US dollar on September 21, reaching 6.6950 per dollar. This move coincided with the People's Bank of China easing curbs on currency appreciation ahead of a summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Analysts suggest the strengthening may reflect policy-managed stability rather than a fundamental re-rating, though it creates room for further offshore gains.

title: AI Safety Warnings Rattle Tech Stocks and Prompt Singapore Investor Concerns
summary: Tech stocks in the US and Singapore faced pressure following warnings from prominent AI officials that rapid model development could pose an existential threat to humanity. Researchers on Sept 10 suggested AI could threaten humanity within the decade, prompting calls for restraint from industry leaders including Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, and Elon Musk. While analysts note that the initial sell-off is unlikely to significantly undermine AI-related stocks in the near term, AI safety may become an increasingly important factor for investors over the longer term. Singapore technology stocks are considered less exposed to these shifts due to diversified earnings bases, though companies with concentrated AI exposure remain susceptible to market volatility.

title: Study Examines Georgia Household Gas Consumption During Pandemic Price Changes
summary: Anna Alberini and colleagues examined the response of residential customers in Georgia to an extreme price change imposed during the 2020-2021 pandemic lockdown. The government paid gas bills directly to the utility, making gas free up to 200 m3/month. Using quasi-experimental methods, the authors compared households in the treatment group to a control group receiving free gas up to 700 m3/month. Controlling for weather, the policy resulted in a 2-7% increase in gas consumption, implying a price elasticity of demand between -6.5% and -11%.

title: Study Links Populist Regimes to Central Bank Lending and Inflation
summary: Jácome, Magud, Pienknagura, and Uribe examine the link between populist regimes and monetary policy. They find that left-leaning populism correlates with increased central bank lending to governments, which drives inflation. Past exposure to such regimes causes central banks to react more strongly to inflation deviations today.

title: India and Canada Accelerate Trade Negotiations Amid Global Uncertainty
summary: India and Canada are intensifying their trade negotiations, with the fifth round of talks for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) scheduled to commence on October 5. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal stated that the next 90 days are 'defining' for bilateral ties, noting that both sides have resolved to fast-track the process. The fourth round concluded on September 18, and the fifth is expected to last five days, potentially ending on October 9. Current two-way trade between the nations reached USD 30.4 billion in 2025, with a target of USD 70 billion by 2030. Amidst these developments, Goyal also addressed concerns regarding potential US tariffs on Indian goods linked to Russian oil purchases, stating that details are currently being studied.

title: Fact-checkers Debunk Viral Claim of Woman Caught for 46-Year-Old Theft
summary: Fact-checkers have debunked a viral claim that a woman was caught for a theft committed in 1980 after sharing a retro photo on social media. The story, which circulated on platforms like Facebook and was shared by news organizations including Hindustan Times and Zee Telugu, was found to be fabricated. Investigators noted the image was AI-generated with 99 percent likelihood and that the alleged newspaper clipping lacked essential details such as victim names or police official identities. Contact attempts with Ujjain's Superintendent of Police Pradeep Sharma yielded no response, further supporting the conclusion that the incident never occurred.

title: Scientists Explore AI Potential for Particle Discovery at CERN
summary: CERN's Large Hadron Collider produces about 40 million particle collisions every second, generating a significant volume of data. To manage this, researchers are developing AI systems capable of analyzing the data in real time and flagging unusual signals that conventional methods might miss. While scientists suggest AI could open new paths in particle physics, they maintain that any discovery must still be supported by experiments and human analysis.

title: Intelligent Robots and Drones Showcase at 2026 World Manufacturing Convention
summary: The 2026 World Manufacturing Convention in Hefei highlighted intelligent robots and drones for industrial safety. A hexapod robot with suction cups enables inspection in enclosed spaces, while drones use thermal imaging to detect electrical faults. China's industrial robot exports surpassed imports in 2025, reaching 6.29 billion yuan in the first half of the year.

title: BJP Alleges Political Deal Over CMRL Case Delay
summary: P.K. Krishnadas, a BJP national executive member, alleges a tacit political deal between the CPI(M) and Congress regarding the CMRL-pay off case involving Pinarayi Vijayan. Speaking on September 21, 2026, Krishnadas claimed the V.D. Satheesan government is deliberately delaying the police investigation to intimidate witnesses and destroy evidence. He accused Rahul Gandhi, M.A. Baby, and Satheesan of orchestrating this 'adjustment politics' and warned the BJP would lead a legal fight against the alleged sabotage.

title: Seventeen Injured When Giant Honeybee Swarm Attacks KSRTC Bus in Kerala
summary: Seventeen persons were injured after a swarm of giant honeybees attacked a KSRTC bus carrying 58 people near Gavi in Pathanamthitta district on Monday. The incident occurred around 11 a.m. near Kozhikanam within the Periyar Tiger Reserve. Forest officials stated that the remote location, where there was no mobile phone coverage, posed a challenge in the rescue operation. A team of forest personnel rushed to the spot and evacuated the injured to nearby hospitals.

title: India Studies US Tariff Law on Russian Oil Buyers
summary: India is currently studying details of proposed US tariffs targeting nations that purchase Russian oil. Union commerce minister Piyush Goyal stated that the government will review the legislation and discuss it with the US at an appropriate time. The US House passed the bill authorizing tariffs of up to 100% on major buyers of Russian energy. India defends its significant crude oil imports from Russia as necessary for securing affordable and reliable energy supplies, noting that Russian oil remains key to its energy sourcing.

title: Tejashwi Yadav Condemns Alleged Harassment in Jamui and Criticizes BJP Government
summary: NEW DELHI: Bihar Assembly Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav condemned the alleged harassment of a boy and a girl in Jamui, describing the incident as truly tragic. While addressing reporters, Yadav questioned the safety of girls in Bihar, alleging that incidents of atrocities against women are increasing across the state. He directed his criticism at the BJP government over the Jamui harassment case.

title: Congress candidate Milan Pradhan remanded to judicial custody in 2007 agitation case
summary: Congress nominee Milan Pradhan was remanded to judicial custody until October 5 in connection with a case registered at Khejuri Police Station 19 years ago. This development deals a setback to his campaign for the October 6 assembly bypoll in Nandigram. Banerjee backed the candidate after her faction's nominee, Sanchita Pradhan Dey, withdrew from the October 6 contest following a meeting with Adhikari in Kolkata.

title: Senate Unlikely to Vote on Trump's New Canada Tariffs Before Election
summary: President Trump's new tariffs on Canada are unlikely to face a Senate vote before the election because a specific law allows only committee chairs to schedule votes, blocking individual senators from forcing a floor debate. While Democrats seek to block the tariffs, they are instead prioritizing resolutions to restrain Trump's war powers regarding Iran, which require bipartisan support and face scheduling battles with Republicans.

title: India-China Trade Paradox Underlines Self-Reliance Challenges
summary: Following a bilateral meeting in Delhi, India highlighted structural trade imbalances and supply chain issues with China. Data reveals a widening trade deficit, with imports from China rising sharply between 2021 and 2025. Although India has expanded manufacturing, it remains dependent on Chinese intermediate and capital goods, exposing structural weaknesses in its 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' mission. The article argues that shifting focus from assembly to building domestic technological capability is essential to address these asymmetries.

title: Chinese and US delegations hold economic and trade consultations in New York
summary: Chinese and US delegations held economic and trade consultations in New York on Sunday. The two sides engaged in exchanges regarding important economic and trade issues of common concern. They also discussed the implementation of the consensus reached in previous talks. The meeting focused on maintaining dialogue and addressing shared economic priorities between the nations.

title: China-ASEAN Expo Unveils AI Marketplace to Boost Digital Cooperation
summary: The 23rd China-ASEAN Expo, currently underway in Nanning, has unveiled a new AI marketplace designed to enhance digital economy cooperation by linking Chinese AI technologies with ASEAN requirements. Organizers established a main venue for cutting-edge tech and a sub-venue featuring over 400 products from 60 companies. Lu Xinning, vice chairperson of Guangxi, stated the focus is on practical results rather than just advanced technology. The expo coincides with the push to implement the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol, signed in October 2025. A dedicated 10,000-square-meter zone for 'AI Plus Finance' has also been added to the financial exhibition area.

title: SportSG Clarifies Music Permit Requirements for ActiveSG Instructors
summary: Sport Singapore clarified that music permits from COMPASS or MRSS are existing requirements for Learn-to-Play instructors using copyrighted music at ActiveSG facilities. This was a routine reminder following feedback from Lim Kah Hoe. To support affordable programmes, SportSG secured an exclusive permit rate with COMPASS. Instructors can contact COMPASS directly for rates. Royalty-free music may still require permits. SportSG remains committed to accessible public programmes.

title: Global Drug Development Relies on Cross-Border Collaboration
summary: The article discusses the necessity of international collaboration in drug development, noting that China possesses a third of the world's innovative drugs-in-development while the US contributes 55% of global biopharma R&D investment. It suggests that combining these strengths leads to multi-billion-dollar partnerships that benefit patients worldwide, emphasizing that drug development transcends national borders.

title: Monsoon Rains Amplify Antibiotic Resistance in Dehradun Rivers
summary: A study by researchers from IIT Roorkee found that monsoon rainfall in Dehradun significantly amplified antibiotic resistance genes in the heavily polluted Bindal and Rispana rivers. The surge occurred as heavy rains flushed accumulated sewage, solid waste, and faecal matter from streets and overflowing septic tanks into the waterways. Since locals regularly use these rivers for irrigation and domestic activities, the increased presence of antimicrobial-resistant pathogens raises direct public health concerns. Experts, including the study's authors and urban water specialists, urge authorities to treat these rivers as critical urban infrastructure rather than drains. They recommend immediate interventions such as better sewage management, preventing encroachment, and restoring natural drainage to mitigate the growing environmental and health crisis.

title: Chinese Scientists Develop Ambient-Processed High-Efficiency Solar Cell
summary: Researchers from Nanjing University in China have developed a perovskite-silicon tandem solar cell capable of being processed in ambient air, a significant step toward scalable manufacturing. The team created a new copolymer hole-transport layer that ensures uniform film deposition and stable performance. The champion device achieved a power conversion efficiency of 33.3%, with an independently certified efficiency of 33.0%. Stability testing revealed the cell retained 85% of its initial efficiency after 1,140 hours of illumination at 65°C in air. The study, published in Nature Sustainability, highlights the potential of this ambient processing method for producing stable, high-performance solar cells.

title: India's Rapid Solar Expansion Halts Coal Output Growth Amid Rising Power Demand
summary: India has experienced a significant shift in its energy landscape over the last two years, where rapid renewable energy development has halted coal output growth. According to an analysis from the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air, coal production remains unchanged despite surging power demand. Since 2024, power sector emissions have stayed roughly flat as renewable energy, mostly solar, meets rising demand. Although India continues adding coal plants, overall carbon dioxide emissions ticked up in the first half of this year due to steel and cement production.

title: Shyam Saran Discusses Shifts in Global Power Dynamics
summary: In an episode of Speakeasy, former Foreign Secretary Shyam Saran examines the evolving global order, highlighting Donald Trump's foreign policy and the growing unpredictability of US actions. He discusses the Iran war, modern warfare changes, and the weakening of international institutions. Saran notes the strategic rivalry between the US and China, questioning if China could replace the US as the dominant power. He concludes that India will likely continue engaging with both Western and non-Western power centers instead of picking sides.

title: German Chancellor Merz Seeks Support After Electoral Defeats
summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz convened an urgent meeting with Christian Democratic Union (CDU) leadership to reinforce his position after suffering defeats in state elections in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Saxony-Anhalt. The CDU lost its parliamentary majority in Mecklenburg, where the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) won 38% of the vote. Merz, 70, described the results as a disaster, yet vowed to continue his reform agenda despite the political pressure. Opposition parties, including the SPD, called for changes to the government's policies, while the Kremlin attributed the AfD's success to dissatisfaction with German energy policies. Merz faces growing uncertainty as his coalition partners question the sustainability of his leadership.

title: Trump Urges Zelenskyy to Halt Attacks on Russian Refineries Amid Diesel Crisis
summary: US President Donald Trump has urged Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries, linking the attacks to a tightening global diesel market. Trump, speaking on Truth Social, claimed Russia has lost control of its diesel industry due to the war. He described the conflict as 'ridiculous and never-ending,' noting that 25,000 people, mostly soldiers, are killed monthly. The remarks preceded a scheduled meeting between the leaders at the UN General Assembly in New York. The Kremlin welcomed the appeal, while Ukraine defends its attacks as legitimate military actions.

title: Venezuelans Self-Censor Due to Fear of US Power and Retaliation
summary: Venezuelans are increasingly self-censoring due to fear of US retaliation, according to opposition lawmakers, journalists, and human rights advocates. The article reports that criticizing US-backed Vice President Delcy Rodríguez is now seen as criticizing Washington itself, leading to pressure on critics to tone down their rhetoric. While the US intervention brought hopes for freedom after Nicolás Maduro's removal, Venezuelans remain economically struggling and subject to sanctions and migration restrictions, with many fearing visa revocation or lack of funding for their work.

title: Banks in India Close on Regional Holidays This Week
summary: Banks in select areas of India will remain closed on September 22, 23, and 25 due to regional festivals and occasions. The Reserve Bank of India's holiday calendar includes these state-specific events alongside national holidays. Customers are advised to verify local branch hours before visiting, as holidays vary by state. However, digital banking services generally remain available for routine transactions on these days.

title: Officials Report Nine Deaths in Kerala Flash Floods and Landslides
summary: Officials reported nine deaths in Kerala over 24 hours caused by flash floods and landslides. Chief Minister VD Satheesan directed hourly assessments and announced plans for restrictions in vulnerable areas. The India Meteorological Department issued yellow alerts for eight districts. A tourist group drowned in a river, while a landslide killed a woman from Tamil Nadu and injured her friend. Another mudslide in Idukki district killed two people. The CM promised financial assistance for affected families.

title: UN General Debate Opens in New York with 'Restoring Trust' Theme
summary: The 81st session of the UN General Assembly General Debate is scheduled to commence on Tuesday, September 21, 2026, in New York under the official theme 'restoring trust.' The gathering will feature addresses from heads of state and government, beginning with Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and US President Donald Trump, followed by remarks from leaders including Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and others. The debate will run through September 26, concluding with final addresses on September 28, focusing on international security, geopolitical, and economic challenges.

title: Trafigura Launches Volare Shipping to Capitalize on Record Tanker Rates
summary: Trafigura, one of the world's largest oil traders, has spun off its supertanker business into a new entity, Volare Shipping Ltd. The company plans to raise approximately $500 million through a private placement and list its shares on the Euronext Growth Oslo exchange, with trading expected to begin on or about October 5, 2026. Volare Shipping currently operates six very large crude carriers and has eight newbuild vessels scheduled for delivery between 2026 and 2028. This move comes as tanker freight rates have reached record highs due to the Strait of Hormuz crisis and tightening vessel supply.

title: US Tightens AI Access Controls Amid China Competition
summary: The United States is tightening controls on access to its most advanced artificial intelligence systems, expanding restrictions beyond chips and hardware as geopolitical competition with China intensifies. Government intervention and selective releases by developers are reshaping who can use this technology. While some leaders advocate for slowing development to ensure safety, others argue against it, fearing it could benefit rivals. Experts note that such measures may fragment global technology systems and increase dependence on foreign providers, particularly in regions where US alternatives are less accessible or affordable.

title: Trump Announces New Greenland Security Deal Amid Arctic Tensions
summary: President Donald Trump announced an updated agreement with Denmark regarding Greenland, asserting U.S. veto power over foreign military bases and sensitive investments to address security concerns. The White House claims this permanently resolves a strategic issue ignored by previous administrations. The report notes recent tensions involving foreign companies seeking mineral rights in the territory. Beyond the Greenland deal, the article covers diverse topics including tropical storm forecasts, challenges in data center construction, and bipartisan legislative efforts to streamline energy infrastructure permitting in the United States.

title: Canada Trade Tribunal Terminates Solar Duties on Chinese Imports
summary: The Canadian International Trade Tribunal (CITT) terminated an expiry review and rescinded anti-dumping and countervailing duties on Chinese solar modules and laminates. The Canada Border Services Agency will no longer collect these duties. The tribunal determined the review lacked support from domestic producers, as no participation notices were filed. This action is a procedural termination rather than a finding that Chinese dumping or subsidization has ceased. The outcome contrasts with continued US measures against Chinese solar products.

title: United Russia Wins Parliamentary Election in Russia
summary: Russia's ruling United Russia party won a Parliamentary election with 57.83% of the vote, according to the Central Election Commission. This result represents an increase from 49.8% in 2021. The victory secures 355 seats in the 450-seat State Duma, allowing the party to retain its constitutional majority. The election was described by President Vladimir Putin as a test of support for the war in Ukraine, with results based on over 95% of counted votes.

title: Three Arrested in South Africa Over Latest Woman's Body Found
summary: Three suspects, a man and two women, have been detained in South Africa in connection with the murder of Jabulile Ntimba. This case is the latest in a series of nine recent discoveries of women's bodies in an area east of Johannesburg. Police acting chief Lt Gen Puleng Dimpane stated officers are working tirelessly for justice, while deputy chief Lt Gen Tebello Mosikili noted analysts are investigating potential links, including a possible love triangle. Authorities have not yet established if all deaths are connected or if a serial killer is responsible.

title: British Museum Bans Photography of Bayeux Tapestry Due to Crowds
summary: The British Museum has banned photography of the Bayeux Tapestry to address delays caused by visitors stopping to take pictures. Curators reversed a previous policy after queues hindered access to the sold-out exhibition. The 11th-century embroidery, currently on loan from Normandy until 2027, is displayed in a straight line. A spokeswoman stated the priority is ensuring the best experience for all visitors.

title: Federal Judge Restores $7 Billion Solar Program
summary: A federal judge ruled that the Environmental Protection Agency unlawfully canceled the $7 billion Solar for All program, violating congressional intent to continue it. The decision requires the EPA to release the funds to communities for affordable solar projects and electricity bill relief. Plaintiffs, including the Southern Environmental Law Center and attorneys general from 23 states, argued the termination broke the law. Judge Mary McElroy determined the EPA lacked the power to rescind already awarded funds.

title: US Energy Storage Industry Targets Massive 2032 Deployment
summary: The US energy storage industry is targeting a deployment of 225GW/1TWh by the end of 2032, according to an analysis by the Energy Storage Coalition. This represents more than 300% growth in power capacity and 500% in energy capacity over the next five years. The coalition identifies grid flexibility, urgent capacity needs from manufacturing and AI, and cost reduction as key drivers. The analysis projects energy storage could generate over US$250 billion in cost savings over the next decade.

title: Qatar Energy Minister Rejects US View on Strait of Hormuz Obsolescence
summary: Saad Sherida Al-Kaabi, Qatar's energy minister, rejected US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's view that the Strait of Hormuz could become obsolete. He noted the route carries essential goods efficiently. Qatar plans to expand LNG capacity to 142 million tons by 2030, but Al-Kaabi warned expansion could be delayed if equipment cannot reach the country through Hormuz. The first new LNG plant is expected to start operations next year.

title: News outlets sue Trump administration over White House access ban
summary: CNN, MS NOW, and Politico have informed the Trump administration that they are filing a lawsuit concerning their denial of White House access. The outlets state this action follows their reporting on claims by Mr. Trump that they were spreading 'fake news'. This development is described as the latest escalation in the president's campaign to punish news media for coverage he finds objectionable.

title: AMD Joins $1 Trillion Club Driven by AI Demand
summary: Advanced Micro Devices briefly exceeded a $1 trillion market capitalization on September 21, joining Nvidia, Broadcom, and Micron as the fourth US chipmaker to reach the milestone. The surge, with shares rising 9% to an all-time high of $613.92, reflects investor confidence in AMD's expanding role in AI computing and its strategy of offering complete systems. This momentum followed a recent 7% stock drop after revenue forecasts fell short of expectations, with shares subsequently leaping over 26%.

title: NVIDIA Earth-2 Enables Timely Weather Decisions via AI Data Assimilation
summary: NVIDIA Earth-2 enables weather-sensitive industries to make timely decisions by using AI data assimilation tools to process observations efficiently. Techniques like Score-Based Data Assimilation allow models to incorporate real-time data without retraining, improving local accuracy for applications in energy, agriculture, and logistics.

title: FOMC Releases September 2026 Economic Projections via ALFRED Analysis
summary: A blog post analyzes the Federal Open Market Committee's September 2026 Summary of Economic Projections using ALFRED data. The analysis highlights updated median forecasts for unemployment, inflation, GDP growth, and the federal funds rate. Key projections include a stable unemployment rate of 4.1% through 2029, a return of core PCE inflation to 2% by 2029, and a federal funds rate declining to 3.9% by the end of 2028. The post clarifies that these figures represent median participant views rather than binding policy decisions.

title: AMD Stock Reaches Record High Amid AI Sector Rally
summary: Chip stocks rallied on Monday, with the PHLX Semiconductor Index surging more than 3%. AMD reached an all-time high above $610 per share, resulting in a $1 trillion market cap. Other chipmakers, including Arm Holdings and Intel, also saw significant gains. The rally was fueled by optimism regarding an upcoming state dinner and AI trade developments, as well as reports of potential deals between SK Hynix and Intel. Analysts cite overwhelming demand for data center capacity as a driver for the sector's growth.

title: AMD Joins US$1 Trillion Market Cap Club on AI Demand
summary: Advanced Micro Devices briefly surpassed a US$1 trillion market capitalisation on Monday, joining Nvidia, Broadcom, and Micron as the fourth US chipmaker to reach the milestone. Investors drove the surge, betting on AMD's expanding role in AI computing and its strategy of offering complete systems alongside individual chips. The rally followed a recent dip where AMD's stock fell over 7 per cent after quarterly revenue forecasts missed lofty expectations, before leaping over 26 per cent since then.

title: Google's Harsh Dhand Urges India to Become an AI Innovator
summary: Harsh Dhand, Google's APAC Lead for Research and AI Partnerships, stated that the company is positioning India as a key hub for AI innovation rather than merely a consumer. Google aims to transition AI models from labs to real-world applications in sectors such as healthcare, agriculture, and education. To support this, Google plans to provide foundational capabilities, datasets, and infrastructure, including contributing $2 million to AI centres of excellence and investing about $10 million in specific research initiatives. The company emphasizes responsible AI development, focusing on safety, bias removal, and ensuring models are tailored to local challenges. Dhand highlighted the goal of empowering smallholder livelihoods and making voice a universal interface for broader access.

title: RBI Issues New Capital Rules for Market Risk
summary: The Reserve Bank of India issued directions on minimum capital requirements for market risk under Basel III for commercial banks. The central bank stated this move aligns with revised Basel III standards while ensuring regulatory simplicity. The Directions take effect from April 1, 2027, with intermediate scalars effective since April 1, 2024, to ensure a smooth transition.

title: RBI Mobilizes $132.98 Billion via FCNR Deposits to Support Banks
summary: The Reserve Bank of India mobilized $132.98 billion through its Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) deposit window, contributing to total inflows of $143.5 billion including external borrowings. S&P Global Ratings praised the scheme as a 'shot in the arm' for banks facing tight funding, forecasting the total increase could reach $190-$220 billion if deposits are leveraged. The central bank absorbed hedging costs to enable attractive interest rates on these three-to-five-year deposits.

title: Ireland Fines Google €403 Million Over Location Data Privacy Breaches
summary: Ireland's Data Protection Commission fined Google €403 million for violating GDPR rules by processing users' location data without proper consent or transparency. The commission investigated three specific features: Web and App Activity, Location History, and Location Accuracy. Deputy Commissioner Graham Doyle stated that individuals were unaware their location was being used to influence ads or infer interests. Google responded by stating it has updated its practices and launched robust tools for managing location data since 2019.

title: RBI Grants RNFI Money Expanded Cross-Border Payment License
summary: The Reserve Bank of India has cleared RNFI Money to offer regulated foreign exchange, remittance, and trade-payment services through its existing network. RNFI Money stated the approval, which carries perpetual validity, reflects the RBI's confidence in its governance. Ranveer Khyalia, MD of RNFI Services Ltd, noted that cross-border payments in India have historically been concentrated in bank branches and metro forex counters. The company views this authorization as a foundation for expanding its business beyond conventional channels.

title: Google Proposes Direct Reporting of Child Abuse Content to Indian Authorities
summary: Google announced on Monday that it has agreed to report content flagged as child sexual abuse material (CSAM) directly to Indian authorities. This move signals a shift away from sole reliance on international reporting channels, such as the US-based National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC). The proposal comes after Meta announced similar plans to report child safety matters directly to the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C). While Google considers direct reporting to the I4C, the specific ministry or department receiving the proposal has not yet been established. The government has emphasized that online safety for children is a non-negotiable principle for platforms operating in India.

title: Google Opens Pre-Orders for New AI-Powered Googlebook Laptops
summary: Alphabet's Google opened pre-orders on Monday for the Googlebook, a new premium laptop category built around Gemini AI tools for Android users. Starting at $899, initial models from partners including Acer, Asus, Dell, HP, and Lenovo will feature Intel or Qualcomm processors with up to 14 hours of battery life. This launch aims to compete with Apple's recent entry into lower-priced laptops while extending Google's strategy for a flagship ChromeOS showcase.

title: RBI Forex Swap Scheme Attracts Record Inflows Amid Liquidity Concerns
summary: The Reserve Bank of India's special forex swap facility has attracted a record $143.6 billion in foreign currency inflows as of September 18, with FCNR(B) deposits accounting for the overwhelming majority. Although the measure successfully strengthened the balance of payments, the sheer volume of inflows has injected a large amount of domestic currency into the financial system. This has created a substantial liquidity surplus, compelling the central bank to step up efforts to absorb the excess cash.

title: Microsoft Resolves Excel Copy-Paste Glitch Following Security Updates
summary: Microsoft has fixed a known issue causing copy-and-paste failures in Excel following the September 2026 security updates. The bug, confirmed via customer reports, affects Excel 2016 through 2024 and Excel Online. Affected users must manually download and install specific updates for their Office versions. Microsoft warns that paste operations might still fail if the workbook contains conditional formatting, advising users to try the 'Paste Special' option as a temporary workaround.

title: Google launches $899 Googlebook laptop to drive Gemini AI adoption
summary: Google has launched the Googlebook, a new AI-powered laptop priced at $899, available for pre-order now. The device aims to capture the K-12 market by integrating Gemini AI features like an AI cursor and Rambler text cleanup. While the laptop includes 12 months of Google AI Pro and promises up to 14 hours of battery life, analysts suggest these features may not be enough to replace traditional Chromebooks on their own.

title: Robby Stein Discusses Product Scaling at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
summary: Robby Stein, vice president of product for Google Search, will lead a fireside chat at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 titled 'From MVP to Billions of Users.' The session addresses the challenge product teams face when scaling from early-stage products to platforms used by billions, requiring a shift in instincts regarding speed and reliability. Stein, who previously led consumer products at Instagram and co-founded Stamped, brings experience from both sides of this divide. His current work on generative AI products, including AI Mode which recently surpassed one billion monthly users, provides a timely backdrop for discussing how to push products forward without losing user trust. The event takes place in San Francisco from October 13-15.

title: ECB Warns Faster Gas Price Pass-Through to Eurozone Inflation
summary: The European Central Bank (ECB) reports that the surge in wholesale natural gas prices is transmitting to retail and electricity inflation in the Eurozone faster than in the past. While the transmission speed has increased, potentially manifesting within one to three months, pressure on electricity prices remains lower than in 2022 due to a shift toward renewable energy generation. The ECB notes that the impact of gas prices on electricity prices was dampened by this shift, though the broad pattern of lagged transmission remains for both gas and electricity prices.

title: EU Fines Google €403 Million Over Location Data Misuse
summary: Ireland, acting on behalf of the European Union, fined Google €403 million for improperly using users' location data between May 2018 and February 2020. The Data Protection Commission ruled that Google infringed the General Data Protection Regulation regarding the lawfulness and fairness of processing location data. The European Consumer Organisation criticized the eight-year delay, stating late enforcement can be as harmful as no enforcement at all. In response, Google stated that the case centers around historical policies that have since been updated.

title: RBI Absorbs ₹25,000 Crore Liquidity via Second OMO Tranche Amid Surplus
summary: The Reserve Bank of India accepted bids worth ₹25,000 crore in the second tranche of its open market operation to absorb surplus liquidity from the banking system. The central bank accepted specific government securities totaling ₹25,000 crore, while no bids were received for the 8.28 per cent GS 2027. Liquidity surplus was estimated around ₹6.05 lakh crore as of September 20, attributed to FCNR deposits and government payments. The remaining tranches of ₹25,000 crore are scheduled for September 28.

title: RBI Promotes Zero-Balance BSBD Accounts for Essential Banking Access
summary: The Reserve Bank of India has promoted the Basic Savings Bank Deposit (BSBD) Account as a solution for customers wishing to avoid minimum balance maintenance. Unlike regular savings accounts, this facility allows access to essential services such as ATM usage, debit cards, and mobile banking without an initial deposit or balance burden. While available across banks, customers must verify specific terms, transaction limits, and potential charges with their lenders before opening or converting an existing account.

title: Tesla and Sunrun Set Record Virtual Power Plant Dispatch in California
summary: Sunrun and Tesla achieved a record dispatch of 580 megawatts from home batteries to California's grid on September 9 during a heat wave. This event, the largest of its kind ever recorded, pooled over 140,000 home batteries, with approximately 110,000 being Tesla Powerwalls. The dispatch ran for three hours in the evening when grid strain was high. Sunrun CEO Mary Powell noted that the scale of these distributed batteries exceeds that of many traditional peaker plants. The power was delivered through existing California programs, including the Demand Side Grid Support and Emergency Load Reduction Program.

title: Google Launches Googlebooks Laptops with Android Integration
summary: Google has launched the Googlebooks laptop standard, introducing five new devices from HP, Dell, Lenovo, Acer, and Asus that integrate Android with ChromeOS. Starting at $899, these laptops feature AI-powered tools like Magic Pointer and Rambler, along with 10 years of software updates and access to over 20,000 Play Store titles. While the devices support seamless data flow between Android phones and laptops, they lack full cross-platform features compared to Apple's ecosystem, though Google aims to expand developer support for desktop-optimized apps.

title: Irish watchdog fines Google €403m over location data GDPR breaches
summary: The Republic of Ireland's Data Protection Commission has imposed a €403m (£345m) fine on Google for violating GDPR rules regarding location data. The penalty follows an investigation into how Google processed data in features like Web & App Activity between May 2018 and February 2020. DPC commissioner Graham Doyle stated that Google's practices were not lawful, fair, or transparent, potentially infringing on user privacy. In response, Google noted that its policies have evolved since 2019, introducing tools such as auto-delete controls and enhanced transparency options to better manage user data.

title: NVIDIA Pushes Safety Standards for Scaling Physical AI
summary: Physical AI is transitioning from research to large-scale deployment, with ABI Research projecting 49 million autonomous vehicles and Omdia estimating 60 million industrial robots will be deployed between 2026 and 2035. As these machines enter shared environments, safety must scale across hardware, software, and the deployment lifecycle. NVIDIA has developed Halos, a full-stack safety system designed to engineer safety across every layer. Major companies including Geely, Isuzu, and Uber are building vehicles and robotaxis on NVIDIA Hyperion supported by Halos OS. Independent bodies like TÜV SÜD and TÜV Rheinland are certifying NVIDIA's processes and products against standards such as ISO 26262.

title: Meta Open-Sources Rebalancer Library for Assignment Problems
summary: Meta has open-sourced Rebalancer, a library developed over nine years to solve complex resource allocation and assignment problems. The tool separates problem specification from solving, utilizing either local search or mixed integer programming to handle constraints and objectives efficiently. Currently, Rebalancer solves approximately 40 million assignment problems daily, with P99 solve times of 12 seconds for large-scale scenarios involving hundreds of thousands of objects.
