AMD expects data centre sales to accelerate in the second half of 2026.

title: Amazon and Stanford Launch Joint Research Initiative for AI and Science
summary: Amazon and Stanford University launched the Stanford and Amazon Research Initiative to advance research at the frontiers of AI, energy, and healthcare. The collaboration formalizes a deep, established relationship where Amazon currently funds more than 10 teams and PhD fellowships at Stanford. By leveraging both institutions' strengths, the partnership aims to tackle harder problems, broaden participation, and shorten the path from breakthrough research to solutions that benefit society. The initiative includes joint research projects, fellowships, and symposia to foster interdisciplinary science.

title: Alibaba Unveils New AI Chip and Larger Model Amid Domestic Push
summary: Alibaba Group announced on Tuesday the development of an artificial intelligence model up to four times larger than its flagship system and unveiled a next-generation AI chip it called China's most powerful. The announcements at Alibaba Cloud's annual Apsara conference in Hangzhou underscore the Chinese technology giant's push to build out every layer of its AI business. The launch comes as Chinese technology companies race to develop domestic alternatives to Nvidia's AI processors amid tightening U.S. export curbs, sending shares up 5%.

title: Nomura Forecasts RBI Rate Hikes Amid Inflation Concerns
summary: According to Nomura, the Reserve Bank of India may raise the repo rate twice in 2026 as persistent inflation challenges policymakers despite resilient economic growth. Rob Subbaraman, Nomura’s Head of Global Macro Research, expects rate increases at the October and December Monetary Policy Committee meetings. While India’s GDP is forecast to expand 7 per cent in FY27, retail inflation could cross 6 per cent soon, strengthening the case for tighter monetary policy.

title: Quadra Achieves AWS MSP Competency After Independent Audit
summary: Quadra Systems announced on September 22, 2026, that it has achieved the AWS Managed Service Provider Competency following an independent audit. This designation recognizes the company's ability to manage cloud environments beyond initial construction, focusing on ongoing security, cost control, and performance optimization. The achievement marks Quadra's fourth AWS Competency, joining AI Services, Migration & Modernisation, and DevOps. The company highlights its proprietary Max-IT system and cites client engagements in healthcare and IT services where it maintained high uptime and reduced AWS spending. Quadra emphasizes that its single-firm approach prevents accountability gaps common when cloud projects are handed between multiple vendors.

title: Airtel Adds Apple Perks to ₹999 Family Plans
summary: Airtel has expanded its family postpaid plans, priced at ₹999 and above, by including Apple perks such as iCloud+, Apple TV, and Apple Arcade. This initiative is part of the telecom operator's broader strategy to focus on premiumisation and extract greater value from its customer base. The move aims to improve average revenue per user through differentiated plans and services, rather than implementing broad-based tariff increases.

title: MP Police Issue Strict Social Media and AI Usage Guidelines
summary: The Madhya Pradesh Police has issued strict 24-point social media guidelines aimed at separating official duties from personal online activity. Personnel are barred from uploading government or sensitive information to AI platforms such as ChatGPT and are prohibited from creating or posting Instagram Reels while in uniform or on duty. Violations may result in disciplinary actions, including show-cause notices or suspension. The rules, based on Union Home Ministry directions, also restrict the use of official resources for personal branding and caution officers against disclosing investigative details or expressing political views on personal accounts.

title: Techie's Viral Post on AI Coding Tools Sparks Debate
summary: An anonymous software engineer known as v0xium sparked a fierce online debate after describing his AI-driven workplace as a soul-sucking environment devoid of critical thinking. He revealed that his role revolves entirely around Claude Code, with employees working 12 to 13 hours a day merely to press enter. Venture capitalist Chamath Palihapitiya echoed these concerns, warning that companies are dangerously close to turning technical experts into people pushing buttons like casino slot machines. While v0xium acknowledged the utility of automation, he emphasized that the world needs new medicine and cures for diseases more than CRUD apps, arguing that developers need the space to solve complex problems.

title: British Columbia Sues OpenAI Over Tumbler Ridge School Shooting
summary: British Columbia has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman in San Francisco federal court, alleging the company failed to alert local law enforcement after its safety team flagged the shooter's violent conversations on ChatGPT. The suit, filed on Monday, seeks damages to fund recovery efforts following the February mass shooting at a school in Tumbler Ridge, which killed nine people. It also requests an order directing changes to how the company handles conversations that could lead to violence. OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri called the shooting an unspeakable tragedy and stated the company remains committed to working with government and law enforcement officials.

title: Adani Group Plans Major Power Investment in Assam
summary: Adani Group plans to invest ₹63,000 crore in Assam's power sector, including 2,700 MW of pumped storage capacity through Adani Green Energy Limited. The project aims to enhance grid flexibility and complement other investments like a thermal power plant. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma laid the foundation stone, with phased commissioning expected from December 2030. Total investments in Assam are projected to exceed ₹80,000 crore.

title: Meta's AI Agent Muse Gains Popularity Amid Privacy Concerns and Mixed Corporate Reactions
summary: Meta's new AI agent Muse quickly became a top app in the US, enabling tasks like email and shopping but requiring access to private accounts, raising security questions. Amazon blocked it over data access concerns, while Shopify partnered with Meta for checkout features. Reports suggest Muse may access sensitive financial data, and a macOS app vulnerability was identified. Meta claims user data is stored in a secure environment, but details remain unclear.

title: AI IPO Wealth Could Boost Global Development Funding
summary: As US overseas development assistance falls, a new wave of philanthropy from AI companies may fill the gap. Anthropic and OpenAI founders and employees have pledged substantial shares to charity, with estimates suggesting billions could reach global health and development by 2030. However, deployment faces bottlenecks like share liquidity and donor commitment. To access these funds, development actors must align with donor expectations for cost-effectiveness and rigorous evidence, adapting their strategies to compete for this emerging capital.

title: British Columbia Sues OpenAI Over ChatGPT Failure to Report Threats
summary: British Columbia has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI in a US federal court, alleging the company failed to notify authorities about concerning user interactions on ChatGPT prior to the Tumbler Ridge mass shooting. OpenAI's safety team had flagged the shooter's account for references to gun violence months before the attack, but the company did not alert local law enforcement. British Columbia attorney general Niki Sharma stated the lawsuit raises questions about technology companies' responsibilities when aware of credible threats. Sharma noted that any financial damages won would go toward rebuilding the secondary school.

title: Singapore's UOL in Talks to Acquire Hong Kong's Hyatt Regency
summary: Singapore's UOL Group is in talks to acquire Hong Kong's Hyatt Regency hotel from New World Development and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority. The potential transaction values the Kowloon property at around HK$3 billion (S$487.71 million). New World, heavily indebted due to a property slowdown, seeks to bolster liquidity. UOL and ADIA declined to comment, noting terms are subject to change.

title: ST Headstart Explores Signs of Micromanagement and Workplace Autonomy
summary: ST Headstart, a weekly newsletter from The Straits Times, examines the difference between standard supervision and micromanagement. It suggests that excessive updates and unexplained rewrites indicate a boss hovering like a helicopter parent. To regain autonomy, the publication shares an anecdote about Annabelle Liang, who spent three days at a silent retreat in Chiang Mai to disconnect from constant notifications.

title: RBI's Record Forex Reserves Create Liquidity and Future Outflow Concerns
summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has accumulated a record $785.7 billion in foreign exchange reserves, primarily by attracting $127 billion in foreign currency non-resident (FCNR(B)) deposits through a special swap window opened in June 2026. This initiative, designed to shore up the rupee amid turmoil from the West Asia war, has generated a surplus liquidity of over ₹11 lakh crore. To manage this excess, the central bank has stepped up efforts to absorb funds, including sovereign bond sales and reverse repo auctions, while inflation remains above its target. While the move successfully stabilized the currency, experts are divided on its necessity, with some viewing it as an unnecessary emergency measure given existing reserves. A significant future concern is the potential outflow of dollars when these deposits mature in three to five years, which could exert pressure on the forex market if external conditions remain unfavorable.

title: Google and Georgia Power Partner for Nuclear Plant Uprates
summary: Google and Georgia Power announced an agreement to support power uprates at Plant Vogtle and Plant Hatch, adding approximately 96 MW to Georgia's grid. The deal, pending approval by the Georgia Public Service Commission, involves extended power uprates for units at both plants. Georgia Power stated the agreement could generate about $900 million in benefits for customers over the life of the units. Google will subscribe to a new tariff to receive zero-emission credits associated with the carbon-free attributes of the nuclear energy.

title: Pinglu Canal May Reshape Trade Routes Between Southwest China and ASEAN
summary: The Pinglu Canal represents a new waterway project connecting southwest China to the Beibu Gulf. By establishing this route, the canal aims to reshape the movement of goods and business connections between southwest China and markets across ASEAN. The initiative is described as more than a major engineering project, potentially opening new possibilities for regional engagement.

title: California Sues Tesla Over Alleged Racial Discrimination at Fremont Plant
summary: Dozens of Black employees at Tesla's California flagship plant allege they faced daily racist slurs, unequal pay, and bullying by supervisors. These complaints form the basis of a lawsuit filed by the state of California, which seeks financial damages and injunctive relief to change labor practices. The trial, proceeding without a jury, features testimony from former employees describing a hostile environment and instances of unchecked discrimination. Tesla denies the allegations, calling the lawsuit misguided and stating it has always disciplined employees who engage in misconduct. The company highlights its majority-minority workforce and claims to offer top-paying jobs in the automotive industry.

title: HDFC Bank Shares Rise on RBI Review of Anup Bagchi for CEO Role
summary: HDFC Bank shares extended gains for a second consecutive session after reports indicated progress in the bank's search for a new CEO. The Reserve Bank of India is reviewing Anup Bagchi, currently MD and CEO of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, for the role. This move follows reports that Bagchi's candidacy was sought from the IRDAI and ICICI Bank CEO Sandeep Bakhshi. The leadership search gained urgency after current HDFC Bank CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan informed the board he would not seek another term, with his tenure ending on October 26. Brokerage Nomura retained its 'buy' rating, suggesting a clear leadership roadmap could support recovery.

title: Alibaba Plans Massive AI Model and Unveils New Chip
summary: Alibaba Group announced plans to train a new artificial intelligence model containing 5 trillion to 10 trillion parameters, according to Chief Executive Eddie Wu. Simultaneously, the company unveiled the Zhenwu V900 AI chip, stating it is the most powerful in China with three times the performance of its predecessor. Additionally, Alibaba aims for its global data centre capacity to surpass 20 GW by 2032.

title: Google agrees to report child abuse content directly to Indian authorities
summary: Google announced on September 22, 2026, that it will report child sexual abuse material directly to Indian authorities, breaking from a global practice of routing reports through a U.S. non-profit. This decision follows pressure from Indian government sources who argued the existing system delays reports in cases of active danger. The move mirrors a similar announcement by Meta and comes after years of friction between tech platforms and Indian officials regarding the speed of reporting.

title: Google Agrees to Report Child Abuse Content Directly to India
summary: Google announced it will report child sexual abuse material directly to Indian authorities, breaking from the global practice of routing such reports through a U.S. non-profit. This decision follows pressure from Indian government sources who argued the existing system delays reports when children are in active danger. A Google spokesperson stated the company invests significantly in detection and removal efforts. This shift mirrors a similar move by Meta, which recently apologized to the Indian government over content issues. Meanwhile, the U.S.-based National Center for Missing & Exploited Children received over 21.3 million reports globally in 2025.

title: Ron Johnson Skeptical of AI Replacing Physical Retail
summary: Ron Johnson, the man who built Apple's retail stores, argues that the industry is overestimating how much shopping people will hand over to AI agents. While acknowledging that AI will improve the online experience and help consumers become more informed before visiting stores, Johnson believes physical stores will continue to thrive. He states that buying a laptop is too personal to delegate to a machine, noting that buyers want to feel the weight and see the display. Johnson contrasts Apple's people-centric approach, where employees are not paid on commission, with his own failed attempt to reinvent J.C. Penney. Despite his skepticism about AI replacing human interaction in retail, he remains an optimist about the technology itself, believing there is no substitute for human intuition.

title: RBI Examines Anup Bagchi for HDFC Bank CEO Role Amid Tight Timeline
summary: The Reserve Bank of India is assessing Anup Bagchi, the managing director and CEO of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance, for the top job at HDFC Bank. Regulators are concerned about his absence from mainstream banking for three years and whether he can adapt quickly. HDFC Bank submitted two candidates, including Bagchi and Kaizad Bharucha, but the process is urgent as incumbent Sashidhar Jagdishan's term concludes on October 26. The bank has sought a tenure relaxation for Bharucha, but the RBI may prefer a candidate offering longer leadership continuity.

title: OpenAI Urges US to Lead Global AI Safety Coalition
summary: OpenAI called on the US to lead an international coalition for coordinating global AI standards as the UN General Assembly approaches. This request coincides with Washington's tentative outreach to China regarding AI development coordination. However, a Semafor columnist described such offers as symbolically limited given current geopolitical instability. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump has shown reluctance to shape domestic AI safety standards, aligning with industry supporters.

title: China and US Agree on Trade Consultations and Tariff Reductions
summary: Chinese and US teams held candid, in-depth, and constructive exchanges on economic and trade issues, including AI-related topics, during consultations in New York. Guided by consensus from heads of state, the two sides agreed to establish a consultation mechanism and implemented tariff reductions. The US committed to removing 91% of tariffs and suspending 24% of reciprocal tariffs for 90 days, while China agreed to remove 91% of counter tariffs and suspend 24% of counter tariffs for the same period. Both sides retained the remaining 10% in tariffs. Subsequent meetings in Geneva, London, Stockholm, Madrid, Kuala Lumpur, Paris, and Seoul further advanced cooperation on trade, investment, and specific issues like TikTok and fentanyl.

title: Nvidia-Backed Iambic Therapeutics Files for US IPO Amid Biotech Surge
summary: Iambic Therapeutics, a drug developer backed by Nvidia and Qatar's sovereign wealth fund, filed for a US IPO on September 21. This move supports a broader trend of biotech listings, which analysts say remain insulated from market uncertainties like rising bond yields. The company, founded in 2019, has raised roughly $461.8 million and is advancing AI-driven drug candidates for solid tumors. Major underwriters include J.P. Morgan and Citigroup.

title: Georgia Power Signs Deal With Google for Nuclear Upgrades
summary: Georgia Power announced a deal with Google to upgrade two nuclear plants, potentially adding 96 megawatts of capacity. Pending regulatory approval, the agreement funds modifications to equipment at the Vogtle and Hatch units. Google's subscription is projected to generate $900 million in benefits for customers. The upgrades allow reactors to produce more electricity from existing infrastructure, helping meet clean-energy goals while shielding non-participating customers from associated costs.

title: Chinese Diplomat Urges EU and Germany to Avoid Trade Conflict
summary: During a phone conversation, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi urged German counterpart Johann Wadephul to avoid a trade war, stating that the EU and China are comprehensive strategic partners. Wang emphasized that closer cooperation serves both nations' interests and advocated for dialogue to resolve concerns. The German Foreign Ministry noted that both sides agreed a stable global economy benefits China, Germany, and Europe, while discussions also covered situations in Iran, Ukraine, and Taiwan.

title: OpenAI Announces Independent Math Advisory Group Amidst Controversy
summary: OpenAI announced a new independent advisory group hosted at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton to provide mathematicians input into its research. While the group will assess results and coordinate releases, it will not control the pace of internal progress. This move follows claims that an internal model resolved more than 100 open math problems, a rapid pace that has drawn criticism from Fields Medal-winning mathematicians concerned about the impact on intellectual work.

title: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi Urges China-Germany Cooperation
summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi urged China and Germany to boost cooperation and free trade during a phone call with German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul. Wang highlighted the need to uphold multilateralism and reject protectionism, while Wadephul affirmed Germany's commitment to the one-China policy. Both sides agreed to resolve economic issues through dialogue and address global challenges together.

title: Textile Stocks Rally After Trump Tariff-Linked Selloff
summary: Textile stocks rallied significantly, with Raymond shares jumping 10% to a fresh 52-week high of Rs 1,193.40. This rebound follows a prior selloff where textile stocks fell up to 5% after the US signed the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which could impose tariffs on countries buying Russian oil. Meanwhile, India and New Zealand finalized a free trade agreement set to come into force on October 20. New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon stated that the deal will bring more opportunities for exporters and higher incomes for the country.

title: Pawan Kalyan Plans Pithapuram Camp Office to Strengthen Jana Sena
summary: Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan announced plans to shift his base to Pithapuram by the year-end to strengthen the Jana Sena Party. Speaking at a public meeting on September 22, 2026, he stated he would establish a camp office within three to four months. Kalyan emphasized that his physical presence is crucial for coordinating with elected representatives and addressing local needs, noting that previous efforts required persuading the Centre to execute ground work. He also expressed a desire to maintain a strong alliance with NDA partners while respecting the Jana Sena's dignity.

title: Jun Kim Joins Hugging Face to Support MLX Community Growth
summary: Jun Kim, the creator and maintainer of oMLX, has joined Hugging Face to support the MLX community. This transition from a side project to a fully maintained initiative allows Kim to better guide contributors and build for the long term. The team expects oMLX to serve as a testbed for new ideas while leveraging existing dependencies like mlx-lm and mlx-vlm. A primary focus is facilitating the quick transition from transformers model definitions to reference MLX implementations, enabling various engines to focus on their unique features. Kim confirms that oMLX remains under the Apache 2.0 license and he continues to lead the project.

title: SpaceXAI Launches Grok 4.7 with Larger Base Model and Updated Pricing
summary: SpaceXAI has released Grok 4.7, its latest flagship model designed for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work. Built on a larger base model and a longer reinforcement learning run, the model maintains the same pricing as Grok 4.6: $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens. Grok 4.7 shows improvements over its predecessor in benchmarks such as EEBench and Harvey's legal agent benchmark. It is available through the xAI API, Cursor, Grok Build, and other platforms, featuring a 500,000-token context window and a new safeguard stack for safety and cybersecurity.

title: Trump pursues massive Belarus fertiliser deal amid Canada trade war
summary: President Donald Trump announced a massive fertiliser deal with Belarus, shifting away from Canada amid an escalating trade dispute. Trump stated the pricing would be substantially lower than current Canadian rates. However, Belarusian opposition leader Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya warned the deal is risky, arguing that potash income funds repression and Russia's war machine. The US imports most potash, with Canada supplying 79% in 2024.

title: IIT Bombay Professor Rejects Allegations Following Student Death
summary: The president of the IIT Bombay faculty forum, Professor Rajkumar Pant, has rejected allegations against Professor Suryanarayana Doolla following the death of student Sahil Wakode. Pant stated that the institute's SC/ST cell had no record of the student approaching them with a complaint in the months preceding his death. This statement was made as the faculty forum staged a march in support of the professor.

title: Evaluating AI Agents Requires Task Completion Over Isolated Tool Calls
summary: The article argues that evaluating AI agents requires moving beyond scoring isolated tool calls to verifying actual task completion in live environments. Scoring individual calls fails to capture whether an agent successfully navigates multi-step workflows or recovers from errors. Robust evaluation demands a full execution environment that tracks state across steps and verifies final outcomes, distinguishing between process accuracy and end-to-end success. Benchmarks like SWE-bench Verified illustrate this shift by measuring whether agents can resolve real-world issues through sequential tool use rather than isolated function accuracy. The text emphasizes that production readiness depends on outcome verification, not just call precision.

title: TinyTorch: A Free Open-Source Curriculum to Build ML Frameworks from Scratch
summary: TinyTorch is a free, open-source curriculum designed to teach machine learning systems by having learners build a functional framework from scratch. The project, developed at Harvard and currently maintained by ETH Zurich, consists of twenty modules written in pure Python that mirror PyTorch's API. It is specifically designed to run on low-end hardware, such as laptops with only 4 GB of RAM and no GPU, making it accessible to students without expensive equipment. Since its launch in December 2025, the project has seen rapid growth, reaching over 27,000 stars and being adopted by more than 50 universities. The authors emphasize that building the framework oneself provides a deeper understanding of concepts like autograd and memory allocation compared to simply using the production library. While the project is in preview for Fall 2026, the team notes it currently lacks GPU support and distributed training features, focusing instead on foundational systems knowledge.

title: US and China Accuse Each Other of Psy-Ops in AI Debate
summary: A recent article explores the reciprocal accusations of psychological operations between the United States and China concerning artificial intelligence policy and infrastructure. Prominent figures, including Elon Musk and David Sacks in the US, and Chinese state media outlets, allege that opposing viewpoints are manufactured by foreign adversaries. The piece notes that these claims highlight a broader information gap, as neither side possesses a fully independent third-party source of truth to adjudicate industry claims. Consequently, the mutual distrust fosters an environment where legitimate regulatory discussions are clouded by allegations of foreign interference.

title: Bihar Minister Criticized for Calling Minor Harassment 'Isolated' Incident
summary: Bihar minister Shrawon Kumar drew criticism for describing the harassment of a minor girl in Jamui as an 'isolated' incident. The remarks followed a viral video showing the assault and groping of the girl returning from a coaching class. Jamui Police are investigating the case, having registered an FIR and arrested three people while forming a special team to identify others involved.

title: Chinese President Xi Jinping visits US to strengthen bilateral ties
summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping is set to visit the United States from September 23 to 25 at the invitation of US President Donald Trump. This state visit, the second between the two heads of state in six months, aims to reinforce 'constructive strategic stability' as the cornerstone of China-US relations. Officials describe this approach as an action-oriented strategy that prioritizes cooperation and manages differences. The visit underscores the importance of stable bilateral ties for global stability. Economic and trade cooperation continues to serve as a stabilizing force, with a 2026 survey indicating that 95% of US firms operating in China consider the market crucial for their global competitiveness. Law enforcement agencies have also engaged in practical cooperation in areas such as counternarcotics and fraud prevention.

title: Tesla Faces Racism Trial at Fremont Plant Amid Broader Allegations
summary: A California agency lawsuit accusing Tesla of allowing rampant race discrimination at its flagship assembly plant is set to go to trial on Monday. The suit, filed in 2022, alleges constant harassment, racial slurs, and that Black employees received lower pay and missed promotions. Reuters reports the case involves no jury, with a judge deciding the outcome, and notes similar lawsuits are pending against the company.

title: Ceer Motors Unveils New EVs to Compete with Tesla in Saudi Arabia
summary: Ceer Motors, a Saudi-backed venture partnering with BMW, has unveiled its first electric vehicles, the EXOBOT, marking a significant step in the Kingdom's push for a domestic EV industry. Supported by the Public Investment Fund and Foxconn, Ceer plans to manufacture seven new vehicles in Saudi Arabia over the next five years. The project is expected to contribute $8 billion to the economy by 2034. While the US faces potential EV adoption challenges due to policy shifts, other nations like Türkiye and Vietnam are advancing their own domestic automotive sectors, highlighting a global trend toward local EV production.

title: Researchers Revisit Marriage Gap in Children's Outcomes Using New Data
summary: Kearney, Levine, and Barson revisit the relationship between family structure and children's outcomes using 2023 PSID data. They find that the association with poverty has greatly diminished, whereas the association with college completion persists and is concentrated among children of mothers with higher levels of education.

title: Study Finds Financial Incentives Boost Wildfire Risk Reduction Participation
summary: Researchers Patrick Baylis, Judson Boomhower, Bob Horton, and Chris Mulverhill report that financial incentives of $100 to $500 increased assessment takeup rates to 12% among Oregon homeowners, whereas information-only approaches achieved at most 3%. The study utilized randomized field experiments to evaluate property protection adoption.

title: Tamil Nadu Combines Satellite Data with Community Monitoring for Mangrove Restoration
summary: Tamil Nadu has emerged as a leader in mangrove restoration, increasing its mangrove area from roughly 4,500 hectares in 2021 to 9,039 hectares in 2024. This expansion is largely tracked using satellite imagery, which maps canopy cover but cannot confirm sapling survival or ecological health. To address this limitation, the article proposes combining satellite data with community-based monitoring through Village Mangrove Councils. These local bodies conduct routine ground checks to provide ground truth, verifying restoration success and ensuring the mangroves are truly alive and functioning.

title: Rob Toia faces family rival Herbie Farnworth in NRL final
summary: Robert Toia of the Roosters will face Herbie Farnworth of the Knights in the NRL preliminary final at Lang Park. The match is a family affair as Toia and Farnworth are cousins. Toia, a 22-year-old with 10 siblings, expects many relatives in the crowd. Farnworth, who leads the NRL in tackle breaks and offloads, is a formidable opponent. The Roosters aim to reach their first grand final since 2019.

title: Fremantle Prepares for AFL Grand Final Crowd with Police Support
summary: Fremantle is bracing for an AFL grand final showdown between the Dockers and the Brisbane Lions, expecting around 40,000 fans to fill the city. Approximately 10,000 fans are anticipated at a licensed event at Fremantle Oval, with thousands more visiting local venues. To ensure safety, WA Police are deploying dozens of officers on motorbikes, horses, and dogs, alongside riot gear.

title: Supreme Court Rejects Challenge to 2018 SC/ST Act Amendments
summary: The Supreme Court dismissed a petition challenging the constitutional validity of the 2018 amendments to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant declined to entertain the challenge, noting that the amendments' validity had already been upheld in 2020. The petitioner argued that provisions restricting anticipatory bail amounted to reverse discrimination and cited low conviction rates and alleged misuse. The court's decision comes amid ongoing legal debates regarding the balance between protecting SC/ST members and preventing law misuse.

title: Anbumani Ramadoss flags Mettur water crisis and seeks aid
summary: PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss flagged a severe water crisis at the Mettur dam, attributing the situation to reduced Cauvery water releases from Karnataka. He warned that nearly 40 per cent of delta farmland may remain uncultivated, threatening the Samba paddy season. Ramadoss urged the Tamil Nadu government to announce direct relief packages and compensation for affected farmers.

title: UK Government Borrowing Surges Amid High Inflation
summary: The UK government borrowed £18.3bn in August, nearly 20% higher than the previous year, as persistently high inflation pushed up spending on public services and benefits. With inflation reaching 3.1% in the year to August, interest on debt rose to £8.8bn, the highest level since 1997. Economists warn this pressure may force the Chancellor to delay spending plans or raise taxes to meet fiscal rules, while opposition parties claim the government has lost control of public finances.

title: G7 Nations Condemn Houthi Strikes on Saudi Arabia
summary: G7 nations issued a statement on Tuesday calling on Yemen's Houthis to immediately cease military actions against Saudi Arabia. The condemnation comes as the Houthi movement has escalated attacks on Saudi infrastructure, including strikes on the Red Sea port of Mokha and facilities belonging to Aramco. Britain and France have pledged defensive military support to Saudi Arabia, while US President Donald Trump did not promise military aid despite requests from Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. The Houthis, backed by Iran, have threatened global trade routes and pushed up energy prices.

title: IIT Bombay Student Suicide Follows Alleged Cheating Incident During Exam
summary: Mumbai Police are analyzing CCTV footage regarding the suicide of a 22-year-old IIT Bombay student found dead in his hostel room. The institute stated the student was caught using a mobile phone to access ChatGPT during an exam, though no disciplinary action was initiated. Student representatives protested, citing systemic issues, while the professor involved, Suryanarayana Doolla, was suspended and charged with abetment to suicide. Faculty members support Doolla, arguing he was discharging his duties.

title: Tiffany Teo Wins Historic Gold for Singapore at Asian Games
summary: Tiffany Teo made history for Singapore on Tuesday, September 22, by winning a gold medal in the women's traditional 60kg final at the 20th Asian Games. The 36-year-old fighter defeated Uzbekistan's Khilola Sobirova at the Nagoya City Inae Sports Center. This event marked the first time Mixed Martial Arts was included in the Asian Games program, which also featured debuts for six other sports.

title: Election Commission announces Rajya Sabha election dates for UP, Uttarakhand and West Bengal
summary: The Election Commission announced on Tuesday that elections for 12 Rajya Sabha seats across Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and West Bengal will be held on October 16, 2026. The notification is set to be issued on September 29, with nominations due by October 6 and vote counting scheduled for October 16. These elections cover 10 seats in Uttar Pradesh and one in Uttarakhand, where terms expire on November 25, along with a bypoll for one seat in West Bengal following the resignation of Rukmini Mallik. Based on current assembly arithmetic, the BJP-led alliance is expected to win eight seats in Uttar Pradesh, while the Samajwadi Party is projected to secure two. The outcome could leave the BSP without representation in the Rajya Sabha as it lacks the numbers to retain Gautam's seat on its own.

title: Two men arrested in Visakhapatnam for possessing a country-made gun
summary: The City Task Force arrested two men, both aged about 30, in Visakhapatnam on Monday night for possessing a country-made gun. Acting on a tip-off, officials raided Gollalapalem and found the men, who run a biryani centre, with the firearm. Police allege the accused brought the weapon from Bihar and are currently investigating how it was procured and why it was brought to the city. II Town police station Inspector B. Appala Naidu stated that they will ascertain the reasons for the procurement as part of the further investigation.

title: U.K. Agrees to Provide Aerial Refuelling Support to Saudi Arabia
summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced on September 22, 2026, that Britain has agreed to provide limited military support to Saudi Arabia to counter attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen. The agreement involves the Royal Air Force providing air-to-air refuelling for Saudi planes on defensive missions, starting in the coming days and lasting for a matter of weeks. Burnham stated the agreement will be kept under review as the conflict reignites with Houthis aiming missile and drone strikes on Saudi Arabia.

title: Syrian President Meets Diaspora Ahead of UN Appearance
summary: Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa met with members of the Syrian community in the US on Tuesday to discuss developments in Syria, reconstruction efforts, and ties with Washington. The meeting, attended by several officials, took place at the start of his visit to New York for the 81st session of the UN General Assembly. This marks his second consecutive participation in the gathering, following his attendance at the 80th session in September 2025.

title: Man Accused of Harassing Minors Shot by Police in Bihar
summary: Nandan Yadav, the main accused in a case involving the alleged harassment of two minors in Jamui, Bihar, was shot in the leg by police. Yadav and another accused person were arrested. The victims, a Class 10 girl and her male friend, were allegedly harassed on September 19 while returning from a scenic spot. Although they did not file a complaint initially due to fear and threats, the incident gained attention after a viral video emerged. Police superintendent Vishwajeet Dayal confirmed they traced the victims using a vehicle registration number visible in the video.

title: India and Israel to commemorate Haifa liberation anniversary
summary: On September 23, 2026, India and Israel intend to jointly commemorate the 1918 British capture of Haifa. Mani Shankar Aiyar, a former Cabinet Minister, criticizes this planned event in an article titled 'Haifa, history, and keeping bad company.' He argues that celebrating alongside Israel is inappropriate because the country did not exist at the time and because the British deception regarding Palestinian self-rule led to ongoing conflict. Aiyar contends that India should honor its own soldiers' sacrifice independently rather than aligning with what he describes as 'genocidal war criminals.' The piece highlights the historical context of the Battle of Megiddo and the subsequent Sykes-Picot agreement while questioning the motives behind the current joint commemoration.

title: Seoul President and Mayor Clash Over Park Development Amid Housing Crisis
summary: A political standoff is unfolding in Seoul between President Lee Jae Myung and Mayor Oh Se-hoon over a 300-hectare site. The president, facing slumping approval ratings due to a national housing crisis, wants to build apartment towers on the land. Conversely, Mayor Oh Se-hoon argues the area is essential to fix Seoul's greenery deficit and environmental flaws. Oh has vowed not to surrender any part of the planned park to the proposed residential development.

title: French President Macron Walks to Trump Tower for UN Meeting
summary: French President Emmanuel Macron walked through busy midtown Manhattan with his delegation, heading to Trump Tower to meet US President Donald Trump. The visit took place on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot was among those in the delegation. Macron walked at a steady pace, flanked by security and aides, and greeted a police officer with a handshake before entering the building. Bilateral talks were high on the agenda as world leaders gathered in the city.

title: Typhoon Dujuan Triggers Evacuations and Cancellations in Japan
summary: Typhoon Dujuan caused significant disruption in Japan as it brushed past Tokyo, prompting evacuation advisories for over one million people and leading to the cancellation of hundreds of flights. The storm brought torrential rain, flooding, and landslides, resulting in two confirmed deaths in Chiba and Kanagawa prefectures. Major events, including the Tokyo Game Show, were cancelled, and railway services were suspended in affected areas. The Japan Meteorological Agency warned that rainfall could exceed monthly averages, creating record-breaking conditions.

title: Election Commission announces Rajya Sabha polls in UP, Uttarakhand and West Bengal
summary: The Election Commission announced that elections for 12 Rajya Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and West Bengal will be held on October 16. The notification is scheduled for September 29, with nominations due by October 6. Ten seats in Uttar Pradesh and one in Uttarakhand are due to expire, while a bypoll in West Bengal follows a resignation. The BJP-led alliance is projected to win most seats, though the BSP may lose representation due to a lack of numbers.

title: G7 Demands Iran Halt Arms to Houthis Amid Yemen Escalation
summary: Foreign ministers from G7 nations issued a joint statement urging Iran to cease arming and supporting the Houthis in Yemen. The ministers condemned recent Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia as a threat to regional and global energy security. While Iran denies supplying weapons, claiming only political support, UN experts concluded that the Houthis have received military assistance from Iran. The statement was released ahead of the UN General Assembly, where Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is scheduled to speak. Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia has requested military support from the UK and US to counter Houthi drone and missile attacks.

title: Main accused in Bihar molestation case injured in police encounter
summary: Police in Bihar shot and injured Nandan Yadav, the main accused in an alleged molestation case involving a minor student, during an encounter on Tuesday. Yadav was attempting to flee near Madwa Hill when police surrounded him. Six individuals, including three adults and three minors, have been arrested in connection with the case. Police identified Yadav as the young man in a viral video showing the assault. Further investigation is underway.

title: CERN Physicists Confirm Quantum Entanglement in Z Bosons at High Energies
summary: Physicists working with the ATLAS and CMS experiments at CERN's Large Hadron Collider have found strong evidence that Z bosons can become quantum-entangled. Published in September 2026, the study examined correlations in particles produced during Higgs boson decays, a process occurring at extraordinarily high energies. Researchers reconstructed the properties of the short-lived Z bosons by analyzing their decay products. The ATLAS measurement reported that a hypothesis assuming the particles were separable was disfavoured at a significance of 4.7 standard deviations, which is described as strong evidence but falls slightly short of the 5 standard deviations required for a discovery standard. This result extends previous studies of entanglement to massive vector bosons and provides a new way to study quantum mechanics in extreme environments.

title: Alibaba Unveils Powerful AI Chip to Drive Global Data Centre Expansion
summary: Alibaba Group Holding has unveiled the Zhenwu V900 AI accelerator, describing it as China's most powerful chip to support a massive expansion of data centre capacity. Chief executive Eddie Wu stated the accelerator trebles the performance of its predecessor and can be clustered up to 500,000 units for training frontier AI models. The company has pledged to spend more than US$53 billion over three years to expand AI capabilities and aims to reach 20 gigawatts of data centre capacity for Alibaba Cloud by 2032. However, Wu acknowledged challenges in meeting surging domestic demand due to US export restrictions on advanced chips from manufacturers like Nvidia and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, leaving it unclear if Alibaba is working with domestic chipmakers to bridge the gap.

title: AMD Joins $1 Trillion Club Driven by AI and Data Center Growth
summary: Advanced Micro Devices joined the rarefied $1 trillion market capitalization club on September 21, becoming the fourth chipmaker to achieve this milestone. The company's stock has surged significantly this year, driven by a rebound in the semiconductor sector and growing investor confidence in its artificial intelligence capabilities. Data center revenue jumped 107% to $6. 7 billion in the second quarter, propelled by strong demand for EPYC server CPUs and Instinct GPUs. Overall revenue reached $11. 53 billion, up 50% from the previous year, with net income rising 163% to $2. 29 billion.

title: AMD Joins $1 Trillion Club Amid AI Rally
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) joined a select group of chipmakers by surpassing a $1 trillion market capitalization for the first time. This milestone reflects a stellar rally driven by investor confidence in AMD's expanding role in AI computing. The Santa Clara-based company, viewed as a close rival to Nvidia, saw its shares rise 9.6% to a record high. While broader chip stocks surged, AMD's 185% surge in 2026 far outpaced the tech-heavy Nasdaq.

title: Transformers Integrates GGUF Quantization for Local AI Inference
summary: The transformers library has integrated support for GGUF quantized models to facilitate local AI inference on Apple Silicon. By reusing ggml kernels through a dedicated library, the integration aims to match the performance of llama.cpp while allowing developers to use familiar PyTorch workflows. Benchmarks on a MacBook Pro M2 Max indicate that the new approach achieves token generation rates comparable to llama.cpp across small dense, larger dense, and mixture-of-experts models. The feature currently supports Qwen3.5 architectures and offers benefits such as inspecting intermediate activations and validating quantization conversions. While the packed inference path is limited to MPS devices for now, the team plans to expand architecture coverage and optimize padding and batching in future updates.

title: RBI Absorbs Liquidity via VRRR Auction Amid Surplus
summary: The Reserve Bank of India absorbed Rs 71,971 crore from the banking system through an overnight variable rate reverse repo auction on Tuesday, accepting full bids against a notified amount of Rs 75,000 crore at a rate of 5.24 per cent. This action addresses a surplus liquidity estimated at around Rs 4.92 lakh crore as of September 21. Additionally, the central bank conducted open market operations selling government securities worth Rs 50,000 crore on September 17 and Rs 25,000 crore on September 21, with a remaining tranche of Rs 25,000 crore scheduled for September 28.

title: Samsung India Electronics Profit Falls Amidst Revenue Growth
summary: Samsung India Electronics reported a 36% decline in profit to ₹7,228.10 crore for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, according to a RoC filing. However, revenue from operations rose slightly by 1.2% to ₹1.12 lakh crore. The company's mobile phone revenue fell 1.35%, while home appliance revenue increased 3.52%.

title: Sunrun and Tesla Deliver Record Battery Power to California Grid
summary: On the evening of September 9, 2026, Sunrun and Tesla coordinated a record 580MW discharge from residential battery energy storage systems to the California grid. This event, the largest virtual power plant dispatch on record, involved approximately 110,000 Tesla Powerwalls and 30,000 batteries from other manufacturers. The coordinated effort was triggered by extreme temperatures and high electricity demand, aiming to increase grid operating margins and apply downward pressure on real-time energy prices. The dispatch utilized programs like the CEC’s Demand Side Grid Support and PG&E’s Emergency Load Reduction Program.

title: Microsoft May Announce Xbox Division Layoffs and Studio Consolidation Today
summary: Microsoft may announce layoffs in its Xbox division later today, citing sources familiar with the company's plans. The Verge reports that Microsoft may lay off hundreds of employees. This would be the company's second major staff reduction this year, following an earlier announcement by Xbox CEO Asha Sharma to eliminate 1,600 roles by the end of the year on top of 1,600 roles cut that month. The layoffs and restructuring come as Sharma tries to improve profits at the gaming business, which has been behind some of its rivals.

title: ECB and EU central banks oppose stablecoin bank deposit rule
summary: The European System of Central Banks (ESCB), comprising the ECB and 27 national central banks, opposed a proposed rule requiring stablecoin issuers to hold 60% of reserves as bank deposits. In a response to MiCA regulations, the ECB and other EU central banks stated that such a requirement could expose lenders to market changes and reduce deposit stickiness. Instead, they recommended requiring reserves to mature within one to five working days. The ESCB also noted material challenges in enforcing crypto regulations due to non-compliant companies accessing EU customers.

title: Author shares 20 Google Docs tips for users
summary: An author shares 20 favorite Google Docs features that might be useful for users. The article was republished with permission from Wonder Tools, a newsletter focused on discovering useful sites and apps. The author notes that Google Docs turned 20 this year and proceeds to list specific features such as voice typing, matching a prior document's format, and adding extensions to the platform.

title: Security Researcher Releases Tool Blocking Microsoft Defender Updates
summary: Security researcher Abdelhamid Naceri, also known as Nightmare Eclipse, released a new zero-day exploit named BigDiskBuster over the weekend. This tool allows standard users to block Microsoft Defender antivirus updates on all supported Windows versions by running in the background. Naceri stated the tool was part of an ongoing dispute with Microsoft regarding an alleged unfair termination in March 2025. While Microsoft has patched some of Naceri's previously disclosed flaws, others still lack official patches. A Microsoft spokesperson was not immediately available to comment when contacted by BleepingComputer.

title: Meta Shares Surge on Muse AI Agent Success
summary: Meta shares surged 11.3% to close at $741.25, adding $192 billion to market cap and $13 billion to Mark Zuckerberg's net worth, driven by the success of its Muse AI agent. The app reached 2.8 million downloads in 12 days, surpassing ChatGPT's early adoption. Analysts note this validates Meta's substantial AI investments and suggests new monetization opportunities through advertising and subscriptions, contrasting with competitors focusing on enterprise revenue.

title: OpenAI CEO Suggests Trump and Xi Could Win Nobel Peace Prize for AI Safety
summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman suggested that US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping could jointly secure the Nobel Peace Prize if they agree on foundational AI safety rules. Speaking ahead of a state dinner, Altman highlighted the urgent need for cross-border alignment, characterizing basic safety accords as a reachable diplomatic milestone. He stated in an interview with Fortune Magazine that such an agreement would be wonderful and easy to achieve.

title: DeepSeek to brief UN Security Council on AI safety
summary: The 15-member UN Security Council is scheduled to meet on Wednesday to discuss AI and international security. Industry leaders, including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, plan to brief the council on risks of AI systems slipping beyond human control. DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng will not attend, though the firm has been invited to make statements. Chinese state media dismissed calls for a slowdown as a Cold War tactic. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent noted that senior US and Chinese officials agreed to hold further talks on AI safety.

title: Microsoft India MD Rajiv Kumar Discusses New Hyderabad Cloud Region and AI Infrastructure Plans
summary: Rajiv Kumar, MD of Microsoft India Development Centre, discussed the company's new Hyderabad cloud region and its selection. He addressed investments in cloud infrastructure, potential job creation, and future data centre plans. Kumar also explained Microsoft's approach to AI infrastructure, skills development in India, and the company's focus on responsible AI safety.

title: OpenAI Urges US to Lead Global AI Standards Effort
summary: OpenAI urged the United States to lead an international effort to establish global technical standards for frontier AI, including recursive self-improvement. CEO Sam Altman and other industry leaders called for a coordinated slowdown, warning that unregulated development could allow AI to slip beyond human control. OpenAI stated that leading now determines whether the US shapes the global framework or watches a fragmented system take hold. The UN Security Council is set to meet on AI risks, with Altman scheduled to brief the body.

title: Analysts Predict RBI Repo Rate Hike Could Increase Home Loan Costs
summary: Analysts anticipate the Reserve Bank of India may raise the repo rate by 50 basis points before December 2026, which could make home loans costlier. This expectation is driven by rising retail inflation, which climbed to 4.82 per cent in August, and concerns over crude oil prices between USD 90 and USD 110 a barrel. Additionally, HSBC estimates a banking system liquidity surplus of about Rs 15 trillion, adding pressure to financial conditions.

title: Apple Pay May Launch in India via Axis Bank Credit Cards
summary: Reuters reports that Apple Pay may debut in India as early as October, initially supporting Axis Bank credit cards for contactless payments. While Apple has not officially confirmed the launch, the service aims to offer a new payment route distinct from the dominant UPI system. Apple is reportedly in talks with HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank, though terms remain unfinalised. The rollout coincides with regulatory changes allowing biometric authentication, yet coverage limitations may require users to switch to UPI apps at many merchants.

title: Residents Protest Google Data Centre Plans in Austrian Town
summary: Residents of Kronstorf, Austria, protested Google's plans for a 50-hectare data centre, citing concerns over transparency, cooling systems, and water use. Approximately 400 people gathered in Linz, while the project, expected to operate by 2027, aims to create around 100 direct jobs. Google claims the facility will support cloud and AI services, though critics argue it may strain local resources and environmental goals.

title: Microsoft Xbox Plans Job Cuts Amid Restructuring
summary: Microsoft Xbox is preparing to cut hundreds of jobs while streamlining studios, reported the Information outlet citing an unnamed source. The company has not formally confirmed or denied the report but previously outlined plans under CEO Asha Sharma. Sharma announced a significant restructure aiming to reduce the team by approximately 3,200 throughout the 2027 financial year to address business health issues and return to growth by the end of FY27.

title: Sharad Pawar Urges Dialogue to Protect Tata Group Legacy Amid Leadership Dispute
summary: Sharad Pawar, president of the Nationalist Congress Party, urged stakeholders to protect the Tata Group's charitable legacy and resolve its leadership dispute through dialogue. He stressed that Tata Trusts, which hold 66% of Tata Sons, must have their governance rights respected to preserve the group's institutional role. Pawar noted that the dispute arose after the Tata Sons board reappointed N Chandrasekaran as executive chairman, a move opposed by Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata. Pawar also highlighted the group's contributions to Maharashtra institutions and called for adherence to the Articles of Association.

title: OpenAI and Anthropic urge Australia to relax AI training copyright ban
summary: Top AI companies OpenAI and Anthropic have urged Australia to reconsider a ban on using local creative content for training AI models. They argue that a limited exemption could protect artists' rights while encouraging investment. The companies, which have signed agreements for data centres in Sydney and Queensland, suggest a narrow form of conditional approval. Meanwhile, Australia has ruled out broad copyright exemptions, and the Joint Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence is due to deliver its report in November.

title: Apple Pay India Launch Timeline and UPI Integration Uncertainty
summary: Reports indicate Apple Pay may launch in India by October, ending a twelve-year wait for the service. While initial rollout might focus on Axis Bank credit cards, it remains unclear if UPI integration will be included. This distinction is critical because UPI dominates Indian digital payments, with over 24.5 billion transactions recorded in August 2026. Users may hesitate to switch from established apps like PhonePe and Google Pay if the new service lacks essential local features.

title: Police Probe School Shooting Linked to Cryptic Post and Recovered Pistols
summary: Police in Lakhimpur Kheri are investigating a shooting where a teacher was killed and the accused, Mohd Saud Ansari, died by suicide. Authorities are examining a cryptic Instagram post found on an account allegedly linked to Ansari, which requested followers to delete his photos and report his Facebook account. Additionally, two country-made pistols were recovered from his bag. Officials state that while these elements form part of the puzzle, a social media message alone cannot establish the motive. Investigators are also scrutinizing Ansari's interactions with the victim and CCTV footage to piece together the sequence of events.

title: Alibaba Unveils New AI Chip and Plans for Larger Model
summary: Alibaba Group CEO Eddie Wu announced the Zhenwu V900 AI chip and plans for a significantly larger AI model at the annual Apsara Conference in Hangzhou. The new chip delivers three times the performance of the previous Zhenwu M890 and supports clusters of up to 500,000 cards. Alibaba aims to train a next-generation model with 5 to 10 trillion parameters, a significant increase from the current Qwen3.8-Max model's 2.4 trillion parameters. The company also targets surpassing 20 gigawatts of cloud data center capacity by 2032, despite supply chain shortages hindering infrastructure expansion.

title: GiveDirectly Explores Scaling Cash Transfers Amidst Research Challenges
summary: GiveDirectly is rapidly scaling its cash transfer operations, a trend that could intensify if a new wave of American philanthropy materializes. Caitlin Tulloch, Senior Director for Research, Learning and Product at GiveDirectly, discusses the organization's evidence-driven approach to managing this growth. Rather than simply asking if results generalize, the organization focuses on predicting outcomes under specific conditions, utilizing predictive models for studies in Malawi and Kenya. Tulloch notes that while fraud rates remain low, the organization is willing to test trade-offs between exacting standards and massive scale. The goal includes developing a global emergency response capability capable of operating within five days anywhere in the world.

title: Trump and Xi to Discuss AI Worm Threats at Summit
summary: Ahead of a meeting between US President Donald Trump and China President Xi Jinping in Washington, D.C., officials are considering establishing a hotline for serious AI incidents. The article highlights the threat of AI-enabled adaptive computer worms, which can self-replicate and adapt strategies, potentially enabling non-state actors to conduct large-scale cyberattacks. Historical examples like the 2017 NotPetya attack, which compromised 2,000 organizations in 60 countries, and the WannaCry outbreak affecting 18,000 Chinese IP addresses, illustrate the severe transnational risks. The summit offers an opportunity to build a framework for cooperation against this emerging threat.

title: Banks Warn AI Shopping Bots Pose Scam and Privacy Risks
summary: Banks including NatWest and Bank of America warned on Sept 22 that using AI agents for online shopping could increase risks of scams, fraud, and data-privacy breaches. While technology companies promote these tools, retailers like John Lewis report searches from AI agents rose to 2.5 per cent from 0.3 per cent a year earlier. The banks plan to discuss proposals with policymakers to improve transparency and safeguards.

title: Meta Shares Surge as AI Agent Muse Tops US App Store
summary: Meta shares surged 11.43%, adding more than $190 billion to market value as its new AI agent, Muse, rapidly climbed US app rankings. Launched on September 8, Muse overtook OpenAI's ChatGPT to become the No. 1 free app on Apple's US App Store, according to Sensor Tower. While Meta describes Muse as a breakthrough for consumer AI, analysts note that early buzz has not erased market concerns regarding privacy and whether the product will sustain momentum beyond a viral hit.

title: China and US prioritize AI safety dialogue over distillation dispute
summary: As leading AI powers, China and the United States are urged to maintain dialogue despite ongoing competition. While recent disputes over model distillation have occurred, experts like Gai Keke and Dean Ball note this is not the core issue. Both nations' experts agree that sharing risks and jointly building rules for AI safety should be the primary agenda, as danger in AI knows no borders.

title: Chinese Tech Firms Showcase Chipmaking Advances Amid US Restrictions
summary: Chinese technology firms showcased advances in chipmaking despite US curbs on access to cutting-edge semiconductor technology. Alibaba shares rose after the company unveiled what it called China's most powerful chip ever, aiming to expand across the AI ecosystem. Additionally, memory chipmaker CXMT stated its latest chip platform is entering mass production, gaining domestic market share from global giants. Researchers at the Chinese Academy of Sciences also reported progress in using older technology to build advanced chips as a potential workaround to US restrictions.

title: EU seals trade deal with Philippines to diversify Indo-Pacific ties
summary: EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič announced a new trade agreement between the EU and the Philippines, designed to diversify trade ties away from reliance on China and the US. The deal provides EU businesses access to a market of 113 million consumers and eliminates over 94% of customs duties. It covers more than 97% of bilateral trade, including machinery, medicines, and agricultural products. Bilateral goods trade reached €17.6 billion in 2025, while services trade hit €10.3 billion in 2024. The EU also plans further agreements with Thailand and Malaysia by year-end.

title: Sri Lanka Replaces Net Metering with Feed-in Tariffs for Rooftop Solar
summary: Sri Lanka's Ministry of Energy announced the discontinuation of the net-metering regime for new rooftop solar connections after March 5, 2026, replacing it with the Net Plus mechanism. The Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka (PUCSL) established feed-in tariffs ranging from LKR 15.81 to LKR 23.11 per kWh, valid until February 24, 2027. New agreements under Net Plus are limited to a maximum term of 12 years, and systems must be equipped with smart meters for remote monitoring.

title: Supreme Court questions machine-generated voter notices in Delhi SIR
summary: On September 22, 2026, the Supreme Court observed that notices issued to over 33 lakh voters in Delhi during the Special Intensive Revision appeared machine-generated without application of mind. Justice Joymalya Bagchi questioned the process, noting that 91% of appealed voters were re-included. The Election Commission assured no deletions would occur before the October 29 deadline, though the court sought a status report and noted the need for better orientation and online verification mechanisms.

title: Kerala Report Shows Widespread Antimicrobial Resistance in Hospitals
summary: A 2025 report by the Kerala Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance Network confirms that antimicrobial resistance is now the norm in the state's hospitals, affecting both intensive care and community settings. The study analyzed 65,849 isolates and found high resistance rates in key pathogens like E. coli and Klebsiella. While Colistin remains largely effective with only 0.1% resistance, experts warn that resistance is emerging. Despite a robust surveillance system, prescribing behaviors have not changed, highlighting a need for targeted stewardship interventions.

title: Senate Democrats Demand Tariff Refunds from Trump Administration
summary: Six Senate Democrats, including Sen. Elizabeth Warren, wrote to US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer urging the Trump administration to refund consumers after the Supreme Court invalidated a round of tariffs. The lawmakers argue that without such a plan, the policy risks transferring wealth to corporations. Meanwhile, the private sector has recovered about $100 billion through price cuts and refunds, though some companies like Ford and Costco face lawsuits for opting out. The Democrats also seek oversight on future tariffs under specific trade acts.

title: Tejashwi Yadav Demands Choudhary Resignation Over Jamui Harassment
summary: RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav demanded the resignation of Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary following a viral video showing minors being harassed in Jamui. Yadav, addressing a press conference in Patna, alleged that the incident demonstrated a collapse of law and order. He invoked a previous statement by Choudhary regarding Munger, asserting that the CM should resign if he lacks the courage to stand by his words. Yadav further accused the ruling alliance of attempting to justify the incident.

title: Vietnam's President To Lam Says Nation Near U.S. Trade Deal
summary: Vietnamese President To Lam indicated that his nation is very close to inking a trade deal with the U. S. Speaking on the sidelines of the U. N. General Assembly, he pledged to buy more high-tech goods like aircraft to narrow the trade gap ahead of talks with U. S. administration officials in New York. Lam emphasized the need to expedite negotiations toward an agreement on reciprocal, balanced and equitable tariffs, noting that Vietnam exports align with U. S. demand without competing directly with U. S. products. He also mentioned that Vietnam wants to import more U. S.

title: Hindustan Copper plans major investment and global partnerships
summary: Hindustan Copper plans to invest Rs 7,000 crore over the next five years to expand its mining portfolio and strengthen India's mineral security. The company has signed multiple MoUs with Indian public sector undertakings like NTPC Mining, RITES, and IOCL. Additionally, it entered a global partnership with CODELCO in Chile for capacity building. In the last four years, Hindustan Copper added 154.14 million tonnes of copper ore reserves.

title: 23rd China-ASEAN Expo Concludes with AI Focus in Nanning
summary: The 23rd China-ASEAN Expo concluded in Nanning, Guangxi, with artificial intelligence emerging as a central theme for trade and investment cooperation. Held at the Nanning International Convention and Exhibition Center, the event saw a 10,000 square meter area increase to 170,000 square meters. A total of 3,432 enterprises from 73 countries participated, with international exhibitors accounting for 30. 5%. The expo unveiled 42 AI application scenarios and generated nearly 100 preliminary cooperation agreements, with intended deal values exceeding 1 billion yuan. An AI-themed marketplace debuted, featuring 70 companies and 500 products, generating 28 million yuan in sales.

title: China and US face shared energy transition challenges requiring cooperation
summary: The article highlights that the energy transition presents a shared challenge for China and the US, demanding cooperation rather than isolation. In 2025, China added over 430 gigawatts of new wind and solar capacity, while the US added 53 gigawatts, 80% of which was solar and storage. Additionally, China manufactures eight of every 10 solar modules globally, driving down costs for clean energy worldwide.

title: China-US trade remains strong despite ongoing disagreements
summary: In 2025, trade between China and the United States surpassed $500 billion. Data indicates that 95% of American firms consider their China operations vital. Although disagreements persist, experts suggest these conflicts should not define the entire bilateral relationship. Michael Wang from CGTN argues that history serves as a warning rather than a predetermined destiny for future interactions.

title: China's Grain Industry Output Expected to Exceed 4.5 Trillion Yuan by 2030
summary: An official announced that China's grain industry output is projected to exceed 4.5 trillion yuan during the 2026-2030 period. Liu Huanxin, head of the National Food and Strategic Reserves Administration, stated that the sector will better meet demand for nutritious food. He attributed China's food security to stable production, ample reserves, and strong processing capacity, noting that output has remained above 650 million tonnes since 2015.

title: El Niño Linked to Extreme Rainfall Events in India
summary: Mandvi taluka in Gujarat received 177 mm of rain in eight hours on September 15, causing waterlogging. This occurred despite a 70% rainfall deficit in the district. A 2025 study in Science indicates that while El Niño suppresses total summer rainfall in India, it increases the frequency of extreme daily rainfall events in specific regions. India ranks among the six most disaster-prone countries globally.

title: British Man Missing After Attempting Lake Como Rescue
summary: Italian authorities are searching for a British man who went missing after diving into Lake Como to rescue a teenager and his father. The incident occurred on Monday afternoon when the man, described as being in his late thirties, jumped into the water to help two people in distress. Although the father and son were later rescued by a passing boat, the British man has not been seen again. Rescuers, including a helicopter and underwater robots, are currently searching the lake's deep waters.

title: Police Arrest Gem Granites Employee Over Sexual Abuse Allegations
summary: Chennai Police arrested Ganesan, a former employee of Gem Granites founder Veeramani, regarding a POCSO investigation. He was remanded to Puzhal Central Prison for failing to report digital evidence of sexual abuse found on his mobile phone. Authorities are probing the video's origin and investigating a suspected 70-crore-rupee money trail allegedly used to suppress the crime.

title: Mexico Restricts Cellphones in Schools to Combat Screen Addiction
summary: Mexico has implemented a ban on cellphones in elementary and middle schools, effective November 3, to combat screen addiction and protect student development. President Claudia Sheinbaum framed the move as a protective measure rather than a strict prohibition, citing data that over 83% of parents worry about device time and that 81% of surveyed teachers support the regulation. This initiative places Mexico alongside Brazil and Chile in Latin America, where similar restrictions have shown positive outcomes like improved attention and reduced bullying. While the policy aims to restore focus and learning, schools have six months to define how the restriction will be applied, with an evaluation of results scheduled for one year later.

title: Congress Wins Tijara Chair Despite One Councillor
summary: Congress secured control of the Tijara Nagar Parishad chairperson post despite having only one elected councillor, as its candidate Ramavatar Saini defeated BJP's Subhash Chand Saini by a margin of two votes. The result hinged on the support of 31 independent councillors, who held the balance of power in the 35-member council. The election was preceded by allegations that Congress-backed councillors were detained by Haryana Police in Panchkula, triggering protests and delaying the vote until approximately 9:45 pm. Former MLA Sandeep Yadav alleged mistreatment of the councillors and threatened legal action, while police denied the claims and promised an investigation.

title: India Wins Gold in Women's Cricket at Asian Games 2026
summary: India secured its first gold medal of the Asian Games 2026 by defeating Sri Lanka in the women's cricket final held in Nagoya on September 22, 2026. India batted first, posting 216/3 led by Smriti Mandhana's 79, and then chased down the target to win by over 100 runs. Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated the team, stating the victory brings India its first gold of this edition. However, the women's team was eliminated after a 1-3 defeat to hosts Japan in the semifinals.

title: Attacker Wounds 11 Near High School in Western Turkiye
summary: Officials reported that an attacker wounded at least 11 people near a vocational high school in Turgutlu, Manisa province, on Tuesday. Justice Minister Akin Gurlek stated that the suspect, possibly a student, used a shotgun taken from his grandmother's home. Police arrested the individual, while two chief prosecutors were appointed to investigate claims of bullying. The incident occurred amid heightened security following previous school shootings in the region.

title: Max Verstappen aims for first Formula One victory of the year in Baku
summary: Red Bull's Max Verstappen is targeting his first Formula One victory of the year at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in Baku, following a recent karting triumph. The 28-year-old driver aims to break his victory duck on the unpredictable street circuit, where he and teammate Sergio Perez are the only drivers to have won more than once. Meanwhile, championship leader Kimi Antonelli enters the weekend with an 81-point lead over George Russell, while Verstappen's team looks to maximize performance against Mercedes.

title: Sir Jim Ratcliffe Halts Ineos UK Production Over High Gas Costs
summary: Sir Jim Ratcliffe, owner of Ineos, has suspended production at three UK facilities, citing gas prices in the UK as twelve times higher than in the US and eight times higher than in China. The company stated that up to 1,000 staff could be affected, with two plants already shut and a third set to stop production in the coming days. Ratcliffe described the current government's energy policy as 'economic vandalism on an industrial scale' and called for tariff protections against Chinese products. The Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade responded by highlighting existing support measures for the chemicals industry.

title: Iran President Vows to Defend Positions at UN Amidst Regional Tensions
summary: Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian vowed to firmly defend his country's positions at the UN General Assembly in New York on Tuesday, September 22, 2026. Speaking before departing, he stated that the Iranian people have stood their ground despite unfairness. He plans to convey Iran's plight to the international community on Wednesday. This visit marks the first time a high-ranking Iranian official has set foot on American soil since the West Asia war began in late February, although his communications team was denied visas.

title: Zoho Founder Warns Engineers Against Over-Reliance on AI Coding Tools
summary: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu warned software engineers against over-reliance on artificial intelligence, stating that technology should assist rather than replace human understanding. Responding to an engineer's report of a company using AI to generate specifications and code, Vembu noted the industry is 'driving too fast in a fancy new car.' The engineer described employees working 12 to 13 hours a day merely to press enter, with no time to review code or resolve bugs.

title: ING Analysts Warn Supply Risks Persist Despite Oil Price Drop
summary: Analysts at ING Bank assert that supply-side risks remain elevated despite a recent decline in crude oil prices. Brent Crude fell to $100 per barrel after Saudi Arabia shut a pipeline, yet higher-than-expected shipments eased concerns. Meanwhile, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent threatened Iranian airlines with service denials. Strategists Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey note that market dynamics balance hopes for peace talks against fresh disruptions in Libya, where output at the Sharara field was slashed to around 127,000 barrels per day.

title: Activist Defends Free Speech Against UP CM Amid Threats
summary: Neha Bora, a PhD scholar and national president of the All India Students' Association, addressed a public meeting in Gorakhpur where she criticized Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Adityanath, calling him a 'goonda' and 'rioter.' Her remarks alleged that his administration presided over riots, unemployment, and persecution of minorities. The response was immediate: three police complaints were filed, BJP functionaries demanded an FIR, and Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar threatened her. Bora's organization, AISA, reported receiving death threats and filed a complaint with the Uttar Pradesh Director General of Police. The article defends Bora's speech as constitutionally protected, noting that Adityanath's government has withdrawn criminal cases involving himself and others, a practice the author describes as amoral. It contrasts Bora's sharp criticism with Adityanath's own rhetoric of force and religious polarization, arguing that holding power to account is central to democracy.

title: UK Doctor Charged with Genocide in Rwanda Case
summary: Dr Vincent Brown, a 65-year-old medical doctor, appeared in Westminster Magistrates' Court as the first person in the UK charged with genocide related to the 1994 Rwanda killings. He faces charges of conduct ancillary to genocide and murder, allegedly linked to a slaughter in Kigali between April 6 and 13, 1994. His barrister, Sam Blom-Cooper, stated Brown denies the allegations and intends to clear them before a jury. The case was passed to the Old Bailey for a hearing on 9 October, with a bail application to follow.

title: MOL Group Inaugurates New Solar Park and Storage System in Hungary
summary: MOL Group has inaugurated a new 37. 4 MWp solar park and an associated electricity storage system rated at 20 MWp nominal and 40 MWh of storage capacity at its Algyő site in Hungary. This facility strengthens the group's renewable portfolio in Central Europe, enhancing electricity supply flexibility and reducing CO2 emissions by approximately 13,000 tonnes annually. The new solar park, combined with existing power plants at Algyő, can fully cover the electricity demand of the Algyő region.

title: Rupee rises against dollar as oil prices fall amid U.S.-Iran tensions
summary: The Indian rupee appreciated 20 paise to close at 95.58 against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday, September 22, 2026. This rise was supported by a sharp fall in crude oil prices following media reports that Iran might open the Strait of Hormuz if the U.S. lifts its blockade.
