Analyst Anuj Choudhary noted that while improved global risk sentiments support the currency, fresh tensions could limit gains, with the USD-INR spot price expected to trade between 95.30 and 95.80.

title: Global Grid-Scale Battery Storage Sees Surge in August
summary: Nearly 21GWh of grid-scale battery energy storage systems were deployed globally in August, with China accounting for the majority of the capacity. European activity increased significantly, commissioning 18.2GWh, which is three times the amount installed in the same period last year. The data comes from Benchmark Mineral Intelligence, which reports monthly figures for ESN Premium.

title: AtkinsRéalis JV Wins Major Nuclear Refurbishment Contract
summary: Candu Energy, an AtkinsRéalis company, and Aecon Group have secured a $1.7 billion, three-year contract with Ontario Power Generation to refurbish Unit 5 of the Pickering CANDU nuclear power plant. This project involves retubing and boiler replacement, serving as the first phase of a broader refurbishment plan for Units 6, 7, and 8. The work aims to extend the plant's operational life into the 2060s, reinforcing energy security and sustaining skilled jobs in Ontario.

title: MP Police Issue New Online Activity Guidelines for Personnel
summary: The Madhya Pradesh Police issued sweeping guidelines restricting online activities for personnel to maintain discipline and protect the force's public image. Police Chief Kailash Makwana introduced rules prohibiting social media use during duty, banning posts in uniform or involving weapons, and restricting engagement with discriminatory content. Officers must report any income generated from social media within 30 days and cannot use AI tools for official purposes or share investigative details.

title: Rajasthan Urban Elections Signal BJP Vulnerability Amid Narrow Victory
summary: Rajasthan's recent urban local body elections resulted in a narrow victory for the BJP, which secured only a 0.94% margin over the Congress. This outcome, described as unexpected, saw a significant number of independents elected, including rebels from both major parties. While the BJP hailed the win as a vindication of its governance, analysts and opposition leaders point to issues like delayed polls, economic unrest, and internal organizational failures as contributing factors. The Congress, despite facing anti-incumbency, struggled to capitalize on the situation. Experts warn that this fragile victory, marked by losses in key strongholds like Jhalawar and Bharatpur, could foreshadow challenges for the BJP in the upcoming 2028 State Assembly elections.

title: IMD Warns Cyclone Arnab May Intensify as Deep Depression Approaches Andhra-Odisha Coasts
summary: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an update regarding Cyclone Arnab, a deep depression currently over the Bay of Bengal. The agency reports that the system intensified into a depression and is expected to strengthen further within the next 10 hours. Officials state it is very likely to cross the north Andhra Pradesh-South Odisha coasts between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur as a deep depression by the night of September 23. Under the system's influence, heavy rains are forecast for isolated places in parts of Andhra Pradesh, including Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam, and Rayalaseema, from September 22 to 25. Residents are advised to follow the latest advisories from the IMD and local authorities.

title: Experts Warn Against AI Hype and Corporate Misrepresentation
summary: The article critiques the recent surge in AI hype, arguing that claims of breakthroughs by companies like Anthropic and OpenAI are often marketing narratives rather than genuine advancements. Experts in cybersecurity and mathematics have debunked specific incidents, attributing hacking to negligence and mathematical claims to plagiarism. The author contends that framing AI as a superintelligent threat distracts from tangible issues like data privacy, environmental damage from data centers, and corporate accountability, urging policymakers to rely on independent experts rather than press releases.

title: AI Sovereignty: Balancing Open Source Tech with Big Tech Dependencies
summary: The article discusses the shift from US-dominated AI development to a landscape seeking AI sovereignty. While US labs initially drove rapid expansion, open-weight models from Chinese entities like DeepSeek and Moonshot have disrupted this dominance. Concerns over power concentration have sparked discussions on sovereignty, defined as localized security and adherence to local laws. However, the Stanford HAI report notes that many sovereignty offerings still deepen dependencies on US tech. The piece argues that true sovereignty requires open source AI, specifically a federated system of models and protocols, to avoid fragmentation and ensure genuine participation across the entire AI stack.

title: Experts Call for Independent AI Accident Investigators
summary: Following recent incidents where AI systems from OpenAI and Google misbehaved, over 100 experts have called for independent safety evaluators to police AI labs. Michael Chatzipanagiotis suggests borrowing from the aviation industry, where separate investigators handle accidents. Marius Hobbhahn notes that while independent groups are useful, full transparency and access to training records are currently lacking. The current system allows companies to frame incidents favorably, raising concerns about the need for a third-party approach.

title: Bihar Minister Criticized for Moral Policing Remark Amid Minor Harassment Case
summary: Bihar Minister Shreyasi Singh faced widespread criticism after describing moral policing as 'decent and elegant' in response to a viral video showing the alleged harassment of two minors in Jamui. While Singh clarified that the manner of confrontation was unacceptable, opposition leaders including Pawan Khera and the Aam Aadmi Party accused her of defending the harassers. Police registered an FIR, arrested three minors, and formed a Special Investigation Team, while authorities warned against sharing footage that reveals minors' identities.

title: NVIDIA Unveils DLSS 5 and RTX Kit Updates for Game Developers
summary: NVIDIA has announced DLSS 5, featuring 3D-Guided Neural Rendering designed to enhance lighting and material detail in real-time 3D rendering while preserving artistic intent. The technology operates on a one-frame-in, one-frame-out model and is available now in NBA 2K27. Concurrent updates include NVIDIA ACE, which expands speech and inference capabilities for interactive characters, and RTX Kit 2026.3, which introduces support for high-density geometry and neural texture workflows. Additionally, RTX Mega Geometry 2.0 enables streaming continuous level-of-detail clusters, set to arrive soon in Gears of War: E-Day to boost performance and image quality.

title: NVIDIA Releases Isaac ROS 5.0 for Agentic Robotics Development
summary: NVIDIA released Isaac ROS 5.0 at the ROSCon conference in Toronto to advance agentic, open-source robotics development. The update introduces new agentic workflows, platform support for ROS Lyrical and Ubuntu 24.04, and specialized skills like FoundationPose that enable AI agents to track objects up to 5.5x faster. By combining GPU-accelerated computing with familiar open-source tools, the platform aims to help developers deploy high-performance applications on edge devices like the NVIDIA Jetson. Several robotics companies, including Mentee Robotics and Universal Robots, are already integrating the system to accelerate perception and deployment.

title: OpenAI Expressed Concerns Over Autonomous AI Risks and Safety Standards
summary: OpenAI has expressed concern regarding the risks associated with AI systems that can improve themselves autonomously without safety measures. The company warns that such systems could grow faster than human understanding and oversight allows, potentially becoming uncontrollable and misaligned with human interests. OpenAI is calling for global technical standards and international cooperation to regulate advanced AI development, emphasizing the need for unified regulations across countries and both open and closed AI models to ensure safety and alignment with human values.

title: Tesla cancels service appointments for false camera alerts in FSD update
summary: Tesla confirmed a bug in its v14.3.9 Full Self-Driving update that falsely flags clean cameras as dirty, prompting unnecessary service visits. The company is canceling these appointments and expects a fix in the upcoming v14.3.10 update, though release notes do not yet confirm specific changes. Drivers reported the alert on clean cars, often triggered by glare, while Tesla Support proactively canceled booked visits.

title: Sharad Pawar Urges Protection of Tata Group's Charitable Ownership Structure Amid Board Dispute
summary: Nationalist Congress Party chief Sharad Pawar has publicly backed Noel Tata in his campaign to maintain Tata Sons as a private entity and safeguard the group's charitable ownership. Pawar, citing his role as a mediator in other industrial disputes, emphasized that the Tata group's Articles of Association must be respected, granting trust-nominated directors a decisive voice in appointing the chairman. He warned that weakening these trusts undermines essential institutions like the Tata Memorial Hospital. Meanwhile, the Shapoorji Pallonji group, holding an 18 per cent stake, has also called for the company's public listing, creating a divergence in opinions within the broader business community.

title: Gabelli Fund Adds AMD to Portfolio Amid AI Focus
summary: Gabelli Investment Management Firm released its Global Growth Fund second-quarter 2026 investor letter, reporting a 12.84% return. The Fund added Advanced Micro Devices Inc. as a new position, representing 1.1% of net assets as of June 30, 2026. While acknowledging the risk and potential of AMD, the fund manager stated their conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns within a shorter time frame. The portfolio remained concentrated with 45 companies at quarter-end.

title: Sebi Settles Adani Group Firms Over Disclosure and Audit Violations
summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) settled adjudication proceedings against five Adani group companies for a collective ₹1.5 crore. The settlements address alleged violations concerning the disclosure of related-party transactions and audit report irregularities, including signing reports without valid peer review certificates. These issues stem from a 2023 Hindenburg Research report. The companies paid specific amounts, with Adani Enterprises paying ₹76.05 lakh and Adani Green Energy paying ₹45.50 lakh, while others paid ₹9.75 lakh each. The firms proposed settling without admitting or denying the findings.

title: X Launches Crypto Trading Feature via Partner Platforms
summary: Social media company X, formerly Twitter, has launched a feature allowing U.S. users to trade digital assets including Bitcoin and Ethereum. The platform redirects users to partner platforms such as Interactive Brokers and Gemini after they tap a crypto tag and a trade button. This move is part of X's broader plan to become an 'everything app' with banking features, as stated by Elon Musk. X currently offers real-time prices and charts for various cryptocurrencies.

title: Tesla Austin Robotaxi Fleet Drops to Eight Active Vehicles
summary: Tesla's active robotaxi fleet in Austin has declined to just eight vehicles over the past seven days, according to data from community tracker Robotaxi Tracker. This figure mirrors the number present when the service launched in June 2025. Although Tesla registered 476 vehicles in Texas, including 67 Cybercabs, trackers have only observed 179 in the last 30 days and just eight carrying passengers recently. An unnamed source attributes the low operational numbers to safety concerns that prevent Tesla from deploying the system at scale, suggesting it is preferable to run a few vehicles in geo-fenced areas rather than risking accidents.

title: West Bengal Chief Minister Meets Mukesh Ambani to Seek Industrial Investment
summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari met industrialist Mukesh Ambani in Mumbai on Monday evening to discuss industrial prospects and employment generation. Adhikari, who posted about the visit on X, highlighted the state's readiness to welcome investments that empower youth and drive sustainable economic resurgence. The discussion included exchanging thoughts on industrial growth possibilities in West Bengal.

title: Palo Alto Networks Launches AI-Driven Cybersecurity Service Using Anthropic and OpenAI Models
summary: On September 22, Palo Alto Networks announced the launch of Unit 42 Continuous Frontier AI Defense, a cybersecurity service designed to help businesses identify security vulnerabilities. The offering utilizes advanced AI models from Anthropic, including Claude Mythos 5, and OpenAI, specifically GPT-5.6-Cyber, alongside open-weight models. The service continuously tests web applications, APIs, and cloud infrastructure to detect potential attack paths as digital environments evolve. Additionally, it provides guidance on fixing security gaps through code-level fixes and virtual patching options. The service will be available globally via annual subscriptions, with pricing determined by the selected mix of AI models.

title: Google Launches Premium AI Laptops with Hardware Partners
summary: Google has launched the Googlebook, a new line of premium laptops priced from $899 and up, designed to integrate its Gemini AI deeply into the laptop experience. Manufactured by partners including Acer, Asus, Dell, HP, and Lenovo, these devices feature 13- to 15-inch touch screens, up to 14 hours of battery life, and processors from Intel, Qualcomm, or MediaTek. Google aims to bridge the gap between Android phones and laptops, offering seamless syncing and on-device AI capabilities, with pre-installed Google AI Pro subscriptions included. The laptops are available for preorder starting Monday, with shipments in the US beginning Oct. 4.

title: RBI Updates Valuation Rules for InvIT and REIT Units
summary: The Reserve Bank of India issued amendments to valuation directions for Infrastructure Investment Trusts and Real Estate Investment Trusts to ensure uniform practices. Under the new framework, units are valued at the Net Asset Value disclosed by the trust. However, if a trust fails to compute or disclose the NAV as specified by SEBI regulations, or if units are classified as infrequently traded, their value is treated as Re 1. The changes take effect immediately and apply to both InvITs and REITs, with existing methodologies continuing for other unquoted instruments.

title: Samsung C&T and Kairos Power Partner for Nuclear Reactor Project
summary: Samsung C&T has agreed to provide up to USD100 million through direct investment and engineering services to support Kairos Power's Hermes 2 demonstration plant in Oak Ridge, Tennessee. This investment strengthens Kairos Power's financial readiness for its fluoride salt-cooled high-temperature reactor technology. Additionally, Samsung C&T will join Kairos Power's engineering team, focusing on power-generation systems and balance-of-plant scope. The collaboration builds on a trilateral memorandum of understanding signed in August, aiming to establish a framework for reliable project execution and future commercial deployment.

title: Flipkart Accidentally Leaks iPhone 17 Price on Instagram
summary: Flipkart's official Instagram account accidentally posted a price tag of Rs. 7X,XXX for the iPhone 17 during a promotional carousel. This leaked figure is substantially lower than the expected Rs. 1,00,000 and Apple's current starting price of Rs. 99,900 in India. The post, intended to discuss phone myths, was published on September 22, 2026, by The Hindu businessline as a company press release. Social media users speculate the social media manager may face consequences for the error.

title: Webinar Examines Real-World Google Workspace Breaches and Response Strategies
summary: BleepingComputer and Material Security will host a live webinar on September 23 titled "Breach autopsy: How fast-growing companies are breached through Google Workspace." The event features Rajan Kapoor and Rick Fitzgerald, who will examine real, publicly documented breaches where attackers used social engineering and malicious OAuth applications. The discussion will cover the initial access phase, the critical first hours of response, and which security controls provide the greatest value for organizations with limited resources.

title: ECB Urges Stricter EU Crypto Regulations and Stablecoin Bans
summary: Europe's central banks, led by the ECB, have issued recommendations to tighten EU crypto regulations. They call for a wider ban on interest payments on stablecoins, extending the prohibition to activities like staking and lending that mimic interest effects. The central banks also urge stronger tools against foreign-pegged tokens and EU-level supervision of crypto firms. These proposals feed into the European Commission's review of the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA). While the recommendations are not binding, EU diplomats expect a revision in 2027, subject to approval by the European Parliament and member states. The ECB highlighted concerns about synthetic central bank digital currencies and the risks posed by US dollar stablecoins in Europe.

title: Google and Georgia Power agree on nuclear uprate support
summary: Google and Georgia Power have reached an agreement to support Extended Power Uprates at the Edwin I Hatch nuclear plant. Under the deal, Google will subscribe to a new tariff structure to receive zero-emission credits for the additional carbon-free power generated. The filings, lodged with the Georgia Public Service Commission on 21 September, include a request to approve the uprate for two units at Hatch. Georgia Power states the program is an innovation designed to help large customers meet clean energy goals while protecting non-participating customers from incremental costs.

title: Sebi Settles Disclosure Case Against Five Adani Group Firms
summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) settled adjudication proceedings against five Adani group companies regarding alleged violations of related-party transaction disclosures and audit compliance. The settlement, totaling Rs 1.50 crore, stems from an examination into issues highlighted in the Hindenburg report. Adani Enterprises paid Rs 76.05 lakh, while Adani Green Energy paid Rs 45.50 lakh, with the remaining three firms paying Rs 9.75 lakh each.

title: EU Regulator Fines Google €403 Million Over Location Data Violations
summary: Ireland's Data Protection Commission has fined Google €403 million for alleged violations regarding the handling of users' location information. The regulator determined the company failed to process this sensitive data in a lawful, fair, and transparent manner. The investigation, which began six years ago, examined Google's Web & App Activity and Location History services under the GDPR from 2018 until February 2020. Deputy Commissioner Graham Doyle noted that while location data offers benefits, it also reveals significant private information about individuals.

title: George Osborne Blames Datacentre Nimbys for Holding Britain Back
summary: George Osborne, now leading AI at OpenAI, stated that datacentre nimbys are impeding Britain's development. Speaking at a festival in Somerset, he compared the resistance to building datacentres to opposition against roads and railways. While the government has classified AI datacentres as critical national infrastructure to expedite construction, the Green Party in England has called for a moratorium. Protesters across the UK, including in London and Edinburgh, argue these structures damage the landscape, consume excessive resources, and divert investment from affordable housing. Verity Harding from Cambridge University suggested the opposition stems from a lack of control rather than the technology itself.

title: ECB and EU central banks suggest dropping stablecoin deposit rules
summary: The European System of Central Banks (ESCB) advised regulators to drop the requirement for stablecoin issuers to hold a minimum proportion of reserves as bank deposits. The ECB and other EU central banks stated that such deposits could expose lenders to runs and instability. Instead, they recommended specifying a minimum percentage held in assets maturing within one and five working days. This recommendation responds to a consultation on MiCA regulations.

title: mm2 Asia's Rescue Investor Gets Waiver to Avoid General Offer
summary: mm2 Asia's proposed rescue investor, MMRA, has received a waiver from the Securities Industry Council to take control of the entertainment company without making a mandatory general offer. The placement involves subscribing for 16.34 billion new shares, with proceeds primarily allocated for debt repayment and working capital. This move aims to address mm2 Asia's financial difficulties and restore its viability as a going concern, pending independent shareholder approval.

title: Wall Street bets Meta's AI agent Muse will drive new revenue
summary: Wall Street analysts anticipate Meta's new AI agent, Muse, will evolve into a major revenue engine. Since its launch, Meta Platforms shares have surged more than 20 per cent, outpacing major tech peers. Brokerages estimate that if Muse attracts 1 billion users by 2027 with a 3 per cent paid conversion rate, it could generate US$10.8 billion in annualised revenue. Analysts cite strong product-market fit and a free tier as drivers of early traction, noting 2.8 million downloads in the first 12 days.

title: Fed Official Discusses Discount Window Modernization and Treasury Market Role
summary: Philip N. Jefferson, Oversight Governor for the Division of Monetary Affairs at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, delivered remarks at the 2026 Treasury Market Conference regarding the modernization of the Federal Reserve's discount window. He outlined three key dimensions of this initiative: business process improvements to standardize operations, automation enhancements through the Discount Window Direct portal which now handles over 60 percent of requests, and strengthened coordination with the Federal Home Loan Banks. Jefferson noted that these changes make borrowing faster and less burdensome, thereby reducing frictions that might cause healthy banks to hesitate. Furthermore, he stressed the critical role of the discount window in supporting Treasury market resilience, particularly by accepting Treasury securities as collateral with same-day value to prevent forced sales during market stress.

title: DeepSeek, OpenAI, and Anthropic to Discuss AI Risks at UN Security Council
summary: The 15-member UN Security Council is scheduled to convene in New York during the UN General Assembly's annual session. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman plans to address the session, according to Reuters. Diplomats also expect participation from senior Anthropic representatives. DeepSeek and fellow Chinese AI startup Moonshot have been invited to make statements, one source told Reuters. DeepSeek's founder, Liang Wenfeng, is not expected to be present, though arrangements could still shift, the source warned.

title: Tesla Faces Major Race Discrimination Trial in California Over Alleged Harassment
summary: Tesla is facing a major race discrimination trial in California. The lawsuit, brought by California's Civil Rights Department, alleges the company allowed pervasive racial harassment and discrimination to go unchecked for years at its Fremont assembly plant, according to The Guardian.

title: Shopify Builds Continual Learning Loop with PyTorch and vLLM
summary: Shopify has developed a continual learning loop using PyTorch and vLLM to compress production failures into model weights daily. This approach allows their specialized model to surpass frontier-model quality while reducing serving costs by 96%. The system captures production knowledge through a self-healing pipeline that converts failures into training signals. Additionally, prompt compression techniques reduce the system prompt length from roughly 6,000 tokens to about 1,500 learned gist tokens, resulting in improved latency and throughput. The GraphQL agent serves up to 2,000 requests per minute, demonstrating the loop's effectiveness in production.

title: Meta Tests Community Notes in Latin America Amid Transparency Concerns
summary: Meta announced a test of its Community Notes program in sixteen Spanish-speaking countries across Latin America, citing US figures showing 1.4 million contributors and 200 million views in July. However, analysts argue the initiative lacks transparency, noting that only 50,000 notes were published against nearly 50 million EU fact-checks. The Oversight Board warned that Community Notes should not replace professional fact-checking, yet Meta has not defined success metrics or publication rates for the new rollout.

title: UN Leaders Urged to Prioritize Undersea Cable Resilience in AI Agenda
summary: As world leaders convene for the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, an article argues that the focus on artificial intelligence risks must not overshadow the protection of undersea cables, which carry 99 percent of international data traffic. Recent incidents, including autonomous cyberattacks and physical cable cuts in the Red Sea and West Africa, have caused billions in damages and significant connectivity outages. While a new UN report provides 39 recommendations for enhancing cable resilience, these non-binding measures require governments to adopt legal frameworks and invest in repair infrastructure, a challenge particularly acute in regions like Africa where repair vessels are scarce. The author contends that safeguarding this critical infrastructure is essential for a robust AI governance agenda.

title: Treasury Trading Concentrates at Month-End Index Strike Times
summary: Research indicates that trading in U.S. Treasury securities is becoming increasingly concentrated on the last trading day of each month and around specific index strike times. This concentration has intensified over the past decade, with activity shifting from 3 p.m. to 4 p.m. following a change in strike time by a major fixed-income index provider in January 2021. The effects are most pronounced on month-end days when indexes are rebalanced, with the half-hour interval between 3:45 and 4:15 p.m. accounting for more than one quarter of total daily activity on these days in 2025. The authors conclude that index pricing conventions materially shape when Treasury trading occurs.

title: Foundry Waste Dumped Near Coimbatore Airport Raises Concerns
summary: Heaps of foundry sand and mixed waste were discovered dumped on vacant plots along Chinniyampalayam–Irugur Road, near the Coimbatore International Airport runway. During a visit by The Hindu, officials found the waste at multiple spots on land acquired for airport expansion. An environmentalist stated that instead of dumping, the waste's suitability for reuse should be assessed. Conversely, a District Rural Development Agency official claimed the administration was unaware of the dumping and promised to inspect the site soon.

title: JPMorgan CEO Warns US Against Punishing India Over Russian Oil
summary: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon has urged the United States to rethink imposing steep tariffs on Indian buyers of Russian oil. Speaking at a conference in Mumbai, Dimon warned that punishing India could disrupt global oil markets and that Indian refineries cannot easily switch to alternative crude grades. This comes after US President Donald Trump signed legislation allowing tariffs of up to 100 per cent on major Russian energy buyers. In response, Indian Ambassador Vinay Mohan Kwatra stated that India's energy policy prioritizes the security and affordability of energy for its people, noting that the country imports over 85 per cent of its crude oil.

title: US Sanctions Law Grants Tariff Power Over India
summary: The US has empowered President Donald Trump with a new tool under sanctions law to target nations purchasing Russian oil and gas, potentially impacting India. While headlines suggest a 100% tariff, the law does not automatically impose this on Indian goods. Instead, it serves as a conditional weapon Washington may use if statutory conditions are met, creating uncertainty for Indian industries and exports.

title: DSS Condemns Pratap Simha for Remarks Against Dalit Community
summary: The Karnataka State Dalit Sangharsh Samiti (DSS) strongly condemned former MP Pratap Simha for remarks against the Dalit community and the wearing of blue scarves, describing them as highly objectionable. Speaking at a press conference, DSS State convener D.G. Sagar stated that Simha's comments reflected a deep disregard for the history of Karnataka's Dalit movement. Sagar demanded an unconditional apology and warned that such statements could provoke communal tensions. He also opposed a proposed Hindu Samavesha in Kalaburagi city.

title: J&K Government Screens and Withdraws Thousands of College Books
summary: The Jammu and Kashmir government informed the Assembly on September 22, 2026, that it had screened approximately 21.81 lakh books and withdrawn 4,812 from government and private college libraries since July. The withdrawn collection included 518 banned books and 4,249 non-banned books. Officials described the scrutiny process as laborious and noted that at least 1,752 books were referred for expert examination. The action follows directives to identify material violating religious sentiments or laws, triggered by allegations of inappropriate content in books under a central scheme.

title: India demands credible action on terror from Pakistan
summary: The Ministry of External Affairs stated Pakistan must take credible action against cross-border terrorism before the world believes its claims. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal accused Pakistan of misrepresenting facts and spreading falsehoods regarding a Permanent Court of Arbitration ruling, calling it an illegally constituted court. Jaiswal noted India seeks constructive ties with Bangladesh and provided updates on missing Indians in Nepal, where a forensic team is working on samples.

title: BJP Likely to Retain Most Rajya Sabha Seats in Uttar Pradesh
summary: The Election Commission announced polls for twelve Rajya Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and West Bengal, with voting scheduled for October 16. Analysis suggests the BJP-led alliance will likely retain eight seats in Uttar Pradesh, while the Samajwadi Party could win two. The BJP is also expected to gain a seat in West Bengal following the resignation of the incumbent. These elections may mark the end of the BSP's representation in Parliament due to vacancies and term expirations.

title: Tan Tock Seng Hospital highlights need for better health literacy in community care
summary: Tan Tock Seng Hospital's initiative to manage delirium at home highlights a broader need for improved health literacy among Singapore's aging population. The author argues that while bringing care closer to home is vital, families and caregivers must also be equipped to recognize significant changes in cognition or function. Practical health literacy should extend beyond basic knowledge to include identifying medical issues like delirium and knowing where to seek help, ensuring capability moves into the community alongside care.

title: Angel One Founder Buys Entire Luxury Tower in Mumbai
summary: Embassy Developments announced a Memorandum of Understanding to sell an entire G+7 residential tower in Juhu to Dinesh Thakkar, founder of Angel One. The deal, valued at approximately Rs 711 crore, covers a carpet area of 63,000 sq ft and is described as the largest single residential unit transaction in the country. The project, named 'Angelus', is part of a larger five-tower development in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region scheduled for completion by December 2031.

title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Highlights Five Critical AI Safety Sessions for Founders
summary: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 will host five specialized sessions focused on AI safety and security as the technology transitions from demonstrations to critical business applications. These sessions, scheduled for the AI Stage and Real World AI Stage, address challenges such as enterprise deployment hurdles, agent security infrastructure, cloud complexity, and physical system reliability. Industry leaders from companies like Anthropic, Okta, AWS, Shield AI, and GM will share insights on building trustworthy AI. The event runs October 13–15 at Moscone West in San Francisco, attracting over 10,000 attendees including founders, investors, and tech leaders.

title: AstroForge Plans AI-Controlled Spacecraft Launch in 2027
summary: AstroForge is developing an autonomous control stack called 'Solo' to operate its spacecraft without ground intervention, addressing communication difficulties experienced with its Odin mission in 2025. The company plans to launch its first autonomous spacecraft in 2027, which will rely on an in-house transformer-based model trained on approximately 2,500 sensors. CEO Matthew Gialich stated the company is removing Earth-based radio reception for this mission to test full onboard intelligence, despite the risks associated with neural network reliability in space.

title: DFC CEO Says US Can Compete With China in Africa
summary: Ben Black, CEO of the US International Development Finance Corporation, stated that the US can still compete with China in African markets despite Beijing's established presence. Speaking at The Next 3 Billion in New York, Black pointed to recent investments in African digital networks, Ukrainian energy storage, and uranium in Niger as examples of how the DFC balances risk and value for American taxpayers. He argued that falling behind does not mean ceding territory, noting that the agency structures deals around market risks to advance US interests.

title: Trump Addresses UN Amid Regional Tensions and Policy Announcements
summary: Donald Trump addressed world leaders at the United Nations in New York, framing his second term as a period of decisive action against perceived threats. He claimed to have defanged Iran militarily and threatened to annihilate the regime if it does not capitulate. Trump also touted his border security record, stating zero illegal aliens were admitted in the past 16 months. However, his interventionist policies in Latin America, including the raid on Venezuela and sanctions on Cuba, drew sharp criticism from other leaders like Brazil's Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who defended the sovereignty of those nations.

title: Amateur Archaeologist Discovers Largest Roman Coin Hoard in Germany
summary: Oliver Riedl, an amateur archaeologist, discovered 934 Roman silver denarii in a field near Wesseling, western Germany. Experts from the LVR Office for the Preservation of Archaeological Monuments identified the find as the largest coin treasure from the era of Emperor Hadrian. The hoard, weighing 3.1kg, was likely buried deliberately in the second century AD to safeguard the wealth, as banking systems were non-existent at that time.

title: Domestic Violence Kills Man in Ramanathapuram; Another Feud-Related Death Reported
summary: Boominathan, 45, died of injuries at Ramanathapuram Government Medical College Hospital on Sunday after being assaulted by his wife Revathi during a domestic altercation. Police stated the couple had a history of quarrels due to financial setbacks and alcohol addiction. Revathi allegedly struck him with a wooden log on Monday morning. She called an ambulance, but he died. Police arrested Revathi and granted her bail. In a separate incident, a 25-year-old man named Sakthivel Pandi was stabbed to death in Mandalamanickam village over a feud originating from a Kabaddi tournament two years ago. Police arrested Murugan and his sons in that case.

title: Anand Giridharadas's New Book Explores Compassionate Journalism Through a Subway Incident
summary: Anand Giridharadas, currently recognized as a progressive political commentator, has released a new book titled Man in the Mirror. This work marks a return to his early roots as a narrative storyteller. The book recounts the tale of a subway confrontation involving Jordan Neely, a homeless man with mental illness, and former Marine Daniel Penny, who was acquitted of killing him. Giridharadas presents the book as a model of journalism that demonstrates compassion for all parties involved in the incident.

title: Xbox to hand Halo development to Activision amid job cuts
summary: Xbox announced it is cutting hundreds of jobs and restructuring its studios as part of a company-wide reset. Consequently, Activision will take over development of future Halo games, while the current Halo studio will focus on supporting existing titles. Xbox chief executive Asha Sharma stated the gaming division had not been healthy, citing rising hardware costs as a pressure. Analysts view the move as a significant shift for the franchise.

title: UN Chief Guterres Calls for Security Council Reform
summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres delivered a final address to the 81st session of the UN General Assembly on September 22, 2026, calling for urgent reform of the UN Security Council. He argued that the body, established in 1945, fails to reflect today's geopolitical realities, specifically noting the absence of permanent African representation. Guterres pointed to deep divisions among permanent members like the U.S., China, Russia, France, and the U.K., which have rendered the Council ineffective in halting conflicts in Gaza and Russia. He warned that without a multilateral system centered on the UN that reflects current power dynamics, humanity faces a trajectory of fragmentation and mistrust in an increasingly multipolar world.

title: Houthis Accuse Saudi Arabia of Deadly Port Strike Amid Escalating Regional Conflict
summary: Yemen's Houthis accused Saudi Arabia of carrying out a deadly airstrike on a key port city on Tuesday, an event occurring over a week into a broader offensive that has seen the group seize control of a crucial strait. The conflict has displaced nearly 130,000 people across seven governorates and resulted in at least 154 deaths in the past two days, according to military sources. While Houthi sources reported 118 deaths in specific governorates, government sources cited 36 killed in their ranks. In response, G7 nations urged the Houthis to halt cross-border strikes and return to the political process. Meanwhile, the UK and France have agreed to provide military support to Saudi Arabia to help secure its energy infrastructure, though France clarified this does not involve direct participation in the conflict.

title: Trump Calls for Global Blockade on Iran at UN General Assembly
summary: Speaking at the United Nations General Assembly, US President Donald Trump called on all nations to impose a complete economic blockade on Iran, which he labeled the number one sponsor of terror. He contrasted his actions with other world leaders, claiming he has made peace and confronted threats. Trump also mentioned upcoming talks with British and Japanese leaders, as well as Gulf Cooperation Council nations, amid concerns over Iran-backed attacks on Saudi Arabia.

title: Lib Dem Leader Davey Proposes Tax Cut Funded by EU Rejoining
summary: Lib Dem leader Davey announced a plan to raise the tax-free personal allowance to £15,000, funded entirely by economic growth generated from rejoining the EU single market. He stated the proposal would take an additional 2 million people out of paying income tax, providing a £680 cut to most taxpayers. However, he noted that due to the time required to make a deal with the EU, the actual tax cuts would only happen in the final year of a parliament, potentially as late as 2034. Davey contrasted this with the Reform party's proposal, criticizing them for suggesting such cuts be funded by removing £22 billion of support from disabled people. He emphasized his party's commitment to paying for the cuts fairly and honestly, rather than through borrowing or stealth tax hikes.

title: EU Commission Proposes Energy Efficiency Standards for Data Centers
summary: The European Commission has presented a package of measures to improve the energy efficiency of data centers and their integration into the European electricity system. The package includes a delegated regulation establishing a common classification and labeling system for data centers with an installed IT power demand of more than 500 kW. A public consultation on future minimum energy-performance standards is also underway. The Commission estimates that recovering waste heat from European data centers could meet the needs of approximately 4 million households.

title: Nepal's $20m Climate Loss Claim Covers Only 0.7% of Flood Costs
summary: The Nepali government has requested $20m from the UN loss-and-damage fund following devastating floods in late August that killed more than 1,400 people. According to Carbon Brief analysis, this request covers only 0.7% of the estimated $2.7bn in physical damage and economic losses, or 0.3% of total recovery needs including $4.8bn in reconstruction costs. While Nepal's claim makes it the fourth-largest to the fund, developing countries have requested $2.8bn total, yet predominantly developed nations have pledged only $822m. As of September, no money has been distributed to any country facing climate-related disasters, raising questions about the fund's ability to respond to emergencies.

title: Three Turkish firms partner to build solar and battery project in Serbia
summary: Fortis Energy and İnelso Energy Systems have signed a joint agreement with Turkish EPC contractor Enkraft Energy to construct a 30 MWp solar power plant combined with a battery energy storage system in Serbia's Vojvodina region. The EUR 25. 5 million project has reached ready-to-build status, with construction permits expected within a month. Once operational, the facility is projected to generate more than 40 GWh of electricity annually, equivalent to the consumption of over 11,000 households, while avoiding an estimated 19,000 tonnes of CO2 emissions per year.

title: Autopsy Confirms Hayden Panettiere Died From Drug Overdose
summary: The Greenville County Coroner's Office in South Carolina completed an autopsy on Hayden Panettiere, confirming she died from the toxic effects of fentanyl, Xanax, and several other drugs. The coroner stated the death was an accident with no signs of trauma. Panettiere, 36, was found unresponsive at a residence last month. Emergency responders attempted advanced cardiac life support, but resuscitation was unsuccessful. Her ex-boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, and his brother were present when services arrived. Panettiere had previously spoken openly about her struggles with substance abuse and postpartum depression.

title: Panelists Debate Delhi Safety After Park Rape Case
summary: A panel discussion addressed the gang rape of a 17-year-old girl in Delhi's Astha Kunj Park, highlighting systemic failures in public park security and women's safety. Congress MP Renuka Chowdhury criticized persistent crimes, stating the national capital has been the capital of rape for many years. The debate emphasized the need for strict accountability, urgent parliamentary intervention, and robust reforms to ensure public safety for women.

title: IRA drives U.S. solar capex to $12.2B by 2026
summary: Terawatt PV Research forecasts that Inflation Reduction Act-stimulated capital expenditure for U.S. solar manufacturing will reach $12.2 billion by the end of 2026. This cumulative figure represents more than half of all solar PV manufacturing spending since 2001. Annual spending has exceeded $2.5 billion since 2023, with 2024 recording a record $4.14 billion, primarily driven by First Solar and Qcells. The report projects Texas will emerge as the dominant hub for module production in 2026, surpassing Ohio, as the industry expands its domestic capacity.

title: Trump Shifts Greenland Focus to Military Security Deal
summary: US President Donald Trump is shifting his strategy regarding Greenland from seeking territorial acquisition to securing a permanent US military security arrangement. He is set to sign a trilateral agreement with Denmark and Greenland at the United Nations General Assembly in New York. The pact allows the US to establish military facilities at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig, expanding its footprint beyond the existing Pituffik Space Base. While Danish officials assert the agreement respects sovereignty and places security under NATO's collective responsibility, the full legal implications remain unclear. The deal marks a major shift from Trump's earlier demands for ownership, which were firmly rejected by Greenlandic and Danish leaders.

title: Consumer Champion Anna Tims Discusses Customer Service Issues and Tips
summary: Anna Tims, a consumer champion for the Guardian, hosts a live session to address reader inquiries regarding customer service. She notes that while AI tools can assist with troubleshooting, they often fail to resolve specific complaints, leading to repetitive platitudes. Tims advises customers to remain calm, gather all relevant evidence such as booking references, and utilize public platforms like Twitter to pressure companies into action. She highlights that although legal frameworks like the Consumer Rights Act 2015 exist, regulatory bodies are frequently overstretched. Consequently, she suggests patronizing companies that demonstrate exceptional service and checking for proper contact details before committing to a provider.

title: Tax Tribunal Grants Conditional Relief for Income Dispute
summary: A Haryana resident faced an income addition of Rs 11.22 crore after the Income Tax Department scrutinized his return for Assessment Year 2017-18, citing unexplained cash deposits of Rs 85.93 lakh and unsecured loans of Rs 9.26 crore. The taxpayer appealed to the ITAT Chandigarh, proposing to plant 500 trees at the Yamuna Bank, Panipat, Samalakha Site as a measure of social responsibility. The tribunal accepted this proposal conditionally, sending the matter back to the Assessing Officer to verify compliance. The taxpayer must complete the plantation or pay for it within one month; otherwise, the original income addition order will be restored. The dispute remains unresolved as the unexplained money has not yet been substantiated.

title: British Father Admits Causing Son's Death in Cyprus Hotel Fall
summary: Joshua Foster, a British man from Essex, pleaded guilty to causing the death of his two-year-old son through a reckless act at the King Evelthon Beach Hotel and Resort in Chlorakas, Cyprus. The boy fell from the fourth floor on 12 July. Foster admitted the charge to avoid a lengthy trial. His lawyer stated the plea allows the family to move forward without reliving the tragedy in court. A further hearing is scheduled for 5 October.

title: Armed Group Blockade Slumps Libya's Sharara Oilfield Production
summary: Libya's largest oilfield, Sharara, has seen crude production slump from an estimated 340,000 barrels per day to about 120,000 bpd after an armed group closed Valve No. 7. The National Oil Corporation stated this closure caused pressure buildup and warned that continued shutdowns would halt exports, harm state revenues, and expose the transport system to risks, potentially necessitating a force majeure declaration.

title: Turkey's COP31 Agenda Targets Global Electrification and AI Governance
summary: Turkish Minister of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change Murat Kurum outlined the COP31 Action Agenda, which targets raising the share of electricity in final energy consumption to 35% by 2035. Kurum stressed the need for responsible artificial intelligence deployment to advance clean technologies. The agenda also includes goals to halve municipal waste increases and reduce building energy-use intensity by at least 25%.

title: Typhoon Dujuan Brings Flooding and Casualties to Japan
summary: Footage shows flooded streets and rescue efforts following Typhoon Dujuan, which brought torrential rain to the Tokyo region. The storm triggered landslides in Chiba and Kanagawa prefectures, swamped roads, and caused flight cancellations and transport delays. Officials confirmed at least four deaths and six missing persons on Tuesday as search and rescue teams worked in affected neighborhoods. Thousands of homes lost power due to record-breaking rainfall disrupting travel across the capital region.

title: Trump to Defend Iran War and Gaza Efforts at UN
summary: U.S. President Donald Trump is expected to deliver a speech at the United Nations on September 22, 2026, where he will defend his ongoing war with Iran and highlight his efforts as a peacemaker. The event is overshadowed by concerns over the war's failure to meet White House objectives and economic damage from the Strait of Hormuz closure. Analysts from the International Crisis Group suggest Trump will contrast his peacemaker claims with military operations, while facing skepticism over a security deal in Greenland. Trump also plans to meet with leaders from Britain, Ukraine, Japan, and Venezuela.

title: PureSky Energy Launches Illinois Community Solar Project for Low-Income Residents
summary: PureSky Energy has commenced commercial operations at McLean 1 Community Solar, marking the company's first solar project in Illinois. The 1. 98-MWDC facility in Bloomington-Normal is dedicated exclusively to low- and moderate-income households through the Illinois Solar for All program. Participating subscribers receive guaranteed savings equal to 50% of the value of their solar credits. The project incorporates pollinator-friendly land management practices to enhance biodiversity. Nicholas Topping, VP of community solar at PureSky, stated that dedicating the project to income-eligible households is an important milestone.

title: Meghalaya High Court Orders Transfer of Detained Foreigners
summary: The Meghalaya High Court ordered the state government to transfer approximately 30 foreign nationals who completed their prison sentences but remained incarcerated to a temporary detention centre in Shillong by September 28. The court, hearing a suo motu matter, directed the transfer to the MBOSE Hostel facility, which has a capacity for around 60 inmates. Authorities were instructed to assist with deportation or repatriation and to address compensation for those detained beyond their sentence completion dates. The matter was posted for further hearing on September 28.

title: India demands credible action from Pakistan on cross-border terror before trusting its words
summary: India's Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated that Pakistan must demonstrate credible action against cross-border terrorism before the world believes its promises. This demand follows Pakistani airstrikes in eastern Afghanistan's Kunar and Paktika provinces, which India condemned as aggression against a sovereign neighbor. The attacks reportedly killed at least three civilians, a toll confirmed by the United Nations, while Pakistan claimed the strikes killed 28 militants. India reaffirmed its steadfast support for Afghanistan's independence and territorial integrity.

title: JSW Group enters ECV market with Ampstar brand and ₹2,500 crore investment
summary: JSW Group has entered the electric commercial vehicle market through its new subsidiary, JSW Greentech Limited, which will operate under the Ampstar brand. The company invested ₹2,500 crore to build a manufacturing facility in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra, with an annual capacity of 15,000 vehicles. Senior executives stated that production is scheduled to commence in October 2026. At peak utilization, the facility is expected to generate a turnover of around ₹12,000 crore. The group aims to reduce India's dependence on imported fossil fuels by promoting domestic power generation.

title: Nordex Unveils New 7.3 MW Wind Turbine for Low-Wind Sites
summary: Nordex is expanding its Delta4000 onshore wind turbine range with the N193/7.X variant, which combines a 193m rotor with a maximum nominal capacity of 7.3 MW. Designed for medium- and low-wind sites, the turbine uses 95m single-piece blades and retains components from the established platform while allowing flexible power configurations. Nordex states the new model can deliver up to 14% higher energy yield than the N175/6.X at typical low- to medium-wind sites. Serial production is scheduled to begin in 2029, with a specific 6.6 MW configuration planned for Germany to address permitting and grid-connection requirements.

title: Military Aircraft Crashes Near US Air Base in Spangdahlem, Germany
summary: A military aircraft reportedly crashed near the US Air Base Spangdahlem in Germany on Tuesday. Local authorities in the Eifel region initially stated that one person was injured. The Eifel District dispatched fire and emergency response teams but declined to comment on further details. The US Air Force did not immediately respond to a request for comment regarding the incident.

title: NVIDIA Showcases AI Advancements Across Southeast Asia at Singapore Event
summary: At AI Day Singapore, NVIDIA and partners showcased breakthrough AI advancements across Southeast Asia. The event highlighted initiatives to move public sector AI from pilot to production, with partners like Singapore's HTX utilizing Nemotron models for public safety. Other organizations, including NCS and ST Engineering, are deploying agentic AI and smart city solutions. Additionally, Sea Limited became the first ASEAN enterprise to adopt the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform, aiming to scale AI capabilities for its platforms serving hundreds of millions of users. The event emphasized building region-specialized AI models tailored to local languages and industries.

title: Federal Reserve Approves BancFirst Merger with Spirit BankCorp
summary: On September 22, 2026, the Federal Reserve Board announced its approval of an application submitted by BancFirst Corporation of Oklahoma City. The approval allows BancFirst to acquire and merge with Spirit BankCorp, Inc. of Bristow, Oklahoma, which would result in the indirect acquisition of SpiritBank in Tulsa. Additionally, the Board authorized BancFirst to merge with SpiritBank and operate branches at the locations previously held by SpiritBank.

title: NVIDIA Optimizes Confidential Computing for High-Performance AI Inference
summary: As large language model inference processes sensitive data, NVIDIA Confidential Computing provides a secure pathway using memory-encrypted virtual machines and GPUs. However, secure execution changes assumptions regarding memory movement and timing, potentially introducing performance overhead. To address this, the NVIDIA performance engineering team evaluated adaptations in TensorRT LLM on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs. Testing across 16 concurrency levels revealed that confidential inference retained between 96.1% and 98.2% of baseline throughput, with latency overhead remaining between 1.2% and 4.3%. Mitigations include CC-aware memory selection, asynchronous token readbacks, and GPU timer adjustments to ensure high performance while maintaining security.

title: Oracle Cloud Layoffs Reveal Age Demographics of Affected Workers
summary: Oracle's recent layoffs in its cloud infrastructure business have shed light on the age profiles of affected workers. According to a Business Insider report, an internal document listed the job titles and ages of 546 employees from Oracle's America Cloud Infrastructure organization who were laid off. These individuals represent approximately 7.6% of the 7,185 people within the organization, indicating a significant portion of the workforce impacted by the cuts.

title: Anthropic Launches Claude Opus 5.5 with Enhanced Safety and Lower Costs
summary: Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5.5, an AI model it claims delivers performance comparable to its top-tier Fable 5.1 while costing 40% less to run. The company stated the model underwent external testing by independent AI safety research groups Frontier Design and METR before launch. Opus 5.5 is priced at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, 20% below Opus 5.

title: US-China Trade Tensions Ease After Tariffs
summary: According to unattributed reporting, the trade war initiated by the U.S. against China and other partners has eased since President Donald Trump implemented his "liberation day" tariffs in April 2025. Data indicates a rise in Chinese imports to the U.S. for five straight months, with August marking the latest increase. However, the report notes that tensions remain, particularly concerning key technology industries.

title: S&P Raises India GDP Forecast to 7% Amid Strong Growth
summary: S&P Global Ratings has raised India's GDP growth forecast for the financial year 2026-27 to 7.0%, up from 6.6%. The agency attributes this revision to robust industrial activity, healthy domestic consumption, and strong exports. Economists at S&P Global also project the Reserve Bank of India to hike the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%. This projection exceeds the Reserve Bank's estimate of 6.7% and aligns with forecasts from Moody's, reflecting economic resilience despite external challenges.

title: Syrian President Caught Scrolling Instagram During Turkish Leader's UN Speech
summary: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa was captured on camera scrolling through Instagram and interacting with his phone while Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan delivered his address at the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York. The moment occurred during the high-level General Debate on September 22, 2026, drawing attention to the informal scene involving the Syrian leader. Al-Sharaa, serving as Syria's interim president since early 2025, was attending his second UN General Assembly as part of Syria's new leadership seeking to strengthen international diplomatic engagement.

title: Apple's New Always-Listening Watch Features Spark Privacy Debate
summary: Apple has introduced new features to its latest Watch models that allow the device to listen to ambient sounds all day, transcribe conversations, and generate summaries. The author argues this creates an 'always-on surveillance' environment that violates social norms of contextual integrity, as bystanders in a room cannot consent to being recorded. Although Apple asserts that audio is never stored, encrypted, and inaccessible even to its own staff, the author expresses skepticism, citing a history of privacy failures by tech companies. The piece concludes that despite Apple's technical assurances, the fundamental issue of a device capturing private conversations without explicit consent from all parties remains a significant barrier to public acceptance.

title: Actress Apple Chan Gives Birth to Baby Girl at 32 Weeks
summary: Actress Apple Chan announced on Instagram that she gave birth to a baby girl at 32 weeks following an emergency C-section. The 37-year-old revealed the pregnancy was complicated, noting the baby weighed 1.1kg at 31 weeks before her water broke. Chan expressed her love and support for her daughter, who she described as a 'little fighter,' while also mentioning her two-year-old son.

title: Salesforce CEO Blames Microsoft for Blocking OpenAI Investment
summary: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff stated on a podcast that Microsoft's 27% stake in OpenAI blocked Salesforce from investing in the rival AI firm. Consequently, Salesforce invested in Anthropic, which is now valued at $965 billion. Benioff noted that this investment could earn Salesforce billions of dollars, while Salesforce continues to add OpenAI capabilities to its own platforms.

title: Incredible Holdings Files for Judicial Management Amid Investigations
summary: Incredible Holdings filed an application with the Singapore High Court to place the company under judicial management, proposing the appointment of Ellyn Tan Huixian and Terrence Chin Khee Loon of Forvis Mazars Consulting as joint managers. The company stated that independent director Eunice Veon Koh Pei Lee is assisting investigations by the Commercial Affairs Department and the Monetary Authority of Singapore into alleged offences under the Securities and Futures Act. Shares have been suspended since September 2022, and the company is in breach of listing rules due to missed meetings.

title: China-ASEAN Expo Connects Businesses Through Diverse Offerings
summary: The China-ASEAN Expo offers a diverse array of discoveries ranging from coffee and snacks to handicrafts, cultural traditions, and new technologies. Beyond showcasing their own offerings, ASEAN businesses are actively looking to China for products, technology, market opportunities, and new partners. CGTN's Wang Tao invites visitors to explore the event and witness these interactions firsthand.

title: Anthropic and OpenAI Launch New AI Models Amid Price War
summary: Anthropic and OpenAI have intensified competition with the release of new AI models. Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5.5, which features a 20% price reduction and improved communication style, while OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. These new models are priced at half the cost of their GPT-5.6 predecessors, with GPT-6 Luna costing $0.10 for input and $0.50 for output per million tokens. However, the author noted that Claude Opus 5.5's 'max' reasoning mode failed to complete a simple SVG generation task, hitting a token limit prematurely.

title: Singapore Core Inflation Rises to 2.2% in August Amid Global Energy Pressures
summary: Singapore's core inflation climbed to 2.2% in August, up from 2% in July, driven by higher inflation in services, retail goods, and food, according to the Singapore Department of Statistics. While overall inflation increased to 2.3%, private transport inflation slowed to 7.5% due to smaller car price increases. Analysts attribute the broader price pressures to elevated global energy prices and supply chain disruptions, warning that households could face further electricity tariff increases in the fourth quarter as businesses pass on higher input costs.

title: OpenAI Executive Sees US-China AI Cooperation as a Starting Point
summary: Sasha Baker, OpenAI's head of national security policy, stated that an AI crisis communications line between the US and China serves as a starting place for superpower relations on technology. Speaking at Semafor's Next 3 Billion event, she described the potential AI safety notification system as substantive and real, though not the end goal. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump rejected international oversight of AI, calling it a globalist scheme. OpenAI plans to internationalize the conversation around AI standards at the UN Security Council.

title: Anthropic and OpenEvidence Partner to Expand Medical AI Access Globally
summary: Anthropic and OpenEvidence announced a partnership to deploy AI-powered clinical decision support in regions without access to the technology. The collaboration offers the platform free of charge to clinicians in the United States, Europe, and about 100 low- and middle-income countries. OpenEvidence founder Daniel Nadler stated that access to medical knowledge should not depend on geography, while Anthropic president Daniela Amodei noted that market incentives alone would not have enabled this rollout. The system adapts to local contexts, addressing limitations in medical literature and specialist expertise that can impair patient care in these areas.

title: Porsche Boxster EV Spotted Charging at Tesla Supercharger in California
summary: A Porsche 718 Boxster EV prototype was spotted charging at a Tesla Supercharger in Carson, California, sparking speculation about the vehicle's release timing. Porsche CEO Michael Leiters confirmed plans to build the model, stating it is the best economic solution, though official sales details remain unannounced. The sighting supports rumors that Porsche is moving toward NACS-only charging for its smaller sportscars, potentially replacing dual-port setups found on current models. While the car remains under consideration, the prototype has been tested on public tracks and observed in public spaces, indicating progress toward production.

title: Amazon Sustainability Chief Calls for Accountability on Data Center Impact
summary: Kara Hurst, Amazon's chief sustainability officer, stated the company needs to improve communication regarding the environmental impact of its data center expansion amid growing opposition in the US and Europe. She emphasized a call for transparency and accountability, noting that Amazon's carbon footprint grew in 2025 as the company accelerated its buildout. Hurst indicated that while Amazon aims for net-zero carbon by 2040, emissions are expected to rise in the near term due to this expansion.

title: American Artist Ryan Mitchell Describes Jingdezhen as a Global Ceramic Hub
summary: American ceramic artist Ryan Mitchell has been a central figure in an international artists' program in Jingdezhen for years. During his time there, he observed the expansion of the Taoxichuan area. Mitchell characterizes Jingdezhen as a 'porcelain capital' where creativity, materials, and talent converge, emphasizing its essential role in ceramic study.

title: NVIDIA Topograph Enables Topology-Aware Workload Scheduling for AI Factories
summary: NVIDIA Topograph is an open-source toolkit that discovers and normalizes cluster network topology to enable topology-aware workload scheduling. By mapping physical interconnects like NVIDIA NVLink and Spectrum-X Ethernet, it allows schedulers to place GPUs in optimal locations, reducing latency and costs in AI factories. The tool supports Kubernetes, Slurm, and Slinky, integrating with systems like KAI Scheduler and Node Feature Discovery to automate placement decisions based on current fabric data.

title: Amazon-Flipkart Festive Sale में AI से बढ़ेगा फ्रॉड का खतरा? खरीदारी से पहले इन बातों का रखें ध्यान!
summary: बैंकों ने फेस्टिव सेल के दौरान बढ़ रहे AI शॉपिंग टूल्स के उपयोग से जुड़े फ्रॉड और डेटा प्राइवेसी जोखिमों के बारे में चेतावनी दी है। Reuters की रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, NatWest, Bank of America, ING, ASB Bank, Capital One और Commonwealth Bank of Australia जैसे बैंकों ने सुरक्षा मानकों की कमी पर चिंता जताई है। OpenAI, Anthropic, Google और Meta जैसे टेक कंपनियां इन टूल्स को बढ़ावा दे रही हैं। ग्राहकों को ऑफर की शर्तों और वेबसाइट की विश्वसनीयता की जांच करने की सलाह दी गई है।

title: Former Google Safety Chief Calls for AI Development Slowdown
summary: Tom Siegel, former Google safety chief, has called for a slowdown in AI development, warning that the industry risks repeating social media-era mistakes with severe consequences for children. He argues that self-regulation is insufficient and that outside intervention is necessary. Siegel recently joined Common Sense Media to lead its Youth AI Safety Institute, where he plans to develop independent testing standards for AI tools comparable to automotive crash testing.

title: SEBI settles Adani group cases; other stocks see updates
summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India settled adjudication proceedings against five Adani group companies for a combined ₹1.51 crore regarding disclosure lapses. The companies settled without admitting or denying findings. Other updates include IRB Infrastructure approving non-core asset monetization, RailTel receiving a ₹14.09 crore work order, Persistent Systems crossing a Nagarro takeover threshold, and leadership changes at 360 ONE WAM.

title: Brazilian Amazon Oil Discovery Sparks Hope and Fear
summary: Petrobras announced in August that it identified signs of oil in a well 175 kilometers off the coast of northern Brazil's Amapa state. Leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva visited the area, calling the find a 'passport to the future.' However, reactions are mixed. Karipuna, a local resident, fears an 'immense disaster' if a leak reaches the Curipi River, while fishermen worry about market access. Petrobras stated that analyses do 'not indicate the probability' of oil reaching the coast in a spill, though Jean Paul Prates noted the risk is low-probability but high-consequence. Production is not expected to begin for another 'six or seven years,' yet the discovery has already intensified population growth and real estate speculation in Oiapoque, where the mayor estimates 40,000 to 45,000 people now live.

title: PM Modi likely to visit Canada in December to lock in trade deal: Canadian PM Carney
summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney indicated that Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi is likely to visit Canada in December to seal a trade deal. Speaking at the UN General Assembly, Carney described the relationship as exceptionally important. Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal confirmed that the fourth round of negotiations concluded in Mumbai, with the fifth round scheduled to begin on October 5. Negotiations had paused in August 2023 but restarted in 2025 following a thaw in diplomatic relations.

title: HRF Condemns Meta's Restriction of Vizag Data Centre Campaign Account
summary: The Human Rights Forum (HRF) condemned Meta for restricting the Instagram account of the 'Stop Vizag Data Centers' campaign in India on September 19. HRF representatives alleged that the action, along with restrictions on nine other posts, curtailed public scrutiny of hyperscale data center projects under India's Information Technology Rules. The campaign, launched in July, attracted 56 lakh views and 11,800 followers in two months. HRF State general secretary Y. Rajesh and V.S. Krishna demanded that Meta restore the account and disclose the legal basis for the restriction.

title: OpenAI and Anthropic Release Cheaper AI Models
summary: OpenAI and Anthropic have released new AI models aimed at lowering costs for enterprise customers. These updates focus on efficiency and speed rather than introducing groundbreaking capabilities. Anthropic's Opus 5.5 is priced at $4 and $20 per million for input and output tokens, a 20% reduction from the previous version, while cache reads are 60% cheaper.

title: 48th WorldSkills Competition Opens in Shanghai with Record Participation
summary: The 48th WorldSkills Competition officially opened in Shanghai on Tuesday evening. The event is scheduled to run from September 23 to 27, featuring nearly 1,400 young professionals representing 68 countries and regions. Organizers state that this year's competition will set four historical records regarding the number of competitions, new events, participating nations, and competitors.

title: Microsoft Grants DARPA Direct Access to New Maryland Quantum Facility
summary: Microsoft announced on Tuesday that it will grant the US Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency direct, on-site access to its latest quantum computing hardware. This access occurs at a new research center in Maryland opened alongside the University of Maryland. The facility houses a system using the Majorana 2 chip for independent testing and evaluation. Microsoft stated it plans to have commercial quantum systems ready by 2029, while DARPA aims to determine if quantum approaches can yield economically feasible systems by 2033.

title: Tesla Secures Largest US Electric Truck Order via ZET SCALE Alliance
summary: Tesla has been named the primary supplier for the largest electric Class 8 order in US history, comprising 2,500 battery-electric trucks purchased through the ZET SCALE alliance. This deal nearly doubles the current number of such trucks on US roads. However, while demand is high, production capacity remains the constraint, with analysts expecting Tesla to deliver only 5,000 to 15,000 Semis in 2026 at a quoted price of around $290,000 per Long Range truck. The orders will be deployed across ten freight hubs over the next few years.

title: India seeks trade deals with US neighbours to avoid tariffs
summary: India is pursuing trade agreements with Canada and Mexico to diversify its commercial ties and avoid potential tariff threats from the United States. Negotiators from India and Canada are scheduled to hold a fifth round of talks starting October 5, with a deal likely to be finalized in December when Prime Minister Narendra Modi visits Canada. Separately, New Delhi is finalizing a framework with Mexico to begin formal trade negotiations, seeking to lower barriers on goods like automobiles and steel. These moves are part of a broader push to expand trade ties and gain greater access to global markets.

title: Microsoft Disrupts AI Platform Compromising 12,000 Accounts
summary: Microsoft announced Tuesday that it led an industry-wide disruption of EvilTokens, a subscription-based scam platform utilizing an AI chatbot to compromise 12,000 Microsoft accounts over a few-month span. Introduced via a Telegram channel in February, the platform charged an initial $1,500 fee and a recurring $500 monthly charge. It helped criminals analyze inboxes and draft fraudulent emails to trick employees into transferring funds. Microsoft, with assistance from SpyCloud, seized 50 websites and 150 domains. The UK's Metropolitan Police Service arrested two men on suspicion of offenses connected to the platform.

title: Residents Sue Over OpenAI Data Center in Georgia
summary: Effingham County residents and environmental advocates have filed a second lawsuit challenging the OpenAI data center project, known as Project Camellia. The new suit targets the Effingham County Industrial Development Authority, alleging it failed to provide proper public notice and meaningful participation opportunities during the project's approval process. While the project has received key approvals and a significant tax break, plaintiffs argue that major decisions were negotiated behind closed doors. OpenAI plans to build a massive campus near Rincon, Georgia, which will require substantial electricity and water resources, prompting concerns about environmental impacts and grid strain. The project is expected to begin construction in 2028.

title: Apple Settles $250 Million Class Action Over Siri AI Claims
summary: Apple agreed to pay $250 million to settle a class action lawsuit alleging the company overhyped its Apple Intelligence tools and delayed the Siri AI overhaul. The settlement covers US customers who purchased certain iPhone 15 or 16 models between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025. Eligible individuals may receive up to $95 per device. Apple denies wrongdoing, stating the resolution allows it to focus on innovation. Claims must be filed by December 21 via a dedicated website.

title: OpenAI Unveils GPT-6 Sol and Luna with Enhanced Efficiency and Accuracy
summary: OpenAI has expanded its GPT-6 generation with updated Sol and Luna models, emphasizing improved efficiency and affordability. The company states that these models offer half the cost of the previous 5.6 series and demonstrate better factual accuracy and lower error rates in coding. OpenAI also claims its new offerings outperform Anthropic's models, noting intense competition in the AI sector.

title: Trump Supports Potential Diesel Export Ban Amid Record Prices
summary: President Trump declared support for a potential ban on diesel fuel exports as prices hit record highs. While Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent noted the administration is considering the ban's effectiveness, Energy Secretary Chris Wright and Interior Secretary Doug Burgum oppose it. Alaska Senator Dan Sullivan called for a temporary pause to rebuild reserves. The national U.S. average for diesel reached $6.5276 according to AAA.

title: Actor Prakash Raj Launches Electoral Rights Tour in Karnataka
summary: Actor and activist Prakash Raj launched a 10-day 'SIR Resistance Tour' in Kalaburagi to protest the deletion of voters during Karnataka's Special Intensive Revision. Raj claimed 5,21,950 voters were placed in the ASDDO category and argued existing voters should not re-register via Form 6. He highlighted disparities in how officials treat prominent citizens versus marginalized communities and plans to submit findings to the Chief Minister on September 30.

title: Samsung India Electronics Profit Falls 36% in FY26 Amidst Mobile Revenue Decline
summary: Samsung India Electronics reported a 36% decline in profit to ₹7,228.10 crore for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, according to a RoC filing. Although overall revenue from operations rose slightly by 1.2%, the company's primary revenue driver, the mobile phone business, saw a 1.35% decrease. Conversely, revenue from home appliances and audio-visual segments increased, reflecting a strategic focus on diversifying beyond smartphones. The company remains the only player in the Indian appliance space with turnover exceeding ₹1 lakh crore.

title: RBI Absorbs ₹71,971 Crore Liquidity via VRRR Auction
summary: The Reserve Bank of India absorbed ₹71,971 crore from the banking system through an overnight Variable Reverse Repo Rate auction held on September 22, 2026. The auction, totaling ₹75,000 crore, received offers for 96% of the amount at a rate of 5.24%. This move aims to manage excess liquidity, which can be inflationary, particularly following a $133 billion inflow from NRI special deposits, and to synchronize overnight call money rates with the repo rate ahead of a potential rate hike cycle.

title: Recent AI Model Updates and Market Developments Listed
summary: A webpage dated 22nd September 2026 lists recent articles concerning artificial intelligence developments. The entries mention the release of Claude Opus 5.5 and various GPT-6 models, a new pricing strategy, and a novel LLM architecture called System One introduced by Jev on 21st September 2026.

title: India accelerates trade talks with Canada and Mexico amid US tariffs
summary: India is accelerating trade negotiations with Canada and Mexico to diversify commercial ties and mitigate the impact of US tariff policies. Negotiators plan to hold a fifth round of talks with Canada starting October 5, building on recent discussions. Separately, India is finalizing a framework with Mexico to begin formal negotiations. Officials aim to make faster progress as all three countries seek new markets and partners.

title: Canada and India Aim to Finalize Trade Talks by G20
summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced that trade negotiations with India are making good progress, with both countries aiming to conclude talks by the G20 summit in mid-December. Carney noted that Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to visit Canada around that time. These efforts follow a deep diplomatic rupture over the 2023 killing of activist Hardeep Singh Nijjar. Carney has moved quickly to rebuild ties, marking his first bilateral visit to India since 2018.

title: Anthropic Releases Opus 5.5 with Lower Prices and Improved Performance
summary: Anthropic released Opus 5.5, a new model claiming state-of-the-art performance in coding and knowledge work that outperforms its larger Fable model in many benchmarks.
